By Jeff Agbodo, Abakaliki
The people of Ndiebor Ishieke Autonomous Community in Ebonyi Local Government Area of Ebonyi State have called for strict compliance with the directive of the Minister of Works, Senator David Umahi, on borrow-pit operations along the ongoing Calabar–Ebonyi–Enugu-Benue–Nasarawa–Abuja Superhighway project.
The community urged the relevant authorities and the project contractor to ensure that further excavation activities complied with the minister’s directive, particularly regarding landowners’ consent, consultation with host communities and the protection of farmlands and economic crops.
The stakeholders, who commended Umahi for his intervention over concerns about alleged damage to agricultural lands in the area, said effective enforcement of the directive was necessary to safeguard rural livelihoods, prevent further encroachment and avert avoidable disputes between affected residents and the project authorities.
The community in a joint statement signed by the traditional ruler of Ndiebor Ishieke Autonomous Community, Eze Hyacinth Awoke Nwiboko; the President of the community.
They acknowledged the interventions and contributions of Ebonyi State Governor, Francis Nwifuru, and Senator Peter Nwebonyi, representing Ebonyi North Senatorial District, towards addressing the concerns associated with the project.
They, however, maintained that the minister’s directive must translate into concrete measures to protect affected landowners and ensure that construction activities were conducted in accordance with the relevant safeguards.
According to the statement, the community supports the superhighway project because of its potential to improve transportation, facilitate the movement of agricultural produce and other goods, and stimulate economic development across the benefiting states.
The stakeholders nevertheless cautioned that the pursuit of infrastructure development should not undermine the property rights, economic security and environmental safety of host communities.
“Our community supports the superhighway project and recognises its potential to boost transportation, trade and economic development.
However, we maintain that infrastructure development must respect the land rights, agricultural livelihoods and environmental safety of host communities,” the statement said.
The community expressed concern over reports of damage to farmlands and economic crops, noting that agriculture remained a major source of livelihood for many households in the area.
It identified yam, cassava, rice, millet and beniseed among the crops cultivated by residents, warning that the destruction of productive farmland could worsen the economic difficulties of affected farming families.
The stakeholders consequently called for a transparent assessment of the alleged losses and appropriate compensation for verified damage to crops, farmland and other legitimate property interests arising from the excavation activities.
They also urged the relevant authorities to establish effective communication channels involving traditional institutions, community representatives, landowners, project supervisors and the contractor before further borrow-pit operations were undertaken.
The community leaders said prior consultation and timely communication would help prevent misunderstandings, promote mutual trust and ensure that legitimate grievances were addressed before they escalated into disputes.
They further called for the reclamation of abandoned or exhausted borrow pits and the implementation of adequate environmental safeguards to protect residents, agricultural land and the surrounding ecosystem from hazards associated with excavation activities.
The signatories stressed that transparent procedures for assessing affected properties and determining compensation were essential to securing the cooperation of host communities and sustaining public confidence in the project.
On the broader development concerns, the community commended Governor Nwifuru for his administration’s development efforts in Ebonyi State and acknowledged Senator Nwebonyi’s representation of the district, including his reported legislative contributions towards attracting the superhighway project.
They appealed to both public officials to sustain their engagement with the relevant federal authorities to ensure that the concerns of affected residents received appropriate attention.
The statement added that the successful implementation of the project required a balance between the Federal Government’s infrastructure objectives and the legitimate interests of communities whose lands were affected by construction activities.
Reaffirming their commitment to peaceful engagement, the traditional ruler and other signatories pledged the community’s cooperation with the Federal Government, the Ebonyi State Government, the Ministry of Works and the contractor in finding a lasting resolution to the concerns.
“Our position is clear: we support the superhighway project, but development must not come at the expense of our land rights, livelihoods and environmental safety,” the statement added.
The stakeholders expressed hope that compliance with Umahi’s directive would lead to practical measures to protect affected landowners, address outstanding compensation claims and ensure that construction activities proceeded without unnecessary conflict with host communities.

….seals unapproved guest house
By Jeff Agbodo, Abakaliki
The Ebonyi State Ministry of Capital City and Urban Planning has arrested 30 suspected sex workers over alleged security concerns and the discovery of suspected hard drugs at the premises in a guest house in Abakaliki.
The team also sealed the Guest House in Abakaliki following an inspection of unapproved building used as guest House.
The Commissioner for Capital City and Urban Planning, Hon. Richard Ugo Idike, in collaboration with the Commissioner for Internal Security, Hon. Prince Etta Uka Ude, alongside security operatives and members of the ministry’s taskforce carried out the operation.
Addressing journalists during the inspection, Hon. Idike expressed concern over the alleged security threats associated with activities at the guest house. He noted that the presence of individuals reportedly from different states had raised concerns about security and public safety in the area.
The Commissioner disclosed that the team discovered substances suspected to be hard drugs, including wrappers allegedly containing substances locally referred to as Colos and Indian hemp, among others.
The suspected substances were reportedly recovered during the operation, while security operatives took charge of the matter.
Idike reiterated the state government’s commitment to ensuring that buildings within Abakaliki are used for lawful purposes and comply with approved development plans.
He called on property developers and building owners to obtain the necessary building approvals from the Ministry of Capital City and Urban Planning before commencing construction, stressing that the government would not tolerate the use of unapproved buildings for activities that could threaten public safety.
The Commissioner subsequently directed that Guest House be sealed indefinitely pending further clarification and compliance with the ministry’s requirements. He also directed the owner of the facility to visit the ministry to explain the circumstances surrounding the building and resolve the outstanding issues
The Commissioner for Internal Security, Hon. Prince Etta Uka Ude, in his remarks said the primary concern of his ministry was to ensure adequate security and protect residents of Ebonyi State.
He stated that the state government would not tolerate the use of any premises as a haven for criminal activities.
Ude added that the Ebonyi State Government, under the leadership of governor Francis Ogbonna Nwifuru, remained committed to maintaining peace, law and order across the state.
He urged security agencies to intensify surveillance and monitoring of establishments suspected of engaging in illegal activities, particularly within Abakaliki, to prevent criminal elements from exploiting business premises to undermine public safety.
The Commissioner stressed the importance of collaboration between government agencies, security operatives and members of the public in identifying and addressing security threats.
At the time of filing this report, the over 30 arrested individuals had reportedly been taken into police custody for further investigation, while the owner of the Guest House had yet to be arrested.
The sealing of the facility underscores the state government’s enforcement efforts concerning building regulations, public safety and security within the capital city.

items.content:
…Adopts zoning arrangement, calls for peaceful election
By Jeff Agbodo, Abakaliki
The Ebonyi State Leaders and Stakeholders’ Political Summit has endorsed Governor Francis Nwifuru for a second term in office ahead of the 2027 governorship election.
The endorsement was made through a unanimous voice vote at the summit held on Tuesday at the Ecumenical Centre, Abakaliki, following a motion moved by the senator representing Ebonyi North, Onyekachi Nwebonyi.
The summit, which brought together political leaders and stakeholders from the three senatorial zones and 13 local government areas of the state, was held under the theme, “Orderly and Peaceful Political Transition in Ebonyi State: The Way Forward.”
Among those who attended were the first civilian governor of the state, Senator Sam Egwu; former Senate President Anyim Pius Anyim; former governor Martin Elechi; former governor and Minister of Works, Senator David Umahi; and Nwifuru, who attended as Special Guest of Honour.
The stakeholders deliberated on the future of the state, with particular emphasis on political stability, zoning, equity, continuity in governance and the need for a peaceful transition ahead of the 2027 general elections.
In a communiqué issued at the end of the summit, the participants reaffirmed their commitment to peace, unity and political stability, describing them as essential to the continued development of Ebonyi.
The communiqué, which was read by Mrs Chioma Nweze, was signed by Umahi, Anyim, Egwu and other leaders present on behalf of the summit.
They called on political leaders, public office holders, traditional rulers, religious leaders, civil society organisations and citizens to protect the state’s unity, irrespective of political affiliation and other differences.
The summit urged political parties, aspirants and their supporters to conduct their activities with restraint and mutual respect, while rejecting inflammatory rhetoric, intimidation, political violence and other actions capable of disrupting public order.
On the contentious issue of zoning, the summit expressed support for the continuation of the governorship rotation arrangement among the three senatorial zones, saying the practice had helped promote inclusion and political stability since the beginning of the Fourth Republic in 1999.
The communiqué noted that the state’s first three elected governors — Egwu from Ebonyi North, Elechi from Ebonyi Central and Umahi from Ebonyi South — each served two four-year terms.
It said the arrangement had encouraged continuity, mutual accommodation and respect for established political understandings among the zones.
The summit consequently resolved that Ebonyi North should complete the governorship slot in the 2027 electoral cycle, in line with the zoning principle recognised by the participants.
It further proposed that the governorship should move to Ebonyi Central in 2031 and remain there for eight years before moving to Ebonyi South in 2039 for another eight years.
The proposed rotation schedule provides for Ebonyi North from 2023 to 2031, Ebonyi Central from 2031 to 2039 and Ebonyi South from 2039 to 2047.
The stakeholders also called for the equitable distribution of public amenities and development projects among the zones, stressing the need to sustain fairness, justice and peaceful coexistence.
On governance, the summit commended Nwifuru’s administration for its development initiatives under the People’s Charter of Needs.
It identified infrastructure and rural development, education, healthcare, agriculture, food security, human capital development, women’s empowerment and youth development as important areas requiring sustained attention.
The summit urged political leaders and other stakeholders to continue promoting dialogue across party lines and discourage actions capable of creating unnecessary tension during the transition period.
It also called on political parties, aspirants, security agencies, electoral authorities and the media to work towards peaceful, credible and orderly elections in 2027.
The participants urged politicians to pursue their ambitions through lawful and democratic means, respect the rights of other citizens, avoid hate speech and misinformation, and recognise the role of relevant institutions in electoral matters.
The communiqué expressed appreciation to the leaders and representatives of the 13 local government areas, political parties and community organisations who participated in the deliberations.
It reaffirmed the summit’s aspiration for an Ebonyi State that remains peaceful, united, inclusive and development-oriented, while urging leaders and citizens to translate the resolutions into practical commitments that would advance the welfare of the people.
“Participants called on all political actors and their supporters to conduct political activities with restraint, mutual respect and a commitment to peaceful engagement. They further urged stakeholders to reject inflammatory rhetoric, intimidation, political violence and any conduct capable of undermining public order.
“The summit recognised that continuity, mutual accommodation and respect for established political understandings have contributed to the State’s stability. It therefore encouraged political leaders and stakeholders to sustain a culture of dialogue, fairness and responsible political engagement in addressing questions relating to succession and the future leadership of the State.
“The summit acknowledged the long-standing practice of senatorial rotation in the distribution of the governorship of Ebonyi State and the role this arrangement has played in promoting a sense of inclusion among the three senatorial zones. In the interest of equity, fairness, mutual trust and the preservation of peaceful coexistence, the summit expressed support for the continuation of the established zoning understanding in the consideration of the 2027 governorship succession.
“Accordingly, the summit resolved that Ebonyi North Senatorial Zone should be allowed to complete the governorship in the 2027 electoral cycle, in keeping with the rotation principle recognised by the participants and the objective of equitable political inclusion.
“The summit called on political parties, aspirants, supporters, security agencies, electoral authorities and the media to contribute to a peaceful, credible and orderly electoral process.
“Political parties and aspirants were urged to pursue their ambitions through lawful and democratic means, respect the rights of fellow citizens, avoid hate speech and misinformation, and accept the legitimate role of relevant institutions in the conduct and resolution of electoral matters” the communique stated.
The post 2027: Ebonyi Stakeholders’ Summit endorses Nwifuru for Second Term appeared first on Vanguard News.

The former Governor of Ebonyi State Dr. Sam Ominyi Egwu, has clarified that the stakeholders’ political summit was not a political party affairs and was not convened to adopt any presidential candidate.
Dr. Egwu who was the Chairman of the Ebonyi 2026 Stakeholders Political Summit while reacting to the motion moved by the Senator representing Ebonyi North Senatorial Zone, Senator Onyekachi Nwebonyi, calling for endorsing of a presidential candidate during the summit held at the Christian Ecumenical Centre, Abakaliki said the event was not for endorsement of a presidential candidate.

He stressed that the summit was not meant to project any political party or presidential candidate, but to affirm the collective support of Ebonyi stakeholders for the zoning arrangement which has brought about a peaceful political atmosphere devoid of marginalisation.

The governor of Anambra State, Professor Chukwuma Soludo, has congratulated His Grace, Most Rev. Valerian Maduka Okeke, the Archbishop of Onitsha and Metropolitan of Onitsha Ecclesiastical Province, on his 73rd birthday.
In the goodwill message, Governor Soludo described the Archbishop as a shepherd of uncommon humility, wisdom and moral courage, whose ministry has strengthened the faith of many and nurtured hope across Anambra State and beyond.
“For more than two decades at the helm of the Archdiocese of Onitsha, His Grace has offered steady, prayerful leadership, speaking truth with charity and guiding the faithful with the quiet authority of a true Servant of God”, the governor said.
Soludo noted that the Archbishop’s impact reaches well beyond the pulpit, adding that through the Church’s schools, health institutions and charitable outreach, he has championed the dignity of the human person, widened opportunity for young people and extended compassion to the poor, the sick and the forgotten.
The governor also commended the Archbishop for his enduring tradition of marking his birthday with the inmates of the Onitsha Custodial Centre, noting that the gesture reflects the Gospel imperative to remember those in bondage and affirms that no one is beyond redemption, mercy or the possibility of a fresh start.
“It is a testimony to a life lived in imitation of Christ, who came to serve and not to be served,” the Governor
While wishing Archbishop Okeke a happy birthday, he also prayed that God will continue to grant him good health, renewed strength, and many more fruitful years in the service of the Church and humanity.

items.title: FG not planning fuel tax, Oyedele clarifies
items.summary:
By Henry Ojelu
The Minister of Finance and Coordinating Minister of the Economy, Taiwo Oyedele, has dismissed reports that the Federal Government plans to introduce a fuel tax when the economy stabilises, describing them as “fake news.”
Oyedele, in a post on Tuesday, reiterated that introducing a fuel tax at this time would be insensitive, particularly following the removal of the petrol subsidy.
He said reports suggesting that the government would introduce the levy after economic conditions improve were false, distancing the Federal Government from the claims.
The minister’s clarification comes amid concerns over the impact of petrol subsidy removal on Nigerians and the wider economy.
Oyedele’s statement sought to dispel speculation about a planned fuel tax, stressing that the reports did not reflect the government’s position.
The post FG not planning fuel tax, Oyedele clarifies appeared first on Vanguard News.

items.author: Emmanuel Okogba
items.content:
By Sola Ogundipe
Uganda has asked Nigeria to provide detailed travel and clinical records of a woman confirmed to have the Ebola virus disease in the Federal Capital Territory (FCT) Abuja, following Nigeria’s confirmation of the infection.
Nigeria confirmed the Ebola case on Tuesday, after laboratory testing of the case, a woman who recently arrived in Nigeria after travelling from Uganda, and currently is receiving medical care in isolation.
In a statement, Prof. Charles Olaro, the Director General of Health Services, Uganda Ministry of Health, said the information was required to guide further investigations and determine whether additional contact tracing was necessary, even as he stressed that the woman’s transit through Uganda did not establish that she contracted the virus there.
The statement, issued on Tuesday in Kampala, said the Ministry of Health was awaiting further information from the Nigerian government to help establish the circumstances surrounding the infection, stating that it would strengthen screening and other public health measures at points of entry in collaboration with relevant agencies.
Preliminary information cited by the Ugandan authorities revealed that the woman, who travelled to the eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo for business, transited through Uganda in early October without showing symptoms, but reportedly developed symptoms after arriving in Nigeria, as the location where she contracted the virus remains under investigation.
The statement, titled “Reported Ebola Case in Nigeria: Ministry Calls for Calm and Vigilance” reads in part: “The Ministry of Health has noted reports of a confirmed Ebola case in Nigeria involving a Nigerian woman who reportedly travelled to the eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo for business.
“Preliminary information indicates that she transited through Uganda in early October without showing symptoms and developed symptoms after arriving in Nigeria. Her transit through Uganda does not establish that she contracted the infection there. The location of exposure remains under investigation.
“The Government of Nigeria is yet to provide detailed information on the woman’s travel itinerary and clinical history to guide further investigations and any necessary contact tracing.
“The Ministry wishes to clarify that, as of the date of this statement, Uganda has no confirmed active Ebola cases.”
It said limited provisions had been maintained to facilitate humanitarian and diplomatic movements. The Ministry, working with relevant agencies, will further strengthen screening and public health measures at points of entry.
The post Uganda seeks details of Nigeria’s confirmed Ebola case appeared first on Vanguard News.

items.author: Oboh
items.content:
*Project to strengthen domestic gas distribution, support industrial growth and expand access to cleaner, cost-effective energy across southwestern Nigeria.
AKURE — OCTAGRAM Fusion CNG Limited (“OCTAGRAM”) and the Ondo State Development and Investment Promotion Agency (“ONDIPA”) have announced a strategic agreement for the development of a proposed 9 million standard cubic feet per day (MMSCFD) Compressed Natural Gas (CNG) mother station within the Ore industrial Park in Omotosho area of Ondo State.
The long-term agreement, executed on 14 October 2026, provides for the location of the proposed facility within the industrial park, in proximity to existing national natural gas pipeline infrastructure. This strategic location is expected to facilitate access to gas feedstock, subject to the necessary technical and commercial arrangements, while positioning the project to serve industrial and transportation energy demand across Ondo State and the wider southwestern Nigerian market.
The agreement follows OCTAGRAM’s successful attainment of a Licence to Establish (LTE) from the Nigerian Midstream and Downstream Petroleum Regulatory Authority (NMDPRA) in May 2026, representing an important regulatory milestone in the project’s development.
The company is currently progressing the requirements for its Licence to Construct (LTC), alongside engineering development, commercial arrangements and other preparatory activities.
Supporting Nigeria’s Gas-Led Industrial Development
The proposed facility is designed to provide a reliable source of compressed natural gas for industrial manufacturers, commercial transportation fleets, independent CNG distribution operators and other energy-intensive businesses.
At its planned production capacity of 9 MMSCFD, the station is expected to support the expansion of virtual pipeline infrastructure, enabling natural gas to be transported by specialised high-pressure containers and delivered to customers beyond the reach of conventional gas pipeline networks.
The investment aligns with Nigeria’s broader ambition to increase domestic natural gas utilisation, diversify energy sources and improve industrial competitiveness.
The development is expected to support the efforts of the administration of Governor Dr. Lucky Orinisan Aiyedatiwa in the drive to growing Ondo State industrial ecosystem, attract complementary investment and create economic opportunities across gas transportation, logistics, engineering, operations and associated services.
A Strategic Partnership for Industrial Growth
Speaking on the agreement, Barrister Emmanuel Omomowo, Chief Executive Officer ONDIPA, said:
“Ondo State remains committed to attracting investments that unlock our natural resources, strengthen industrial infrastructure and create sustainable economic opportunities for our people.
“Our agreement with OCTAGRAM Fusion CNG represents another important step towards positioning Ondo State as a competitive destination for energy-intensive industries and private-sector investment.
“We welcome this project and look forward to supporting its successful development in accordance with the applicable regulatory framework.”
Olutunde Odeyale, CEO, OCTAGRAM Fusion CNG Limited, commented: “Our investment thesis is built around a clear commercial opportunity: Nigeria has substantial natural gas resources, yet many industrial and commercial consumers remain unable to access reliable and competitively priced gas.
“By locating our proposed mother station close to existing gas transmission infrastructure at Omotosho, we intend to bridge that gap through an efficient CNG production and distribution platform.
“The agreement with ONDIPA and our attainment of the Licence to Establish are significant steps towards delivering that vision. Our immediate priorities are to complete the remaining regulatory processes, advance our infrastructure development plans and establish long-term relationships with customers and commercial partners.”
Expanding Access to Natural Gas
The proposed facility is expected to serve customers within an economically viable distribution radius of Omotosho, including industrial clusters and transportation corridors connecting Ondo State with Lagos, Ekiti, Ogun, Edo and neighbouring markets.
OCTAGRAM intends to deploy a distribution model combining mother-station compression capacity with specialised CNG transportation equipment and downstream delivery infrastructure.
The company is actively exploring long-term gas supply and offtake arrangements with industrial consumers, power producers, fleet operators, CNG daughter-station operators and other prospective customers.
The project remains subject to the necessary regulatory approvals, satisfactory technical arrangements and completion of commercial and financing requirements.
Looking Ahead
Following the execution of the ONDIPA agreement and receipt of its Licence to Establish, OCTAGRAM will continue progressing the necessary regulatory, engineering, procurement and commercial activities ahead of construction.
Further announcements will be made as the project achieves subsequent development milestones, including the receipt of its Licence to Construct and the commencement of construction activities.
About OCTAGRAM Fusion CNG Limited
OCTAGRAM Fusion CNG Limited is a Nigerian energy infrastructure development company focused on expanding access to compressed natural gas through strategically located compression and distribution facilities.
The company is developing a proposed 9 MMSCFD CNG mother station in the Omotosho industrial area of Ondo State, with the objective of providing reliable and commercially competitive natural gas supply solutions to industrial, commercial and transportation customers.
About ONDIPA
The Ondo State Development and Investment Promotion Agency (ONDIPA) is the one-shop investment promotion and facilitation agency of the Ondo State Government.
The agency works to attract and facilitate private investment, promote strategic economic opportunities and support sustainable industrial and economic development across Ondo State.

items.author: Emmanuel Okogba
items.content:
By James Ogunnaike, Abeokuta
The Nigerian Medical Association (NMA) has called on the Federal Government to provide doctors with internationally competitive remuneration, improved working conditions and safer workplaces to stem the growing exodus of medical professionals from the country.
The association warned that excessive workloads, occupational stress, inadequate healthcare infrastructure, poor remuneration and declining welfare were undermining physicians’ wellbeing and threatening the future of medical practice in Nigeria.
The Chairman of the NMA in Ogun State, Dr Sunday Enimola, made the call at a press conference in Abeokuta as part of activities marking the 2026 Physicians’ Week, themed “Securing the Future of Medicine in Nigeria.”
Enimola said Nigeria must move beyond lamenting the migration of doctors and implement practical policies that would encourage medical professionals to remain in the country and build fulfilling careers.
According to him, appeals to patriotism alone would not reverse the trend without deliberate efforts to improve the conditions under which doctors work and live.
“Patriotism should be supported by decent working conditions, professional dignity, security, competitive remuneration, opportunities for career development and a health system in which doctors can see a future for themselves and their families,” he said.
He urged the government and hospital chief executives to prioritise physicians’ welfare, occupational safety and professional development, stressing that the survival of Nigeria’s healthcare system depended largely on the wellbeing and retention of its medical workforce.
Enimola called for a fundamental shift in the culture of medical practice, which, he said, often expected doctors to sacrifice their personal wellbeing in the service of patients.
He argued that the longstanding expectation that physicians should continue working despite exhaustion and neglect their health in fulfilling their professional responsibilities was neither sustainable nor beneficial to patients.
According to him, a physician who is physically exhausted, emotionally depleted and chronically stressed cannot indefinitely deliver the quality of care patients deserve.
He called for greater awareness of the mental and physical health challenges confronting medical professionals, urging doctors to embrace preventive healthcare, regular medical examinations, healthy lifestyles, adequate rest and confidential professional and psychological support.
The NMA chairman also advocated work environments where doctors could take leave without guilt, rest without shame and seek assistance without fear of being perceived as weak.
He maintained that physicians’ wellbeing should be treated as an essential component of patient safety and overall health system performance, rather than a personal concern left to individual practitioners.
Enimola identified excessive working hours, occupational stress, unsafe working environments, inadequate staffing, violence against healthcare workers, poor remuneration and delayed entitlements as some of the factors exposing doctors to physical and psychological risks.
He warned that Nigeria could not afford to continue losing medical professionals to preventable causes while they were still actively engaged in saving lives.
The association also condemned threats, intimidation, assaults and other forms of violence against healthcare workers, insisting that hospitals must provide safe environments for both medical professionals and patients.
“Hospitals must be places of healing, not theatres of violence,” Enimola said.
He stressed that doctors could not deliver compassionate and effective healthcare while constantly worrying about their personal safety.
Among the measures he identified as necessary to protect physicians were safer workplaces, adequate security, appropriate medical equipment, functional healthcare infrastructure, decent accommodation where necessary and improved conditions of service.
“The safety of doctors is not negotiable. And when doctors are safe, patients are safer,” he added.
Enimola further called for greater investment in emerging technologies, warning that Nigeria must prepare its healthcare system for the rapid transformation taking place in medical practice globally.
He identified artificial intelligence (AI), telemedicine, electronic medical records, precision medicine, digital diagnostics, remote patient monitoring, robotics and genomics as innovations increasingly reshaping healthcare delivery.
According to him, Nigeria could not afford to remain on the margins of the technological revolution transforming the health sector.
He, however, cautioned that technology should complement medical professionals rather than undermine the human relationships at the heart of healthcare.
“Technology must serve the doctor and the patient, not replace the humanity at the heart of medicine,” he said.
He explained that future physicians would require skills beyond traditional clinical knowledge, including data analysis, artificial intelligence, digital health, cybersecurity, research methodology, health economics, communication, leadership and interdisciplinary collaboration.
He consequently urged medical schools to review their curricula to ensure that students and young doctors were adequately prepared for the changing demands of healthcare delivery.
The NMA chairman also called for increased investment in undergraduate and postgraduate medical education, improved teaching hospitals, stronger research capacity and better support for academic physicians.
He warned against compromising the standards of medical training, maintaining that the quality of future healthcare would depend largely on the quality of education provided to medical students and young doctors.
“The quality of tomorrow’s healthcare depends on the quality of today’s medical education. We cannot afford to compromise standards,” he said.
While advocating the preservation of high training standards, Enimola called for the adoption of modern educational methods, including simulation, digital learning, virtual collaboration, competency-based education and interdisciplinary training.
He said medical education must equip future physicians with the ability to think critically, adapt to emerging challenges and pursue continuous professional development throughout their careers.

items.author: Emmanuel Okogba
items.content:
Phil Foden hit a hat-trick to underline his long-awaited return to form as Manchester City crushed AEK Athens 5-1 in the Champions League on Tuesday.
After a significant dip over the last two seasons, Foden provided hope of a renaissance for the England playmaker with a sublime display at the Etihad Stadium.
The 26-year-old, who has admitted struggling with mental health issues, hadn’t scored for 10 months prior to his goal in Saturday’s win against Ipswich.
Long heralded as one of England’s brightest talents, Foden was left out of his country’s World Cup squad earlier this year in a damning sign of his fall from grace.
Having ended his run without a goal in the Champions League since November 2025, Foden now has to produce nights like this on a regular basis to complete his revival.
Elliot Anderson put City ahead early in the first half with his first goal for the club since his close-season move from Nottingham Forest.
Foden doubled City’s lead before the break and although Stavros Pilios pulled one back for the Greek side after the interval, the Premier League leaders finished with a flourish.
Rayan Cherki bagged City’s third goal in typically flamboyant fashion and Foden struck twice more to complete his treble.
It was City’s second win in the league phase after beating Porto in their opening game and losing to holders Paris Saint-Germain last week.
City’s future remains in limbo as they wait the result of their appeal against an independent commission’s verdict that they were guilty of more than 100 breaches of the Premier League’s financial rules.
With reports emerging that City are set to be hit with a massive points deduction that will almost certainly condemn them to relegation, this season’s Champions League campaign could be the club’s last for some time.
Enzo Maresca and his players have shown little sign of being affected by the scandal, while City’s fans defiantly show their backing for the Abu Dhabi-owned club.
They have won 10 of their 11 games in all competitions this season and even the absence of Erling Haaland couldn’t derail them.
Manchester City’s English midfielder #47 Phil Foden celebrates scoring the team’s fourth goal during the UEFA Champions League football match between Manchester City and AEK Athens at the Etihad Stadium in Manchester, north west England, on October 20, 2026. (Photo by Oli SCARFF / AFP)
– Fantastic Foden –
City started with Haaland on the bench after the Norway striker limped down the tunnel at the final whistle with a foot injury following his double against Ipswich.
Maresca made eight changes from the Ipswich game, with 17-year-old academy graduate Floyd Samba showing flashes of his talent on the flanks.
City’s understudies took just 12 minutes to seize the lead.
Enzo Fernadez’s free-kick cannoned down off the bar and Anderson reacted quicker than the flat-footed AEK defence as the midfielder slotted into the empty net from 10 yards.
Foden doubled City’s lead at the climax of an eye-catching move in the 34th minute.
Exchanging passes in a blur of movement and precision, Foden and Rico Lewis cut through AEK with ease before Foden fired high into the roof of the net from an acute angle.
Perhaps overconfident after such a one-sided half, City lost their focus, allowing Pilios to reduce the deficit with their first shot on target in the 52nd minute.
City quickly regained their two-goal lead in the 57th minute.
Picked out by Foden on the edge of the area, Cherki unfurled a balletic turn that took him into space for a fine finish in keeping with his graceful first touch.
In the 65th minute, Cherki’s long ball was knocked down by Lewis and Foden arrived to caress his shot into the top corner from 18 yards.
Foden made a perfectly-timed run to tap home Ryan McAidoo’s cross in the 76th minute, sealing his first hat-trick for over two years.

items.author: Emmanuel Okogba
items.content:
By Emmanuel Okogba
The National Basketball Association (NBA) has announced a record number of players born in Africa or with at least one parent born on the continent on opening-night rosters for the 2026-27 season, with six Nigerian players listed among the international contingent.
According to the league, more than 60 players with African backgrounds feature on opening-night rosters, while the overall number of international players stands at 125 from 43 countries across six continents.
The NBA said this marks the sixth consecutive season with at least 120 international players and the 13th straight season with at least 100.
The six players listed under Nigeria are Ugonna Onyenso of the Detroit Pistons, Charles Bassey of the Golden State Warriors, Adem Bona of the Philadelphia 76ers, Precious Achiuwa of the Sacramento Kings, Josh Okogie of the Utah Jazz and Felix Okpara of the Washington Wizards.
The league also reported that more than 25 of the players with African backgrounds have Nigerian connections, including those born elsewhere or with at least one parent from Nigeria.
Among the prominent players with Nigerian heritage are Miami Heat star Bam Adebayo, New York Knicks forward OG Anunoby and Milwaukee Bucks forward Giannis Antetokounmpo. The African-connected group also includes Philadelphia 76ers centre Joel Embiid and Indiana Pacers forward Pascal Siakam, both of whom were born in Cameroon.
The NBA said France leads the international player count with 17, followed by Canada with 16. Australia has nine players, Germany seven, while Nigeria and Serbia have six each.
France’s representation is led by San Antonio Spurs star Victor Wembanyama, the reigning NBA Defensive Player of the Year. Canada’s contingent includes Oklahoma City Thunder guard Shai Gilgeous-Alexander, the reigning two-time NBA Most Valuable Player.
The Dallas Mavericks, Miami Heat and Washington Wizards have the highest number of international players among NBA teams, with seven each. All 30 franchises have at least one international player on their opening-night rosters.
The league also recorded 70 European players for the season, marking the second consecutive campaign with at least that number.
International players have continued to make their mark on the NBA’s individual awards. According to the league, four international stars have shared the last eight Most Valuable Player awards: Gilgeous-Alexander, Nikola Jokić, Joel Embiid and Giannis Antetokounmpo.
Last season also marked the fifth consecutive campaign in which three international players finished among the top three in MVP voting, with Gilgeous-Alexander first, Jokić second and Wembanyama third.
The NBA further announced that a record 19 international players who have previously been named All-Stars are on opening-night rosters for the 2026-27 season.
More than 45 players on the rosters have also participated in Basketball Without Borders, the NBA and International Basketball Federation’s global basketball development and community outreach programme.
The 2026-27 campaign is the NBA’s 81st regular season. The league said its games would reach fans in 214 countries and territories in more than 50 languages through broadcast partners and NBA League Pass.
The record African representation and Nigeria’s six-player contingent underscore the continued presence of Nigerian talent in the NBA as the league expands its international reach.

By Dickson Omobola
Following the confirmation of an Ebola Virus Disease case in the Federal Capital Territory, FCT, the Federal Airports Authority of Nigeria, FAAN, has said it is working with the Nigeria Centre for Disease Control and Prevention, NCDC, Port Health Services, the Nigeria Civil Aviation Authority, NCAA, and other relevant agencies to support ongoing containment efforts.

Director of Public Affairs and Consumer Protection at FAAN, Henry Agbebire, in a statement, said the authority had maintained heightened vigilance across airport operations and would continue to coordinate with public health authorities.
The statement reads: “The early identification of the case and commencement of contact tracing underscore the importance of established public health protocols, effective surveillance and inter-agency collaboration in responding to potential health threats.
“FAAN is maintaining heightened vigilance across airport operations and will continue to coordinate with public health authorities, align its response with further guidance and support additional measures considered necessary to safeguard passengers, airport personnel and the wider public.
“The authority urges passengers, airport users, airlines and other stakeholders to remain calm, vigilant and cooperative with health officials. The public is also advised to rely on verified information and avoid spreading unconfirmed reports.
“FAAN reassures the travelling public of its continued readiness to work with relevant agencies to protect public health and support the safe operation of Nigeria’s airports.”

items.author: Emmanuel Okogba
items.content:
Holders Paris Saint-Germain made it three wins from three in this season’s Champions League, beating Barcelona 4-2 thanks to late goals from Vitinha and Fabian Ruiz on Tuesday, while Liverpool clinched a dramatic comeback victory over Villarreal.
Phil Foden scored a hat-trick as Manchester City thrashed AEK Athens 5-1, while there were also much-needed wins for Roma and Napoli.
PSG kept their place at the top of the early league-phase table, but could yet count the cost of injuries suffered by Ousmane Dembele, Marquinhos and Khvicha Kvaratskhelia at the Parc des Princes.
Barcelona twice levelled against the two-time defending champions, but were ultimately well beaten as they slipped to their first defeat of the season.
Hansi Flick’s men had won their previous 11 games in all competitions this term.
Kvaratskhelia hit the post, Dembele hobbled off and Ferran Torres was denied by Barca goalkeeper Joan Garcia in a fast-paced opening.
PSG took a deserved lead in the 38th minute as Desire Doue collected the ball outside the area and thumped a shot into the bottom corner.
Garcia made another excellent save shortly after the break from Achraf Hakimi, before Xavi Espart burst through to level for Barca against the run of play.
Kvaratskhelia and Marquinhos both pulled up injured within seconds of each other and had to leave the field.
The home team continued to press, though, and Lucas Hernandez restored their advantage 18 minutes from time with a brilliant header, shortly after former Barcelona forward Torres hit the post.
Lamine Yamal powered past Warren Zaire-Emery to equalise again seven minutes later.
But Vitinha hammered home from outside the box in the 81st minute and Ruiz’s tap-in gave Luis Enrique’s team a second straight 4-2 Champions League win after seeing off Man City by the same scoreline last week.
– Liverpool fight back –
Liverpool battled back from two goals down to also maintain their 100-percent record by edging out Villarreal 4-3 at Anfield.
Liverpool fell behind in the fourth minute when Georges Mikautadze pounced on a terrible error from Virgil van Dijk, before Villarreal defender Sergi Cardona strolled through their defence to make it two.
Alexis Mac Allister pulled one back for the hosts nine minutes before half-time by heading in Kostas Tsimikas’s corner.
Andoni Iraola’s men were level in first-half added time through Ronald Araujo’s back-post header after Cardona inexplicably left Rio Ngumoha’s cross.
Mac Allister completed the turnaround by firing in from Ngumoha’s square pass, and half-time substitute Florian Wirtz’s first goal of the season gave the Reds some breathing space.
Tani Oluwaseyi set up a nervy finish for Iraola, but Liverpool held on.
At the Etihad, Elliot Anderson put Manchester City in front with his first goal for the club, tapping in a 12th-minute opener after Enzo Fernandez’s free-kick bounced back off the crossbar.
Phil Foden made it two goals in as many games after scoring against Ipswich at the weekend, but AEK halved the deficit early in the second half through Stavros Pilios.
Rayan Cherki capped a fine individual performance by sweeping in City’s third in the 57th minute.
Foden later fired in his second and third goals in a comprehensive victory, despite Erling Haaland being rested after picking up a knock at the weekend.
– Respite for Serie A clubs –
Roma eased to their first Champions League win since 2019 as the capital club brushed aside pointless Slovan Bratislava 4-0 at the Stadio Olimpico.
All four Serie A clubs in the competition lost last week, but Napoli made it two wins from two on Tuesday for the Italian sides.

items.content:
Senior Special Assistant to the President on Community Engagement (North-West), Hon. Abdullahi Tanko Yakasai, has disclosed that plans are underway to mobilise at least ₦20 billion over the next four years to confront flooding, drought, desertification, migration and other climate issues across the North West zone.
He made the disclosure at the North-West Climate Summit, which held at the Banquet Hall of the Presidential Villa, Abuja.
Yakasai said the gathering was aimed at creating the enabling environment for states and local governments to connect with development partners, financial institutions and investors.
The initiative, he said, is being implemented in partnership with the Northern Governors’ Forum, the North-West Governors’ Forum and the North-West Development Commission.
He explained that there would be a Climate Academy expected to train 10,000 young people across the North-West on climate resilience, climate action and related areas.
Also, the Climate Fund will channel resources towards interventions on flooding, drought, renewable energy and other climate-related challenges.
“That fund will be channelled through the Office of the SSA on Community Engagement to tackle those issues,” Yakasai said.
“We are looking at the region of N20 billion in the next four years. All these are aimed at easing the problems of climate, because this is what is bedevilling the whole world.”
He further explained that the initiative began last year and is intended to strengthen Nigeria’s position ahead of the forthcoming United Nations Climate Change Summit.
“We want to take up what we have gotten here, the discussions we have had here, because we have had a lot of interactive sessions,” Yakasai said.
“We take it up and see where we can match our strength with what we can see at the international climate change summit that is coming up.”
Yakasai identified flooding, migration, drought, dry-season pressures and the need for renewable energy as major challenges facing the North-West.
“Anything that has to do with climate challenge, we focus on it and see how we can help in alleviating those challenges,” he said.
The summit is positioned as an investment-focused platform for climate-resilient agriculture, renewable energy, water security and youth-led green enterprises across Kaduna, Kano, Jigawa, Katsina, Kebbi, Sokoto and Zamfara states.

items.author: Masudul Zarif
items.content:
‘We cannot change the river, and we cannot stop moving’
Originally published on Global Voices
Boats and people on the Turag River, Dhaka, Bangladesh. Image via Flickr by Wonderlane. CC BY 2.0.
For nomadic Bede families on the Jamuna River in central Bangladesh, moving is a routine part of life. A study published in May 2026 in the journal Cambridge Prisms: Global Mental Health looked at three nomadic settlements in Tangail district of central Bangladesh: Jugiyar Char, Palima and Char Nikrail. It found that these families move several times a year, driven by seasonal floods and erosion, as well as searches for paying audiences. However, climate change and increasingly unpredictable river conditions are forcing these communities to land.
The researchers conducted a micro-case study through 12 interviews and one focus group during Bangladesh’s 2025 monsoon season (June through October). It describes displacement as an ongoing condition, not a single event. “We cannot change the river, and we cannot stop moving,” one sardar, or community leader, told them.
A second study, published online in August 2026 in Dhaka University’s Social Science Review, highlights the dire environmental exposure and disaster vulnerabilities of Bede settlements in Munshiganj, calling for organized cooperation between government agencies and relief NGOs.
Who are the Bede?
The Bede are a traditionally mobile community that has lived and worked on Bangladesh’s rivers for generations. They have long been marginalized in Bangladeshi society, and many make a living as snake charmers, folk healers, sellers of herbal medicine and amulets, and street performers.
Historical accounts often trace the community’s roots to 1638, when groups arrived in Dhaka alongside the exiled king of Myanmar’s northwestern coastal region (then Arakan). It is difficult to get an accurate count of how many Bede exist in Bangladesh today. Climate Watch, a Bangladeshi news site, has cited figures ranging from about 75,000, from the Department of Social Services, to roughly 800,000.
Families traditionally travel in boat groups led by a sardar (leader). When they stop on land, they often camp on riverbanks or on chars, the sandbars that big rivers build up and wash away.
This is not ordinary migration. Researchers from the study published in Cambridge Prisms: Global Mental Health contrast it with refugees who flee a single event: Bede families are almost always on the move, which makes them hard to reach for clinics, schools, and civil registers that assume a fixed address.
Inland migration
Today, many of these families are being forced to move away from their river roots and are settling on land.
Community members share that climate change has forced many to give up on the river as worsening floods, erosion, and storms make their former settlements uninhabitable. They also said some canals and channels are drying up, making life on the water impossible in some areas.
In terms of income, one sardar explained that families stay about a month in one place and leave when audiences stop coming. In Munshiganj, respondents told the Dhaka University team that demand for traditional work is falling, that stigma pushes people away from it, and that a recent ban on snake-catching has cost them income. About 88 percent said they did not want their children to follow the traditional trades.
Concerning work on land, in 2019, leaders of the Bede settlement in Savar, near Dhaka, one of the country’s largest, told a police officer that poverty and dying rivers meant families could no longer sail to other areas, and that interest in snake-charming and other old trades was fading.
To expand Bede people’s economic opportunities, the Uttaran Foundation, a local NGO, has trained about 200 young Bede women, who now work in garment factories. While both aforementioned studies are hyper-local and may not apply to all settlements, they reflect a tension between modern life, environmental realities, and traditions.
Services built for people who stay put
The Dhaka University study notes that many Bede families are landless and lack official citizenship documents, which limits their access to relief and disaster programs.
Part of the problem is simple logistics. In Bangladesh, official papers are tied to a fixed address, and many Bede families don’t have one. The Red Cross Red Crescent Magazine noted in 2023 that because the Bede usually live in temporary settlements and “don’t have permanent addresses,” getting the ID cards and other documents needed for basic services becomes impossible. The gap runs deeper than paperwork, though. Legal researcher Tamanna Tabassum Kabir wrote in the Indraprastha Law Review in 2020 that the Bede are not listed as an ethnic group in the national census, and that they “have not been officially recognized as citizens” even though they have lived in Bangladesh for centuries.
Kabir writes that Bede people could not enroll as voters until 2008. That mattered beyond the ballot box. According to a Canadian immigration board report, the government issued national ID cards using data collected for voter registration, so getting on the voter list was a way into other documents. The door hasn’t fully opened, though. In 2019, Philip Gain reported in The Daily Star, a local news outlet, that many Bede households own no land or house where they could be registered as voters.
A 2026 report by Bangladesh’s statistics bureau and the UN’s Economic and Social Commission for Asia and the Pacific (ESCAP) found that children from smaller ethnic communities, and from families that have recently moved, are among the least likely to have their births registered.
United Nations Children’s Fund (UNICEF) described what that looks like in Aftabnagar, in eastern Dhaka, during the 2023 Human Papillomavirus (HPV) vaccination campaign. The girls in the local Bede community had no birth certificates, so they could not be registered in the usual way. Kamrun Nahar, a vaccinator appointed by the Dhaka North City Corporation, spent many hours winning over the community leader and families, and visited at night, when everyone was home. The girls were eventually enlisted by hand. All 24 girls in the community received the vaccine in a single day, UNICEF reported in April 2024.
Some schools have tried to follow the families. An Ashoka profile of fellow A.K.M. Maksud describes six boat schools that traveled with Bede fleets near Dhaka, plus a fixed school in Aminbazar, run through his non-profit organization, Grambangla Unnayan Committee.
Adapting, not only enduring
The Cambridge study also documents how families manage the move. They negotiate with landowners and local youth before they settle, lean on a reputation built on earlier visits, and share food, money, and care within the group. Asked what would help improve their lives, participants named modest things: a small plot to live on, some help with work, medicine, and schools. The authors recommend mobile, community-based support designed with community leaders, not clinic-only models.
A 55-year-old Bede woman interviewed for the Munshiganj study said the younger generation no longer wants to live on boats and hopes education will help remove the stigma of being Bede.
Field observations from riverbank settlements in Savar, near Dhaka, highlight how these practical struggles play out. “Our ancestors lived and died on boats, but the rivers are no longer what they used to be,” observed Alamgir Sardar, a community leader in the area. “Without a permanent address on land, our children cannot get birth certificates or regular schooling. Moving to land is no longer a choice for us, as it is a matter of survival.”
For parents, the transition is also driven by hopes of breaking historical stigma. “I never went to school because we were always moving from one river ghāt to another,” shared Rahela Begum, a mother living in a temporary land settlement in Savar. “I want my children to study and live with dignity on land so they do not have to face the disrespect we experienced.”
Written by Masudul Zarif

Ogun State Governor, Dapo Abiodun, has suspended the Eselu of Iselu Kingdom in Yewa North Local Government Area, Oba Akintunde Akinyemi, with immediate effect over alleged partisan political activities.
The suspension was conveyed in a letter dated October 20, 2026, signed by the Commissioner for Local Government and Chieftaincy Affairs, Hon. Ganiyu Hamzat.
According to the letter, the suspension was approved by the State Executive Council pursuant to Section 52(1) of the Ogun State Obas and Chiefs Law, 2021, pending a detailed investigation into the allegations against the monarch.
The letter explained that the council acted following “several complaints concerning the traditional ruler’s conduct, particularly his alleged involvement in overtly partisan political activities, some of which were reportedly publicised by him.”
Mobile Policemen accused of gunning down herder in Plateau
Tinubu Lacks What to Campaign with in Bayelsa – NDC
The government noted that partisan politics was contrary to customary law and prohibited by statute, warning that such conduct could undermine the dignity of the traditional institution and threaten peaceful coexistence among subjects with different political affiliations.
It said the suspension was in the interest of peace, order and good governance in Ogun State, particularly in Iselu Kingdom, while the allegations were subjected to an official and detailed review.
As part of the conditions of the suspension, Oba Akinyemi has been directed to vacate the palace and refrain from entering it throughout the period of his suspension.
He has also been instructed not to present himself as, or claim recognition as, the Eselu of Iselu Kingdom.
The government further prohibited him from “wearing or using any crown, whether beaded or otherwise, ileke, beaded staff, irukere or other paraphernalia associated with the office of an Oba during the suspension.”
The letter also directed the monarch to make himself available promptly for any meeting or sitting convened by the state government to investigate the allegations against him.
Copies of the letter were sent to the Secretary of Yewa North Local Government and the Commissioner of Police, Ogun State Command, for their information and necessary action.

items.author: Daily Trust
items.content:
The Nigerian Guild of Editors (NGE) has called on relevant authorities to revisit the unresolved assassination of renowned journalist, Dele Giwa, insisting that the passage of 40 years must not extinguish the quest for justice.
Giwa, a co-founder of Newswatch magazine and one of Nigeria’s most influential journalists, was killed by a parcel bomb delivered to his home on October 19, 1986. Four decades after the incident, his killers have not been brought to justice.
In a statement on Monday by its President, Eze Anaba and General Secretary, Onuoha Ukeh, to mark 40 years anniversary of Giwa’s murder, the Guild described the unresolved murder as a painful test of Nigeria’s commitment to press freedom, public accountability and the rule of law.
The NGE said the country could not afford to allow the case to disappear into history.
“Forty years is a long time to wait for justice. It is an unconscionably long time for a nation that claims to uphold the rule of law,” it said.
The Guild urged the appropriate authorities to examine credible evidence that might still be available, preserve relevant records and pursue every lawful avenue towards establishing the truth about Giwa’s death.
The media professional body, however, cautioned against trial by media, stressing that it was not seeking the condemnation of anyone without evidence but demanding a credible investigation into a grave crime against a journalist and press freedom.
“We are not calling for trial by media. We are not asking anyone to be condemned without evidence. We are demanding that a grave crime against a Nigerian citizen, a distinguished journalist and the freedom of the press should not remain an enduring symbol of impunity,” the Guild said.
The NGE described Giwa as a journalist of uncommon audacity, intellectual rigour and literary elegance, whose work demonstrated that Nigerian journalism could be fearless in interrogating power while maintaining high standards of professional excellence.
According to the Guild, Giwa understood that journalism was neither a public relations department for those in authority nor an instrument for flattering the powerful, but a public trust.
It said the late journalist’s assassination was not merely the killing of an individual but an attack on the freedom to ask questions, expose wrongdoing and hold those in authority accountable.
The NGE also expressed concern about the implications of the unresolved murder for journalists investigating corruption, probing abuses of power or exposing the activities of influential interests.
It said the failure to bring the perpetrators to justice sent a troubling message to media practitioners and underscored the need for stronger protection of journalists and effective investigations whenever crimes were committed against them.
The NGE commended NEWSWATCH Plus Limited and its head, Ray Ekpu, the only surviving member of the original Newswatch quartet, for preserving Giwa’s legacy through the publication.
It said the publication would ensure that Giwa’s voice and contribution to journalism continued to inspire generations of media practitioners.
Beyond remembering Giwa, the Guild challenged contemporary journalists and editors to reflect on the state of the profession, particularly its independence from political and commercial interests.
The NGE said the quest for justice for Giwa demanded more than provocative headlines or dramatic public appearances, but requires verification, courage, independence, fairness and a commitment to truth.
“Courage without accuracy can become recklessness; independence without ethics can become irresponsibility,” the Guild said, adding that journalism worth defending must be both fearless and scrupulous, independent and accountable.
The NGE urged editors to protect newsroom integrity, publishers to resist intimidation and journalists to uphold professional discipline, especially amid growing disinformation, political propaganda, economic pressures and the weaponisation of social media.
It also called on public authorities to tolerate scrutiny and security agencies to protect media practitioners from threats and attacks, stressing that press freedom required more than constitutional guarantees, insisting that it must be supported by responsible journalism, independent media institutions and the effective enforcement of laws.
The Guild further warned against reducing Giwa’s memory to annual commemorations without concrete efforts to address the circumstances of his death.
“Remembrance without action risks becoming an elaborate way of accommodating injustice,” the Guild said.
The elite media group called for Giwa’s professional ideals to be taught in journalism schools, discussed in newsrooms and preserved in the national historical record, while urging younger journalists to appreciate the sacrifices made by earlier generations in defending press freedom.
It said the defence of press freedom was not the exclusive responsibility of journalists but a public cause, because attacks on journalists also threatened citizens’ right to reliable information.
The Guild urged successive governments to recognise that the responsibility to investigate serious crimes did not expire with the passage of time or changes in political leadership.
It said Giwa’s legacy should serve both as a monument to professional courage and a reminder that crimes against journalists must not become permanent symbols of impunity.
According to the Guild, “a parcel bomb may have ended Dele Giwa’s life, but it could not extinguish the ideals he represented.
“Dele Giwa is gone, but the questions his murder left behind remain alive. The man was silenced; the search for justice must not be.”

The federal government aims to collect around Rs. 188.58 billion through the new Automotive Development Levy on locally assembled or manufactured vehicles over five years, according to revenue projections in the draft auto policy approved by Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif.
The estimates put projected collections at Rs. 37.71 billion in 2026-27, rising to Rs. 38.46 billion in 2027-28, ProPakistani has learnt.
The government expects collections of Rs. 38.29 billion in 2028-29, followed by Rs. 37.30 billion in 2029-30 and Rs. 36.83 billion in 2030-31.
The five-year total comes to Rs. 188.58 billion.
The draft policy sets different levy rates according to vehicle type and engine capacity.
Cars below 1,000cc would carry a zero rate, while vehicles between 1,001cc and 2,000cc would face a 2 percent levy.
Cars above 2,000cc would carry a proposed rate of 10 percent.
The rates would also cover imported and locally assembled or manufactured internal combustion engine vehicles.
Two- and three-wheelers and agricultural tractors would be exempt, while trucks and light commercial vehicles, buses and vans, and specified prime movers would carry a 2 percent rate.
The government expects collections from the locally assembled or manufactured vehicle category to remain relatively stable throughout the five-year period, ranging from Rs. 36.83 billion to Rs. 38.46 billion annually.
The policy document also provides separate estimates for levy collections on imported vehicles.
The final revenue impact would depend on the policy’s implementation, the applicable calculation mechanism and the volume and mix of vehicles sold or imported during the 5-year period.

items.summary:

items.author: Arooj Fatima
items.content:
New Zealand’s Employment Court has ruled that charging workers money to secure jobs in the country is illegal, even if the payments are made overseas.
The ruling clarifies the Wages Protection Act 1983, which prohibits charging workers for employment. Previously, there was uncertainty over whether the law covered payments made outside New Zealand.
According to Immigration New Zealand (INZ), the ban also applies when payments are made by family members, friends, or agents on behalf of prospective employees. It also covers payments received by agents or other individuals representing employers.
INZ National Manager Risk and Verification Aaron Smith said the decision establishes an important legal precedent to help tackle migrant exploitation.
He noted that migrant workers are often charged large sums of money in exchange for promises of employment and residency. The ruling makes it clear that charging for a job in New Zealand is illegal, regardless of where the payment is made, the amount involved, or who receives it.
Smith urged anyone who has been misled or pressured into paying for job offers or visa support to report the matter.
While INZ cannot recover money lost through job scams, it can take action against New Zealand employers and their representatives involved in charging migrants for employment.
The agency also advised employers and recruitment agents to ensure transparent hiring practices and comply with employment laws, including when working with overseas recruiters and third parties.
Smith warned that employers and agents involved in exploiting migrant workers for financial gain, including through fake job offers, would face consequences.

The couple had contested repairs linked to Hurricane Ian's 2022 storm damage. The court concluded that Citizens had fulfilled its duties, even while the homeowners pursued legal action during the appraisal phase, indicating that Citizens acted in good faith throughout the claim.

items.summary:

items.author: Arooj Fatima
items.content:
A new oral treatment for hair loss has shown promising results in a late-stage clinical trial, significantly improving hair growth in men after six months.
US drugmaker Veradermics announced that its experimental pill, VDPHL01, performed better than a placebo in a study involving more than 500 men with mild to moderate male pattern hair loss.
The company said the trial met all its primary and secondary goals, with consistent improvements in hair growth among participants. The treatment was also generally well tolerated, with no serious drug-related side effects reported.
VDPHL01 contains a specially formulated version of minoxidil that releases the medication slowly over time. Minoxidil is already widely used as a topical treatment applied directly to the scalp for hair loss in both men and women.
Although cheaper generic oral versions of minoxidil are available, Cantor Fitzgerald analyst Prakhar Agrawal said the positive trial results have strengthened the commercial potential of Veradermics’ treatment.
The company identified Nutrafol, a hair growth supplement backed by Unilever, as a possible pricing benchmark for its pill. Nutrafol costs around $90 per month, or approximately $1,000 annually.
The company plans to announce additional results from another part of the study later this year.
Other pharmaceutical companies, including Pelage Pharmaceuticals and Cosmo Pharmaceuticals, are also developing new treatments for hair loss.

The main suspect arrested in connection with the suicide case of student Laiba Ejaz died after being wounded during an armed attack on an Islamabad Police team in the jurisdiction of Ramna Police Station, according to a police spokesperson.
The deceased suspect was identified as Muhammad Nauman.
Islamabad Police said officers were taking Nauman for a recovery operation based on information and identification provided by him during the investigation.

Police said the attackers intended to free Nauman from custody.
During the firing, Nauman was struck by bullets allegedly fired by his own associates and sustained injuries. The police team remained unharmed because officers were wearing bulletproof jackets and had taken other safety precautions.
Police immediately shifted the injured suspect to a hospital for medical treatment. However, Nauman later succumbed to his injuries.
According to Islamabad Police, Nauman was an accused in the case involving Laiba Ejaz, a student who died by suicide within the jurisdiction of Ramna Police Station.
Police have launched search operations to trace and arrest the other suspects allegedly involved in the attack. Authorities said further investigation into the incident is underway.

items.title: Govt Rejects 18% IMF Tax on EVs
items.summary:

items.author: Afaq Wajdan Malik
items.content:
Meta has revised upcoming terms for business accounts after publishers and other businesses raised concerns that the company could use them to broadly scrape websites connected to Facebook and Instagram accounts.
As reported by Engadget, Meta removed an explicit reference to AI training from the updated commercial terms. However, the revised language still gives the company permission to use automated tools to access and collect content from websites associated with business accounts.
The terms are scheduled to take effect on October 30.
Original Terms Included AI Training
Nieman Lab first highlighted the changes after Meta added language allowing it to use web scrapers, bots, spiders, crawlers, and other automated software to access, index, cache, analyze, collect, and retrieve content from websites linked to business accounts.
The original wording said Meta could use that material to “provide, develop, improve, research, train, and maintain the integrity” of its products and services.
That raised concerns because most major digital publishers maintain business accounts on Facebook or Instagram, potentially bringing their websites under the terms.
Meta Removes the Word “Train”
Meta later quietly revised the terms again.
The company removed the word “train” and narrowed the stated purpose of scraping to supporting, developing, improving, researching, and maintaining its advertising and business products.
The updated terms still authorize Meta and entities acting on its behalf to use automated software to crawl domains, web pages and URLs associated with businesses and periodically pull updates from them.
Meta spokesperson Andy Stone said the company had clarified the language to show that the changes apply only to its advertising and business products.
He also said the update was “not about scraping news sites” and that Meta was not changing how it currently uses web crawlers.
Legal Experts Still See Broader Scraping Rights
Despite the revision, Nieman Lab reported that the new language still represents a significant expansion of Meta’s scraping permissions.
Several legal experts told the publication that the revised terms appear to give Meta broad permission to scrape news websites with relatively few restrictions.
Stone said the changes do not give Meta new rights to override website owners’ robots.txt preferences.
However, robots.txt instructions are not legally binding, and AI companies have previously been accused of ignoring or working around them.
Publishers Push Back
The dispute comes amid Meta’s strained relationship with news publishers.
The company stopped paying publishers for news in 2022 and removed its dedicated news tab in 2024. More recently, Meta has signed agreements with several publishers to supply news content to its AI chatbot.
Media industry groups have strongly criticized the new terms.
Danielle Coffey, CEO of the News/Media Alliance, called the rules “outrageous and probably illegal.”
Theo Bamber, head of the UK’s News Media Association, described the changes as a “shameless landgrab attempt.”
Meta maintains that the revised terms concern only its advertising and business products, but publishers continue to question how broadly the company will be able to scrape content from websites connected to Meta business accounts.

items.title: CDA to Seize Ancient Land on Murree Road
items.summary:
The Capital Development Authority (CDA) has completed the demarcation of government land in Mouza Malpur, Islamabad, ahead of a planned operation against illegal encroachments.
The exercise identified the boundaries separating state-owned land from privately owned properties to establish which structures fall within government land.
Malpur (also known as Malpur Rajgan or Phulwari) is one of the oldest historic villages in Islamabad, located off Murree Road near Rawal Lake.
The demarcation findings will help CDA and district administration identify illegal occupation and determine the areas where enforcement action may be required.
Authorities are preparing for the anti-encroachment operation, with action expected against unauthorised occupants in accordance with the law.
