items.author: Shahbaz Rana
items.content:
As Pakistan's tax system becomes more unfair during the first two years of the International Monetary Fund (IMF) programme, the Fund's Regional Director, Jihad Azour, on Tuesday emphasised a fairer and more neutral tax system for improving compliance and business expansion.
The opening speech by Azour during the first day of a two-day conference on the tax system appeared divorced from ground realities, where the salaried class has been squeezed but the retailers, agriculture and real estate sectors largely remained untaxed.
"A fairer tax system can encourage compliance, better services can strengthen trust, and a more neutral tax structure can allow productive firms to expand rather than remain small or informal," Azour said while delivering the opening speech.
He further said that broadening the tax base, strengthening revenue administration, reducing tax expenditures, protecting priority spending and improving public service provision are Pakistan's priorities.
However, during the first two years of the IMF programme, tax contributions by influential sectors such as retailers, agriculture and real estate remained negligible, and IMF management agreed to reduce withholding tax rates for the real estate sector this June. The IMF also endorsed a tax scheme for traders that allowed them to deal in cash and would promote informality in the economy.
Yet retailers remained outside the tax net, and as of October 15 only 137 new retailers joined the scheme against the annual target of one million. According to the Federal Board of Revenue's (FBR) data, income tax collection from the real estate sector dived 38% to a mere Rs35.2 billion in the first three months of the current fiscal year. It was Rs22 billion less than the comparative period of the last fiscal year after the government cut income tax for the realty sector by 50%, which the IMF also endorsed.
In fiscal year 2024, the realty sector had paid Rs200 billion in income taxes, which hardly increased to Rs236 billion in the last fiscal year, but it may now dip even below Rs150 billion after rate cuts.
Punjab and Sindh cumulatively collected Rs5.1 billion in agriculture income tax as of June this year under the new regime introduced as part of the IMF programme. According to details shared with the IMF, in the last fiscal year, the agriculture income tax target was Rs2 billion but the Sindh government collected only Rs1.1 billion. The Punjab government's budget books showed that against the last fiscal year's target of Rs10.5 billion, the collection was only Rs4 billion.
Compared with this, before the start of the IMF programme, the annual contribution of the salaried class was Rs391 billion, which within two fiscal years of the IMF programme increased to Rs629 billion as of June 2026.
In his speech, Azour stated that the tax workshop comes at a critical moment in Pakistan's reform journey. Despite an era of shocks and uncertainty, Pakistan has made important progress toward restoring macroeconomic stability, rebuilding confidence, strengthening external buffers and supporting gradual recovery, he added. The workshop was taking place in the middle of a discussion at the highest level of government on whether the current FBR can deliver. The prime minister has shelved a plan to abolish the FBR, but the discussion reinforced the failure to bring tax broadening reforms.
The regional director stated that the next milestone is to turn this stabilisation into stronger and more durable growth.
"Moving beyond the cycles of adjustment toward a more competitive, investment-friendly and inclusive economy is the ambitious set of reforms that was set clearly by the government and supported by the IMF through the Extended Fund Facility (EFF)," he added.
Azour said Pakistan's exposure to higher energy and food prices, disruption to trade and supply chains, weaker external demand and an abrupt tightening in global financing conditions heightens the premium on preserving stability while supporting the recovery.
In this context, he added, fiscal policy must do more than achieving the primary balance targets and protecting that sustainability.
Planning Minister Ahsan Iqbal has recently questioned Pakistan's economic stabilisation, terming it "stunted and borrowed". In his letter to the prime minister, Iqbal stated that the focus of the economic stabilisation was on fiscal numbers. Azour said Pakistan must reinforce policy credibility, foster the recovery and create space for the public investment and social spending needed to support stronger long-term growth and the well-being of the Pakistani people.
He said tax reform was critical to Pakistan's economic growth agenda and was at the centre of the EFF objectives. A stronger, broader, fairer and more predictable tax system can support fiscal sustainability while reducing distortions that hold back investment, productivity growth and formal job creation, said the regional director. The director said Pakistan's stabilisation gains have been hard won. Credibility now depends on continuing to meet fiscal and external objectives and enhancing resilience, while demonstrating that reforms are sustained and institutionally anchored, he added.
A medium-term tax strategy can serve this purpose if it sets clear objectives, well-designed policies, ambitious sequencing and transparent implementation responsibilities, according to the regional director.
The EFF-supported programme recognises that stabilisation is necessary, but not sufficient. Pakistan needs reforms that raise productivity, improve competitiveness and unlock private investment, he added.
"When the tax system is simpler, more neutral and predictable, it lowers the cost of formality, improves resource allocations and gives businesses greater confidence to invest and grow," according to Azour.
He emphasised that fairness is central to reform's success. Taxpayers are more likely to comply when rules are transparent and when the system does not reward informality or provide preferential treatment, according to the regional director.
But contrary to this concept, Pakistan's tax system has become more unfair, and the government launched an easy tax scheme for traders that promotes informality by allowing them to deal in cash. The scheme has also been endorsed by the IMF.
Azour said many countries have strong reform ideas, but fewer translate them into durable results. Implementation requires ownership, coordination, engagement and communication. Ownership across institutions, coordination between the federal government and provinces, engagement with the private sector and civil society, and a careful communication strategy so that citizens and businesses can understand and trust, he added.

items.author: Our Correspondent
items.content:
Pakistan Stock Exchange (PSX) closed lower on Tuesday after a topsy-turvy session with the benchmark KSE-100 index swinging between gains and losses before extensive selling dragged it down by 814 points.
In the morning, trading opened in positive territory as investors bought stocks of automobile assemblers, cement firms, commercial banks, oil and gas exploration companies and oil marketing companies. However, sentiment remained fragile as repeated swings failed to establish a sustained upward move. The index was marginally higher at midday, but selling pressure subsequently intensified, pulling it close to the session's low by the close.
The bourse touched the intra-day high of 166,425.56 and low of 165,111.14 and eventually settled at 165,151.64 points, down 0.49%. Internationally, oil prices advanced, with Brent crude hovering around a five-month high as traders priced in a geopolitical risk premium following Houthi attacks on Saudi infrastructure and reports of vessel attacks in the Gulf. The developments kept geopolitical risks in focus amid concerns over potential disruptions to regional energy supplies.
KTrade Securities wrote in its market wrap that the KSE-100 index dropped 814.44 points (-0.5%) amid cautious investor sentiment and subdued trading volumes of 144 million shares. Weakness was broad-based, led by commercial banks, technology, refinery and power sectors, where Attock Refinery, Systems Ltd, Habib Bank, Hub Power and Fauji Fertiliser were the largest drags.
Meanwhile, Brent crude remained elevated at $109 per barrel, reinforcing macroeconomic uncertainty and weighing on risk appetite. "We expect the market to remain range bound, with near-term direction contingent on global oil prices, geopolitical developments and corporate earnings. A sustained recovery in trading volumes remains critical to supporting a durable market recovery," KTrade said.
Arif Habib Limited Deputy Head of Trading Ali Najib commented that the PSX witnessed a negative trading session, where the benchmark KSE-100 index declined 814 points (-0.49%) to close at 165,152. The market opened on a positive note, reaching the intra-day high of 166,426 (+460 points), before reversing course and touching the low of 165,111. Rising oil prices weighed on investor sentiment, prompting cautious trading and driving the index lower.
Among corporate results, Pakistan Oilfields reported earnings of Rs8.2 billion (EPS: Rs28.86), up 51% year-on-year, while Attock Petroleum's earnings increased 74% YoY to Rs6.64 billion (EPS: Rs53.36), supported by higher petroleum prices, inventory gains and improved other income. Attock Refinery posted a sharp 13x YoY increase in net profit to Rs18.6 billion.
"Going forward, the market may remain volatile amid rising oil prices and cautious sentiment. Selective buying could support recovery, while investors should prioritise fundamentally strong stocks and monitor geopolitical developments," Najib said.
Cumulatively, trading volumes increased to 446.8 million shares versus 370.9 million a day ago. The value of traded shares stood at Rs19.4 million. Of the 499 companies traded, 128 rose, 324 declined and 47 remained unchanged.
Cnergyico Pk was the volume leader with trading in 46.5 million shares, falling Rs0.47 to close at Rs12.41. Foreign investors bought shares worth Rs206 million, the National Clearing Company reported.

items.author: Our Correspondent
items.content:
Federal Minister for National Food Security and Research Rana Tanveer Hussain on Tuesday directed authorities to strengthen market surveillance and warned that artificial shortages, hoarding and unjustified price increases would not be tolerated, as he chaired a meeting of the Fertiliser Review Committee to assess availability, market prices, distribution and supply requirements for the ongoing Rabi cropping season.
The meeting reviewed the prevailing stock position, domestic production, supply chain arrangements and anticipated fertiliser demand during the wheat sowing season, according to a press release issued by the Ministry of National Food Security and Research. Ministry officials and fertiliser industry stakeholders attended.
Hussain expressed satisfaction over the overall fertiliser supply situation and reaffirmed the government's commitment to maintaining sufficient stocks, particularly urea and diammonium phosphate (DAP), to meet farmers' requirements throughout the Rabi season. Officials briefed the meeting on measures to maintain a balanced supply across the country and ensure smooth movement of fertilisers to agricultural markets.
The minister directed close coordination with relevant departments and fertiliser manufacturers to prevent supply disruptions. He observed that fluctuations in international fertiliser markets and global economic uncertainties continue to pose challenges to agricultural input costs, but said the government remained focused on protecting farmers from unnecessary financial pressures.

items.content:
Gold prices in Pakistan fell Rs3,600 per tola to Rs435,436 on Tuesday, while 10-gram gold dropped Rs3,086 to Rs373,316, according to the All-Pakistan Gems and Jewellers Sarafa Association, as international bullion remained range bound amid uncertainty over the US rate outlook.
Silver prices remained unchanged at Rs6,234 per tola. In the international market, spot gold was largely steady at $4,138.54 per ounce by 1519 GMT, while US gold futures for December delivery declined 0.1% to $4,157.90 per ounce. Investors remained cautious ahead of next week's Federal Reserve meeting and the release of personal consumption expenditures (PCE) inflation data, which could provide fresh direction about monetary policy. "Inflation and the Fed rates are the big stories that gold is fighting at the moment," said Bob Haberkorn, Senior Market Strategist at StoneX.
Adnan Agar, Director at Interactive Commodities, said international gold had touched the intra-day high of $4,155 per ounce and low of $4,111. Later, it was trading around $4,127. He said the market was moving within a tight range, with resistance on the upside and support limiting the advance and decline, making a breakout likely over the coming days.
According to Agar, gold's broader trading range was from $4,060 to $4,220 per ounce. A sustained decline below $4,000 could push prices towards $3,700-$3,800, while a breakout above the $4,250-$4,280 zone could open the way towards $4,400 and potentially $4,600. He said the market's next move would depend on whether inflation data and Federal Reserve signals strengthened demand for gold or made interest-bearing assets more attractive. Meanwhile, the Pakistani rupee closed at 276.87 against the US dollar, gaining Rs0.03 from Monday's close at 276.90.

items.title: Desi Bela Bajaria leaves Netflix after giving global blockbusters
items.summary: Bela Bajaria has stepped down from her role as chief content officer at Netflix amid significant challenges in the media landscape. She oversaw an impressive annual budget of almost $20 billion while bolstering Netflix's international content strategy. With a decline in audience engagement highlighting the industry's evolution, the streaming giant is poised for a transformative approach. Peter Rice, formerly of Disney and Fox, is set to take the helm.

items.author: Onsa Mustafa
items.content:
Copyright protected content copied from PhoneWorld website.
Senator Syed Waqar Mehdi has raised concerns over the National Cyber Crime Investigation Agency’s (NCCIA) failure to resolve an online fraud case in Karachi, despite a complaint being pending for the past year.
Speaking during a Senate session, Mehdi said an unidentified person in Karachi was using his photograph as a display picture on a mobile phone and contacting people to demand money in his name.
He explained that the individual had been calling people and using his identity to seek money, creating the risk of fraud and damaging his reputation.
Senator Waqar Mehdi Raises Online Fraud Case Against NCCIA in Senate
The senator said he had submitted a complaint to the NCCIA around a year ago, but the agency had yet to resolve the matter. He criticised the agency’s Karachi office, describing the officials responsible for handling the case as highly incompetent.
Mehdi also complained that the additional director in Karachi had repeatedly delayed the matter by asking him to wait for another day. He said he had informed the NCCIA about the fraudulent activity, but his complaint had not produced any meaningful results.
The senator further claimed that he had tried to contact the newly appointed NCCIA director general but had been unable to reach him, as the official was not answering his calls.
Mehdi said he had also discussed the issue with Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi in an effort to secure action against the impersonator.
Responding to the matter, Minister of State for Interior Talal Chaudhry assured the senator that they will resolve the issue within two to three days.
Senator Raza Rabbani? [Correction: Rana Sanaullah] also intervened during the session, asking Mehdi to accompany him that very day so they could contact the NCCIA director general and push for a resolution.
See Also: Pakistan Government Working on Smartphone Installment Scheme, IT Minister Confirms
“Senator Waqar Mehdi, please come with me today,” Rana Sanaullah said, offering to call the NCCIA director general and help resolve the case.
The matter has highlighted concerns about delays in addressing cybercrime complaints, particularly cases involving identity theft and financial fraud. Such incidents can expose unsuspecting citizens to financial losses while damaging the reputation of individuals whose identities are misused.
The senator’s complaint has renewed attention to the need for timely investigations and effective responses from cybercrime authorities. The NCCIA’s response to the allegations and the outcome of the promised action were not provided in the information shared.

items.summary:
Information Minister Attaullah Tarar said on Tuesday that a ban on the Pakistan Tehreek-i-Insaf (PTI) might no longer be necessary following the imposition of governor’s rule in Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa, adding that the party had already lost its government in the province due to its alleged support for terrorism.

Speaking on a private television program
items.author: Web Desk
items.content:
Information Minister Attaullah Tarar said on Tuesday that a ban on the Pakistan Tehreek-i-Insaf (PTI) might no longer be necessary following the imposition of governor’s rule in Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa, adding that the party had already lost its government in the province due to its alleged support for terrorism.
The emergency and governor’s rule were declared on October 11 after negotiations between the government and opposition failed, culminating in a PTI long march towards Islamabad that began on October 4. Last week, a joint session of parliament adopted two separate resolutions ratifying the presidential proclamations imposing a state of emergency and governor’s rule in K-P for two months, amid protests from the opposition. Before that, both houses of parliament had separately approved the emergency in the province by majority vote under Clause 1 of Article 232 of the Constitution, despite objections from opposition lawmakers.
Speaking on a private television programme, Capital Talk, the minister said non-functional K-P Chief Minister Sohail Afridi was in protective custody. He added that an advisory council would decide whether Afridi should be arrested or whether a case should be registered against him.
Defending the decision to place Afridi in protective custody, Tarar said it was a natural step after the imposition of an emergency to take key figures into protective custody to prevent potential sabotage or threats to law and order.
Read: PHC seeks Centre’s response over imposition of emergency, governor’s rule in K-P
Criticising the PTI government’s performance in the province, he alleged that it had failed to deliver development projects and improve infrastructure.
“There is no infrastructure in Kohat. The Kohat Tunnel and motorway were built during the PML-N government, and no work has been done there since,” he said, adding that no development had taken place across the province.
“Peace is the fundamental requirement for all these things to happen. They have not even taken a stand for peace. In their view, the TTP are very good people, whom they do not want to condemn,” Tarar said.
Talking about the negotiations with the opposition, the minister said members of the PTI delegation involved in negotiations had been disappointed after Afridi rejected the terms of an agreement reached with the government while blaming the former chief minister and his associates for the collapse of the talks.
Reiterating his earlier position on banning the PTI, Tarar said a principled decision had already been taken, while a final decision would follow the completion of legal preparations. However, he said a ban might no longer be required.
“I believe there may no longer be a need for it because the PTI, as a party, is already absent from parliament. As a result of violations, it did not have an electoral symbol, and its members are not present in the House,” he said.
Lashing out at the PTI over what he described as its alleged support for the banned Tehreek-e-Taliban Pakistan (TTP) and other militant groups, Tarar said the party had governed the province for more than 13 years.
The minister said that terrorism had been brought under control after 2017 through the complete implementation of the National Action Plan, but alleged that the PTI government had subsequently facilitated the return of militants.
Also Read: Tariq Fazal rubbishes linking governor's rule in K-P to mineral extraction
He said the party had lost its provincial government as a consequence of its alleged facilitation of terrorism, adding that there was little point in pursuing a ban under the circumstances.
The minister also praised Jamiat Ulema-e-Islam-Fazl (JUI-F) chief Maulana Fazlur Rehman for his role in the negotiations but urged him not to politicise the issue of terrorism.
“Maulana Sahib is an experienced and astute politician. I believe it does not suit him to bring politics into the security of the province,” Tarar said, adding that the elimination of terrorism was an unequivocal objective that had to be achieved at all costs.
Acknowledging JUI-F’s sacrifices and efforts in the fight against terrorism, the minister said all political parties should unite against the menace.
“This is the time for everyone to stand together against terrorism, but terrorism and politics must be kept separate because this is a matter of the safety and security of the people,” he said.

items.title: Brent falls as Iran's president discusses mediation with CDF Munir
items.summary:
Oil prices settled down ​after touching a five-month high on Tuesday as traders weighed a meeting between the Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian and Chief of Defence Forces (CDF) and Chief of Army Staff Field Marshal Asim Munir, a key US-Iran mediator, against continued Houthi attacks on Saudi infrastructure and reports of vessel attacks in the Gulf.
Brent crude futures settled down 76 cents, or 0.69%, at $108.79. Earlier in the session, the front-month contract reached $111.99, a five-month high.
The November contract for US West Texas Intermediate crude, which expired on Tuesday, settled ​down $1.87, or 1.8%, at $101.79. That was down from the session high of $110.48, the highest since April for a nearby contract. ​The more active December contract settled down 72 cents at $97.82 a barrel.
Iran's President Pezeshkian discussed mediation efforts ⁠and regional developments during a meeting with Field Marshal Munir in Tehran, Iran's Nournews reported on Tuesday.
Read: CD
items.author: Reuters
items.content:
Oil prices settled down ​after touching a five-month high on Tuesday as traders weighed a meeting between the Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian and Chief of Defence Forces (CDF) and Chief of Army Staff Field Marshal Asim Munir, a key US-Iran mediator, against continued Houthi attacks on Saudi infrastructure and reports of vessel attacks in the Gulf.
Brent crude futures settled down 76 cents, or 0.69%, at $108.79. Earlier in the session, the front-month contract reached $111.99, a five-month high.
The November contract for US West Texas Intermediate crude, which expired on Tuesday, settled ​down $1.87, or 1.8%, at $101.79. That was down from the session high of $110.48, the highest since April for a nearby contract. ​The more active December contract settled down 72 cents at $97.82 a barrel.
Iran's President Pezeshkian discussed mediation efforts ⁠and regional developments during a meeting with Field Marshal Munir in Tehran, Iran's Nournews reported on Tuesday.
Read: CDF Munir meets senior Iranian officials as Pakistan continues diplomatic push to end conflict
Pakistan's mediation efforts ​resulted in an interim peace agreement signed in June. But that deal quickly faltered amid new fighting between Iran and the US weeks ​later.
The talks in Tehran are against the backdrop of continued attacks by Yemen's Iran-aligned Houthis, who said on Monday they launched several attacks on Saudi energy, airport and military targets, such as an Aramco site in Yanbu, the Shaybah oilfield, Riyadh's King Khalid International Airport and Abha airport.
Saudi authorities did not immediately confirm the ​Houthi claims, and Reuters could not independently verify them.
"Oil prices remain well-supported... This suggests the market is pricing in a significant risk ​premium, given the situation's volatility," ING analysts said in a note on Tuesday.
At least 18 vessels were reportedly attacked over two weeks, which keeps the risk ‌premium ⁠intact, shiptracker Kpler said in a note on Monday.
Also on Monday, a Houthi attack on a training camp for government security forces in Yemen's Shabwa province killed 58 people and injured more than 200.
Read More: Death toll from Houthi attack on Yemen training camp rises to 73
The renewed attacks heightened fears about regional stability and underscored continuing risks to energy supply from the region, keeping oil prices above $100 a barrel.
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said in a statement he is "committed to completing the elimination of ​the Iranian regime," and spoke with ​US President Donald Trump about it ⁠on Sunday.
Diesel supply
Russian diesel cargoes are returning to their traditional destinations after the US suspended sanctions and secured the lifting of an export ban, with at least two tankers signalling trips to Turkey and Brazil ​in recent days, according to shipping data from Kpler and LSEG.
The US is working with domestic refiners to ​squeeze more crude ⁠through its refining complex, US Energy Under Secretary Kyle Haustveit said on Tuesday at the Drake Forum in Titusville, Pennsylvania, a sentiment echoed by US Energy Secretary Chris Wright later on Tuesday in Houston.
The US is also pushing shuttered domestic refineries to reopen, Wright added.
US crude oil stockpiles ⁠were expected ​to have fallen last week along with product inventories, an extended Reuters poll showed ​on Tuesday. Eight analysts polled by Reuters estimated, on average, that crude inventories fell by about 800,000 barrels in the week ended October 16.

items.author: Anadolu Agency
items.content:
North Korean leader Kim Jong Un appeared in photos released by state media on Tuesday after rumours circulated on social media claiming he had died of a brain haemorrhage.
Kim visited a consumer goods exhibition featuring clothing and footwear on Monday, according to the state-run Korean Central News Agency (KCNA).
The report was accompanied by photos showing Kim touring the exhibition alongside his daughter, Ju Ae, and party and government officials.
Earlier on Sunday, Xie Wanjun, who identifies himself as chairman of the China Democracy Party, a group banned by China, claimed in a social media post that Kim had suffered a "severe cerebral haemorrhage and fallen into a coma" before being transferred to Peking Union Medical College Hospital for emergency treatment due to "the poor medical conditions in North Korea."
Read: What would happen to North Korea if Kim Jong Un died
Xie, who lives in the US, further claimed that Kim had died from the severity of his condition and a delay in receiving optimal treatment, adding that his body had been secretly transported back to North Korea and that authorities were concealing news of his death.
North Korean state media regularly publishes photos of Kim and reports on his activities.
Rumours about Kim's death have circulated before, as North Korea's limited access to information makes it difficult to independently verify reports about the country's leadership.
The North Korean leader, who is believed to be 42, is also believed to have health problems, although his medical condition has not been publicly confirmed.

items.title: New AI tool can predict cancer survival chances from selfie: study
items.summary:
US researchers have developed an artificial intelligence (AI) tool that can predict cancer patients' survival chances from a single facial photograph, according to a study published on Monday in the journal The Lancet Digital Health.

items.author: Anadolu Agency
items.content:
US researchers have developed an artificial intelligence (AI) tool that can predict cancer patients' survival chances from a single facial photograph, according to a study published on Monday in the journal The Lancet Digital Health.
Developed by researchers at Mass General Brigham in the US state of Massachusetts, the system, called FAHR-Face, analyses facial features to estimate biological age and mortality risk, potentially helping doctors make treatment decisions.
The model was trained on more than 40 million facial photos and adapted into two tools: FAHR-FaceAge, which estimates biological age, and FAHR-FaceSurvival, which predicts cancer patients' survival directly from facial images without relying on age estimates.
Read: Alibaba open-sources AI model detecting cancer, 150 medical conditions
Researchers found that the survival model focused mainly on areas beneath the eyes and around the nose, while the age-estimation model examined facial features around the mouth and temples, suggesting the two systems identify different health-related patterns.
The survival model was trained on images of 34,363 patients and tested on another 3,820, with results independently validated using data from 4,892 cancer patients in the Netherlands.
Researchers found that patients classified in the highest-risk group had more than three times the mortality risk of those in the lowest-risk group, even after accounting for clinical factors.
Read More: Scientists train AI model to predict future illnesses
Patients whose faces appeared at least five years older than their actual age also had a 21% higher mortality risk, while those appearing at least five years younger had a 17% lower risk.
Combining the two models further improved the accuracy of survival predictions, according to the study.
Researchers said the technology could help doctors assess patients' health and guide treatment decisions, although further validation is needed before it can be widely used in clinical practice.

Sam Altman became a ‌face ⁠of the artificial intelligence boom after the chatbot ChatGPT was released in 2022.
Annie Altman filed her lawsuit in St Louis, Missouri, federal court in January 2025.
She accused her brother of sexually abusing and raping her ​between 1997 and ​2006 at ⁠the family home in suburban Clayton, Missouri, starting when she was 3 and he was 12. She ​said the last acts of sexual abuse and rape ​occurred when ⁠Sam Altman was an adult. He is now 41.
The Altman family has said Annie Altman has mental health challenges and received financial support. Sam ⁠Altman has ​said she began accusing him on social ​media of sexual abuse after the family rejected her demands for more funds.

items.author: Naeem Asghar
items.content:
The primary suspect in the case involving the suicide of former International Islamic University Islamabad (IIUI) student Laiba Ejaz died after being wounded by gunfire from his own accomplices during an exchange of fire with police in Islamabad.
According to a police spokesperson, the suspect, identified as Muhammad Nauman, was in custody and was being taken to a location for recovery on the basis of information provided by him when the incident occurred.
The spokesperson said four of Nauman’s accomplices, travelling on two motorcycles, had been lying in wait along the route. They opened indiscriminate fire on the police team in an attempt to secure his release.
Read: Islamabad student found dead after allegedly losing Rs7m in education scam
Nauman was wounded by gunfire from his own accomplices, the spokesperson said, adding that police personnel remained unharmed due to their bulletproof jackets and other precautionary measures.
The injured suspect was taken to a hospital for medical treatment but later succumbed to his injuries, the spokesperson confirmed.
Search operations were under way to arrest the remaining suspects, according to the police.
Laiba, who had aspired to study at a top US university, was found hanging from a tree near a road in Islamabad on October 9, after her family allegedly lost around Rs7 million to a consultant who had promised to secure her admission and a scholarship.
Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif also took notice of the incident and directed the inspector general of Islamabad police and the chief commissioner to take immediate action against the suspect. Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi also vowed to look into the case personally.
The FIA’s Anti-Human Trafficking Circle in Islamabad registered a case against Nauman and Fatima Sarwar under Sections 419 (cheating), 420 (cheating and dishonestly inducing delivery of property) and 109 (abetment) of the Pakistan Penal Code, read with Sections 18 and 22 of the Emigration Ordinance, 1979.
Preliminary investigations revealed that the suspects allegedly acted in connivance to deceive Laiba with promises of a US visa and scholarship. They allegedly received a total of Rs9.3 million from the family.
The FIA said the suspects allegedly prepared fake scholarship award letters, university admission offer letters and fee payment receipts to keep the family under the impression that the process was genuine. Of the total amount, Rs2.9m was transferred through Laiba’s personal bank account, while the remaining sum was received in cash, according to the agency.
Also Read: Islamabad court grants five-day remand of suspect in Laiba suicide case
Laiba's family stated that she had aspired to enrol at Harvard University for further studies and that they had made significant financial sacrifices to secure Laiba’s academic future and fulfil her dream. Laiba’s father sold his plot and pitched in Rs2.1 million from the sale’s proceeds, while her mother sold her gold jewellery.
According to the family, the suspect who reportedly defrauded them claimed to be an accounts officer at the Islamabad High Court and at other times presented himself as an employee of the superior judiciary or an officer of a sensitive institution. The family claimed that despite the substantial payment, the promises regarding admission and the scholarship given to Laiba were never fulfilled.
Laiba’s maternal uncle, Rana Amjad, stated that the Harvard University admission letter, scholarship letter and other documents provided by the suspect turned out to be fake upon verification.
He said that Laiba suffered severe distress and mental anguish after the alleged fraud came to light. Her family demanded a thorough investigation into the matter, the arrest of all individuals involved in the alleged fraud, and the recovery of the money.

items.author: Anne Florentyna
items.content:
Last week, Hunger Pangs Limited, the parent company of restaurant chain Burma Burma, filed its DRHP with SEBI, proposing a fresh issue of shares worth up to ₹150 Cr and an offer for sale (OFS) of up to 2.79 Cr shares.
Hunger Pangs has 110 shareholders, including its promoters and public shareholders. Cofounders Ankit Gupta and Chirag Chhajer each hold a 33.35% stake in the company and plan to offload up to 60 Lakh shares each.
Negen Capital, through its Negen Undiscovered Value Fund and Negen Tech Opportunities Angel Fund, holds about 10% stake in the company. The investment firm first invested in Hunger Pangs in November 2022 and doubled down in 2023.
Hunger Pangs’ shareholding remains concentrated, with its top eight shareholders collectively holding 83.19% of the company on a fully diluted basis.
Among the other shareholders, rubber and plastic manufacturing company Bbigplas Poly Private Limited holds a 2.72% stake, while Venture Catalysts owns 1.88%. Individual investors, including Sagun Capital founder Saket Agarwal and Nazara backer Nisarg Ajaykumar Vakharia, each hold about 1% stake in Hunger Pangs.
Burma Burma’s Business
Meanwhile, the fresh issue will help Burma Burma expand its restaurant network, with plans to open 27 company-owned outlets in new Tier I and Tier II cities. The company expects to open 12 outlets in FY28 and another 15 in FY29. The funds will cover civil and interior work, kitchen equipment and other setup costs.
To note, Burma Burma opened its first restaurant in Mumbai in 2014 and specialises in vegetarian Burmese cuisine. As of July 31, 2026, the chain operated 22 restaurants across nine cities, including Mumbai, Bengaluru, Hyderabad, Kolkata and Delhi NCR. It also operated a delivery kitchen in Mumbai and three warehouses.
The chain operates in the broader Asian dining segment, competing with restaurant brands such as Mainland China, Mamagoto, Yum Yum Cha and Berco’s.
In March 2026, Burma Burma raised ₹38 Cr at a valuation of ₹500 Cr. The round was led by Negen Capital, with participation from Endurance Capital and Coheron Wealth. The company’s total private funding to date stands at about $11 Mn.
Hunger Pangs’ net loss surged to ₹15.4 Cr in FY26 from ₹50 Lakh in FY25, while operating revenue rose 46.6% YoY to ₹155.5 Cr from ₹106.1 Cr. Dine-in contributed 88.82% of operating revenue in FY26, while delivery accounted for 10.76%.
Who’s At Burma Burma’s Helm?
Board of Directors
Shivakumar Dega
Dega has served as chairman and independent director at Hunger Pangs since July 2026. He has been an operating partner at Advent International since April 2023, according to his LinkedIn profile. He also serves on the boards of companies including iD Fresh, Intellect Design Arena, Leapfrog Strategy Consulting, PGP Glass and Yes Bank.
Ankit Virendra Gupta
Gupta is the cofounder and joint managing director of Hunger Pangs. After completing his management trainee programme at The Taj Mahal Palace in Mumbai, he worked in hotel operations for about two years. Around 2011, he returned to his family business before launching Burma Burma with Chhajer.
Chirag Narendra Chhajer
Chhajer is the cofounder and joint managing director of Hunger Pangs. He graduated in international business from Swinburne University in Melbourne, Australia, in 2008. He subsequently joined Chhajer Synthetics, his family’s textile trading business, before cofounding Burma Burma with Gupta.
Kushal Budhia
Budhia joined Hunger Pangs as an independent director in July 2026. He is the cofounder and group CFO of BetterPlace. Before joining BetterPlace, he spent more than two years at Pepperfry. Over a career spanning 17 years, he has also worked with Barbeque Nation Hospitality, Jupiter Capital and Goldman Sachs.
Lavanya Nalli Ramanathan
Ramanathan joined Hunger Pangs as an independent director in September 2026. She has served as vice chairman of Nalli Silk Sarees since January 2016. Her previous experience includes roles at Myntra and McKinsey. She also serves on the boards of Nalli Silk Sarees and Etnische Fashions.
Pavitra Joshi Singh
Singh joined Hunger Pangs as an independent director in September 2026. She is the chief human resources officer and vice president for PepsiCo India and South Asia, where she has held various leadership roles over a 20-year career.
Key Managerial Personnel And Senior Management
Vishnu Kumar Agarwal
Agarwal joined Burma Burma in 2014 and was elevated to CFO in 2026. His total compensation for FY26 stood at ₹58.5 Lakh.
Abhinav Agarwal
Agarwal was designated company secretary in May 2026 and compliance officer in September 2026. He joined Hunger Pangs in April 2026. Before this, he served as AVP of finance, strategy, legal and investor relations at BRISKPE. He has more than a decade of experience and has also worked with Vayana, theremin.ai and Pantomath Capital Advisors.
Ansab Ajaz Khan
Khan joined Burma Burma in 2014 and was appointed chief of kitchen operations in September 2026. He has previously worked with Mahindra Holidays and Resorts India and Mehul Restaurant and Bar. His total compensation for FY26 was ₹78 Lakh.
Sahil Mohan
Mohan was appointed chief of restaurant operations in September 2026, after 12 years with Burma Burma. He previously worked with Indian Hotels Company Limited and Taj Lands End, Mumbai. His total compensation for FY26 was ₹59.4 Lakh.
Pooja Soman
Soman joined Hunger Pangs in November 2024 and was elevated to chief human resources officer in April 2026. She has more than 17 years of experience in human resources management. Her total compensation for FY26 stood at ₹43.4 Lakh.

items.author: Web Desk
items.content:
President Asif Ali Zardari on Tuesday reaffirmed Pakistan’s commitment to fiscal sustainability, energy sector reforms, privatisation and social protection, saying the government was pursuing inclusive and green economic growth.
In a meeting with International Monetary Fund (IMF) Middle East and Central Asia Department Director Jihad Azour at Aiwan-e-Sadr in Islamabad, the president said Pakistan had moved from economic stabilisation towards recovery, according to a press release issued by the President’s Secretariat.
The president cited an increase in the size of the economy to $452.1 billion in the fiscal year 2025-26, while real gross domestic product (GDP) growth accelerated to 3.7% from 3.2% in the preceding fiscal year.
He also highlighted improvements in fiscal management, saying the fiscal deficit had declined to 2.6% of GDP in FY2025-26 and the country recorded a primary surplus for the third consecutive year.
Read: KDA's cash crunch fails to stop perks for favoured officials
President Zardari appreciated the IMF’s continued engagement with Pakistan and its support for the country’s reform programme under the Extended Fund Facility (EFF) and the Resilience and Sustainability Facility (RSF).
Referring to the conclusion of the fourth review of the EFF and the third review of the RSF, along with the staff-level agreement, he expressed confidence in the country’s continued progress towards “economic recovery and stability”.
The president reiterated the government’s commitment to increasing revenue mobilisation, improving tax administration and reforming public sector institutions. He said efforts were underway to expand tax documentation, digitalise revenue collection and curb tax evasion.
He added that the reform programme enjoyed the support of all political stakeholders, with provincial governments also contributing towards meeting the agreed targets.
Read more: Pakistan seeks global finance overhaul
The president also underscored Pakistan’s efforts to promote peace amid the ongoing conflict in the Middle East.
Azour acknowledged Pakistan’s continued engagement with the IMF under the ongoing programme and stressed the need to sustain reforms to strengthen macroeconomic stability, maintain fiscal discipline and support sustainable economic growth.
The IMF delegation included Pakistan mission chief Iva Petrova and resident representative Mahir Binici.
Finance Minister Muhammad Aurangzeb, Senator Sherry Rehman, Senator Saleem Mandviwalla, former finance minister Syed Naveed Qamar and the finance secretary also attended the meeting.
Pakistan remains engaged with the IMF under a $7 billion EFF and a $1.4 billion RSF. Earlier this month, Pakistan and the Fund reached a staff-level agreement following the fourth review under the EFF and the third review under the RSF.
The staff-level agreement is subject to approval by the IMF Executive Board and upon approval, Pakistan will have access to about $1 billion (SDR 760 million) under the EFF and about $210 million (SDR 154 million) under the RSF, bringing total disbursements under the two arrangements to about $5.7 billion.
Pakistan will chair the Boards of Governors of the IMF and the World Bank Group in 2027, marking the country's first return to the leadership of both institutions since 1953.

items.author: Reuters
items.content:
Heat waves have evolved from sporadic, isolated episodes to massive, cascading weather events that can blanket vast swaths of the planet for months or even years at a time.
To continue calling such sprawling phenomena “heat waves” would be like calling a monsoon a rain shower. To understand the new reality of these immense expanses of heat, Reuters consulted with two dozen climate researchers and analysed temperatures around the globe for every hour of every day since 1960. From those results, we developed a new concept: the “heat storm.”
Scientists and researchers often discuss global warming in the context of risks that will arise if the planet’s average global temperature rises more than 2°C (3.6°F) above pre-industrial levels. What is an ordinary person to make of that? Not much.
Heat waves are the connective tissue between the science of global warming and our everyday experience.
But supersized heat waves used to be rare. No longer. Now they swarm the planet.
2020s: The 10 largest heat storms mark a new era, with massive, cascading heat events touching virtually every person on the planet. Illustration: Reuters
Naming events is “a powerful way for people to understand that something is happening”, Anthony Leiserowitz, director of the Yale Programme on Climate Change Communication, told Reuters. Yet “we don't currently do that with heat waves”, he said, even though heat has been estimated to kill almost half a million people a year.
These are the key findings of the Reuters investigation, The Age of Heat Storms:
What is a heat storm?
There is no universal definition of a heat wave. So, in consultation with climate scientists, we have defined an ordinary heat wave as five or more consecutive days of abnormally high temperatures. We call the largest heat waves — those that at their peak cover at least 1% of the globe, roughly half the size of Canada — heat storms.
More and bigger
Heat storms were rare in the 1960s, when they averaged about five active storms per year. This decade, heat storms have averaged about 102 a year. One of them caused this summer’s deadly heat in Europe.
Read: Heatwave in Karachi leaves eight dead, rescue confirms
Biography of a 367-day heat storm
The largest heat storm on record, named Heat Storm Vera, lasted for 367 days over 2023-2024 and swept over nearly 85% of the globe. Reuters tells the story of how Vera impacted every corner of the world, from a football player going to the hospital in Texas, to Amazonian river dolphins dying in a “circus of death", to a cocoa farmer whose livelihood was destroyed in Ivory Coast.
After heat storms battered Bolivia in October 2023, Lake Titicaca, one of South America’s largest lakes, edged towards record low levels. Photo: REUTERS
Greenhouse gas emissions
As greenhouse gas emissions have increased, so too have heat storms and ordinary heat waves. From the 1960s to this decade, the amount of carbon dioxide in the atmosphere has increased by more than 30%. Over that time, the average portion of the planet likely to be covered by heat storms and heat waves has risen more than 12-fold.
18 years without a break
Another new phenomenon we identified: heat storms that run consecutively, simultaneously, or both — heat storm cascades. The duration of these cascades swelled from an average of roughly two months in the 1960s to nine months in the early 2000s.
Then, on July 6, 2008, a cascade started — and still has not stopped. For more than 18 years straight, at least one heat storm has been roiling the planet, and often more than one.
We are in a heat storm now
The world is now in the grip of Heat Storm Raimundo, which broiled Europe and stoked massive wildfires in Spain and France this summer. Since its inception on February 28, 2026, Raimundo has touched almost three-quarters of the planet’s surface.
Live tool to track heat storms

items.content:
The National Cyber Crime Investigation Agency (NCCIA) Lahore Zone on Tuesday arrested Faheem Akram, a Pakistani national indicted by United States authorities over an alleged online scheme involving the sale of more than 5.1 million counterfeit US postage labels, causing losses exceeding $126 million to the country’s postal service.
According to the NCCIA, Akram allegedly operated the scheme from August 2023 till last month, selling counterfeit shipping labels for around $2 each. The agency cited transactions worth approximately Rs35 billion, while clarifying that the $126 million figure represented alleged losses to the US Postal Service.
A case has been registered and the investigation is under way.
Read: Pakistani national indicted in US over alleged $126m postage fraud
The US Department of Justice had announced on September 28 that a federal grand jury in the Southern District of Florida had indicted Akram, 33, a resident of Khanewal, on charges including conspiracy to defraud the US government, counterfeit postage and wire fraud.
According to US prosecutors, a website, LabelsBank.com was not authorised to sell US Postal Service products and services. It allegedly offered counterfeit postage at a fixed price, irrespective of a parcel’s weight, size or destination, allowing customers to ship packages at rates substantially below legitimate postal charges.
US court records showed that more than 5,200 people had used the website to purchase over 5.1 million counterfeit shipping labels. A court order authorised the seizure and shutdown of the website.
The investigation identified 16 bank accounts allegedly linked to the case, of which seven belong to the suspect, five to his brother, two to his wife, and one each to a sister and maternal aunt.

The turmoil shock
items.author: Reuters
items.content:
France will reinforce police with troops and mount a huge security operation for ​more protests planned on Saturday, the government said on Tuesday, acknowledging failures in its response to last weekend's violence.
"The deployment next Saturday will be massive," Prime Minister Sebastien Lecornu ‌said, adding that the immediate priority was to restore order after rioting and looting swept Paris, Marseille, Lyon and other cities on October 17.
In a sometimes rowdy debate, Interior Minister Laurent Nunez said the military would be deployed alongside police, while the government pledged to overhaul tactics after widespread criticism that city centres had been left vulnerable.
Targeted curfews help restore calm
Framing the crisis as a choice "between violence and the Republic", Lecornu blamed the unrest on far-left groups, who ​in turn have accused the government of underestimating public anger over high living costs and declining public services.
The turmoil shocked France because of both its scale and the apparent inability of ​police to contain it, inflaming tensions ahead of presidential elections next year with candidates from the far right and hard left performing strongly in polls.
Read: Trump warns Kansans that US will 'burn' like France if Democrats win
Protests ⁠in other European countries, including Italy and Albania, have added to concerns that anger over living standards risks spreading around the continent at a time when many nations, including France, are struggling with budget woes.
A ​night of relative calm in France followed targeted curfews imposed in several areas affected by the chaos, which the government said had helped reassert control. The localised curfews, some directed at children and teenagers under ​age 18, were extended to Tuesday night, police said.
Lecornu acknowledged shortcomings in the state's response at the weekend, saying there had been intelligence failures, while police deployments had been too static and authorities had erred by not cancelling planned police leave.
Nunez apologised for the mistakes. "I deeply regret what happened. I accept my share of responsibility," he said.
Suspect arrested for Limoges town hall destruction
Parliament is setting up a commission of inquiry to establish the causes of the unrest, ​while authorities have assigned 200 investigators to identify and track down those involved in the street violence.
Police arrested on Tuesday a man suspected of starting a blaze that destroyed a historic town hall ​in the central city of Limoges during the rioting. Officials said he had been on a security watch list and belonged to an ultra-left group.
Sylvain Maillard, a Renaissance deputy for Paris, told Reuters some apps had become "a ‌walkie-talkie system ⁠for rioters and looters".
Read more: France places Paris, Nice under partial curfews
Underscoring the broad impact of the crisis, French borrowing costs rose further on Tuesday as investors fretted about the prospect of more unrest, with the yield on benchmark 10-year government bonds touching its highest level in 24 years.
Supermarket chain Carrefour said it had lost tens of millions of euros through theft and damage, warning that it faced an "unprecedented situation" because of the disorder.
France's main student union UNEF has called for further protests on Saturday, pledging to maintain pressure on Macron's government over what it says is a deteriorating and underfunded education system. "We carry on," it said on social media.
Separately, groups identifying ​themselves as "Gilets Jaunes" (Yellow Vests) called for protest actions ​over rising fuel costs.
The yellow vest movement, ⁠largely inactive in recent years, sprang up in 2018 during Macron's first term over plans to raise petrol taxes. Traffic blockades continued for months until the government made costly concessions it can ill afford now.
Italy faces new form of unrest, minister says
Northern Italian cities, including the financial capital Milan, were also ​hit by riots last weekend.
Though not on the scale seen in France, the unrest nonetheless jolted Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni's government, which was ​expected to introduce new security ⁠measures at a cabinet meeting on Tuesday.
Also Read: French police clash with protesters as tens of thousands rally over cost of living
Defence Minister Guido Crosetto described the disturbances as a form of "hybrid warfare" conducted through social media platforms such as TikTok, YouTube and other online networks.
"The events in Milan and elsewhere in Italy are fundamentally different from those seen in other eras," Crosetto wrote on X. "The West has yet to realise this or take any meaningful action in response."
In Milan's central Corso Vittorio Emanuele II, sportswear retailer ⁠On and a ​Levi's store that were targeted during the unrest had reopened on Tuesday but remained boarded up. Luxury stores had ​restored merchandise to window displays after temporarily removing it for security reasons.
In Albania, protesters were expected to take to the streets of Tirana for a seventh consecutive day against the government of Prime Minister Edi Rama.

items.author: Usama Anjum
items.content:
Copyright protected content copied from PhoneWorld website.
The Securities and Exchange Commission of Pakistan (SECP) has officially launched its Security Operations Center (SOC) to strengthen cybersecurity, protect critical information assets, and improve its ability to detect and respond to cyber threats.
The new facility was inaugurated in Islamabad on October 20 by National Database and Registration Authority (NADRA) Chairman Lieutenant General Muhammad Munir Afsar, who appreciated SECP’s initiative and highlighted the growing importance of cybersecurity in protecting critical digital infrastructure.
SECP Chairman Dr. Kabir Ahmed Sidhu, Commissioners Imtiaz Haider, Muzzafar Ahmed Mirza and Zeeshan Khattak, along with other senior officials, attended the inauguration ceremony.
The Security Operations Center will continuously monitor SECP’s networks, servers, endpoints, and private cloud environments to identify potential security threats at an early stage. The initiative is expected to strengthen the Commission’s operational resilience and enable faster responses to cybersecurity incidents.
The project has been funded by Karandaaz Pakistan, which serves as the implementing agency for the UK Government’s Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office (FCDO). It has been enabled by Inara Technologies Pakistan, with cybersecurity support from REWTERZ under a Managed Security Services Provider agreement.
According to SECP, the facility will operate in accordance with recognized international cybersecurity standards and best practices.
SECP Plans Sector-Wide Cybersecurity Coordination
Beyond protecting its internal digital systems, SECP is also working toward a broader cybersecurity framework for Pakistan’s capital markets.
The regulator plans to integrate the Security Operations Centers of Capital Markets Institutions (CMIs) into a coordinated sector-wide system. The proposed framework would allow participating institutions to share threat intelligence and coordinate responses to cybersecurity incidents.
This initiative supports SECP’s envisioned role as a Sectoral Computer Emergency Response Team (CERT) and Sectoral SOC, potentially improving how cybersecurity risks are identified and managed across the country’s capital markets.
During a separate meeting, SECP Chairman Dr. Kabir Ahmed Sidhu also briefed the NADRA Chairman on the Commission’s ongoing IT reforms, infrastructure modernization, and adoption of artificial intelligence and emerging technologies.
These technological improvements are intended to enhance service delivery, streamline regulatory processes, and facilitate ease of doing business.
The launch comes as financial regulators and institutions increasingly depend on digital systems to manage sensitive information and deliver services. By establishing a dedicated cybersecurity monitoring facility and planning greater coordination across capital market institutions, SECP aims to strengthen the security and resilience of Pakistan’s financial regulatory ecosystem.

items.author: Shrishti Bisht
items.content:
The Central Consumer Protection Authority (CCPA) has taken regulatory action against seven ecommerce platforms, including IndiaMART and Justdial, over the listing and sales of unauthorised hazardous explosives.
The material listed on these platforms included ammonium nitrate, gun powder, picric acid and pentaerythritol tetranitrate (PETN).
Except for ammonium nitrate, all of the aforementioned chemicals are exclusively used in manufacturing explosives.
The regulatory action has resulted in the delisting of 3,940 sellers and listing entries, while the authority has imposed penalties totalling ₹30 Lakh on Dial4Trade and ExportersIndia, the Ministry of Consumer Affairs, Food and Public Distribution said in a statement yesterday.
IndiaMART accounted for the highest number of affected sellers and listings, with 3,092, followed by ExportersIndia with 421, Justdial with 206 and TradeIndia with 166, according to the ministry. Other platforms facing regulatory action include Dial4Trade, Sigma-Aldrich India and Ibuychemikals.
In its statement, the consumer protection body shared that it had issued notices to both Justdial and IndiaMART over the listings. Following the notices, Director General – Investigation investigated the matter and shared their reports with the companies.
IndiaMART submitted its reply to the investigation report and, subsequently, approached the Delhi High Court challenging the SCN issued by the CCPA. Meanwhile, Justdial has sought adjournments in the matter till now and is yet to respond to the investigation. The next and final hearing in the matter is scheduled to be held on October 23.
Meanwhile, the CCPA has imposed a penalty of ₹10 Lakh on Dial4Trade for facilitating the sale of ammonium nitrate. ExportersIndia was fined ₹10 Lakh in two separate cases, one involving ammonium nitrate and Pentaerythritol Tetranitrate (PETN), and the other involving picric acid.
The CCPA’s action covers both marketplaces that host third-party sellers and platforms that sell products directly. Sigma-Aldrich Chemicals and Ibuychemikals have told the authority that they sell their own products and do not host third-party sellers. Investigations into TradeIndia, Sigma-Aldrich Chemicals and Ibuychemikals are ongoing.
Dial4Trade challenged the order before the National Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission (NCDRC), which dismissed its appeal on October 9. The commission held that the listings amounted to misleading advertisements and unfair trade practices under the Consumer Protection Act, 2019.
ExportersIndia has also appealed against the CCPA’s orders before the NCDRC. The appeals are expected to be listed for hearing in the coming period.
Consumers can report listings of explosives on online platforms through the national consumer helpline at 1915.
Under the Explosives Act, 1884, the sale and purchase of these substances require prescribed licences. The CCPA expects platforms to ensure sellers display valid licences issued by the petroleum and explosives safety organisation (PESO) and verify buyers’ identities and licence status before allowing purchases.
“The action reinforces the Government’s commitment to ensuring that digital marketplaces do not facilitate unauthorised access to regulated or dangerous substances in violation of applicable laws and consumer safety standards,” the ministry said.

OnePlus has confirmed that its upcoming Ace 7 series will launch in China later this month. Ahead of the launch, OnePlus has revealed details about a new dual-airflow cooling system designed to improve performance and comfort, particularly during gaming.
Although OnePlus has not announced the exact launch date. However, it has shared a teaser video on the Chinese social media platform Weibo. The new lineup is expected to bring major improvements in performance and build quality compared to the previous Ace 6 series.
OnePlus Reveals Dual-Airflow Cooling System for Upcoming Ace 7 Series
One of the main highlights of the OnePlus Ace 7 series will be its built-in active cooling fan. According to OnePlus China President Li Jie, the system uses two separate airflow pathways to manage heat more effectively.
The first airflow channel focuses on cooling the phone’s chipset. It directs hot air out through the side of the device, helping prevent heat from building up during demanding tasks such as gaming.
The second channel serves a different purpose. It directs cool air toward the phone’s rear panel to help keep the surface more comfortable to touch.
This design aims to reduce heat around the areas where users typically hold the phone. It may also help reduce sweaty hands during long gaming sessions, making the device more comfortable to use.
Designed for Better Gaming Performance
Smartphones can generate considerable heat when running graphics-intensive games or other demanding applications. Excessive heat can affect performance and make a device uncomfortable to hold.
By using an active cooling fan and two airflow channels, OnePlus aims to address both issues. The system is designed to cool internal components while also improving the temperature of the phone’s exterior.
However, the company has yet to share detailed performance figures or explain how much more effective the new cooling system is compared to conventional smartphone cooling solutions.
OnePlus Ace 7 Series: Expected Specifications
The upcoming lineup is rumoured to include two models: the standard OnePlus Ace 7 and the Ace 7 Pro.
Both phones are expected to feature a 200-megapixel main rear camera. Reports also suggest that the devices could pack a large 9,000mAh battery and use Qualcomm’s Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 5 chipset.
If these specifications prove accurate, the Ace 7 series could combine high-end processing power, a large battery, and an advanced cooling system aimed at demanding users.
OnePlus has not officially confirmed these specifications, so further details are expected closer to the launch.
Launch Expected Later This Month
OnePlus has confirmed that the Ace 7 series will debut in China later in October 2026, although the exact date remains unknown.
The new dual-airflow cooling system is one of the most notable features revealed so far. More information about the phones’ hardware, design, and other features should become available as the launch approaches.

items.author: Abbas Naqvi
items.content:
A flurry of late-night phone calls, a WhatsApp message seeking Rs30 million, the sudden disappearance of social media accounts and a trail of CCTV footage that eventually runs cold — the final five hours and 14 minutes of Mir Raza Ali’s life are marked by a series of unexplained developments.
A forensic examination of his mobile phone has pieced together a timeline of his movements and communications in the hours before he vanished on July 28, offering a minute-by-minute account of his final known activities.
The sequence began late on July 27, with a series of calls between Mir Raza and his friends.
At 11:24pm, his friend Raziq called him for 30 seconds. Six minutes later, Mir Raza called Ahmed Bhardey. The two spoke again at 11:39pm, a minute after Raziq had called Mir Raza for the second time. Another call from Raziq followed at 11:43pm, but it lasted just two seconds.
At 11:49pm, Mir Raza made a much longer call to his friend Sarim bin Tahir, speaking for 168 seconds. Three minutes later, he sent Sarim a WhatsApp message asking for Rs30 million, adding that something was going to happen in the morning that he was not prepared for. What he meant by the message remains unclear from the available timeline.
At around 1:30am, Mir Raza and Raziq had a meal at Ghaffar Kabab House, before the trail of calls resumed.
Read: In damning report, judicial commission seeks JIT for Mir Raza probe, FIA-led inquiry into police conduct
At 2:13am, Mir Raza called Ali Jimani, who returned the call three minutes later. Their conversations lasted 42 and 75 seconds, respectively. At 2:23am, Mir received a call from his business partner, Abdullah Bhardey. They spoke for 201 seconds.
Then, around 3am, another development emerged: Mir Raza’s social media accounts began to be deactivated.
His fiancée, Salwa Khan, noticed the disappearing accounts and tried to reach him through WhatsApp calls and messages. She received no response until 3:58am, according to the timeline.
By then, Mir Raza was making arrangements to travel.
At 3:57am, Bykea driver Ehsanullah received a ride request from Mir’s number. The ride was booked at 4am. Until 4:02am, Mir continued exchanging WhatsApp messages with Ahmed Bhardey, even as he remained unresponsive to his fiancée.
At 4:07am, the Bykea ride reached Cheese Valley in PECHS.
Two minutes later, at 4:09am, Salwa informed Mir Raza’s friend Haitham that all his social media accounts had been deleted. Around the same time, his WhatsApp account was also deleted, adding another unexplained turn to the sequence of events.
At 4:11am, CCTV footage from Cheese Valley showed Mir Raza sitting in the front seat of a vehicle.
The next recorded attempts to contact him went unanswered. Between 4:20am and 4:22am, Salwa made eight calls to his SIM number. Shahryar, an employee of Wafflix, also tried to reach him during the same period. Neither received a response.
Read more: Judicial commission visits Mir Raza murder site, summons key witness
At 4:28am, CCTV footage captured Mir Raza getting out of a vehicle outside United Charter School in Gulistan-e-Jauhar’s Block 3. He was subsequently seen walking along Qila-e-Street towards University Road.
The trail continued for another 10 minutes.
At 4:38:27am on July 28, Mir Raza was last seen on CCTV footage from a rent-a-car office on Hill View Road. After that, the available footage offered no further sighting of him.
His body was recovered on July 29, at a location some distance from where he was last seen.
The timeline leaves several questions unanswered: what prompted Mir Raza’s request for Rs30 million, why his social media accounts disappeared within hours, and what happened after he was last captured on CCTV.
The phone records and camera footage establish a sequence of calls, messages and movements. But the circumstances surrounding his disappearance — and the events that led to the recovery of his body the following day — remain the central mystery.

items.author: Onsa Mustafa
items.content:
Copyright protected content copied from PhoneWorld website.
The Directorate General of Immigration and Passports has revised the deadline for the transition to electronic passports (e-passport) in Pakistan. Under the updated schedule, authorities will continue issuing and renewing machine-readable passports (MRPs) until October 22, 2026.
Pakistan Revises Deadline for Mandatory E-Passport Transition
From October 23, 2026, all passport offices across Pakistan and Pakistani diplomatic missions abroad will issue only e-passports to new applicants. The authorities had initially planned to complete the transition by mid-October but have now extended the deadline.
Existing Machine-Readable Passports Will Remain Valid
The revised schedule does not require citizens with valid machine-readable passports to replace their documents before their expiry dates.
According to the directorate, all MRPs issued before October 23, 2026, will remain valid until their respective expiry dates. Citizens can continue using their existing passports without applying for an e-passport solely because of the new policy.
The extension provides additional time for applicants who need to obtain or renew a traditional machine-readable passport before the transition takes effect.
E-Passports to Become the Standard
After the deadline, passport offices in Pakistan and Pakistani diplomatic missions abroad will issue e-passports as the standard option for new applicants.
E-passports contain an electronic chip that stores the passport holder’s personal and biometric information. This technology helps authorities verify a traveller’s identity and strengthens document security.
The move is part of the government’s efforts to modernize passport services and bring Pakistan’s travel documents in line with international security standards.
What Applicants Need to Know
Citizens who want to obtain or renew a machine-readable passport should complete the process by October 22, 2026, under the revised schedule.
Those who already hold valid MRPs do not need to apply for new passports before their current documents expire. However, applicants seeking passports from October 23 onward should prepare for the mandatory e-passport system.
The transition is expected to support more secure travel documents and improve passport verification procedures. By extending the deadline, the directorate has provided applicants with additional time before the new system becomes mandatory.

items.author: Anjali Jain
items.content:
Apple India reported a 66% year-on-year (YoY) increase in its net profit during the fiscal year ended March 31, 2026 (FY26) to ₹5,311 Cr from ₹3,196 Cr it reported in the year-ago period.
The iPhone-maker’s operating revenue increased 31.4% to ₹1.04 Lakh Cr from ₹79,060 Cr in FY25, buoyed by a significant jump in its sales of iPhone, MacBooks, iPad and other products.
Apple India’s revenue from the sale of traded goods jumped to ₹99,068 Cr in the period under review, an almost 33% increase from ₹74,680 Cr in FY25.
Its remaining operating revenue came from its support services, including Apple Care services, which grew 7.6% YoY to 4,292.8 Cr, while revenue from maintenance contracts fetched ₹492.4 Cr.
Meanwhile, it earned ₹463 Cr from finance income and ₹291 Cr in other income during the fiscal year, taking its total income to ₹1.05 Cr.
To note, the tech giant had earlier said that its India market operations delivered strong double-digit revenue growth during the June quarter (Q1 FY27), aided by exceptional demand for its more affordable MacBook Neo.
Apple has continued to deepen its presence in India, expanding beyond its flagship iPhone business into a broader ecosystem spanning Macs, iPads, wearables and services. India has also become central to Apple’s global manufacturing strategy, with the country emerging as one of Apple’s largest production bases outside China. iPhone exports from India crossed ₹2 Lakh Cr in FY26.
It is now expanding its foothold in the country further through its financial services unit Apple Pay, which it launched in India last month in partnership with Axis Bank. The rollout has allowed iPhone, iPad and Apple Watch users to make payments in apps, online and at contactless-enabled stores, with Mac support coming soon.
It has already onboarded a host of merchants for Apple Pay, including Apple Store physical locations, Blinkit, Chaayos, Comet, Croma, Interflora, ixigo, Le15 Patisserie, Reliance brands, Tata 1mg, Zomato, among others.
Despite the strong growth, the company now expects supply constraints in the coming months due to a shortfall in advanced semiconductor manufacturing capacity, along with constraints around memory components. The company expects the constraints to affect availability of iPhones, Macs and iPads globally, which could also have an impact on markets such as India if component shortages persist.
Where Did Apple India Spend In FY26?
Apple India’s total expenses during the fiscal year under review grew 28% to ₹96,224 Cr from ₹75,190.7 Cr it reported in FY25. Notably, the company paid ₹10,373.7 Cr in license fee during the year, more than double of ₹4,257.8 Cr it spent in FY25.
Purchase Of Traded Goods: Apple India’s inventory expenses stood at ₹78,228.7 Cr during the fiscal year, a 21.6% jump from ₹64,335.8 Cr in FY25, making it the company’s biggest expense.
Employee Benefit Expenses: Its expenditure under this head surged 13% YoY to ₹3,531.3 from ₹3,126.1 Cr in FY25, including spending on wages, PF contributions, gratuity and staff welfare. Notably, the company paid ₹17,80.4 Cr in salaries and bonuses during the year.
Marketing & Advertisement: Another major expense head, marketing and advertising cost Apple India ₹1,075.2 Cr during the year, increasing 22.6% YoY from ₹877.1 Cr in the year-ago period.

items.author: Onsa Mustafa
items.content:
Copyright protected content copied from PhoneWorld website.
Google has opened its SynthID Detector tool to the public, allowing anyone to check whether images, videos, and audio files contain hidden AI watermarks. After more than a year of limited testing, the tool is now available for free through its official website.
Users can visit synthid.com to upload a file and check for signs of AI-generated content. The tool scans the file for an invisible watermark and provides results within seconds.
Google Makes Its AI Content Detector Free for Everyone – Here’s How It Works
SynthID Detector looks for hidden watermarks embedded in content created using supported AI tools. These watermarks help identify AI-generated material even when someone edits the original file.
According to Google, the watermarks can survive common changes such as cropping, applying filters, compression, and adjusting playback speed. This allows the system to detect watermarks in certain edited images, videos, and audio recordings.
The tool supports several popular file formats, including JPG, PNG, WEBP, and GIF for images, MP4 and MOV for videos, and MP3, WAV, and FLAC for audio.
However, the detector does not determine whether every file was created using AI. It specifically searches for SynthID watermarks, which means its results depend on whether the content contains a watermark supported by the system.
From Limited Testing to Public Access
Google first introduced SynthID Detector at its I/O 2025 event. Initially, the company limited access to journalists, researchers, and media professionals who wanted to verify AI-generated content.
In May 2026, Google expanded its SynthID verification features to Search. Support for Chrome followed a few weeks later.
The company launched the public version of the detector on October 7, 2026. This move gives ordinary users access to the technology without requiring them to join a limited testing programme.
See Also: AI-Generated Woman Fools Brazilian Man Into 2,000 km Journey
Other AI Companies Also Use SynthID
SynthID is not limited to content created through Google’s own AI services. According to the company, OpenAI, NVIDIA, ElevenLabs, and Kakao also use the technology to watermark AI-generated content.
Google has also indicated that Apple support is coming soon. This could make the detector more useful as additional AI platforms adopt compatible watermarking methods.
The technology has already reached a significant scale. Google says it has added SynthID watermarks to more than 180 billion images and videos, along with 240,000 years of audio.
Meanwhile, its verification systems process more than one million requests every day across Google Search, Gemini, and Chrome.
The Tool Has Some Important Limitations
Although SynthID Detector offers a convenient way to check AI-generated material, it is not a universal AI detection system.
The tool can identify content carrying a compatible SynthID watermark. It may not detect AI-generated files produced by tools that do not use this technology.
Similarly, a file that returns no watermark detection should not automatically be considered human-made. The absence of a SynthID watermark does not prove that a person created the content.
Google describes the detector as a clue rather than a final verdict. Users should therefore consider its findings alongside other evidence when checking the authenticity of digital material.
To prevent misuse and attempts to discover how to remove watermarks, Google has also limited users to approximately 10 checks per day.
Overall, the public launch of SynthID Detector gives users a free way to investigate the origins of supported digital content. While it cannot identify every AI-generated image, video, or audio file, it offers another option for journalists, researchers, content creators, and ordinary internet users who want to verify digital media.
