Copyright protected content copied from PhoneWorld website.
The federal government is working on a smartphone installment scheme aimed at improving access to mobile devices in Pakistan, Federal Minister for IT and Telecommunication Shaza Fatima Khawaja has confirmed.
Speaking during a panel discussion at the Global AI and Digital Summit 2026 in Seoul, South Korea, the minister revealed that work on the initiative is underway as part of the government’s broader efforts to improve digital connectivity and inclusion.
A government-backed installment initiative could potentially make smartphones more accessible by allowing eligible consumers to spread the cost over multiple payments. However, the minister did not provide a launch date or explain how the proposed scheme would operate.
Who Will Be Eligible for the Smartphone Installment Scheme?
Important details have yet to be announced, including eligibility requirements, participating smartphone brands, available devices, installment durations, down payments, and any financial institutions or service providers involved.
It is also unclear whether the scheme would require a credit card, support alternative payment methods, or include government financial assistance.
Until an official framework is released, consumers should avoid relying on websites or social media advertisements claiming to offer registration for the government scheme.
The proposed program could be relevant to students, young professionals, and other consumers who need smartphones for education, work, and digital services but face affordability constraints.
During the same discussion, Shaza Fatima Khawaja said 17.6 million smartphones were locally manufactured or assembled in Pakistan during 2025.
The figure, attributed to the minister, highlights the role of local smartphone production as the country works to improve access to mobile technology.
Greater availability of locally assembled devices, combined with accessible financing, could help expand ownership if the installment initiative is implemented successfully. However, no official details have been provided about whether locally assembled phones would receive preference under the scheme.
For now, the scheme remains under development. Consumers will need to wait for official eligibility criteria, payment structures, partners, and application procedures.

items.author: Usama Anjum
items.content:
Copyright protected content copied from PhoneWorld website.
Pakistan has recorded a 68.1% increase in internet download speeds over the past two years, while 5G services have expanded to 1,700 sites across 24 cities, according to Federal Minister for IT and Telecommunication Shaza Fatima Khawaja.
Speaking at a panel discussion on the second day of the Global AI and Digital Summit 2026 in Seoul, South Korea, the minister highlighted Pakistan’s progress in digital infrastructure, mobile connectivity, and artificial intelligence. She stressed that AI development and digital inclusion must move forward together.
During the question-and-answer session, the minister shared developments in fiber-optic networks, 5G deployment, and satellite connectivity plans.
According to her, Pakistan has deployed more than 234,000 kilometers of optical fiber nationwide. She said the government had removed Right of Way (RoW) charges across the country to reduce the cost of obtaining permissions for fiber deployment.
She described the March 2026 spectrum auction as the largest in Pakistan’s history, reportedly involving 480 MHz of spectrum and generating $509 million.
Within six months of the auction, 5G services had reached 1,700 sites across 24 cities, she said.
Satellite Internet to Support Connectivity in Remote Areas
Pakistan is finalizing a satellite licensing framework to improve connectivity in underserved regions, particularly the mountainous northern areas and remote parts of Balochistan.
The minister clarified that satellite connectivity would complement existing terrestrial telecom networks rather than replace them.
She also said the Universal Service Fund (USF) had helped extend network connectivity to more than 38 million people across over 22,000 settlements in 110 districts.
Digital Inclusion and AI Development Remain Key Priorities
Shaza Fatima said the gender gap in mobile connectivity had declined from 25% to 8% and that Pakistan had improved its position by 27 places in the Global Digital Index 2026.
She emphasized that artificial intelligence and digital inclusion must progress together, so AI adoption is not limited to people already connected to reliable internet and digital services.
Referring to an estimated 2.6 billion people worldwide who remain unconnected, she said connecting them was achievable because the technology and resources exist.
The figures and rankings were presented by the minister during the summit and have not been independently verified in this report. The long-term impact will depend on network reliability, affordability, and access in underserved communities.

items.author: Shrishti Bisht
items.content:
Twenty-two founders across 15 new-age tech companies earned a combined ₹61.28 Cr in fixed remuneration in FY26, up 4.6% from ₹58.54 Cr in FY25, according to data compiled by Inc42. Average fixed remuneration per founder increased to ₹2.79 Cr from ₹2.66 Cr.
Of these, 16 founders received increases in fixed pay, four saw reductions, and two reported unchanged remuneration.
Honasa Consumer cofounder Ghazal Alagh recorded the highest percentage increase, with her fixed remuneration rising 60% to ₹2.4 Cr from ₹1.5 Cr. Delhivery cofounder Sahil Barua followed with a 21.4% increase to ₹3.4 Cr from ₹2.8 Cr.
Ola Electric founder Bhavish Aggarwal recorded the steepest percentage decline, with his remuneration falling 34.8% to ₹4.5 Cr from ₹6.9 Cr. Nykaa founder Falguni Nayar’s fixed pay fell 14% to ₹74 Lakh from ₹86 Lakh, while Swiggy cofounder Sriharsha Majety’s remuneration declined 12.5% to ₹1.4 Cr from ₹1.6 Cr.
Lenskart cofounder Peyush Bansal drew the highest fixed remuneration among the founders tracked, despite a 1.7% decline to ₹5.7 Cr from ₹5.8 Cr. Meesho cofounders Vidit Aatrey and Sanjeev Kumar followed with ₹4.8 Cr each, ahead of Ola Electric’s Aggarwal at ₹4.5 Cr and Paytm founder Vijay Shekhar Sharma at ₹4 Cr. Sharma’s fixed remuneration remained unchanged from FY25.
However, fixed pay tells only part of the story. Peyush Bansal received ₹12 Cr in bonuses and performance incentives – more than twice his fixed remuneration – along with perquisites and retirement benefits. Fellow Lenskart cofounder Neha Bansal received ₹6 Cr in bonuses and performance incentives, in addition to her ₹2.7 Cr fixed pay.
Honasa Consumer cofounder Varun Alagh received ₹2.4 Cr in performance incentives, equal to his fixed remuneration.
Share-based compensation also featured prominently. Majety’s ESOP gains stood at ₹549.3 Cr, while Delhivery cofounder Kapil Bharati recorded ₹6.9 Cr in ESOP gains.
Separately, the cost of stock options granted to FirstCry founder Supam Maheshwari stood at ₹31.7 Cr. He also received ₹2.1 Cr in perquisites and ₹84 Lakh in performance incentives.
These components require separate treatment. Stock-option costs and ESOP-related benefits do not necessarily represent cash received by a founder during the year and should be distinguished from fixed salaries and cash incentives.
Inc42 has been tracking founders’ remuneration since FY23, covering the startup ecosystem’s shift from the era of funding boom to the funding winter and now, more recently, towards profitability and IPOs.
Building on the FY25 edition, the FY26 tracker examines changes in fixed pay, other compensation components, and the financial performance of the companies these founders lead.

Peyush Bansal | Lenskart
The Lenskart cofounder and CEO earned ₹5.7 Cr in fixed remuneration in FY26. In addition to his fixed pay, Bansal also received ₹12 Cr in bonus and performance incentives, along with ₹24.04 Lakh in perquisites and ₹7.5 Lakh in retirals.
Lenskart’s net profit rose 69% YoY to ₹500.9 Cr in FY26, while operating revenue increased 33% YoY to ₹8,814 Cr. Its profit growth was aided by operating leverage, premiumisation, and growth in international markets.
Vidit Aatrey & Sanjeev Kumar | Meesho
Meesho cofounders Vidit Aatrey and Sanjeev Kumar each earned ₹4.8 Cr in fixed remuneration in FY26, up 6.7% from ₹4.5 Cr a year earlier.
The data reviewed by Inc42 did not disclose additional perks for either founder.
The ecommerce company’s operating revenue increased 34.5% YoY to ₹12,626 Cr in FY26, while its net loss narrowed 65.6% YoY to ₹1,357.7 Cr.
Its annual transacting user base grew 33% YoY to 26.4 Cr in Q4 FY26, while order volumes increased 43% YoY to 71.7 Cr during the quarter.
Bhavish Aggarwal | Ola Electric
Ola Electric founder and CMD Bhavish Aggarwal earned ₹4.5 Cr in remuneration in FY26, compared with ₹6.9 Cr in FY25.
In FY26, the EV maker’s net loss narrowed nearly 20% to ₹1,833 Cr from ₹2,276 Cr in the previous fiscal. Operating revenue nearly halved to ₹2,460 Cr from ₹4,932 Cr.
Bhanu Chopra | RateGain
RateGain founder and CEO Bhanu Chopra earned ₹3.7 Cr in fixed remuneration in FY26, unchanged from FY25.
The company’s operating revenue rose 69.4% to ₹1,823.6 Cr from ₹1,076.7 Cr, while net profit declined 6.9% to ₹194.4 Cr from ₹208.9 Cr.
Sahil Barua & Kapil Bharati | Delhivery
Delhivery cofounders Sahil Barua and Kapil Bharati earned ₹3.4 Cr and ₹3.3 Cr, respectively, in fixed remuneration in FY26.
Barua’s fixed pay increased 21.4% from ₹2.8 Cr in FY25, while Bharati’s rose 17.9% from ₹2.8 Cr.
In addition, Barua received ₹33.7 Lakh in performance incentives. Bharati received ₹33 Lakh in performance incentives and ₹6.9 Cr in ESOP gains.
The logistics company’s operating revenue rose 17% YoY to ₹10,486 Cr in FY26, while net profit grew 8% YoY to ₹321 Cr.
Vijay Shekhar Sharma | Paytm
Paytm founder and CEO Vijay Shekhar Sharma earned ₹4 Cr in fixed remuneration in FY26, unchanged from the previous year. He also received ₹33 Lakh in perquisites.
The fintech company reported its first full-year net profit of ₹552 Cr in FY26, compared with a loss of ₹663 Cr in FY25.
Operating revenue increased 22.3% YoY to ₹8,437 Cr. It also posted an EBITDA of ₹502 Cr, against an EBITDA loss of ₹1,506 Cr in the previous year.
Tarun Mehta & Swapnil Jain | Ather
Ather Energy cofounders Tarun Mehta and Swapnil Jain each earned ₹2.1 Cr in fixed remuneration in FY26, up 5% from ₹2 Cr a year earlier. They also received ₹90 Lakh each in variable compensation, taking their individual fixed and variable pay to ₹3 Cr.
The EV maker’s operating revenue rose 62.8% YoY to ₹3,671.8 Cr, while its net loss narrowed 36.3% YoY to ₹517.2 Cr.
EBITDA loss declined 51.6% YoY to ₹257 Cr, with its EBITDA margin improving to -6.7% from -23% in FY25.
Last Updated: October 21, 2026, 14:40 IST

items.author: Anjali Jain
items.content:
Walmart-owned ecommerce major Flipkart is reportedly targeting an October-end public launch for its food delivery service, ‘Eat-in by Minutes’, to compete with Eternal-owned Zomato and Swiggy.
The company has expanded its internal pilot in Bengaluru to more than 8,000 employees, according to a TechCrunch report citing people familiar with the development.
National Restaurant Association of India (NRAI) president Sagar Daryani told the publication that Flipkart had informed restaurant partners of plans to launch publicly by October-end and expand to five or six cities by the end of 2026.
Inc42’s queries to Flipkart remained unanswered till the time of publication. The story will be updated on receiving a response.
The expanded trial follows Flipkart’s initial employee pilot in Bengaluru.
Flipkart Taps Ekart, ONDC
Flipkart’s food delivery service currently appears as a separate tab on its main shopping app, alongside its quick commerce offering Flipkart Minutes and travel bookings. The company has also deployed a dedicated fleet of delivery riders through its logistics arm Ekart, separate from the riders handling quick commerce deliveries.
For restaurant onboarding, Flipkart is tapping the government-backed Open Network for Digital Commerce (ONDC), while also signing up restaurants directly.
The company is positioning its food delivery service around a lower-cost model for restaurant partners. Flipkart has reportedly proposed a base commission of around 10%, as per Daryani. This is much lower than the 20%-25% commission that restaurants typically pay established platforms, he said.
However, commissions account for only part of restaurants’ costs on food delivery platforms. Advertising, discounts, and promotions add to their overall expenditure, making the total cost of selling through Flipkart an important consideration for prospective partners.
Beyond restaurant pricing, Flipkart’s existing commerce ecosystem gives it a customer base to which it can cross-sell food orders.
Food Delivery Market Sees Fresh Competition
Flipkart’s planned launch comes amid fresh competition for Zomato and Swiggy, with challengers focusing on restaurant commissions and the cost of ordering food online.
Rapido has been expanding Ownly, its food delivery service offering a zero-commission model for restaurants.
Quick food delivery startup Swish has also begun piloting Swish Go, allowing users in select Bengaluru pincodes to order from third-party restaurants and cloud kitchens. The service is advertised as charging no packaging or platform fees.
Similarly, cloud kitchen operator Curefoods announced its MegaBite pilot yesterday, offering dishes priced at ₹49-₹199 from brands across its portfolio. Currently available in Bengaluru’s HSR Layout, the app claims to charge no delivery or platform fees.
These moves reflect growing pressure on incumbent platforms to offer more affordable options to customers while addressing restaurant partners’ concerns over platform commissions and promotional expenses.
For Flipkart, food delivery adds another business alongside its expanding quick commerce operations through Minutes.
The expansion also comes amid uncertainty over its IPO timeline. Former senior executives, including Mukesh Bansal, Sanjay Baweja, and Ankit Nagori, have urged Walmart to buy back their vested ESOPs.
On the financial front, the Flipkart Group reported an 18.2% YoY jump in consolidated revenue from operations to ₹1.45 Lakh Cr in FY26, while its consolidated net loss narrowed marginally by 2.1% to ₹8,468 Cr from ₹8,646 Cr in FY25.

Brokerages Get A Ticket To Wall Street
The Nifty 50 has dropped 12.4% YTD in 2026, the first yearly decline in over a decade, and FPIs had pulled a cumulative ₹3.1 Lakh Cr (around $33 Bn) over this time from Indian equities. With the stock market sliding and SIPs returning negative returns, retail investors also want to hedge bets against rallying US tech stocks. A clutch of discount brokerages like Zerodha, Groww, Angel One and Upstox are now enabling this exposure. So, what’s on offer?
Green Card For Indian Folios: Zerodha is now offering eligible users an option to invest in up to 2,000 US-listed companies and around 1,000 ETFs through its Kite platform. Users can opt for fractional investing, same-day delivery or SIPs. Funds can simply be transferred to dollar-denominated wallets through net banking, with UPI and card payments yet to be introduced.
Desi Discount Brokers Go Global: Peers like Groww and Upstoxx had already launched similar offerings recently, with Angel One also joining the club on Monday. All four received approval from the International Financial Services Centres Authority in June to offer investors international and US stock options from GIFT City. Prior to this, IND Money and HDFC Securities were popular platforms for international investing.
US Stocks Take The Cake: Direct exposure to international markets will allow Indian investors to not only hedge domestic concentration and diversify geographical risk, but also gain access to global technology megatrends like AI, cloud computing, and semiconductors, which are yet to enter Indian equity markets meaningfully.
Brokers Eye Revenue Mix: The market slowdown in India, combined with SEBI’s derivatives reforms, is squeezing discount brokers’ core trading income, forcing them to diversify into lending and allied financial services. New demat account additions were down 22% YoY to 3.2 Cr in FY26, and discount brokers need to cross-sell more exciting products to existing users, making US stocks an enticing choice.
So, as Indian investors look beyond domestic markets, here’s what Zerodha and its peers have to offer now…
From The Editor’s Desk
Tonbo Imaging’s IPO Concludes With A Bang
The defence tech startup’s ₹852.1 Cr IPO was subscribed almost 140X on the final day of bidding, receiving bids for 115.87 Cr shares against the 85.3 Lakh shares on offer.
QIBs led the demand with a 293.56X subscription of their quota, followed by NIIs at 170.94X, while retail investors bid for 31.07X their allotted shares.
Tonbo’s IPO comprises only an OFS of up to 1.22 Cr shares, with a price band of ₹665–₹700 per share valuing the company at around ₹4,010 Cr at the upper end.
Even Healthcare Bags $50 Mn
Even Healthcare raised $50 Mn in a Series B round led by Khosla Ventures, with participation from Alpha Wave, to expand its hospital network across Bengaluru.
Founded in 2020, the startup operates a managed-care model combining preventive healthcare, diagnostics, hospitalisation and post-discharge recovery. It has raised a total of $120 Mn in funding to date.
The startup plans to open one hospital by end-2026 and three more by end-FY27 before expanding to more cities, while shifting focus towards hospital-led healthcare.
Curefoods Enters Budget Food Delivery
Curefoods is piloting MegaBite in Bengaluru’s HSR Layout, offering dishes priced at ₹49–₹199 from its brands, including Rolls On Wheels, Olio Pizza, and Eatfit, with no delivery charges or platform fees.
Founded in 2020 by Cult.fit founder Ankit Nagori, Curefoods has built a cloud kitchen portfolio through acquisitions. It paused its IPO process after receiving the SEBI nod due to valuation concerns.
This is the startup’s first attempt at running its own delivery platform, placing it in direct competition with other budget food providers like Swiggy’s Toing, Rapido’s Ownly and Rebel Foods’ EatSure.
Hunar.AI’s Agentic Hiring Bet
Bengaluru-based Hunar.AI raised ₹40 Cr ($4.2 Mn) in a Series A round led by Blume Ventures, with participation from existing and new investors. The funds will strengthen its AI infrastructure, products and go-to-market strategy.
Founded in 2022 by Krishna Khandelwal and Shantanu Bhattacharyya, Hunar.AI is building conversational AI agents to automate frontline hiring, onboarding, training and employee retention across multiple industries.
Hunar.AI claims its agents handled over 1.5 Cr conversations through September 2026, with volumes doubling QoQ. Its customers include Swiggy, Zepto, Croma, Starbucks and Bajaj Finserv.
Meta Faces Meity Algorithm Review
The IT ministry has asked Meta to review Facebook and Instagram’s recommendation algorithms to prevent misleading or out-of-context content from being disproportionately amplified and to promote diverse, credible information.
Meta has faced repeated scrutiny this year over its content moderation policies and the availability of CSAM on its platforms, resulting in stricter reporting guidelines.
The October 10 advisory calls for stronger content-review mechanisms, contextual information on visuals depicting public events, and faster escalation of posts that could trigger public confusion or disorder.
Inc42 Markets
Inc42 Startup Spotlight
How Factrika Is Solving Blue-Collar Hiring Gaps For Factory
Manufacturers can lose valuable production time when workers fail to turn up, or demand spikes leave them short-staffed. To address this, Factrika is building an on-demand workforce platform that helps factories source, deploy and manage blue-collar workers based on skills, location and shift requirements.
Staffing On Demand: Founded in 2024 by Kshitij Puri and Gaurav Asthana, the New Delhi-based startup offers same-day staffing, absentee replacement, seasonal workforce deployment, project-based hiring and full-time recruitment. Its platform coordinates worker deployment, tracks attendance and arranges replacements when workers fail to show up.
Building A Factory Workforce: Factrika claims to have access to more than 10,000 workers through a network spanning over 4,000 ITIs and 1,000 polytechnic institutes. It says it has completed over 65,000 shifts with a 90% job-fill rate, operating across Bhiwadi, Bawal, Kharkhoda, Gurugram and Bahadurgarh. Its customers include Lenskart, Asahi India Glass and Jubilant FoodWorks.
Scaling Operations: Factrika recently raised ₹8.9 Cr to expand its team, strengthen its technology and enter more manufacturing clusters. As factories contend with fluctuating labour requirements and tight delivery schedules, the startup is betting that on-demand staffing will make shop-floor workforce management less chaotic.
As manufacturers look for faster, more reliable ways to fill shop-floor roles, can Factrika become the go-to workforce platform for India’s factories?

The National Database and Registration Authority (NADRA) has warned citizens in Punjab about fraudulent websites claiming to offer civilian arms license services. The authority urged applicants to use official online channels and verify website addresses before sharing personal information or making payments.
According to the alert, scammers have created fake websites that look like legitimate platforms for arms license applications. These websites reportedly target people seeking licenses and may charge them excessive fees while putting their sensitive personal information at risk.
NADRA Warns Punjab Citizens Against Fake Arms License Websites
NADRA has advised applicants to carefully check a website’s authenticity before starting the application process. Citizens should verify the web address before entering their identity details, uploading documents, or transferring money.
Fraudulent websites may appear genuine and use official-looking designs to gain the trust of visitors. However, submitting information through these platforms can expose applicants to financial fraud and the misuse of their personal data.
The authority has urged citizens to avoid unverified websites that promise assistance with arms license applications. Applicants should not trust a platform simply because it offers online services or claims to speed up the licensing process.
See Also: NADRA Enables Online CNIC Replacement Through PakID App
Fake Websites Pose Financial and Privacy Risks
Using fraudulent online platforms can lead to more than financial losses. Scammers may collect sensitive information, including identity details and documents submitted during the application process.
Criminals could misuse this information for identity fraud or other unauthorized activities. Applicants may also lose money by paying fees to websites that have no connection with the relevant government authorities.
NADRA’s warning highlights the need for greater caution when accessing online services related to government documents and licenses.
Use the Official NADRA Arms License Portal
Citizens seeking civilian arms licenses in Punjab should use the official NADRA portal for the process rather than relying on third-party websites.
Applicants can visit the official portal at pal.nadra.gov.pk/pal to access the relevant services.
Before submitting an application, citizens should confirm that they are using the correct website. They should also avoid making payments through unofficial platforms or sharing personal documents with unknown service providers.
NADRA has urged applicants to remain vigilant against online scams and rely on verified channels for arms license-related services. Following these precautions can help citizens protect their money, identity information, and personal documents from fraudulent websites.

Touchscreen MacBook Pro Could Be the Main Highlight

According to Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman, Apple will unveil a touchscreen MacBook Pro as part of its upcoming announcements. The new device could offer users another way to interact with macOS, although its final design and features remain unconfirmed.
Apple is also reportedly preparing a new 14-inch MacBook Pro powered by its upcoming M6 chipset. The new processor could bring improvements in performance and power efficiency, making the laptop more capable of handling demanding professional workloads.
New iMac and OLED iPad Mini Also Expected
The October event may include other product announcements beyond the MacBook Pro. Reports suggest that Apple could introduce an upgraded iMac, potentially bringing improvements to its all-in-one desktop computer.
An iPad mini with an OLED display is also in development. OLED technology could deliver better contrast, deeper blacks, and improved image quality compared with traditional LCD screens.
However, Apple has yet to confirm whether the updated iMac and OLED iPad mini will appear at the October 28 event.
Apple Expands Its October Product Announcements
The upcoming event follows Apple’s recent announcements of several smart home products. These include the HomeView, HomePod mini 2, a new Apple TV 4K, and additional smart home devices developed with partner companies.
The October 28 event could therefore bring another major round of hardware announcements from the company, with the MacBook Pro expected to take center stage.
Apple has not yet shared the full specifications, prices, or availability details of the rumored products. More information should become available during the event, when the company will reveal its plans for the next generation of Mac and other devices.

items.author: Palak Sharma
items.content:
Food has a way of taking us back in time. A familiar aroma or a single bite can bring back memories. For some, it may be their Nani’s dal fry; for others, their mother’s achaar — a taste passed down through generations. Yet, no matter how many times we try to recreate these dishes, they rarely taste quite like the originals.
Unfortunately, with busy schedules, long commutes and the demands of everyday life, finding time to cook a meal is not always easy. The pandemic, however, offered an opportunity, and people did return to their kitchens, dusted off family recipes and learnt to cook meals they would otherwise have ordered online.
But as offices reopened, so did the daily grind. For professionals, it became a herculean task to fit cooking into their busy routines. This is where AI-powered cooking assistants have found an opening, according to Mahek Mody, the founder of upliance.ai, a provider of smart cooking appliances.
“People want to eat home-cooked food, but there are two things we need to do to get people to cook at home. First, make it convenient. Second, make it interesting,” Mody said, adding that by combining automated cooking functions with guided recipes and software that can be updated or improved over time, advanced cooking appliances are making home cooking less time-consuming and more accessible.
In India, a growing set of players, including established brands such as Wonderchef and Philips, is betting on this proposition. Their products range from guided cooking machines to more automated devices that handle multiple steps of a recipe.
But the opportunity is still in its nascency. While these appliances promise to bridge the gap between wanting home-cooked food and having the time to prepare it, their relatively high prices raise questions about the size of the addressable market, who will pay for them, and whether they can move beyond early adopters to become a fixture in Indian kitchens. Let’s find out…
India’s Smart Kitchen Shift
From the perfect tadka to that secret family ingredient, every Indian kitchen has its own way of doing things. For automated cooking to catch on, these appliances must get the Indian palate right. This is where AI, data and machine learning can help.
At upliance, the company uses generative AI to translate recipes into instructions that its appliance can execute. For instance, its YouTube recipe feature breaks down a cooking video into steps and maps them to the device’s capabilities, from chopping ingredients to adjusting cooking sequences. AI also helps identify cooking styles and adapt recipes to Indian preferences.
Customers can also access recipes through the company’s app and leave a voicemail if something goes wrong while cooking. The team responds to their queries and uses ratings and feedback to improve recipes over time.
“A general-purpose AI chatbot can explain how to cook something, but it cannot necessarily send instructions to a physical device that performs the cooking. Connecting AI-generated instructions to the appliance is the distinction we are trying to create,” Mody said.
Machine learning helps the appliance respond to variations during cooking. He said data from several lakh tadka preparations has helped the company refine its algorithms.
However, not everyone in the category believes such capabilities should automatically be labelled AI. The founder of Wonderchef, Ravi Saxena, argued that many features marketed as AI-powered are based on connectivity, memory or basic analytics.
“Wonderchef’s appliances, too, can download recipes from the internet. There is a limited role for AI in improving our products, and we do not want to exaggerate that role,” Saxena said.
The company also analyses usage patterns to improve cooking instructions. If users consistently boil a dish for 18 minutes instead of the recommended 15, the company can spot the trend and adjust the recipe accordingly. The appliances can also track how users vary ingredient quantities while cooking. According to him, these improvements do not necessarily require AI.
AI In The Kitchen: What’s Driving Adoption?
According to MarkNtel Advisors Research, India’s smart kitchen appliances market is estimated at $800 Mn-$1.48 Bn in 2026. Cooking appliances account for approximately 48% of the market. AI-powered cooking assistants and automated kitchen appliances, including products from upliance and Wonderchef, also fall within this broader segment.
Besides, new-age brands such as Nosh, Posha, On2Cook and Geek Robocook are also betting on the emerging segment. Meanwhile, legacy players like Philips are entering the space, with the company launching its automated, all-in-one smart cooking device, Philips OneChef, in India earlier this year.
But Wonderchef’s Saxena believes the category is still some way from a tipping point. He compared it with air fryers — a category that took seven years to gain widespread adoption. Automated cooking appliances will similarly need consumer education, while excessive complexity and higher prices in the name of AI could deter buyers.
Repeat usage offers one sign of whether these products are becoming part of everyday kitchens. Saxena says Wonderchef’s Roti Magic is used daily by its buyers, Chai Magic around three times a day, and Chef Magic roughly three times a week.
Similarly, upliance reported that more than 7,000 Indian households have cooked 6.68 Lakh meals on its platform since December 2022.
The Conundrum
As of now, the segment is plagued with white-labelled products, which has its own demerits. Factors such as inconsistent cooking results, the need for manual intervention and cleaning hassles raise questions about the hands-free convenience these appliances promise.
According to Saxena, at ₹30,000 or more, buyers expect consistent results and convenience, not another appliance gathering dust in the kitchen.
Ravi of upliance said that many products in the industry may look similar but fail to deliver on their promises and compromise on pillars like post-sale services while pushing up customer acquisition costs, giving a bad name to peers offering real innovation and satisfactory aftersales.
“The base of this problem is white labelling,” he said. Mody also argued that having an IP can open the room for improving it over time, unlike selling a fixed third-party product.
While the technology and price point may appeal to a specific segment of Indian consumers, reaching a wider market remains a challenge. At the same time, high upfront costs could limit adoption, making affordability and the ability to deliver consistent value crucial to scaling the category.
Archana Jahagirdar of Rukam Capital proposes a solution — designing regionally suitable cooking assistants that provide functional value and are available at affordable prices. “But the success of AI-powered cooking assistants will ultimately depend on how well brands balance convenience, affordability and reliability,” she said.
All in all, while technology can make home cooking easier, winning over Indian households will require more than smart features. Products must cater to regional tastes, deliver consistent results and offer value for money to move beyond early adopters and become everyday kitchen essentials.
THE STARTUP SPOTLIGHT | HOW EATNACK IS PUTTING A HEALTHY SPIN ON SNACKING
EatNack sells health-focused snacks and convenient meal options, positioning itself around the idea of combining taste, nutrition and convenience. It uses processes such as freeze-drying and steam-roasting to retain taste and nutrients while avoiding artificial additives.
Its portfolio spans snacks such as masala almonds, lime-and-mint peanuts and seasoned cashews, alongside ready-to-eat meal options. It has 11–20 SKUs across its product range that clock an average MRR of ₹3.5 Lakh.
Marketplaces contribute to 70% of sales, offline channels account for 25%, and its own website generates the remaining 5%. The brand is now targeting institutional and hospitality customers, alongside opportunities in export markets like Canada, Australia, New Zealand, the UAE and Mauritius.
The Deep Dive
ECOMMERCE BUZZ
UC Hungry For More Funds: The home services company’s board has approved a proposal to raise up to ₹2,500 Cr through equity and convertible securities to strengthen InstaHelp’s market position and make new business investments. It reported a 208% YoY jump in net loss to ₹182.5 Cr in Q2 FY27.
Flipkart Group Cuts Losses: Walmart-backed Flipkart Group’s consolidated operating revenue grew 18.2% YoY to ₹1.45 Lakh Cr in FY26, while net loss narrowed 2.1% to ₹8,468 Cr and gross margins rose 23%.
Shopify To Bring Shop Pay To India: Ecommerce major Shopify is preparing to launch its accelerated checkout service, Shop Pay, in India by Q1 2027. It will leverage its existing relationships with D2C brands for a ready merchant base.
Udaan’s FY26 Revenue Rises 13%: B2B ecommerce unicorn Udaan’s operating revenue increased 12.6% YoY to ₹5,134 Cr in FY26 from ₹4,561 Cr, while its net loss narrowed 19.4% to ₹851.5 Cr from ₹1,055.4 Cr.
Traya Eyes ₹300 Cr: The D2C haircare startup is in talks to raise around ₹300 Cr from Belgium-based investment firm Verlinvest at a proposed valuation of ₹2,500 Cr-₹3,000 Cr, possibly comprising both primary and secondary components.
DealShare’s CEO Quits: Kamaldeep Singh has stepped down to lead EV battery-swapping company Indofast Energy. The exit comes as the ecommerce startup explores a potential sale to online pharmacy Truemeds, amid a prolonged business turnaround and leadership churn
The Operator Question
When a consumer is willing to spend ₹50,000 on an AI-powered cooking assistant, what factors determine their choice between legacy appliance players and newer AI-first brands, and how can brands differentiate themselves beyond price?
In conversation with Inc42, Nosh founder Yatin Varachhiya said that at ₹50,000, consumers will choose a product that gives them clear, distinct value.
Such a product should be able to solve an everyday need by cooking complete meals independently, allowing people to enjoy cuisines from around the world using ingredients they know and trust.
Beyond price, many differentiate through true autonomy, everyday convenience, and an experience that consumers cannot get from a traditional kitchen appliance.

items.content:
By Chioma Obinna
The Pharmaceutical Society of Nigeria (PSN) on Monday called for tougher punishment for manufacturers and distributors of fake drugs, proposing a minimum fine of N25 million and prison terms of between five and 20 years for offenders to deter offenders and protect public health.
Addressing a press conference ahead of the society’s 99th Annual National Conference, the PSN President, Pharm. Ayuba Tanko Ibrahim, urged the National Assembly to expedite work on the amendment of the Fake Drug Act.
Ibrahim said the existing penalties, including fines as low as N5,000 and N10,000 in some cases, were inadequate to discourage offenders operating in the lucrative counterfeit drug business.
“How can you say somebody is caught faking drugs and pays a fine of N5,000 or N10,000? So it encourages them,” he said.
The PSN president explained that the proposed amendment would prescribe a fine of not less than N25 million, imprisonment for a term of not less than five years and up to 20 years, or both, as well as forfeiture of assets where applicable, depending on the nature of the offence.
He said the society had presented its position at a recent public hearing at the Senate, expressing hope that lawmakers would accelerate the legislative process to ensure the proposed changes became law.
According to him, the profitability of counterfeit medicines makes stronger sanctions necessary, even as regulatory agencies intensify enforcement operations.
“Drug faking has come to stay. Nobody should assume that it can be eliminated because it’s a very lucrative business. So, as they are doing, we should be thinking of how to checkmate them,” Ibrahim said.
He urged the National Agency for Food and Drug Administration and Control (NAFDAC), the Pharmacy Council of Nigeria (PCN) and the Federal Ministry of Health and Social Welfare to sustain efforts to identify, arrest and prosecute those involved in the trade.
Beyond tougher punishment, Ibrahim called on federal and state governments to fully implement the National Drug Distribution Guidelines (NDDG), approved in 2015, to improve the regulation of medicine distribution and curb the circulation of fake and substandard products.
The guidelines provide for the relocation of major open drug markets to Coordinated Wholesale Centres (CWCs), where medicine distribution can be better monitored.
The PSN identified the major open drug markets in Idumota, Lagos; Head Bridge, Onitsha, Anambra State; Sabon Gari, Kano; and Ariaria, Aba, Abia State, as requiring sustained government attention under the reform.
Ibrahim said the CWC initiative had recorded progress in Kano, while projects in Lagos and Anambra required continued attention to ensure their completion and effective operation.
He added that Abia State Governor, Alex Otti, had promised support for the initiative in the state.
He urged the Federal Government to collaborate with the affected state governments to remove administrative and other obstacles delaying the establishment and operation of the centres.
According to him, effective implementation of the guidelines, alongside stronger penalties, would help strengthen the medicine supply chain and improve patient safety.
The PSN president also warned against placing the responsibility for identifying fake medicines on patients, insisting that pharmacists and other qualified professionals had a critical role to play in protecting consumers.
He said manufacturers conducted quality-control checks before releasing medicines to the market, while some companies had introduced product-verification systems to help detect suspected counterfeits.
“It is not the job of a patient to check or confirm whether a drug is fake or not. The pharmacist that showed the drug to him should be able to check if the drug is fake or not,” he said.
Ibrahim advised Nigerians to purchase medicines from registered pharmacies rather than unregulated outlets, warning that unauthorised sales of prescription medicines, including antibiotics, could expose consumers to serious health risks.
He stressed the need for public education on the safe purchase and use of medicines, noting that patent medicine vendors were subject to restrictions on the products they could legally sell.
On the rising cost of medicines, the PSN president said government incentives for pharmaceutical manufacturers would have limited impact unless authorities addressed the broader costs of local production.
He explained that reductions in import tariffs alone might not translate into cheaper medicines if manufacturers continued to face high diesel prices, electricity costs and transportation expenses.
“Unless the government takes a holistic view of the drivers of the prices of pharmaceuticals, we are not going to see any appreciable decrease in the cost of drugs,” he said.
Ibrahim urged the government to consult pharmaceutical manufacturers and their industry associations before introducing policies intended to reduce medicine prices, arguing that manufacturers could provide practical insights into the factors driving production costs.
He also called for stronger collaboration between government agencies responsible for natural-product research and pharmaceutical manufacturers to develop promising research findings into medicines for local use.
The PSN president warned that the high cost of medicines was pushing some Nigerians away from conventional healthcare towards traditional remedies, underscoring the need to improve access to affordable and quality-assured medicines.
Meanwhile, PSN National Secretary, Pharm. Gafar Madehein, cautioned Nigerians against assuming that herbal products were safe simply because they carried NAFDAC registration numbers.
He explained that a registration number issued for listing purposes did not necessarily mean that a product had undergone clinical trials demonstrating its safety and efficacy.
Madehein also warned that combining herbal remedies with conventional medicines could trigger harmful interactions, urging consumers to seek professional advice before using them together.
The pharmacists spoke ahead of the PSN’s 99th Annual National Conference, scheduled to hold in Awka, Anambra State, from November 1 to 6, 2026, under the theme, “One Health, One Pharmacy: Bridging Knowledge, Practice and Policy for National Impact.”
The conference is expected to bring together pharmacists, policymakers, regulators, researchers and other healthcare professionals to discuss pharmacy practice, clinical collaboration, education, research and pharmaceutical policy.

items.content:
If the veto is the United Nations’ original sin, Gaza is its crucifixion. After the horrific Hamas attacks of October 7, 2023, which killed some 1,200 Israelis and saw hundreds taken hostage, Israel launched a campaign that many international observers have described as genocide—tens of thousands of Palestinians killed, the overwhelming majority women and children, hospitals, schools and homes reduced to rubble, and an entire population besieged without food, water, medicine or fuel. The United Nations was powerless to stop it.
The Secretary-General, António Guterres, invoked Article 99 of the Charter—unused for decades—to warn the Council of impending catastrophe. Resolutions demanding an immediate humanitarian ceasefire, the release of all hostages and unimpeded aid were tabled, and the United States vetoed them, granting Israel diplomatic cover while the death toll climbed. When a resolution finally passed calling for a ceasefire, Israel simply ignored it. The International Court of Justice issued provisional measures ordering Israel to prevent acts of genocide and allow aid in; those measures were ignored too. The message to every small nation on earth was unmistakable: international law applies to some, but not to those protected by a permanent member of the Security Council.
Why should any nation, and least of all any African nation, respect the authority of an institution whose most powerful members treat its decisions as suggestions? Africa watched the Council fail in Rwanda and has watched it fail in the Sahel. It has seen the illegal embargo on Cuba condemned annually for 30 years and continue regardless. When resolutions are ignored, the entire edifice of international law is undermined. When the Council is paralysed, the world grows more dangerous. When the powerful are never held accountable, the weak arm themselves, and an arms race follows that makes everyone less safe. Gaza is not only a Palestinian tragedy; it is proof that the machinery built to prevent such tragedies is broken. The only remedy is accountability for all—including the most powerful. The veto must be reformed, the Council expanded, and the law applied equally. Washington must answer for its illegal sanctions on Venezuela and Cuba and for its complicity in Gaza. Every nation, however mighty, must abide by the Council’s decisions and the Court’s rulings. This is not utopianism; it is survival.
And then there was Trump, standing at the same podium where Mottley had stood, demonstrating in a single speech everything this series has argued about the arrogance of power. His address was not a statement of American policy; it was a confession of American impunity. He boasted of the capture of Venezuela’s President Nicolás Maduro—seized in a military raid on Caracas on January 3, 2026, flown to New York in chains—and declared, without a trace of irony, “to the victor belong the spoils.” He announced that the United States would “run” Venezuela until a “proper transition” could take place, and that American oil companies would “go in, spend billions of dollars, fix the badly broken infrastructure and start making money for the country.” This is not diplomacy. This is pillage dressed in the language of liberation. He then turned to Cuba, calling it “an absolutely failed state” that “will fall,” and the Cuban delegation walked out in protest. He spoke of Greenland not as a sovereign territory of the Danish kingdom but as a strategic asset to be acquired, announcing military bases on the island. And on Iran, he stood before the world and asked whether he should “annihilate the Islamic Republic” or make a deal. This is the language of empire, spoken without shame, in the very chamber built to prevent it. Yet the desperation beneath the bravado is unmistakable. A nation that must abduct presidents, threaten invasions, and boast of controlling the world’s oil is not a confident hegemon; it is a power whose grip is slipping, and it knows it.
But there is a deeper mirror that Africa must be brave enough to look into, and it concerns not the arrogance of Washington but the choices of African capitals themselves. Two nations, Nigeria and Niger, have taken opposite paths in the struggle for resource sovereignty, and the contrast is instructive. Nigeria, through its Minister of Solid Minerals Development, Dele Alake, signed a framework agreement with the United States on the sidelines of this very General Assembly, opening American access to an estimated $700 billion in mineral resources .
The minister insisted that Nigeria is not “here to remain a source of raw material for the values that others create,” and that the goal is local processing and value addition . Nigeria has signed similar frameworks with France and Australia, focused on geological data mapping, training and technology . The approach is one of “opening up while seeking dominance”—using foreign capital, but insisting on retaining control. Yet the fine print remains shrouded, and civil society has warned that without enforceable safeguards, the agreement risks reproducing the extractive model that devastated the Niger Delta, replacing oil with lithium while sacrificing lives, lands and ecosystems . Foreign capital is regarded as a tool. But a tool can become a master if the hand that wields it is weak.
Niger chose the opposite path. Prime Minister Ali Mahamane Lamine Zeine declared from the UN podium: “Our resources belong to our peoples. Our future will no longer be decided elsewhere.” He accused France of coveting Niger’s uranium, Mali and Burkina Faso’s gold, lithium, gas and oil, describing terrorism in the Sahel as “the cynical machinery of recolonisation dressed in the trappings of extremism” . Niger nationalised the French-owned SOMAÏR uranium mine in June 2025, transferring its permit to a state-owned entity, and announced that the stockpiled uranium belongs exclusively to Niger . Production restarted entirely with Nigerien workers and experts. The approach is “first recover, then discuss”—pushing foreign capital out and taking full control. But sovereignty has its costs. International arbitration orders, the loss of traditional buyers, and regional border closures have left Niger with a stockpile of yellowcake and fewer customers than it hoped . The uranium may belong to Niger, but selling it is another matter. Foreign capital is regarded as a threat. But a threat can also be a lifeline if the terms are right.
The lesson for Africa is not that one path is righteous and the other craven. It is that both are experiments in the same laboratory, conducted under the watchful eyes of former colonial powers whose interest in African resources has not diminished. Nigeria’s framework agreements and Niger’s nationalisation are two answers to the same question: how does a resource-rich nation escape the curse of extraction without surrender? The answer will not be found in Washington or Paris. It will be found in the quality of African leadership—in whether the continent can produce leaders of the calibre of Mia Amor Mottley, who stood before the assembly without notes and held it spellbound, not because she commanded armies but because she commanded facts, law and moral clarity. Her brilliance was the product of a small nation with a strong democratic tradition, a vibrant civil society and a genuine commitment to the rule of law. That is the dividend of democracy: it elevates the competent and the courageous instead of rewarding mediocrity, corruption and nepotism. Africa has produced Mandela, Nkrumah and Nyerere.
It holds today immense reservoirs of intellect and vision. What it needs is a system that lets them rise. And yes, we need more men like her in the leadership of the South—men who possess her intellect, her moral courage, her mastery of detail, and her capacity to command a room without raising her voice. The irony is not lost on those who have watched the procession of male leaders across the podiums of the Global South, many of whom have held power for decades while their people remained in darkness, while she—a woman from a small island—illuminated the path forward with nothing more than the power of her ideas.
The 81st General Assembly was a moment of reckoning—Lula, Ruto, Mahama, Shettima, Zeine, Mottley, Erdoğan and Ramaphosa demanding a new order in one chorus, while Trump demonstrated in a single speech why that order is so desperately needed. Their demands are just and their moment is now. The South must unite, build a wider coalition, bring solutions rather than grievances, hold the powerful accountable through every instrument available, and never give up. The founders of the United Nations knew this fight was worth making, and so did every leader who spoke in New York. They spoke not for themselves but for billions who long for peace, justice and dignity. The world is watching; the people are waiting; let us not disappoint them.

items.author: Nwafor
items.content:
…Open probes into NIPCO gas licences,
NNPCL executive
By Gift ChapiOdekina, Abuja
The House of Representatives Committee on Petroleum Resources (Downstream) has passed votes of confidence on President Bola Ahmed Tinubu, the Nigerian Midstream and Downstream Petroleum Regulatory Authority (NMDPRA) and industrialist Aliko Dangote, declaring that Nigeria’s drive towards energy security is gaining momentum.
The committee, however, called on the Federal Government to increase funding for pipeline surveillance, enforce domestic crude supply obligations and strengthen legislation to protect local refineries from supply disruptions and unfair competition.
Chairman of the committee, Ikenga Imo Ugochinyere, announced the votes of confidence on Monday in Abuja at the technical briefing marking the end of Downstream Week 2026.
He said the committee’s assessment of developments in the downstream petroleum sector showed improvements in domestic refining, fuel supply and pipeline security, while stressing the need for sustained government support to consolidate the gains.
Ugochinyere commended the NMDPRA Chief Executive, Rabiu Abdullahi Umar, and the authority’s executive directors for what he described as a job well done, saying the regulator had “brought stability where there was uncertainty”.
According to figures presented at the briefing, domestic refineries now contribute more than 75 per cent of national petrol supply, while the country has recorded no supply shortfalls and maintained more than 25 days of national sufficiency.
The committee also highlighted the commissioning of the Port Harcourt petroleum product laboratory, the licensing of a petroleum liquid trading exchange described as Africa’s first, and the completion of a framework for a National Strategic Stock capable of covering up to 20 days of supply.
It said plans were underway to increase the strategic reserve to 90 days in 2027.
Pipeline security, crude supply
On crude oil production, the committee expressed confidence that Nigeria could achieve its target of three million barrels per day, attributing the recent increase in output partly to improved pipeline surveillance and security.
Ugochinyere said better protection of oil infrastructure would reduce crude losses, increase feedstock availability for domestic refineries and boost government revenue.
“Fewer breaches mean less crude lost, more product for our refineries, and more revenue for the Federation,” he said.
The committee urged the Federal Government to increase funding for pipeline surveillance contractors and ensure the timely release of funds and logistics needed to sustain operations.
It commended the contractors for their contributions but maintained that improved funding and operational support would further strengthen crude oil production.
The chairman said the committee was also working on legislation to address the persistent challenge of crude oil availability to domestic refineries.
“A refinery without reliable crude is an investment at risk,” he said, stressing the need for statutory guarantees on crude supply, fair market access and a stable policy environment.
On petroleum product importation, Ugochinyere said imports should only be permitted to address verified supply shortfalls rather than serve as a permanent alternative to domestic refining.
“Our goal is balance: security of supply today, and a strong domestic refining industry for tomorrow,” he said.
The committee also disclosed that it had rejected a World Bank recommendation on import licences, insisting that Nigeria’s energy policy must reflect the country’s economic and industrial priorities.
“Nigeria’s energy policy must be written in Nigeria,” Ugochinyere said.
He added that the committee was advancing the Petroleum Industry Act (Amendment) Bill to strengthen provisions on domestic crude supply, licensing, protection of local refiners and regulation of petroleum product imports.
Dangote refinery, marketers
The committee also commended Dangote over the ongoing initial public offering of the Dangote Petroleum Refinery, describing the facility as a strategic national investment valued at about $20 billion.
Ugochinyere said the refinery had introduced fresh momentum into the downstream petroleum market, adding that the National Assembly would support measures to protect domestic refining investments while ensuring fair competition.
He also praised petroleum marketers’ associations, including the Major Oil Marketers Association of Nigeria, the Depot and Petroleum Products Marketers Association of Nigeria, the Independent Petroleum Marketers Association of Nigeria and the Petroleum Products Retail Outlets Owners Association of Nigeria.
He said the associations had invested in depots, jetties, trucks and filling stations, helping to sustain distribution and bridge supply gaps whenever domestic output fell short.
The committee said the contributions of the marketers remained important to national fuel security, particularly as Nigeria worked to expand local refining capacity.
Reps open probe into petitions
Meanwhile, the committee has established two sub-committees to investigate petitions seeking the cancellation of gas distribution licences issued to NIPCO Plc and alleging money laundering and abuse of office against NNPC Limited’s Executive Vice President, Downstream, Dr Mumuni Dagazau.
The petition against NIPCO seeks the investigation, suspension and cancellation of gas distribution licences issued by the NMDPRA to the company for Lagos, Ogun, Oyo and Osun states, as well as the Lagos and Lekki Free Trade Zones.
The petitioners have also requested a public hearing on the matter.
The committee appointed a sub-committee chaired by Mathew Nwogu, with Shehu Dalhatu as deputy, to conduct a preliminary investigation and report its findings to the main committee.
In the second petition, Dagazau was accused of money laundering and abuse of office.
The committee appointed a sub-committee chaired by Aliyu Ibrahim Al-Mustapha, with Cyril Hart as deputy, to investigate the allegations and submit its report within seven days.
Ugochinyere emphasised that the petitions had not been proven and that the committee had yet to reach any conclusion on the allegations.
“These are allegations, and the Committee has reached no conclusion on them. All parties will be given a full and fair opportunity to be heard,” he said.
He added that the committee would not ignore complaints capable of affecting public confidence in the downstream petroleum sector.
The chairman also disclosed that the committee had opened an inquiry into alleged underpayment for crude oil by some companies and questioned NNPC Limited over legacy transactions and refinery rehabilitation.
“We will not accept silence as an answer,” he said.
Neither NIPCO Plc nor Dagazau had publicly responded to the petitions as of the time of the briefing.
The committee said the investigations would proceed alongside its legislative and oversight activities aimed at strengthening transparency, accountability and efficiency in Nigeria’s petroleum industry.

items.author: Hussein Yahaya
items.content:
Senator Abdulaziz Yari, Director-General of the All Progressives Congress Presidential Campaign Council (APC-PCC) and Senator representing Zamfara West, continued his nationwide consultative tour on Monday with high-profile visits to prominent traditional rulers across Northern Nigeria.
Following Sunday engagements with the Ooni of Ife, Oba Adeyeye Enitan Ogunwusi, and the Emir of Ilorin, Alhaji (Dr.) Ibrahim Kolapo Sulu-Gambari, Senator Yari led a delegation of political heavyweights to pay royal homage to the Emirs of Gwandu, Katsina, Daura, and Zaria.
According to an official statement from his media office, the visits are part of a broad-based consultation strategy aimed at building national consensus and galvanizing support ahead of major campaign activities leading up to key dates on the 2027 electoral calendar.
During the visits, Senator Yari reaffirmed the campaign council’s profound respect for the country’s traditional institutions, describing them as essential pillars for sustaining peace, unity, and national stability.
He clarified that the visits were not primarily intended to solicit direct political endorsements, but rather to seek the prayers, moral support, and wise counsel of the royal fathers as the nation navigates its political transition.
In response, the traditional rulers in their respective palaces offered royal blessings and prayers for peaceful elections, unity, and the continued progress of Nigeria’s democratic journey.
 
Underscoring the strategic importance of the tour, Senator Yari was accompanied by a high-level delegation of prominent political figures, including Sen. Ali Modu Sheriff (Former Governor of Borno State), Dr. Abdullahi Umar Ganduje (Former Governor of Kano State), Sen. Adamu Aliero (Former Governor of Kebbi State), Sen. Sani Ahmad Yarima (Former Governor of Zamfara State), Sen. Aliyu Magatakarda Wamakko (Former Governor of Sokoto State), Sen. Muhammad Danjuma Goje (Former Governor of Gombe State)

The suspension was announced pending investigations into allegations against Ibezim and recent developments in the diocese.
The Primate also barred Ibezim from officiating at any activity of the Church of Nigeria (Anglican Communion), the Province of the Niger or the Anglican Diocese of Awka during the period of his leave.
The Bishop of Aguata Diocese, Rt. Rev. Samuel Ezeofor, was subsequently directed to oversee the Diocese of Awka and the Archdiocese on the Niger.
However, the Board of the Diocese of Awka has rejected the suspension, threatening to leave the Church of Nigeria and join the Church of England if the Primate insists on enforcing the decision.
Against this backdrop, police operatives were heavily deployed at St. Faith’s Anglican Cathedral, Awka, on Sunday as Ibezim conducted the service.
Reacting to reports about the police presence, the Police Public Relations Officer in Anambra State, SP Tochukwu Ikenga, described some accounts of the deployment as misleading.
Ikenga cautioned against what he called the misrepresentation of security interventions in ways that could heighten tensions surrounding the ecclesiastical dispute.
“The Command wishes to clarify that the deployment of police personnel to any location is guided by the need to maintain law and order, prevent a breakdown of peace, protect lives and property, and ensure the safety of all concerned, irrespective of their affiliations or positions in the dispute,” he said.
He stressed that the police presence should not be interpreted as an endorsement of any party or position in the church disagreement.
“The Nigeria Police Force remains a neutral institution committed to enforcing the law, safeguarding citizens’ rights, and preventing disputes from escalating into threats to public peace and security,” Ikenga added.
The police spokesman urged members of the public to refrain from circulating narratives capable of inflaming tensions or deepening divisions within the religious community.
He assured that the command would continue to discharge its constitutional responsibilities professionally and impartially, without fear or favour.
Ikenga added that the police would not allow any disagreement, whether religious or otherwise, to degenerate into a breach of public peace and security.

By Henry Umoru
ABUJA — The Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) has faulted the Federal Government’s warning that a return to petrol subsidy could push the naira to between N3,000 and N4,000 per dollar, demanding explanations for the failure of the country’s refineries to operate effectively.
The party also questioned why Nigeria had mortgaged a sizeable portion of its crude oil to secure foreign loans, alleging that the arrangement had affected the country’s ability to supply the Dangote Refinery with sufficient crude oil to meet domestic demand.
The NDC’s National Publicity Secretary, Osa Director, made the remarks while reacting to comments by the Minister of Finance and Coordinating Minister of the Economy, Taiwo Oyedele, who warned against a return to petrol subsidy.
Oyedele had said reinstating the subsidy could trigger capital flight, undermine investor confidence and weaken the naira to N3,000, N3,500 or even N4,000 to the dollar.
In response, Director said the government should address the underlying problems in the petroleum sector rather than focus solely on the potential consequences of restoring the subsidy.
“The most important aspect of the subsidy conversation is not yet addressed. Why are our refineries not working? Why did the APC government mortgage a sizeable portion of our crude oil to take foreign loans to the extent that we are unable to supply Dangote Refinery the needed crude oil to satisfy domestic consumption and demand?” he asked.
He argued that addressing the challenges affecting domestic refining and what he described as criminality in the subsidy regime would make the minister’s warning unnecessary.
“If all these and the criminality in the subsidy regime are addressed, the doomsday prediction of the Minister of Finance would not be necessary,” Director said.
Oyedele had issued the warning during a press briefing at the International Monetary Fund and World Bank Annual Meetings in Bangkok, Thailand, on Monday.
The minister said investors had repeatedly questioned whether the Federal Government would abandon its economic reforms ahead of the next election cycle.
He added that President Bola Tinubu had maintained that the national budget had made no provision for petrol subsidy since June 2023, insisting that the subsidy had therefore been removed.

items.author: Nwafor
items.content:
By Chioma Obinna
As competition in Nigeria’s non-alcoholic beverage market continues to evolve, Maltina, one of the country’s longstanding malt drink brands, has unveiled a refreshed visual identity to mark its 50th anniversary, retaining its familiar taste while introducing redesigned packaging across its product range.
The new identity, unveiled by Nigerian Breweries Plc last week, features updated designs across glass bottles, cans and PET bottles, with enhanced gold elements and a stronger orange colour scheme aimed at giving the brand a more contemporary appearance.
The redesign highlights a broader challenge facing established consumer brands: how to modernise their appearance to appeal to changing consumer preferences without losing the familiarity and trust built over decades.
For Maltina, which has been part of Nigeria’s beverage market since 1976, the anniversary presents an opportunity to reinforce its heritage while repositioning the brand for a new generation of consumers.
However, beyond the visual changes, the success of the refresh will depend on how consumers respond to the new packaging and whether the brand can sustain its relevance in an increasingly competitive market.
Other features of the refreshed identity include a gold crown cork, brighter sunrays, a more prominent golden barley icon, a bolder calcium coin and a “Since 1976” heritage mark, underscoring the brand’s five-decade history in Nigeria.
Despite the packaging changes, Nigerian Breweries said Maltina’s familiar taste and nutritional composition remain unchanged.
The company said the drink is fortified with calcium, with one 33cl bottle providing the equivalent of half a glass of milk. The brand is also endorsed by the Nutrition Society of Nigeria as a non-alcoholic drink rich in Vitamin A.
Speaking on the refreshed identity, the Marketing Director of Nigerian Breweries Plc, Sarah Agha, said the redesign was intended to keep the brand relevant to contemporary consumers while preserving its heritage.
“For 50 years, Maltina has grown alongside generations of Nigerians. This refreshed identity is an evolution of a much-loved brand, designed to keep Maltina fresh, relevant and connected to today’s consumers while preserving the nourishing taste they know and trust,” Agha said.
Her remarks reflect the company’s effort to balance continuity with change, maintaining the product attributes familiar to existing consumers while introducing a new visual experience that could attract younger buyers.
For established brands, packaging plays an important role in consumer recognition, influencing how products stand out on retail shelves and how customers relate to them. A redesign, therefore, must do more than create a different appearance; it must preserve the identity that consumers associate with the product.
Maltina’s decision to retain its taste and nutritional composition while updating its packaging suggests that the company is seeking to refresh its market appeal without altering the product experience on which its reputation has been built.
As part of the relaunch, Nigerian Breweries is introducing a consumer engagement campaign tagged “What’s Your Word?”, inviting Nigerians to describe their first impressions of the new packaging in one word.
According to Agha, the campaign is intended to involve consumers in shaping the brand’s next chapter by encouraging them to share their reactions to the refreshed identity.
“This relaunch is about more than a new pack. It is an invitation for Nigerians to help shape the next chapter of a brand that has been part of their lives for five decades. We look forward to hearing the words the new Maltina inspires,” she added.

items.author: Nwafor
items.content:
The Catholic Bishops Conference of Nigeria, CBCN, has declared a nationwide prayer and fasting programme to promote free, fair, credible and peaceful elections in 2027.
The programme, themed ‘Let Justice and Peace Flow’, is drawn from Amos 5:24.
The bishops announced the initiative in a statement signed by their President, Archbishop Matthew Ndagoso, and Secretary, Bishop Peter Odetoyinbo, yesterday in Abuja.
They said the programme was necessary as Nigeria approached the 2027 general elections amid recurring challenges of electoral violence, rigging, vote-buying and ethno-religious divisions.
The bishops urged dioceses, parishes, church societies, prayer groups, families and individuals to participate actively in the spiritual exercise.
They said the initiative was aimed at seeking God’s guidance for electoral officials and security personnel to discharge their responsibilities faithfully, while inspiring citizens to vote conscientiously and discouraging electoral malpractice and violence.
According to the statement, all parishes would observe October 31 and November 28 as days of prayer and fasting for Nigeria.
Activities would include fasting, the Rosary procession, Holy Mass and the recitation of the CBCN prayer for the 2027 elections.
The bishops also designated December 8, the Solemnity of the Immaculate Conception of the Blessed Virgin Mary, as a nationwide diocesan day of prayer.
The programme would begin with Holy Mass at 3 p.m., presided over by the diocesan bishop, during which a pastoral letter titled “2027 Elections: Call to Responsible Choice and Action” would be read.
The Mass would be followed by a Rosary procession to the cathedral at 4:30 p.m. and conclude with Eucharistic Benediction.
The statement further declared January 15, 2027, the eve of the general elections, a nationwide parish day of prayer and fasting.
The bishops urged Nigerians to reject tribalism, corruption, bribery and voter apathy, while encouraging citizens to vote and protect their votes peacefully.
They called for a credible electoral process free from rancour and bloodshed.

The union said the intervention reflected its commitment to giving back to society and supporting people facing difficult circumstances.

The Director-General of All Progressives Congress, APC, Presidential Campaign Council, PCC, Senator Abdulaziz Yari, has said President Bola Tinubu should not be blamed solely for the widespread insecurity in the country.
Yari, who stated this during a visit to Kebbi, where he met with Governor Nasir Idris, traditional rulers and other party leaders in Birnin Kebbi, Kebbi State, yesterday, said ex-President Muhammadu Buhari, a retired general, did his best but could not tackle insecurity completely.
He acknowledged the security challenges facing the country but maintained that the Tinubu administration was making efforts to address them.
He recalled that former President Muhammadu Buhari, a retired Army general, had also made efforts to tackle insecurity during his administration, although the challenge was not completely eliminated.
“If a retired general did his best but could not completely tackle insecurity, what do you expect of President Tinubu, who is not a general? Nevertheless, the President has done his utmost best to address the security challenges confronting the country,” he said.
Yari also urged Nigerians to reflect on their relationship with God, noting that addressing insecurity required collective responsibility alongside government efforts.
He commended the governor and other APC leaders for their efforts in mobilising support for the party, expressing confidence that their collective commitment would ensure victory for Tinubu and other APC candidates in 2027.
“We are leading the campaign for the President’s re-election and other candidates of our party. We appreciate you for bringing the emirs together under one umbrella at the Emir of Gwandu’s palace.
“We recognise what you are doing as governors and your contributions towards ensuring victory for our party in 2027,” he said.
Yari said the campaign council would work with all individuals and groups committed to Tinubu’s re-election, regardless of their positions, to achieve the party’s objectives.
He expressed confidence in the APC’s chances in Kebbi, citing the support observed during his visit to the state.
On the economy, he said the hardship being experienced by Nigerians was not peculiar to the country, adding that inflation had declined and fertiliser prices reduced.
He said the federal government was implementing measures to ease the burden on citizens, including cash transfers to vulnerable households.
According to him, the measures are intended to strengthen the economy and improve living conditions for Nigerians.
Yari acknowledged that governments worldwide faced challenges, citing the United States and Saudi Arabia as examples of countries still working to address various national concerns.
He urged Nigerians to appreciate the efforts of the Tinubu administration and support its development agenda.
In his response, Governor Idris described the visit by the PCC delegation as a welcome development, expressing happiness over the gathering of APC leaders and traditional rulers to receive the team.
He said the emirs decided to come together at the palace to demonstrate solidarity and welcome the delegation.
Idris said Kebbi had benefited from federal government projects under Tinubu’s administration, adding that the development initiatives had strengthened the state’s support for the President.
“We have no reason not to support the President. We have prominent leaders such as Sen. Atiku Bagudu, Sen. Adamu Aliero and Amb. Saidu Dakingari.
“You have seen the people of Kebbi and their overwhelming support. We are for the APC and we are for President Tinubu,” Idris said.
The governor expressed confidence that the state would continue to support the APC ahead of the 2027 general elections.

items.author: Henry Oduah
items.content:
By Sola Ogundipe
Medical doctors, scientists and teachers are the most trusted professions globally, while politicians and social media influencers rank among the least trusted, according to a survey of 23,530 online adults under 75 across 32 countries.
The survey, known as the Ipsos Global Trustworthiness Index 2026, conducted by Ipsos, an international market research and public opinion polling company, showed that doctors lead the rankings, with 58 percent of respondents expressing trust in them, followed by scientists at 56 percent and teachers at 54 percent.
Restaurant serving staff ranked fourth at 44 percent, followed by the armed forces at 43 percent. Police officers, judges and ordinary men and women each recorded 38 percent, while lawyers received 31 percent.
Television news anchors recorded 30 percent, while pollsters and clergy or priests each scored 29 percent. Taxi drivers and civil servants followed at 28 percent. Journalists and bankers each recorded 27 percent, while business leaders scored 26 percent.
At the lower end, government ministers recorded 20 per cent, followed by advertising executives at 19 per cent. Social media influencers and politicians generally ranked last, with 15 per cent each.
The percentages represent the share of respondents expressing trust in each profession or group, not those selecting it as their single most trusted occupation. The precise survey question and response options should be verified against the original Ipsos report.
The findings highlight a marked contrast between trust in health and scientific professionals and confidence in political figures and social surveys.
