items.author: Henry Oduah
items.content:
A Kenyan court has convicted pastor Paul Mackenzie of murdering 191 people, including 190 children, after he allegedly directed members of his religious group to starve themselves and their children to death to “meet Jesus”.
The BBC reported on Monday that 28 other leaders of the religious group were also convicted of murder. All the defendants had pleaded not guilty, repeatedly maintaining that nobody had been forced to die.
Delivering an eight-hour judgement in the coastal city of Mombasa, Justice Diana Mochache said Mackenzie’s followers regarded him as “Jesus’s mouthpiece”.
According to the report, one of Mackenzie’s co-accused told the court that the pastor had instructed followers to use violence against anyone who refused to fast.
The co-accused said anyone who “resisted the directive to fast must be forced to go to heaven through kicks and blows”.
The judge also revealed that burials in the forest where the group operated were referred to as “weddings”, with those who died described as people who “were celebrated as having wedded with Jesus”.
The court heard that 17 men from a nearby town were hired to excavate shallow graves in the forest, with some reportedly receiving as little as $8 (£6) a day.
One of the gravediggers, identified as James, recounted the disturbing discoveries made during the exercise.
“Every grave we found had at least three bodies,” James told the BBC. “Some of the remains were of children as young as a few weeks old.”
He added, “We once found 12 bodies of children in a line inside a grave. It was massive, the bodies were arranged like clothes. One on top of another.”
The workers also reported finding children whose “hands and legs tied and bodies wrapped in bedsheets”.
Another gravedigger, Salim Karisa, said some of the victims were known to residents of neighbouring Shakahola town, as members of the group regularly visited to purchase supplies and collect water from the River Galana.
“We would sometimes carry people on our motorbikes into the forest. But it was so planned and secretive that nobody could tell what was happening inside,” Karisa said.
Mackenzie established Good News International Ministries in 2003, building a following of thousands over the next 16 years through church branches across Kenya.
The church also ran a television station, Times TV, which aired his sermons from Malindi. His teachings reportedly described education as “evil”, healthcare as “against the doctrine” and digital identity cards as “the mark of the devil”.
Mackenzie’s son, Dan Paul Mackenzie, said he worked as a cameraperson for the church and recalled how worship services were organised.
“The children would sit at the back, adults in the middle, and everyone would sing worship songs all morning,” he said.
The pastor usually began preaching at noon, with some sessions featuring what was described as “casting out demons”.
After the church’s main branch shut down in 2019, Mackenzie relocated to Shakahola forest and encouraged his followers to move there.
Among those who followed him was Peter Shukrani, 23, who relocated to the forest with his mother. He had joined the church at the age of eight and considered Mackenzie his “spiritual father”.
Despite his experiences, Shukrani said he would “never say a bad word about him”.
However, he fell ill while living in the forest, where medication was prohibited. His condition worsened after his mother discarded the medicines he needed.
“My mother would throw away all the medicine I was supposed to take because she believe that only God could heal me,” Shukrani said.
He described the group’s living conditions, saying members stayed in mud houses scattered across the expansive forest.
“We lived a quiet normal life, fasting for a few days then having a small meal,” he said.
The first bodies were discovered by local herders in March 2023, by which time hundreds of people had reportedly died.
Karisa said some victims were so severely weakened by starvation that they died while being transported out of the forest.
“We would carry someone out of the forest but they were so frail that they would die in our arms,” he said.
Shukrani was among those rescued. He said he had been bedridden for weeks before his rescue and believed he would not have survived without intervention.
“My mother believed Pastor Mackenzie’s doctrine that medicine was evil. I would have died if I wasn’t rescued from Shakahola forest,” he said.
Many of the recovered bodies remain unidentified because of decomposition. Court records reportedly identify several victims as “unknown male child”, using the locations of their graves and the dates of discovery to distinguish them.
Despite accounts of starvation, strangulation and bludgeoning among the victims, Shukrani continued to defend Mackenzie before the verdict.
He described the pastor as “a good person who cares for me”.
“Mackenzie didn’t force anyone to fast. People made those choices by themselves because of their beliefs. I still love him and he is still my pastor,” Shukrani said.
Dan Mackenzie, however, argued before the ruling that his father should be held responsible for the deaths because of his leadership position within the group.
“He was the leader, he was someone who they were looking [up to]. So he is a murderer of mass killing,” he said.

It added that some candidates were also disqualified over irregularities identified in their selection process.
The NCS urged affected applicants who believe they were unfairly disqualified to submit their details and complaints to helpdesk@customs.gov.ng for review.
It said applicants seeking reconsideration would be subjected to fresh screening, stressing that the review would not automatically guarantee admission into the training college.
The Service further warned that applicants found to have engaged in criminal conduct, including certificate fraud and other offences, would be referred for appropriate legal action and prosecution.
It urged the affected candidates and the general public to remain calm and use the designated channel to submit their complaints.

items.author: Henry Oduah
items.content:
James Maddison made a sensational return to Tottenham’s starting line-up after 17 months away on Monday as Spurs beat Coventry 3-1 to claim their long-awaited first Premier League win of the season.
The England midfielder has featured only fleetingly since May 2025, when he suffered the first of two serious knee injuries.
But Maddison needed less than a quarter of an hour to put Spurs ahead at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium with a stunning first-time strike from outside the penalty area.
Jack Rudoni levelled early in the second half but the home side were back in front just before the hour mark when Omar Marmoush lashed home his first goal for the club and substitute Ben Davies made the points safe late on.
Roberto De Zerbi’s team came into the match bottom of the Premier League and with the unwanted record of being the only team in England’s top six divisions without a league win this season despite a huge summer spend.
The Spurs boss had taken his squad to Marbella in southern Spain for some warm-weather training in a bid to kickstart their season.
He named Maddison in his starting line-up while Sweden midfielder Dejan Kulusevski returned to the matchday squad for the first time in 17 months.
Maddison ruptured the anterior cruciate ligament in his right knee in August 2025, just three months after injuring the same knee.
The 29-year-old wasted little time in making his mark, putting his side ahead in the 14th minute in spectacular style after fine work from Mohammed Kudus on the right.
Maddison, lurking just outside the penalty area, received the ball from Kudus and sent it curling past Coventry goalkeeper Carl Rushworth and into the top corner, sparking wild scenes of delight among the home fans.
Tottenham now had their tails up and threatened to overwhelm the visitors but Frank Lampard’s newly promoted Coventry, who had won their previous two games, re-established a foothold.
Maddison went close to putting Spurs 2-0 after half an hour but his half-cross, half-shot curled narrowly wide.
But they failed to stretch their lead and Coventry were level in the 49th minute, courtesy of a Rudoni strike from close range.
Spurs lost the ball in the Coventry half and the visitors swept forward. Rudoni’s cross hit a teammate but the ball fell kindly for him and he drove home.
Just nine minutes later Spurs were back in front when former Manchester City forward Marmoush held off Milan van Ewijk before unleashing an unstoppable shot.
Kulusevski, who suffered a knee injury in May 2025, was introduced in the final minutes to a huge ovation from the home fans.
Spurs veteran Davies made the three points safe deep into added time, poking home from the edge of the penalty area as Tottenham could at last relax.
AFP

Florida’s top prosecutor announced an arrest warrant Monday for former Cuban president Raul Castro on state murder charges that echo a federal indictment unveiled earlier this year.
Raul Castro, 95, is wanted on murder charges connected to the February 24, 1996 shooting down of two civilian aircraft from “Brothers to the Rescue,” an organization assisting Cubans fleeing to the US state by sea.
“Raul Castro ordered the murder of four Floridians in cold blood, and Florida will never stop pursuing accountability for that communist conspiracy,” Florida Attorney General James Uthmeier said in a statement.
Castro, brother of the late revolutionary leader and US nemesis Fidel Castro, was indicted on federal charges related to the incident in May.
The move came as President Donald Trump’s right-wing administration steadily ramped up economic, political and legal pressure on the Cuban communist government.
“We’re committed to pursuing every lawful, prosecutable avenue to bring accountability, including parallel federal and state prosecutions,” US Attorney Jason A. Reding Quinones said in a statement supporting Florida’s action.
“We’re proud to stand with Florida in seeking justice for the four Americans murdered in the Brothers to the Rescue shootdown nearly 30 years ago,” the federal prosecutor said.
In a statement on X, Cuba’s Foreign Minister Bruno Rodriguez condemned “the latest futile maneuver by anti-Cuban politicians in South Florida,” which he said was a “reflection of political rot and moral collapse.”
Trump previously seized on a US indictment to justify military action in January that toppled Venezuela’s then-president Nicolas Maduro, a staunch ally of the Cuban authorities.
Current Cuban President Miguel Diaz-Canel has said the US federal indictment against Castro has “no legal basis” and was an attempt “to justify the folly of a military aggression against Cuba.”
AFP

items.content:
By Johnbosco Agbakwuru
The Indigenous People of Biafra (IPOB) has urged the British Government to use its diplomatic channels to press Nigeria to hear the pending appeal of its leader, Mazie Nnamdi Kanu, without further delay.
In a statement on Monday signed by its spokesperson, Emma Powerful, IPOB said the British Government should engage Nigerian authorities over the delay in the hearing of Kanu’s appeal and other related cases.
The group questioned Britain’s response to Kanu’s legal situation, arguing that its stated policy of assisting British nationals detained abroad when internationally accepted standards are not met should inform its engagement with Nigeria.
IPOB asked the British Government to explain how Kanu’s treatment aligns with international standards on legality, due process and fundamental human rights.
The group raised five issues, including Kanu’s rendition from Kenya to Nigeria in June 2021, the Court of Appeal’s judgment of October 13, 2022, his conviction in November 2025, the status of some charges and the delay in hearing his appeal.
On his rendition, IPOB cited Opinion No. 25/2022 of the United Nations Working Group on Arbitrary Detention, which it said called for Kanu’s immediate release.
It also questioned the subsequent proceedings against him in light of the Court of Appeal’s judgment, which discharged him on specified counts.
The group further challenged the legal basis of Kanu’s conviction, arguing that the terrorism legislation underlying the charges had been repealed. It cited Section 36(12) of the Nigerian Constitution, which provides that a person cannot be convicted of a criminal offence unless the offence and its penalty are prescribed in a written law.
IPOB also questioned the inclusion of counts it said had previously been discharged by the Court of Appeal, arguing that the issues required clarification in the ongoing legal process.
On the delayed appeal, the group urged Britain to make representations to the Nigerian Government to ensure that the case is heard promptly.
IPOB maintained that diplomatic representations over due process, human rights and delays in judicial proceedings would not amount to interference in Nigeria’s judicial independence.
It said it was not asking Britain to dictate the outcome of the case but to use its diplomatic engagement to encourage the timely hearing of Kanu’s appeal.
The group called on the British Government to press Nigeria to list and hear the appeal, alongside related cases before the relevant courts, without further delay.
Kanu was convicted on terrorism-related charges in November 2025 and sentenced to life imprisonment. His legal team has challenged his conviction.
IPOB said the British Government should demonstrate its commitment to protecting its citizens by seeking a prompt hearing of the pending appeal.

By Hadiza Yusuf
A chieftain of the All Progressives Congress (APC), Dr Musa Iliyasu Kwankwaso, has said former Vice President Atiku Abubakar cannot rely on ethnic and religious sentiments to win support in northern Nigeria ahead of the 2027 presidential election.
Kwankwaso said political dynamics in the North had changed, arguing that voters were increasingly concerned about leadership performance, development and issues affecting their daily lives.
He made the position known in a signed statement on Monday.
He insisted that Atiku lacked the level of acceptance and political influence once enjoyed in the region by the late President Muhammadu Buhari.
“Atiku is not Buhari. He does not possess the size, stature and acceptance of the late Nigerian President to pose a threat to Asiwaju Bola Ahmed Tinubu,” Kwankwaso said.

“The North has gone beyond primordial sentiment, and his penchant for relying on the ethno-religious card will certainly fail him,” he said.

He argued that the former vice president had yet to present a convincing account of the development achievements from his time in office.
He maintained that the 2027 election would be shaped by voters’ expectations of better leadership and improved living conditions rather than ethnic or religious loyalties.
The APC chieftain further alleged that Atiku’s political associates were aware of his limited influence among Hausa-Fulani voters.
Kwankwaso expressed confidence that President Bola Ahmed Tinubu would remain a strong contender in the North despite efforts by opposition groups to build a regional coalition against him.

items.author: Laura
items.content:
Disinformation surrounding DRC-Rwanda relations has weakened the diplomatic and public standing of both countries
Originally published on Global Voices
Featured image from DRC media, created using screenshots from ACP's YouTube channel
This post is part of Global Voices’ October 2026 Spotlight series, “Big Tech and Authoritarianism.” In this Spotlight, we explore how Big Tech facilitates and hinders authoritarian governments and practices, and how these choices influence the Global South. You can support this coverage by donating here.
In September 2026, Anthropic, an artificial intelligence (AI) development and research company, exposed a network of fake news sites targeting the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC). The investigation revealed that large-scale, AI-powered disinformation campaigns have emerged at a time of conflict when trust in the news is already at an all-time low and resources are severely limited.
This revelation rang alarm bells for African media watchdogs. The network coordinated around 70 AI-powered fake news sites and generated at least 318 articles on the eastern DRC conflict, relations with Rwanda, and contested mineral resources. The operation was highly robust.
On X, coordinated accounts amplified content from the AI-run sites, mimicking legitimate media outlets and rewriting articles for different audiences.
According to Anthropic’s report, the LKM Company, a French advertising agency serving clients with strong interests in the DRC-Rwanda conflict, was behind it all. They found no evidence of direct government involvement.
When Global Voices approached Hobab Watukalusu, a fact-checker, editor, and head of the training and research department at Soma Média Lab in Kinshasa, the capital of the Democratic Republic of the Congo, he shared:
Nous n’avions pas identifié cette opération dans toute son ampleur avant sa révélation. Cela montre les limites auxquelles nous sommes confrontés face à des campagnes capables de produire, à très grande échelle et dans des délais très courts, des contenus qui peuvent paraître crédibles et s’insérer rapidement dans l’écosystème informationnel.
We hadn’t recognized the full extent of the operation before this revelation. This highlights our limitations when dealing with campaigns that can rapidly generate large-scale, credible-looking content and quickly gain a foothold in the infoscape.
He added that local journalists on the front lines are struggling to keep up as new technologies make it easier than ever to facilitate massive disinformation campaigns.
Fact-checking obstacles
DR Congolese fact-checkers face a litany of obstacles in slowing disinformation flows across regions. Hobab outlines the fundamental constraints:
L'accès encore difficile à l'électricité, à une connexion Internet stable et abordable, ainsi que le coût élevé de la vie constituent des contraintes réelles pour les professionnels de l'information.
Ongoing difficulties in accessing electricity, stable and affordable internet connections, and high living costs pose real-world constraints for journalists.
In the DRC, where journalists are already overwhelmed by covering an active military conflict, analyzing potential industrial-scale, AI-generated content is virtually impossible.
Joël Kaseso, another journalist covering disinformation narratives, told Global Voices:
Des ressources existent, mais la plupart sont payantes. Ce qui limite notre capacité à tout analyser dans ce contexte tendu où les relations diplomatiques et sécuritaires avec les pays voisins, notamment le Rwanda, ne sont plus au bon fixe.
Although resources exist, most are not free. Amid this tense environment, where diplomatic and security relations with neighboring countries, particularly Rwanda, are strained, this financial barrier limits our ability to conduct a full analysis.
Kaseso has also identified a simple but critical methodology that most journalists use to navigate this situation: analyzing the author’s intentions, the source’s profile (anonymous accounts versus identifiable influencers), and amplification patterns. However, this requires time and tools that many newsrooms don’t have.
The challenge extends far beyond detection. Hobab explains:
Détecter qu'un contenu a été généré ou manipulé à l'aide de l'intelligence artificielle ne constitue que la première étape. Il faut ensuite déterminer si ce contenu est trompeur, identifier sa source, comprendre comment il se diffuse et, surtout, établir dans quel objectif il a été produit. C'est cette chaîne complète de vérification qui demande du temps, des compétences et des ressources.
Detecting AI-generated or AI-manipulated content is only the first step. The next steps involve determining whether the content is misleading, identifying its source, understanding how it spreads, and, above all, establishing why it was created in the first place. This comprehensive verification process requires time, skill, and resources.
The resource gap is pivotal. It ultimately determines who controls the narrative during a crisis. While an AI-powered operation can generate 318 targeted articles in just a few days, a genuine newsroom must verify its sources, contact those involved, corroborate images, and provide context, all of which can take weeks.
When disinformation becomes a weapon
The Anthropic report revealed another major threat jeopardizing investigative reporting in the DRC. Accusations of disinformation can themselves become weapons of censorship. Hobab points out a troubling precedent:
Il existe malheureusement des cas où les accusations de désinformation ou de diffusion de fausses informations ont été utilisées dans des procédures visant des journalistes. Le cas de Stanis Bujakera est particulièrement révélateur de cette tension.
Unfortunately, accusations of spreading disinformation and fake news have been weaponized in legal proceedings against some journalists. Stanis Bujakera’s case is a prime example.
In September 2023, DR Congolese journalist Stanis Bujakera was arrested for spreading false information. In March 2024, the court subsequently sentenced him, raising serious concerns among press freedom organizations.
The current state of affairs complicates fact-checkers’ work and could stifle journalists’ efforts. When asked how media personnel can combat genuine disinformation without giving governments a new tool to silence their critics, Hobab stated:
Pour éviter que les politiques de lutte contre la désinformation ne deviennent elles-mêmes des instruments de répression, il faut mettre en place des mécanismes de régulation réellement indépendants et transparents. Le risque est de transformer une réponse à un problème informationnel en un nouveau problème pour la liberté de la presse.
To prevent anti-disinformation policies from becoming instruments of repression themselves, establishing truly independent, transparent regulatory mechanisms is vital. Solutions to information-related problems risk becoming another threat to press freedom.
Diplomatic impact
Although Hobab remained cautious about claiming direct causality, he noted that the 318 AI-generated articles had a tangible impact on the region. As Joël Kaseso put it:
Oui, la désinformation autour des relations RDC-Rwanda a beaucoup fragilisé la position diplomatique et publique congolaise. Cela a alimenté une haine envers les Rwandais et renforcé des faux récits sur le Rwanda.
Yes, disinformation surrounding DRC-Rwanda relations has significantly weakened the DRC’s diplomatic and public standing, fueling hatred towards Rwandans and reinforcing false narratives about Rwanda.
Heavy exposure to biased, manipulated, and highly emotional narratives, often framed as “true patriotism,” makes it harder to distinguish verified information from propaganda. Hobab also points out specific political consequences: measures affecting universities in AFC/M23-controlled areas and restrictions that Burundi announced on entry from M23-controlled areas.
Ces décisions illustrent à quel point le contexte sécuritaire et informationnel régional peut avoir des répercussions concrètes sur la vie des populations.
These decisions illustrate just how much the regional security and information landscape impacts people’s lives.
In Rwanda, the situation seems much the same. Manzi (a pseudonym), a Rwandan journalist, explains:
Au Rwanda, nous constatons que la désinformation pro-RDC circule largement. Les citoyens rwandais sont exposés à des récits qui dépeignent le Rwanda comme occupant militaire, ce qui renforce les divisions. Mais un défi demeure. Ici, distinguer entre désinformation malveillante et critique légitime devient politiquement chargé.
In Rwanda, DRC disinformation circulates widely. Rwandan citizens are exposed to narratives portraying Rwanda as a military occupier, deepening divisions. However, one challenge remains. Here, distinguishing between malicious disinformation and legitimate criticism becomes politically charged.
Encouraging initiatives
Despite the challenges, DR Congolese journalists are actively working to build effective resistance techniques. Hobab mentioned Kinshasa News Lab, a newly formed space where fact-checkers, media professionals, and media literacy educators meet to discuss the causes of disinformation and possible solutions. Joël Kaseso also noted partnerships producing measurable results:
Les collaborations avec l'IFCN et Meta nous ont beaucoup aidés à combattre les faux récits autour des relations RDC-Rwanda. Le signalement des comptes propagandistes et des trolls a vraiment fait diminuer la désinformation.
Our collaborations with the IFCN [the International Fact-Checking Network] and Meta have helped combat false narratives surrounding DRC-Rwanda relations. Reporting propaganda accounts and trolls has really helped reduce disinformation.
He also lists freely available tools that do not require any expensive licenses: InVID We Verify, Google Image Search, Yandex, Hive Moderation, and Zero GPT to detect AI-generated content.
Training journalists in fact-checking has enabled them to critically analyze online content and distinguish fact from fiction. However, according to Hobab, this training remains insufficient. He warns:
Le défi n'est plus seulement d'apprendre aux journalistes à vérifier l'information classique. Il faut désormais les préparer à comprendre les mécanismes de l'IA générative, les réseaux de diffusion, les campagnes coordonnées et les nouvelles formes de manipulation.
The challenge is no longer just a matter of teaching journalists how to fact-check conventional information. We must now help them understand how generative AI works, how information spreads, how coordinated campaigns operate, and new forms of manipulation.
Instrumentalizing fact-checking poses yet another threat. Fact-checking is the ultimate safeguard for verified information. However, if it instead becomes a tool in the political, economic, or institutional sphere, it loses much of its credibility.

items.summary:

This is the same privilege available to members of the National Assembly.

The Senate also approved a Criminal Laws Amendment Bill.

items.author: Business Desk
items.content:
The Federal Board of Revenue (FBR) has suspended two senior tax officials for 120 days following a pen-down strike call against the government’s proposed restructuring plan, ProPakistani has learnt.
The suspended officers are Commissioner Inland Revenue Regional Tax Office (RTO) Zone-I Hyderabad, and Additional Commissioner Inland Revenue RTO Sargodha.
Separate FBR notifications dated October 19, 2026, confirm that both suspensions took effect immediately under the Civil Servants (Efficiency and Discipline) Rules, 2020.
During the suspension period, both officers must report daily to the office of the FBR Member Administration and Human Resources. Their attendance will be recorded at 9 AM, noon, and 4 PM, and they must maintain punctuality.
Earlier, strong opposition was announced by the Inland Revenue Association against FBR restructuring. The association had announced a pen-down strike but later withdrew the call after a meeting with FBR’s Member Administration and Member Operations.
Sources said Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif had expressed displeasure over the strike announcement.
The government is also considering establishing dedicated sales tax zones within the FBR’s Large Taxpayer Offices and Corporate Tax Offices to improve monitoring, enforcement, and compliance.
Apparently the sales tax gap is larger than those for income tax and federal excise duty.
Other proposed changes include expanding the FBR chairman’s powers over appointments and removals and hiring professionals from the private sector. These measures may require amendments to relevant civil service rules.
The prime minister has also called for action against corrupt officials and said employees who improve their conduct and performance should be given an opportunity to reform. He warned that continued corruption and persistently poor performance would not be tolerated.

items.title: Geological Engineering Scholarships in Canada With CAD $40,000 Per Year
items.summary:
University of British Columbia (UBC) in Canada has opened applications for its Doctor of Philosophy (PhD) in Geological Engineering, offering eligible full-time doctoral students a minimum annual funding package of CAD 40,000.
The university provides this financial support for the first four years, bringing the minimum funding package to CAD 160,000. Both Canadian and international students, including Pakistani applicants, can qualify after they are admitted.
UBC has set January 15, 2027, as the application deadline for the September 2027 intake.
The research-based program covers geological hazards, geotechnical engineering, groundwater management, environmental geology, and rock mechanics. Students conduct independent research and complete a doctoral dissertation.

Doctor of Philosophy in Geological Engineering Scholarship Benefits
The University of British Columbia guarantees a minimum funding package of CAD 40,000 annually for eligible full-time PhD students at its Vancouver campus.
The funding commitment covers the first four years of doctoral study, providing at least CAD 160,000 during that period.
UBC introduced the increased minimum funding requirement in September 2026. The policy applies to both Canadian and international doctoral students.
Financial support can come from university scholarships, external awards, teaching assistantships, research assistantships, and graduate academic assistantships.
According to UBC’s funding statistics for September 2024 to August 2025, Geological Engineering PhD students included in its analysis received a median annual gross funding of CAD 40,549.
Tuition Fees and Additional Financial Support
UBC charges tuition fees for its Geological Engineering PhD program. The university currently lists annual tuition of approximately CAD 10,081.65 for international students and CAD 5,738.52 for domestic students.
Eligible international students can receive an International Tuition Award worth up to CAD 3,200 annually.
The Department of Earth, Ocean and Atmospheric Sciences also publishes Faculty of Science tuition awards as part of its doctoral funding arrangements.
Its 2026–27 funding table includes tuition support for eligible doctoral students, although the exact award breakdown depends on student status and funding conditions.
Eligibility Criteria for UBC Geological Engineering PhD Scholarship
Applicants must meet UBC’s general doctoral admission requirements and the specific academic standards established for Geological Engineering.
The university normally expects candidates to hold a master’s degree in Applied Science, Engineering, or a related discipline, with clear evidence of research ability or potential.
The program also normally requires an undergraduate background in engineering. However, the program director can consider candidates with sufficient relevant engineering work experience.
UBC generally requires a minimum academic average in the B+ range, equivalent to approximately 76%, although individual graduate programs can apply higher admission standards.

items.title: Punjab Announces New Timings for Non-Formal Schools
items.summary:
The Punjab government has revised school timings for non-formal schools across the province, with the new schedule taking effect immediately and remaining in force until March 31, 2027.
According to an order issued by the Directorate General of Literacy and Non-Formal Basic Education on October 19, non-formal schools will operate from 8:45 AM to 12:45 PM, Monday through Saturday.
The order, issued with the approval of the competent authority, allows district officials to adjust school timings on a case-by-case basis to accommodate the needs of the target population.
The directorate has instructed districts to update the revised timings on the Non-Formal Education Management Information System (NFEMIS) portal immediately.
It has also directed all District Education Officers (Literacy) across Punjab to ensure full compliance with the new schedule. The order applies to non-formal schools across the province and replaces the previous timings until the end of March 2027.

items.author: Gaurav Bagur
items.content:
Ahead of opening its public issue on Wednesday (October 19), telecom major Jio Platforms has raised ₹8,109.8 Cr from anchor investors.
The company allotted 7.25 Cr equity shares to anchor investors at a price of ₹1,119 per share, the upper end of its price band.
Around 2.48 Cr shares, more than a third of the overall, were picked up by 25 domestic mutual funds via a total of 95 schemes. Domestic mutual funds that anchored Jio’s IPO were SBI Mutual Funds, HDFC Mutual Fund, ICICI Prudential Mutual Fund, Aditya Birla Sun Life Mutual Fund, Kotak Mahindra Mutual Fund, among others.
Besides, 97 Lakh equity shares (13.4% of the anchor round) were picked up by insurance companies and pension funds including Life Insurance Corporation of India, HDFC Life Insurance, SBI Life Insurance, and ICICI Prudential Life Insurance.
Global investors such as Fidelity, Allianz, BlackRock, Government of Singapore, Abu Dhabi Investment Authority, Goldman Sachs also picked up stakes in Jio ahead of its IPO.
Earlier in the day, it was reported that the anchor book has attracted demand of more than 30X its size. As per reports, Jio commands a grey market premium of ₹260, indicating a potential premium listing. The company is expected to get listed on the bourses on October 28.
The IPO, which comprises a fresh issue of up to 27 Cr equity shares, will open for public subscription on October 21 and close on October 23.
Jio is seeking to raise ₹30,213 Cr at the upper end of the price band, making it India’s largest public offering till date. This pricing would imply a valuation of ₹10.3 Lakh Cr for the telecom major.
The company expects to use the fresh capital generated from the IPO to reduce its subsidiary, Reliance Jio Infocomm Ltd’s (RJIL), net debt and interest burden, and improve its leverage.
The proposed repayment covers three external commercial borrowing (ECB) facilities worth a combined ₹29,971 Cr, secured from a consortium of Indian and international lenders, including SBI, Bank of America and First Abu Dhabi Bank.
The loans were originally raised to fund 5G infrastructure deployment and spectrum acquisition, with repayments scheduled between March and June 2028. Their interest rates range from 1.40% to 5.13% per annum.
The remaining proceeds earmarked for general corporate purposes may be used for strategic initiatives, growth opportunities, capital expenditure, working capital, marketing and other business requirements.
Jio Platforms reported a 9.2% YoY increase in consolidated net profit to ₹7,764 Cr in Q1 FY27, from ₹7,110 Cr a year earlier. Operating revenue rose 11.8% YoY and 2.4% QoQ to ₹39,173 Cr, while gross revenue grew 12% YoY to ₹45,961 Cr.

The university generally requires a minimum academic average in the B+ range, equivalent to approximately 76% under its grading system.
Candidates with different academic backgrounds may also receive consideration if they have relevant research experience.
Pakistani students must meet UBC’s country-specific admission requirements. The university recognises eligible four-year bachelor’s degrees, pharmacy degrees, engineering degrees, medical qualifications, and other accepted academic credentials with first-class or first-division standing.
English Language Requirements
International applicants whose previous universities did not primarily teach in English must submit accepted English-language proficiency results.
UBC requires an IELTS Academic overall score of 7.0, with at least 6.5 in Reading, Writing, Speaking and Listening.
For TOEFL iBT examinations taken before January 21, 2026, applicants must achieve an overall score of 100, with at least 22 in each component.
For examinations taken on or after January 21, 2026, UBC requires an overall score of 5.0 under the revised six-point scoring system, subject to the university’s component requirements.
Candidates submitting the Duolingo English Test must achieve an overall score of 130, along with the specified minimum component scores.
Required Documents for UBC Pharmacology Scholarship
Applicants must prepare their academic documents before completing the online admission process.
UBC requires academic transcripts from all previously attended post-secondary institutions and three letters of recommendation.
Candidates should also prepare a statement of interest describing their academic background, research experience, and proposed field of study.
Applicants must identify potential research supervisors and provide any additional information requested by the department.
How to Apply for the Master of Science in Pharmacology Scholarship
Interested candidates can submit their applications through the University of British Columbia’s official graduate admissions portal.
Applicants should first visit the UBC MSc Pharmacology program page and review the admission requirements, research opportunities, and funding arrangements.
Candidates should identify suitable faculty supervisors and contact them to discuss potential research projects.
Applicants must then create or use a UBC Campus-Wide Login account and complete the online graduate application.
They must provide their academic qualifications, research interests, and contact details for three referees. Candidates must also upload the required documents and pay the applicable application fee.

The Balochistan Economic and Investment Forum 2026 will be held on October 21, 2026 at Faletti's Hotel in Lahore, jointly organised by the Federation of Pakistan Chambers of Commerce and Industry (FPCCI) and the Board of Investment and Trade Balochistan (BBoIT), the two bodies announced, according to a statement issued on Monday.

It will explore opportunities across key sectors, promote industrial development, encourage utilisation of mineral resources and strengthen public-private collaboration.
Zaki Aijaz and Bilal Khan Kakar said Balochistan offers immense potential for investment and sustainable growth, supported by abundant natural resources, mineral reserves, an extensive coastline and a strategically significant location.
They said Balochistan, Pakistan's largest province, sits at the crossroads of South Asia, the Middle East and Central Asia, with borders with Iran and Afghanistan and a long coastline along the Arabian Sea offering opportunities to strengthen trade links with Gulf states and Central Asian markets.
They also underscored Gwadar Port's potential to emerge as a hub for international trade, transit and logistics and catalysing development in Balochistan and Pakistan.

items.author: Our Correspondent
items.content:
Pakistan Stock Exchange (PSX) closed lower on Monday as subdued activity and persistent selling in key sectors kept investors cautious, with the benchmark index failing to sustain its recovery amid a lack of positive triggers.
The KSE-100 index shed 453.63 points, or 0.27%, to settle at 165,966.09 at the end of trading. Earlier, the session began on a weak note, when the index dropped to 166,120.90, down 298.81 points, or 0.18%, at 9:38 am, reflecting early selling pressure.
The market attempted to recover during the day, with the index climbing to the intra-day high of 166,698.46 points. However, the recovery proved short-lived and the index later touched the low of 165,918.35 before ending the session in negative territory.
Selling was observed in major sectors, including automobile assemblers, cement, commercial banks, oil and gas exploration companies and oil marketing companies. The broad-based pressure limited the market's ability to build on its intra-day recovery and left the benchmark below the previous close.
Investor sentiment remained fragile as the market lacked fresh positive cues that could encourage sustained buying. With selling pressure persisting across key sectors, investors remained cautious, keeping the overall tone subdued through the session.
According to KTrade Securities, the KSE-100 index declined 454 points (-0.27%) to close at 165,966 amid cautious investor sentiment and subdued volumes reaching 109 million shares. Trading activity was concentrated in Pakistan Refinery, Cnergyico Pk, TPL Trakker, WorldCall Telecom and Saif Power, while selective buying in MCB Bank, Attock Refinery, Pakistan Oilfields, TRG Pakistan and Bank Alfalah provided partial support.
Sectoral weakness was broad-based, led by commercial banks, cement firms, investment banks and technology companies, where UBL, Systems Ltd, Fauji Fertiliser and Hub Power led the decline. Meanwhile, Brent crude remained elevated above $100/barrel, resulting in macroeconomic uncertainty.
"We expect the market to remain cautious and range bound, with near-term direction contingent on global oil prices, geopolitical developments and corporate earnings. A sustained recovery in trading volumes is critical to underpinning broader market participation and a durable rally," KTraded added.
In his report, Arif Habib Limited (AHL) Deputy Head of Trading Ali Najib mentioned that the market opened on a negative note and touched the intra-day low of 165,918 before staging a recovery to the high of 166,698. However, the recovery proved short-lived as selling pressure intensified in the second half, erasing the gains and dragging the index back towards its intra-day low by the close.
On the corporate front, Engro Fertilisers reported 3QCY26 net profit of Rs9.1 billion (EPS: Rs6.83), up 57% year-on-year (YoY), supported by strong fertiliser offtake. The company announced a cash dividend of Rs5.50/share, compared with Rs4.50/share in the same period of last year, implying an 80% payout ratio. The payout may reflect a cautious capital allocation approach amid potential liabilities.
"Going forward, the market is likely to remain volatile and range bound between 164-168k amid cautious investor sentiment and evolving macroeconomic and geopolitical developments," Najib said.
Overall trading volumes decreased to 370.9 million shares against Friday's total of 396.9 million. The value of traded shares stood at Rs19.6 billion.
Shares of 499 companies were traded in the ready market. Of these, 163 stocks closed higher, 302 fell and 34 remained unchanged.
Pakistan Refinery was the volume leader with trading in 52.9 million shares, gaining Rs1.86 to close at Rs108.81. Foreign investors sold shares worth Rs254.1 million, the National Clearing Company reported.

items.author: Our Correspondent
items.content:
Portugal Ambassador Paulo Domingues has called for a major transformation in Portugal-Pakistan economic relations, stressing that the two countries must move beyond cordial diplomatic ties and translate their longstanding friendship into tangible trade, investment and joint-venture opportunities.
Highlighting the significant untapped potential between the two economies, he urged businesses on both sides to forge direct partnerships, explore new markets and pursue practical projects that could substantially expand bilateral commerce.
Addressing a meeting at the Karachi Chamber of Commerce and Industry (KCCI), the ambassador said that although relations between Portugal and Pakistan were friendly and steadily improving, bilateral trade remained considerably below its potential. He emphasised that the two countries had complementary economic strengths and considerable scope to deepen cooperation across multiple sectors.
"Portugal and Pakistan have much more to offer each other. We must work together to turn our friendly relations into real business opportunities. Our political and economic relations are good and growing steadily, but the trade figures remain relatively low compared with the enormous potential that exists between our two countries. There is significant untapped potential that we must identify and develop through sustained efforts," he said.
Domingues observed that Portuguese businesses had yet to fully explore the Pakistani market, partly because they remained insufficiently aware of the opportunities it offered. In contrast, he noted that Pakistani businesses were increasingly exploring Portugal, with business missions already visiting the country to examine commercial prospects in different sectors. He expressed confidence that trade would increase as these initiatives gained momentum.
"The challenge is to bring our business communities together and encourage more Portuguese entrepreneurs and companies to visit Pakistan. Portugal and Pakistan may be geographically far apart, but geography should never limit our ambitions. We have a strong foundation for cooperation and what we need now is greater engagement between our companies," he remarked.
The ambassador identified several promising areas for cooperation, including trade and industry, renewable energy, technology, agriculture, fruit cultivation and innovation. He said the Portuguese embassy could help Pakistani and Portuguese companies identify buyers, suppliers, distributors and reliable long-term commercial partners.
Highlighting Portugal's experience in clean energy, he pointed out that approximately 70% of Portugal's electricity generation came from renewable sources, offering valuable opportunities for knowledge-sharing, technology cooperation and potential investment partnerships.

items.author: Gaurav Bagur
items.content:
The Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) has issued show-cause notices to quick commerce unicorn Zepto as well as several food and nutraceutical brands amid a broader crackdown on food safety violations.
The notice against Zepto followed a consumer complaint on social media alleging delivery of expired packets of besan (gram flour). The regulator directed the platform to submit order logs, seller details, warehouse tracking, root-cause analysis, and proof of stock withdrawal and customer refunds.
Besides Zepto, nutraceutical brands BMS Lifescience and HealthyHey Foods, as well as bakery brand Bakelite Food Processing, received show-cause notices over misleading labelling and advertising.
Bakelite: The parent company behind Pune-based Malpani Foods was targeted over describing its product, ‘Malpani’s Bakelite Puneri Cream Roll’, as ‘creamy’. However, the product includes no cream or any other dairy-based ingredients but hydrogenated vegetable fat, margarine, and sugar.
BMS Lifescience: The brand was marketing ‘HAOG’s Cranberry Urinary Tract Health Capsules’ under an expired FSSAI registration certificate, and also made health-related claims around disease risk reduction pertaining to the kidney and urinary tract without approval from the regulator. It was also pulled up for misleading usage of the official FSSAI logo, non-compliant use of the claim “as directed by healthcare practitioner”, and making potentially misleading claims online.
HealthyHey Foods: The regulator called out the brand for discrepancies in labelled ingredients across its website and Flipkart regarding its “HealthyHey Nutrition Natural Cranberry Extract 25% Capsules”. It further alleged the brand was making unapproved claims like “100% Natural”; and marketing the product with the FSSAI logo and “FSSAI certified” in a misleading way.
The regulator has directed all the companies to submit comprehensive written explanations and corrective action reports within stipulated deadlines or face license suspensions and statutory penalties.
Just days earlier, the regulator pulled up BigBasket and Flipkart over misleading promotions carried by products sold on the respective platforms.
Besides, the FSSAI has also sanctioned adjudication proceedings against beverage brand Storia. It had earlier flagged the brand’s pomegranate juice for containing only 4% pomegranate juice concentrate and 12% apple juice concentrate, in spite of misleading front-of-pack branding and visual imagery.
The authority had also cited non-compliant declarations, including prominent “No Added Sugar” claims alongside obscured disclosures, and the unapproved claim “Equivalent to 100% Fruit Juice (Reconstituted)”.
Notably, the Central Consumer Protection Authority (CCPA) had also fined the brand ₹1 Lakh for misleading consumers. The consumer protection body pulled up Storia for using the branding “100%” in their product labelling, due to reconstituted ingredients and lack of evidence.
The latest series of notices fits into a larger pattern of the FSSAI identifying illegal food labelling and marketing practices on products sold online. Till now, it has also penalised multiple platforms — Amazon, Bigbasket, Flipkart, Swiggy Instamart and Zepto — for allegedly engaging in misbranding, misleading claims, and sale and display of prohibited or poisonous food articles.
For Zepto, the fresh regulatory scrutiny adds on to legal issues the quick commerce major has been facing ahead of its proposed public plans.
Zepto disclosed multiple ongoing regulatory and labour-related proceedings in its updated DRHP, which was filed with the markets regulator SEBI earlier in June.
These include consumer protection cases over alleged dark patterns, food safety violations as well as an Enforcement Directorate inquiry into its ownership structure under FEMA. The company’s subsidiary has also faced allegations of overcharging beyond MRP and misleading advertisements. Other pending matters involve alleged wage underpayment, trade licence violations and food safety issues across several states.
Besides the regulatory challenges, Zepto had faced unalignment with institutional investors over its IPO valuations which led the company to pause its IPO until May 2027. The quick commerce major is currently chasing a pre-IPO placement of about ₹1,000 Cr.

Original | October 19, 2026 14:17 IST
B2B manufacturing company Zetwerk’s ₹5,012.3 Cr IPO has been oversubscribed on the final day of bidding, receiving bids for 19.83 Cr shares against the 18.51 Cr shares on offer. This translates to an oversubscription of 1.07X, as per BSE data on 13:45 IST.
Qualified institutional buyers (QIBs) have shown the highest interest in the IPO, oversubscribing their quota by 1.44X. These investors have placed bids for 14.28 Cr shares against 9.89 Cr shares on offer till now.
Following QIBs, non-institutional investors (NIIs) have placed bids for 3.74 Cr shares against 5.13 Cr shares reserved for them, subscribing their quota by 73%. Within the NII category, the portions for bids above ₹2 Lakh and up to ₹10 Lakh was subscribed 36%, and those above ₹10 Lakh subscribed 91%.
The retail portion was also subscribed 51%, attracting bids for 1.71 Cr shares against an allocation of 3.42 Cr shares.
Meanwhile, employees bid for 7.8 Lakh shares against 7 Lakh shares reserved for them, oversubscribing by 1.12X of their quota.
The company has set a price band of ₹143-₹151 per share, implying a valuation of around ₹25,583 Cr (about $2.7 Bn) at the upper end.
The IPO comprises a fresh issue of ₹2,830 Cr and an OFS of up to 14.45 Cr shares, worth ₹2,182.3 Cr at the upper end.
Ahead of the issue, Zetwerk raised ₹2,251.2 Cr from anchor investors. Domestic mutual funds, including SBI Mutual Fund and ICICI Prudential Mutual Fund, accounted for around 46% of the anchor book. Global institutional investors, including Goldman Sachs, BlackRock, and ADIA, also participated.
Founded in 2018, Zetwerk operates a full-stack manufacturing platform serving businesses across industrial and consumer goods categories.
It combines capacity from third-party suppliers and its own facilities to manage manufacturing orders across sectors including renewable energy, consumer electronics, aerospace, defence, oil and gas, and industrial automation.
The company has raised over $900 Mn in funding to date from investors like Peak XV Partners, Lightspeed Venture Partners, Accel India, Greenoaks Capital Partners, and D1 Capital Partners.
On the financial front, operating revenue from continuing operations rose 55.4% to ₹4,117.9 Cr from ₹2,649.4 Cr in Q1 FY26. Net loss narrowed 46.4% to ₹733 Cr from ₹1,368.5 Cr in the year-ago period.
Of the latest quarterly loss, ₹668.9 Cr came from discontinued operations, while continuing operations accounted for ₹64.1 Cr. The year-ago quarter included ₹803.2 Cr in exceptional charges from continuing operations and the ₹453 Cr impairment charge in the discontinued business.

items.author: Gaurav Bagur
items.content:
In a bid to expand into the budget food delivery segment, cloud kitchen operator Curefoods has begun piloting a new service, MegaBite, in Bengaluru.
Available on the Play Store and App Store, MegaBite appears to serve dishes — in the range of ₹49-₹199 — from restaurants across its brand portfolio. Dishes from Rolls On Wheels, Olio Pizza, Krispy Kreme, Eatfit, Arambam, among others, are live on the platform.
The app is currently operational only in Bengaluru’s HSR Layout and claims to charge “no delivery charges” and “no platform fee”. The company’s founder and CEO Ankit Nagori announced the launch on social media today.
MegaBite is being marketed as “built for value-conscious, digitally-savvy consumers” and claims to make food delivery “faster, more affordable, and convenient”.
However, much hasn’t been shared by the IPO-bound company. The company declined to respond to Inc42 on our queries regarding the launch.
Curefoods follows suit as food delivery competitors are focused on reducing fees and commissions. Rapido’s Ownly, Swiggy’s Toing and Swish Go are some such names that are increasingly doubling down on this proposition.
To note, this would be the first attempt Curefoods is operating its own delivery platform. It’s unclear as of now if Curefoods itself will handle delivery and fulfilment or if it will join hands with third-party logistics partners.
Interestingly, rival cloud kitchen operator Rebel Foods has long operated its own delivery app EatSure, which competes with Swiggy and Zomato with offerings from restaurant brands it owns. The startup had also launched a 15-minute food delivery app QuickiES, which it shut down earlier this year, after almost one year of operations.
Founded in 2020 by ex-Flipkart executive Nagori, Curefoods started off as ‘Eat.fit’, a food brand under the umbrella of fitness startup Cult.fit, but later broke off into a separate business. It has since grown to become a complete house of brands following an elaborate acquisition strategy for expansion.
The startup has raised $150 Mn to date from the likes of Accel, Iron Pillar and 3State Ventures. Notably, it secured the green light from market regulator SEBI for a public listing around a year ago. The proposed IPO would comprise a fresh issue of ₹800 Cr and an offer for sale (OFS) of up to 4.85 Cr equity shares.
However, Curefoods later put its plans on hold after mutual funds reportedly raised concerns around its desired valuation of ₹4,000 Cr, given market volatility.

items.author: Reuters
items.content:
SpaceX and Tesla will report third-quarter results on consecutive days this week, giving investors a rare side-by-side look at Elon Musk's two most valuable companies ​as merger speculation gathers momentum.
The results will test whether Starlink's steady growth and Tesla's car profits can fund the AI spending powering the merger debate.
"In ‌terms of metrics, it would have to be Starlink revenue growth more than launch counts and improvement in auto margins for Tesla," said Shawn Campbell, an adviser at Camelthorn Investments who owns shares in both companies, describing what investors will focus on.
Barclays suggested last week that a deal could be announced before Tesla's annual meeting, with SpaceX the more likely acquirer, though neither company nor Musk has officially committed to pursuing a deal.
Tesla ​on Monday said its annual meeting would be held on December 3.
In an all-stock deal, Barclays estimates Musk would hold about 37% of the equity and ​56% of the votes.
"A SpaceX acquisition of Tesla would be cleaner as it would make it easier to deal with the China business ⁠as an asset that is dealt with separately," Campbell said.
Tesla gave the speculation a showpiece on Thursday, unveiling a new Roadster sports car, slated for production in 2028, that can ​jump and turn over mid-air using rocket technology at a SpaceX test site in Texas.
"Musk is blending the future of mobility together by integrating auto and rocket technology; at the very ​least it's a subtle plant in investors' minds making an engineering efficiency argument for a merger," said Bill Birmingham, head of research at REX Financial.
He said the timing, ahead of Tesla's annual shareholders meeting, was no coincidence.
SpaceX absorbed Musk's xAI in February, months before its June IPO, and spending by Tesla and SpaceX now points to the same place: AI.
The businesses still differ, with SpaceX earning from launches, ​Starlink and AI compute, and Tesla from cars and energy storage.
SpaceX reports on Tuesday and Tesla on Wednesday after markets close.
SpaceX: AI spending in focus
SpaceX reports only its second results ​as a public company, with investors watching whether its surging AI spending is turning into revenue.
The company is expected to report third-quarter revenue of about $12.74 billion and earnings of 14 cents a share, ‌just four ⁠months after going public, according to data compiled by LSEG.
That compares with second-quarter revenue of $7.8 billion, a net loss of $541 million, and AI capital spending of $15.8 billion.
Evercore ISI expects SpaceX to exit 2026 at an annualised revenue run-rate of about $104 billion, driven by the AI segment doing "most of the heavy lifting," and estimates capital spending reaching about $151 billion in 2027.
Connectivity revenue, which includes Starlink, rose 66% to $4.3 billion in the second quarter.
SpaceX also agreed on October 8 to buy 800 MHz spectrum from Grain Management for about $8 billion, a deal that needs Federal ​Communications Commission approval and underpins its Starlink ​Mobile push.
Shares closed at $146.03 on Friday, above ⁠the $135 IPO price but well below their post-debut peak.
Tesla: robotaxis and long-term bets
Tesla is on track to grow deliveries this year for the first time since 2023, but investors are more focused on profits and its robotaxi bets.
Analysts expect Tesla to report adjusted earnings of ​roughly 43 cents a share on revenue of about $27.88 billion, compared with 50 cents a year earlier.
Second-quarter profit fell well short ​of estimates, with negative ⁠free cash flow of $1.1 billion — slipping into the red for the first time in over two years.
Still, Tesla delivered 486,532 vehicles in the third quarter, beating analysts' estimates.
Tesla has said capital spending will exceed $25 billion this year, and its shares are down about 17% in 2026 as analysts expect the company to post negative free cash flow of $4.92 billion for the third quarter.
Still, Wall Street ⁠has largely focused ​on robotaxis and the Optimus humanoid robot to assess the company's growth, citing them as high-margin product ​lines that could overshadow its traditional car sales business eventually.
While Tesla's robotaxi business and fleet are small compared to Waymo, the company expects to roll out its self-driving taxis widely in the coming years.
Its valuation has largely ​hinged on such long-term ambitions instead of the car business, which contributes the lion's share of the company's revenue.

items.author: Anadolu Agency
items.content:
A Brazilian court gave US tech company Meta 24 hours to prove that its artificial intelligence systems do not favour either candidate ahead of next Sunday’s presidential runoff, local media reported on Monday.
The Superior Electoral Court order, signed by magistrate Marco Aurelio Bellizze Oliveira, covers Meta's algorithmic systems managing social media platforms Instagram, Facebook, and WhatsApp, reported Brazilian outlet Universo Online.
The company must prove that it is not limiting the distribution of political content after President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva's campaign alleged that it suppressed material favourable to the incumbent while permitting the spread of hostile AI-generated posts.
Read: Brazil's Lula accuses Meta of election interference
"These inconsistencies in metrics demand explanations and immediate correction," said Michel Bertoni, a lawyer representing Lula’s campaign.
Bertoni argued that when a major digital platform restricts the circulation of political content unevenly, it directly compromises electoral regularity and interferes with national sovereignty.
The measure follows reporting by Brazilian daily Folha de S.Paulo, which cited internal communications indicating that Meta employees acknowledged restrictions affecting Lula's accounts while algorithms recommended the profile and WhatsApp channel of challenger Flavio Bolsonaro.
Read More: AI able to manipulate elections worldwide, expert says
Meta denied giving preferential treatment to any candidate ahead of the October 25 runoff vote, maintaining that its rules apply equally to all political figures and that internal discussions focused on the severity of public technical issues rather than political bias.

On July 17, the government announced a new pricing mechanism under which petroleum product prices would be reviewed and notified daily, replacing the weekly pricing mechanism, as renewed tensions between the United States and Iran continued to drive volatility in global oil markets and raise concerns over fuel supplies.
On September 13, PM Shehbaz announced a special relief scheme offering Rs100 per litre off petrol for motorcycles, three-wheeler rickshaws and cars with engines up to 800cc, in an attempt to shield lower-income consumers from the impact of rising petroleum prices.
Under the proposal, an estimated 11.8 million beneficiaries would be covered. Around 10 million two-wheeler users and 800,000 three-wheeler users would be entitled to relief on 20 litres of fuel per month, translating into a maximum monthly benefit of Rs2,000 per beneficiary.
Another one million users of cars up to 800cc would receive relief on 30 litres per month, providing them with a maximum benefit of Rs3,000 each.
On Sept 17, the government reintroduced austerity and fuel conservation measures amid rising fuel prices, tightening business operating hours and restricting public events.
Under the measures, notified with immediate effect, shops, markets, shopping malls, bazaars, departmental stores, grocery stores, general stores and kiryana shops would close by 9pm throughout the week, according to a notification issued by the Cabinet Division.
Marriage halls, marquees and other commercial venues hosting festive events would close by 10pm, while restaurants, cafes, eateries, food outlets and standalone fruit and vegetable shops would be allowed to operate until 11pm. Takeaway and home delivery services would remain exempt from the timing restrictions.
Global geopolitical developments continue to pose significant risks. International oil prices are influenced by decisions taken by OPEC+, conflicts in the Middle East, sanctions on oil-producing nations, and disruptions in critical shipping routes such as the Strait of Hormuz and the Red Sea. Any interruption in these supply chains can immediately increase crude oil prices and freight costs. Since Pakistan imports the majority of its petroleum requirements, these developments quickly translate into higher domestic fuel prices.
Brent crude futures rose slightly on Monday after attacks by Yemen's Iran-aligned Houthis on a Yemeni ‌military training camp and renewed attacks on Saudi energy, airport and military facilities.
Brent crude futures rose 17 cents, or 0.15%, to 110.03 a barrel at 1:08 pm ET (1708 GMT), after falling more than $3 earlier in the session as investors booked profits following last week's rally to a five-month high.
Yemen's Houthis said on Monday they had carried out attacks on Saudi energy, airport and military targets, ​including an Aramco facility in Yanbu, the Shaybah oilfield, King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh and Abha airport. Saudi authorities did not immediately confirm the claims, and ​Reuters could not independently verify them.
Separately, an oil tanker caught fire and exploded after striking a naval mine in the southern Strait of Hormuz on Sunday, Iran's Revolutionary Guards said, according to Iranian media.
"Ongoing strikes on vessels transiting the Strait of Hormuz and flows remaining below pre-conflict levels continue to support prices," UBS analyst ‌Giovanni Staunovo ⁠said.

items.title: US banning Chinese AI DeepSeek from government agency IT systems
items.author: Reuters
items.content:
The US Homeland Security Department is ordering the removal of DeepSeek products and third-party services ​using the Chinese AI model from US civilian agency IT systems, according ‌to a notice published on Monday.
The department is also banning the acquisition of DeepSeek products and third-party services developed using DeepSeek by US civilian government agencies. DHS said DeepSeek models pose "multiple threat vectors" ​and raised concerns that use of the product "may result in the transfer of ​sensitive data to the PRC if used by US government employees ⁠or vendors."
DHS also said use of DeepSeek by government agencies "could produce actionable ​intelligence on US persons and/or government agencies. The models themselves may contain malware or ​other security vulnerabilities."
Read: US flags DeepSeek, Chinese firms over AI theft allegations
In a July memo made public on Monday, DHS told federal agencies to monitor flows of traffic in and out of government websites to address potential risks from DeepSeek.
Previously, ​several US agencies, including the Department of Commerce and the Navy, have banned ​the use of DeepSeek on government devices. Multiple states, including New York, Tennessee, and Virginia, have ‌taken ⁠similar steps.
The Chinese Embassy in Washington did not immediately comment.
The Trump administration has taken a series of steps to crack down on Chinese tech companies.
The Federal Communications Commission will vote on October 29 to bar all Chinese labs from ​testing electronic devices such ​as smartphones, cameras ⁠and computers for use in the US. Last year, 82% of US electronics were tested in China.
Read More: China's AI agents can lie and scheme - just like their US rivals
In December, the FCC ​banned the import of all new models of Chinese drones and ​also banned ⁠imports of new models of Chinese-made consumer routers, the boxes connecting computers, phones and smart devices to the internet.
In July, the FCC voted to bar sales of devices ⁠in ​the US that contain key hardware from Chinese ​companies deemed to be national security risks and proposed to prohibit US telecommunications carriers from interconnecting with ​Chinese telecom firms deemed national security risks.

Copyright protected content copied from PhoneWorld website.
Federal Minister for National Food Security and Research, Rana Tanveer Hussain, welcomed the cooperation agreement between StarCharge, a leading global provider of electric vehicle (EV) charging and smart energy solutions, and McDonald’s Pakistan, aimed at expanding access to electric vehicle charging facilities and promoting environmentally sustainable transportation across Pakistan.
Speaking at the ceremony held in Islamabad, the Federal Minister appreciated the initiative, describing it as an encouraging step towards developing modern, environmentally friendly infrastructure and accelerating Pakistan’s transition towards cleaner energy solutions.
“The future of Pakistan depends on sustainable development, technological innovation and responsible investment. Initiatives such as this demonstrate how the private sector can contribute to national efforts to promote clean energy, reduce environmental pollution and build a greener Pakistan,”
the Minister said.
Under the cooperation agreement, StarCharge and McDonald’s Pakistan will explore opportunities to establish EV charging facilities at suitable McDonald’s locations across the country. The proposed collaboration will combine StarCharge’s expertise in EV charging technology with McDonald’s extensive customer network, enabling customers to conveniently charge their electric vehicles while dining.
The participating organisations will jointly assess potential locations based on technical feasibility, infrastructure requirements and commercial viability before proceeding with implementation.
Rana Tanveer Hussain emphasised that the expansion of electric mobility infrastructure would help reduce dependence on conventional fuels, encourage the adoption of environmentally friendly transportation and support Pakistan’s broader objectives of energy efficiency and environmental sustainability.
He highlighted the importance of public-private collaboration in introducing modern technologies and attracting investment into emerging sectors of the economy.
“Pakistan needs innovative partnerships that translate technological advancement into practical benefits for citizens. The expansion of EV charging infrastructure will not only facilitate electric vehicle users but also encourage greater private-sector participation in sustainable development,”
the Minister remarked.
The Federal Minister further stressed that environmental sustainability and economic development must advance together, adding that initiatives promoting cleaner transportation could contribute to improved air quality, reduced carbon emissions and a more resilient national economy.
He appreciated the commitment of StarCharge and McDonald’s Pakistan to exploring investment in green infrastructure and expressed hope that the cooperation would encourage other businesses to adopt similar environmentally responsible initiatives.
The agreement reflects the growing role of private-sector partnerships in supporting the Government of Pakistan’s efforts to encourage electric mobility, strengthen charging infrastructure and promote a cleaner, greener and more sustainable future.

items.author: Staff
items.content:
Copyright protected content copied from PhoneWorld website.
The Pakistan Telecommunication Authority (PTA) has proposed a new licensing framework for radio-based communication services, introducing a 10-year licence term, online application processing and a 15-working-day deadline for communicating decisions on complete applications, while tightening eligibility, equipment and compliance requirements.
Under the draft Radio Based Services (RBS) Licensing Regulations, 2026, the regulator has proposed four categories of licences covering private radio networks, aircraft mobile stations, maritime mobile stations and amateur radio operators, including a separate category for junior operators.
The draft regulations, circulated for public comments, seek to establish a standardised licensing procedure for services ranging from wireless communication networks and trunking systems to microwave links, telemetry, weather radars and supervisory control and data acquisition (SCADA) systems.
The proposed framework requires applicants to submit applications electronically through the PTA’s online system, while private radio network applicants would first have to obtain radio-frequency spectrum assignment through the Frequency Allocation Board (FAB) portal before applying for a licence.
The PTA would examine applications for completeness within seven working days and communicate any deficiencies to applicants. Applicants would have 15 days to address each set of deficiencies, with applications allowed to be returned for corrections no more than three times.
The authority would communicate its decision on a complete application within 15 working days, subject to completion of the required formalities and, in the case of private radio networks, assignment of spectrum by FAB.
Under the proposed rules, licences would generally remain valid for 10 years, while junior amateur radio licences would have a five-year term. Applicants seeking renewal would have to apply at least three months before expiry, while spectrum revalidation cases would require an application at least six months before expiry.
The draft also proposes a streamlined renewal mechanism for private radio network licensees where they have applied on time, cleared outstanding dues and sought renewal without changes to their existing network parameters, but FAB has not completed spectrum revalidation before expiry. Such renewal would remain subject to subsequent spectrum revalidation.
The proposed fee structure includes a non-refundable application processing fee of Rs5,000 and an initial licence fee of Rs10,000, where applicable. Amateur radio licences would carry a charge of Rs2,000 for 10 years, while junior amateur radio licences would be issued without fees.
Aircraft and maritime mobile station licences would each carry charges of Rs100,000 for the complete licence term. An Inmarsat terminal installed aboard an aircraft or vessel would attract an additional charge of Rs250,000 for the licence term.
For private radio networks, annual charges would be calculated using a formula incorporating the base price, frequency band, number of assigned frequencies, bandwidth, equipment output power and location factor. The proposed structure would distinguish between urban, suburban and rural areas, with higher location factors applying to more urbanised areas.
The draft also makes type approval mandatory for radio equipment, subject to specified exemptions for equipment installed aboard aircraft or vessels and certified by the relevant aviation or maritime authorities. Licensees would be required to operate within their authorised frequencies, output power and technical parameters.
The PTA would retain the power to refuse a licence where its grant could threaten national security. It would also be authorised to inspect licensed radio equipment, with prior notice, while inspections without notice could be conducted where there is a reasonable apprehension of harmful interference, unauthorised spectrum use or a national security threat.
For amateur radio operators, the proposed rules set the minimum age at 18 years, require valid membership of the Pakistan Amateur Radio Society and make a police clearance certificate mandatory. Applicants aged 14 to under 18 could qualify for junior licences with sponsorship and parental or institutional consent.
Existing licensees would be required to register their licence particulars on the PTA’s online system within six months of the regulations taking effect, without any registration fee. Existing licences would remain valid on their current terms until expiry.
Also Read: PTA Steps Up Nationwide Monitoring to Improve Mobile Network and Internet Services
