items.author: Web Desk
items.content:
Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif on Saturday defended the imposition of an emergency and governor’s rule in Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa (K-P), saying the government had been left with no other option amid fears of bloodshed during Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) long march and a breakdown of law and order.
The remarks came amid continuing political tensions following the federal government's imposition of emergency and governor's rule in K-P on October 11 under Articles 232 and 234 of the Constitution, which suspended the PTI-led provincial administration and transferred executive authority to Governor Faisal Karim Kundi.
The federal government defended the decision by citing security concerns and a lack of cooperation from the provincial government.
“We were left with no other option. We understood that we could not simply remain silent and watch bloodshed unfold,” the prime minister said while explaining the circumstances that led to the decision during a media talk in Gujranwala.
Invoking the familiar expression about Rome burning while Nero played his fiddle, PM Shehbaz said the government could not continue to watch the situation deteriorate and risk being held responsible by future generations.
“That would have amounted to criminal negligence,” he said, adding that the decision had been taken in the best interests of Pakistan. He prayed that it would produce positive results.
The prime minister made the remarks during a visit to Gujranwala, where he was accompanied by Federal Ministers Azam Nazeer Tarar and Attaullah Tarar to offer condolences on the death of Barrister Mahmood Virk, a party worker.
Describing the deceased as a loyal party worker and a decent person, the premier acknowledged his contributions.
During the speech, he appreciated Punjab Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz’s performance and hoped her efforts would bring prosperity.
Turning to the situation in K-P, the prime minister said he had held several meetings with the province’s former chief minister and also with Chief Minister Sohail Afridi, making what he described as sincere efforts to address the issues facing the province.
Read: K-P is rich in minerals; we will 'extract and sell them', says Kundi
He said K-P was an integral and beautiful part of Pakistan, whose people possessed courage and resilience, and that the federal government remained willing to extend all possible assistance for the province’s development and prosperity. However, he noted that the province was suffering from a spate of violence.
PM Shehbaz said the security situation, particularly the resurgence of terrorism and infiltration from Afghanistan since 2018, required collective efforts to defeat terror groups. The premier pledged to provide “all available resources and administrative facilities” to eliminate the menace.
He regretted that law-enforcement personnel and security forces, including Pakistan Army officers, continued to sacrifice their lives in the fight against terrorism. Innocent civilians, including women and children, had also been killed in attacks, he added.
The prime minister said the government had made repeated efforts to defuse political tensions in view of the poor security outlook but alleged that long marches and protests organised by the PTI had disrupted the country’s functioning one after the other.
Recalling the political turmoil of 2013-14, he said the unrest had brought economic activity to a standstill and affected imports, exports, agriculture and employment, inflicting what he described as enormous and irreparable losses on the country.
He said similar disruption had occurred last year and alleged that PTI had planned widespread violence during the October long march.
According to PM Shehbaz, the government had established a committee and held discussions with the relevant parties for around 48 hours in an effort to reach a negotiated settlement and stop the long march from happening.
“A comprehensive agreement had eventually been prepared, with the expectation that PTI would withdraw its call for a long march while Pakistan pursued economic recovery and development, but the talks fell out after consultations with the now-suspended K-P chief minister.”
He also referred to disagreements over consultations with the K-P chief minister, saying the situation had subsequently deteriorated and the government could not ignore the risk of further violence.
Read more: Fazl seeks joint in-camera session as ministers reject 'spoils of war' charge
Now that the march had stopped, the prime minister said Pakistan’s international standing improved and the domestic economy had begun to stabilise.
“Today, the economy has not only stabilised but is gradually moving towards recovery and growth.”
Advisory council to oversee K-P
Defending the interim governance decision for two months, the prime minister said the government had concluded that inaction was no longer an option for the sake of the people of the province.
He said an advisory council had been established to help address the situation, describing it as a neutral body whose members were overwhelmingly non-political and included highly respected individuals.
“God willing, this council will help fix the situation in K-P,” he said, adding that he would remain involved and attend its meetings whenever required.
The prime minister expressed hope that the measures would improve the situation and help restore peace and stability in the province.
War in the Gulf and its impact on Pakistan
Referring to the impact of unrest in the Middle East and resulting inflationary pressures, he said the government had provided relief to the public through a fuel subsidy scheme.
He said the initiative had benefited around 12 million people, including motorcyclists, rickshaw users and owners of vehicles up to 800cc. The provincial government had allocated Rs75 billion for the scheme, which was intended to be utilised by the end of the year, he added.
PM Shehbaz noted that given the average household size of 5-6 people per family, the scheme’s indirect benefits could extend to nearly 65 million people.
‘Consultations not an option anymore’
Separately, PTI leader Asad Qaiser has said that talks are not on the cards after what the federal government has done.
“There is no room for consultations after what the federal government has done [imposed governor’s rule and emergency],” Qaiser outlined.
He said that from now on, all decisions would be undertaken by the joint opposition after careful deliberations and in uniformity. He also said all the opposition parties will put forth their stance and reach a conclusion in the All Parties Conference.
“PTI will not engage in talks on its own as the government is guilty of mishandling the situation,” he added.
The PTI stalwart lamented that CM Afridi and Speaker Babar Saleem Swati were arrested.
“Is this a democratic move?” he questioned.

items.content:
Egyptian President Abdel Fattah al-Sisi said on Saturday that his term would end in 2030 and outlined a plan for the country's main military academy to train potential future leaders for 30 months before then.
The proposal gives ​the Egyptian Military Academy a central role in preparing future leaders, underscoring the armed forces' ​influence beyond national defence. Under Sisi, a former general, the military has expanded ⁠its presence in the economy and civilian affairs.
Speaking at a graduation ceremony at the academy, Sisi ​said a committee overseen by the speaker of parliament and including intellectuals, politicians and the ministers of higher ​education and justice, would develop criteria for selecting candidates and draft legislation for the training programme.
Read: Egypt's Sisi and Saudi crown prince stress need for security of Red Sea navigation
Reiterating that Egypt's constitution would not be amended, he said the end of his presidential term in 2030 was "a matter that has been completely ​settled and will not be discussed".
He said the programme would allow Egyptians to "elect and choose ​from among" its graduates, but gave no details on how they would be put forward for elected or appointed posts.
"I ‌will ⁠not leave the Egyptian state except when it is replete with sons and daughters capable of assuming responsibility," Sisi said.
The programme would target PhD holders from reputable Egyptian and foreign universities, who would spend 30 months at the academy learning about the state, its resources and how to preserve them, ​Sisi said. He said graduates ​would be prepared ⁠for leadership roles ranging from the presidency to ministries, governorates and parliament.
Also Read: Egypt rules out 'popular normalisation' with Israel without just peace, Palestinian state
Sisi, 71, is serving a six-year term after being reelected in December 2023. Constitutional amendments ​approved in a 2019 referendum extended presidential terms from four to six ​years and allowed ⁠him to seek a third term, clearing the way for him to remain in office until 2030.
The latest in a line of Egyptian rulers drawn from the military, he became president in 2014, a year ⁠after toppling ​Mohamed Morsi of the Muslim Brotherhood — Egypt's first democratically elected ​leader — following mass protests.
He proceeded to crush the Brotherhood, the Middle East's oldest Islamist organisation, and maintain a grip on power.

items.title: USCIS: Anyone who ‘guarantees’ a faster visa or Green Card is scamming you
items.summary: USCIS warns immigrants and visa applicants about fraudulent schemes that promise quicker visa approvals in exchange for monetary fees. These scams frequently involve false claims of having special ties to government officials. USCIS insists that no one can hasten the immigration process through personal connections. Individuals should file applications independently and trust assistance only from recognized professionals. Recognizing fraudulent emails and suspicious offers is essential to protect against these scams.

items.content:
Copyright protected content copied from PhoneWorld website.
Vivo has announced the global launch of the Vivo V80 after introducing the smartphone last week. The company plans to bring the device to Southeast Asia, the Middle East, and other markets, although availability, pricing, and specifications may vary by region.
The Vivo V80 features a high-refresh-rate AMOLED display, a large battery, and a camera system that includes a periscope telephoto lens. It also runs Android 17 and comes with a long-term software support commitment.
Vivo V80 Goes Global With 144Hz AMOLED Display and 7,200mAh Battery
The Vivo V80 comes with a 6.59-inch AMOLED display that offers a resolution of 1260 x 2750 pixels. The screen supports a 144Hz refresh rate for smoother scrolling, animations, and gaming.
Vivo also claims a peak brightness of 5,000 nits, which should help improve screen visibility in bright outdoor conditions.
The phone is powered by Qualcomm’s Snapdragon 7 Gen 4 processor. It comes with 8GB of RAM and storage options of 128GB, 256GB, and 512GB.
The 128GB variant uses UFS 3.1 storage, while the 256GB and 512GB models feature the faster UFS 4.1 standard.
50MP Cameras With Periscope Zoom
The Vivo V80 offers a versatile camera setup. Its rear camera system includes a 50MP main sensor with optical image stabilisation (OIS), a 50MP periscope telephoto camera with OIS and 3x optical zoom, and an 8MP ultrawide camera.
The main camera’s stabilisation helps reduce blur caused by minor hand movements. Meanwhile, the periscope telephoto camera allows users to capture distant subjects with 3x optical zoom.
For selfies and video calls, the smartphone features a 50MP front camera.
Large Battery With 90W Fast Charging
The Vivo V80 packs a 7,200mAh battery, which should provide substantial capacity for daily use. The phone also supports 90W wired charging to reduce the time needed to recharge the battery.
Actual battery life and charging times may vary depending on usage, settings, and other conditions.
Android 17 and Long-Term Software Support
The Vivo V80 runs Android 17 with Vivo’s OriginOS 7 interface. The company promises four major Android updates and six years of security updates.
This support policy could make the phone a more appealing option for users who plan to keep their devices for several years.
Global Availability and Colours
Vivo will offer the V80 globally in four colour options: Starwish Purple, Wander Green, Sunrise Anthem, and Vast Gray.
The company has not announced a single global price or a specific release date for every market. Pricing, availability, and some specifications will depend on local market conditions and consumer preferences.
The Vivo V80 combines a high-refresh-rate display, a large battery, a 50MP periscope camera, and extended software support. However, buyers will need to wait for local announcements to confirm its price and availability in their respective markets.

items.author: Onsa Mustafa
items.content:
Copyright protected content copied from PhoneWorld website.
The Punjab government has announced the distribution date for e-bikes under its student scheme. Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz Sharif said the distribution of e-bikes would begin on November 5, 2026, to help students travel to educational institutions and manage their daily commuting expenses.
Under the scheme, the provincial government plans to provide 100,000 electric bikes to students, with a larger share reserved for female students. The initiative aims to make transportation more accessible and affordable for students across Punjab.
Punjab Announces Distribution Date for E-Bikes Under Student Scheme
The scheme has received more than 1.2 million registrations and over 600,000 applications, according to the reported figures. The strong response highlights the demand for affordable transport among students.
The government also plans to support students who do not know how to ride a bike. These students will receive two days of free riding training to help them learn the basics and travel independently.
The initiative is expected to make daily journeys easier for students who rely on public transport or face difficulties reaching their educational institutions.
Punjab Green Bus Fare to Remain at Rs. 20
Maryam Nawaz also announced that Punjab’s fully electric Green Bus service would continue charging Rs. 20 per ride despite rising petrol and diesel prices.
The service currently operates 700 buses. The provincial government plans to increase the fleet to 3,000 buses within the next six to eight months.
The government also provides free travel on these buses to women, students, senior citizens, and people with disabilities.
See Also: How to Buy an Electric Rickshaw on 0% Markup Installments in Pakistan? Complete Guide
Green Bus Service to Expand Across Punjab
The electric buses offer several facilities, including air conditioning, Wi-Fi, and CCTV cameras, to improve passenger comfort and safety.
The Punjab government aims to expand the Green Bus service to all 148 tehsils across the province. The expansion is expected to improve access to public transport for residents in more cities and towns.
The e-bike scheme and electric bus expansion form part of the provincial government’s efforts to promote affordable and environmentally friendly transportation. The upcoming e-bike distribution will provide students with another transport option, while the Green Bus service will continue to offer low-cost travel to the public.

items.author: Onsa Mustafa
items.content:
Copyright protected content copied from PhoneWorld website.
Google is introducing changes to its AI search results to make website links and news articles easier to find. The move comes as news publishers and online businesses raise concerns about declining website traffic as more users rely on AI-generated answers instead of opening individual websites.
The company announced on Thursday that it would display links more frequently and place them higher in AI-generated search results. The changes aim to help users discover original sources and encourage them to visit websites for more information.
Google to Make News Articles and Website Links More Visible in AI Search
Google has gradually expanded artificial intelligence features in its search engine over the past two years. In May 2024, the company introduced AI Overviews, which provide summarised answers to users’ questions instead of relying only on traditional search links.
In March 2025, Google introduced AI Mode, a separate search experience that offers more detailed responses and additional links to relevant sources.
Under the latest changes, Google will show contextual links more frequently and place them more prominently within AI-generated content. This could make it easier for users to find news reports, articles, and other websites related to their searches.
Google will also expand its link carousel worldwide. The feature displays cards with headlines and images from relevant articles directly below AI Overviews.
Preferred Sources and Social Media Content
Google will give greater attention to articles published by websites that users have selected as preferred sources. This approach could help users find content from publications they already trust or regularly follow.
The company also plans to include relevant posts from social media platforms and online forums in its search results. This could give users access to a wider range of perspectives and discussions alongside traditional news articles.
Google will also make links appearing at the end of AI-generated summaries more noticeable and engaging. These changes are intended to encourage users to explore original sources when they want more detailed information.
News Publishers Face Declining Website Traffic
The changes come as publishers express growing concerns about the impact of AI-powered search on their audience numbers.
AI-generated summaries allow users to find answers without visiting the websites that provide the underlying information. As a result, some publishers have reported fewer clicks from search results.
According to a report by consultancy Chartbeat, news publishers experienced a 40% decline in traffic from Google between July 2025 and July 2026.
The issue has also raised concerns among media organisations in Europe. In August, Apig, a group representing daily newspapers in France, approached the country’s Competition Authority over Google’s AI summaries. The group argued that the summaries violated agreements reached with news publishers in 2022.
Google’s AI Search Continues to Grow
Google’s AI search features have reached a large global audience. Alphabet CEO Sundar Pichai said during the company’s second-quarter 2025 earnings results that AI Overviews had more than two billion monthly users across over 200 countries.
However, the growing use of AI summaries has created challenges for websites that depend on search traffic to reach readers and generate revenue.
By making links more visible, Google could help users discover original articles while addressing some of publishers’ concerns. However, it remains to be seen whether the changes will lead to a meaningful recovery in website traffic.
For news organisations and other online publishers, the key question is whether improved link visibility will encourage more users to click through to the original content rather than relying solely on AI-generated answers.

items.author: Onsa Mustafa
items.content:
Copyright protected content copied from PhoneWorld website.
WhatsApp is testing a new feature that could make it easier for users to request someone’s location directly through a chat. The feature aims to simplify the process by allowing users to send a location request without having to explain how the other person can share their location.
The feature was spotted in WhatsApp version 2.26.41.11 during an APK teardown. According to the findings, the messaging platform is testing a new “Request location” option within the existing “Send location” screen.
How the New Location Request Feature Works on WhatsApp
The new option reportedly appears alongside the existing features for sharing a current location or live location. When users select “Request location,” WhatsApp creates a card titled “Location request” that appears in the conversation.
This could make it easier to ask friends, family members, or colleagues to share their location. Instead of sending a separate message and explaining the steps, users may be able to send a request directly through WhatsApp’s location menu.
The feature could also reduce confusion for people who are unfamiliar with the app’s location-sharing options. It may help users receive a map location instead of relying on a typed address or additional messages.
Recipient Experience Remains Unclear
Although the feature has appeared in testing, its complete functionality remains unknown. The initial test reportedly worked on one device but failed to function properly on another. On the second device, the request appeared as a message indicating that the feature was not supported.
This suggests that WhatsApp has not yet completed the feature or made it available across devices. The testing also leaves questions about how recipients will see location requests and whether they will have different options for responding.
One possibility is that tapping the request card will open WhatsApp’s location-sharing screen, allowing recipients to choose between sharing their current location and their live location. However, this is only a possible explanation, and the actual process has not been confirmed.
WhatsApp May Improve Location Sharing
Apple’s iMessage already offers a similar option that lets users request another person’s location through its Location menu. WhatsApp’s proposed feature could bring comparable convenience to its large user base.
However, WhatsApp has not confirmed when the feature will become available or whether it will be included in a future update. For now, the option remains under development, and its final design and functionality may change before a public release.

items.author: Shrishti Bisht
items.content:
Hunger Pangs, the parent of restaurant chain Burma Burma, has filed its DRHP for an IPO comprising a fresh issue of up to ₹150 Cr and an offer for sale (OFS) of up to 2.8 Cr shares.
Cofounders and promoters Ankit Gupta and Chirag Chhajer will offload up to 60 Lakh shares each through the OFS. Other selling shareholders include Bbigplas Poly, Negen Tech Opportunities Angel Fund, Venture Catalysts Angel Growth Fund, and an LV Angel Fund scheme.
Burma Burma plans to use ₹117.29 Cr from its fresh issue to open 27 company-owned restaurants over FY28 and FY29, expanding in existing markets and entering new Tier I and Tier II cities. The company expects to open 12 outlets in FY28 and 15 in FY29, with the funds covering civil and interior work, kitchen equipment and other setup costs.
While no IPO-funded restaurant is expected to begin operations in FY27, the company has earmarked ₹10 Cr that year for advance payments towards fit-outs and other preparatory expenses. It plans to deploy ₹54.63 Cr in FY28 and ₹52.66 Cr in FY29.
Burma Burma has identified locations for five outlets in Bengaluru, Surat, Jaipur, Kolkata and Delhi, and signed letters of intent for the sites. Locations for the remaining restaurants are yet to be finalised. The remaining net proceeds will be used for general corporate purposes, capped at 25% of the gross proceeds.
The development comes months after Burma Burma raised ₹38 Cr at a valuation of ₹500 Cr, to expand its footprint into new cities. It has raised over $11 Mn to date from the likes of Negen Capital, Endurance Capital, Coheron Wealth, among others.
Founded in 2013, Hunger Pangs opened its first Burma Burma restaurant in Mumbai in 2014. The chain serves vegetarian Burmese cuisine and operates in the premium casual dining segment.
As of July 31, it operated 22 restaurants across nine cities, including Mumbai, Bengaluru, Hyderabad, Kolkata, and Delhi NCR, alongside a delivery kitchen in Mumbai.
Burma Burma competes in the broader Asian dining segment with restaurant chains such as Mainland China, Mamagoto, Yum Yum Cha, and Berco’s.
Beyond Burma Burma, the company has conceptualised a premium casual dining chain of Japanese restaurants and noodle shops. The proposed brand remains under research and development.
Revenue Grows, But FY26 Loss Widens
On the financial front, Hunger Pangs’ operating revenue rose 46.6% to ₹155.5 Cr in FY26 from ₹106.1 Cr in FY25. However, its net loss widened to ₹15.4 Cr from ₹50.5 Lakh a year earlier, as expenses grew faster than revenue.
Total expenses increased 61.8% to ₹175.8 Cr from ₹108.7 Cr in FY25. EBITDA grew 20.2% to ₹25.7 Cr from ₹21.4 Cr. However, EBITDA margin contracted to 16.5% from 20.1%.
During FY26, the company expanded its restaurant network from 12 to 21 outlets, taking its seating capacity to 1,991 from 1,082. However, the average bill value declined to ₹2,400 from ₹2,560.
For Q1 FY27, Hunger Pangs reported operating revenue of ₹53.7 Cr and EBITDA of ₹11.4 Cr, translating into an EBITDA margin of 21.3%.
It posted a net profit of ₹1.1 Cr during the quarter, supported by a ₹2 Cr deferred tax credit. Before tax, the company recorded a loss of ₹89 Lakh.

Copyright protected content copied from PhoneWorld website.
Zong, has won Gold in Creative Excellence for its AI-powered 5G launch campaign at the Dragons of Asia Awards 2026. The international recognition builds on Zong’s success at the Dragons of Pakistan Awards earlier this year and places the brand’s work among the region’s best in marketing and communications.
The winning entry, AIsa Hai Future, blended artificial and augmented intelligence with Pakistani creativity, reimagining the nation’s digital future through a distinctive, customer-focused brand narrative.
The recognition also reflects Zong’s evolution as a future-focused, AI-driven digital brand. By combining technology, innovation and data-led insights, Zong continues to develop more relevant customer experiences and strengthen its approach to brand communication thus engaging customers more meaningfully. By earning Gold against regional competition, Zong has demonstrated that Pakistani brands can deliver internationally recognized creative work when they combine a clear brand purpose with a genuine understanding of their audiences.
Commenting on the achievement, Hina Ali, Head of Marketing Communication at Zong, said:
“Winning Gold in Creative Excellence at the Dragons of Asia Awards is a proud moment for Zong. We believe great creativity begins with understanding people: what matters to them, what resonates with them, and how our brand proposition can become meaningful in their lives. With AIsa Hai Future, we set out to move beyond conventional telecom advertising and tell a story that brings together the possibilities of 5G and AI with the creativity and aspirations of Pakistan. This recognition reinforces our belief that when technology, insight, and a distinctive brand idea come together, the result is a communication that truly stands apart.”
Through continued investment in 5G, AI and next-generation products and services, Zong is advancing its vision of a connected, inclusive and future-ready Digital Pakistan – where technology enables opportunity, and every brand experience reflects the promise of “Aisa Hai Future”.

Key Startup Funding Highlights Of The Week
AI dominated the funding charts this week, attracting $53.4 Mn across six deals. RapidCanvas’ $29 Mn Series B round accounted for 54.3% of the total capital deployed in the segment.
Ecommerce emerged as the second-most funded sector and lapped up $48.3 Mn, followed by travel tech at $34.6 Mn and enterprise services at $31.8 Mn. Advanced hardware and technology also attracted $23.2 Mn.
Early-stage funding continued to gather steam as pre-seed and seed-stage startups raised $25.9 Mn across 11 disclosed deals this week.
Accel emerged as the most active investor of the week, backing four startups. Other backers such as Hitachi Ventures, 3one4Capital and Inflection Point Ventures also participated in multiple rounds this week.
Startup M&A Updates Of The Week
IT advisory firm Infotech acquired Bengaluru-based SaaS startup Zluri to strengthen its application discovery and identity governance capabilities. The terms of the deal were not disclosed.
Nasdaq-listed SaaS major Freshworks signed a definitive agreement to acquire SaaS management platform Torii for an undisclosed amount to expand into AI spend management. The deal is expected to close by Q3 FY26.
Startup IPO Updates Of The Week
Zetwerk’s public issue was subscribed 31% at the end of the second day of bidding. The B2B manufacturing startup’s IPO comprises a fresh issue of shares worth ₹2,830 Cr and an OFS component of up to 14.45 Cr shares.
Investors made a beeline for Tonbo Imaging’s ₹852 Cr IPO. The issue was subscribed 7.78X on the second day of bidding, receiving bids for 6.63 Cr shares as against 85.26 Lakh shares on offer. It is scheduled to list on the bourses on October 23.
Other Developments Of The Week
Bengaluru-based manufacturing Whizzo is in talks to raise around $26 Mn in a Series B round, which will likely be co-led by Aavishkaar Capital and Bertelsmann Investments.
Haircare startup Traya is also in talks to raise around ₹300 Cr from Verlinvest. The round, which will likely include both primary and secondary deals, could potentially value the startup between ₹2,500 Cr and ₹3,000 Cr.

items.content:
… Track celebrates self-expression, spontaneous moments
By Chioma Obinna
Desperados has teamed up with award-winning Afrobeats artiste, producer and songwriter Young Jonn to release “Let It Go”, a cross-cultural collaboration blending Latin music with Afrobeats to celebrate self-expression and living in the moment.
The track, produced by Yung Willis, draws inspiration from “Guao Guao”, a reggaeton record created by Desperados in partnership with Venezuelan artiste Micro TDH and Colombian producer Ovy On The Drums.
Built around a sample of the original song, “Let It Go” reinterprets its Latin-inspired sound through Young Jonn’s distinctive style, creating an Afrobeats record shaped by Nigeria’s vibrant music and nightlife culture.
The collaboration reflects Desperados’ strategy of using music and cultural experiences to connect with younger audiences, drawing on the brand’s Latin roots and the influence of Nigerian music.
According to the brand, the song captures the spirit of spontaneous nights out, unexpected link-ups with friends and moments when music brings people together.
“Let It Go” is designed to encourage listeners to loosen up, express themselves and enjoy experiences that create lasting memories, while bringing two musical cultures together.
Yung Willis, whose production credits include artistes such as Wizkid, Davido, Kizz Daniel, Falz, Niniola, BNXN, Zlatan, Patoranking and Ice Prince, handled the production, combining global influences with contemporary Afrobeats sounds.
Rather than recreate the original reggaeton record, the collaboration gives it a fresh identity through the rhythms and movement of Nigerian music, with Young Jonn providing the creative link between the two styles.
For Desperados, the release goes beyond music to create opportunities for audience participation through dance moves, lifestyle content and fans’ own interpretations of the “Let It Go” experience.
The brand said the collaboration reinforces its association with music, culture and self-expression, positioning the song as a meeting point for different influences and shared experiences.
By blending Latin rhythms with Afrobeats, “Let It Go” seeks to capture the freedom of enjoying the moment and the role of music in bringing people together.

items.author: Nwafor
items.content:
By Johnbosco Agbakwuru
ABUJA —Nigeria’s First Lady, Senator Oluremi Tinubu, has urged state governors to establish functional community food banks in each of their three senatorial districts as part of efforts to strengthen food security and address malnutrition among vulnerable groups.
The First Lady made the call while formally handing over food items to the wife of the Katsina State Governor, Hajiya Zulaihat Dikko Radda, for distribution to vulnerable residents under the Renewed Hope Initiative’s (RHI) Food Outreach Scheme.
Senator Oluremi Tinubu, represented by the Wife of the Vice President, Hajiya Nana Shettima, announced that Katsina State had become the 30th beneficiary of the scheme, following distributions in 29 states and the Federal Capital Territory.
Mrs Tinubu in a statement by Kwapchi Bata Hamman, Special Assistant to the President Media and ICT, was quoted as saying: “Renewed Hope Initiative food outreach has so far successfully distributed food items to 29 states and the Federal Capital Territory, making Katsina the 30th beneficiary
“Insha Allah, Osun, Ogun and Akwa Ibom states will be the next beneficiaries of this growing initiative.
“Our goal at the Renewed Hope Initiative is to complement the Renewed Hope Agenda of President Bola Tinubu by ensuring that every Nigerian receives the support required, irrespective of their circumstances,” she said.
The First Lady according to the statement by Kwapchi Bata Hamman
Special Assistant to the President
Media and ICT, disclosed that the initiative is sustained by the generosity of two partners, who donate two truckloads of food items monthly, enabling it to support two states each month.
.
As part of efforts to tackle food insecurity and malnutrition, the First Lady also announced the successful nationwide rollout of the National Community Food Bank Programme, which aims to combat child malnutrition and support pregnant women and nursing mothers.
She called on state governors to adopt the framework and establish functional community food banks across their senatorial districts, stressing that federal and zonal interventions alone would not be enough to address the scale of the challenge.
Mrs Tinubu said stronger collaboration between the federal and state governments would help expand nutritional support to more communities and ensure vulnerable Nigerians have access to essential food supplies.
Katsina State Governor, Mallam Dikko Umaru Radda, CON, described the event as a day of hope and renewed commitment to the welfare of the people, noting that the intervention reflects the Federal Government’s resolve to reach vulnerable Nigerians at all levels.
He described the initiative as a practical intervention with tangible impact, complementing the Katsina State Government’s efforts to improve the well-being of its citizens.
The Governor noted that his administration in alignment with President Bola Ahmed Tinubu’s Renewed Hope Agenda is working towards building a future where every Nigerian could live with dignity through investments in Education , Healthcare and Agriculture .
He added that the state government has made concerted efforts to improve security across communities by supporting security agencies with the necessary equipment to strengthen their operations.
Governor Radda further stated that the Renewed Hope Agenda is designed to empower Nigerians to achieve their aspirations, urging the people of Katsina State to support the ruling party in the next election to sustain continuity in governance and development.
Hajiya Zulaihat Dikko The Wife of the Katsina State Governor expressed appreciation to the First Lady of Nigeria, Senator Oluremi Tinubu for the gesture stating that the Renewed Hope Initiative has continued to play an important role in promoting the welfare of Nigerians particularly women, persons with disabilities and other vulnerable groups through its various social intervention programmes.
Osun, Ogun and Akwa Ibom States are expected to be next beneficiaries of the food distribution Scheme
The food items were formally handed over to the Wife of the Katsina State Governor by Wife of the First President Hajiya Nana Shettima for distribution to the intended beneficiaries.
Launched in March 2024 under the Renewed Hope Initiative’s Social Investment Programme, the Food Outreach Scheme offers nutritional assistance to persons with disabilities, widows, and other vulnerable groups, helping to ease hardship and enhance family well-being.

items.author: Ayobami
items.content:
…Commission says check confirms type approval, verification for Nigerian networks
…231m devices in use before October 7 already verified
By Juliet Umeh
The Nigerian Communications Commission, NCC, has urged Nigerians to check the verification status of mobile phones before buying them, using its device checker code, *315#.
The commission said buyers could also use the device checker on its website to establish whether a phone had received type approval and had been verified for use on Nigerian mobile networks.
Speaking on Newsnight on Arise Television, the NCC’s Director of Technical Standards and Network Integrity, Eduyemi Ogoh, said the check was particularly important for people buying second-hand phones or devices imported from abroad.
“Before you buy the phone, dial *315# and confirm that the phone is fully verified before you pay,” he said.
Ogoh said the NCC introduced the checker to meet its statutory responsibility under the Nigerian Communications Act 2003, protect consumers and address complaints about poor network service linked to mobile devices.
“The whole intent of [type approval] is to ensure that every device coming into the country is genuine and works the way it should work,” he said.
He said consumers should be confident that they were spending their money on genuine devices, rather than “an old phone device that is fake or an imitation of the real thing.”
Ogoh said the commission had found that some service quality complaints were attributable to the devices consumers were using. Unapproved or improperly functioning phones could affect both their users and others in the same area, he added.
To check a phone, buyers can dial *315# and follow the prompts to enter its International Mobile Equipment Identity (IMEI), a unique number assigned to each mobile device. Ogoh said buyers could check a phone’s IMEI before paying, including by asking the seller to provide it.
A device that fails the check is not necessarily counterfeit, he said. Type approval involves laboratory testing of a phone model to establish that it meets applicable standards and can operate properly on Nigerian networks. Verification confirms that an individual device has been registered on the NCC’s device checker system using its IMEI.
“Type approval is done just once per model,” Ogoh said, adding that manufacturers, vendors or importers, not buyers, were responsible for obtaining it.
The enhanced compliance process applies to devices brought into the country from October 7. Ogoh said devices already operating on Nigerian networks at midnight on October 6 had been onboarded and verified. The NCC had registered about 231 million such devices, he said.
“We know that people have spent their money to do this, so you cannot be asking them to go and throw those phones out,” he said.
Ogoh also sought to allay privacy concerns, saying the checker uses only the IMEI to verify a device and does not give the NCC access to a user’s calls, contacts, messages or stored information.
He said verification could help buyers avoid unexpected device problems and establish whether poor service was caused by an unapproved phone.
Consumers with complaints about the device checker can dial 315, while the NCC’s consumer complaint line is 622.

items.title: Trump’s new press secretary leaves job after five days
items.author: Ayobami
items.content:
White House Press Secretary Katie Zacharia was pushed out Friday after less than a week in the high-profile job, following a series of blunders that added to distractions for her embattled boss President Donald Trump.
“Can confirm,” a White House official told AFP, after Fox News reported that Zacharia, 41, was “transitioning out.”
The writing was on the wall earlier when Trump made clear he was ready to see his newly minted spokeswoman go amid criticism that she had pretended to be a lawyer and over her one, much-mocked press briefing.
“I said, ‘Katie, is this for you?,'” Trump told reporters. “I said, ‘Katie, you don’t have to do this’… I said to her, ‘Honestly if I were you I’d reconsider.'”
Zacharia only began her job five days ago, taking over from the combative Karoline Leavitt, who helped Trump reshape White House coverage by bringing in more friendly outlets and fiercely attacking critical media.
Zacharia had got off to a rocky start with her debut press room briefing Tuesday morning.
It lasted less than 15 minutes, beginning with a remarkably slow reading out of what she said were Trump’s many accomplishments — then taking just three questions from journalists.
She then was plunged into controversy when it emerged that her previous claims to be a lawyer were not true.
The kerfuffle is a distraction for 80-year-old Trump as he flies around the country trying to boost Republican candidates ahead of the November 3 congressional midterm elections, with polls predicting a drubbing.
The Republican leader himself also faces ever-lower polls as Americans sour over the war against Iran, inflation and perceptions of corruption.
– Not a real lawyer –
Zacharia had described herself as a lawyer during television appearances and on social media, and listed herself as general counsel of a California-based conservative nonprofit.
While she does have a law degree from a California university, she acknowledged Thursday she had failed the bar exam, a prerequisite for practicing law in the United States.
She embarked on a series of damage-control interviews on Trump-friendly outlets, but they did no good.
In one of them, Fox News’ Sean Hannity, a close Trump ally, appeared dismissive of Zacharia.
He asked the press secretary if she ever retook the bar exam. She replied: “I did not.”
“It was never my intent to go into the practice of law,” she said.
In another interview Thursday with pro-Trump outlet Real America’s Voice, Zacharia said she had registered to take the bar exam but was “distracted and overwhelmed” by plans to move to China with her husband.
Zacharia said “many people in the field” had assured her that she could “label myself a lawyer,” given her law degree.
– China’s toilets –
“Fox and Friends,” which often conducts friendly interviews with Trump administration officials, was unusually direct Friday when a host asked Zacharia if she still had the confidence of the president.
“I hope to be able to build the trust and confidence of everyone around me,” she said, sidestepping the question.
Zacharia further stirred controversy on Thursday when she disparaged China, whose leader Xi Jinping was recently Trump’s guest in a pomp-filled Washington visit.
The press secretary recalled the perception in 2016 was that China would soon overtake the United States.
“I remember this very distinctly, having just come from China, thinking, ‘How is China the next country on the horizon? They don’t even have proper toilets,'” she told right-wing influencer Jack Posobiec in an interview.
Chinese Foreign Ministry spokeswoman Mao Ning responded Friday that Zacharia should “visit China more often.”

The trial continued in his absence, culminating in his conviction and sentence to 14 years’ imprisonment by Justice Okon Abang in 2021.

It further directed that, if found outside the country, the Federal Government should take lawful steps to secure his extradition to serve his prison term.
“The handover of Faisal to the EFCC is expected to facilitate the enforcement of the Court’s judgment and ensure that he serves his sentence in accordance with the law”, a source declared.

items.author: Ayobami
items.content:
By Golok Nanmwa, Jos
Gunmen have killed two persons at a mining site in Burdinga, Gashish District of Barkin Ladi Local Government Area of Plateau State, the Berom Youth Moulders-Association (BYM) has confirmed.
The victims, identified as Goodluck Bulus and Emmanuel Monday, both in their mid-20s, were reportedly killed on Friday, in an attack that has renewed concerns over persistent insecurity in the area.
Our correspondent gathered that the gunmen stormed the mining site at about 6pm and opened fire on the miners, killing the two young men.
The National Publicity Secretary of BYM, Rwang Tengwong, who confirmed the incident to newsmen, condemned the killings and called on the Plateau State Government and security agencies to take urgent action.
In a statement, Tengwong said, “The Berom Youth Moulders Association, under the leadership of its National President, Dalyop Solomon Mwantiri, strongly condemns the killing of two young men at a mining site in Burdinga, Gashish District, Barkin Ladi Local Government Area of Plateau State.”
He said, “The victims, identified as Goodluck Bulus and Emmanuel Monday, both in their mid-20s, represent yet another painful loss of young lives in a community already burdened by years of insecurity.”
The BYM spokesman said the killing was particularly heartbreaking because Goodluck’s father was reportedly killed in an attack more than a decade ago.
“More heartbreaking is the report that Goodluck’s father was killed in an attack by Fulani herdsmen more than a decade ago,” he said.
The association described the killings in the state by gunmen as a painful reminder of the human cost of insecurity, saying the incidents had left families devastated and communities living in fear.
“These are not mere statistics; they are human lives cut short, families shattered, and communities left in fear,” Tengwong said.
He called on the Plateau State Government and relevant security agencies to investigate the killings and ensure that those responsible were arrested and prosecuted.
“We therefore call on the Plateau State Government and relevant security agencies to urgently investigate these killings, apprehend and prosecute the perpetrators, strengthen security surveillance around mining sites and vulnerable communities, and establish effective measures to protect residents and commuters,” he said.
The BYM spokesman also called for sustained security operations and intelligence-driven interventions to prevent further attacks, abductions and killings across the state.
“We also demand sustained security operations and intelligence-driven interventions to prevent further attacks, abductions and killings across Plateau State,” he said.
He added, “The continued loss of innocent lives must not become normalised. The people deserve protection, the victims deserve justice, and the perpetrators must be held accountable.”

items.author: Ayobami
items.content:
The National Agency for Food and Drug Administration and Control (NAFDAC) has debunked reports that a Corp member whose death occurred in Enugu died of effects of substandard and falsified medicines.
This is contained in a statement by the Director-General of the agency, Prof Mojisola Adeyeye, in Abuja on Friday.
The statement noted that the deceased Corp member previously at NYSC Orientation Camp, Awgu, in Enugu State, did not die of what people insinuated.
According to the statement, preliminary investigations revealed that the Corp member was brought to the Camp clinic aided by two other Corp members on Wednesday, Oct. 7, at about 9:00pm with symptoms suggestive of severe malaria and a known peptic ulcer disease patient.
The statement stated that the deceased was however, stabilised with intramuscular antimalarial and other supportive medications given intravenously.
It stated that the deceased was placed on bed rest for observation till Oct 8 morning when he was discharged with oral medications.
“He came back unaided on Saturday, Oct. 10, with complaints of right thigh pain for which he was asked to see a physiotherapist.
“His profuse sweating caught the attention of the medical doctor, who measured his blood pressure and found it to be low (80/40 mmHg). He was stabilised with intravenous Normal Saline.
“Serial monitoring showed recurrent episodes of hypertension. This development, coupled with poor urine output despite adequate fluid resuscitations, prompted his referral to the University of Nigeria Teaching Hospital (UNTH), Ituku-Ozalla, Enugu State, in an ambulance accompanied by another doctor.
“He went into a coma at about the time of arriving at the UNTH. All efforts at resuscitating him failed.
“His friend later informed the Camp clinic doctor that his deceased friend was vomiting for two days after the initial admission at the camp. The doctor was not aware of this development.
“It is instructive to note that the same medications given to the deceased were also administered to several other patients in the camp who got well after receiving their treatments.
“The medical doctors, pharmacists, and other healthcare workers at the camp clinic not only prescribed but also used the medications by themselves at different times,” the statement said.
According to the statement, the doctors believed that the cause of death was acute kidney injury secondary to severe dehydration and shock in the meantime.
It stated that NAFDAC officers had visited the clinic, interviewed the doctors and other staff and taken samples of the medications for further necessary actions which included laboratory analysis.
The NAFDAC commiserates with the family of the late Youth Corp member and prays that God grants the family the fortitude to bear the irreparable loss.
NAFDAC, however, enjoined the general public to remain calm as the agency was taking all necessary steps to ensure that all medicines made available to the public were safe and of good quality and efficacious.
It advised the public to call the NAFDAC Call Centre on the following lines: 0800-1-623322 or 0700-1-623322 for complaints and enquiries.
The agency also advised the general public to email reforms@nafdac.gov.ng (NAN).

items.title: Ex-convicts arrested over alleged N50m robbery in Osun
items.summary:

The suspects were arrested at separate locations in Lagos by operatives of the command’s Anti-Kidnapping Unit after months of investigation.

items.content:
Two ex-convicts, Ejike Ani, 32, and Chubuzor Anasihwe, 31, have been arrested by operatives of the Lagos State Police Command over alleged robbery operations along the Ife-Ilesha Expressway in Osun State, where five vehicles and valuables estimated at N50m were reportedly stolen.
The suspects were arrested at separate locations in Lagos by operatives of the command’s Anti-Kidnapping Unit after months of investigation.
The Commissioner of Police, Fatai Tijani, disclosed that preliminary investigations linked the suspects to robbery incidents allegedly committed on August 20 and September 20, 2026.
According to him, the arrests followed a directive by the Inspector-General of Police, Olatunji Disu, to intensify the fight against criminal activities nationwide.

Rivers: DPO removed over alleged renovation of police station by cultists
“During interrogation, the suspects reportedly revealed that they met while serving jail terms at the Kirikiri Correctional Centre in Lagos and later reunited after their release,” he said.
Ani, an indigene of Ebonyi State and a former clothes seller, blamed his alleged involvement in robbery on poverty, debts and his mother’s medical expenses.
He said he returned to his village after his release from prison in January 2026 but became frustrated by his inability to meet his mother’s eye surgery expenses, estimated at N800,000, and settle outstanding debts.
Ani said he subsequently contacted a former prison acquaintance, identified as Chinedu, who invited him to Lagos and introduced him to other alleged gang members.
He claimed the gang initially abandoned an attempted robbery after motorists were alerted to their presence, but later returned to the highway, where they allegedly dispossessed three men assisting occupants of a broken-down vehicle of a Toyota Corolla, mobile phones and cash.
He further alleged that the gang later snatched a bus during heavy rainfall and robbed a vehicle belonging to a traditional ruler.
Ani claimed the monarch and his driver escaped, while the gang took valuables from the vehicle.
He alleged that he received only N20,000 in two separate payments as his share of the proceeds from one of the operations.
He also claimed the gang sometimes used sticks wrapped in sellotape and fireworks to imitate firearms.
Anasihwe, who also previously sold clothes on Lagos Island, said he met Ani in prison while serving a sentence following a fight with two passengers during his time as a commercial motorcyclist.
He said they reunited in Ijora after their release and subsequently participated in a robbery operation.
However, he denied involvement in the robbery involving the traditional ruler, claiming he had already been arrested.
Meanwhile, investigations were still ongoing to establish the suspects’ respective roles in the alleged robberies.

Operatives of the Department of State Services (DSS), the military and police have arrested five suspected members of a criminal gang allegedly responsible for the abduction of 20 prospective National Youth Service Corps (NYSC) members in Imo State on Nigeria’s 66th Independence Day.

The string of operations mark a significant breakthrough in efforts to track down the perpetrators, dismantle the criminal network allegedly responsible for the abduction and bring those involved to justice.
A security source described the development as a major relief, noting that security agencies had sustained a wide-ranging manhunt for the abductors.
“This is a huge sigh of relief. Security agencies have been on a manhunt for the abductors, and we are elated that they have been captured. We strongly believe they will be charged to Court by DSS and the corps members will get justice,” the source said.

items.content:
A private jet operated by Triton Aviation made an emergency landing at the Nnamdi Azikiwe International Airport, Abuja, after losing a door mid-air on Thursday.
The Nigerian Safety Investigation Bureau (NSIB) confirmed the incident to TheCable on Friday, saying an investigation had commenced.
“The incident happened yesterday and investigations are ongoing,” a source at the bureau said.
According to a report by Punch on Friday, the aircraft, with registration number T7-SEI and flight identification DWC052, was heading to the Murtala Muhammed International Airport, Lagos, when the incident occurred at about 4:20 pm.
Citing an incident report, the publication said the aircraft was about three nautical miles from the airport and climbing through 3,000 feet when the crew issued a distress call.
“Mayday, Mayday, Mayday,” the crew reportedly transmitted.
Following the distress call, airport fire and emergency personnel, alongside the medical team, were alerted and placed on standby.
Fire and rescue teams were also directed to designated positions in preparation for the aircraft’s return.
The report further stated that at about 4:29 pm UTC, while communicating with the Abuja control tower, the crew asked whether air traffic controllers could confirm if the door was open.
“The duty air traffic controller attempted to observe the aircraft using binoculars, but could not establish the door’s condition because of the aircraft’s position. The crew was subsequently informed that the controller could not confirm the situation visually,” the report said.
The aircraft subsequently landed safely on Runway 22 at approximately 4:34 pm UTC, about 14 minutes after the Mayday call.
Following the landing, the duty controller reportedly observed that the aircraft’s door was missing from the fuselage.
The jet was then taxied to the international apron extension and parked with the assistance of a marshaller.
Meanwhile, a video circulating on social media showed what appeared to be an aircraft door lying on farmland near Abuja.
According to Billionaires.Africa, the NSIB confirmed that the door had been recovered.
“The door has been recovered and secured at the NSIB wreckage hangar,” the bureau said.
The NSIB said it had commenced an investigation to establish the circumstances surrounding the incident and would provide updates as the investigation progresses.

items.content:
…Says omission will be addressed soon, insists PDP candidate will win
By James Ogunnaike, Abeokuta
The Deputy Governorship Candidate of the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) in the 2027 Ogun State governorship election, Hajia Yemi Sowunmi-Kolapo, has expressed confidence that the omission of her principal, Ladi Adebutu, from a list published by the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) was unintentional and would be addressed soon.
Sowunmi-Kolapo also expressed confidence that Adebutu would emerge as the next governor of Ogun State in the 2027 election, describing recent political developments in the state as signs of the ticket’s growing prospects.
She spoke with journalists and Muslim faithful shortly after Jumat prayers at the headquarters of the Nawair-ud-Deen Society in Abeokuta on Friday.
The gathering featured prayers for the PDP governorship ticket, with leaders of the Muslim society expressing support for Sowunmi-Kolapo and Adebutu ahead of the election.
The Chief Imam of the Nawair-ud-Deen Society’s Abeokuta headquarters and Ogun State, Sheikh Tiamiyu Olamigoke, led other Islamic leaders in prayers for the candidates’ success and the continued peace and development of Ogun State.
The clerics acknowledged Sowunmi-Kolapo’s contributions to the Muslim community and her record of service before venturing into partisan politics, expressing confidence that she would demonstrate compassion and commitment to public service if elected alongside Adebutu.
They also cited Adebutu’s contributions to the development of Ogun State, including his support for the Muslim community, as reasons he deserved the electorate’s backing.
Addressing the controversy surrounding the INEC list, Sowunmi-Kolapo dismissed suggestions that Adebutu’s omission, alongside celebrations reportedly witnessed among members of the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC), indicated an advantage for the party ahead of the 2027 governorship election.
She maintained that the omission was not deliberate and would be resolved by the electoral commission.
Sowunmi-Kolapo described the appointment of Professor Joash Amupitan as INEC chairman as one of the appointments she believed President Bola Tinubu had got right.
She described Amupitan as a globally recognised professional and expressed confidence that he would protect his reputation by upholding the integrity of the electoral process.
While acknowledging the pressures associated with the position, the PDP deputy governorship candidate said she remained optimistic that the INEC chairman would discharge his responsibilities professionally.
She also expressed confidence in Tinubu’s commitment to ensuring free, fair and credible elections, irrespective of the political interests involved.
Reacting to the excitement reportedly expressed by APC members following the publication of the INEC list, Sowunmi-Kolapo described their reaction as premature, insisting that it would not determine the outcome of the 2027 governorship election.
“They are ‘soon-to-be IDPs (Internally Displaced Politicians),’ exhibiting the symptoms of ‘IDPA (Impending Defeat Panic Attack),’” she said with laughter.
She maintained that no force could stop what she described as a genuine movement driven by people determined to protect their heritage and secure a better future for coming generations.
“We will soon separate the wheat from the chaff. There is a difference between those fighting for their pockets or struggling to retain their juicy positions and those fighting to protect our heritage in the interest of generations of genuine Ogun indigenes, who must not be relegated to second-class citizens by imported leaders,” she said.
Sowunmi-Kolapo stressed the need for Ogun State’s resources to be deployed for the benefit of its people, describing the principle as the foundation of the PDP’s ITURA DE agenda.
“Ogun’s resources must work for its people. This is the bedrock of our ITURA DE mandate. A PDP administration led by Hon. Ladi Adebutu will prioritise the welfare of citizens and ensure real financial autonomy for local governments, with a view to promoting accountability and effective service delivery at the grassroots,” she said.
Earlier, the Otun Iya Sunnah of Egbaland and Iya Sunnah of the Nawair-ud-Deen Society, Alhaja Risikat Ogunfemi, urged members of the society, the Egba Muslim Community and the wider Ogun State Muslim Community to support Sowunmi-Kolapo and Adebutu.
Ogunfemi described the deputy governorship candidate as a source of pride to the Muslim community and expressed confidence that she would prioritise the welfare of the people if elected alongside Adebutu.
The gathering ended with prayers by imams and Islamic scholars for the protection and success of the PDP candidates in the 2027 election, as well as peace, progress and prosperity in Ogun State.
The post 2027: Adebutu’s omission from INEC list unintentional — Sowunmi-Kolapo appeared first on Vanguard News.

items.content:
By Sola Ogundipe
The Federal Government has approved a ₦40.76 billion disbursement under the Basic Health Care Provision Fund (BHCPF) for the third quarter of 2026, combining a major financial boost for primary healthcare with the extension of health insurance to nearly 90,000 prison inmates nationwide. The approved allocation marks an increase of approximately ₦7.88 billion over the previous quarter’s allocation of ₦32.88 billion.
The Coordinating Minister of Health and Social Welfare, Prof. Muhammad Ali Pate, disclosed the decisions in Abuja following the 16th meeting of the Ministerial Oversight Committee (MOC) on the BHCPF. He said the decisions reinforce the Federal Government’s commitment to quality, affordable and accessible healthcare, particularly for poor, vulnerable and underserved populations, in line with the Renewed Hope Agenda and the Nigeria Health Sector Renewal Investment Initiative (NHSRII).
Pate noted that monthly statutory releases into the Fund had increased from approximately ₦8.95 billion to ₦13.08 billion and subsequently ₦20.43 billion. He stressed that increased financing must translate into timely disbursement, transparent financial management and improved health outcomes.
According to the Minister, the approved Q3 fund is being distributed across the four statutory gateways according to their required shares.
“The National Health Insurance Authority (NHIA) receives ₦19.87 billion (48.75 percent), while the National Primary Health Care Development Agency (NPHCDA) gets ₦18.34 billion (45 percent). Additionally, the National Emergency Medical Service and Ambulance System (NEMSAS) receives ₦2.04 billion (5 percent), and the Nigeria Centre for Disease Control (NCDC) is allocated ₦509.48 million (1.25 percent).”
To widen healthcare access, the Minister announced plans to expand BHCPF support from 8,309 to 13,521 primary healthcare facilities nationwide, adding 5,212 facilities across the 36 states and the Federal Capital Territory.
To improve access to essential medicines, the MOC approved the operationalisation of changes to the NPHCDA gateway, including pooled procurement through MEDIPOOL, Nigeria’s national Group Purchasing Organisation. The arrangement will incorporate value-for-money safeguards, pricing benchmarks and supply-chain monitoring to strengthen transparency, quality assurance and reliable commodity supply.
Following a request from the Nigerian Correctional Service, the Committee approved extending health insurance coverage to approximately 90,000 inmates of correctional facilities nationwide through the NHIA, the implementation will be subject to regular reporting and safeguards, with inmates already covered by state schemes excluded.
The Committee also considered a phased financing model to support states in recruiting and progressively absorbing Skilled Birth Attendants and Community-Based Health Workers.
To address funding delays, the MOC resolved to establish a subcommittee to investigate bottlenecks in the flow of funds through the gateways, states and local government areas to health facilities, with the subcommittee expected to report within six weeks. The Committee also directed that letters be sent to state governors on the financial requirements for the NCDC to respond adequately to disease outbreaks.
On accountability, Pate said the Federal Government was collaborating with the Independent Corrupt Practices and Other Related Offences Commission (ICPC) to track health sector funds and prevent their misapplication.
“Government will not condone any act that is capable of depriving ordinary Nigerians of the health goods these funds are meant for,” he said.
Pate commended the Governor of Katsina State for releasing ₦243 million to the State Health Insurance Agency to expand BHCPF coverage and urged other states and the FCT to fulfil their counterpart funding obligations under the National Health Act, 2014.
The Federal Government reaffirmed its commitment to strengthening primary healthcare financing, expanding access to essential services and ensuring that public health investments deliver measurable improvements in the lives of Nigerians, particularly the most vulnerable.

items.content:
Iran on Friday denied having anything to do with attacks by Yemen’s Houthis, a day after Saudi Arabia accused it of having encouraged the group’s recent escalation against the kingdom.
Since Yemen’s civil war flared back to life in July, the pro-Iran Houthis have repeatedly struck Saudi targets including Red Sea tankers, oil facilities and Riyadh’s international airport, where 13 people were killed in a single attack last week.
A Saudi-led military coalition has supported Yemen’s internationally recognised government for more than a decade, and reported on Friday having intercepted more missiles and drones as the kingdom comes under sustained attack from the Houthis.
A day earlier, a Saudi foreign ministry official said Iran had “encouraged” the escalation, which Tehran denied.
“The Islamic Republic of Iran rejects any claim that Iran has played a role in Yemeni (Houthi) operations,” Iranian foreign ministry spokesman Esmaeil Baqaei said in a statement.
“Yemen’s armed forces act according to their own interests and assessments, and such claims are not credible to those familiar with relations between Iran and its friends. Nevertheless, Iran does not consider an escalation of tensions to be in the interests of any party,” he added.
The Saudi official, deputy minister for public diplomacy Dr. Rayed Krimly, had said the Houthis rejected an offer to meet in Oman at the outset of the latest round of hostilities.
Baqaei however reiterated an offer to mediate between the two sides, saying Tehran “has always been ready to use its good offices to help end the hostilities”.
On Friday, a spokesman for the Saudi-led military coalition said it had “intercepted and destroyed three drones in the southern area and Riyadh… and two cruise missiles over the Red Sea”.
He added that “in the past hours, we intercepted and destroyed a ballistic missile over Yanbu”, a city home to the terminus of a major oil pipeline on the Red Sea coast.
The Houthi attacks have proliferated since the group launched a lightning offensive in Yemen in September, seizing strategic government-held territory along the Red Sea coast overlooking a major chokepoint for global shipping.
The pressure on Saudi Arabia, the world’s largest oil exporter, comes as global energy markets were already rattled by Iran’s closure of the Strait of Hormuz at the outset of the wider Middle East war in February.
– Palace struck –
The UN Security Council on Thursday “condemned in the strongest terms continued and escalatory Houthi attacks against the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia”, as well as their “attacks and threats against commercial shipping in the Red Sea and Bab al-Mandab” Strait, the southern gateway to the Suez Canal.
The Security Council also denounced the group’s “reckless strikes” on Riyadh’s airport, which the Saudi-led coalition said had been targeted at least 20 times so far this month.
Krimly, of the Saudi foreign ministry, accused Iran on Thursday of continuing “to arm, train and support the Houthi militia in violation of UN security council resolutions”.
“We think that the escalation by the Houthis at this latest stage of the conflict is encouraged by Iran,” he added.
Yemeni government forces have launched a counteroffensive with Saudi air support to retake areas seized by the Houthis, but have so far failed to reverse their gains.
On Thursday, the group launched a deadly missile attack on the presidential palace in the interim seat of the Yemeni government in Aden, killing five people and wounding 16 others, according to the health minister.
Yemeni Prime Minister Shaya al-Zindani denounced the “cowardly” act on X, calling it a “continuation of (the Houthis’) criminal pattern”.
A government minister said on condition of anonymity that Zindani had been present at the time, but “was not harmed in any way”.
The minister said the Houthis hit a command centre for Yemeni government forces at the complex with three missiles, and another for Saudi coalition forces with two missiles.
Media affiliated with the Houthis said they had targeted “the headquarters of military operations, led by Saudi officers, at the Al-Maashiq Palace in Aden, as well as weapons depots belonging to them”.
The post Iran denies Saudi accusation of involvement in Houthi attacks appeared first on Vanguard News.

By Dickson Omobola
United Nigeria Airlines Company Limited is set to become the first domestic airline to issue commercial paper, with an initial tranche of N20 billion under its N100 billion programme.
According to its September 2026 investor presentation, which outlined its financial performance and five-year expansion strategy, the commercial paper will be issued in Series 1 and 2, with tenors of 270 days and 364 days, respectively. The proposed issuance will be the first under the airline’s N100 billion commercial paper programme.
Meristem Capital Limited will serve as the lead arranger for the transaction, while Cordros Advisory Services Limited, Coronation Merchant Bank Limited, FCMB Capital Markets Limited, FSL Advisory Limited and Quantum Zenith Capital & Investments Limited will serve as dealers.
The issuance comes as the airline seeks to strengthen its financial position and expand its domestic, regional and international operations.
United Nigeria Airlines has also secured investment-grade ratings from two rating agencies. Agusto & Co. assigned the airline a short-term rating of A3 and a long-term rating of BBB-, with a stable outlook, while DataPro assigned it short-term and long-term ratings of A1 and BBB, respectively.
The airline’s financial performance has recorded significant growth, with revenue rising from N10.3 billion in the 2021 financial year to N90.8 billion in 2025.
Profit after tax also increased from N1.3 billion to N23.8 billion over the same period.
The airline recorded revenue of N95.6 billion in the first half of 2026. Its August performance also showed an improvement, with turnover rising to N19.4 billion from N14.1 billion in July, while it returned to a net profit of N1.2 billion.
The airline expressed optimism that its performance would continue on an upward trajectory for the rest of the year and beyond.
United Nigeria Airlines currently operates 10 aircraft, including Embraer ERJ-145s, Boeing 737-800s, Embraer E190s and CRJ900s. It plans to take delivery of six additional aircraft before the end of the year.

. As Tijani commissions first NUCAP site in Abia
. Kalu identifies 16 more locations needing coverage in Bende
By Steve Oko
UMUAHIA — The Federal Government has unveiled plans to deploy 3,700 telecommunications towers nationwide to connect about 20 million Nigerians currently without access to telephone and internet services.
Minister of Communications, Innovation and Digital Economy, Dr Bosun Tijani, disclosed this on Friday while commissioning a telecommunications tower under the National Universal Communications Access Programme (NUCAP) in Bende, Abia State.
Tijani said the Bende facility was the first site being commissioned under the national initiative aimed at extending reliable telecommunications and broadband services to unserved and underserved communities.
“President Bola Ahmed Tinubu has given us a clear mandate: work towards bringing every Nigerian online. Through NUCAP, we are delivering 3,700 telecommunications towers across Nigeria. Today, we are commissioning the first of these sites here. More will follow across the country in the coming days, weeks and months,” he said.
The minister said the project was designed to bridge the digital divide and ensure that geographical location did not prevent Nigerians from accessing opportunities.
According to him, rural farmers should be able to contact buyers without struggling to find network signals, while traders should not lose sales because customers cannot make electronic transfers.
He also said families should be able to contact loved ones and seek emergency assistance without the difficulties associated with poor network coverage.
Tijani urged residents to see the telecommunications tower as an investment whose benefits would extend beyond immediate connectivity to education, commerce, skills acquisition and improved social interaction.
Drawing an analogy between the tower and a tree, he said its benefits would grow over time, creating opportunities for farmers to find new markets, young people to acquire digital skills, traders to secure orders from other towns and families to communicate more easily.
He assured that the intervention in Bende would not end with the commissioning of the first facility, adding that the Federal Government would continue working with Deputy Speaker of the House of Representatives, Rt. Hon. Benjamin Okezie Kalu, network operators and community leaders to reach other unconnected communities.
Speaking at the event, Kalu described reliable telecommunications connectivity as a critical requirement for financial inclusion, education and effective healthcare delivery, particularly in rural communities.
He said that although reliable network service might appear ordinary to people who enjoyed it daily, its absence could deny rural residents economic opportunities and access to essential services.
“For a rural trader whose payment repeatedly fails, a student who cannot join an online lesson, or a family struggling to contact a doctor, it is anything but ordinary. It can determine whether an opportunity is secured or lost,” Kalu said.
The Deputy Speaker noted that financial inclusion increasingly depended on reliable telecommunications infrastructure, as mobile banking applications, electronic transfers and agent banking services required dependable network coverage.
He explained that poor connectivity could prevent traders from confirming payments, make it difficult for farmers to receive money for their produce and deny households access to funds sent by relatives.
According to him, improved connectivity, combined with affordable services, financial literacy and consumer protection, would help more rural residents participate in the formal economy.
On education, Kalu said the facility would expand learning opportunities beyond the physical classroom, enabling pupils to access online lessons and educational materials while helping teachers improve their skills through wider learning resources.
He added that young people in Bende would be better positioned to apply for scholarships, acquire digital skills and explore opportunities without travelling elsewhere simply to access a network signal.
“The talent is already here in Bende. We must provide the connections through which that talent can grow,” he said.
Kalu also identified healthcare as a major beneficiary of the intervention, noting that reliable connectivity would enable health workers to consult specialists, exchange medical information securely and coordinate referrals for patients in remote communities.
He further linked the project to civic engagement and public safety, saying residents needed access to accurate information and reliable channels to communicate with their representatives, while electoral and emergency personnel required dependable communication networks.
Describing Bende’s location and proximity to neighbouring states as an advantage, the Deputy Speaker said improved connectivity would facilitate trade, movement and relationships among communities beyond the constituency.
He, however, disclosed that 16 additional locations requiring telecommunications intervention had been identified in Bende Federal Constituency.
Kalu urged the Ministry of Communications, Innovation and Digital Economy and its implementing partners to work with his office and community leaders to validate the locations, assess coverage gaps and establish a clear programme for extending services to them.
He stressed that the success of the intervention would depend not only on installing towers but also on ensuring reliable service, adequate power supply, regular maintenance and prompt repairs when faults occurred.
The Deputy Speaker expressed appreciation to President Bola Tinubu and the Federal Ministry of Communications, Innovation and Digital Economy for the initiative and for choosing Bende for the commissioning.
He also commended Abia State Governor, Dr Alex Otti, for supporting federal development efforts in the state, assuring that he would continue to collaborate with the state government to accelerate development.
Kalu called on traditional rulers and Presidents-General of town unions to protect the telecommunications infrastructure against vandalism, describing it as a critical national asset whose benefits should be safeguarded for present and future generations.
The event featured a live demonstration of e-learning at Bende Grammar School using the newly deployed infrastructure and the distribution of mobile phones to constituents.
