items.author: Nwafor
items.content:
By Ndahi Marama, Maiduguri
The African Democratic Congress (ADC) in Borno State and former Commissioner for Home Affairs, Information and Culture, Inuwa Bwala, have traded accusations over claims about Governor Babagana Zulum’s treatment of opposition parties in the state.
The dispute followed a Facebook post by Bwala defending Zulum’s record on political tolerance, which the ADC described as a distortion of the situation on the ground.
In a statement issued on Thursday, the ADC State Publicity Secretary, Baba Ahmed Mustapha, challenged Bwala’s position, citing the demolition of a property belonging to opposition figure Atom Magira, alleged threats against opposition supporters, the detention of youths who displayed “Tinubu Must Go” placards, and claims that the party had faced restrictions on campaign venues and billboards.
But Bwala dismissed the ADC’s response, questioning Mustapha’s experience in public communication and describing the party’s statement as an attempt to misrepresent his earlier analysis.
The ADC said it was disheartening for Bwala to portray Zulum’s administration as tolerant of opposition parties.
“Ordinarily, we would not join issues with a former commissioner looking for relevance and patronage, but when falsehood is dressed as analysis, the record must be set straight for Borno people and for history,” Mustapha said.
The party questioned whether the demolition of Magira’s three-storey plaza in Maiduguri, alleged threats by the Commissioner for Sports, Youths and Poverty Alleviation, Saina Buba, and the arrest and detention of five youths who displayed “Tinubu Must Go” placards were consistent with political tolerance.
It also alleged that it had been denied approvals for campaign venues in Maiduguri, that its billboards had been removed by the Borno State Environmental Protection Agency (BOSEPA), and that some of its members had been profiled.
The ADC called on the Nigerian Bar Association, Borno Chapter, the Nigeria Union of Journalists and civil society organisations to speak out over what it described as a shrinking political space in the state.
However, Bwala denied that his earlier article was directed at the ADC, saying it was an opinion piece written from his perspective as a member of the All Progressives Congress (APC).
“In the first place, what I wrote was neither a letter nor a rejoinder, rather, it was an opinionated analysis from a partisan viewpoint, because I am a stakeholder, as a member of the APC,” he said.
Bwala also rejected the ADC’s claim that Magira’s property was demolished because of his political affiliation.
He said the Borno State Urban Planning Board (BOSUPB) had issued multiple notices over alleged violations of building approval requirements and encroachment on the right of way.
According to him, properties belonging to APC members had also been demolished for similar violations.
“To reduce an urban renewal enforcement to ‘opposition witch-hunt’ is mischief, no matter what coloration you try to give it,” he said.
Bwala challenged the ADC to publish any court judgment supporting its claim that due process was not followed in the demolition.
On the alleged threat by Buba, Bwala said the commissioner had clarified his remarks, which he described as a warning against political violence and thuggery at a youth rally.
He said the ADC was interpreting the comments as a threat to attract public sympathy, adding that any genuine threat should be reported to the police.
Addressing the arrest of the youths who displayed “Tinubu Must Go” placards, Bwala said security agencies acted to maintain public order during a period of heightened tension.
He denied that Zulum ordered their detention and said the state government facilitated their release after preliminary investigations.
“I challenge the ADC to prove otherwise,” he said.
Bwala also disputed the party’s claim that it had been denied campaign venues and that its billboards had been removed unfairly, urging it to produce documentary evidence of rejected applications and the removal of the billboards.
He argued that opposition parties had held major rallies in Borno during the 2023 elections without attacks, and said Zulum had encouraged constructive criticism of his administration.
On the governor’s support for President Bola Tinubu and Vice-President Kashim Shettima ahead of the 2027 elections, Bwala said the position reflected political conviction rather than an attempt to undermine opposition parties.
He advised the ADC to concentrate on building its structures at the ward level rather than engaging in public exchanges with him or the governor.
“Professor Zulum will not be distracted. He is focused on resettlement, security, and rebuilding Borno,” Bwala said.

items.author: Nwafor
items.content:
By Juliet Umeh
Pan-African technology company, Onafriq, has announced plans to wind down its agent banking business in Nigeria, operated under the Baxi brand by Onafriq Nigeria Payments Limited, citing inflation, naira depreciation and intensifying competition.
The company said the economic pressures had increased operating costs and affected transaction volumes, while the rapid growth of instant account-to-account payments had altered the mix of transactions handled by point-of-sale (PoS) agents.
It added that tighter margins and increased competition had further undermined the sustainability of its agent banking operations.
Onafriq said it entered Nigeria’s agent banking market in 2021 through the acquisition of Baxi, also known as Capricorn Digital Limited, and invested in the business through 2023 to strengthen and expand its agent network.
“This investment reflected the Group’s belief in agent banking’s role in expanding financial access and digitising cash-based transactions,” the company said in a statement.
However, it said trading conditions changed significantly from 2024, prompting a review of the long-term strategy and sustainability of the operation.
Founder and Chief Executive Officer of Onafriq, Dare Okoudjou, said the company entered the Nigerian market “with conviction and commitment” but did not achieve its expected results.
“Closing this business was a difficult decision to arrive at, one that affects colleagues, agents, and business partners across Nigeria who poured their hearts and soul into building out the Baxi network,” he said.
Okoudjou said the company remained committed to ensuring “honesty, fairness, and a well-managed transition” for those affected by the decision.
The planned closure will affect employees whose roles are linked to the agent banking business. Onafriq said it would consult each affected employee and provide support throughout the transition.
The company also disclosed that agents using the Baxi payments platform had been transferred to another principal bank. It advised them to move their funds to a principal bank of their choice within 30 days.
“Onafriq’s teams are available to provide support and guidance throughout the process,” the statement said, adding that the company would honour its commitments to affected stakeholders and maintain open communication during the transition.
Despite the planned closure, Okoudjou said the decision was limited to the agent banking business and did not represent the company’s exit from Nigeria.
“Nigeria remains central to our mission, and we will continue to serve the market as a Payment Solution Service Provider through the Onafriq payments network and our card issuing services,” he said.
Onafriq said it would now focus on integrating its payments network and card-issuing services into Nigeria’s financial ecosystem.

items.content: Shares of major US banks headed for their longest weekly losing streak since the 2008 global financial crisis after mixed quarterly earnings failed to improve sentiment toward the struggling sector, Bloomberg News reported.The 24-member KBW Bank Index fell about 1.3% during the week and remained in correction territory, having declined roughly 13% from its August record. Although the group had suffered steeper selloffs—including a nearly 17% decline earlier in the year—it was on course for a sixth consecutive weekly loss, its longest such run since 2008.Bank stocks had already come under pressure amid concerns about how artificial intelligence could disrupt financial services. A hotter-than-expected inflation reading added to uncertainty over how aggressively the Federal Reserve would act to rein in persistent price pressures.Also Read | Chip selloff deepens Wall Street losses as doubts grew over AI returnsAccording to Bloomberg Intelligence analyst Herman Chan, large banks faced several challenges, including the prospect of interest rates remaining elevated for longer, which could slow economic growth and increase loan losses. Third-quarter results did little to reverse the weakness, as disappointing fixed-income trading offset strength in equities.Persistent weakness in bank shares also raised concerns about the wider economy because lenders played a key role in supporting growth through credit.Chan said rising funding costs for AI companies had created fresh uncertainty about the durability of capital-markets revenue linked to infrastructure investment. He added that agentic AI could pose a longer-term threat to the stable, low-cost deposits that supported bank profitability.The KBW Bank Index underperformed the S&P 500 in 18 of the 21 trading sessions following the Fed’s September 16 interest-rate increase, Barclays analyst Jason Goldberg wrote. He said no comparable rolling 21-session stretch had occurred since the index was created in May 1992.(Disclaimer: This article is based on inputs from agencies. …As Nawair-ud-deen Society Offers Prayers, Support
By Jimoh Babatunde
The deputy governorship candidate of the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) in Ogun State for the 2027 election, Hajia Yemi Sowunmi-Kolapo, has expressed confidence that her principal, Ladi Adebutu, will emerge as the next governor of the state.
Kolapo spoke on Friday after Jumat prayers at the headquarters of the Nawair-ud-deen Society in Abeokuta, where leaders of the Muslim organisation offered prayers for her and Adebutu ahead of the 2027 elections.
She said recent developments in the political space, including the controversy surrounding a list published by the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC), reinforced her confidence in the PDP ticket.
The leaders, led by the Chief Imam of the Nawair-ud-deen Society in Abeokuta and Ogun State, Sheikh Tiamiyu Olamigoke, took turns to pray for the success of the candidates.
They described Kolapo, who is the Iya Sunnah of Egbaland and Ameerah of Ogun State Muslims, as a compassionate prospective leader, citing her conduct and community service before entering politics.
The leaders also said Adebutu had contributed to the welfare of Ogun residents, including members of the Muslim community, and deserved their support.
Responding to questions about the jubilation among members of the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC) following the publication of the controversial INEC list, Kolapo expressed confidence that the omission in question was unintentional.
She commended the appointment of INEC Chairman, Prof. Joash Amupitan, by President Bola Tinubu, describing him as a globally recognised professional whose integrity she believed would withstand political pressure.
Kolapo also expressed confidence in Tinubu’s commitment to ensuring free and fair elections, irrespective of the political interests involved.
She dismissed the excitement among APC members over the INEC list as a sign of panic, describing their reaction as a “dead-on-arrival mission.”
“They are ‘soon-to-be IDPs (Internally Displaced Politicians)’ exhibiting the symptoms of ‘IDPA (Impending Defeat Panic Attack),” she said, drawing laughter from those present.
The PDP deputy governorship candidate maintained that no force could stop what she described as a genuine movement by people determined to protect their heritage.
“We will soon separate the wheat from the chaff. There is a difference between people who are fighting for their pockets or fighting to retain their juicy positions and those fighting to protect our heritage, in the interest of generations of true Ogun indigenes, who must not be relegated to second-class citizens by imported leaders,” she said.
Kolapo said the PDP’s Itura De mandate would prioritise citizens’ welfare and ensure greater financial autonomy for local governments to promote accountability and grassroots service delivery.
She added that an Adebutu-led administration would seek to ensure that Ogun State’s resources worked for the benefit of its people.
Earlier, the Otun Iya Sunnah of Egbaland and Iya Sunnah of the Nawair-ud-deen Society, Alhaja Risikat Ogunfemi, urged members of the society, the Egba Muslim Community and Muslims across Ogun State to support Kolapo and her principal.
Ogunfemi described Kolapo as a source of pride to the Muslim community, expressing confidence that she would serve the people if elected alongside Adebutu.
The gathering ended with joint prayers for the PDP ticket, the protection of both candidates and the continued progress of Ogun State.
The post Ogun 2027: Adebutu will win, running mate insists appeared first on Vanguard News.

items.author: Nwafor
items.content:
…accuses him of aiding Tinubu
By Luminous Jannamike
ABUJA – The African Democratic Congress Presidential Campaign Council, ADC-PCC, has declared that former Vice President Atiku Abubakar will win Kano State in the 2027 presidential election without Senator Rabiu Musa Kwankwaso’s support, accusing the former Kano governor of working to divide the opposition and advance President Bola Tinubu’s re-election bid.
The council was reacting to Kwankwaso’s call for Atiku to step down for Peter Obi, describing the intervention as self-serving and an attempt to distract opposition parties from the task of dislodging the ruling All Progressives Congress, APC, amid mounting hardship, hunger, poverty and insecurity.
In a statement by its Director of Media and Publicity, Kola Ologbondiyan, the ADC-PCC questioned why Kwankwaso was targeting opposition leaders instead of challenging the Tinubu administration.
“Rather than campaigning against President Tinubu, whose administration Nigerians are eagerly working to vote out, Kwankwaso is fixated on Atiku Abubakar, the ADC candidate, whom millions of Nigerians believe can restore economic stability and make life affordable again,” Ologbondiyan said.
He accused Kwankwaso of playing into the hands of the APC by allegedly sowing division within the opposition, insisting that the former Kano governor’s political influence should not be mistaken for the ability to deliver a presidential victory.
“What Kwankwaso is doing amounts to advancing President Tinubu’s interests. It is a familiar APC strategy to use willing collaborators within the opposition to create confusion, sow division and weaken the collective efforts to bring about political change,” he said.
Dismissing the suggestion that Atiku would need Kwankwaso’s backing to win Kano, Ologbondiyan cited former President Muhammadu Buhari’s victories in the state in the 2003 and 2007 presidential elections, arguing that Kwankwaso’s support was not indispensable to electoral success there.
He also contrasted Atiku’s nationwide political networks with Kwankwaso’s concentrated influence in Kano, questioning whether the latter could translate his regional strength into broader national support.
“Atiku Abubakar is a cosmopolitan, detribalised and nationally recognised political figure who has built relationships across the North, South, East and West over more than three decades.
“Kwankwaso, on the other hand, has concentrated much of his political strength within Kano State. His ability to translate that regional influence into broad national electoral success remains a major question,” Ologbondiyan said.
The ADC-PCC spokesman further pointed to Kwankwaso’s fourth-place finish in the 2023 presidential election to challenge claims about his national electoral strength.
“If his political relevance were as extensive as he suggests, why did he finish fourth in the last presidential election?” he queried.
Ologbondiyan also alleged that Kwankwaso’s position on Obi’s candidacy was influenced by personal calculations ahead of the 2031 presidential race, rather than a genuine commitment to defeating the APC in 2027.
The council urged Kwankwaso and other opposition leaders to set aside personal ambitions and unite behind Atiku, warning that division could undermine efforts to remove Tinubu from power.
“The task before opposition leaders is not to undermine one another for personal political advantage but to unite around the urgent national mission of rescuing Nigeria,” Ologbondiyan said.

items.author: Nwafor
items.content:
By Henry Umoru
ABUJA — President Bola Tinubu’s nominee for chairman of the board of the Fiscal Responsibility Commission (FRC), Abdullahi Saidu, has told the Senate that the commission has operated without a board for more than 13 years, a situation he said has hindered its operations.
Saidu spoke on Wednesday when he appeared before the Senate Committee on Finance for screening alongside six other nominees.
He said the absence of a board had left the commission with significant institutional challenges, adding that the incoming board would have to rebuild its operations if confirmed.
Saidu said the commission was expected to establish offices in at least one location in each of the six geopolitical zones but currently operated only from Abuja.
He pledged to work with the National Assembly and other stakeholders to strengthen the commission and improve its capacity to discharge its mandate.
The nominee also disclosed that the commission lacked prosecutorial powers, explaining that it could investigate cases and forward its findings to the Attorney-General of the Federation and Minister of Justice for prosecution.
He said the proposed board would seek a review of the law establishing the commission to strengthen its independence and operational capacity.
Saidu further pledged to improve government revenue by strengthening the monitoring of operating surpluses generated by government-owned and other organisations covered by the commission’s mandate.
According to him, some revenue-generating organisations fail to remit the appropriate share of their operating surpluses to the Federal Government.
He said such organisations were expected to remit 80 per cent of their operating surpluses to the Consolidated Revenue Fund while retaining 20 per cent for their operations.
“Because the commission is not informed, so they just declare whatever they feel they want to declare,” he said.
Saidu assured the committee that, if confirmed, the board would strengthen monitoring to ensure that the appropriate revenues were declared and remitted.
He expressed confidence that the commission’s performance could improve within a year, provided it received the necessary support from the National Assembly and other stakeholders.
The screening was presided over by Senator Lere Oyewumi, vice-chairman of the committee, who represented its chairman, Senator Sani Musa.
Addressing the nominees, Oyewumi said managing the commission required specialised knowledge and preparation, noting that the assignment differed from other public service roles.
He urged them to participate in retreats with experts and undertake extensive reading to prepare for the responsibilities ahead.
Senator Osita Ngwu, representing Enugu West, moved a motion for Saidu and the other nominees to take a bow and leave, while Senator Sadiq Suleiman Umar, representing Kwara North, seconded the motion.
The other nominees screened alongside Saidu were Muhammad Asma’u, Muhammad Makama, Suleiman Gidado, Louis Ndukwe, Amechi Ugwele and Olaniyi Onikola.
The committee is expected to submit its report to the Senate for further legislative action.

The high-refresh-rate screen is suited to smooth scrolling and gaming, while the large battery provides substantial capacity for extended daily use.

However, its official model identity, specifications and market availability should be independently verified before it is included in a purchasing shortlist.

The Oukitel WP100 Titan stands out for its 33,000mAh battery, which is more than three times the capacity of a typical 10,000mAh phone.

Its enormous battery makes it suitable for users who value endurance over a compact design. However, its size and weight make it less convenient for people who prefer lightweight everyday smartphones.

The reinforced design also targets people who need greater physical durability than a typical consumer handset offers.

The university guarantees financial support for the first four years, bringing the minimum funding package to CAD 160,000.
Both Canadian and international students, including applicants from Pakistan, can qualify for the funding after securing admission.
UBC has set December 21, 2026, as the application deadline for the September 2027 intake. The research-based program offers specializations in development economics, econometrics, international trade, public economics, and several other fields.

Doctor of Philosophy in Economics Scholarship Benefits
The University of British Columbia provides a minimum annual funding package of CAD 40,000 to eligible full-time PhD students at its Vancouver campus.
The funding guarantee applies to the first four years of doctoral study, providing at least CAD 160,000 over that period.
UBC introduced the increased minimum funding requirement in September 2026. The policy covers both domestic and international doctoral students.
Financial support can come from university scholarships, external awards, research assistantships, teaching assistantships, and graduate academic assistantships.
According to UBC’s funding statistics for September 2024 to August 2025, supported Economics PhD students received a median annual gross funding of CAD 46,889.
The university also reported a median annual net funding of CAD 37,054 after deducting tuition and student fees.
Tuition Fees and Additional Financial Support
UBC charges tuition fees for its Economics PhD program. The university’s published first-year tuition amounts are approximately CAD 10,081.65 for international students and CAD 5,738.52 for domestic students.
Eligible international students can receive an International Tuition Award worth up to CAD 3,200 annually. The university also lists additional student fees of approximately CAD 1,203.20 per year.
Applicants should review their individual funding offers to understand how scholarships, assistantships, and tuition charges affect their available financial support.
The CAD 40,000 minimum funding package does not automatically provide a complete tuition waiver.
Eligibility Criteria for the UBC Economics PhD Scholarship
Applicants must meet UBC’s general graduate admission standards and the Vancouver School of Economics’ academic requirements. The university generally expects candidates to hold a master’s degree in Economics.
However, applicants with outstanding academic records in an undergraduate honours program in Economics can qualify for direct admission.
Candidates seeking admission directly from undergraduate studies must demonstrate strong performance in economic theory, mathematics, statistics, and econometrics.
UBC generally requires an academic average in the B+ range, equivalent to approximately 76%, although the Economics PhD program can apply higher standards.
English Language Requirements
International applicants whose previous universities did not primarily teach in English must submit accepted English-language proficiency results.
UBC requires an IELTS Academic overall score of 6.5, with at least 6.0 in each component. Candidates submitting the Duolingo English Test must achieve an overall score of 125. The minimum component scores are 115 in Reading and Listening and 120 in Writing and Speaking.
For TOEFL iBT examinations taken before January 21, 2026, applicants must achieve an overall score of 93, with at least 22 in each component.
Required Documents for the UBC Economics PhD Scholarship
Applicants must prepare their academic records and supporting documents before submitting their online applications.
UBC requires transcripts from every post-secondary institution attended, along with three confidential academic letters of recommendation.
Candidates must also submit a statement of intent describing their academic background, research interests, and reasons for pursuing doctoral studies.
The statement must not exceed two pages. Applicants must use US letter-size paper, one-inch margins, single spacing, and a 12-point professional font.
Candidates must provide English-language proficiency results where required and GRE scores if the department requires them.
How to Apply for the Doctor of Philosophy in Economics Scholarship
Interested candidates must submit their applications through the University of British Columbia’s official online graduate admissions system.
Applicants should first visit the UBC Economics PhD program page to review the admission requirements, funding arrangements and application instructions.
Candidates must create or use a UBC Campus-Wide Login account and complete the online graduate application.
Applicants must provide their academic qualifications, research interests, and contact details for three academic referees. They must also upload the required supporting documents and pay the applicable application fee.

items.title: PTA Orders Telcos to Fix Network Issues
items.summary:
The Pakistan Telecommunication Authority (PTA) has stepped up nationwide monitoring of telecom services to improve mobile network coverage, voice calls, and internet quality.
Between October 8 and 14, 2026, the authority carried out monitoring activities through its 10 zonal offices in Thatta, Dera Ghazi Khan, Mandi Bahauddin, Quetta, Faisalabad, and Gilgit-Baltistan.
During these visits, PTA officials assessed telecom services and identified issues affecting consumers. Telecom operators were directed to resolve problems related to mobile network coverage, voice calls, and internet services within the specified deadlines.
The authority also confirmed that an issue involving the closure of a telecom site in Faisalabad had been resolved.
PTA said it would continue working with telecom operators, relevant organizations, and local administrations to improve network performance and ensure more reliable telecom services across the country.

items.author: Muhammad Bilal
items.content:
The National Cyber Emergency Response Team (National CERT), in collaboration with the National Telecommunication Corporation (NTC), has warned internet users about the privacy and security risks of sharing their real time locations online.
The advisory, issued as part of Cybersecurity Awareness Month 2026, highlights how location sharing can expose sensitive personal information and leave users vulnerable to cyber threats.
According to National CERT, location data reveals more than a person’s position on a map. It can provide insights into daily routines, personal habits and movements, allowing malicious actors to identify where individuals live, work and frequently visit.
The advisory also warns that location data can reveal when people are at home or away, potentially exposing them to stalking, unauthorized tracking and other malicious activities. It can also reveal social connections by showing which people an individual regularly meets.
To reduce these risks, National CERT has advised users to disable location sharing when it is not needed and regularly review privacy settings on their devices and applications.
Users have also been urged to exercise caution when sharing personal information online and offline, particularly when using applications that offer live location updates or allow location data to be shared with others.
National CERT and NTC said simple preventive measures could help protect personal privacy and improve digital safety. As part of the Cybersecurity Awareness Month 2026 campaign, the two organizations emphasized responsible location sharing, stronger privacy practices and greater public awareness to help build safer digital communities in Pakistan.

items.author: Our Correspondent
items.content:
Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif on Friday, appreciating the remarkable progress in Pakistan-Saudi Arabia relations in recent years, reaffirmed Pakistan's commitment to further strengthening existing institutional mechanisms to deepen and broaden bilateral cooperation across various sectors.
The prime minister, in a meeting with newly appointed Saudi Ambassador Dr Rajeh Tami Albugamy, who called on him, reaffirmed that Pakistan stood shoulder-to-shoulder with the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia in safeguarding its sovereignty, security and territorial integrity.
He strongly condemned the recent escalation in Houthi attacks against Saudi Arabia, which had resulted in the loss of precious lives and injuries to scores of innocent people, including Pakistani nationals.
He underlined that Pakistan and Saudi Arabia had always stood by each other and that the Strategic Mutual Defence Agreement and the Makkah Joint Defence Alliance marked historic milestones in their longstanding fraternal relations and reflected their shared commitment to regional peace and security.
Welcoming the ambassador to Pakistan, the prime minister congratulated him on assuming his new responsibilities and wished him success in his diplomatic assignment.
He thanked the Saudi leadership for its longstanding economic and financial support to Pakistan.
The prime minister also wished the ambassador every success in his assignment and assured him of Pakistan's full support and cooperation in further strengthening the longstanding fraternal ties between the two countries.
Ambassador Albugamy also met Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar, where the latter underscored longstanding fraternal and strategic ties between Islamabad and Riyadh, according to the Foreign Office (FO).
He also reaffirmed Pakistan and Saudi Arabia's "shared commitment to further strengthen bilateral cooperation for mutual progress and prosperity".
The FO added that the new Saudi envoy conveyed greetings from the kingdom's leadership to Pakistan, with Dar reciprocating and conveying his best wishes to Saudi King Salman bin Abdulaziz Al Saud, Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman and other Saudi leaders.
Houthi attack
The Saudi-led coalition fighting Yemen's Houthis said on Friday that it intercepted missiles and drones over Riyadh and other areas, as the kingdom comes under sustained attack from its Iran-backed foes.
Since Yemen's civil war flared back to life in July, the Houthis have repeatedly struck Saudi targets including Red Sea tankers, oil facilities and Riyadh's international airport, where 13 people were killed in a single attack last week.
Saudi Arabia leads a military coalition that has supported Yemen's internationally recognised government against the Houthis for more than a decade.
"We intercepted and destroyed three drones in the southern area and Riyadh... and two cruise missiles over the Red Sea," coalition spokesman Turki al-Malki wrote on X.
He added that "in the past hours, we intercepted and destroyed a ballistic missile over Yanbu", a city home to the terminus of a major oil pipeline on the Red Sea coast.
The pressure on Saudi Arabia, the world's largest oil exporter, comes as global energy markets were already rattled by Iran's closure of the Strait of Hormuz at the outset of the wider Middle East war in February.
The Houthi attacks have proliferated since the group launched a lightning offensive in Yemen in September, seizing strategic government-held territory along the Red Sea coast overlooking a major chokepoint for global shipping.
The UN Security Council on Thursday "condemned in the strongest terms continued and escalatory Houthi attacks against the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia", as well as their "attacks and threats against commercial shipping in the Red Sea and Bab al-Mandab" Strait, the southern gateway to the Suez Canal.
The Security Council also denounced the group's "reckless strikes" on Riyadh's airport, which the Saudi-led coalition said had been targeted at least 20 times so far this month.
Palace struck
A Saudi foreign ministry official accused Iran on Thursday of continuing "to arm, train and support the Houthi militia in violation of UN security council resolutions".
"We think that the escalation by the Houthis at this latest stage of the conflict is encouraged by Iran," added Dr. Rayed Krimly, deputy minister for public diplomacy.
Yemeni government forces have launched a counteroffensive with Saudi air support to retake areas seized by the Houthis, but have so far failed to reverse their gains.
On Thursday, the group launched a deadly missile attack on the presidential palace in the interim seat of the Yemeni government in Aden, killing five people and wounding 16 others, according to the health minister.
Yemeni Prime Minister Shaya al-Zindani denounced the "cowardly" act on X, calling it a "continuation of (the Houthis') criminal pattern".
A government minister said on condition of anonymity that Zindani had been present at the time, but "was not harmed in any way".
The minister said the Houthis hit a command centre for Yemeni government forces at the complex with three missiles, and another for Saudi coalition forces with two missiles.
Media affiliated with the Houthis said they had targeted "the headquarters of military operations, led by Saudi officers, at the Al-Maashiq Palace in Aden, as well as weapons depots belonging to them".
(With additional input from AFP)

items.author: Kamran Yousaf
items.content:
Pakistan on Friday reaffirmed its commitment to Saudi Arabia's security but declined to be drawn into Riyadh's latest accusation that Iran continues to arm and train Yemen's Houthi militia, signalling Islamabad's effort to balance its close defence ties with Saudi Arabia with its engagement with Tehran.
Foreign Office spokesperson Sajjad Haider Khan said Pakistan could not comment on the Saudi allegation against Iran while reiterating Islamabad's broader position that regional conflicts should be resolved through diplomacy.
Asked about Saudi Foreign Ministry Deputy Minister for Public Diplomacy Rayed Krimly's accusation that Iran continued to arm, train and support the Houthi militia in violation of UN Security Council resolutions, Sajjad told reporters that Pakistan could not comment on the allegation.
"I would not be able to comment on the alleged accusation against Iran that you mentioned," he said.
The spokesperson instead reiterated Pakistan's broader position that the regional conflict should be resolved through diplomacy.
"Pakistan is keen to see peace and stability return to the entire region, including the Middle East and West Asia, and will continue to engage with all relevant stakeholders in this regard," he said.
"There is no solution through war. Peace can only be restored through negotiations and the peaceful settlement of disputes."
Pakistan, however, reaffirmed its commitment to Saudi Arabia's security and condemned the latest Houthi attack on King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh.
Sajjad said one Pakistani was killed at Riyadh airport and six others were injured in the recent attacks. The injured, he added, were receiving treatment at different locations in Riyadh while the Pakistani mission was in contact with them and their families.
Pakistan has repeatedly condemned Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia, including attacks targeting civilian and economic infrastructure, while also supporting dialogue for a political settlement of the Yemen conflict.
The spokesperson said Pakistan remained committed to the sovereignty, territorial integrity, unity and independence of Yemen and supported diplomatic efforts to end the conflict.
He also reiterated that Pakistan would fulfil its obligations under its defence arrangements with Saudi Arabia.
"Pakistan will fulfill its obligations under these agreements," Sajjad said when asked whether the Makkah defence agreement could be practically invoked following repeated attacks on Saudi territory.
However, he stopped short of giving any timeline for military action, saying operational matters, including deployment and action on the ground, fell within the domain of the armed forces, ISPR and the General Secretariat of the Makkah Joint Alliance.
Sajjad also said Pakistan supported Saudi Arabia's right to defend itself under Article 51 of the UN Charter.
Against this backdrop, Pakistan also played down recent remarks by an Iranian lawmaker questioning Islamabad's mediation efforts between Iran and the United States, making clear that the comments would not affect its broader engagement with Tehran.
Sajjad described Iran as a "brotherly country" and said Pakistan's role in facilitating the Islamabad understanding between Iran and the US had been appreciated by the Iranian leadership.
"Iran is a brotherly country, and its leadership has greatly appreciated Pakistan's role in mediation and in bringing the Islamabad MoU to fruition," Sajjad said at his weekly briefing.
He was responding to a question about Iranian lawmaker Mohsen Zanganeh's recent remarks during his visit to Kabul, in which he reportedly questioned Pakistan's mediation role and suggested that even a Pakistani tweet on the issue had been written by Americans.
Sajjad said he had seen the reported remarks but would not comment on their credibility.
"They may also have been taken out of context, as Iran's leadership and people are grateful for Pakistan's efforts," he said, adding that members of Iran's National Assembly had also applauded Pakistan's "constructive role" in the region.
The remarks indicate that Islamabad does not want the comments by an individual Iranian lawmaker to undermine its broader engagement with Tehran, particularly after Pakistan's efforts to facilitate the Islamabad MoU between Iran and the United States.
On Afghanistan, Sajjad said Pakistan remained open to dialogue but made clear that any talks with the Taliban would not be unconditional.
He said Islamabad wanted a "verifiable mechanism" ensuring a complete cessation of terrorist activities emanating from Afghan soil.
Responding to questions about a possible Russian mediation initiative following the recent Moscow Format meeting, he said Pakistan valued its engagement with Russia and would welcome "any sincere efforts by friendly countries" that could address its security concerns.
"At present, I am not aware of any separate, formal Russian mediation initiative being under discussion," Sajjad said.
He added that meaningful progress would ultimately depend on "concrete and verifiable action on the ground" by the Taliban authorities against terrorist groups operating from Afghanistan.
He also confirmed that Pakistan's participation in the Moscow Format meeting was at the special representative level and noted that the absence of a joint communiqué was significant.
"The fact that no joint communiqué was issued after the Moscow Format is self-evident that Afghanistan did not accept the formulation which had been acceptable until last year particularly about presence of terrorist network in Afghanistan," Sajjad said.
On India, the Foreign Office strongly rejected recent remarks by the Indian defence minister threatening aggression against Pakistan, warning that any military action would receive a "forceful response".
"Let there be no ambiguity: Pakistan remains fully prepared to safeguard its sovereignty and territorial integrity against any ill-advised aggression," Sajjad said.
"Our restraint and commitment to peace must never be mistaken for weakness. Any aggression will be met with a forceful response."

Opposition parties on Friday vowed a joint struggle against the imposition of governor's rule and emergency in Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa (K-P), demanding constitutional supremacy, parliamentary sovereignty and free and fair elections, while keeping open the option of resigning from the assemblies.
Opposition Leader in the National Assembly Mahmood Khan Achakzai said he would contact opposition parties and convene an all-parties conference (APC).
He said the option of resigning from the assemblies remained open, but stressed that the opposition favoured a peaceful, constitutional struggle and was ready for talks.
Speaking at a news conference at the Peshawar High Court, Achakzai said he had come to express solidarity with the people of Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa, alleging that the federal government had acted unconstitutionally by removing the elected provincial government.
He said the Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) had won seats in the elections but the government had been handed to another party. He also cited the disqualification of lawmakers and alleged irregularities in the electoral process.
Achakzai said no one should be prevented from meeting a prisoner and alleged that PTI founder Imran Khan was being pressured into an agreement.
He said former prime ministers Nawaz Sharif and Benazir Bhutto had faced similar treatment in the past, adding that the same was happening under the current governments led by the Pakistan Muslim League-Nawaz (PML-N) and the Pakistan Peoples Party (PPP).
He questioned the whereabouts of Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa Chief Minister Sohail Afridi and said information about him should be made public. He also expressed concern over reports that provincial ministers, lawmakers and party workers had gone missing.
"This is not the time to remain silent but to stand up for the people's rights and constitutional protection," Achakzai said. "We will neither throw stones at anyone nor resort to violence. We will pursue a peaceful struggle."
He said the opposition was willing to negotiate if the government was serious about dialogue. Policies should be made in parliament, he added, and all institutions should operate within their constitutional limits.
Achakzai said the opposition had set out its demands in response to the government's offer of talks. These included upholding the Constitution, withdrawing controversial amendments, restoring parliament's role as the principal centre of decision-making and establishing an independent commission to ensure free and fair elections.
The country's problems could not be resolved unless parliament became the primary forum for decision-making, he said, adding that contacts with opposition parties were under way and all would be invited to the proposed APC.
On provincial rights, Achakzai said the people of Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa had the first claim to the province's mineral resources. He called for unity across political lines to protect the country and safeguard public rights.
He also cited the merger of the former Federally Administered Tribal Areas (Fata) with Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, saying decisions of national importance should be made through constitutional and democratic procedures.
Akhtar Mengal, head of the Balochistan National Party, criticised those who claimed to be the architects of the Constitution while, he said, violating its provisions.
He alleged that the imposition of governor's rule in Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa amounted to blaming the entire province for terrorism. Counterterrorism operations had also been under way in Balochistan for years, he said, but insecurity continued to affect the province.
Mengal questioned whether such measures could resolve the country's problems. He also alleged that the elected chief minister of Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa had been taken away and cited reports concerning the whereabouts of the provincial assembly speaker and ministers.
He said people elected through what he called "Form 47" were occupying the assemblies and argued that such a system could not endure.
Allama Raja Nasir Abbas, opposition leader in the Senate, said lawlessness had worsened and accused the government of taking control of a province because it could not manage the existing system. Government ministers had themselves acknowledged the system's failure, he said.
He alleged that those who had stolen the public mandate were seeking to silence dissent and protests. Citing rising poverty, he said remaining silent about the country's situation was inconsistent with patriotism. He pledged to continue his struggle regardless of the circumstances.

items.author: Our Correspondent
items.content:
The Peshawar High Court (PHC) has listed for hearing the petitions challenging the federal government's October 11 decision to impose emergency and governor's rule in Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa (K-P). The court will take up the pleas on October 20.
PTI Chairman Barrister Gohar Ali Khan approached the PHC on October 14, challenging the imposition of emergency and governor's rule in K-P and seeking the annulment of the presidential proclamation issued on October 11. National Democratic Movement (NDM) leaders Mohsin Dawar and Bushra Gohar also separately filed similar petition in the court.
In his petition, filed through Advocate Ali Zaman, Gohar termed the measures unconstitutional and discriminatory, arguing that terrorism cannot be used as a pretext to curtail the powers of an elected provincial government.
The PTI chairman contended that terrorism had affected different parts of the country in the past without elected provincial governments being removed on that basis.
He cited the security situation in Balochistan, where terrorist attacks and casualties had been continually reported, arguing that governor's rule had not been imposed there despite the serious law and order challenges.
He referred to the period between 2007 and 2015, when K-P and the former tribal areas experienced a severe wave of militancy, resulting in substantial casualties among civilians and security personnel.
The petitioner argued that the elected provincial government had not been removed through governor's rule during that period and urged the court to examine the constitutional justification and alleged motives behind the current measures.
Gohar maintained that the PTI opposed terrorism and supported action against militant elements and efforts to restore peace. He rejected allegations that the party's provincial government had failed to take effective action against terrorism or had shown leniency towards militants.
He stated that such accusations were being used to exert political pressure and weaken the mandate PTI secured in the 2024 general elections.
The petition argued that the party had won a two-thirds majority in the province and that the federal government could not curtail the powers of an elected government because of political differences.
It also questioned the use of the failure of negotiations as a justification for action against PTI, maintaining that the party had not planned any unlawful activity during its long march and that peaceful political protest could not, by itself, justify suspending an elected government.
Invoking Articles 232 and 234 of the Constitution, the petition asked the court to examine whether the requirements for imposing an emergency and invoking governor's rule had been met.
Article 232 deals with emergency powers in specified circumstances, while Article 234 provides a mechanism for a presidential proclamation where a provincial government cannot be carried on in accordance with the Constitution.
Separately, NDM President Mohsin Dawar and Bushra Gohar filed a constitutional petition through Advocate Yousaf Orakzai, challenging the October 11 presidential proclamation as unlawful, unconstitutional and beyond the president's authority.
The NDM leaders asked the high court to declare the proclamation unlawful and set it aside. They have also sought interim relief suspending its implementation until the petition is finally decided.

items.content:
Pakistan will chair the Boards of Governors of the International Monetary Fund (IMF) and the World Bank Group (WBG) in 2027, marking the country's first return to the leadership of both institutions since 1953, the Ministry of Economic Affairs said on Friday.
Economic Affairs Minister Ahad Cheema, who also serves as Pakistan's governor to the World Bank, was formally announced as the incoming chairman during the plenary session of the 2026 WBG-IMF Annual Meetings in Bangkok.
The annual meetings, being held from October 12 to 18, brought together policymakers, central bank governors, business leaders and other participants from around the world to discuss the global economy.
The ministry described the appointment as a historic milestone, saying the chairmanship would provide Pakistan with an opportunity to contribute to international economic and development discussions and facilitate constructive dialogue among member countries.
Following the plenary session, the WBG Corporate Secretariat briefed Cheema on the responsibilities associated with the chairmanship. He also met WBG Vice President and Corporate Secretary Aradhana Kumar-Capoor to discuss institutional support and coordination during Pakistan's tenure.
Cheema separately met outgoing chairman Carlos Carvallo Spalding, governor of Paraguay's central bank, congratulating him on completing his tenure and commending his stewardship. The two discussed the responsibilities of the office and priorities for the coming year.
During the meetings, Cheema reaffirmed Pakistan's commitment to strengthening the voice of developing countries, improving coordination among multilateral development institutions and promoting effective and predictable development financing.
He emphasised the importance of mobilising private investment to support sustainable and inclusive growth. He said Pakistan would work closely with the WBG, the IMF and member countries to encourage constructive dialogue and contribute to a more responsive multilateral development and financial system.
Separately, Finance Minister Muhammad Aurangzeb met World Bank Group President Ajay Banga at a dinner hosted by the Thai prime minister on the sidelines of the annual meetings in Bangkok, according to state-run Pakistan Television.
Pakistan remains engaged with the IMF under a $7 billion Extended Fund Facility (EFF) and a $1.4 billion Resilience and Sustainability Facility (RSF). Earlier this month, Pakistan and the Fund reached a staff-level agreement following the fourth review under the EFF and the third review under the RSF.

Pakistan has also signed agreements with US-based US Strategic Metals to develop critical minerals, reflecting efforts to attract international investment and build partnerships in the sector.
To promote investment opportunities, the Pakistan Minerals Investment Forum 2026 is scheduled for November 12 and 13 at the Jinnah Convention Centre in Islamabad.
The event is expected to bring together Pakistani authorities, international investors and industry stakeholders to discuss mineral exploration, investment and the development of the mining sector.

items.author: Meha Agarwal
items.content:
Sixteen years since FirstCry began its journey, what began as a kidswear marketplace has spawned a massive multi-channel ecommerce and retail empire, and a house of brands that’s grown well beyond kids today.
Today, FirstCry is not just a listed kidswear retailer, but also the engine dragging the Globalbees house of brands and a budding education business that will become hard to ignore soon. But how exactly do each of these engines work?
Before we dive in, here’s a look at where FirstCry stands after the last quarter, ahead of its Q2 FY27 results.
The first quarter (Q1) of FY27 saw its consolidated revenue climb 13.1% year-on-year to ₹2,106.2 Cr, while its overall net losses were slashed by nearly 34%, dropping to ₹44 Cr from ₹66.5 Cr in Q1FY26.
According to founder Supam Maheshwari, this milestone marks the company’s strongest baseline revenue expansion over the last five years on a consolidated level. It builds cleanly on the momentum of the previous financial year, where FirstCry closed its books at ₹8,548 Cr in total sales while narrowing its statutory consolidated net loss down to approx ₹204 Cr.
However, beneath those headline numbers, take a closer look at the business structure and a different story will unfold. While its top-line revenue signals absolute category dominance, FirstCry’s true bottom line is being heavily squeezed by a highly rigid corporate framework and expensive side-bets.
For starters, GlobalBees, FirstCry’s D2C brand aggregation subsidiary, contributed ₹1,894.3 Cr, or roughly 22% of its consolidated operating revenue in FY26 while revenue from international businesses in the UAE and Saudi Arabia grew 10% to ₹947.4 Cr. However, together these two businesses accounted for ₹148.5 Cr in segment losses.
Further, in Q1FY27, while India multichannel revenue grew 17.7% and international business rose 12%, GlobalBees remained largely flat. The fastest growth, at 47%, came from the much smaller ‘Others’ segment, primarily comprising the FirstCry Intellitots preschool business.
Notably, the segment growing fastest is contributing hardly 1% to the overall consolidated revenue, underscoring the uneven economics behind FirstCry’s expanding revenue base.
The Overburdened India Goliath
A majority 70% of FirstCry’s consolidated operating revenue comes from its India multi-channel business. In Q1FY27, the segment generated around INR 1456 Cr in revenue, up 17.7% YoY. However, despite operating across 10+ categories for mothers, babies, and kids from conception up to approximately 12 years of age, this revenue channel is continuously losing out on gross margin.
In Q1FY27, the gross margin fell to 35.2% from 37.8% in Q1FY26. In other words, FirstCry was selling significantly more but retaining less from every rupee of revenue before accounting for delivery, marketing and other operating expenses.
A major pressure point is the diapers business, which although just a 15% contributor to GMV, acts as the primary top-of-funnel customer acquisition gateway. It is a high-volume category hit heavily by quick-commerce and private-label discounting, which temporarily drags down the overall multi-channel gross margins.
FirstCry’s parent company, Brainbees Solutions Limited, holds a 76.59% stake in Swara Baby Products Limited, which gives it a promoter status in the company, which is about to go for an ₹1,000 Cr IPO separately. This will allow FirstCry to further vertically integrate its supply chain for the diapers category.
To combat the short-term pressures on the diapers segment, Firstcry has been pushing on its private labels particularly Babyhug, Pine Kids, Cute Walk and Babyoye, to gain greater control over product pricing, sourcing and margins.
At the same time, FirstCry has been actively pushing efforts around three initiatives. First, it is rapidly deploying internal logistics networks. Its in-house logistics platform RocketBees has scaled rapidly to 72 cities and covers around 50% of total online shipment as of June 2026. In Q1FY27 earnings call, Maheshwari also pointed out a 20% improvement in turnaround time from delivery perspective.
The under-3-hour delivery pilot, FC Qwik, is also live across 12 cities completing approximately 1.25 Lakh shipments in June 2026 alone.
Founder and MD Maheshwari said, “We had an overall ambition of growing to 10% of our overall shipment onto the FC Qwik platform. Now, we will aim to grow to 20% of our volumes.”
He also highlighted that the FC Qwik TAT has been reduced from three to two hours in selected cities and the team is working on further reducing it.
As its third pillar, the company continues to be bullish on its physical retail network, which had grown to around 1,190 stores by FY26. Its offline business recorded approximately 15% year-on-year GMV growth in Q1FY27, with management targeting another 90-100 net store additions during FY27.
This gives FirstCry an advantage in product discovery and customer reach, particularly beyond large metropolitan markets, but also requires it to manage the costs of an extensive physical network alongside faster online fulfillment.
The trade-off is becoming increasingly visible.
Despite the 17.7% revenue growth in Q1FY27, the India business’s adjusted EBITDA declined from approximately ₹107 Cr to ₹84 Cr. Its adjusted operating margin consequently contracted from around 8.6% to 5.8%. This suggests that higher sales volumes have yet to compensate for the combined pressure of product margins and operating costs.
The company expects some relief as higher raw material and currency-related costs are gradually passed on through product pricing, with a fuller recovery anticipated from Q3FY27, as per management disclosures after Q1.
However, competitive pressure in diapering could take longer to ease. In essence, the India multichannel goliath is growing faster, but whether that growth can translate into stronger profits remains the bigger test. The Q2 results will clear up some questions around which direction this key business is headed in.
Globalbees’ Drag Effect
If the India multi-channel business is FirstCry’s heavy brick-and-mortar anchor, GlobalBees is its high-stakes venture capital pivot. In FY26, Globalbees registered a solid 20% y-o-y growth in overall revenue, however, the momentum doesn’t seem to continue. In Q1FY27, the revenue remained almost flat with marginal reduction, while core categories revenue saw only 2% year on year growth.
GlobalBees has been a significant capital allocation bet for FirstCry. Parent Brainbees Solutions earmarked ₹169 Cr from the IPO proceeds for GlobalBees to gain further control of its portfolio under the house of brands model. By March 2026, it had deployed ₹104.81 Cr of this allocation. Separately, in March 2025, Brainbees approved a further infusion of up to ₹146 Cr.
Despite this capital backing GlobalBees has not acquired a single new brand since September 2022. During the FY26 earnings call, CEO Anuj Jain acknowledged that the company rationalised its portfolio, cutting off brands struggling with slower growth and persistent losses. Instead, the focus has shifted towards four core categories spanning home improvement, appliances, personal care and lifestyle.
Thanks to this, even on flat revenue, the segment delivered a remarkable 308% year-on-year surge in Adjusted EBITDA, jumping from ₹4.1 Cr to ₹16.7 Cr, and operating margins grew from 1% to 3.9%.
Jain said the cutbacks are a temporary and planned transition that should be completed in the second quarter and growth should bounce back in the winter months. Globalbees can unlock more growth in these categories, but how profitable will this model remain in the long run? Investors will undoubtedly be looking at the next three quarters keenly.
The International & Preschool Hedge
The other two parts of FirstCry’s business are part of its vision of targeting customers early and making a global retail giant.
The company entered the UAE in 2019 and Saudi Arabia in 2022, betting on far higher spending per child than in India. While average spend per child on its Indian platform is around ₹9,280–₹9,350, the corresponding figures are approximately ₹61,000–₹71,000 in Saudi Arabia and ₹1,60,000–₹1,70,000 in the UAE. But converting that premium opportunity into profits has proved difficult amid aggressive discounting by larger ecommerce rivals.
FirstCry has reduced its proposed allocation for the international business after the IPO. The move raises questions about the pace and capital demands of its overseas rollout, even as management maintains that the region remains a long-term opportunity. And to be fair, international revenue growth is in line with the overall topline.
International revenue rose 12% year on year to ₹232.1 Cr in Q1FY27, from ₹207.2 Cr, while adjusted EBITDA losses narrowed 22% to ₹16.7 Cr. The adjusted EBITDA loss margin improved from about 10% to 7%.
For now, management is prioritising unit economics over a breakneck expansion push and has avoided committing to a break-even quarter. The premium-spending thesis remains attractive, but the international business still has to prove it can turn that opportunity into sustainable profits.
Away from the bruising battles of babycare retail and overseas expansion, FirstCry harbors a smaller, highly lucrative engine quietly gathering momentum. Its preschool operations, housed under the ‘Others’ segment, are emerging as an unlikely margin champion in a sprawling consumer empire historically plagued by cash burn.
The numbers present a striking contrast. In Q1 FY27, the Intellitots preschool business saw net revenue surge 47% year-on-year to ₹19 Cr, while its adjusted EBITDA improved 65% to hit ₹5 Cr. Operating at a 26% adjusted EBITDA margin, this division outperforms FirstCry’s primary retail segments.
With management aiming to scale the network to 1,000 preschools over the next few years, this asset-light education bet offers a clear blueprint for high margin revenue beyond traditional retail operations.
But the ₹19 Cr quarterly revenue base is small and the preschool business accounts for less than 1% of FirstCry’s consolidated topline. The profitability offers little immediate relief to the group as a whole. But it could become a bigger lever if and when the core business matures.
Is FirstCry Stuck In The Past?
When you zoom out, FirstCry’s consolidated revenue model reveals a business in a state of transition, which has not really been solved by its IPO and the funds raised through the listing. It is caught between defensive strategies for margin recovery and an aggressive push for growth. It’s not a crisis by any means but it is a time for the company to reassess its strengths once again and push for growth in that direction.
FirstCry is increasingly feeling the weight of over 1,000 physical storefronts, which have saddled the company with fixed, unyielding operational overheads like high commercial rent and retail payroll.
The ecommerce moat is also rapidly eroding under a fierce, industry-wide quick commerce frenzy led by Blinkit, Zepto, Swiggy Instamart and Flipkart Minutes as well as specialised players, which we had reported in detail here.
Having gone beyond kidswear and babycare, the harder question in front of FirstCry is whether its disparate pieces can start to show an ecosystem effect to generate enough operating leverage to sustain the business without another major funds infusion, as has been the major trend in the public markets this year for new-age listed companies.
The post FirstCry’s Core Revenue Engine Is Fighting Too Many Battles appeared first on Inc42 Media.

items.author: Gaurav Bagur
items.content:
The Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) has issued show-cause notices to quick commerce and ecommerce platforms BigBasket and Flipkart alongside manufacturer Gemini Edibles & Fats India for allegedly promoting misleading claims, “Freedom Cooking Rice Bran Oil”.
According to the FSSAI notice, Gemini’s oil was marketed using health-benefit claims, including statements that it “reduces bad cholesterol and maintains/increases good cholesterol” and contains “10,000+ PPM Natural Oryzanol”.
Associating edible vegetable oils with heart health is not permitted under the Food Safety and Standards (Advertising and Claims) Regulations, 2018.
The regulator claimed that Gemini was selling food products via its proprietary ecommerce website without holding a valid Central Licence covering ecommerce activity.
The action follows an examination of promotional material across digital media platforms and ecommerce storefronts.
Notably, the FSSAI is mulling the introduction of dedicated regulations for ecommerce and quick commerce platforms as well as cloud kitchens, its CEO recently revealed. The proposed rules would require food listings on ecommerce platforms to display manufacturing and expiry dates and batch numbers online. In this, platforms would be held accountable for misleading claims made by manufacturers.
It is also considering mandatory disclosure of cloud kitchen photographs and addresses and stricter checks on dark store storage conditions.
This adds to the intensity of the ongoing scrutiny of ecommerce and quick commerce platforms over food safety violations. A few weeks ago, the FSSAI penalised multiple platforms — Amazon, Bigbasket, Flipkart, Swiggy Instamart and Zepto — for allegedly engaging in misbranding, misleading claims, and sale and display of prohibited or poisonous food articles.
Earlier in the year, the regulator also issued nine notices to Instamart following consumer complaints over alleged delivery of expired, spoiled, and contaminated food products.
Besides, state-level authorities, too, have been cracking down on quick commerce platforms over food safety and hygiene violations at their dark stores.
In August, the Maharashtra Food and Drug Administration (FDA) suspended the licences of 14 dark stores after checking 86 such outlets in a state-wide inspection drive. Shortly before that incident, Karnataka food safety officials also sealed a major Zepto warehouse in Bengaluru’s Hoskote over multiple breaches of food safety regulations.

items.title: Karachi to Remove 2 Traffic Signals on Major Road

KMC Director General of Engineering Tariq Mughal said planning for the project had reached its final stage. The proposed changes aim to make the road signal-free up to the Society Office.
Under the plan, authorities will introduce one U-turn before Allah Wali Chowrangi and another between Allah Wali Chowrangi and Noorani Chowrangi.
The changes will facilitate traffic traveling from Shahra-e-Faisal toward Mazar-e-Quaid by removing the two signals that currently interrupt traffic flow.
However, the signal near Khudadad Colony will remain operational, meaning that stretch will not become completely signal-free.

items.author: Business Desk
items.content:
The Securities and Exchange Commission of Pakistan (SECP) is initiating regulatory action over material discrepancies in the IPO prospectus of SE Fruits and Vegetable Limited, which was based on information in the company’s audited financial statements.
The regulator suspended further proceedings after the book-building process to protect investors. The company later withdrew its IPO voluntarily, with plans to resubmit it at a later stage with more detailed disclosures. All subscription money has been refunded to investors.
SECP is reviewing the case to determine responsibility for procedural irregularities and said appropriate action would follow if violations are established.
Companies seeking to raise funds through an initial public offering (IPO) must disclose their financial position, business plans and associated risks in a prospectus to help investors make informed decisions.
The process begins with the company preparing its financial records and disclosures, which are audited by an external auditor. The consultant to the issue then conducts due diligence, prepares the draft prospectus and submits the application to the Pakistan Stock Exchange (PSX).
The PSX listing committee reviews the application and seeks public comments on the draft prospectus. The company and its consultant must address observations, update disclosures and submit a due diligence certificate before the listing application and prospectus proceed for approval by the relevant authorities.
Once approved, the prospectus is published on SECP’s PRIDE platform, which stands for Public Offerings Revolutionized through an Integrated and Digitized Experience. The book-building process can then begin.
Under Sections 134 and 136 of the Securities Act, 2015, fraudulently inducing securities transactions and making false or misleading statements are criminal offences.
SECP has also emphasized the need to strengthen the Audit Oversight Board (AOB) and bring its legal framework closer to international practices and the principles of the International Forum of Independent Audit Regulators (IFIAR).
Effective audit oversight requires sufficient inspection and enforcement powers, qualified technical staff and stable funding to hold auditors accountable and protect the reliability of financial reporting.

items.author: ​ Our Correspondents
items.content:
The Lahore High Court (LHC) has declared the Pakistan Medical and Dental Council's (PMDC) decision to collect question papers from candidates after the recent Medical and Dental College Admission Test (MDCAT) illegal and unconstitutional, directing the council to immediately upload the papers to its official application.
Justice Ahsan Raza Kazmi allowed petitions challenging the policy, ruling that collecting question papers from candidates after they had completed the examination was unlawful. The court ordered the PMDC to make the papers available on its official app so that all candidates could access and review them.
The petitions were filed by two candidates, Anabia Tahir and Rehan Shahid. Their counsel, Barrister Imran Afrasiab, argued that candidates should be allowed to retain question papers after completing an examination, adding that this was the established practice worldwide.
He contended that students were entitled to question papers after examinations, including those conducted by schools, colleges and universities, and that examination authorities could not forcibly retrieve them once candidates had been allowed to use them.
Afrasiab said the PMDC had unilaterally introduced the policy this year, requiring candidates to return their question papers along with their answer sheets immediately after the examination. He challenged the move as illegal.
Federal government counsel Malik Zaheer Arshad partially supported the petitioners' position, while the PMDC's lawyer defended the council's decision and urged the court to dismiss the petitions.
After hearing the arguments, the court declared the practice illegal and directed the PMDC to upload the question papers to its official application without delay, enabling candidates to access and study them. The court also ordered immediate implementation of its decision.
Afghan students
The Lahore High Court (LHC) has extended its interim order restraining all medical colleges in Punjab from expelling Afghan students in view of a controversial Pakistan Medical and Dental Council (PMDC) notification.
Justice Khalid Ishaq on Friday heard petitions filed by more than 30 Afghan students against their expulsion from medical colleges.
During the hearing, the PMDC's counsel sought an adjournment. The court accepted the request, postponed further proceedings, and extended the interim relief granted to the petitioners.
The petitioners submitted that they had secured admission to medical colleges under the Afghan refugees' quota. They maintained that they had gained admission on merit.
In a notification dated September 1, the PMDC ordered medical colleges in Punjab to ask Afghan medical and dental students to complete official formalities for their return to Afghanistan while also suspending future admissions, transfers and migration involving Afghan nationals.
The LHC on September 11 restrained all medical colleges in Punjab from expelling Afghan medical students.

items.author: Usman Hanif
items.content:
The overall balance of payments (BoP) swung to a deficit of $4.39 billion in September, compared with $118 million in August, as the current account deficit widened to $356 million from $73 million, according to State Bank of Pakistan (SBP) data.
For July-September, the BoP recorded a deficit of $3.12 billion, against a surplus of $274 million in the corresponding period last year. The figures highlight the growing gap between Pakistan's foreign exchange earnings and payments, with the merchandise trade deficit remaining the largest component of the goods and services trade imbalance.
Pakistan's goods trade deficit widened 21.1% to $9.33 billion in the first quarter of fiscal year 2026-27 as imports grew nearly twice as fast as exports, highlighting mounting pressure on the external account despite a recovery in merchandise exports in September.
Goods imports increased 14.3% to $17.78 billion during July-September, compared with $15.56 billion in the same period last year. Goods exports rose 7.7% to $8.45 billion from $7.85 billion. The widening trade gap contributed to a deterioration in the current account, which recorded a deficit of $874 million during the first quarter, compared with $755 million a year earlier.
Goods exports increased 15.5% year-on-year to $3.02 billion in September, reversing a 1.5% decline recorded in August. However, imports grew faster, rising 22.7% to $6.17 billion from $5.03 billion a year earlier. Consequently, the monthly goods trade deficit widened to $3.16 billion in September from $2.42 billion a year earlier. The contrasting growth rates suggest the recovery in exports has yet to keep pace with the expansion in import payments.
Pakistan's services exports increased 22.8% to $2.72 billion in the first quarter, compared with $2.21 billion a year earlier. Telecommunications, computer and information services remained a major contributor, generating $1.25 billion during July-September, up from $1.06 billion in the same period last year. Other business services exports rose to $622 million from $486 million, while travel services exports increased to $322 million from $157 million. Services imports, however, also increased to $3.55 billion from $3.05 billion. The resulting services trade deficit narrowed slightly to $831 million from $840 million a year earlier.
Remittances remain a key support
Workers' remittances rose 14% to $10.88 billion during the first quarter, compared with $9.54 billion in the corresponding period last year, providing an important source of foreign exchange. However, monthly remittances declined to $3.59 billion in September from $3.66 billion in August, a decrease of around 1.9%.
The secondary income balance, which includes remittances and other current transfers, reached $11.61 billion during July-September, compared with $10.06 billion a year earlier. Despite these inflows, the current account remained in deficit as the combined goods, services and primary income balance deteriorated.
Pakistan's primary income deficit widened slightly to $2.32 billion during the first quarter from $2.27 billion a year earlier. Primary income payments reached $2.56 billion, compared with credits of $244 million, reflecting the continued imbalance between income paid abroad and income received from overseas. The primary income account includes cross-border income flows such as investment income and compensation of employees.
Monthly FDI slows
Foreign direct investment (FDI) inflows into Pakistan increased to $720 million during the first quarter, up 20% from $600 million in the same period last year. However, monthly FDI inflows slowed to $219 million in September from $322 million in August.
Portfolio investment recorded a net inflow of approximately $2.93 billion into Pakistan during July-September, compared with a net outflow of $631 million a year earlier. The September figure included a $2.87 billion net portfolio inflow, largely reflected in debt securities. Despite these investment flows, the financial account recorded a net outflow of $4.16 billion during the first quarter, compared with $726 million in the corresponding period last year.
The SBP's balance of payments table reported gross foreign exchange reserves, including cash foreign currency holdings and excluding unsettled claims on the Reserve Bank of India, at $22.88 billion in September, compared with $18.49 billion in August. The central bank's reserve-assets measure recorded an increase of $4.38 billion in September, while the overall balance of payments showed a deficit of $4.39 billion.
Furthermore, the Pakistani rupee edged up Rs0.01 against the US dollar on Friday, closing at 276.91 in the inter-bank market, compared with 276.92 on Thursday. Internationally, the dollar was heading for its first weekly decline in five weeks as concerns over artificial intelligence investment and falling US yields lifted the euro from a 17-month low.
Meanwhile, gold prices in Pakistan rose by Rs2,800 per tola on Friday to reach Rs440,636, tracking gains in the international market, according to the All-Pakistan Gems and Jewellers Sarafa Association (APGJSA). The price of 10-gramme gold increased by Rs2,401 to Rs377,774. On Thursday, gold had remained unchanged at Rs437,836 per tola. In the international market, gold gained $28 to reach $4,181 per ounce. Meanwhile, silver prices climbed by Rs108 to a record high of Rs6,256 per tola.
