items.title: The Personal Agents Era Comes With Caveats
items.summary:
In November 1996, Japanese toymaker Bandai put a pet inside a plastic egg. The Tamagotchi, whose name blends tamago, Japanese for egg, with watch, had a tiny screen and three buttons to feed the creature, play with it and switch off its lights. Neglect it for too long, and it died. The toy went on to sell about 40 Mn units.
Thirty years later, Meta has its own take on the idea.
At its Connect event last month, CEO Mark Zuckerberg showed off the Muse Charm, a keychain-sized device with a small screen and an animated avatar representing Meta’s AI agent Muse. Tap the device, and you can talk to it and get it to do tasks for you.
But unlike the Tamagotchi, which demanded its owner’s constant attention, Muse is designed to keep working without guilt-tripping its owner.
Muse is part of Meta’s bet on always-on AI agents that can take everyday tasks off users’ hands. By connecting to their apps and services, the agent can send emails, fill forms, make plans and even make purchases autonomously
items.author: Shraddha Goled
items.content:
In November 1996, Japanese toymaker Bandai put a pet inside a plastic egg. The Tamagotchi, whose name blends tamago, Japanese for egg, with watch, had a tiny screen and three buttons to feed the creature, play with it and switch off its lights. Neglect it for too long, and it died. The toy went on to sell about 40 Mn units.
Thirty years later, Meta has its own take on the idea.
At its Connect event last month, CEO Mark Zuckerberg showed off the Muse Charm, a keychain-sized device with a small screen and an animated avatar representing Meta’s AI agent Muse. Tap the device, and you can talk to it and get it to do tasks for you.
But unlike the Tamagotchi, which demanded its owner’s constant attention, Muse is designed to keep working without guilt-tripping its owner.
Muse is part of Meta’s bet on always-on AI agents that can take everyday tasks off users’ hands. By connecting to their apps and services, the agent can send emails, fill forms, make plans and even make purchases autonomously. In return, users must grant it access to personal information, accounts and digital workflows.
The same idea is now moving into the workplace. OpenAI introduced Dots on September 29, while xAI has been developing Grok Bot. These agents are designed to work across applications and pursue goals without requiring users to guide every step. OpenAI says its teams use Dots to investigate software bugs, while xAI has cited tasks such as cleaning up sales records and processing invoices as potential uses for agents.
For businesses, the proposition is straightforward: instead of asking employees to use AI to complete individual tasks, let AI handle entire workflows.
From Taking Orders To Taking The Wheel
Much of the current interest in always-on AI agents can be traced to OpenClaw, an open-source framework that gained traction among developers earlier this year. Meta has also drawn inspiration from OpenClaw for Muse.
Unlike AI tools that require users to keep prompting them, always-on agents can take a goal and work towards it independently. They keep working even after you log off.
Always-on AI agents run on their own computer in the cloud instead of the user’s device. They can be connected to apps and assigned a goal instead of step-by-step prompts. Over time, these models remember preferences and learn from feedback. These agents, however, come back to users when they need approval for a sensitive action or an update.
Now AI companies are selling this to businesses.
Google has announced a Gemini agent for work that can handle tasks, create content and write code based on an employee’s desired outcome. The agent is designed to work across Google Workspace, Microsoft 365, Slack and other environments.
Microsoft is also pursuing agents that can function as digital teammates. Its agent initiative, described as ‘Autopilot’, is built on OpenClaw and is intended to work autonomously towards predefined goals.
India has an early example in Bengaluru-based Emergent, better known for its vibe-coding platform. In April, the company launched Wingman, an autonomous agent that users can direct through WhatsApp and Telegram. It works in the background across email, calendars and workplace software, handles routine actions and seeks approval before taking bigger steps.
Who Answers For The Agent?
Despite the stride, these agents pose a new kind of risk for enterprises, as they can act with little or no intervention.
With access to company systems, one flawed decision could trigger a financial, operational or security incident. The risks range from agents holding more permissions than they need to prompt injection, where hidden instructions in an email or web page hijack an agent.
Early users have already seen what can go wrong. Earlier this year, an OpenClaw agent deleted tens of thousands of emails from the inbox of Summer Yue, Meta’s director of AI alignment, after she had asked it only to suggest what to archive or delete.
There is also a growing list of cases involving AI agents interacting with real-world systems in unexpected or unauthorised ways.
In regulated sectors, the bar is higher. For instance, at the Global Fintech Fest in September, SBI chairman CS Setty said banks will need ‘know your agent’ (KYA) rules for agent identity, customer consent, transaction limits and accountability as AI moves from recommending actions to executing them.
According to Jaspreet Bindra, the cofounder of AI consultancy AI&Beyond, enterprises must learn to deploy that autonomy safely, with trust and accountability at its core. “A phased approach is key: start with well-defined, low-risk workflows, establish clear permissions and accountability, and gradually expand autonomy as reliability improves,” he added.
As companies adopt these digital coworkers, employees will need to learn how to set clear limits on what they can do independently. Unlike the Tamagotchi, these agents do not demand constant attention, but they still need someone to keep an eye on them.
Top Stories From India & Around The World
Anthropic Bans ‘Cruel’ Behaviour Towards Models: The lab’s updated usage policy bars “sustained and needless abusive behaviour” towards Claude, adds controls for autonomous physical actions and tightens rules on deceptive campaigns and election interference.
OpenAI, Anthropic War-Game: The two labs are rehearsing responses to a failure that could potentially cripple critical infrastructure or financial systems, with insiders expecting a major incident within six to twelve months.
Miko Maker Eyes ₹300 Cr: The IIT Bombay-incubated robotics firm launched perception, action and safety models, including the Kavach safety layer, and is closing a ₹300 Cr round that will lift its total funding to about $100 Mn.
The Fight To Get AI’s Attention: As consumers turn to AI assistants for recommendations, brands are racing to master GEO and AEO. But with limited visibility, uncertain attribution and no standard metrics, marketers are still figuring out what drives discovery and sales.
Indian AI Startup Funding Up 265% YoY: Indian AI startups raised a record $438 Mn in Q3 2026, up 265% YoY, taking nine-month funding past $1.1 Bn. However, investor concerns over valuations and capital-intensive business models are growing.
The Weekly Buzz: Anthropic on AI Worms Hijacking Smart Devices
Anthropic’s latest research warns that AI models could soon copy themselves across internet-connected devices, creating a new kind of cyber threat. In a study, the company’s Frontier Red Team found that AI models can already perform several steps needed to spread from one device to another, although completing the entire process reliably remains difficult.
The researchers showed that a 26 Bn-parameter AI model could run across 15 inexpensive Android TV boxes, each costing around $55. In another experiment, the GLM-5.2 model spread across all eight computers in a simulated network in four out of five trials. However, the experiment made it easier for the model to gain access to other devices, so it does not prove that the same attack would work reliably in the real world.
Anthropic estimates that smaller AI models could become capable of copying themselves across devices by the end of 2026 if their capabilities continue improving at the current pace. Such AI-powered attacks could target poorly secured smart TVs, cameras and other connected devices, using their computing power to run AI models and spread further. Unlike traditional malware, these systems could also learn how to work on unfamiliar devices and pass successful methods on to their next copies.
The threat is not yet a proven reality at scale, but the findings point to a growing security risk as AI becomes better at carrying out complex tasks independently. Anthropic recommends stronger security on connected devices and better monitoring of suspicious network activity. The concern is that an AI programme could eventually spread across thousands of devices without relying on a central computer or human instructions to keep it going.
Startup In The Spotlight: Bharat Intelligence
Founded in 2024 by Azhaan Merchant and Gourav Sanghai, Bharat Intelligence is building AI to bridge the gap between Indian farmers and available farm labour.
India’s agricultural sector continues to grapple with a persistent labour shortage, driven by seasonal migration and growing disinterest in farm work. This scarcity disrupts critical activities such as sowing and harvesting, reducing productivity and threatening farmer incomes amid changing climate patterns and market volatility.
The startup’s AI-driven platform predicts labour demand, schedules work crews and connects farmers with skilled workers through intuitive vernacular interfaces, giving farmers a digital route to coordinated farm work.
By accounting for migration cycles, crop seasons and local trust networks, the platform streamlines labour coordination in places where availability alone rarely decides whether work gets done on time, thereby enhancing rural workforce efficiency and access.
Bharat Intelligence’s differentiation lies in treating labour coordination, and not just labour matching, as the problem worth solving for Indian agriculture, which helps farmers overcome labour bottlenecks that sit outside their control.
Prompt Of The Week
What prompts and hacks are CTOs, CEOs and cofounders using these days to streamline their work?
Here’s Ganesh Shankar, CEO & cofounder of Responsive with a prompt he uses to get a one-page executive memo on a Monday.
“Role: You are my Chief of Staff.
Context: It is Monday morning. Assume you have read every important customer conversation, product metric, competitor announcement, AI breakthrough, analyst report and internal update.
Task: Write me a one-page executive memo.
Format: Use only five sections, in this order:
What changed
Why it matters
Decisions I need to make this week
Risks I’m underestimating
One bold idea worth exploring. Constraint: Include nothing outside these five sections, and keep it to one page.”
Editor’s Note: Some prompts may need to be adjusted by users for best results or may not work as intended for certain users.
[Edited by Shishir Parasher]

items.author: Gaurav Bagur
items.content:
Agentic AI startup RevRag.AI has raised $2.5 Mn (about ₹24 Cr) in a seed funding round led by Accion Ventures to expedite product development and expand to the US market. Cedar Hill Capital, Wyser and Venture Catalysts have also backed the startup.
“From the perspective of financial services, the US has a vast number of companies from insurance to credit cards to loans. There is huge penetration there and a large market. And we see that there’s not much competition yet in the category we’re building in,” cofounder and CEO Ashutosh Singh told Inc42 in an interaction.
While expanding to the US market appears to be on the top of the list, the startup is also looking to invest further in fine-tuning its own multimodal small language models (SLMs) to bring its tech layers in-house. Important to highlight that all of its platform is built on third-party proprietary models.
Singh, with schoolmates Neeraj Gupta and Pankaj Gupta, had founded Revrag in 2023 initially modelled as a savings-oriented fintech platform. The idea of pivoting to a SaaS platform came when the trio realised that, while fintech users have slick interfaces and fast transactions at their disposal, onboarding customers continues to be bogged down by repetitive data entry, multiple verifications and cumbersome documentation.
Pivoting early in 2025, RevRag.AI now aims to bridge this gap by streamlining onboarding and sales for banks and fintechs. For this, it offers autonomous AI agents that are capable enough to act as virtual relationship managers embedded within the financial institutions app.
Beyond onboarding, the AI agents also automate customer product sales, support functions as well as provide real-time, multilingual assistance. This helps minimise conversion drop-offs, particularly when it comes to users from underserved backgrounds who have limited trust in digital systems and need assistance navigating financial terminology or English interfaces.
As per Singh, RevRag’s offerings can save up to 70% of costs when compared to traditional channels while simultaneously helping in revenue generation. Thus, the startup will remain sharply focused on this problem statement rather than expanding into additional use cases.
Earlier in 2025, the startup had told Inc42 that it was mulling to launch a no-code flow builder and expand its presence in Indian and American BFSI markets.
The startup has shared aspirations to touch an annual recurring revenue of $50 Mn by FY28. It has lined up innovations like AI-led cross-selling, real-time risk scoring, and automated claims handling.
As of now, it serves over 45 customers across India including the likes of PhonePe, Razorpay, Bajaj Finance, Motilal Oswal, and IIFL. It earlier raised $1 Mn from Powerhouse Ventures and various angel investors including WhatsApp head Kunal Shah.
The fresh round comes at a time when the use of AI in automating fintech business functions is picking up. The global AI in fintech market is pegged to be valued at $45.53 Bn in 2026 and is projected to cross $241 Bn by 2034, growing at a compound annual growth rate (CAGR) of 23.20%.

items.author: Team Inc42
items.content:
UC Taps Public Markets Again for Funds
Urban Company is hungry for more cash. Despite sitting on over hundreds of crores in cash, the consumer services giant’s board will convene next week to consider a fresh fundraise. So, why is Urban Company heading back to the public markets less than a year after its IPO?
UC Seeks Fresh Capital: The startup’s board will meet on October 16 to consider raising capital through equity shares or convertible securities. Besides this, the board will also take a call on which route to take for the fundraise. But what makes this episode interesting is that UC was sitting on ₹2,019 Cr in cash and treasury investments at the end of June. Even ₹310.8 Cr of the startup’s ₹472 Cr fresh issue also remains unutilised. So, why is it chasing more money?
The Cash Guzzler: The likely pressure point is InstaHelp, UC’s instant services vertical. The company is investing heavily in the new arm to create a new category as competition continues to intensify from Snabbit and Pronto. On top of this, InstaHelp continues to weigh heavily on UC’s overall profitability, reporting an adjusted EBITDA loss of ₹132 Cr in Q1 FY27.
Management expects InstaHelp to remain loss-making for the next few years and is unlikely to achieve breakeven before FY31
A Wider Trend: Urban Company’s post-IPO fundraise move reflects a broader pattern among listed new-age tech companies. For companies still investing in expansion, secondary issuances offer capital without interest obligations or repayment pressure. Strong share prices can also allow businesses to raise more money with less dilution. Rather than viewing an IPO as a final exit, founders are using public markets as an ongoing liquidity engine.
But, investors are also shifting focus from gross revenue to earnings per share and ROIC to ensure fresh money creates genuine accretion rather than capital hoarding. Amid this backdrop, will Urban Company’s latest fundraise find any takers? Let’s find out…
From The Editor’s Desk
DailyObjects’ Slow-Burn Playbook
From selling smartphone cases in 2014 to selling accessories and bags, DailyObjects has come a long way in the past decade. What has helped the brand move beyond a market dominated by low-cost, unbranded accessories is its design-led differentiation.
The startup reported a revenue of ₹200 Cr in FY26, and is targeting a ₹400 Cr top line and EBITDA profitability in FY27. This has come on the back of a richer product mix, greater offline contribution and supply-chain efficiencies.
DailyObjects also currently operates 13 exclusive brand outlets and is present in 300 Apple premium reseller stores. It plans to open two to three stores a month, add 30–35 stores in FY27 and build a network of 150–160 stores over five years.
GreenCell Bags ₹330 Cr
The EV startup has raised $34.6 Mn in an equity funding round led by Impact Fund Denmark to support the rollout of about 4,500 electric buses, execute its order book and streamline service delivery.
Founded in 2019, GreenCell Mobility acquires e-buses from contract manufacturers and then deploys them for both intercity and intracity travel. It claims to operate more than 1,200 electric buses and runs over 270 charging stations. It has raised $37 Mn to date.
The fundraise comes as the homegrown electric bus ecosystem continues to scale rapidly on the back of growing government procurement, GCC models, rising EV adoption and electric transition mandates.
UPI MDR Saga Continues
The National Payments Corporation of India has deferred the re-introduction of merchant discount rate on select UPI transactions. Instead of the earlier October 15 rollout, the MDR will now be implemented “immediately after Diwali”.
The NPCI said it took the decision keeping the festive season in mind. The revised implementation date will be notified separately. This follows reports that the Centre was considering delaying the MDR rollout to January 2027.
Under the proposed framework, merchants would be charged an MDR of 0.40% on P2M UPI transactions above ₹2,000, capped at ₹300 per transaction. The move had invited significant push back from retailers, which had demanded the rollback of MDR.
DealShare CEO Exits
Kamaldeep Singh has stepped down as the CEO of the troubled ecommerce unicorn after a three year-long stint. He has now joined electric mobility solutions provider Indofast Energy as its new CEO. DealShare has not announced Singh’s replacement.
The exit comes amid a slew of departures at the beleaguered ecommerce unicorn. CFO Ashish Shah is also looking to exit the startup, while DealShare’s founding team – Sourjyendu Medda, Vineet Rao, Sankar Bora and Rajat Shikhar – all exited in 2024.
Known for online grocery delivery in tier-II+ cities, DealShare is trying to douse fires on multiple fronts. The startup has been scaling down its operations as online business has dwindled to “next to zero”. It is also in talks with Truemeds for a potential fire sale.
Freshworks To Acquire Torii
The Nasdaq-listed SaaS major has signed a definitive agreement to acquire the SaaS management platform for an undisclosed amount. Freshworks expects the deal to close by 2026-end.
By integrating Torii’s SaaS management capabilities into Freshservice, the listed giant aims to help its clients have a better visibility of their AI usage and spending.
Founded in 2010, Freshworks offers SaaS tools to help enterprises manage customer engagement, sales, IT service management, marketing and automation. It reported a net profit of $3.2 Mn in the quarter ended June 2026 against a revenue of $237.4 Mn.
Inc42 Markets
Inc42 Startup Spotlight
How Lickicious Is Betting Big On India’s Pet Parents
India’s pet parents want more than generic kibble or home-cooked meals. Yet, specialised and nutrition-led options remain limited. To solve this, Lickicious is building a pet nutrition brand around food, treats and supplements for dogs and cats.
A Desi Pet Brand: Founded in 2024, Lickicious sells dry and wet foods, treats, supplements and nutritional toppers for dogs and cats. It positions its products around palatability and balanced nutrition, while the startup also operates its own manufacturing setup.
Owning The Supply Chain: Unlike brands that rely entirely on contract manufacturing, Lickicious runs its own manufacturing setup and is developing a 60,000 sq ft manufacturing and distribution footprint. The startup claims that this will increase production capacity, improve supply reliability and strengthen quality control.
The Road Ahead: Backed by Prath Ventures, the startup now plans to scale its R&D and expand into new categories, formats, species and sales channels. The brand is targeting ₹100 Cr in annual revenue going forward and aims to become one of the biggest pet food companies in the country over the next decade.
With India’s pet food market projected to become a $2.2 Bn opportunity by 2030, can Lickicious scale into a durable pet food brand for dogs and cats?
Infographic Of The Day
From Indian textiles and traditional motifs to handcrafted accessories and heritage wear, homegrown craftsmanship is finding a growing audience beyond borders. Can Bharat’s next global D2C success story be woven from its own traditions?

2. GoI will have the option to retain additional subscription up to ₹2,000 crore against the security mentioned above.
3. The security will be sold through Reserve Bank of India Mumbai Office, Fort, Mumbai – 400001. The sale will be subject to the terms and conditions spelt out in the ‘Specific Notification’ mentioned above and the General Notification F.No.4(2)–B(W&M)/2018, dated March 26, 2025.
4. The auction will be conducted using multiple price method. Both competitive and non-competitive bids for the auction should be submitted in electronic format on the Reserve Bank of India Core Banking Solution (e-Kuber system) on October 16, 2026 (Friday). The non-competitive bids should be submitted between 10:30 a.m. and 11:00 a.m. and the competitive bids should be submitted between 10:30 a.m. and 11:30 a.m. The result will be announced on the same day and payment by successful bidders will have to be made on October 19, 2026 (Monday).
5. Bids for underwriting of the Additional Competitive Underwriting (ACU) portion can be submitted by ‘Primary Dealers’ from 09:00 a.m. up to 09:30 a.m. on October 16, 2026 (Friday) on the Reserve Bank of India Core Banking Solution (e-Kuber system).
6. The security will be eligible for “When Issued” trading for a period commencing from October 13, 2026 – October 16, 2026.
7. Operational guidelines for Government of India dated securities auction and other details are given in the Annex.
Ajit Prasad          
Deputy General Manager
(Communications)    
Press Release: 2026-2027/1314
ANNEX
Type of Auction
1. For multiple price-based auction, successful bids will get accepted at the respective quoted yield/price for the security. For uniform price-based auction, bids will get accepted at the cut off yield/price accepted in the auction.
2. The auction will be yield based for new security and price based for securities which are re-issued.
3. In case of a Floating Rate Bonds (FRB), the auction will be spread-based for new security and price based for securities which are reissued. At the time of placing bids for new FRB, the spread should be quoted in percentage terms.
Minimum Bid Size
4. The securities will be issued for a minimum amount of ₹10,000/- (nominal) and in multiples of ₹10,000/- thereafter.
Non-Competitive Segment
5. In all the auctions, Government security up to 5% of the notified amount for sale of individual security will be allotted to the eligible individuals and institutions under the Scheme for Non-competitive Bidding Facility in the Auctions of Government Securities. Individual investors can also place bids as per the non-competitive scheme through the Retail Direct portal (https://rbiretaildirect.org.in).
6. Each bank or Primary Dealer (PD) on the basis of firm orders received from their constituents will submit a single consolidated non-competitive bid for individual security on behalf of its constituents in electronic format on the Reserve Bank of India Core Banking Solution (e-Kuber system).
7. Allotment under the non-competitive segment will be at the weighted average rate of yield/price of the successful bids that will emerge in the auction on the basis of the competitive bidding.
Submission of Bids
8. Both competitive and non-competitive bids for the auction should be submitted in electronic format on the Reserve Bank of India Core Banking Solution (e-Kuber system).
9. Bids in physical form will not be accepted except in extraordinary circumstances.
Business Continuity Plan (BCP)-IT failure
10. Only in the event of system failure, physical bids will be accepted. Such physical bids should be submitted to the Public Debt Office, Mumbai through (email; Phone no: 022-22603456, 022-22603457, 022-22603190) in the prescribed form which can be obtained from RBI website (https://www.rbi.org.in/Scripts/BS_ViewForms.aspx) before the auction timing ends.
11. In case of technical difficulties, Core Banking Operations Team should be contacted (email; Phone no: 022-69870466, 022-69870415).
12. For other auction related difficulties, IDMD auction team can be contacted (email; Phone no: 022-22702431, 022-22705125).
Multiple Bids
13. An investor can submit more than one competitive bid in electronic format on the Reserve Bank of India Core Banking Solution (e-Kuber system).
14. The aggregate amount of bids submitted by an investor in an auction should not exceed the notified amount of auction.
Decision Making Process
15. On the basis of bids received, the Reserve Bank will determine the minimum price/maximum yield up to which tenders for purchase of Government Security will be accepted at the auctions.
16. Bids quoted at rates lower than the minimum price/higher than the maximum yield determined by the Reserve Bank of India will be rejected.
17. Reserve Bank of India will have the full discretion to accept or reject any or all bids either wholly or partially without assigning any reason.
Issue of Securities
18. Issue of securities to the successful bidders will be by credit to Subsidiary General Ledger Account (SGL) or to Constituents’ Subsidiary General Ledger Account (CSGL), maintained with Reserve Bank of India.
Periodicity of Interest Payment
19. Interest on the Government Security will generally be paid half-yearly other than in case of securities with non-standard maturities. The exact periodicity of coupon payment is invariably mentioned in the specific notification for the issue of security.
Underwriting of the Government Securities
20. The underwriting of the Government Securities under auctions by the ‘Primary Dealers’ will be as per the “Revised Scheme of Underwriting Commitment and Liquidity Support” announced by the Reserve Bank vide circular RBI/2007-08/186 dated November 14, 2007 as amended from time to time.
Eligibility for Repurchase Transactions (Repo)
21. The securities will be eligible for Repurchase Transactions (Repo) as per the conditions mentioned in Master Direction – Reserve Bank of India (Repurchase Transactions (Repo)) Directions, 2025 as amended from time to time.
Eligibility for ‘When Issued’ Trading
22. The securities will be eligible for “When Issued” trading in accordance with the guidelines on ‘When Issued transactions in Central Government Securities’ issued by the Reserve Bank of India vide circular No. RBI/2018-19/25 dated July 24, 2018 as amended from time to time.
Investment by Non-Residents
23. Investments by Non-Residents are subject to the guidelines on ‘Fully Accessible Route’ for Investment by Non-residents in Government Securities and other related guidelines as issued by the Reserve Bank from time to time.

items.content: ET Intelligence Group: Nifty 50 banks are expected to report 11.5% year-on-year growth in aggregate net interest income (NII) for the September quarter, according to the average of estimates by ETIG and four broking firms. However, growth in pre-provision operating profit and net profit will be slower, at around 10%, given the pressure on treasury income due to hardened bond yields. Credit costs are expected to stay benign during the quarter amid stable asset quality.The quarter was marked by strong capital inflows for the banking system through the RBI's 2026 Foreign Currency Non-Resident-Bank (FCNR-B) deposit swap scheme, which collected over $127 billion, exceeding expectations. This is expected to support deposit growth, which has not kept pace with the pick-up in credit demand for the past several quarters. On the flip side, it is likely to affect the CASA (current account savings account) ratio and net interest margins (NIMs).134929652"For large private banks, these inflows may dilute reported CASA ratios and create a short-term drag as funding raised at attractive offshore spreads takes time to be deployed," said Kotak Securities in a report. The broker estimates a 10-15 basis point quarterly impact from FCNR deposits on NIMs.Read more: Sebi extends IPO-size flexibility on the back of soaring primary market activity"Provisional business updates for 30 banks show loan growth accelerating sharply to 19.1% year-on-year and 6.6% sequentially, and deposit growth to 15.8% year-on-year and 5.8% sequentially, aided meaningfully by the FCNR-B mobilisation drive," noted JM Financial Institutional Securities in a preview report. The broking firm expects net profit of the banks under its coverage to grow by 12% year-on-year.Read more: Anand Rathi Share and Stock Brokers Q2 results: Profit jumps 50% YoY to Rs 42 crore, revenue rises 20%"NIMs may remain compressed in the September quarter but should gradually recover in the second half as banks retire high-cost liabilities and deploy liquidity into loans," said Global Financial Services in a preview report, adding that banks with high floating-rate loans may benefit from the recent rate hike. For investors, management commentary by banks on FCNR-related deployment, trends in fee income and the impact of the recent rate increase will be crucial. "Key metrics to monitor are deployment trajectory and yields on FCNR deposits, impact of rate hike, upcoming ECL transition and any stress in SME and unsecured loans," stated JM Financial in the report. Among the top private sector banks, Axis Bank is expected to report the highest YoY net profit growth of 41% for the September quarter, followed by Kotak Mahindra Bank with a 29% increase. For SBI, profit is likely to grow by 11.2%. All three banks expected to report double-digit NII growth.For non-banking financial companies, performance is expected to remain strong, driven by growth in disbursements and stable asset quality. "Resilient retail demand and a gradual recovery in loan against property should support diversified financiers," said JM Financial in a preview report. The broker expects 20% YoY growth in aggregate assets under management.

items.title: Can RBI’s six forex measures help stabilise the rupee?
items.summary: Kolkata: The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has taken a slew of steps since Saturday to help lift the rupee to what Governor Sanjay Malhotra described as its "correct" value. items.content: Kolkata: The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has taken a slew of steps since Saturday to help lift the rupee to what Governor Sanjay Malhotra described as its "correct" value. These measures have helped the rupee recover to 95.28 a dollar, about 150 paise over two days. An immediate fallout is the reduction in speculative bets on the currency and discouraging over-hedging by companies in anticipation of further rupee depreciation. An inevitable inflation in hedging costs, a natural outcome of the reserves to be set aside by banks against client exposures, has caused some noses to wrinkle in the importer community.Separately, total removal of the dollar needs of three state-run fuel retailers from the spot rupee market reduces the pressure on the currency.Here's an ET explainer on the measures taken by the central bank and their impact.Introduction of Foreign Exchange Risk Reserve (FERR)A first-time measure imposing a 20% cash reserve requirement on large forex derivatives contracts over $2 million. This means banks will have to set aside funds as a percentage of their total exposure, and that money will no longer be available for onlending until the exposure is fully cancelled.For instance, for a $10 million hedging contract for a client, a bank will have to keep around ₹19 crore everyday with the central bank until the expiry of the contract. This money is not available for lending.Hence, banks will have to pass on this cost to their clients. This would inflate the hedging cost for importers by at least 150 basis points (one basis point is a hundredth of a percentage point) and, therefore, they would be discouraged to hedge their exposure, experts said.Read more: Anand Rathi Share and Stock Brokers Q2 results: Profit jumps 50% YoY to Rs 42 crore, revenue rises 20%FERR Impact on the Forwards MarketsAnother fallout of the FERR curbs is an immediate cut in the rates on forward premium, as the aggregate demand for hedging itself would reduce. Since importers would keep open positions, it would ultimately soften forward premium rates, currency experts believe. Softening forward premiums will also help reduce pressure on the spot rupee in the local market.However, a section of the importers is worried their cost would climb significantly as the funds needed to hedge will eat into their working capital buffers, potentially requiring them to borrow to plug the gap.Read more: Strong buzz! Reliance Jio said to see over $20 billion bids as investors line up for India's biggest IPOExtension of FERR restrictions for contracts with overseas entitiesThe regulator Monday widened the ambit of FERR, extending the rule for non-deliverable contracts involving rupee to non-resident customers, only for the purpose of hedging. The move also eliminates the probability of dollar hoarding by companies and importers because of the steep FERR costs, limiting their dollar exposure to genuine and foreseeable business needs.Threshold for foreign exchange derivative transactions reducedThe limit has been reduced to $5 million equivalent from $100 million across all authorised dealers. This will curb speculative trading in the rupee. A corresponding reduction has been introduced in exchange-traded currency derivatives involving the rupee, across stock exchanges taken together.Restrictions on rebooking of cancelled foreign exchange derivative contractsBanks cannot allow users to rebook any previously cancelled foreign exchange derivative contract involving the rupee - whether deliverable or non-deliverable. Rollover of foreign exchange derivative contracts on maturity shall continue to be permitted.Special dollar window for State-run oil retailersThe RBI would use its own dollar stockpile to meet the daily dollar needs of Indian Oil Corp, Bharat Petroleum Corp and Hindustan Petroleum Corp. This reduces dollar demand in the spot market, easing the pressure on rupee.This would also mask the underlying pressure on balance of payments while dollars will be drained from the central bank's foreign exchange reservess. The Reserve Bank of India opened this window Monday, albeit for a temporary period.Stricter verificationRBI tells banks to obtain additional documentation for verification of underlying exposures. This will prevent users from entering into foreign exchange derivative contracts involving the rupee to hedge contracted exposures, using the same underlying exposure that has been hedged with any other bank. Banks have to keep the documents for a minimum two-year period.Overall views of forex market and treasury professionalsEconomists see these measures as tactical steps to support the rupee, not structural solutions ensuring its durable stability. They believe that defending the rupee amid the continued geopolitical headwinds would be a costly policy trade-off, requiring broader capital market reforms to encourage stable and long term foreign capital inflows.India still levies a security transactions tax, even when the long-term capital gains tax was reintroduced in 2018, and increased it to 12.5% last year. Experts suggest a broader response spanning lowering of taxes, exchange-rate flexibility and further monetary policy tightening to bolster the rupee.

By James Ogunnaike, Abeokuta
The Peoples Democratic Party (PDP), candidate for Ifo Constituency I in the Ogun State House of Assembly, Adebari Adekunle, has cautioned the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC), over the omission of the party’s gubernatorial candidate from the election.
Adekunle also warned the All Progressives Congress, APC, gubernatorial candidate, Senator Solomon Adeola, popularly known as Yayi, against actions that could heighten political tension in the state.
The final list, signed by INEC Secretary, Rose Oriaran-Anthony, contains the candidates of 13 political parties, including the APC. However, PDP is missing from the list.
Adekunle, while reacting to the development, said the exclusion of Oladipupo Adebutu and his running mate, Lateefat Sowunmi-Kolapo, from INEC’s list had gone beyond the two candidates and had become a matter of concern for the entire state.
He recalled that President Bola Tinubu expressed displeasure over the desperation of some political associates, warning that their actions could damage his administration’s image and democratic legacy.
According to Adekunle, the Presidency’s comment is a “great indictment” on INEC and raises serious questions about its credibility and Yayi’s role in the controversy.
The Assembly candidate cautioned INEC against undermining public confidence in the electoral process and urged the commission to act transparently and reverse the omission.
Adekunle insisted that Ogun State must not become a battleground for desperate political interests ahead of the 2027 elections.
“A situation where APC party members would be celebrating that they would remove names from the INEC list even before it actually happened was a reckless one,” he said.
Adekunle said many residents, angered by what they perceive as an attempt to undermine their choice, had threatened to protest, while elders and stakeholders were appealing for calm to prevent a breakdown of peace.
“Ogun State must not become a battleground for desperate political interests. Political ambition should not take precedence over democratic principles. People are already burdened by economic hardship, are looking towards 2027 for change and will resist any attempt to deny them a fair opportunity to choose their leaders. Peace must not be mistaken for weakness,” he warned.
He urged the Presidency to ensure that no individual uses the President’s name to advance personal ambition and stain his efforts at credible elections.
The Assembly hopeful also urged INEC to act transparently and address the controversy without delay, stressing that peace must not be mistaken for weakness and the people’s patience must not be taken for granted.

items.content:
The All Progressives Congress (APC) spokesperson, Felix Morka, has dismissed reports of a rift between the party’s governors and Minister of the Federal Capital Territory, Nyesom Wike, saying there was no real tension between them.
Morka said the perceived disagreement was a “false battle” because both the APC governors and Wike were committed to President Bola Tinubu’s re-election bid ahead of the 2027 general elections.
He spoke on Tuesday during an interview on Arise Television’s News Day, following Wike’s inclusion in the APC presidential campaign council.
“It was a false battle to begin with. I mean, I don’t think there was any real tension between those positions because they united in their extraordinary commitment to the re-election of the president,” Morka said.
He noted that the Progressive Governors Forum comprised governors elected on the APC platform, while Wike, a former Rivers State governor, was a member of Tinubu’s cabinet and a vocal supporter of the President.
According to him, their shared political interest made reports of a disagreement between them largely insignificant.
Morka said the publication of the presidential campaign council list had also clarified the roles of those involved in Tinubu’s re-election campaign.
He pointed to the inclusion of governors who do not belong to the APC, describing it as evidence of Tinubu’s ability to attract support across party lines.
“Governors, who are not of the APC, now [are] front and centre, coordinating some of our activities in their respective jurisdictions,” he said.
The APC spokesperson described the development as a new phase in Nigeria’s democratic politics, arguing that the President was bringing politicians from different parties together around a common objective.
“What we’re witnessing today in our country is novel. It’s really a new dawn for democracy,” Morka said.
He argued that the collaboration was unusual in a presidential system, where political parties are generally expected to compete against one another.
According to Morka, Tinubu was transcending party differences by building a coalition of political actors to support his administration and re-election campaign.
“We’re seeing a president who is transcending all of the divides and really nullifying what I call the politics of difference between these partisans and bringing them together under the same umbrella to pursue a common agenda for the good of the people,” he said.

items.author: Emmanuel Okogba
items.content:
By Gabriel Ewepu
ABUJA – Investors and key players in Nigeria’s mining sector have called for clearer regulations, improved security and stronger collaboration among government agencies to attract investment and unlock the country’s vast solid mineral resources.
They made the call at the opening of the 11th Nigeria Mining Week in Abuja, identifying insecurity, regulatory conflicts, poor inter-agency coordination and inadequate infrastructure as major barriers to the growth of the sector.
President of the Miners Association of Nigeria, Oba Ayandele Ayanleke, said insecurity along mining corridors and jurisdictional disputes between federal and subnational authorities were undermining operations and eroding investors’ confidence.
Ayanleke urged the government to establish a clearer and more predictable regulatory framework, stressing that stronger partnerships between local and international stakeholders were critical to attracting capital, facilitating technology transfer, creating jobs and generating wealth.
On a recent mining incident, he disclosed that the government had constituted an investigative panel, urging stakeholders to await the outcome of its findings.
Meanwhile, the Country Manager, Segilola Resources Operating Limited, Austin Menegbo, said Nigeria must build on the achievements of its first large-scale commercial gold mine to establish a competitive and sustainable mining industry.
Menegbo disclosed that Segilola produced 91,910 ounces of gold in 2025, with Nigerians accounting for 99 per cent of its workforce.
According to him, the mine has demonstrated that responsible investment, technical expertise, effective regulation and sustained engagement with host communities can support globally competitive mining operations.
He, however, identified regulatory uncertainty, illegal mining, insecurity, poor infrastructure and limited access to finance as challenges requiring urgent government intervention.
He called for streamlined government approvals, predictable regulatory timelines and sustained engagement among operators, investors, host communities and other stakeholders to improve the sector’s investment climate.
He also advocated the formalisation of artisanal and small-scale mining through safety training, improved access to finance, technical support and cooperative structures.
He stressed that efforts to attract investment must go hand in hand with environmental protection, workers’ safety and responsible engagement with host communities.
Similarly, Head of Mission of the Swedish Embassy in Nigeria, Ambassador Anna Westerholm, called for partnerships that prioritise local value addition, workplace safety, community welfare and transparency.
Westerholm said Nigeria could leverage Sweden’s expertise in mining technology, automation, skills development and responsible mineral production to strengthen its mining industry.
She noted that the long-term success of mining projects depended largely on their impact on host communities and the environment, adding that companies must earn public trust to operate sustainably.
The Swedish envoy also underscored the importance of mineral traceability, saying the ability to verify the origin of minerals and the conditions under which they were produced would boost Nigeria’s competitiveness in international markets.
She expressed Sweden’s readiness to deepen cooperation with Nigeria through technical assistance, trade and investment partnerships.
Earlier, Partner and Mining Industry Leader at PwC Nigeria, Cyril Azobu, said the country must translate its abundant mineral resources and growing international interest into bankable projects and sustainable economic growth.
He said achieving this would require a predictable investment environment, credible projects and partnerships capable of connecting local opportunities with international capital, technology and expertise.
Azobu also called for a shift from exporting raw minerals to domestic processing and value addition, saying the move would enable Nigeria to retain more economic benefits from its mineral resources.
He reaffirmed PwC Nigeria’s commitment to supporting the sector through technical expertise, regulatory guidance and engagement with industry stakeholders.
The 11th Nigeria Mining Week is being held under the theme, ‘Unlocking Investment and Growth through Partnerships’.
The post Mining Week: Investors demand clear rules, stronger security appeared first on Vanguard News.

items.author: Emmanuel Okogba
items.content:
Pope Leo XIV had a cancerous growth removed from his right lung in a 90-minute operation on Tuesday and “woke up normally” after the procedure, the Vatican said.
A Vatican source said further tests were being carried out to determine if the cancer had spread.
“To ensure the procedure was radical, the lower lobe of the right lung was removed,” the Vatican said in a statement.
The operation “confirmed the diagnosis of a pulmonary adenocarcinoma, as suspected from the pre-operative tests”, it said.
The pope was in the operating room for a total of three hours and the operation lasted half that time.
“The surgery was successful and there were no complications,” the Vatican said.
A Vatican source said he requested dinner after the procedure.
Leo had entered the hospital smiling and waving earlier on Tuesday hours before the surgery.
The Vatican has said it expects the pope to stay in his room on the 10th floor of Rome’s Gemelli hospital to recover for several days.
His audiences have been cancelled until October 20 and the operation raises questions about whether the pope will go on a lengthy visit to Latin America next month.
– ‘I will pray a lot’ –
The surgery marks the 71-year-old Leo’s first hospitalisation since he became head of the Catholic Church on May 8, 2025.
In a surprise announcement following Angelus prayers on Sunday, Leo told crowds in St Peter’s Square that doctors had discovered a nodule “at a very early stage” during medical checks.
“The doctors believe it would be right to intervene,” he said.
The Vatican has historically been very secretive about the health of popes, but began to be more transparent during the illness of Leo’s predecessor Francis, an Argentine who freely discussed his ailments.
Ahead of the operation, people outside the hospital expressed concern over the pope’s condition.
Giorgia Fei, a 57-year-old Italian, said she had been worried.
“However, the Holy Father is in very good hands here at the hospital because we have some outstanding doctors,” she said.
“I will pray a lot for him.”
Giuseppe Purpura, 72, said he too was concerned.
“He’s still quite young and I really wasn’t expecting this. I thought he was in better health,” he said, noting that “thankfully it was caught in time.”
The Vicar General for the Diocese of Rome, Cardinal Baldassare Reina, led a rosary prayer for the pope inside the hospital chapel which was broadcast by the Vatican. Dozens of people attended and Reina asked all the city’s parishes to join in.
The Vatican secretary of state, Cardinal Pietro Parolin, told ANSA news agency that Leo had been “very calm” about his condition when they met on Monday.
The Vatican told AFP the nodule was found during routine health checks, and there were no symptoms that led to checking the pope’s lungs.
Chicago-born Leo, the first US pope, is sporty and believed to generally be in good health.
He is scheduled to travel to South America from November 6-17 to visit Uruguay, Argentina and Peru.
It was not immediately clear what would happen if the pope was forced into a longer recovery.
Under Church law, a figure known as the Cardinal Camerlengo — or chamberlain — takes over administrative duties if the pope dies, but pontiffs do not have a deputy to replace them if they become incapacitated.

items.author: Emmanuel Okogba
items.content:
Atletico Madrid eased to a 2-0 win over Manchester United in the Champions League on Tuesday to pile pressure on Red Devils coach Michael Carrick.
Pablo Barrios pounced inside the first minute for Diego Simeone’s side and after Leny Yoro’s 74th minute red card set United back further, Ademola Lookman added another for the hosts in Madrid.
Man United have made their worst domestic start in 40 years and this league phase defeat in the Spanish capital was another blow, with the team now winless in five games across all competitions.
Carrick handed Carlos Baleba his first start for the club since arriving from Brighton this summer, as well as pushing captain Bruno Fernandes out to the right side.
Atletico were without their skipper Koke, after the death of his mother, while coach Simeone selected Julian Alvarez from the off for the first time this season at the Metropolitano stadium, after he tried to force a departure this summer.
“Defend what we love,” Atletico fans ordered their supporters with a banner display before kick-off and the Rojiblancos were ahead after just 50 seconds.
Manchester United’s English head coach Michael Carrick applauds at the end of the UEFA Champions League, league phase, matchday 2, football match between Club Atletico de Madrid and Manchester United at the Metropolitano stadium in Madrid on October 13, 2026. Atletico Madrid won 2-0. (Photo by Oscar DEL POZO / AFP)
Alex Baena found a way in behind United’s defence and cut the ball across for Barrios, with Ayden Heaven unable to keep the midfielder’s shot from crossing the line.
Bryan Mbuemo might have equalised for the visitors, nudging the ball through Cristian Romero’s legs but firing just wide.
Alejandro Grimaldo came inches away from extending Atletico’s lead with a free-kick which hit the angle between post and crossbar.
The hosts thought they had a second when Johnny Cardoso finished neatly from the edge of the box before half-time but the goal was disallowed after a VAR review showed the ball had struck Marcos Llorente’s hand during the build-up.
Alvarez, yet to score this season for Atletico, hit the post early in the second half.
United rallied and Fernandes’s lob drifted narrowly wide before the Portuguese playmaker hit the crossbar from the left of the box after a corner routine.
However the three-time European champions suffered a setback when defender Yoro was harshly dismissed after a VAR review for bringing down Canada striker Jonathan David as the last man.
It opened the door for Atletico to grab their second, with David foiled by goalkeeper Senne Lammens but London-born Nigeria international Lookman on hand to tuck home the rebound after 79 minutes.
Carrick withdrew playmaker Fernandes, looking ahead to the weekend visit to face rivals Leeds in the English top flight, where improvement is badly needed.
Atletico goalkeeper Jan Oblak saved from United substitute Matheus Cunha in the final stages but there was no way back for United.
Simeone’s side were able to claim their first points after an opening defeat at Liverpool.

items.content:
Original | Oct 14, 02:37 IST
The government has selected Blume Ventures, Speciale Invest, Chiratae Ventures and 16 others as second-level fund managers (SLFM) for deploying ₹7,131 Cr from the ₹1 Lakh Cr research, development and innovation (RDI) fund.
This is the first cohort of the SLFM under the fund. Overall, the empowered group of secretaries (EGoS) under the science ministry has approved 14 alternative investment funds (AIFs) and five focused research organisations (FROs) for this purpose earlier this month.
The other selected AIFs also include YourNest Capital Advisors, Sixth Sense Ventures, Celesta India, AdvantEdge Investment Managers, IvyCap Ventures, Ideaspring Capital Fund, TVS Capital Funds, AMA Capital Advisors, Translation Endeavors and “Campus”.
Meanwhile, the selected FROs include the likes of IISc Bengaluru’s AI & Robotics Technology Park (ARTPARK), Centre for Cellular and Molecular Platforms (CCAMP) in Bengaluru, IIT-Madras Research Park, Pilani Innovation & Entrepreneurship Development Society (PIEDS) at BITS-Pilani, and Society for Innovation & Entrepreneurship (SINE) at IIT-Bombay.
Update | Oct 12, 21:48 IST
Central government-backed ₹1 Lakh Cr Research, Development and Innovation (RDI) Fund has approved 19 second-level fund managers (SLFMs) with a total commitment of ₹7,131 Cr.
The Ministry of Science and Technology’s Empowered Group of Secretaries (EGoS) approved 14 alternative investment funds (AIFs) and five focused research organisations (FROs) for this purpose earlier this month, the ministry announced.
The selected entities will channel capital from the RDI Fund to eligible technology enterprises undertaking research, development and innovation activities at Technology Readiness Level (TRL) 4 and above.
The fund managers are also expected to mobilise private capital equivalent to the RDI Fund’s contribution, potentially expanding the pool of financing available to research-driven businesses.
Alongside approving the first cohort of fund managers, the EGoS approved five additional technologies for coverage under the RDI Fund. The government did not specify these technologies in its announcement.
The government said it would continue inviting applications and onboarding additional cohorts of fund managers, expanding the reach of the scheme and encouraging public-private investment in India’s research and innovation ecosystem.
Launched in November 2025, the RDI Scheme has an overall outlay of ₹1 Lakh Cr and aims to address the funding gap faced by companies developing high-risk, high-impact technologies. It is managed by an independent business unit housed within the Anusandhan National Research Foundation (ANRF), under the Department of Science and Technology (DST).
The fund is designed to spur private investment in research-intensive businesses. However, its impact on investor sentiment, however, remains unclear. In August, The Indian Express reported that nearly two-thirds of the more than ₹2,000 Cr allocated to deeptech companies under the scheme had gone to firms linked to members of the panel involved in selecting beneficiaries. The report raised concerns about potential conflicts of interest.
Inc42’s Q3 2026 Indian Investor Ranking & Sentiment Survey, which covered 85 institutional investors, found that 52% considered disclosure and recusal safeguards adequate, but said visibility into the process remained limited.
Another 25% viewed the issue as a governance failure that required independent oversight, while 14% said potential conflicts could be managed through disclosure and recusal. The remaining 9% said the issue was not a concern, arguing that the focus should be on selecting the right companies.
As per Inc42’s ‘Indian Tech Startup Funding Report, Q3 2026’, deeptech startup funding in the September quarter zoomed 176% YoY to $290 Mn raised across 28 deals, compared with $105 Mn across 29 deals in Q3 2025. The sector outpaced the broader startup ecosystem, where funding grew 5% to $2.2 Bn.

Beyond the roster news, players and EVO viewers have complained that assists are too strong and too easy to spam. Many said matches are hard to follow when both sides keep firing assists. Director Kazuto Sekine has said assist and tag use exceeded the team’s plans and that longer cooldowns are being prepared. A build shown at EVO reportedly tested tighter assist timing, pointing to a balance update aimed at those complaints.
High Stakes for Arc System Works
If the patch works, Arc System Works may steady Marvel Tokon after a rocky post-launch stretch. The title is one of the studio’s biggest games in a long time. Some fans warn that if it fades quickly, talk of an “Arc System Works curse” — games dying within about six months — will only get louder.

items.author: Akinbayo Wahab
items.content:
A Kaduna State High Court on Tuesday has overruled an objection by former Governor Nasir El-Rufai’s defence team to the testimony of the Department of State Services (DSS) digital forensic expert.
The presiding Judge, Justice Darius Khobo ruled that the prosecution could call the witness, who was subpoenaed by the court, despite his name and evidence summary being absent from the prosecution’s witness list.
The judge held that the defence’s right to fair hearing could be protected by allowing it to cross-examine the witness.
The ruling followed objections by El-Rufai’s senior counsel, Paul Erokoro, who argued that the defence had not received the witness’s evidence summary or the subpoena.
Erokoro submitted that the omission denied the defence adequate notice to prepare for cross-examination and understand the case it was required to answer.
The ICPC prosecution counsel, Ayodele Adedipe, however, argued that failure to include a subpoenaed witness in the proof of evidence did not automatically render the testimony inadmissible.
In its ruling, the court confirmed that the witness had been subpoenaed through an order signed by the court on June 30, 2026.
Khobo said the prosecution’s position reflected the applicable law, citing previous cases in support of the ruling.
The judge held that the witness’s absence from the prosecution’s witness list and evidence summary did not prevent him from testifying because he had been subpoenaed.
He added that the defence’s fair-hearing concerns could be addressed by allowing it to cross-examine the witness.
Earlier, the DSS digital forensic examiner, Shegun Kayode, testified about a forensic examination of communication records and audio recordings allegedly linked to the defendant.
Kayode told the court that specialised software revealed two-way communications involving El-Rufai and suspected associates, including Bashir El-Rufai and another person, between October. 25 and 28, 2025.
He said the findings prompted further analysis of audio recordings received from a communication intelligence server.
The witness explained that he immediately created a forensic image of the original audio file, sealed it and secured it to preserve its technical integrity.
Kayode said subsequent software examination showed that the audio was authentic and had not been artificially generated or manipulated using artificial intelligence.
The News Agency of Nigeria (NAN) reports that El-Rufai arrived at the court amid heavy security, accompanied by his wife, Asiya El-Rufai, and Isa Ashiru Kudan, the governorship candidate of the African Democratic Congress (ADC) in Kaduna State.
El-Rufai was brought to court for the continuation of his trial over alleged corruption in a suit filed against him by the Independent Corrupt Practices and Other Related Offences Commission (ICPC).
During the proceedings, an audio recording of his interrogation by the DSS concerning the alleged importation of about 10 kilogrammes of thallium sulphate, a highly toxic and strictly regulated substance, into Nigeria was played.
The recording, which lasted about one hour and 30 minutes, contained the interrogation and other exchanges.
The case was adjourned until November. 30 and December 1 for continuation of the cross-examination of the DSS witness by the defence counsel.
Speaking with journalists after the court proceedings, Adedipe said the prosecution had opened its case by calling its first witness, a forensic expert.
He said the witness testified and tendered a forensic investigation report before cross-examination commenced.
Adedipe explained that the proceedings took considerable time because of objections and legal arguments but said the prosecution was able to conclude its presentation with the witness for the day.
He confirmed that the case had been adjourned until November 30 and December 1 for continuation of cross-examination.
Erokoro, counsel to El-Rufai, said the prosecution had opened its case and called its first witness, adding that the lengthy proceedings showed the parties’ commitment to ensuring the trial progressed.
He expressed confidence that his client would be discharged and acquitted of all the charges.
Erokoro said the defence had begun examining the witness’s testimony and would continue to scrutinise the evidence when the court reconvened.
He maintained that the next hearing would provide the defence with an opportunity to test the accuracy and credibility of the prosecution’s evidence.

items.content:
By Kingsley Omonobi
The outgoing and incoming Chairmen of the ECOWAS Committee of Chiefs of Defence Staff (CCDS) have called for sustained Nigerian support to strengthen regional security cooperation and address growing threats across West Africa.
The two military chiefs made the appeal on Tuesday during a courtesy visit to the Chief of Defence Staff (CDS), General Olufemi Oluyede, at the Defence Headquarters in Abuja.
The outgoing Chairman, Lieutenant General Amara Idara Bangura, who is Sierra Leone’s Chief of Defence Staff, expressed appreciation to Nigeria for its continued support for the ECOWAS defence framework and regional security initiatives throughout his tenure.
Bangura disclosed that he and his successor had spent the previous two days conducting formal handover activities ahead of the transition in the leadership of the ECOWAS defence committee.
He commended Nigeria’s longstanding contributions to peace and stability in West Africa, particularly its support for Sierra Leone during the country’s civil war and subsequent peacebuilding efforts.
He also highlighted Nigeria’s contributions to regional peacekeeping operations, counter-terrorism cooperation and logistical support, describing the country’s role as critical to the security of the sub-region.
The outgoing chairman urged Oluyede to extend the same level of cooperation and goodwill to his successor to ensure continuity in regional security efforts.
In his remarks, the incoming Chairman of the ECOWAS Committee of Chiefs of Defence Staff and Senegal’s Chief of Defence Staff, Vice Admiral Oumar Wade, thanked the Nigerian military leadership for the warm reception accorded the delegation.
Wade identified terrorism, violent extremism, transnational organised crime and maritime insecurity as some of the complex and evolving threats confronting ECOWAS member states.
He described Nigeria as a key regional power and an anchor of security in West Africa, stressing that its continued guidance, participation and support would be essential to the committee’s ability to fulfil its mandate.
Responding, Oluyede thanked the two defence chiefs for their commendation of Nigeria and its Armed Forces, describing their visit as a demonstration of solidarity and a shared commitment to regional peace and security.
The CDS called for stronger unity, cooperation and mutual understanding among ECOWAS member states, urging countries to set aside political differences, divergent interests and bilateral disputes to confront common security threats.
He emphasised that security was indivisible, noting that no country could effectively guarantee its own safety in isolation from its neighbours.
Oluyede reaffirmed Nigeria’s commitment to supporting ECOWAS security initiatives, citing the country’s determination to promote regional peace, integration and development.
He also assured Wade of Nigeria’s full support during his tenure as chairman, expressing confidence that sustained cooperation among member states would strengthen the region’s collective security architecture.

items.author: Emmanuel Okogba
items.content:
Duane “Keffe D” Davis, the former Los Angeles gang leader who boasted for years of his involvement in the killing of rapper Tupac Shakur, only to deny it when he came to trial, was sentenced to a minimum 40 years in prison on Tuesday.
The sentence, which will likely see him die in custody, comes three decades after the gunning down of one of the most influential hip hop artists of the late 20th century, and after years of criticism over investigations that went nowhere.
Davis, 63, formerly ran a branch of the feared Crips, one of a patchwork of rival gangs that controlled parts of Los Angeles in the 1990s.
He spent years evading justice and seemingly believed he was beyond the reach of the law when he wrote in his memoir that he had ordered the killing of Shakur.
“For three years, I’ve heard you say some variation of the same thing to law enforcement… in your book, and it’s something like, ‘Yeah, I was involved in this, but I’m different. I’ve moved on. I got out of Compton. I’m a grandfather now,'” Judge Carli Kierny told Davis as she handed down the sentence in a Las Vegas courtroom.
“I’m here to tell you that’s not how this works.”
“You don’t get to take a man from his family. You don’t get to take his very life, his whole future from him, and just walk away from it. Especially when that man is Tupac Shakur,” the judge said.
Shakur was a key figure in a hip-hop rivalry pitting the US East Coast against the West Coast. He was just 25 when he was gunned down in Las Vegas.
A trial heard how Davis ordered the September 7, 1996 killing of the hip-hop artist after his own nephew had been beaten by members of Shakur’s entourage at a Las Vegas casino.
The “California Love” artist was shot about two hours after the casino confrontation by a gunman in a white Cadillac that pulled up at a red light alongside the BMW in which the rapper was riding.
Davis handed the gun to someone sitting in the back seat of the Cadillac and ordered that person to shoot Shakur, who died six days later.
The name of that person has not been definitively revealed and Davis is the only person who was in the Cadillac that evening who is still alive.
The driver of the BMW, Death Row Records co-founder Marion “Suge” Knight, was wounded.
– ‘Born an icon’ –
The killing of Shakur, also known as 2Pac, was one of America’s most famous cold cases, prompting endless debate among music fans over who did it, and why.
Known for hits including “All Eyez on Me,” Shakur — the son of a Black Panther activist — was raised in Harlem and Baltimore, but quickly became the epitome of California hip hop when he signed with Los Angeles-based Death Row Records.
His sister Sekyiwa Shakur paid emotional tribute on Tuesday to her brother, a man whom she said “was born an icon.”
She said their mother “consciously raised him to be a human rights activist, someone to stand up for those weaker and smaller than he was, and that’s who he was to me and all the family. He was the person that you go to for protection.
“He dedicated his career to the advancement of his people. He was gentle and kind to women and children. He fed anyone he knew that didn’t have. He was truly my shining star, my shining prince. He was who God trusted to take care of me.”
Davis offered no words of contrition ahead of the sentence being handed down, vowing only to appeal the guilty finding.

items.author: Akinbayo Wahab
items.content:
The Deputy Gov. of Lagos State, Dr Obafemi Hamzat, has unveiled a policy agenda for the state, promising reforms in transportation, housing, security, technology, food distribution and justice delivery ahead of the 2027 governorship election.
Hamzat made the commitments while presenting his Promise Agenda, tagged, ‘An Afternoon to Discuss the Facts and Figures of Lagos State: The 8th Largest Economy in Africa’.
The event was organised by the Lagos Chamber of Commerce and Industry (LCCI) in collaboration with the Contact and Mobilisation Committee, Formal Sector for PBAT and KOH on Tuesday in Victoria Island, Lagos State.
 .
Hamzat, the All Progressives Congress (APC) governorship candidate for the 2027 elections, described it as a social contract with Lagos residents, which he pledged to implement from May 29, 2027, if elected governor.
He said the agenda was designed to establish measurable targets for government, enabling residents to assess performance and hold the administration accountable for its promises.
Hamzat said transportation remained one of Lagos most pressing challenges, noting that traffic congestion costs the state an estimated economic losses of N1 trillion annually, with residents spending an average of four hours daily in traffic.
He said Lagos had a vehicle density of 212 vehicles per kilometre, compared with the national average of 16, making the development of alternative transportation systems imperative.
According to him, the state has identified 63 traffic junctions for improvement and addressed 33 of them, while plans are underway to expand Bus Rapid Transit services, improve terminals, develop rail infrastructure and increase water transportation.
He said his administration would prioritise waterways to reduce pressure on roads, including developing ferry terminals and improving connections between communities such as Ikorodu, Badagry and other parts of Lagos.
Hamzat also promised improved pedestrian walkways, greener public spaces and better organised bus terminals to separate commuters from vehicular traffic.
He said the state aimed to plant 10 million trees within four years.
On water supply, Hamzat said the completion of an ongoing water infrastructure project would provide additional access to water for six million people.
On Jobs, technology and business growth, the APC candidate said the Lagos State Employment Trust Fund had supported businesses and activated about 340,000 jobs since 2019.
He added that his administration if elected, would strengthen mentorship and business management support to help small enterprises survive and expand.
He said the state had proposed four industrial parks in Epe, Badagry, Ikorodu and Ojo under its 2025–2030 industrial policy.
Hamzat also pledged to harmonise government levies and regulatory processes to reduce the burden on businesses, while reviewing charges imposed on petty traders and micro-enterprises.
On technology, he described Yaba as a major technology hub, saying its technology ecosystem had developed into a 15.3-billion-dollar economy with about 2,000 start-ups.
He noted that Lagos was implementing a 1,000-kilometre fibre-optic cable network, with plans to expand it to 6,000 kilometres, while reducing broadband costs and supporting local technology companies.
The deputy governor further added that the state would adopt a local-first procurement approach by giving qualified Nigerian technology firms the first opportunity to supply products required by the government.
On food security and creative economy, Hamzat said the state was developing a 420-hectare food logistics hub and cold-chain network to reduce food wastage, improve storage and cut transportation costs between farmers and markets.
He said: “The cold-chain facilities in Mushin and Gbagada has helped market women reduce logistics costs by 40 per cent while government is expanding medium-scale markets across the state.”
“Also, the state will support farmers through a proposed N500 billion guarantee scheme, alongside arrangements in facilitating the purchase and distribution of locally produced food.”
On the creative industry, Hamzat said Lagos would strengthen training in contract negotiation and intellectual property to enable artists and other creative professionals to earn better returns from their work.
On Justice, inclusion and social welfare,
 the APC governorship candidate said the state was working with the judiciary to increase the civil jurisdiction of magistrates courts from N10 million to N15 million to reduce the backlog of cases in the High Courts.
He said the government also wanted landlord-tenant disputes resolved within three months, adding that more courts would be established to improve access to justice.
He disclosed that about 198 people had been prosecuted for domestic violence, stressing the need to strengthen support for survivors and encourage more victims to seek justice.
On inclusion, Hamzat said women-led enterprises performed well among small businesses, adding that the government planned to allocate five per cent of its business support to women-led enterprises.
He also promised to certify artisans and other skilled workers in their preferred languages and establish an online platform where customers could assess their services through reviews.
He said the government would pay 40 per cent of the stipends of trainees placed in companies under its vocational and technical training programmes to encourage businesses to employ them.
Hamzat added that the state would strengthen child protection by ensuring that children below 18 years were either in school or acquiring vocational skills.
On security, he said Lagos had about 6,800 personnel in its safety agency and was recruiting an additional 2,500, adding that the personnel could form a foundation for state policing if the necessary constitutional approval was secured.
He said the state had increased insurance benefits for police officers who died in service to N4 million for junior officers and N10 million for senior officers, stressing the need to improve support for their families.
Hamzat also called for stronger climate adaptation measures, including improved drainage, community protection and early-warning systems to prepare residents for extreme rainfall and flooding.
On housing, the deputy governor said the state would collaborate with private developers to increase the supply of affordable homes, noting that the average period for an African to build a house was about 17 years.
According to him, we will explore housing and mortgage arrangements that enabled young people and low-income earners to secure decent accommodation without sacrificing other basic needs.
Hamzat said the commitments would be assessed against measurable targets to ensure accountability, adding that government, businesses and residents must work together to achieve a more inclusive and prosperous Lagos.
Earlier, the LCCI President, Mr Leye Kupoluyi, stated that the engagement provided an opportunity for the business community to assess the economic policies and development priorities of prospective political leaders.
He said: “it gives us direct impact of government policies on investment, operating costs and business growth.”
Kupoluyi identified five key priority areas for the next administration, which included reducing the cost of doing business, improving infrastructure and mobility, reforming the tax and regulatory framework, promoting economic growth and investment, and empowering small and medium-scale enterprises (SMEs).
He said addressing high energy and logistics costs, traffic congestion, freight bottlenecks and regulatory challenges would improve productivity and create a more conducive business environment.
The LCCI president also called for improved access to capital, technology and markets for SMEs, emphasising the need for stronger collaboration between government and the private sector to unlock Lagos State economic potential.
He reaffirmed the Chamber’s commitment to constructive, evidence-based engagement with political leaders and future administrations.
The LCCI Deputy President, Mr Knit Ulvmoen, emphasised the need to strengthen local manufacturing and reduce Nigeria’s dependence on imported finished goods.
He noted that the country had the people, market and raw materials required to produce more goods locally.
He cited the transformation of Nigeria’s cement industry from heavy reliance on imports to local production and exports as evidence of the benefits of adding value to domestic resources.
Ulvmoen called for greater investment in sectors such as agriculture, pharmaceuticals, textiles, petrochemicals and renewable energy, while stressing that education and skills development are essential to preparing Nigerians for industrial growth and economic self-sufficiency.
In his goodwill message, the Managing Director of Sterling Bank, Mr Abubakar Suleiman, identified Lagos State real estate sector as a major untapped source of capital.
Suleiman urged the government to make land assets more accessible to investors through funding.
He added that Lagos possessed a unique economic advantage as a financial hub, with substantial lending and investment activities already concentrated in the state.
According to him, unlocking real estate value can significantly expand development funding.
“If the government can do this, I am confident that the initiative could attract more domestic investment, boost development and strengthen Lagos ambition to become a leading global financial centre,” he said.
The post 2027: Hamzat unveils policy agenda, promises reforms in transport, housing, security appeared first on Vanguard News.
