items.author: Muhammad Bilal
items.content:
The Ministry of Information Technology and Telecommunication has identified limited training facilities, poor connectivity, a shortage of qualified instructors and low awareness as major barriers to expanding artificial intelligence (AI) training in rural and underserved areas of Pakistan.
According to a ministry document, the government plans to improve access to advanced technology education through regional training hubs, online and hybrid learning programs, partnerships with universities and industry, and targeted scholarships for women and disadvantaged groups.
Under the AI Policy 2025, the government aims to train one million new and existing IT graduates in IT and related technologies over the next five years. The policy also targets training 10,000 instructors in emerging technologies by 2027.
Existing initiatives include DigiSkills, Code4AI, the National Artificial Intelligence Initiative and the AI SEEKHO Program, which aims to train more than 100,000 people in artificial intelligence and natural language-based application development.

More than 900,000 training sessions were delivered through various DigiSkills courses during fiscal year 2025-26.

The Directorate General of Customs Valuation has issued and revised valuation rulings for various products, including yarn and fabrics, in consultation with industry associations and other stakeholders. items.author: Anne Florentyna
items.content:
Everstone Capital-backed EV startup GreenCell Mobility has raised ₹330 Cr ($34.6 Mn) in an equity funding round led by Impact Fund Denmark to support the rollout of about 4,500 electric buses currently under deployment.
The Mumbai-based startup is eyeing expanding its fleet to more than 5,000 e-buses across 105 cities across India.
“Our focus is on executing our order book with rigour, strengthening service delivery and ensuring that the organisation keeps pace with the size and complexity of our operations. This equity investment gives us greater headroom to accelerate our plans while maintaining the standards of reliability, efficiency and customer experience that are fundamental to our business,” GreenCell Mobility managing director and chief executive Devndra Chawla said.
Founded in 2019, GreenCell Mobility focuses on deploying and operating electric buses for public transportation. It acquires electric buses via contract manufacturing arrangements with vendors and then deploys them for both intercity and intracity travel.
Backed by Eversource Capital, a joint venture between Everstone Capital and Lightsource, GreenCell primarily operates under the brand NueGo.
It claims to operate more than 1,200 electric buses in India, including 900 on intra-city routes, 300 under its NueGo brand for inter-city travel, and 50 for MSRTC. The startup also runs over 270 charging stations to support its fleet.
The startup previously raised $37 Mn from World Bank’s International Finance Corporation and also counts Eversource Capital, British International Investment and Tata Capital among its backers.
India’s electric bus segment has so far drawn strong interest from development finance institutions and lenders backing vehicle deployments under long-term public transport contracts. GreenCell’s latest round suggested that investors are also beginning to back the operating platform layer in the category, not just asset financing.
The investment highlights the role of institutional capital in expanding electric public transportation infrastructure in India. Large-scale electric bus deployments require funding not only for vehicles but also for the operational capabilities and charging infrastructure needed to support them.
Earlier in March, electric bus manufacturer PMI Electro Mobility, along with its electric bus platform Allfleet, has signed a definitive agreement with private equity giant KKR for an investment commitment of up to $310 Mn, to help scale the electric bus platform and focus on expanding its presence across India. PMI subsequently filed for an IPO via the confidential route last month.

items.author: Anjali Jain
items.content:
Home services company Urban Company is considering a fresh fundraise a little over a year after its stock market debut in September 2025, amid continued spending on its instant household services vertical InstaHelp.
The company’s board will meet on Friday (October 16) to consider raising funds through equity shares or securities convertible into equity shares, in one or more tranches, it said in an exchange filing.
The routes under consideration include a preferential allotment, private placement, QIP, or another legally permissible mode, or a combination of these.
Urban Company is also scheduled to release its Q2 FY27 numbers on the same day.
The fundraise proposal comes as the company continues to invest in InstaHelp amid intensifying competition from Snabbit and Pronto. The vertical’s expansion weighed on Urban Company’s profitability in FY26 and remained a drag in Q1 FY27.
InstaHelp Weighs On Profitability
Urban Company reported a consolidated net loss of ₹235 Cr in FY26, compared with a net profit of ₹240 Cr in FY25, while operating revenue grew 34% YoY to ₹1,692 Cr.
In Q1 FY27, operating revenue rose 44% YoY to ₹528 Cr, while its consolidated adjusted EBITDA loss narrowed to ₹65 Cr from ₹98 Cr in the preceding quarter. Excluding InstaHelp, the company reported an adjusted EBITDA profit of ₹67 Cr.
InstaHelp’s revenue grew 26% QoQ to about ₹11 Cr, while its adjusted EBITDA loss widened to ₹132 Cr from ₹119 Cr in Q4 FY26. However, its adjusted EBITDA loss per order narrowed to ₹346 from ₹447 over the same period.
Management has said spending on InstaHelp will remain elevated as the company seeks to strengthen its position in the category. During the Q1 FY27 earnings call, cofounder and CEO Abhiraj Singh Bhal said the vertical would continue to require investment for at least the next two years.
He also said InstaHelp was likely to remain a low-margin business compared with Urban Company’s core India consumer services operations. Management does not expect to make money from the vertical over the next five years and is working on the assumption that it will break even by FY31.
The proposed fundraise also comes while Urban Company retains a sizeable cash balance. It reported cash and treasury investments of ₹2,019 Cr as of June 30.
Separately, ₹310.83 Cr of the ₹472 Cr raised through its IPO’s fresh issue remained unutilised at the end of Q1 FY27. The proceeds were allocated towards technology and cloud infrastructure, office lease payments, marketing, general corporate purposes, and issue expenses.
Post-IPO Fundraising Gathers Pace
Urban Company’s proposed fundraise comes at a time when publicly listed new-age tech companies are increasingly tapping equity fundraise opportunities, especially QIPs, to fund further growth soon after their IPOs.
QIPs allow listed companies to offer equity shares or convertible securities directly to institutional investors like mutual funds, banks, and insurance companies.
For instance, Kissht parent OnEMI Technology Solutions received shareholder approval to raise up to ₹832 Cr through a preferential issue, around four months after raising approximately ₹926 Cr through its IPO.
Meanwhile, Swiggy raised ₹10,000 Cr through a QIP in December 2025, around a year after its stock market debut. Ola Electric raised ₹780 Cr through a QIP in June 2026, while Ather Energy raised ₹1,300 Cr through a QIP roughly 14 months after its IPO.
Zaggle, RateGain, Nazara have also tapped institutional investors through QIPs. Travel tech company ixigo raised around $146 Mn through a preferential issue roughly 16 months after its listing.
Ola Electric is now raising a further ₹1,000 Cr via rights issue that is set to open on October 22 for and close on October 30 at an issue price of ₹27 per share.

items.author: Pierre Boutin
items.content:
Le conseil d’administration de la GSMA a détaillé les priorités du secteur en matière de connectivité, appelant à agir en faveur de l’accessibilité financière des smartphones, contre les arnaques en ligne et pour l’investissement dans les réseaux, tout en soutenant un renforcement de la coopération internationale sur les futures normes 6G.
À l’issue d’une réunion du conseil à New Delhi, la GSMA a rappelé que, si 97 % de la population mondiale vit dans une zone couverte par le haut débit mobile, 3,4 milliards de personnes restent privées d’internet mobile. Le coût des appareils reste un frein important : un terminal d’entrée de gamme connecté à internet équivaut à 44 % du revenu mensuel moyen des 20 % les plus pauvres dans les pays à revenu faible ou intermédiaire.
La GSMA met en avant des mesures possibles pour améliorer l’accessibilité financière, comme des dispositifs de financement, des baisses d’impôts ciblées et une coopération renforcée entre fabricants d’appareils et fournisseurs de mémoire.
L’association s’inquiète par ailleurs du danger croissant lié aux fraudes et aux escroqueries, avertissant que, si le secteur mobile continue de renforcer ses outils de détection réseau et de cyberdéfense, « aucun secteur ne peut combattre seul cette menace ». La GSMA relève que les contenus générés par l’IA et les deepfakes aggravent encore les risques pour les consommateurs, la confiance du public et les objectifs des gouvernements, et appelle le secteur à « unir ses forces pour contrer les arnaques par des solutions concrètes ».
Investissement soutenu
La GSMA souligne également la nécessité d’investir dans les réseaux et de mener des politiques favorables pour accélérer la croissance de la connectivité. Elle estime que les technologies et services mobiles ont généré 6 000 milliards de dollars (5 376 milliards d’euros) de valeur économique en 2025, soit 6,4 % du PIB mondial, un chiffre qui devrait atteindre 11 300 milliards de dollars (10 125 milliards d’euros) d’ici 2030.
Par ailleurs, les opérateurs devraient investir 1 200 milliards de dollars (1 075 milliards d’euros) en capex entre 2025 et 2030 pour étendre et moderniser leurs réseaux, et 57 % des connexions mobiles devraient utiliser la 5G d’ici la fin de la décennie.
Pour Vivek Badrinath, directeur général de la GSMA, la prochaine priorité du secteur doit être de transformer l’expansion de la 5G en « valeur significative », afin qu’un plus grand nombre de personnes puissent participer à l’économie numérique. « Cela exigera des investissements soutenus, des politiques favorables et une collaboration à travers l’ensemble de l’écosystème », a-t-il insisté.
L’association sectorielle a réaffirmé en outre son soutien à des normes mondiales et à un spectre harmonisé à mesure que le développement de la 6G se poursuit. Elle a souligné que des pays représentant plus de 80 % de la population mondiale soutiennent l’usage mobile de la bande 6 GHz supérieure, qui pourrait offrir les largeurs de canal de 200 à 400 MHz jugées nécessaires pour la 6G.
Le président de la GSMA, Gopal Vittal, estime quant à lui qu’« en travaillant à travers des normes mondiales et en collaborant d’un marché à l’autre, nous pouvons accélérer l’innovation, renforcer la confiance et la résilience » à mesure que le secteur développe la prochaine génération de connectivité.
The post La GSMA se focalise sur la 6G, les menaces de l’IA et l’inclusion numérique appeared first on Mobile World Live.

items.author: Web Desk
items.content:
The federal government on Tuesday decreased the price of petrol and high-speed diesel (HSD) by Rs2.71 and 3 paisas per litre, respectively, for October 14.
According to a notification issued by the Petroleum Division, the price of petrol was fixed at Rs392.66 per litre, while HSD would cost Rs396.82 per litre for Wednesday.
The latest revision comes a day after the government decreased the price of petrol by Rs2.93 per litre, while increasing the price of HSD by 61 paisas per litre for October 13.
Read: Govt cuts petrol by Rs2.93, increases diesel by 61 paisas for Oct 13
On July 17, the government announced a new pricing mechanism under which petroleum product prices would be reviewed and notified daily, replacing the weekly pricing mechanism, as renewed tensions between the United States and Iran continued to drive volatility in global oil markets and raise concerns over fuel supplies.
On September 13, PM Shehbaz announced a special relief scheme offering Rs100 per litre off petrol for motorcycles, three-wheeler rickshaws and cars with engines up to 800cc, in an attempt to shield lower-income consumers from the impact of rising petroleum prices.
Under the proposal, an estimated 11.8 million beneficiaries would be covered. Around 10 million two-wheeler users and 800,000 three-wheeler users would be entitled to relief on 20 litres of fuel per month, translating into a maximum monthly benefit of Rs2,000 per beneficiary.
Another one million users of cars up to 800cc would receive relief on 30 litres per month, providing them with a maximum benefit of Rs3,000 each.
On Sept 17, the government reintroduced austerity and fuel conservation measures amid rising fuel prices, tightening business operating hours and restricting public events.
Under the measures, notified with immediate effect, shops, markets, shopping malls, bazaars, departmental stores, grocery stores, general stores and kiryana shops would close by 9pm throughout the week, according to a notification issued by the Cabinet Division.
Marriage halls, marquees and other commercial venues hosting festive events would close by 10pm, while restaurants, cafes, eateries, food outlets and standalone fruit and vegetable shops would be allowed to operate until 11pm. Takeaway and home delivery services would remain exempt from the timing restrictions.
Global geopolitical developments continue to pose significant risks. International oil prices are influenced by decisions taken by OPEC+, conflicts in the Middle East, sanctions on oil-producing nations, and disruptions in critical shipping routes such as the Strait of Hormuz and the Red Sea. Any interruption in these supply chains can immediately increase crude oil prices and freight costs. Since Pakistan imports the majority of its petroleum requirements, these developments quickly translate into higher domestic fuel prices.
Oil prices ​were mixed on Tuesday as hopes that the US-Russia diesel deal could free up more supplies from Moscow offset attacks in Saudi Arabia ‌and Yemen that could result in additional supply disruptions.
Brent futures were down 59 cents, or 0.6%, at $106.06 per barrel at 12:59 pm EDT (1659 GMT), while US West Texas Intermediate crude futures rose 73 cents, or 0.8%, to $94.47.
Diesel prices rose to record highs in many parts of the world in recent ‌weeks due ⁠to global supply disruptions linked to Ukraine's attacks on Russian energy infrastructure and Iran's attacks on Middle East energy infrastructure.

items.author: APP
items.content:
Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif on Tuesday said the government had been left with "no option" but to impose an emergency and governor’s rule in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa amid the deteriorating security situation in the province, saying “Pakistan comes first” and nothing was more important than the country’s progress and survival.
The federal government imposed an emergency and governor’s rule in K-P on Sunday under Articles 232 and 234 of the Constitution. The government cited the deteriorating law and order situation and what it called a lack of support from the provincial administration in the fight against terrorism.
Addressing the PML-N’s parliamentary party meeting, the prime minister praised the “brave people” of K-P for their sacrifices in the fight against terrorism, saying the menace had been eradicated from the province by 2017 but resurfaced after the PTI came to power.
“After that, terrorists had started returning to Swat. They were given a free hand and brought back,” he said.
" میں آپ سب کا دل کی اتھاہ گہرائیوں سے شکر گزار ہوں کہ آپ میری درخواست پر یہاں تشریف لائے۔
یہ ایک ایسا موقع ہے جب پاکستان کے صوبہ خیبر پختونخوا میں گزشتہ چند ماہ سے صورتِ حال انتہائی خراب، بلکہ دل خراش رہی ہے۔ یہ وہ صوبہ ہے جو پاکستان کے خوبصورت ترین صوبوں میں سے ایک ہے۔ وہاں کے… pic.twitter.com/ofQt3RAjqG
— Government of Pakistan (@GovtofPakistan) October 13, 2026
The prime minister stated that after the PTI formed the government in K-P in 2024, the federal government had made every effort over the past two and a half years to resolve issues through engagement.
The premier said meetings had been held with former chief minister Ali Amin Gandapur, who was assured of the federal government's full support in the fight against terrorism, further adding that meetings had also been held with non-functional chief minister Sohail Afridi.
"2024 میں پی ٹی آئی کی حکومت بنی تو ان اڑھائی سالوں میں ہم نے حتی المقدور کوشش کی۔ ان کے سابق وزیراعلیٰ علی امین گنڈاپور سے ہماری کئی ملاقاتیں ہوئیں اور ہم نے ہر طریقے سے انہیں یہ باور کرانے کی کوشش کی کہ ہم آپ کے ساتھ چلنے کے لیے تیار ہیں۔ ملک کی ترقی اور خوشحالی کا یہ سفر ہمارا… pic.twitter.com/Ro8wUChZVq
— Government of Pakistan (@GovtofPakistan) October 13, 2026
“Every day, our people, our armed forces and police personnel are being killed. There are daily sacrifices in Balochistan and Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa. If this brutality is not completely eliminated, the progress we have made over the past two and a half years will come to a halt,” he said.
PM Shehbaz said the government had made progress over the past two and a half years through a “unique partnership”. However, he added, if a provincial government was bent on dismantling that partnership, a political party was intent on destruction and stood in the way of the country's journey towards development, action would have to be taken.
Referring to his meeting with the International Monetary Fund (IMF) managing director in New York, the premier said the lender's chief had praised Pakistan's recent reforms, describing the country as “a new Pakistan”.
وزیراعظم محمد شہباز شریف نے مسلم لیگ (ن) کے پارلیمانی پارٹی کے اجلاس سے خطاب کرتے ہوئے کہا کہ نیویارک میں آئی ایم ایف کی مینیجنگ ڈائریکٹر اور لندن میں سٹی بینک، جے پی مورگن سمیت عالمی مالیاتی اداروں کے نمائندوں سے ملاقاتوں میں پاکستان میں گزشتہ ڈھائی سال کے دوران ہونے والی… pic.twitter.com/od7hpNFK8U
— Government of Pakistan (@GovtofPakistan) October 13, 2026
He said delegations from six leading banks had also appreciated the country's recent progress, although they had expressed reservations over incidents of terrorism in Pakistan.
The prime minister said that while terrorism was spreading and instability was being created, the PTI was devoting all its resources and time to political agitation, including long marches and sit-ins, instead of focusing on development and prosperity.
"یہ دھرنے اور لانگ مارچ، کون نہیں جانتا کہ گزشتہ سال اسلام آباد میں کیا ہوا؟ 2014 میں کئی مہینوں تک ڈی چوک خالی نہیں کیا گیا، وہاں گندے کپڑے دھوئے گئے اور قبریں کھودی گئیں۔ اسی دوران چینی صدر کا دورۂ پاکستان بھی مؤخر ہو گیا۔
جب کوئی ملک کی ترقی روکنے پر تُلا ہو اور دہشت گردی کے… pic.twitter.com/3GSad2inec
— Government of Pakistan (@GovtofPakistan) October 13, 2026
He added that the people of K-P had been waiting for development projects for 13 years, but the provincial government's time and resources had been consumed by long marches and sit-ins, further asking how any civilised society could tolerate this.
“What option did we have in these circumstances? Should we have sat back as silent spectators and, after everything had been destroyed, said that this was our fate? No, this is not our fate. God willing, we have to build Pakistan,” the PM said.
Read: Emergency, governor's rule imposed in K-P after president signs summary on PM Shehbaz's advice
The prime minister said that after the dialogue process collapsed, the government decided, following deliberations and consultations, to impose an emergency in the province.
Referring to the negotiations, PM Shehbaz said the final draft had been almost ready for signing after all the demands had been met. However, at the last moment, the other side said it wanted to consult the K-P chief minister, he added, adding that “the rest is history”.
وزیراعظم محمد شہباز شریف نے مسلم لیگ (ن) کے پارلیمانی پارٹی کے اجلاس سے خطاب کرتے ہوئے کہا کہ پیپلز پارٹی اور مسلم لیگ (ن) کے نمائندوں کی شرکت سے دن رات مذاکرات جاری رہے اور معاہدے کا متفقہ مسودہ بھی تیار ہو گیا، تاہم آخری مرحلے میں مذاکرات ناکام ہو گئے۔
بعد ازاں مولانا فضل… pic.twitter.com/slo3ivqyoS
— Government of Pakistan (@GovtofPakistan) October 13, 2026
The prime minister said that after a two-and-a-half-hour cabinet meeting attended by representatives of all coalition partners, the government decided to impose an emergency and governor's rule in K-P.
“We decided that this is the moment when we must stop waiting any longer to save Pakistan, otherwise, everything will burn, and we will be left wringing our hands,” he said.
Read More: 'Govt can't keep sleeping when it comes to citizens' security': DPM Dar on K-P emergency, governor's rule
The premier said the government had been compelled to decide to impose an emergency because “Pakistan comes first”, adding that nothing was more important than the country's progress and survival.
The prime minister further stated that an emergency and governor's rule had now been imposed in K-P and an advisory council comprising experts and professionals had been formed. The council included doctors, educationists and financial experts, he added.
وزیراعظم محمد شہباز شریف نے مسلم لیگ (ن) کے پارلیمانی پارٹی کے اجلاس سے خطاب کرتے ہوئے کہا کہ خیبرپختونخوا میں ایک ایڈوائزری کونسل قائم کی گئی ہے جس میں ماہرین، پیشہ ور افراد، ڈاکٹرز، ماہرین تعلیم اور مالیاتی امور کے ماہرین شامل ہیں۔ حکومت کی کوشش ہے کہ صوبے میں بنیادی سہولیات کی… pic.twitter.com/TmMMoOIydn
— Government of Pakistan (@GovtofPakistan) October 13, 2026
He noted that the people of K-P were proud and hospitable and the decision had been taken solely to restore their happiness, development and dignity.
PM's meeting with parliamentary delegations
Earlier, the prime minister took delegations of Pakistan Muslim League (Q), Balochistan Awami Party (BAP), Istehkam-e-Pakistan Party (IPP) and Pakistan Muslim League (PML-Zia) into confidence over the government’s decision to impose emergency and governors' rule in K-P during a meeting at the prime minister’s office.

PM Shehbaz explained the reasons behind the federal government’s decisions, stating that the conduct of the PTI government in the province and its failure to adopt an unequivocal stance against terrorism had posed risks to Pakistan’s growing economy.
The premier noted that the provincial government had neither clearly condemned terrorism nor taken effective action against terrorist groups. Referring to the sacrifices of security personnel, he said numerous members of the Pakistan armed forces, security forces and police had laid down their lives over the past several years while defending the country.
PM Shehbaz said the federal government had provided more than Rs800 billion to K-P under the National Finance Commission (NFC) arrangements to support efforts against terrorism.
However, he said the provincial government had failed to take effective measures to strengthen the capacity of its Counter Terrorism Department (CTD) and establish Safe City projects to improve its counterterrorism capabilities.
During the meeting with a parliamentary delegation, the premier said an impartial technocratic advisory council had been established to assist the governor in improving law and order, strengthening the economy and eliminating terrorism in the province.
The parliamentary delegation expressed its support for the federal government amid the prevailing situation and appreciated the prime minister’s leadership during what it described as difficult circumstances.
The delegation also said the people of K-P had remained deprived of adequate development in health, education and infrastructure during the PTI’s tenure in the province.
It expressed confidence that, with the federal government’s cooperation, development and prosperity in K-P would advance in line with other parts of the country.
MQM-P backs govt decisions on K-P
Separately, the Muttahida Qaumi Movement-Pakistan (MQM-P) assured Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif of its full cooperation with the government’s decisions regarding K-P.
The assurance was given during a meeting between the prime minister and an MQM-P delegation led by party convener and Federal Education Minister Dr Khalid Maqbool Siddiqui.
The delegation included Federal Health Minister Syed Mustafa Kamal, Senator Aamir Waliuddin Chishti, Senator Khalida Ateeb and several members of the National Assembly.

During the meeting, the two sides exchanged views on the country’s overall political situation, while the prime minister took the delegation into confidence regarding the situation in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa.
PM Shehbaz described the decision to impose emergency and governor’s rule in the province as a difficult one, taken in the best interest of its people. He said the government had made every effort to avoid the step and had engaged in negotiations in good faith, but had not received a positive response from the other side.
He said terrorist attacks in K-P were increasing, targeting civilians and security personnel, while the provincial government had failed to openly raise its voice against terrorist groups.

items.content:
AI video startup Clueso has raised $10 Mn (about ₹95 Cr) in a Series A funding round led by Dharana Capital.
The round also saw participation from new investors Founders Future and Neotribe Ventures, alongside existing backers Y Combinator and F7 Ventures.
With the latest round, Clueso has raised a total funding of about $12 Mn to date. The startup last raised $1.4 Mn in a seed funding round led by F7 Ventures.
Clueso plans to deploy the fresh capital towards expanding its enterprise sales and marketing operations and developing the AI agents powering its platform. It will also improve its video editing capabilities and deepen integrations with systems that store product and company information.
Automating Enterprise Video Production
Founded in 2023 by IIT Madras batchmates Akash Anand, Prajwal Prakash, and Neel Balar, Clueso helps businesses create and update videos using AI agents.
The startup says its platform identifies gaps in existing video content, captures software workflows, and generates videos with scripts, voiceovers, animations, and captions. Users can edit these videos through a browser-based editor and refresh them when products, processes, or brand guidelines change.
To support this, Clueso integrates with business tools to access company information and keep video content consistent. Its Model Context Protocol (MCP) integration also enables AI assistants such as Claude and ChatGPT to create, edit, and manage videos on the platform.
“We position ourselves as a dedicated end-to-end platform for enterprises and not a single prompt-to-video tool that consumers or creators use,” Anand told Inc42.
Clueso charges a subscription fee based on the volume of videos created and updated, the number of teams using the platform, and the products covered.
The startup claims to have over 1,000 paying customers globally, including Atlassian, GitLab, Zendesk, Gainsight, Global Partners, Seismic, and Ironclad. Its Indian customers include PhonePe, Zoho, and MoEngage.
According to Clueso, about 65% of its customers are based in the US, 20% in Europe, and around 10-15% in India.
More than 70% of the videos created on the platform are customer-facing, including product launch videos and educational content. Other uses include employee training, onboarding, and compliance.
Headquartered in San Francisco, Clueso has a 39-member team, including around 35 employees in India, with a significant presence in Bengaluru.
Over the next 12-18 months, the startup plans to expand its enterprise integrations and customer base while automating more of the video production process. It also aims to track viewer engagement and use that data to improve video content.
Anand said the long-term goal is to turn video into “a living system rather than a one-time asset you produce and forget about”.

items.author: Debarghya Sil
items.content:
Do you remember the first smartphone you bought around 2012? Chances are, you spent more time choosing the phone than thinking about its case. Phone cases were largely an afterthought, sold by local stores and small sellers in an unorganised market dominated by inexpensive, China-sourced products and copies of established brands.
That began to change as smartphone adoption accelerated. Indians were increasingly willing to spend ₹20,000, ₹30,000, ₹40,000 and even ₹50,000 on their phones.
As these phones became more central to everyday life, consumers began looking beyond basic protection, even demanding accessories that reflected their personal style — an opportunity DailyObjects tapped into early on.
Founded by Pankaj Garg, in 2012, as a multi-category online business, the company narrowed its focus to smartphone cases in 2014. Over time, it expanded into bags, charging products and workspace accessories, building its brand around design and quality.
Today, DailyObjects revenue crossed ₹200 Cr in FY26, nearly doubling year-on-year. It is targeting ₹400 Cr in FY27 while working towards EBITDA profitability.
But the more interesting part of DailyObjects’ story is not just how quickly it is growing today. It is how long it took to build a brand in a category that many consumers once barely thought about.
Making Phone Cases More Than A Commodity
DailyObjects had started as a multi-category online business, but by 2014, it decided to focus on smartphone cases. Rather than spread its resources across different product lines, the startup chose to focus on one category, differentiate through design and quality, and build a customer base willing to pay a premium.
The category offered an opportunity to build a design-led brand in a market crowded with inexpensive, unbranded products. Consumers could walk into almost any mobile shop and find a case, while copies of products from established international brands were also widely available. DailyObjects’ answer was to make the product itself more distinctive.
The startup began offering designer cases and collaborating with artists, bringing design into a category largely treated as a commodity. But differentiation was not limited to aesthetics. DailyObjects also wanted its products to compete with global brands on quality and materials.
But building a better product was only half the battle. DailyObjects also had to decide how it wanted to grow.
The startup had begun as a multi-category business, but it chose to drop car accessories and other retail products to concentrate on smartphone cases, which it saw as a larger and faster-growing opportunity. The idea was to build depth in one category before expanding into others.
The same thinking shaped its distribution strategy. DailyObjects could have leaned on marketplaces to reach a wider audience and chase volumes. Instead, it largely stuck to its own channels, believing marketplaces could help sell a product but could not build a brand for it, even though it was a slower, more demanding route.
The startup had to generate its own traffic, establish a distinct design identity and convince consumers to pay more for products they could find at a fraction of the price elsewhere.
During this period, the startup raised ₹9 Cr from Ronnie Screwvala’s Unilazer Ventures. But according to Garg, the business had an important advantage: it had been profitable from its early stages. That gave it the room to grow without relying heavily on deep discounts or chasing marketplace volumes simply to keep the business running.
DailyObjects stayed focused on phone cases for nearly five years before entering another major category. Its approach was to establish a foothold in one category, build distribution around it and then move to the next.
By resisting the rush to scale through marketplaces, DailyObjects had more time to build a direct relationship with its customers. That strategy continues to define the business today, with nearly 70% of its sales coming through its own channels.
DailyObjects’ Playbook: Making Everyday Products Desirable
There was a logic to what DailyObjects added next. The startup was not looking to build a sprawling catalogue of accessories. It wanted to find products that appealed to the same customer it had won over with phone cases. The idea took DailyObjects into bags in FY21, opening up a much bigger opportunity than phone cases. However, it also brought a new challenge: manufacturers were unwilling to take on its small orders. Therefore, DailyObjects decided to make bags itself. The operation began with just two tables and eventually grew into its own factory.
Today, bags account for around 40-45% of the company’s revenue. They are manufactured entirely in India at its own facility, which employs around 600 people. DailyObjects’ average order value is now around ₹26,000 and has been rising about 10% every year. The startup attributes the increase to products such as bags, power banks, and premium phone cases.
Two years later, in FY23, DailyObjects entered into charging products. It was during this time that the startup bagged $10 Mn from 360 One Asset for product innovation and expanding its manufacturing capabilities.
Its charging and STAC categories have grown nearly threefold since. The latest example is NODE, a modular wireless charging system around consumers carrying several devices between home, work and travel.
The startup currently has around 50 core SKUs, excluding colour and size variants. Its revenue has grown from ₹ 24.1 Cr in FY21 to ₹39.2 Cr in FY22, to ₹84.4 Cr in FY24 and ₹110 Cr in FY25 . Garg said that the startup closed FY26 at over ₹200 Cr. While the founder didn’t divulge bottomline details for FY26, DailyObjects posted a loss of ₹16 Cr in FY25. The startup is yet to file its FY26 audited financials with the Ministry of Corporate Affairs.
The Next Challenge: Taking The Brand Beyond Metros
DailyObjects spent years building its own traffic and customer base, a slower process that gave it greater control over how its products were presented and how they were priced. The payoff is beginning to show in its customer metrics.
The company says its lifetime repeat purchase rate stands at around 45%. Its average order value has also risen by roughly 10% YoY to about ₹2,600, suggesting that customers are increasingly spending across its wider product range. Its customer base has also moved beyond the metros.
Around 35–40% of DailyObjects’ sales now come from Tier III and IV cities, while another 20–25% comes from Tier II markets. The shift points to a broader opportunity: consumers in smaller cities are increasingly willing to spend on products that combine design with everyday utility.
DailyObjects is now expanding its reach into cities such as Vizag, Patna, Ludhiana, Indore, Lucknow and Surat. But reaching more customers is only one part of the next phase. The other is making that growth more profitable.
DailyObjects is currently operating close to break-even and remains on track to achieve EBITDA profitability in FY27. It expects operating margins, currently around 5%, to expand to 15-20% over the next four to five years.
The improvement is expected to come from a combination of factors, including a higher-value product mix, a larger contribution from offline retail and greater supply-chain efficiencies.
Recently, D2C lifestyle startup DailyObjects has raised ₹332 Cr ($34.3 Mn) in a Series C funding round co-led by Xponentia Capital Partners, Anicut Capital and Axiom Asia Private Capital. The funds will allow DailyObjects to scale its offline network, deepen its product and R&D capabilities, strengthen brand building and evaluate opportunities in international markets.
DailyObjects’ Offline Push Comes With A Bigger Test
For years, DailyObjects’ biggest asset was something consumers could not touch: the brand itself. Now, it is bringing that proposition into physical stores.
The startup currently operates 13 exclusive brand outlets. It is opening two to three stores a month and plans to add 30-35 stores in FY27. Over the next five years, it aims to build a network of 150-160 stores. It is also present at 300 Apple premium reseller outlets.
For DailyObjects, this is more than a conventional D2C brand moving offline. It is a chance to put the products at the centre of the buying experience. Consumers may discover them online, but a physical store lets them feel the materials, examine the finish and understand how a product works before paying a premium for it.
According to the founder, all stores become profitable from the first month of operations. Its airport stores, in particular, are generating margins of close to 15% from the first month.
Rather than limiting itself to India’s largest cities, DailyObjects is using physical retail to reach markets where it already sees significant online demand. It is also beginning to explore international markets. The startup is researching the US, where it already receives around 1,000 orders a month without dedicated marketing.
But as the business grows, so will the challenge. With DailyObjects targeting ₹400 Cr in revenue in FY27, can it scale its offline and international presence while building a profitable business without losing what made its brand distinctive?
Edited By Shishir Parasher
Creatives: Abhyam Gusai

items.author: Team Inc42
items.content:
India’s quick commerce story is no longer about convenience. What started as a channel for forgotten groceries and last-minute essentials is now reshaping how Indians shop, consume and expect to receive products.
With India’s quick commerce market projected to become a $40 Bn opportunity by 2030 and platform GMV expected to cross $68 Bn by 2031, instant delivery is evolving from being an optional consumer convenience into a core retail channel.
The scale of this transformation is already visible. Blinkit reported a GOV of ₹13,300 Cr in Q3 FY26, while Swiggy Instamart clocked ₹7,938 Cr during the same period. Together with Zepto, these platforms now operate more than 4,300 dark stores across the country, fundamentally changing how products are discovered, purchased and consumed.
For consumer brands, this momentum has far-reaching implications.
Categories such as beauty, personal care, packaged foods, beverages, baby care, wellness and household essentials are witnessing growing demand through high-intent purchases completed within minutes. At the same time, a new generation of D2C brands is using quick commerce for more than distribution. They use it to acquire customers, test demand, and drive growth.
Meanwhile, as consumer behaviour shifts, brands must rethink how they operate. Brands are redesigning product portfolios around immediacy. Packaging formats are evolving for smaller baskets and impulse purchases. Demand forecasting, inventory allocation and replenishment cycles are becoming significantly more dynamic as businesses adapt to an always-on consumption environment.
Yet, success in the channel requires much more — a series of decisions around assortment, pricing, inventory, fulfilment, visibility and platform strategy.
Against this backdrop, Inc42, in collaboration with Nitro Commerce, is launching “The Quick Commerce Code” — a five-part series that explores how consumer brands are building, adapting, and scaling within India’s rapidly expanding 10-minute economy.
Through conversations with founders and operators, the series will look beyond headline growth metrics to understand what works on the ground. From customer acquisition and assortment strategy to operational execution and profitability, the series will examine the playbooks shaping the next phase of consumer commerce in India.
Here’s What To Expect
The Quick Commerce Code series will spotlight a diverse set of consumer brands navigating India’s rapidly evolving instant commerce ecosystem. From customer acquisition and category creation to inventory management and profitability, each brand offers a different lens into what it takes to win in the 10-minute economy.
“With The Quick Commerce Code series, we want to decode how the next generation of D2C and FMCG founders are building businesses around real-time intelligence, rather than fragmented data. The winners will be those who can connect inventory, margins and platform dynamics into a single decision layer and act on it quickly,” said Umair Mohammed, founder and CEO of Nitro Commerce.
The series will be packed with crucial insights from Zodiac, an autonomous AI copilot designed to help D2C and FMCG brands manage and scale their business across quick commerce platforms, giving visibility into inventory, sales, competitor pricing, share of shelf and ad performance. Notably, Nitro Commerce acquired Zodiac in March this year.
Here’s a sneak peek at some of the brand stories coming up in the series:
How Fix My Curls Is Turning Quick Commerce Into A Discovery Engine
For Fix My Curls, quick commerce has evolved from a fulfilment channel into a powerful customer acquisition and discovery engine. The brand uses affordable SKUs to drive product trials, unlock demand from new consumer cohorts and adapt its portfolio for impulse-led purchases.
The article will decode how Fix My Curls is using quick commerce to expand beyond its core audience and build a stronger top-of-funnel engine.
PeeSafe: How To Build Demand In An Emerging Category
PeeSafe’s quick commerce journey highlights how instant delivery can become a powerful lever for category creation. The company has used the channel not only to improve accessibility but also to drive awareness, encourage repeat purchases and expand demand across its portfolio.
In an interview with the cofounder of PeeSafe, Rithish Kumar, we will break down how the brand is navigating evolving consumer behaviour while building one of India’s leading women’s wellness brands.
Gramiyaa’s Game Plan For Quick Commerce’s Toughest Arena
Operating in the highly competitive food and staples segment, Gramiyaa offers an insider look at the realities of building a quick-commerce-led business. The company has focused on a concentrated SKU portfolio, prioritised stock availability, and navigated the operational complexities of scaling in quick commerce.
In this article, we will talk about the economics, inventory challenges and execution playbook behind Gramiyaa’s growth journey.
Decoding The New Rules Of Consumer Commerce
The Quick Commerce Code documents how consumer brands are adapting to the biggest shifts underway in India’s commerce ecosystem.
Curated for founders, operators and investors, the series goes beyond traditional growth narratives to uncover decisions that have the potential to directly impact brands’ growth metrics.
On this, Mohammed of Nitro Commerce urged brands to move beyond chasing GMV or simply spending more on ads in their quick commerce endeavour.
“They need to maintain high fill rates, connect ad spending to real-time inventory, automate routine decisions and optimise for contribution margin. The brands that get this right can scale the channel profitably while continuing to build their own D2C channels and long-term customer relationships,” Mohammed added.
All in all, the highly anticipated series The Quick Commerce Code from Inc42 will tap into similar fundamentals (as Mohammed mentioned) to decode strategies, trade-offs, and operating playbooks for brands sparring in the 10-minute delivery war zone.
The post The Quick Commerce Code: Breaking Playbooks Of Brands Winning The 10-Min Delivery Game appeared first on Inc42 Media.

items.author: Usama Anjum
items.content:
Copyright protected content copied from PhoneWorld website.
Pakistan and the European Union are exploring cooperation in electric vehicle (EV) training and skills development as the country prepares to expand its electric mobility industry.
Advisor to the Prime Minister for Industries and Production Haroon Akhtar Khan discussed possible collaboration with an EU delegation during a meeting in Islamabad on October 13. The talks focused on technical training, workforce development, and building local capabilities to support the shift towards electric vehicles.
Khan said Pakistan aims to increase the share of electric vehicles to 30% by 2030, but meeting the target would require more than bringing new vehicles into the market. The country would also need trained technicians, engineers, local suppliers, and an industry capable of supporting new technologies.
With several companies entering Pakistan’s EV market, the advisor said demand for qualified professionals was growing. Developing these skills could create employment opportunities for young Pakistanis while strengthening domestic vehicle production and technology adoption.
New Auto Policy and Battery Storage Framework in the Works
The advisor said the government’s forthcoming Auto Policy, expected in the coming weeks, would give particular attention to electric vehicles and the broader automotive industry. Work is also underway on a Battery Energy Storage System (BESS) policy to support cleaner-energy technologies.
He argued that Pakistan could not afford to miss the opportunities presented by the global EV transition, having previously fallen behind during earlier shifts in the automotive industry.
Greater adoption of electric vehicles could help reduce Pakistan’s oil import bill and encourage local manufacturing, he said. However, achieving those benefits would depend on developing a skilled workforce, reliable supply chains, and domestic industrial capacity.
EDB to Identify Areas for Cooperation With EU
Khan directed the Engineering Development Board (EDB) to engage with the EU delegation and identify practical areas for cooperation in EV training, skills development, and capacity building.
Secretary of Industries and Production Ihsan Ali Mangi stressed the need for training programs that reflect the automotive industry’s changing requirements. He said coordination between government institutions, businesses, and international partners could help identify skills shortages and improve technical training standards.

items.content:
Copyright protected content copied from PhoneWorld website.
WhatsApp is working on a new sticker format that could make conversations more interactive by allowing users to send stickers with short audio clips attached.
The feature was identified by WABetaInfo in WhatsApp beta for Android version 2.26.41.3. It remains under development and is not yet available to beta testers, meaning regular users cannot try it for now.
Unlike the static and animated stickers currently supported by WhatsApp, the proposed sound stickers would combine a visual sticker with an audio track. A small audio icon on the sticker would signal that sound is available, and recipients could tap the sticker to hear it.
According to the report, both the sticker and the accompanying audio would be protected by WhatsApp’s end-to-end encryption.
Custom Sound Stickers and Playback Controls
WhatsApp is also developing tools that would let users create their own sound stickers instead of relying solely on ready-made sticker packs. The planned options include attaching audio to a sticker and potentially converting video content into an animated sticker with sound.
The feature is being designed to respect a phone’s audio settings. On devices set to silent mode, sound stickers would not produce audible playback. Users would also be able to mute sticker audio using a volume icon, with WhatsApp expected to remember that preference until it is changed.
The development comes as WhatsApp continues to adjust how users express themselves in chats. The messaging platform already offers static and animated stickers, but adding sound would introduce a new way to share short reactions and personalized content.
There is no confirmed release date for sound stickers. The feature is currently being developed for Android, and WhatsApp has not announced when beta testers or the wider public will receive it.

items.author: Reuters
items.content:
Swedish activist Greta Thunberg joined protesters outside a high school in a working-class ‌suburb of Paris on Tuesday as French pupils took to the streets for another day of demonstrations over poor learning conditions.
Now in its fourth week, the nationwide protest movement over teacher shortages, classroom overcrowding and crumbling school buildings has involved marches, blockades of hundreds of schools and, in some cases, clashes with police.
Pupils clustered outside several schools in Paris and other cities on Tuesday morning, ​brandishing placards and megaphones.
Read: France's high school students plan fresh protests
"We are inspired by the young people who are demanding their basic rights," Greta told reporters outside Lycee Paul Eluard in ​Saint-Denis, north of Paris, one of the schools where the protest movement first gained traction.
Climate and social justice activist Greta Thunberg joined students at a high school in the Paris suburb of Saint-Denis, as France faced a new day of nationwide marches and strikes on top of the blockades at schools. pic.twitter.com/gC3Zx4x3Cn
— The Associated Press (@AP) October 13, 2026
"Whether it's not funding schools enough, or ⁠the climate crisis, or social injustice crises ... it's about time that young people are stepping up and reclaiming that future," she said.
Mostly peaceful protests, with outbreaks of ​violence
Large crowds marched peacefully through Nantes in the west, Strasbourg in the east and Marseille in the south, holding hand-made signs with slogans such as "Tear gas doesn't make ​us cry as much as the state of the national education system". Marchers were also mustering in Paris.
Footage from BFM TV showed clashes between people dressed in black and riot police in Strasbourg and Nantes, with clouds of tear gas in some streets.
In Lyon, the local authorities asked organisers to call off a march after a group of "hostile individuals" preceding the main procession ​vandalised shops and a petrol station and clashed with police.
While there was no immediate information on who was involved, it is not uncommon in France for street ​protests to attract so-called "casseurs", a fringe of rioters who seek to confront police and destroy property.
Read More: French policing under scrutiny as student protest injuries mount
The scene was calmer in front of Paris city hall, where a youth orchestra played Antonin ‌Dvorak's "New World ⁠Symphony". Some musicians had protest stickers on their cellos and violins.
The education ministry said 214 schools were closed, down from 800 on a similar protest day a week ago. It said 94.2% of high schools were open.
The cash-strapped government has promised to act to address the pupils' concerns, but has little room for manoeuvre at a time when concerns over the national debt and the budget deficit are pushing up borrowing costs to the highest level in years.
It has expressed sympathy with the students' grievances, but has ​deployed riot police to quell the protests, ​leading to confrontations in which hundreds ⁠of people have been injured and thousands arrested.
Political polarisation ahead of election
The government suspended the use of stun grenades last week after one teenager lost a hand.
Six months ahead of a presidential election, the protest movement and the police response have elicited polarised ​responses from leading contenders to replace Emmanuel Macron.
"The police are losing their breath running after young people to beat ​them up and injure ⁠them," said hard-left candidate Jean-Luc Melenchon, who has a chance of making the runoff according to opinion polls, in a post on X on Tuesday.
La hargne médiatique s'essouffle dans son invisibilisation des violences policières. Le ministre s'essouffle à fermer les lycées. Les policiers s'essoufflent à courir derrière les jeunes pour les tabasser et les blesser. Seuls les jeunes ne s'essoufflent pas à protester…
— Jean-Luc Mélenchon (@JLMelenchon) October 13, 2026
"The only ones not losing their breath are the young people bravely protesting," he added, accusing the media of failing to show the extent of police brutality and renewing his call for adults to stand ⁠with the ​students to protect them.
Far-right leader Marine Le Pen, the frontrunner in the presidential race according to polls, ​has denounced violence by protesters and called for those who have damaged schools — or their parents if they are minors — to pay for repairs.
The government has already introduced a bill that would allow precisely ​that. It is going through parliament.

items.title: What is fuelling India's protests over changes to voter lists?
items.summary:
Major protests have convulsed the Indian capital for more than a week as the opposition Congress party and young people, spearheaded by the "Cockroach" movement, demand the resignation of the top election official.
The dispute centres on the removal of 130 million voters from electoral rolls, a move that critics say benefited Prime Minister Narendra Modi's party in recent state ​elections, claims denied by the poll body and his Bharatiya Janata Party.
What is the revision and why it being done?
The exercise, or Special Intensive Revision (SIR), ‌is a house-to-house revision of the voter rolls, launched in the eastern state of Bihar in June 2025 by the Election Commission, to update voter lists and remove duplicate and ineligible voters, before being expanded nationwide. The commission is an independent constitutional body, though its chief was appointed by a government-majority panel, drawing allegations of political bias, which it denies.
In contrast to the past system
items.author: Reuters
items.content:
Major protests have convulsed the Indian capital for more than a week as the opposition Congress party and young people, spearheaded by the "Cockroach" movement, demand the resignation of the top election official.
The dispute centres on the removal of 130 million voters from electoral rolls, a move that critics say benefited Prime Minister Narendra Modi's party in recent state ​elections, claims denied by the poll body and his Bharatiya Janata Party.
What is the revision and why it being done?
The exercise, or Special Intensive Revision (SIR), ‌is a house-to-house revision of the voter rolls, launched in the eastern state of Bihar in June 2025 by the Election Commission, to update voter lists and remove duplicate and ineligible voters, before being expanded nationwide. The commission is an independent constitutional body, though its chief was appointed by a government-majority panel, drawing allegations of political bias, which it denies.
In contrast to the past system of voluntary updates to electoral rolls by voters, the ​SIR — the largest such exercise in nearly two decades —  has drawn criticism for using centralised software, with limited powers given to local election officials who check if voters ​have died, moved or are ineligible.
Critics say the centralised system denies local officials the chance to correct errors, resulting in discrepancies that have struck ⁠millions from voter rolls or sent many scrambling to locate ancestral documents or launch legal challenges.
Why is it contentious?
The strict paperwork rules, short deadlines and large-scale deletions that characterise the exercise ​have provoked criticism that they could disproportionately exclude poor, migrant, elderly, homeless and nomadic people.
Read More: Indian police detain 'cockroach' movement founder Abhijeet Dipke
Those dropped are hunting for decades-old documents regarding themselves, their parents and even grandparents in some cases, while ​others seek to correct names altered by translation, spelling or data-entry errors.
Many have been asked to show that they or their parents figured on electoral rolls.
Protesters say more than 130 million voters, or a number larger than the population of Japan, have been dropped from draft rolls across 30 states and territories, an assertion disputed by the Election Commission.
Led by its chief, Gyanesh Kumar, the commission panel says its deletions largely cover the dead, ​or those who moved, registered more than once or are otherwise ineligible.
Critics say the effort shifts to citizens the burden of proving they belong on the rolls, and warn that mismatched ​records could complicate efforts to establish citizenship or receive state welfare benefits.
Why is pressure mounting on the election commission?
Pressure grew after the Indian Express newspaper reported that two of Kumar's panel colleagues had raised at ‌least 14 formal ⁠objections over 10 months concerning voter rolls, registration procedures and digital systems.
Differing views are a part of normal deliberations, the panel says. But opposition parties led by Congress and youth groups have protested, calling for Kumar to step down.
Were Eastern state elections a flashpoint?
This year's elections in the state of West Bengal, swept by Modi's BJP in its first such victory there, became a major political issue after millions of voters were excluded or subjected to review, excluding them from voting.
Opposition parties said eligible voters were disenfranchised, which disproportionately affected Muslim voters, benefiting the BJP. The party ​and the poll body denied the accusations.
What did the Supreme Court say?
In May, the ⁠Supreme Court upheld the Election Commission's SIR exercise, saying accurate electoral rolls were essential for free and fair elections, but ruled that the poll panel could not make a final determination on citizenship.
Opposition parties returned to court this week, citing arbitrary voter deletions and other irregularities, while the ​Election Commission on October 1 directed officials to identify omitted voters and ease the path to re-enrolment.
What are the implications for future state elections?
The revision comes ahead ⁠of a series of important state elections beginning in early 2027, including in India's most populous state of Uttar Pradesh, ruled by the BJP. It is unclear if people left off the electoral rolls will be put back in time to vote.
In Bihar, several people are still appealing for their names to be put back on the electoral roll more than one year later.
What is the political risk for Modi?
The "cockroach" youth ​movement, which has mobilised protests in recent months against a range of issues from government school infrastructure to ​jobs for young people, is one of the biggest political challenges to Modi and the BJP in his 12 years in power.
The movement forced the resignation of Modi's education minister in July over an exam leak scandal. The group continues to ​put pressure on Modi's government for economic and social reforms. The group's success has also inspired opposition parties to join forces.

items.author: Palak Sharma
items.content:
Manufacturing startup ThinkMetal has raised ₹27 Cr (around $2.8 Mn) in a funding round led by India Angel Network’s VC fund IAN Alpha Fund. Other investors, including deeptech focused VC 3i Partners, among others, also participated in the round.
The fresh funding will help ThinkMetal in developing its product stack, expand the type of materials it utilises as well as strengthening its R&D capabilities. The Chennai-based metal additive manufacturing startup is also looking to fuel its hiring with the fresh capital.
“This investment is an important step in ThinkMetal’s journey from technology development towards commercialisation. We’ll use this capital to strengthen our product development, expand our team and materials capabilities and accelerate adoption across industrial applications,” cofounder and CEO Sabyasachi Ghosh said.
Founded in 2021 by Ghosh and Arushi Sharma (CTO),ThinkMetal is a Chennai-based metal additive manufacturing startup that builds industrial printing systems that can manufacture tools such as moulds, dies, jigs and fixtures.
Its SistemT1 machine uses metal fused additive manufacturing to build components layer by layer from wound metal feedstock. The process is followed by debinding and sintering to achieve the required strength.
The hardware works alongside the startup’s proprietary FuseX materials and Thinkware software. ThinkMetal claims its system can produce metal parts up to 10X faster and at half the cost of conventional manufacturing methods.
Its customers include Ants Ceramics, ZeQube Technologies and Hosur CNC, while its components serve applications across the automotive, aerospace and defence sectors.
Prior to this round, ThinkMetal raised around $1.1 Mn from YourNest Venture Capital to scale production of its first-generation system.
The startup operates in India’s additive manufacturing market, which is projected to grow from $677.4 Mn in 2023 to $3.75 Bn by 2030.
The funding comes at a time when the need for deeptech-focus manufacturing firms is rapidly escalating, with the sector attracting a significant interest from institutional investors in recent times.
As per Inc42’s ‘Indian Tech Startup Funding Report, Q3 2026’, deeptech startups raised $290 Mn across 28 deals, a 2.8X jump from $105 Mn across 29 deals in Q3 2025.
Hence, startups in the deeptech manufacturing domain are emerging and also getting significant traction from VCs. For instance, Ethereal Machines recently raised $28.5 Mn in its Series B funding round led by Avataar Ventures to build a 3 Lakh sq ft mega-factory near Bengaluru.
Similarly, companies like Fledgetec System also develop custom-built components, assemblies, and engineering solutions for the aerospace, defence, industrial, and specialised technology sectors.

items.author: Anne Florentyna
items.content:
Bengaluru-based NuSynth Technologies has raised ₹36.5 Cr (about $4 Mn) in a seed funding round co-led by Avaana Capital and Shastra VC.
The startup will use the fresh capital to strengthen its R&D and technology capabilities, develop an initial portfolio of proprietary chemical processes, build scale-up capabilities, and expand its team.
Founded in 2026 by Poorvank Purohit, Ramesha A R, Abhishek Deo and Dipak Bajaj, NuSynth combines chemical R&D with AI to develop alternative processes for making complex chemicals, initially focusing on pharmaceuticals and electronics chemicals.
The startup aims to address challenges associated with conventional chemical synthesis, including complex, multi-step processes, high material and energy costs, dependence on imported intermediates, and the use of hazardous reagents.
To address these challenges, NuSynth re-evaluates starting materials, reaction pathways, and process economics. According to Avaana Capital, its processes seek to reduce reaction steps, eliminate hazardous reagents, lower temperature requirements, and replace solvent-intensive processes with catalytic and water-based alternatives.
NuSynth follows an asset-light manufacturing model, working with Indian manufacturing partners to translate its laboratory research into industrial-scale production, the investor said.
Supporting this work is an R&D platform that combines predictive synthesis models with an AI-enabled engine. The startup said the engine converts experimental data from each R&D cycle into a proprietary knowledge base to accelerate future molecule selection, experimentation, and commercial scale-up.
“At NuSynth, we are going back to first principles – questioning established routes, redesigning processes and engineering them for commercial scale from day one. Our ambition is to build proprietary processes from India that can deliver superior economics and sustainability, and serve customers across global markets,” Purohit said.
India has built considerable capacity in chemical manufacturing but developing proprietary synthesis processes could help companies address dependencies on imported intermediates and improve manufacturing economics.
NuSynth joins a clutch of startups combining R&D with manufacturing partnerships in the speciality chemicals segment. Investors have previously backed startups like Distil, Scimplify, and Mstack to develop chemical solutions and expand their reach in global markets.
The funding also comes at a time when India’s deeptech sector continues to draw investor attention across industrial and manufacturing innovation themes.
Indian deeptech startups raised $290 Mn across 28 deals in Q3 2026, a 176% increase from $105 Mn across 29 deals in Q3 2025. This outpaced the broader startup ecosystem, where funding grew 5% to $2.2 Bn.

items.summary:
Leader of the Opposition in the Senate Allama Raja Nasir Abbas on Tuesday alleged that negotiations with the government were a sham, claiming that the decision on governor’s rule in Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa had already been made before the talks concluded.

The upper house opened the floor for debate on the move.

items.author: Naeem Asghar
items.content:
Leader of the Opposition in the Senate Allama Raja Nasir Abbas on Tuesday alleged that negotiations with the government were a sham, claiming that the decision on governor’s rule in Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa had already been made before the talks concluded.
The federal government imposed an emergency and governor’s rule in K-P on Sunday under Articles 232 and 234 of the Constitution. The government cited the deteriorating law and order situation and what it called a lack of support from the provincial administration in the fight against terrorism.
The upper house opened the floor for debate on the move.
خیبر پختونخوا میں ایمرجنسی کے نفاذ کے خلاف سینیٹ میں قرارداد پیش
اسلام آباد: جمعیت وکلاء فورم پاکستان کے مرکزی صدر سینیٹر کامران مرتضیٰ سینیٹر مولانا عبدالواسع سینیٹر مولانا عطاء الحق درویش نے خیبر پختونخوا میں ایمرجنسی کے نفاذ کے خلاف سینیٹ میں قرارداد پیش کردی۔ pic.twitter.com/GKPvQxCv5Q
— Kamran Murtaza (@KamranM69045926) October 13, 2026
“The negotiations were a sham. You had already made up your mind,” Abbas said, arguing that the opposition had shown flexibility by stepping back from its demand for a meeting with Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf founder Imran Khan, while the government had refused to reconsider its position.
Speaking during a Senate session chaired by Senate Chairman Syed Yousuf Raza Gilani, Abbas said the opposition wanted to meet Imran to seek his guidance in light of the prevailing global situation, adding that denying access to a detained political leader raised questions about the government’s commitment to political dialogue.
“We are not being allowed to meet Imran Khan, who is a prisoner and the head of a political party,” he said.
Abbas maintained that the opposition had demonstrated a willingness to compromise during negotiations but alleged that the government had already decided on its course of action.
He also criticised the reported move towards imposing governor’s rule in K-P, warning that such measures could deepen political tensions and undermine efforts to restore peace in the province.
Questioning the message being conveyed to young people in K-P, the opposition leader said the authorities’ actions suggested that political struggle and recourse to the judiciary carried little weight. He warned that pushing people away from democratic and political processes could increase frustration and potentially contribute to further instability and militancy.
Referring to the governor’s reported remarks urging people to leave their homes, Abbas argued that such statements could have the opposite of their intended effect by encouraging more people to take up arms.
He cautioned that policies pursued in the name of "restoring order" could aggravate terrorism and unrest, rather than address their underlying causes.
Drawing a comparison with former military ruler Pervez Musharraf, Abbas said that even Musharraf had tolerated dissent to some extent, questioning why a government operating under a democratic system could not accommodate political disagreement. He also alleged that PTI lawmakers, including members of the National Assembly and provincial assemblies, were being abducted.
Abbas said the political crisis could still be resolved through dialogue and corrective action.
He urged the government to end governor’s rule, warning that the move would not deliver lasting peace and could instead inflict further damage on the country.
“Peace cannot be established through such measures. Pakistan will suffer the consequences,” he said.
Earlier, the Senate session began with prayers for those who lost their lives in the Multan railway incident, with Abbas leading the prayers. The house also approved a motion to defer the question hour.
The panel of presiding officers was announced, with Senators Shahadat Ahsan, Manzoor Ahmed and Abdul Qadir nominated to the panel. Then the upper house moved to the discussion on emergency and governor's rule.
Interior minister says negotiations with PTI collapsed over intra-party differences
Later in the session, Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi said that the government had approached the opposition for negotiations with sincerity. He claimed that the options of imposing an emergency or governor’s rule had been available as early as November 24, but insisted that the government had not wanted to take either step.
He urged opposition leaders to confirm that he had continued contacting them until the night before the possibility of an emergency was discussed.
Recounting the negotiations with the opposition, Naqvi said the initial discussions had focused primarily on terrorism, with the first seven or eight points concerning the security situation. He said PTI leader Asad Qaiser had assured the government of cooperation on the issue and indicated that he would consult the Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa government before proceeding further.
“After that, we discussed political issues,” Naqvi highlighted.
Naqvi said he had also approached Barrister Gohar Ali Khan and asked him to identify the changes the opposition wanted in “paragraph four” of the draft proposal.
During the negotiations, the interior minister said Asad Qaiser had subsequently indicated that the opposition was willing to support measures concerning terrorism, including an emergency.
According to the minister, six proposals were sent in the final draft.
He claimed that after the draft was finalised, it was forwarded to the K-P chief minister, who then shared it with Murad Saeed. Naqvi alleged that the process broke down following these consultations.
Naqvi also questioned whether Murad Saeed alone was responsible for the collapse of the negotiations, suggesting that other factors and people within the party may also have played a role.
“Imposing an emergency or governor’s rule was not easy. None of us wanted it,” he said.
At the same time, he said, “We did not want our security personnel to be martyred in Peshawar while no provincial assembly representative was present,” referring to the security situation in K-P.
He added that government representatives had attended the funerals of security personnel in the province, accusing the provincial government of failing to provide similar support.
The interior minister also alleged that around 80% of terrorism-related activity was emanating from Afghanistan. He said the government had never singled out any tribe in its statements on militancy.
Naqvi said the government had raised concerns about alleged contacts between certain individuals associated with the PTI-led provincial administration and the Taliban.
“We told them that several of their people were linked to the Tehreek-e-Taliban Pakistan (TTP), and we have evidence,” he said, adding that the government also had information about financial transactions involving individuals connected to the matter.
The minister also recalled previous negotiations with PTI leaders over a planned protest on November 25.
“The government had offered the opposition a venue to hold its protest, but the opposition had instead demanded that a telephone conversation be arranged [with the PTI founder].”
According to Naqvi, the call was facilitated, and the conversation took place, but differences emerged within the opposition, with some party members refusing to accept the outcome. The minister said the government was subsequently asked to arrange a video message from the PTI founder, Imran Khan.
Naqvi claimed that he asked Barrister Gohar to go and record the message, but Imran Khan declined to avail the offer. The minister maintained that the government had reminded the PTI founder that his party was preparing to stage a sit-in and that the message needed to be recorded immediately, but he ignored the call.
Naqvi concluded this part of his remarks by praying for the success of security forces in the fight against terrorism and saying the federal government would work alongside the people of K-P.
PTI refutes govt's claim
Addressing Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi, PTI-backed Senator Ali Zafar accused the government of violating the Constitution by arresting the chief minister, speaker and other ministers in K-P, warning that the move would weaken state institutions and undermine democracy.
Speaking during a Senate session, Zafar said the government had inflicted an “indescribable wound” on the state by taking actions that, he argued, were contrary to the Constitution.
The senator questioned, “Which constitutional provision allows the federal government to take control of a province in the guise of combating terrorism?”
“We are all united in our resolve to defeat terrorism. However, while fighting this war, we must not throw the Constitution into the dustbin,” he took the interior minister to task.
Zafar maintained that counterterrorism measures could not be used as a justification for dismissing a provincial government or imposing governor's rule and emergency provisions at the government's discretion. He said an emergency could be declared in circumstances such as a foreign attack, while internal disturbances required adherence to the constitutional process, including the relevant role of the provincial assembly.
He urged the government to bring the relevant summary for imposing governor's rule and an emergency before the Senate for consideration, as well as present the evidence before the upper house for its claims that a provincial government consists of terrorists or their facilitators.
Disputing the government's account of negotiations, Zafar said it contradicted “facts”.
Warning against attempts to suppress political dissent through administrative measures, Zafar said the government could remove an elected administration but could not eliminate a political movement or control public opinion.
“You can remove a government, but you cannot end a movement. You cannot restrict the thinking of the people,” he asserted before the upper house.
He added that the government's actions were not only harming its political opponents but were also damaging the country and weakening the state.
Concluding his address, the PTI senator appealed to the government to reverse its actions and engage the opposition in dialogue.
Dar defends emergency and governor's rule, says suspended K-P govt failed to curb terrorism
Leader of the House in the Senate Ishaq Dar also defended the government's position on the imposition of an emergency and governor’s rule, saying the Constitution allows such a measure in the event of a threat of external aggression.
Towards the end of today’s session, Dar said the government was not taking any step outside the Constitution and maintained that the president could also proclaim an emergency and summon a session of parliament within 10 days.
“Whatever has happened has been done entirely in accordance with the Constitution and the law,” he reiterated the government’s stance.
He assailed the suspended K-P government over the province's security situation, claiming that terrorist attacks had tripled since Sohail Afridi assumed the charge of chief minister.
“The KP chief minister has failed to discharge his responsibilities in his own province.”
The deputy prime minister also questioned the provincial government's performance in combatting militancy, saying it had failed to establish an effective Counter Terrorism Department (CTD) despite the PTI remaining in power in the province for 13 years.
“How many times has the PTI government condemned terrorism?” Dar demanded answers, urging the party to publicly denounce terrorist attacks. The minister urged the K-P government to reconsider its leadership and take a clear stand against terrorism.
Speaking on the current ground reality of the province, Dar said the government had attempted to ensure that the advisory council established for K-P did not have a political background, adding that professionals had been appointed to the body, citing the importance of involving qualified professionals in public administration.
“We will make every effort to extend our full support to the K-P advisory council,” he stressed during the speech.
Dar also referred to the previous imprisonment of President Asif Ali Zardari, saying he had spent over a decade in prison, while reiterating his preference for reconciliation over confrontation. Adding that he hoped that PTI founder Imran Khan would eventually be released from prison, as he also stands for “political reconciliation”.
“May Allah facilitate the release of the PTI founder from prison,” he emphasised, while cautioning against placing political interests above national stability.
“The country should not be pushed towards uncertainty simply because a political leader or party failed to get its way.”
Outlining the lapses of the PTI-backed suspended K-P government, Dar said that around Rs800 billion had been transferred to the provincial government through the National Finance Commission (NFC) award and asked Zafar to seek an explanation from his party about how the money had been spent.
“One per cent of the NFC share continued to be allocated to K-P for counterterrorism efforts,” he detailed during the session of the upper house.
He lamented that the provincial government had failed to establish an effective CTD despite receiving substantial financial resources from the centre.
“The K-P chief minister has failed to discharge his responsibilities in his own province,” DPM Dar remarked.
He concluded his speech while expressing confidence that the provincial assembly would be called into session after six months.
The Senate was then adjourned till 4pm tomorrow.
