By Hadiza Yusuf
The Kano State Government has said contractors handling public projects have no reason to stay away from their sites, stressing that it is intervening to resolve challenges between contractors and government agencies.
The Commissioner for Public Procurement, Project Monitoring and Evaluation, Comrade Nura Ma’aji Sumaila, stated this on Monday during a press briefing on the ministry’s monitoring and evaluation exercise for September 2026.
Sumaila said the ministry had been engaging contractors and the relevant ministries, departments and agencies (MDAs) to address issues affecting project execution.
He explained that payment delays could sometimes prevent contractors from working at project sites, adding that the ministry intervened to resolve such challenges.
“When you are given a contract, it is because you have been found capable and technically qualified, so there is absolutely no reason why a contractor should stay away from a project site,” he said.
“We have been engaging the relevant government agencies and contractors to resolve issues affecting project execution and ensure that work continues. The contractors handling the road projects mentioned are also on site,” he said.
According to him, the ministry would continue to monitor projects and engage relevant parties to address delays and ensure that public investments deliver the expected benefits.
During the September monitoring exercise, the ministry inspected projects across Kabo, Dawakin Tofa, Tofa, Shanono, Gwarzo and Bagwai local government areas.
The commissioner said the exercise covered roads, school buildings and renovations, healthcare facilities, neighbourhood security infrastructure, solar-powered streetlights, drainage systems and water supply projects.
He disclosed that the ministry’s consolidated records contained 106 projects with a combined contract value of approximately ₦48.91 billion.
Of the projects monitored, 80 had reached 100 per cent physical progress, representing about 75.5 per cent of the total, while 20 were at different stages of completion and six had recently been awarded.
Sumaila said the ministry’s technical teams assessed the quality of work, identified challenges and recommended corrective measures where necessary.
He added that projects with incomplete work or quality concerns would undergo further technical reviews, while the ministry would continue engaging contractors and implementing agencies to address outstanding issues.

Country: South Africa
Sector: Banking and financial services

The latest position earned by Nedbank puts it ahead of other African banking groups, including Standard Bank Group, Absa Group and FirstRand.
Standard Bank Group — 54th globally
Country: South Africa
Sector: Banking and financial services
Standard Bank Group ranks second among African companies with the best employers and 54th globally. The bank fell from 28th position in 2025, dropping 26 places in the latest edition.
Despite the decline, it remains one of Africa’s highest-ranked employers, alongside three other South African banking groups in the global top 105.
Absa Group — 98th globally
Country: South Africa
Sector: Banking and financial services
Absa Group ranks third among African companies and 98th worldwide. The South African financial services group recorded a slight decline from 97th position in the previous edition. Absa’s latest ranking significantly keeps it among the continent’s four highest-ranked employers, all of which are South African banking groups.
FirstRand — 104th globally
Country: South Africa
Sector: Banking and financial services
FirstRand ranks fourth among African companies and 104th globally. The financial services group is the parent company of banking brands including First National Bank and Rand Merchant Bank.
MTN Group — 133rd globally
Country: South Africa
Sector: Telecommunications

MTN operates across multiple African markets, including Nigeria. Its ranking refers to the wider group rather than its Nigerian operations alone.

Sector: Banking and financial services

items.author: Henry Oduah
items.content:
A Houthi official on Monday warned the US it would receive a “painful response” if it entered the war in Yemen, where Saudi Arabia has reportedly requested Washington’s help in dealing with the group as it weathers repeated attacks.
Yemen’s civil war — in which a Saudi-led military coalition supports the government against the Iran-backed Houthis — reignited in July, months into the wider regional conflict that has roiled energy markets and plunged the Middle East into crisis.
The Houthis quickly began targeting Saudi oil facilities, tankers and transport hubs, including with a string of lethal strikes on Riyadh’s airport, rocking the world’s top oil exporter.
Blasts resounded over the capital again on Monday night, with the Saudi coalition saying it had intercepted a Houthi missile.
Following an attack Saturday at the airport that killed 13 people, US President Donald Trump said he was considering joining Saudi strikes against the group, after having reportedly rebuffed previous requests for help from the kingdom.
“If the US becomes involved in the aggression against Yemen, we will not deliberate over the decision to respond, rather, there will be a swift and painful response targeting the US and all its interests in the region,” Houthi political bureau member Mohammed Al Bukhaiti told AFP in an interview.
He also warned “all employees and workers at Saudi oil facilities and airports to stay away from these sites, as they have become legitimate targets”.
Saturday’s strike on King Khalid International Airport was the deadliest attack on Saudi soil in more than a decade, and also left hundreds wounded.
Trump said the attack was “not acceptable” and that he would be speaking to the kingdom’s de facto leader Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman, telling reporters the US was “going to look at” the possibility of joining Saudi strikes.
Four people died in earlier strikes on Wednesday and Thursday, and another was killed on Sunday. Operations remained suspended at the sprawling airport on Riyadh’s outskirts on Monday.
– ‘Serious’ response –
Bukhaiti said the purpose of the campaign against Saudi targets was to send a message to the crown prince “that he can no longer wage aggression against Yemen from a safe position”.
Saudi energy minister Prince Abdulaziz bin Salman told a conference in Riyadh on Monday that the recent events had “tested our infrastructure, our institutions, our people, and our resilience”.
“The events of recent weeks are serious, our response must be equally serious.”
CCTV footage of Saturday’s attack released by Saudi authorities showed Muslim pilgrims in religious attire waiting in departure lounges before a sudden blast tore through the building and brought down flaming debris.
The atmosphere in Riyadh remained tense on Monday, as state broadcaster Al Ekhbariya said the military coalition was responding to drone and missile threats.
In the evening, mobile phones received a loud government alert warning of a “hostile aerial threat” before the announcement of the interception.
It was the first use of the phone alert system in Riyadh in weeks, with no official reason given for the lack of messaging during the attacks targeting the capital in recent days.
– Flights suspended –
The US embassy in Saudi Arabia said US government employees must obtain its authorisation before using any airport in the kingdom, and urged US citizens to “take extreme caution” if they chose to do so.
The mission also said “American citizens have been detained for taking photos of recent events” in Saudi Arabia.
The UAE’s national carrier Etihad Airways announced on Monday that it was cancelling all flights to and from Riyadh until next week, and also suspended flights to Dammam and Jeddah.
Bahrain’s national carrier Gulf Air said it too was cancelling all Riyadh flights until Saturday.
US operator Delta announced it would delay the launch of direct flights from Atlanta to Riyadh, scheduled for October 23.
Despite vast spending on military hardware, the Houthi attacks on oil, military and transport facilities across the large, mostly desert country are stretching Saudi defences.
Thomas Juneau, security analyst at Ottawa University, said that despite some success, “Saudi Arabia is so large that it’s simply impossible for them to consistently defend themselves”.
Riyadh leads an international coalition that has supported Yemen’s government militarily since 2015, including by seeking to exert control over Yemeni airspace and the airport in the Houthi-held capital Sanaa.
Juneau said the Houthis now “want to do to Saudi Arabia what Saudi Arabia does to them”.
The long-running Yemeni civil war has created a deeply entrenched humanitarian crisis in the impoverished country.
UN rights chief Volker Turk said he was “appalled by the repeated attacks” on Saudi Arabia, but urged both sides to back down, adding “continued fighting will only unleash further misery with no end in sight”.
AFP

The Federal Government says construction of the 750-kilometre Lagos-Calabar Coastal Highway is progressing as planned, dismissing reports that the project had been abandoned for the East-West Road.
Sen.​‌‍‍‍‍⁠⁠‍​‍​‍⁠​​‍‌​ David Umahi, Minister of Works, stated this while briefing newsmen on Monday at the State House in Abuja.
Umahi said construction is ongoing along various sections of the highway, adding that the project remained intact and was being implemented as designed.
“The Lagos-Calabar Coastal Highway is moving and moving even faster than envisaged. Don’t forget that Section One, covering 147.47 kilometres, is being fully constructed in Lagos,” he said.
The minister said Section Two, covering 55 kilometres, was expected to be ready by mid-November.
He said work is ongoing on Sections Three A and Three B, covering about 75 kilometres in Akwa Ibom and Cross River states, with progress exceeding 40 per cent.
Umahi added that construction is ongoing on Sections Four A and Four B, covering 65 kilometres across Ogun and Ondo states.
He said work had also commenced on Section Five, covering 62.5 kilometres in Akwa Ibom, with more than 20 per cent progress recorded within less than three months.
The minister explained that the ministry is seeking President Bola Tinubu’s approval to incorporate about 400 kilometres of the East-West Road into the ongoing infrastructure development programme.
He said the proposed intervention would cover sections linking Edo, Delta, Bayelsa, Rivers, Akwa Ibom and Cross River states.
Umahi said the East-West Road required attention because some sections had suffered damage from flooding, citing affected portions in Delta and Edo.
He stressed that the proposed work on the East-West Road would complement, rather than replace, the Lagos-Calabar Coastal Highway.
“Nobody has abandoned the 750-kilometre Lagos-Calabar Coastal Highway. We have designers and surveyors working along the route, including in Edo, Delta, Bayelsa and Rivers,” he said.
Umahi said the Federal Government is undertaking surveys along the route to ensure the project’s continued development and integration with other infrastructure projects in the Niger Delta.
He added that the highway remained part of the Federal Government’s legacy infrastructure projects and that its alignment would not be altered.
“The 750-kilometre coastal highway is intact and cannot be changed. Nobody has the power to change it because it is already designed and ongoing,” he said.
(NAN)

“Nigeria needs a complete RESET under a Makinde Presidency and not this propaganda-driven administration that have failed in all ramifications,” Ihediwa said.

By Adegboyega Adeleye
As Nigeria approaches the 2027 general elections, the careers of its longest-serving senators offer a look at the lawmakers whose years in the upper chamber have been shaped by electoral victories, political shifts and returns to office.
Some have served for several terms, building lengthy records in the Senate, while others have had breaks in their legislative careers before returning to the chamber.
Their years of service reflect the different paths they have taken to remain in the Senate since Nigeria’s return to democracy in 1999.
Here is a look at Nigeria’s longest-serving senators.
Ahmad Lawan (19 years in the Senate)
Party: All Progressives Congress (APC).
Ahmad Lawan, who represents Yobe North Senatorial District, began his federal legislative career in 1999 when he was elected to the House of Representatives to represent Bade/Jakusko Federal Constituency in Yobe State.
He served in the lower chamber until 2007, when he transitioned to the Senate. He has represented Yobe North since then and served as President of the Senate from 2019 to 2023.
Lawan’s 27-year legislative career spans both chambers, while his Senate tenure began in 2007. The former senate president remains one of the lawmakers who have served in the National Assembly since the beginning of the Fourth Republic.
Ali Ndume (15 years in the Senate)
Party: All Progressives Congress (APC).
Ali Ndume.
Ali Ndume, who represents Borno South Senatorial District, entered the National Assembly in 2003 as a member of the House of Representatives, representing Chibok/Damboa/Gwoza Federal Constituency in Borno State.
He served in the House until 2011, when he was elected to the Senate. Since then, he has won successive elections to represent Borno South and held leadership positions, including Senate Majority Leader and Senate Chief Whip.
Ndume’s federal legislative career spans both chambers. He was previously affiliated with the All Nigeria Peoples Party and the Peoples Democratic Party before joining the APC.
Enyinnaya Abaribe (19 years in the Senate — since 2007)
Party: Labour Party (LP)
Sen. Enyinnaya Abaribe
Enyinnaya Abaribe has represented Abia South Senatorial District since 2007, when he was elected to the Senate on the platform of the Peoples Democratic Party.
Before joining the National Assembly, Abaribe served as deputy governor of Abia State from 1999 to 2003 under Governor Orji Uzor Kalu.
He won successive elections to retain his Senate seat and served as Senate Minority Leader during the Ninth National Assembly. He left the PDP and joined the All Progressives Grand Alliance in 2022 before moving to the African Democratic Congress in March 2026. He subsequently joined the Labour Party in May 2026.
Unlike lawmakers who moved from the House of Representatives to the Senate, Abaribe’s federal legislative career began in the upper chamber as his service in the Senate dates to 2007.
Adamu Aliero (about 12 years in the Senate)
Party: All Progressives Congress (APC)
Adamu Aliero, who represents Kebbi Central Senatorial District, first entered the Senate in 2007 after serving two terms as governor of Kebbi State from 1999 to 2007.
His initial Senate tenure ended in 2008 when he was appointed Minister of the Federal Capital Territory. He returned to the Senate in 2015 and won re-election in 2019 and 2023.
Aliero’s legislative career has therefore not been continuous since 2007. He served in the Senate from 2007 to 2008 before returning in 2015, accumulating approximately 12 years in the chamber across the two periods.
He won his 2023 Senate seat on the platform of the Peoples Democratic Party but defected to the APC in May 2025. The Senate formally announced the defection during plenary.
Solomon Olamilekan Adeola (11 years in the Senate)
Party: All Progressives Congress (APC)
Solomon Olamilekan Adeola, popularly known as Yayi, represents Ogun West Senatorial District. He began his federal legislative career in 2011, when he was elected to the House of Representatives to represent Alimosho Federal Constituency in Lagos State on the platform of the defunct Action Congress of Nigeria.
Adeola served in the House until 2015, when he won election to the Senate representing Lagos West. He retained the Lagos West seat for two terms before winning the Ogun West senatorial seat in 2023.
His legislative career spans both chambers and two senatorial districts. His National Assembly service dates to 2011, while his Senate tenure began in 2015.
Danjuma Goje (15 years in the Senate)
Party: All Progressives Congress (APC)
Goje was elected to the Senate in 2011 and won re-election in 2015, 2019 and 2023. His federal legislative career began in the Senate rather than the House of Representatives.
He initially contested for the Senate on the platform of the Peoples Democratic Party before moving to the APC. He remains an APC senator representing Gombe Central.

items.author: Henry Oduah
items.content:
By Peter Egwuatu
Dangote Petroleum Refinery and Petrochemicals FZE (DPRP) has announced the extension of the application period for its Initial Public Offering (IPO) by two weeks, following approval from the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC), amid what has become one of the most significant capital market offerings in Nigerian and African history.
The IPO, which consists of 4,100,000,000 ordinary shares of US$0.000013 each at N525.00 per share, opened on Monday, September 14, 2026, and was originally scheduled to close on Tuesday, October 13, 2026. The application period will now remain open until Tuesday, October 27, 2026.
The extension follows exceptionally strong interest from a broad spectrum of eligible investors across Africa and other international markets. Since the launch of the offer, investor participation has underscored the growing confidence in Dangote Refinery’s long-term growth prospects and its strategic role in transforming Africa’s energy landscape.
In a chat with media men in the Refinery, President of Dangote Group, Aliko Dangote said: The IPO is going very well. We will extend the closing date because we want more of our African brothers and sisters to participate. Following our discussions with the Nairobi Stock Exchange, we have identified what we believe is the best way to facilitate participation. We are now trying to replicate that arrangement with other African exchanges to ensure wider participation…But when it comes to the amount of money we originally intended to raise, we have already received subscriptions amounting to more than three or four times that figure…So, it is not about the amount of money. It is about the number of people who will have the opportunity to participate in this offer. That means quite a lot to us.”
The company said, the additional two-week period will support ongoing market-access initiatives across African jurisdictions, including the expansion of distribution channels and the rollout of unsponsored depository receipt programmes designed to facilitate seamless cross-border investment.
It will also provide more time for prospective investors to complete account-opening procedures, identity verification processes, and other regulatory requirements necessary for participation in the offer.
Speaking on the extension, David Bird, Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer of Dangote Petroleum Refinery and Petrochemicals FZE, said: “We welcome the SEC’s approval of the extension, which will give more investors across Africa the opportunity to participate in the Offer. From the outset, our ambition has been to enable as many people as possible to participate in the IPO and share in DPRP’s future growth. The additional time will help us extend that opportunity to more investors across Africa.”

items.author: Publishing Partner
items.content:
For many Pakistani families, the best part of owning an SUV is not the spec sheet; it is the journey. The long drive up north, a weekend escape to Murree, or a memorable the family road trip. Omoda & Jaecoo Pakistan is now inviting its J5 and J7 owners to share those moments with the campaign #MyJaecooJourney, with 100 winners winning Free Service for a Year.
The question at the heart of the campaign is simple: Have you taken your JAECOO J5 or J7 on a memorable journey? Owners who have travelled and have pictures and videos from any memorable trip with their JAECOO can participate.
Since its arrival in Pakistan, Omoda & Jaecoo has grown quickly, with the J5 and J7 becoming familiar sights around the country. #MyJaecooJourney puts the people behind those vehicles in front of the camera. Road trips, Northern Area travels, family holidays, weekend getaways and any other journeys worth remembering are all eligible. Pictures or videos from a recent or a previous journey both count!
How to Participate
Taking part is deliberately straightforward. Eligible J5 and J7 customers need to follow four steps:
Step 1 – Post: Share a JAECOO J5 or J7 travel picture or video on social media.
Step 2 – Go public: Make sure the profile or post is set to Public so the entry can be seen.
Step 3 – Use the hashtag: Add #MyJaecooJourney as a hashtag on your post
Step 4 – Tag The Official Page: Tag @omodajaecoopk on Facebook and @omoda_jaecoo_pk on Instagram.
How the 100 winners will be chosen
One hundred winners will be selected from eligible participants based on the highest combined engagement, calculated as likes plus comments plus shares. To keep the contest fair for every owner, engagement must be genuine and organic. Entries with artificially generated or seeded comments, abnormal or inflated engagement, bots, automated tools, paid engagement services or other artificial means may be disqualified, as per full discretion reserved for Omoda & Jaecoo Pakistan.
The Prize: Free Service for a Year!
Each winner will receive Free Service for a Year, covering the standard periodic maintenance schedule up to an estimated 20,000 km per year. The package includes:
Service 1: Engine oil, oil filter, air filter and cabin/AC filter
Service 2: Engine oil and oil filter
Service 3: Engine oil and oil filter
Service 4: Engine oil and oil filter
Ownership that goes beyond the showroom
By rewarding owners who are already out exploring the country, and by covering the routine maintenance that keeps those journeys going, Omoda & Jaecoo is putting its after-sales commitment where its community is.
With 100 winners, the opportunity is open to owners across the country, so a J5 or J7 owner who has made the climb to the Northern Areas stands as good a chance as anyone with a favourite weekend drive.
Join the journey
If you own a JAECOO J5 or J7 and have a journey worth sharing, post your picture or video, use #MyJaecooJourney, tag JAECOO Pakistan, and let your journey take you closer to winning Free Service for a Year!
Terms and conditions apply. Winners are selected from eligible entries by genuine, organic engagement.

items.title: Major Airlines Suspend Flights to Riyadh
items.summary:
Several international airlines have suspended flights to Riyadh following attacks on King Khalid International Airport, with hundreds of flights canceled or delayed across Saudi Arabia.
Saudi Arabia’s General Authority of Civil Aviation has extended the closure of King Khalid International Airport by another 24 hours due to security concerns. According to a new Notice to Airmen (NOTAM), the airport will remain closed until midnight on Monday.
Authorities said the extension was necessary to inspect the airport’s radar and communication systems.
The disruption has prompted several major airlines to temporarily suspend flights to Riyadh. Lufthansa Group has extended its suspension until October 16, SriLankan Airlines until October 18, Akasa Air until October 13, and Air India and Air India Express until October 15.
Other affected airlines include Etihad Airways, flydubai, Emirates, Air Arabia, Kuwait Airways, Turkish Airlines, IndiGo, and Pakistan International Airlines (PIA).
items.author: Arooj Fatima
items.content:

Authorities said the extension was necessary to inspect the airport’s radar and communication systems.
The disruption has prompted several major airlines to temporarily suspend flights to Riyadh. Lufthansa Group has extended its suspension until October 16, SriLankan Airlines until October 18, Akasa Air until October 13, and Air India and Air India Express until October 15.
Other affected airlines include Etihad Airways, flydubai, Emirates, Air Arabia, Kuwait Airways, Turkish Airlines, IndiGo, and Pakistan International Airlines (PIA).
Flight operations between Pakistan and Riyadh have also been severely affected. On Sunday, PIA flight PK-753 from Islamabad to Riyadh was diverted to Dammam, while 28 flights from airports across Pakistan were canceled.
According to aviation sources, another 32 Riyadh-bound flights from various Pakistani airports have been canceled on Monday as uncertainty over Saudi flight operations continues.
The closure has also disrupted operations at Jeddah, Madinah, and Dammam airports. However, flight operations at Dammam have resumed following a six-hour suspension.

items.content:
By Chimaobi Nwaiwu
NNEWI — The Indigenous People of Biafra (IPOB) has rejected an alleged police intelligence report claiming that the group and its Eastern Security Network (ESN) planned to resume enforcement of Monday sit-at-home orders in the South-East.
The group, in a statement issued by its Media and Publicity Secretary, Emma Powerful, said it had no plan to enforce a sit-at-home order from October 12, 2026.
The statement was a response to an alleged police intelligence report dated October 9, 2026, which reportedly raised concerns about a possible resumption of sit-at-home enforcement in the region.
IPOB said it did not issue any directive to its members or the ESN to enforce the order, maintaining that its position on the matter remained unchanged.
“There is no voice note. There is no order from IPOB or ESN to resume any sit-at-home. There is no plan by this movement to enforce anything on the people of the South-East or Imo State,” the statement said.
The group also called on the Nigeria Police Force to provide verifiable evidence for the allegations contained in the reported intelligence document, including the basis for linking the alleged message to IPOB or ESN.
IPOB said its activities were focused on its stated objective of Biafran self-determination through peaceful means.
The group further reiterated its position on the forthcoming elections, saying it intended to boycott them.
IPOB also called on the Federal Government to give greater attention to the economic challenges facing Nigerians, including hunger and unemployment.
It urged the authorities to prioritise measures that would ease hardship and address the concerns of citizens.
The statement did not include a response from the police on the reported intelligence document or the allegations attributed to it.

items.title: Punjab Cancels Sanitation Contracts in 26 Tehsils Over Poor Performance
items.summary:
The Punjab government has decided to cancel sanitation contracts in 26 tehsils over poor cleaning services, administrative negligence, and delays in paying workers’ salaries.
In the first phase, contracts covering 21 tehsils will be terminated following complaints of poor performance and mismanagement. All 21 contracts were awarded to a single company.
The government has also ordered a 90-day temporary takeover of sanitation operations in the affected areas to ensure cleaning services continue under government management.
The handover of machinery is already underway, while arrangements are being made for waste collection directly from its source.
The respective deputy commissioners will supervise sanitation operations during the 90-day period.
Contracts have already been canceled in Multan, Faisalabad, Jhang, Bhakkar, and Layyah, with similar action underway in the remaining tehsils.

items.summary:

items.author: Our Correspondent
items.content:
The federal and the Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa (K-P) governments on Monday pledged coordinated action against terrorism, promising to strengthen the police and Counter-Terrorism Department (CTD) and accelerate development in the province following the imposition of emergency and governor's rule.
The commitment was made at a meeting of the Provincial Apex Committee at the Governor House, co-chaired by Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi and Governor Faisal Karim Kundi. The meeting reviewed the security situation and measures to eradicate terrorism and establish lasting peace.
Speaking a press conference after the meeting, Governor Kundi said addressing problems that had accumulated over the past 13 years was a major challenge. He stressed that decisions concerning the province would henceforth be made in Islamabad, not Kabul.
The forum directed all relevant institutions to take "coordinated, effective and decisive" steps against terrorism, reiterating that intelligence-based operations (IBOs) would continue and all available resources would be utilised to improve law and order.
It decided to strengthen the operational capacity of the police and CTD by providing modern equipment, vehicles, armoured vehicles, weapons and the required manpower. Participants paid tribute to security personnel who had sacrificed their lives in the fight against terrorism and offered Fateha for the martyrs.
The meeting also agreed to prioritise long-standing public issues relating to education, healthcare, living standards and basic amenities, particularly in underdeveloped and affected areas. Public needs, local priorities and suggestions would be incorporated into policymaking.
Naqvi said the federal government would extend full support to the province in combating terrorism and strengthening its law-enforcement agencies. He said the fight against terrorism could be pursued more effectively if the provincial administration took the lead through firm, coordinated and sustained efforts.
He said 10 new armoured vehicles belonging to the Islamabad Police had been handed over to the K-P police on the directives of Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif. "The vehicles have been provided to strengthen counterterrorism operations in K-P," Naqvi added.
The interior minister said the security situation had deteriorated over the past two and a half years because of an ineffective counterterrorism approach. He added that the federal and provincial governments were now on the same page in their efforts to restore lasting peace.
Separately, Naqvi also chaired a meeting of the Area Development Secretariat (ADS) to review security, development requirements and public grievances in 12 designated districts, including the merged tribal districts, Bannu, Lakki Marwat, Tank and Dera Ismail Khan.
The meeting decided to provide immediate funds to support peace and development, stressing the timely completion of ongoing projects and the transparent and effective use of federal allocations. Participants also discussed measures to reduce unemployment and create job opportunities for young people.
The governor said security would remain the administration's first priority, followed by development. He stressed that the government would pursue practical, results-oriented measures rather than cosmetic steps and called for restoring freedom of movement in terrorism-affected districts.
Kundi later told reporters that a decision had been taken to investigate alleged corruption and irregular recruitment during the ousted Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) government. "Whether someone is small or powerful, anyone found involved in corruption will be arrested, punished and made to return the money."
The governor said the public had rejected the politics of chaos and that no one would now be allowed to engage in vandalism. He alleged that the PTI had supported terrorism, adding, "We have to eliminate terrorism. Now, policy will come from Islamabad, not Afghanistan," he said.
"The people of Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa have made immense sacrifices in the fight against terrorism. The people of the province and the security institutions are united in this fight. This is our own war, and we must fight it together," he added.
Governor Kundi said addressing problems that had accumulated during the PTI's 13 years in power in the province was a major challenge, but efforts would be made over the next three months to improve and reform the system.
The governor said the federal cabinet had decided the previous day to establish an advisory council, whose members had all assumed their responsibilities. A security committee meeting had been held the previous day, while the Apex Committee meeting was convened on the first working day.
He made it clear that there would be no compromise on law and order in the province. He said the provincial government stood with the Pakistan Army, police, Frontier Constabulary (FC) and other law-enforcement agencies and would provide them with all necessary resources and facilities.
He said steps would be taken to equip the police with modern weapons and essential equipment. The government would also review proposals to increase the salaries of K-P police personnel and enhance the compensation package for the families of police martyrs.
Kundi said the federal interior minister had handed over 10 armoured personnel carrier (APC) vehicles to the K-P police. He added that pending projects aimed at strengthening the force's operational capacity would be completed soon.

items.author: Arooj Fatima
items.content:
Punjab Chief Minister (CM) Maryam Nawaz Sharif has launched a mobile healthcare program to provide medical services to more than 4.6 million industrial workers and their families at workplaces and doorsteps.
The Social Security Mobile Health Program will initially cover Lahore, Kasur, and Sheikhupura before expanding to 12 additional districts by March 2027.
The program includes 65 mobile healthcare units, comprising 10 mobile hospitals, five mobile clinics, a dental hospital, a cardiac unit, 40 motorcycles, and 10 scooters.
These units will provide medical consultations, basic medicines, first aid, diagnostic tests, telemedicine, and health awareness services.
The mobile hospitals will have male and female doctors, radiologists, nurses, laboratory technicians, and X-ray technicians, along with outpatient departments, radiology facilities, and pathology laboratories.
The mobile dental hospital will offer dental treatment, X-rays, intraoral camera systems, and telemedicine services.
As part of the initiative, mobile screening teams will visit 29,845 factories, industrial units, and other establishments across Lahore, Kasur, and Sheikhupura to support the early detection of rheumatic heart disease (RHD).
The program will also screen 54,000 children enrolled in workers’ welfare schools across Punjab for heart diseases. The mobile cardiac unit will provide initial screenings and medical consultations to industrial workers and their families.
All mobile units will be connected to a digital hub at the Punjab Employees Social Security Institution (PESSI) headquarters, allowing authorities to monitor their locations, routes, and field operations in real time.
Speaking at the launch, CM Maryam Nawaz said the program would improve access to healthcare for registered workers and their families while ensuring timely diagnosis and treatment.
She said the provincial government was already providing medical treatment and medicines through 24 social security hospitals, with services also set to be offered through 250 PESSI medical outlets.
The chief minister added that mobile healthcare services would be available at factories, commercial establishments, and industrial units, helping reduce the burden on hospitals.

items.title: Digital Public Infrastructure Is Supposed To Be Interoperable: Why Does the Standardization End When Something Goes Wrong?
items.summary:
There should be no digital public infrastructure (DPI) without redress. As a growing number of governments focus on building population-scale digital systems for identity, payments and data exchange, redress — i.e., citizens’ ability to challenge errors and obtain remedy — should be part of their architecture rather than an afterthought.
That raises a harder question: What would infrastructure-grade redress actually require?
Every service needs a way to fix mistakes, but DPI raises a distinct version of the problem. A single user’s identity, payments and data are handled by separate institutions, so one failure can cascade — and even national DPI systems with strong complaints systems, like Brazil’s and India’s, are not built to track and resolve these intertwined issues across government agencies and tech platforms. items.author: Arooj Fatima
items.content:
As many as 3,191 morphine injections have expired at the National Institute of Cardiovascular Diseases (NICVD) after remaining unused.
The hospital administration, however, has denied any financial loss to the public treasury, claiming that the supplier will replace the expired injections at no additional cost after the required legal procedures are completed.
According to official documents, pharmacist Talha Mehboob Khan informed Assistant Manager of Pharmacy Services Saima Saleem in a letter dated December 24, 2025, that 3,191 morphine injections were lying unused in the hospital’s narcotics cabinet, just six days before their expiration date of December 30.
The records show that NICVD used 2,809 morphine injections between October 2023 and November 2025, while the remaining 3,191 injections accounted for nearly 53% of the total stock of 6,000.
The letter also confirmed that the unused injections were stored in the narcotics cabinet and its key had been handed over to the designated custodian.
Responding to the matter, NICVD spokesperson Abdul Naseer said morphine is a controlled narcotic drug, and its procurement, transportation, storage, use, and return are subject to strict legal requirements.
He explained that the injections are supplied through imported shipments and cannot be returned like ordinary medicines. Their return requires inspection and verification by a drug inspector, along with the completion of other legal formalities.
Once the process is completed, the supplier will replace the expired stock with fresh injections without charging the hospital, he added.
The administration maintained that NICVD has an inventory management system and stock registers to monitor the receipt, storage, distribution, and use of medicines, with additional oversight measures for controlled drugs.

items.author: Christopher Louis
items.content:
Android 17 membawa pendekatan baru untuk melindungi aktivitas pengguna saat memanfaatkan AI. Salah satunya melalui AISeal, lingkungan pemrosesan terisolasi yang dirancang untuk menjaga data ketika Gemini membaca konten layar, mengakses pesan, atau menjalankan tugas lintas aplikasi. Teknologi ini memanfaatkan perlindungan berbasis perangkat keras agar pemrosesan tertentu berlangsung secara lokal.
Namun melansir dari PCMag, penerapan perlindungan Android 17 disebut bergantung pada kemampuan perangkat. Ponsel kelas atas dengan kapasitas memori dan pemrosesan AI yang memadai dapat menjalankan tugas tertentu langsung di perangkat. Sementara itu, sebagian ponsel kelas menengah dan entry-level harus mengandalkan pemrosesan cloud untuk mendapatkan fitur otomatisasi serupa.
Kondisi ini memunculkan pertanyaan mengenai kesetaraan privasi di ekosistem Android terkhusus di Android 17. Jika perlindungan data lokal hanya tersedia pada perangkat dengan spesifikasi tinggi, pengguna ponsel lebih terjangkau mungkin harus lebih bergantung pada server eksternal. Meski demikian, pemrosesan cloud tidak otomatis berarti data pengguna disalahgunakan, tetapi mekanisme perlindungan dan pengelolaannya menjadi faktor penting yang perlu diperhatikan.
Baca Juga: OPPO Reno X Dirumorkan Usung Layar 16:9, Lebar Bodi Capai 85 mm
AISeal Andalkan Perlindungan Berbasis Perangkat Keras
AISeal dalam Android 17 menggunakan teknologi protected Kernel-based Virtual Machine (pKVM) untuk membentuk lingkungan pemrosesan yang terisolasi di perangkat. Dalam skenario yang dijelaskan sumber, ketika pengguna mengizinkan Gemini memahami isi layar atau menjalankan tugas tertentu, data dapat diproses di lingkungan tersebut tanpa mudah diakses sistem operasi maupun aplikasi pihak ketiga. Pendekatan ini berpotensi mengurangi risiko paparan data saat AI menangani informasi pribadi.
Tantangan Android 17, pemrosesan model AI secara lokal membutuhkan sumber daya perangkat yang besar, termasuk RAM dan unit pemrosesan neural atau NPU. Artikel sumber mencontohkan Samsung Galaxy S26 sebagai perangkat kelas atas yang dapat mendukung pemrosesan tersebut, sementara Google Pixel 10a dengan RAM 8 GB disebut tidak mampu menjalankan pemrosesan Gemini Intelligence yang lebih berat secara lokal. Namun, kemampuan tiap perangkat dan fitur yang tersedia tetap perlu dilihat berdasarkan implementasi teknis serta dukungan resmi Google.
Privasi Android dan Apple Jadi Perbandingan
Sebagai pembanding, Apple memiliki Private Cloud Compute (PCC) untuk menangani permintaan AI yang membutuhkan komputasi eksternal. Menurut pendekatan yang dijelaskan Apple, data diproses secara sementara dan tidak disimpan secara permanen, dengan perlindungan yang dirancang agar pihak internal pun tidak dapat mengaksesnya secara bebas. Meski demikian, efektivitas perlindungan tersebut tetap bergantung pada implementasi dan mekanisme keamanan yang diterapkan.
Bagi Google, pemrosesan cloud memungkinkan fitur AI menjangkau lebih banyak perangkat tanpa menuntut spesifikasi tinggi. Di sisi lain, pengguna perlu memahami data apa yang dikirim, bagaimana data diproses, dan perlindungan apa yang berlaku. items.author: Gaurav Bagur
items.content:
Listed gaming major Nazara Technologies announced a major leadership reshuffle today, highlighted by founder Nitish Mittersain stepping down as the company’s managing director.
Mittersain, who founded the company in 1999 and took it public in 2021, has assumed a new role as “Founder and Non-Executive Director”. He will continue to provide strategic guidance to the board.
Meanwhile, CaratLane founder Mithun Sacheti, who joined the board as an additional director earlier this year, has been elevated to an executive whole-time director role for a period of five years. Sacheti will now assume a new position to oversee strategic initiatives and take on some operational responsibilities.
“He understands the consumer business space, digital consumer ecosystems … He brings extensive entrepreneurial,consumer and brand building experience,” the gaming major said in its disclosures to the bourses earlier today.
Besides, the board also noted the resignation of Rohit Sharma as Whole-time Director, effective from January 1, 2027, onwards, as he decided to pursue entrepreneurial opportunities. Sharma joined the company’s board as an advisor in January 2025 and was later roped in as executive director in August.
Additionally, Nazara’s CFO Rakesh Shah has also resigned to pursue external opportunities and will be replaced by Arun Agrawal, former global CFO at Ness Digital Engineering. Shah, who has been with the gaming major since 2010, will exit the company on October 15 though he will assist with transition duties for 90 days.
The change at the top of Nazara’s hierarchy comes shortly after Mittersain exited as CEO amid a turning point in the listed company’s journey.
Back in March, Nazara acquired a 50% stake in Spanish casual gaming studio Bluetile Games and its associate BestPlay Systems for a deal worth $100.3 Mn at base value, with performance-linked earn-outs of up to $98.2 Mn.
However, the terms of the deal were later restructured such that Nazara acquired 100% of Bluetile and BestPlay for a fixed cash consideration of $303 Mn, shelling out $89 Mn upfront and committing to pay the remainder in agreed tranches by April 1, 2027.
Besides, the gaming giant also approved a ₹733.5 Cr fundraise via preferential issue of equity shares to the founders and senior leadership team of Bluetile and BestPlay, including Bluetile’s founder and CEO Raymond Stauffer, who also took over from Mittersain as CEO on September 1.
Notably, Bluetile and BestPlay together generated nearly ₹1,400 Cr in revenue in calendar year 2025. Yet, Bluetile’s EBITDA remained flat in the quarter despite a 54% revenue jump as the company faced climbing user acquisition costs.
Besides all this, the company also faced de-subsidiarisation of its gaming and esports media arm NODWIN Gaming this year. Nazara opted not to participate in a $100 Mn external funding round raised by NODWIN, resulting in its shareholding slipping below 51%. NODWIN is also seeking to list independently on the bourses in the near future.
On the financial front, Nazara reported a net loss of ₹82.5 Cr on operating revenue of ₹428.8 Cr in Q1 FY27. The gaming major’s operating revenue also declined 14% YoY to ₹428.8 Cr.

items.author: Debarghya Sil
items.content:
Bengaluru-based Whizzo is in talks to raise around $26 Mn in its Series B funding round which could be co-led by Aavishkaar Capital and Bertelsmann Investments (BI), Inc42 learnt.
As per sources, existing backers Fundamentum, Lightspeed Ventures, among others, are also likely to participate in the round.
Questions sent to Whizzo didn’t elicit any response at the time of publication of the story. The article will be updated based on their responses.
The fresh round of funding comes almost six months after the startup raised around $15 Mn in its Series A funding round led by Fundamentum, with participation from Korean investor LB Investment Fund, and Lightspeed. Back then, the startup said it would utilise the funds for strengthening research and development of in-house IP for materials science innovation. Prior to this, Lightspeed Ventures led Whizzo’s seed round in 2025.
The Bengaluru-based startup raised its maiden institutional funding round in January 2025 to develop its advanced R&D capabilities, creation of a design lab for fashion-engineered textiles and the expansion of its supply chain.
Founded in 2024 by Shrestha Kukreja, Whizzo is a CDMO (contract development and manufacturing organisation) that offers textile design services and textile research & development services to clients across India, Vietnam, China and Bangladesh.
The startup integrates R&D, formulation, prototyping, process engineering, and commercial-scale manufacturing under one roof.
Whizzo works with B2B manufacturers and produces a wide range of materials for applications across geotextiles, agriculture textiles, protective and flame-retardant materials, specialty yarns, engineered apparel textiles, and industrial composites. It claims to combine sustainability with advanced materials science, offering proprietary textile blends.
The potential fundraise comes amid continued investor interest in tech-led textile manufacturing and fabric innovation, as startups look to improve product development and manufacturing processes through proprietary materials and R&D capabilities.

items.author: Christopher Louis
items.content:
Sony dikabarkan mengalihkan ratusan paten terkait teknologi extended reality (XR) kepada Meta. Informasi yang beredar menyebutkan, proses pengalihan mencakup puluhan paten di Amerika Serikat yang berkaitan dengan perangkat virtual reality (VR), augmented reality (AR), dan mixed reality (MR). Langkah ini memunculkan pertanyaan mengenai arah pengembangan teknologi XR Sony ke depannya.
Dalam laporan ZDNet Korea, mereka disebut telah mengalihkan 43 paten yang terdaftar di Amerika Serikat kepada Meta melalui proses yang berlangsung antara Juni hingga September 2026. Paten-paten itu mencakup teknologi layar yang dipasang di kepala atau head-mounted display, kacamata XR, serta berbagai teknologi yang dikembangkan Sony sejak 2010 hingga 2022.
Pengalihan tersebut diklaim mencakup total 419 paten secara global. Dari jumlah itu, sekitar 180 paten terdaftar di Amerika Serikat, sedangkan 239 lainnya berasal dari berbagai negara, termasuk Jepang, China, Korea Selatan, dan sejumlah wilayah Eropa. Meski demikian, informasi ini belum cukup untuk memastikan bahwa Sony sepenuhnya meninggalkan pengembangan perangkat XR.
Baca Juga: Sony Patenkan AI yang Bisa Membuat NPC dan Boss Beradaptasi dengan Gaya Bermain
Masa Depan Headset VR Sony Jadi Tanda Tanya
Saat ini memiliki PlayStation VR2 (PSVR 2), headset VR yang dirilis pada 2023 untuk digunakan bersama PlayStation 5. Perangkat tersebut awalnya berfokus pada ekosistem konsol PlayStation, sebelum Sony menghadirkan adaptor yang memungkinkan headset digunakan pada PC. Kehadiran dukungan PC memperluas penggunaan PSVR 2, meski perangkat ini tetap berkaitan erat dengan ekosistem gaming.
Pengalihan paten tersebut memunculkan spekulasi bahwa peluang hadirnya penerus PSVR 2 dalam waktu dekat semakin kecil. Namun, kepemilikan paten yang dialihkan tidak otomatis berarti Sony menghentikan seluruh riset XR atau membatalkan produk generasi berikutnya. Tanpa pernyataan resmi mengenai strategi produknya, arah pengembangan headset VR Sony masih belum dapat dipastikan.
Meta Berpotensi Memperkuat Teknologi Headset XR
Bagi Meta, akuisisi hak kekayaan intelektual tersebut berpotensi memperluas portofolio teknologi yang dapat dimanfaatkan untuk mengembangkan perangkat XR. Pengalaman dalam merancang perangkat VR untuk kebutuhan gaming bisa menjadi referensi yang relevan bagi Meta, terutama jika perusahaan ingin memperkuat kemampuan headset-nya di luar penggunaan umum.
Meski begitu, pengalihan paten tidak menjamin teknologi tersebut akan langsung digunakan dalam produk Meta berikutnya. Pemanfaatannya bergantung pada strategi pengembangan, kebutuhan teknis, dan keputusan bisnis perusahaan. Untuk saat ini, langkah tersebut lebih tepat dilihat sebagai potensi penguatan aset teknologi Meta, sekaligus perkembangan yang membuat masa depan bisnis XR menarik untuk diamati.

items.author: Amiya Johar
items.content:
Elon Musk pledged to make Starlink affordable in India as he renewed his attack on billionaire Mukesh Ambani’s (pictured) telecoms dominance, days before Jio Platforms launches a record-breaking IPO.
In a series of posts on social media platform X, the SpaceX chief argued that competition from Starlink would benefit Indian consumers by expanding connectivity options. “The reality is that competition would greatly benefit the average citizen in India by giving them more choices, as it always does,” he explained, adding, “Ambani’s profits will be lower, but he is not going out of business”.
Musk also dismissed claims that Starlink would struggle to compete with Jio’s low-cost data plans while also posing a threat to the incumbent operator. “This is absurd hypocrisy and hyperbole,” he said.
His comments come as Jio Platforms targets a valuation of around $106 billion, according to Reuters, in a planned IPO that could become India’s largest-ever listing. The business includes telecoms operation Reliance Jio, which reported 524.4 million subscribers at the end of March, including 268.5 million 5G customers.
“Prime Minister Ambani“
Musk has escalated his criticism of India’s regulatory process in recent days, accusing authorities and “certain oligarchs” of delaying Starlink’s entry into the country to maintain a “monopolistic chokehold on the Indian people”.
In a separate post on Friday (9 October), he sarcastically addressed the Jio Platforms-owner as “Prime Minister Ambani” and asked whether he would “consider allowing Starlink to compete”.
He argued satellite connectivity could bring internet access to underserved communities, improve educational opportunities and enable small businesses to reach international markets.
“Please accept my humble apologies for not realizing that you are the real boss of India,” he wrote, adding “Starlink would change their lives for the better”.
India’s Ministry of Communications has rejected allegations of discriminatory treatment, stating that Starlink and incumbents Bharti Airtel and Reliance Jio were at broadly the same stage of the regulatory process. All three have secured initial approvals but remain subject to outstanding security clearances before they can obtain spectrum access.

items.author: Fiaz Mahmood
items.content:
An anti-terrorism court (ATC) in Islamabad on Monday directed jail authorities to facilitate meetings between lawyer Imaan Mazari, her husband Hadi Ali Chattha and their legal team, which had been unable to meet them in connection with a case involving the removal of barriers.
ATC Judge Tahir Abbas Sipra issued the directions during the hearing, which was attended by former human rights minister Shireen Mazari and lawyers Riasat Ali Azad and Aimal Khan. During the proceedings, Azad argued that the case could not proceed without allowing the legal team, comprising Azad, Zainab Janjua and Aimal Khan, to meet their clients.
The judge observed that anti-terrorism law required trials to be conducted on a daily basis and asked the prosecution how many witnesses it intended to produce. The prosecutor said there were nine witnesses. The judge subsequently directed the prosecutor to ensure that the accused were given access to their lawyers.
Also Read: Barricade removal case: ATC rejects plea to drop terrorism charges against Imaan, Hadi
Chattha questioned why he and Imaan were not being brought before the court, arguing that their continued absence undermined the requirements of a fair trial. He said they had been in jail for eight months and questioned how they could defend themselves and proceed with the case under such circumstances.
He also raised concerns about the confidentiality of meetings between lawyers and their clients, pointing out that cameras had been installed in the areas where meetings were held inside the jail. “The court has to decide our fate. Please summon us to court,” Chattha said, adding that it was for the court to determine whether he and Imaan were terrorists.
The court adjourned further proceedings until October 14.
Case background
Imaan and her husband Chattha were rearrested on September 17, shortly after the Supreme Court granted them bail and suspended their sentences in a separate social-media posts case. They were produced before an Islamabad ATC in connection with a case registered at Kohsar Police Station.
Police sought 30-day physical remand, but ATC Judge Abul Hasnat Muhammad Zulqarnain rejected the request and sent the couple on judicial remand. The judge noted that although they had been nominated in the FIR as members of an unlawful assembly, no weapon had been attributed to either accused.
Read More: SC suspends trial court order, grants bail to Imaan Mazari, Hadi Ali Chattha
On September 27, the court issued a contempt notice to the Adiala jail superintendent after the authorities failed to facilitate the signing and transmission of the documents and also failed to produce the accused through video link. Two days later, the issue was resolved after Imaan and Chattha signed the required powers of attorney.
On September 29, the ATC ended the contempt proceedings against the jail authorities and separately confirmed that notices had been issued on the couple’s bail applications, with arguments scheduled before Judge Abul Hasnat.
On October 7, the ATC had framed charges against Imaan and Chattha in the case related to the alleged violation of a designated route and incitement during the arrival of an international cricket team, despite defence objections that legal requirements had not been fulfilled.

“That gives us a rare advantage to securely engineer and deploy Agentic AI at scale and deliver the business outcomes that matter most to our clients.”
HCLTech’s deal with Anthropic follows an agreement worth $1.1 billion in July with a major unnamed European company to deploy AI services and boost enterprise services for the business.

items.author: Palak Sharma
items.content:
PharmEasy parent API Holdings narrowed its consolidated net loss by 67% to ₹520 Cr in the fiscal year ended March 2026 (FY26) from ₹1,572 Cr in the previous fiscal, with its operating revenue growing 12.7% YoY to ₹6,618.5 Cr.
The company attributed the improvement to its focus on customer experience, higher-value profitable segments, capacity utilisation, increasing wallet share and leveraging digital capabilities.
In its FY26 annual report, API Holdings said it improved margins by focusing on higher-margin products, particularly its private label brands, and optimising discounts in its B2R business.
Including other income of ₹70.8 Cr, the company’s total revenue stood at ₹6,689.2 Cr for FY26. However, it continued to report a loss before tax of ₹456.1 Cr.
In the first quarter of FY27, API Holdings reported a 10% YoY increase in revenue to ₹1,754 Cr while EBITDA rose to ₹39.3 Cr. Gross margin improved to 21.4% from 19.9% in FY26, and EBITDA margin reached 2.2%. Its B2B business grew 8.2% YoY to ₹1,006 Cr revenue and turned EBITDA-positive at ₹70 lakh.
The company said that PharmEasy’s B2C business posted ₹348 Cr revenue, with EBITDA losses narrowing to ₹17 Cr. Thyrocare reported 24% YoY revenue growth to ₹240 Cr, processed 5.4 Mn patients and conducted 55.2 Mn tests.
Where Did API Holdings Spend In FY26?
API Holdings’ consolidated expenses declined marginally by 0.9% to ₹7,146.7 Cr in FY26 from ₹7,208.6 Cr in the previous fiscal year. Purchases of stock-in-trade remained its largest expense, while lower employee benefit costs contributed to the overall reduction.
Purchases Of Stock-In-Trade: The expense rose 10.9% to ₹5,244.8 Cr from ₹4,729.6 Cr, accounting for about 73% of total expenses. The increase came as the company’s operating revenue expanded during the year.
Employee Benefit Expense: Employee costs fell 47.5% to ₹476.9 Cr from ₹908.4 Cr in FY25. A substantial part of the decline came from lower employee share-based payment expenses, which dropped to ₹62 Cr from ₹482.2 Cr in FY25.
Other Expenses: This category increased 7.5% YoY to ₹656.7 Cr from ₹610.7 Cr. Major components included ₹111.8 Cr of contractual payments to delivery associates, ₹73.4 Cr of sales promotion and marketing, ₹72.6 Cr of manpower charges, and ₹63.4 Cr of legal and professional fees.
API Holdings also reported a tax expense of ₹64.2 Cr, comprising ₹68 Cr in current tax, offset by a deferred tax credit of ₹4.2 Cr, and a prior-period charge of ₹0.4 Cr.
Products Account For 86% Of Revenue
API Holdings generates revenue from the sale of products and services. Product sales contributed ₹5,670 Cr, or 85.7% of revenue, in FY26. These include pharmaceutical, over-the-counter (OTC), surgical, consumable and private label products.
The company sources products from manufacturers and wholesalers and supplies them to local chemists, large pharmacies, doctors, clinics, online retailers on the PharmEasy platform and hospitals.
A significant part of this business flows through its chemist-focused distribution operations, while Aknamed supplies hospitals. The group also generates product revenue through collection kits sold by Thyrocare.
Services contributed ₹941.3 Cr, or 14.2% of revenue, in FY26. This includes diagnostics, teleconsulting, licensing and technology services.
Thyrocare’s diagnostic operations account for a substantial part of this stream, serving franchise partners, consumers, hospitals, diagnostic companies and independent phlebotomists. API Holdings also earns service revenue from diagnostic tests sold through the PharmEasy marketplace, fulfilment services and technology platforms, including Retailio, which connects pharmaceutical wholesalers and pharmacies.
How API Holdings’ Subsidiaries Contribute
Although API Holdings has six direct subsidiaries and 18 step-down subsidiaries, four businesses account for much of its activity across B2B distribution, diagnostics and consumer healthcare.
B2B: Ascent Wellness And Pharma Solutions, Aknamed
Ascent Wellness and Pharma Solutions supplies pharmaceutical products to chemists and institutions, sourcing directly from pharmaceutical companies and enabling retailers to place orders through a platform. Aknamed supplies hospitals with pharmaceutical products, consumables and surgical products sourced from pharmaceutical companies and distributors.
Together, the B2B businesses generated ₹4,082.4 Cr in revenue in FY26, with an EBITDA loss of ₹3.6 Cr. In Q1 FY27, they recorded combined revenue of ₹1,005.6 Cr and EBITDA of ₹70 Lakh.
Diagnostics: Thyrocare Technologies
Thyrocare, API Holdings’ listed diagnostics arm, is a key contributor to the group’s profitability. In FY26, it operated 41 laboratories, offered 1,275 tests, processed about 21 Cr tests and had more than 10,800 franchisees.
Its revenue grew 24% YoY to ₹240 Cr in Q1 FY27.
B2C: PharmEasy
PharmEasy operates the group’s consumer-facing healthcare marketplace. In FY26, the segment generated ₹1,334.5 Cr in revenue and reported an EBITDA loss of ₹44.1 Cr.
In Q1 FY27, it recorded revenue of ₹347.9 Cr, alongside an EBITDA loss of ₹17 Cr.

items.author: AFP
items.content:
UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham said Monday that last month’s alleged terror plot targeting a British air base was “almost certainly” directed by Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC), as he announced fresh sanctions against two Iranian men.
However, Iran on Monday denied any involvement in an incident at Britain's RAF Fairford airbase, which has been used by the United States in its war with the Islamic republic.
"The Iranian ambassador in London, Ali Moussavi, has again categorically rejected the accusations concerning Tehran's role in the incident at the Fairford military base," state news agency IRNA reported, adding that he "called on the British government to present evidence supporting its allegations if it possesses any".
Addressing Parliament, Burnham said the UK assessment was that the alleged plot, which led to five arrests on suspicion of terror offenses, was highly likely to have been coordinated in Iran.
“I can confirm our assessment that it is highly likely to have been coordinated in Iran, almost certainly directed by Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard,” he told MPs.
“We will not tolerate these threats on our soil. We will crack down on Iran’s use of criminal networks, using our full range of powers to target them and their funding streams.
“And we will bring further sanctions to restrict the capacity of Iran and the IRGC to do us harm.”
In late September, a major security incident occurred at RAF Fairford, a Gloucestershire airbase used by the US Air Force. The incident triggered a large-scale counter-terrorism investigation.
Separately, the UK government also announced that it summoned Iran’s ambassador for ongoing "malign activity."
Read More: US removes B-1 bombers from UK base amid security concerns
“Iran’s continued attempts to undermine the security of the United Kingdom and international partners through its criminal networks, proxy groups and state-backed malign activity is unacceptable," Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband said in a statement.
"This Government will never waiver in our commitment to tacking Iran’s unacceptable actions and protecting our national security. We have already designated the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) under our new state threats powers," he added.
Britain has also imposed sanctions on two Iranian men, including an asset freeze and a ban on entering the UK.
'We stand with Saudi Arabia against the Houthis'
Burnham also addressed the escalating situation involving Saudi Arabia and the Houthis, saying he had discussed the issue with US President Donald Trump last month on the sidelines of the UN General Assembly.
“In my meeting with President Trump, we discussed the situation in the Middle East. I confirmed Britain's decision to send air defense and a Voyager aircraft to Saudi Arabia to provide air-to-air refueling support," he said.
"I can confirm today it has already completed 14 operational missions. This support is needed to protect civilians. I condemn the appalling attacks on the King Khalid International Airport. We will continue to stand with Saudi Arabia against the Houthis,” he added.
No reopening 2016 Brexit referendum
Burnham also ruled out reopening the Brexit referendum or revising his government's manifesto commitments on relations with the EU, while advocating closer cooperation with the bloc to boost economic growth and address migration.
He also said he respected the result of the 2016 referendum, in which Britain voted to leave the EU, but argued that pragmatic cooperation with European partners could serve the country's interests.
"I am not reopening the referendum. I respect the referendum result," he said.
Also Read: UK examines foreign state involvement in airbase plot
Burnham said his government would pursue opportunities to strengthen the British economy and improve cooperation to tackle migrant boat crossings in the English Channel.
"The deal that I've inherited coming into office represents an opportunity to secure progress on both of those things," he said, adding that rejecting such opportunities would be "a dereliction of duty from any member of this House," he noted.
‘It’s a conversation we must have’
Ahead of next month's UK-EU summit, Burnham called for discussions on the future relationship between Britain and the bloc, saying closer ties could help promote growth, control migration, and strengthen security.
"If we are serious about promoting growth, controlling migration, upholding our values and our security, it is a conversation we must have," he said.
However, Burnham ruled out rejoining the EU single market or customs union or restoring freedom of movement, citing commitments in Labour's 2024 general election manifesto.
Mentioning what he “can’t do” to improve growth in the UK, he said: “I also want to maintain trust in politics. And I'm afraid I'm not prepared to revisit the red lines in our manifesto.”
The manifesto pledged to keep Britain outside the EU while seeking to reset relations and deepen ties with European partners.
Conservative Party leader Kemi Badenoch accused Burnham of attempting to distract the public by raising claims of Russian interference in the 2016 referendum.
She questioned whether he considered the referendum result legitimate and called on Burnham to publish evidence if he believes Russia influenced the outcome.
"This is lazy thinking from people who don't have solutions to the real problems we face," Badenoch said.
But Burnham accused the Conservatives of being "in denial about, and not open to seeing, how we can move forward to a better position for the country."
He said public opinion in Britain has shifted in favor of a different approach to relations with the EU, while insisting that his government would respect its existing commitments.

items.author: Shraddha Goled
items.content:
“Have you ever clicked your mouse HERE? You will.”
That was the text accompanying the first banner ad on the internet, launched by telecommunications company AT&T on HotWired.com in 1994. The ad reportedly clocked a 44% click-through rate in its first four months, a figure that would be extraordinary by the standards of almost any digital marketing channel today.
Over three decades, online advertising has evolved from banner ads to search, social media, programmatic buying, influencer marketing and performance marketing.
Then, with the emergence of search engine optimisation (SEO) practices, brands started optimising websites, building backlinks, targeting keywords and creating content to improve their visibility. Over time, SEO grew into a $90 Bn industry.
But the search box is now changing again.
Today, a growing number of consumers are turning to AI assistants instead of typing keywords into Google and opening a dozen links. Whether they are looking for accounting software, a nearby restaurant or the best smartphone under ₹50,000, they can simply ask an AI assistant for recommendations.
Their interaction with AI is no longer limited to a query or a list of results. Users/consumers ask follow-up questions, compare options, refine their requirements, and direct AI to recommend what they should buy.
This is where answer engine optimisation (AEO) and generative engine optimisation (GEO) have emerged as a new trend. But there is no single platform to optimise for, no standard ranking system and no clear way to measure success.
Much like what the SEO function was in its early days, marketers are still figuring out what works. Agencies are experimenting with how brands appear in answers generated by ChatGPT, Gemini, Perplexity and Google’s AI-powered search products. They are tracking brand mentions, citations and recommendations, while trying to understand why one company gets surfaced over another.
But as brands scramble to show up in AI-generated answers, a bigger question is emerging: How can they ensure they are not just recommended by AI, but show up at the right moment?
The Missing Link In AI Marketing
Currently, for brands, the challenge is not how to appear in AI answers but figure out whether that visibility brings more visitors, customers or sales.
Google historically gave marketers detailed visibility through tools such as Search Console and keyword-level paid search data. This model is considerably harder to replicate when consumers interact with AI through multi-step conversations.
AI platforms currently offer limited visibility into the prompts driving discovery. A user may start with a broad question, ask several follow-ups, compare products, and only then arrive at a purchase decision. For marketers, identifying which interaction influenced that journey is harder than attributing a click to a specific search query.
Organic visibility is also inconsistent across platforms such as ChatGPT, Claude and Perplexity. For queries around the “best” or “top” products and services, AI models may rely heavily on third-party publishers, reviews and user-generated content rather than brand websites.
As a result, brands need to build a consistent information ecosystem across websites, ads, influencers and third-party platforms.
“So, eventually, for optimising, it becomes a lot more important to produce content in the broader ecosystem. We often ask brands to be consistent with their communication,” said Rishabh Mahendru, senior vice president of client success and growth at AdLift.
Marketers are also grappling with how much control they have over their brands’ visibility in AI-driven discovery. AI platforms can answer users’ questions without sending them to an external website. These zero-click answers may be convenient for consumers, but they can reduce traffic to publisher and brand websites.
Even when AI search leads to a sale, tracing that purchase back to a specific interaction can be difficult. A consumer may discover a brand through an AI assistant, research it elsewhere and make a purchase days later. Traditional last-click attribution models may fail to capture the role AI played in that journey.
There is also less certainty around where and how brands appear. AI platforms determine which ads match a user’s intent, while changes in how models cite sources can make organic visibility unpredictable. Brands also risk appearing alongside misinformation, hate speech or polarising content in AI-generated responses. To address these, OpenAI is exploring geo-based ad experiments and brand-suitability pilots to give advertisers more insight into where their ads appear and how they perform.
Overall, with its ChatGPT Ads in India, OpenAI is bringing sponsored messages into conversations on the AI chatbot in one of its largest markets. Ads have been rolled out to users on Free and Go tiers, while Plus, Pro, Business, Enterprise and Education users get an ad-free experience. More than 50 brands were planned to go live during the initial rollout, with WPP and Omnicom as OpenAI’s first agency partners in India. Businesses can access ChatGPT’s self-serve Ads Manager, with daily budgets starting at ₹725.
The Next Frontier Of Brand Visibility
With no standard way to measure AI search visibility or predict which brands will surface in AI-generated answers, startups are building tools to help businesses navigate the new landscape.
Antler-incubated RankinLLM, for instance, is building a GEO and AI search visibility platform. “We operate across three layers: an observability layer to track LLM activity, an intelligence layer to extract meaningful signals from noisy data, and an optimisation layer to fix identified gaps. Optimiser agents create a closed loop, while KPIs such as brand mentions, share of voice, citations and sentiment measure the impact,” said cofounder and CEO Kartik Sharma.
Bengaluru-based TruCommerce has taken a different approach. It initially built a tool to track how often brands appeared in AI-generated answers. But it found that much of the traffic coming from AI platforms was being wrongly counted as direct website visits. This led the startup to shift its focus to helping brands sell directly through AI platforms.
TruCommerce now connects brands’ product catalogues and inventory with AI assistants. This helps businesses track visitors coming from AI, make product information easier for AI tools to understand, and enable customers to buy products without leaving the conversation.
Meanwhile, Lightspeed-backed Gushwork helps small and medium-sized businesses attract potential customers through traditional search engines and AI tools. Its AI agents create content designed to appear in search results, while its platform tracks the enquiries this content generates.
Other startups, including Nexad, Parsnip and AdCreative AI, are also building tools to help brands advertise and improve their visibility across AI platforms.
For marketers, however, this shift is still in its early stages. Traditional SEO took decades to develop its tools, metrics and best practices. AI is at the same crossroads.

items.author: Anne Florentyna
items.content:
India’s deeptech startups raised substantially more capital in Q3 2026, even as the number of deals edged lower.
As per Inc42’s ‘Indian Tech Startup Funding Report, Q3 2026’, deeptech startups raised $290 Mn across 28 deals, compared with $105 Mn across 29 deals in Q3 2025. The 176% YoY increase outpaced the broader startup ecosystem, where funding grew 5% to $2.2 Bn.
For context, deeptech startups are the ones that develop advanced technologies and hardware and include innovations across sub-segments like spacetech, robotics, defence technology and semiconductors.
Large Spacetech Rounds Drive Deeptech Funding Surge
The sharp rise in funding, despite a marginal decline in deal count, points to a concentration of capital in a smaller pool of startups.
In this, large spacetech rounds accounted for a significant share of the funding deployed during the quarter, with the startups in the sector netting $130 Mn, accounting for about 45% of deeptech funding in Q3. Six-year-old spacetech startup Pixxel’s $100 Mn round was one of four mega funding rounds recorded during the quarter. The round accounted for over three-fourths of the segment’s total.
Sustaining this momentum will require capital to reach beyond a select group of companies. As per a recent report by the Indian Venture and Alternate Capital Association (IVCA), deeptech startups continue to face a funding gap at the Series B and C stages, with few funds equipped to write the larger cheques needed to take technologies from development to commercial scale.
IVCA President Rajat Tandon said bridging this gap, deepening domestic limited partner participation, and improving exit pathways will be critical to building globally competitive deeptech companies.
“India’s deeptech opportunity is moving from promise to more investible commitments, with an increasingly institutionalised ecosystem play. The growth in capital flowing into deeptech over the past decade reflects the confidence investors have in India’s scientific and technological capabilities. However, taking deeptech startups and entrepreneurs from the laboratory to global scale will require capital that is patient, appropriately structured, and available across the entire growth journey,” he said.
Government Push Adds To Deeptech Funding Momentum
Bharat Innovation Fund cofounder and partner Ashwin Raguraman attributed some of the recent momentum to the government’s ₹1 Lakh Cr Research, Development and Innovation (RDI) Fund and its wider push to support technology-led businesses.
“I attribute (growth in deeptech funding) this quarter and maybe even last quarter predominantly due to the announcement on the government’s deeptech-focused ₹1 Lakh Cr RDI Fund and a fairly solid government push, which is making capital available to VC funds,” Raguraman told Inc42.
The RDI Fund aims to catalyse private investment in research-intensive businesses. Its framework includes eligibility requirements for R&D-intensive technologies at technology readiness level (TRL) 4 or above, indicating that they have progressed beyond basic laboratory validation.
New investment vehicles also emerged during the quarter. Asiana Fund and JC Capital jointly launched a ₹1,000 Cr deeptech fund, while Transition VC and Accel launched funds to back technology-led businesses.
Access Free Report
RDI Fund Faces Questions Over Governance
However, the extent to which the RDI Fund has influenced investor sentiment remains uncertain. In August, The Indian Express reported that nearly two-thirds of the more than ₹2,000 Cr allocated to deeptech companies under the scheme had gone to firms with links to members of the panel involved in selecting beneficiaries, raising concerns over potential conflicts of interest.
Inc42’s Q3 2026 Indian Investor Ranking & Sentiment Survey, which covered 85 institutional investors, found that 52% considered disclosure and recusal safeguards adequate but said visibility remained limited.
Another 25% viewed the issue as a governance failure requiring independent oversight, while 14% said such investment ties could be managed through disclosure and recusal. The remaining 9% said it was not a concern, arguing that the focus should remain on company selection.
The findings suggest that the availability of government-backed capital is only part of the equation. Transparency in its allocation and the availability of patient capital across funding stages will also shape the sector’s ability to turn promising technologies into globally competitive businesses.
