items.author: AFP
items.content:
The campaign of Brazilian President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva accused tech giant Meta of election interference on Saturday after his social media content was allegedly blocked on the company's platforms.
The leftist leader is seeking a fourth non-consecutive term in the October 25 runoff, where he will face Senator Flavio Bolsonaro, the son of far-right former president Jair Bolsonaro.
In a statement, Lula's campaign reported instances where platforms owned by Meta -- the parent company of Facebook, WhatsApp, and Instagram -- allegedly restricted the distribution of his content.
The campaign claimed that in recent days, Meta "prevented President Lula's profile from promoting Instagram feed posts," while a post from his official account "experienced an interruption in view counts, which affected its reach."
It also said that prior to last Sunday's first round of voting -- in which Flavio Bolsonaro finished first -- the profiles of Lula and other leftist leaders "suddenly disappeared from Instagram's search function."
"The series of technical issues... raises strong suspicions that Meta's actions constitute an attempt to interfere in the Brazilian electoral process to the benefit of Flavio Bolsonaro's candidacy," the statement added.
Brazil's Superior Electoral Court (TSE) on Saturday gave the social media giant 48 hours to clarify whether it reduced the reach of posts by Lula's campaign and to explain the irregularities reported.
Read More: Bill Gates warns cyberattacks most imminent AI threat
Meta was ordered to "report, profile by profile, all the measures applied" to "Lula's official accounts" and to "explain the anomalies in the metrics" of the videos, the TSE said.
Meta's Brazil office denied the charges, calling them "simply false" and "not supported by the facts."
"Many of the technical issues mentioned did not affect only Brazil or specific accounts," Meta told AFP in an email.
"We comply with electoral regulations and are committed to a level playing field regarding the use of our platforms."
Lula's campaign has filed a complaint with the electoral court over the alleged social media blocks.
Following the first round of voting, Lula -- who does not use a mobile phone -- launched a social media push that includes videos of him addressing his online followers.

items.title: Bill Gates warns cyberattacks most imminent AI threat
items.summary:
Bill Gates on Sunday warned that unregulated artificial intelligence poses a growing threat and predicted an escalation in AI-powered cyberattacks in the coming year.
The Microsoft co-founder said the risk of AI "getting out of control" remained years away and emphasized that the immediate concern was "bad people" using existing systems without safeguards.
"The front that we'll probably see most dramatically in the next year is cyberattacks," Gates said in an interview with ABC News.
"The real danger right now is not the AI's getting out of control. We need to work on that, but that's years away in terms of the big impact that might have," he said.
"It's really bad people using AI, particularly in AI where you can take out all the safeguards," he said, adding that increased restrictions were needed to prevent bad actors using AI for bioterrorism and cyberattacks.
Read More: Anthropic discloses fake tip to police among new rogue AI
items.author: Reuters
items.content:
Bill Gates on Sunday warned that unregulated artificial intelligence poses a growing threat and predicted an escalation in AI-powered cyberattacks in the coming year.
The Microsoft co-founder said the risk of AI "getting out of control" remained years away and emphasized that the immediate concern was "bad people" using existing systems without safeguards.
"The front that we'll probably see most dramatically in the next year is cyberattacks," Gates said in an interview with ABC News.
"The real danger right now is not the AI's getting out of control. We need to work on that, but that's years away in terms of the big impact that might have," he said.
"It's really bad people using AI, particularly in AI where you can take out all the safeguards," he said, adding that increased restrictions were needed to prevent bad actors using AI for bioterrorism and cyberattacks.
Read More: Anthropic discloses fake tip to police among new rogue AI incidents
"But right now, you're allowed to take all those safeguards out. So when you have bad people, no safeguards, and then the latest models, that's where, over the next year, primarily in the cyber area, we are going to have a lot of negative surprises," he told ABC.
Gates -- who warned in a lengthy August post that the world was dangerously unprepared for the upheaval brought by AI, especially to employment -- is the latest tech magnate to sound the alarm on the threats posed by the new technology.
In his interview Sunday, he dismissed the idea -- advocated by US President Donald Trump -- that self-regulation by AI companies was sufficient to keep the world safe.
"The idea that for the most dangerous technology humans ever invented, that that's the final word, that just the companies themselves are the only check that society has...it's clear we're not doing enough," Gates said.

items.author: Web Desk
items.content:
Jamiat Ulema-e-Islam-Fazl (JUI-F) chief Maulana Fazlur Rehman on Sunday accused the government of backing out of negotiations with the Pakistan Tehreek-i-Insaf (PTI) and the opposition despite initially agreeing to their demands, and categorically rejected the imposition of governor’s rule or an emergency in Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa (K-P).
Speaking to the media, Fazl said his party rejected the government’s decision to impose an emergency or governor’s rule in the province, describing it as an attack on democracy and the rights of the people.
“This is an assault on democracy and the rights of the people,” he said, adding that the JUI-F would use all democratic avenues to oppose the move, including taking the matter to the public, parliament and the courts.
Read: Emergency, governor's rule imposed in K-P after president signs summary on PM Shehbaz's advice
Explaining the sequence of events, Fazl said he had returned to Pakistan on Oct 7 after performing Umrah and met a PTI delegation the same day. The party had expressed a desire for him to play a role in resolving the crisis, he added.
He said he had conveyed to the PTI delegation his view that the government had left no room for negotiations. Despite this, he met a government delegation the following day, which also asked him to play a mediatory role.
Following his involvement, Fazl said, the PTI confined its long march to K-P and suspended its plan to move towards Islamabad, while making no major announcement. The government, meanwhile, postponed its plan to impose governor’s rule, which, according to his information, had been scheduled to be announced on that day.
“Since steps towards the long march were postponed on one side and the decision to impose an emergency was deferred on the other, we thought both sides were serious about reaching an understanding,” he said.
Fazl said Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif subsequently invited him to dinner, an offer he accepted after consultations within his party. However, he added, the positions of the two sides became clear during the meeting.
“The government’s position was that the long march should first be called off, while the PTI demanded that it be allowed to meet Imran Khan and that Khan sahib be taken to a hospital for treatment in accordance with court orders,” he said.
Fazl said he asked both sides whether they agreed to these demands and suggested that they avoid arguing over which side should act first. If both agreed to the demands, he said, they could then decide whether he should assume the role of negotiator.
He said he first contacteDPM d the PTI leadership and held a conference call attended by K-P Chief Minister Sohail Afridi and party chairman Gohar Ali Khan along others. He asked the PTI whether it was willing to call off the long march, to which the party responded that it would be prepared to do so if its demands were accepted.
Fazl said he met the prime minister on Sunday, who agreed to accept the PTI’s demands. Both sides had agreed to reach a decision before a Cabinet meeting scheduled for the morning, with the possibility of postponing the meeting until the evening if necessary, he added.
According to Fazl, the prime minister called him at 9:30am and said he would present the proposals he had made before the Cabinet. Fazl said he initially took this as a positive indication that the prime minister wanted to take the Cabinet into confidence.
However, about an hour later, Deputy Prime Minister (DPM) and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar called him and informed him that the Cabinet had decided to impose governor’s rule.
“At 10:30am, DPM Dar called and said the Cabinet was leaning towards imposing governor’s rule and an emergency,” Fazl said. “I asked him on what grounds an emergency or governor’s rule could be imposed in K-P and told him to explain the reasons.”
He said DPM Dar cited the provincial government’s ineffectiveness in the fight against terrorism as the reason for the proposed action.
“I asked him whether the Balochistan government had not failed in dealing with terrorism, and why an emergency was not needed there but was needed here,” Fazl said.
The JUI-F chief accused the government of reneging on its commitments despite agreeing to the proposals.
“I am a witness to the fact that the government backed out after agreeing to the demands,” he said, asking why it had broken its commitment.
Fazl rejected the use of the fight against terrorism as a justification for imposing an emergency and criticised the role of the Pakistan Peoples Party (PPP), a coalition partner in the federal government.
He said it was the third or fourth time that the PPP, which presented itself as a champion of democracy, had been in government when an elected provincial administration faced what he described as an assault on democracy or an emergency.
“Whenever a provincial government has been subjected to an assault, or an emergency has been imposed, it has happened when the PPP is in government and Asif Ali Zardari is president,” he said.
Discussing military operations, Fazl blamed what he called flawed policies pursued from the era of former military ruler Gen (r) Pervez Musharraf to the present for the country’s deteriorating security situation. Repeated military operations had failed to produce results, he said, describing this as a failure of policy.
He said he had been asked to support a military operation in the region and had no objection to doing so, but demanded an account of the outcomes of operations conducted between 2010 and the present.
Pointing to the deteriorating security situation in K-P, Fazl said people could no longer move freely in Dera Ismail Khan and police were unable to remain safely inside their stations.
“Police stations are emptied, and police personnel spend the night in houses in neighbourhoods rather than staying at their stations,” he said.
He questioned why the government wanted to focus only on terrorists while refusing to discuss its own failures and flawed policies.
“Will we discuss only the terrorists and not your failures? Will we not discuss your flawed strategy?” he asked.
Fazl said that if an emergency had to be imposed, it should be imposed on the federal government, which he described as illegitimate.
Reiterating his opposition to the decision, the JUI-F chief said his party would challenge the move through parliamentary and judicial forums.
“We categorically reject the decision to impose an emergency and will use parliament and the courts to oppose it,” he said.

items.author: Onsa Mustafa
items.content:
Copyright protected content copied from PhoneWorld website.
WhatsApp is introducing a new security alert that requires users to update their device’s operating system before they can log in to the messaging app. The change applies to both Android and iOS devices and aims to improve account security by encouraging users to install the latest available software updates.
According to WABetaInfo, WhatsApp displays an alert when users try to access the app from a device running an outdated operating system. The alert instructs them to open their device settings and install the latest available update before continuing.
Users cannot skip this requirement, meaning they must update their device software to regain access to WhatsApp if the app blocks their login.
WhatsApp Introduces New Security Alert for Android and iPhone Users
The new requirement works through a server-side update. This means users do not need to install a new version of WhatsApp to receive the alert. Instead, the change comes from WhatsApp’s servers and applies to supported Android and iOS devices.
WhatsApp has not yet specified which operating system versions will trigger the login restriction. The rollout may also take time to reach all users.
The new measure highlights the importance of keeping smartphones updated. Operating system updates often include security patches that fix vulnerabilities and protect devices against potential attacks.
Why WhatsApp Wants Users to Update Their Devices
Outdated operating systems can expose devices to known security vulnerabilities. Cybercriminals may exploit these weaknesses to install malicious software, access sensitive information, or intercept data stored on affected devices.
Although WhatsApp offers security features to protect conversations and accounts, the overall security of the app also depends on the device it runs on.
By requiring users to install available operating system updates, WhatsApp aims to reduce risks associated with outdated software. The alert also helps users understand why keeping their devices updated is important for digital security.
WhatsApp Is Also Working on Other New Features
Alongside the security change, WhatsApp is developing and rolling out several other features for Android, iOS, iPad, and Mac.
On iOS, WhatsApp is introducing a refreshed video player with Apple’s Liquid Glass design. The updated interface features a translucent progress bar with rounded corners and a redesigned control bar. The new design is also reaching the iPad and Mac versions of the app.
WhatsApp is also testing a dedicated Contacts tab for Android. It will provide a central place to view contacts, identify people who are online, check birthday reminders, and invite new users. The feature will also let users sort contacts by activity or alphabetically, while respecting their existing privacy settings.
Another improvement allows Android users to play WhatsApp Status updates at double speed. Users can activate 2x playback by pressing and holding the right side of the screen. The faster playback remains active only while they hold the screen.
Meanwhile, WhatsApp is testing a redesigned navigation experience for iOS chats. The new interface adds a shortcut to access useful conversation options without opening the chat information screen.
The company is also testing a redesigned Settings interface on iOS. The proposed layout separates frequently used options from other settings, making it easier for users to find features related to privacy, notifications, storage, linked devices, and parental controls.
What Users Should Do
WhatsApp users should regularly check their smartphone settings for available operating system updates. Installing these updates can help protect their devices from known security threats and maintain compatibility with apps.
For now, WhatsApp has not confirmed the exact operating system versions that will trigger the new login restriction. Users who receive the alert should follow its instructions and install the latest update available for their device.

items.author: Ahtesham Bashir
items.content:
Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf’s (PTI) long march effectively fizzled out in Swabi on Sunday amid heightened security arrangements following the imposition of an emergency and Governor’s rule in K-P.
Police were deployed at key locations across the district to prevent possible protests and restrict the movement of the long march caravan led by former chief minister Sohail Afridi. Mobile phone networks and PTCL internet services remained suspended across Swabi, causing inconvenience to residents and disrupting routine communications.
Read More: PTI rejects emergency, governor's rule in K-P as unconstitutional, vows to continue struggle
According to sources, the PTI caravan was expected to reach Swabi on the night of October 11. However, the party’s local leadership remained largely absent, and no significant protest activity was reported anywhere in the district on Monday.
Heavy police contingents were stationed at important locations, including Aman Chowk in Swabi, Topi, Swabi Interchange and Shiwa Adda in Razaar tehsil. In view of security concerns, containers were also brought to Swabi Interchange, Jahangira Bridge and the Indus River bridge on the M-1 Motorway.
Despite these arrangements, the Peshawar-Islamabad Motorway and the Grand Trunk Road remained open to traffic.
Police sources said raids were conducted at several locations in Shiwa Adda and adjoining areas following reports of the expected arrival of the long march. The action was aimed at arresting PTI workers, but no arrests were reported.
Sources said PTI leaders had directed party workers to assemble at the Razaar Sports Complex to make arrangements for the march, prompting police to step up security and surveillance.
Some PTI workers and youth wing members gathered at Shiwa Adda ground and Ismaila Interchange in preparation for the march. However, police dispersed some of the workers, and the anticipated mobilisation failed to materialise.
Following the imposition of the emergency, the situation at Aman Chowk remained completely normal, with traffic moving smoothly and businesses operating as usual.
Police said security measures had been put in place to deal with any eventuality. With no major demonstration reported and the party’s local leadership largely absent, the long march showed little sign of proceeding through Swabi as anticipated.
Police vow action against rioters, violence
Meanwhile, K-P Police resolved to deal firmly with protest demonstrations, warning that those involved in rioting, vandalism or disrupting law and order would face the full force of the law.
Authorities made clear that no damage to government installations, buildings or public property would be tolerated during any protest or disturbance. The public had been advised to stay away from illegal gatherings, violent activities or any form of provocation. Failure to do so would result in the strictest legal action.
Police said they would take action against anyone who threatened peace, attacked security forces or buildings, or endangered citizens’ lives and property. Citizens had been urged to remain peaceful, respect the law and avoid being misled by troublemakers.
Special security arrangements were being put in place to protect police stations, government buildings, banks, petrol pumps, commercial centres and major highways. All protest activities and police responses would be video-recorded to support any subsequent legal proceedings.
To ensure an effective response, the police would maintain close coordination with the district administration and other relevant agencies. Officials emphasised that while peaceful expression of views was a right, violence and lawlessness would not be allowed under any circumstances.
Peshawar cantonment sealed
Even before the formal imposition of emergency and governor’s rule in K-P, authorities sealed the Cantonment area of Peshawar, bringing commercial activity and traffic to a standstill.
Saddar Bazaar and other commercial centres inside the Cantonment remained closed. Containers were placed at key points to seal all access routes into the area. Roads leading to the Provincial Assembly, Mall Road, Khyber Road and the High Court were also blocked. Containers had been brought into the city overnight and positioned at Firdous Chowk, Assembly Chowk, University Road, Pajagi Road, Kohat Road and other approaches to Saddar.
The sealing of Cantonment roads also forced the closure of markets in Saddar Bazaar. Traffic movement was suspended, leaving residents facing significant difficulties in daily movement.
Read: Emergency, governor's rule imposed in K-P after president signs summary on PM Shehbaz's advice
A heavy police contingent was deployed on routes leading to Saddar to handle any protests against the emergency decision. TransPeshawar suspended the Bus Rapid Transit (BRT) service indefinitely due to the situation, keeping all BRT stations closed and causing hardship for citizens dependent on public transport.

items.content:
Copyright protected content copied from PhoneWorld website.
The Islamabad Chamber of Commerce and Industry (ICCI) and the National Cyber Crime Investigation Agency (NCCIA) have agreed to strengthen cooperation to address the issues related to cybercrime faced by the business community and improve digital security awareness among traders and entrepreneurs.
Both institutions also decided to establish a joint coordination committee, set up a dedicated cybercrime committee at the ICCI, and organize special awareness sessions to help businesses understand cyber threats and adopt preventive measures.
The decisions came during a meeting at the ICCI House between NCCIA Additional Director Muhammad Shoaib Khan and ICCI President Muhammad Zakria Akbar Zia. Senior Vice President Muhammad Ashfaq Hussain Chattha and Vice President Muhammad Waqas Khan also attended the meeting.
ICCI and NCCIA Agree to Strengthen Cooperation Against Cybercrime
During the meeting, the NCCIA representative reviewed the concerns of the business community regarding cybercrime and assured participants of the agency’s full cooperation in addressing their issues.
The two sides agreed to form a joint coordination committee comprising representatives from both institutions. The committee will improve communication, develop a coordinated strategy to address business-related concerns, and help ensure the timely resolution of complaints.
The institutions also agreed to arrange special awareness sessions for traders and business owners. These sessions will focus on emerging cyber threats, digital security, and practical steps businesses can take to protect their data, financial transactions, and online activities.
ICCI President Muhammad Zakria Akbar Zia said protecting the business community from growing cyber threats remains a top priority. He stressed that stronger cooperation between the chamber and the NCCIA has become essential as businesses increasingly rely on digital platforms for communication, financial transactions, and commercial activities.
Moreover, he said preventing cybercrime and improving digital protection are necessary to build confidence in the digital economy. He also announced that the ICCI would establish a dedicated cybercrime committee, similar to its other specialized committees.
The proposed committee will identify cybercrime-related problems faced by businesses, coordinate with the NCCIA, and help affected chamber members find practical solutions.
ICCI Senior Vice President Muhammad Ashfaq Hussain Chattha and Vice President Muhammad Waqas Khan also highlighted the challenges businesses face because of cybercrime. They assured the NCCIA of the chamber’s full support and emphasized the importance of regular communication between the two institutions.
They said stronger institutional coordination and greater digital security awareness among traders would help prevent cybercrime and improve the business community’s ability to respond to emerging online threats.
See Also: NCCIA Recovers Rs300,000 in Online Fraud Case in Peshawar and Returns Money to Citizen
ICCI Executive Member Abrar ul Haq also briefed the NCCIA Additional Director on specific concerns affecting the Islamabad Computer Association, Islamabad Mobile Association, and Islamabad Realtors Association. He emphasized the need for a coordinated mechanism to address the distinct challenges faced by businesses in different sectors.
Other ICCI executive members and representatives attended the meeting, including Israr Mashwani, Syed Imran Bukhari, Chaudhry Mazhar, Malik Rashid Tufail, Shoaib Arshad Malik, and Shahid Abbasi, along with other chamber members.
Participants expressed confidence that the joint coordination committee, the proposed cybercrime committee, and the planned awareness sessions would strengthen cooperation between the two institutions. They said these initiatives would help Islamabad’s business community address cybercrime-related concerns and conduct commercial activities with greater digital security and confidence.

items.author: Reuters
items.content:
US President Donald Trump said on Sunday that Ukraine and Russia had agreed to what he described as an "energy ceasefire", hours after Ukrainian leader Volodymyr Zelenskiy had pushed back against US pressure for a unilateral end to strikes on Russian refineries.
In a social media post, Trump said the energy ceasefire would take effect immediately, but did not elaborate further.
In an interview with Axios, Zelenskiy said Trump's post was the first he had heard of the deal, though a senior Ukrainian official told Reuters that Ukraine was ready to agree to such a ceasefire if Russia was.
Trump, whose war in Iran has been blamed for high diesel prices that are weighing on Republicans' prospects at next month's midterm elections, had previously announced an energy ceasefire in Ukraine in mid-September, though neither side ever confirmed such an agreement was reached.
"Effective immediately, there is an ENERGY CEASEFIRE in the War between Russia and Ukraine. Both parties have agreed. Do not break it!" Trump wrote on Truth Social.
Earlier on Sunday, Zelenskiy had repeated Ukraine's long-standing position that it was willing to halt attacks on Russian refineries but only if Moscow ceased its own strikes on Ukrainian power infrastructure.
Any such deal would need to come with "real guarantees", Zelenskiy said.
"The real cause of the war in Europe is Russia and Russia alone," Zelenskiy said. "It's possible to stop strikes on energy infrastructure as early as today, but Putin does not want to do so."
Promise of elections
In a dramatic deterioration in their relations, Trump on Saturday had warned Zelenskiy that he had "better damn well stop" attacking Russian refineries, and had urged Ukrainians to replace him as their leader via new elections because he had missed several opportunities to strike a deal with Moscow.
Read More: Trump says ‘it’s time for Ukraine to get a new president’ who can ‘make a deal’ with Russia
Appearing on ABC's "This Week" on Sunday, Zelenskiy responded that he would organise elections in Ukraine if Russian President Vladimir Putin agreed to a 60-day ceasefire.
Zelenskiy said it was "up to Ukrainians" to choose their leader, but noted that there needed to be an end to the fighting first. Ukrainian law prohibits elections under martial law for security reasons.
"Please tell Putin, give us two months, 60 days of total ceasefire, 60 days, and we will organise elections," Zelenskiy said.
The Ukrainian leader rejected being blamed for energy price rises, adding that "everybody in the world" knew that the war in the Middle East was a bigger factor.
The steep rise in global diesel prices, which followed the outbreak of the Iran war in February, has become a political liability for Trump's Republican Party ahead of the midterms, when opposition Democrats could gain control of one or both houses of Congress.
On Saturday, Zelenskiy had responded angrily to Trump's announcement of a diesel supply deal with Russia, saying it would embolden Moscow's attacks on Ukraine and lead to a greater loss of civilian lives.
I just spoke with @MarkJCarney, @alexstubb, and @SecGenNATO Mark Rutte. We discussed the energy ceasefire announced by President Trump. Ukraine supports the ceasefire, and it is important that Russia support it as well. We are awaiting details from the American side. For our…
— Volodymyr Zelenskyy / Володимир Зеленський (@ZelenskyyUa) October 11, 2026
Analysts said Trump's diesel supply agreement with Moscow was unlikely to lead to sustained lower fuel prices as the volumes involved were too small.
The diesel deal was also criticised by US lawmakers, including one of Trump's fellow Republicans, Representative Don Bacon, who said it was time to apply more sanctions, not lift them.
Kyiv residents angry
On the streets of Kyiv, several residents expressed anger at Trump's suggestion that Ukraine should find a new leader willing to make a deal with Russian President Vladimir Putin.
"No one has the right to tell us what to do, especially since elections cannot be held during wartime," said Sabina, a 40-year-old primary school teacher. "In my view, it is a betrayal by our partners," she said, describing Trump's remarks.
Zelenskiy said he would continue discussions with European leaders on Sunday, and there were daily conversations around additional air defence packages, including ammunition for combat aircraft that are used to down Russia's jet-powered drones.
On Monday, Ukrainian Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha is due to participate in a European Union Foreign Affairs Council meeting that is expected to discuss increasing sanctions pressure on Russia and advancing negotiations on Ukraine’s EU accession.

items.author: SHAHID HAMEED
items.content:
Governor’s rule has been imposed in Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa (K-P) for the fourth time, transferring powers once again from the provincial government to the Governor.
The first imposition came in 1975 under the central government of Zulfikar Ali Bhutto. An emergency was declared after Hayat Muhammad Khan Sherpao was assassinated in a bomb blast while addressing a gathering at the Department of History of Peshawar University. The National Awami Party (NAP) was banned and arrests were made as the province came under Governor’s rule.
The second instance occurred in 1994 when Benazir Bhutto’s federal government moved against the Muslim League administration of Pir Sabir Shah. Assembly members were made to disappear, a no-confidence motion was brought against Chief Minister Pir Sabir Shah, and Aftab Ahmad Khan Sherpao subsequently formed the government.
The third imposition followed the 1999 counter-coup by then-army chief Pervez Musharraf against the Nawaz Sharif government. Muslim League Governor Mian Gul Aurangzeb was removed and replaced by Lieutenant General (retd) Muhammad Shafiq.
He was later succeeded by Lieutenant General (retd) Syed Iftikhar Hussain, who administered the province with his own cabinet until the formation of the Muttahida Majlis-e-Amal (MMA) government in November-December 2002.
Read More: Emergency, governor's rule imposed in K-P after president signs summary on PM Shehbaz's advice
Now, for the fourth time, the Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf government of Sohail Afridi has been suspended and Governor’s rule imposed. Governor Faisal Karim Kundi will run the province with an interim cabinet.
This latest imposition is unique in that emergency has simultaneously been declared in 12 districts of the province under Article 232 of the Constitution of Pakistan. The districts include the eight merged tribal districts (former tribal agencies), Khyber, Mohmand, Kurram, Orakzai, Bajaur, North Waziristan, South Waziristan Upper and South Waziristan Lower, along with the southern districts of Dera Ismail Khan, Tank, Bannu and Lakki Marwat.
The emergency applies fully in the Bannu and Dera Ismail Khan divisions and partially in the Peshawar, Kohat and Malakand divisions. The Hazara and Mardan divisions remain exempt.
The disruption of internet services caused widespread confusion across the province.

items.author: Onsa Mustafa
items.content:
Copyright protected content copied from PhoneWorld website.
A well-known Grand Theft Auto (GTA) 6 leaker has threatened to release a full playable version of the highly anticipated game, claiming that players could experience the entire story mode from beginning to end. However, the authenticity of the claim remains uncertain.
The leaker, known online as “cybeleek,” made the announcement on a website. According to the post, the alleged build includes the complete story mode and allows players to finish the game and reach the end credits.
GTA 6 Leaker Threatens to Release Full Playable Version of the Game
The threat has attracted attention because GTA 6 remains one of the most anticipated video games, with Rockstar Games keeping most details about its story and gameplay under wraps.
GTA 6 Leaker Sets a $30 Million Condition
According to the leaker’s website, the alleged playable build will become available if a cryptocurrency linked to the leaker reaches a market capitalization of $30 million.
The post also demands that Take-Two Interactive, the parent company of Rockstar Games, apologize for not releasing a physical version of GTA 6 and make the game available in physical format. However, the leaker has not provided a deadline for these demands.
It remains unclear whether the leaker actually possesses a complete playable build or is using the claim to attract attention to the cryptocurrency project.
Previous GTA 6 Gameplay Leaks Raise Questions
The latest threat follows several earlier leaks attributed to cybeleek. The leaker has reportedly shared more than an hour of GTA 6 footage online, including a video containing around 25 minutes of gameplay.
Some of the leaked footage also appears to contain modified character models and scenes. These details have raised questions about the source and condition of the material.
Many online observers believe the footage may come from an older development build rather than the latest version of the game. If that is the case, the alleged playable version might not represent the final product planned for release.
The possibility of a complete game leak remains unverified. The leaker has not provided enough publicly confirmed evidence to establish that the build exists in the claimed form.
Players should also avoid visiting suspicious websites claiming to host leaked game files, as such pages may contain malware or attempt to steal personal information.
See Also: Delayed Again? GTA 6 Online Could Take Years to Arrive After the Game’s Launch
GTA 6 Release Date Remains November 19, 2026
Rockstar Games currently plans to release Grand Theft Auto 6 on November 19, 2026. The game is scheduled to arrive on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S.
With the release date approaching, any genuine leak of the full game could have significant consequences for Rockstar Games and its publisher, Take-Two Interactive. However, there is currently no confirmed evidence that the alleged build will be released.
For now, the threat should be treated with caution. Until the leaker provides verifiable proof, it remains uncertain whether the claim represents a genuine leak or simply another attempt to gain attention before the game’s launch.

items.content:
Nepali authorities urged villagers on Sunday to move to safer places after ​a flood in a river in the central part of the ‌country swept away several houses and infrastructure, but there were no reports of any casualties.

The Budhi Gandaki is ​a tributary of the Trishuli River, downstream from another tributary where a glacier collapse caused a catastrophic flood in August that killed 1,457 people, with thousands still missing.
"We have asked ​villagers living along the river banks downstream to evacuate and remain safe," ​said Dharmendra Kumar Mishra, the Gorkha district's most senior bureaucrat.
Read More: Resilience in the age of climate breakdown
The flood swept away about a ‌dozen ⁠houses and two suspension bridges and damaged a hydroelectric project camp, carrying some of the construction equipment away, the National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Authority said.
The flooded river carrying muddy sludge was rising and had washed away a highway bridge ​connecting Gorkha with the ​neighbouring Dhading district, ⁠said Dharam Raj Uprety, chief of the Authority.
National disaster authorities alerted people living along the river in the Gorkha, ​Tanahun, Chitwan, East Nawalparasi and West Nawalparasi districts about ​the flood.
"Please ⁠help ensure that people in at-risk areas are moved to safe locations in time and assist search and rescue operations as needed," the National Disaster Risk Reduction ⁠and ​Management Authority said in a social media post.
Officials ​said army and police rescue personnel had reached the area and were also monitoring the situation ​from a helicopter.

items.author: Sports Desk
items.content:
Pakistan on Sunday took 2-0 unassailable lead in the three-match T20I series when they whipped Sri Lanka by 82 runs in their second show at the Pindi Stadium in Rawalpindi.
Pakistan rode on superb batting display from Maaz Sadaqat (96) and skipper Sahibzada Farhan (73) to pile-up 215-3 in the stipulated 20 overs. This is also a record total at this venue, eclipsing the previous 195-5 which Pakistan had scored against Zimbabwe on November 23, 2025.
Young pacer Imran Randhawa, who made his Test debut against England recently, then took 3-11 in four overs to restrict Sri Lanka to 133-7.
This is also the heaviest win from Pakistan against Sri Lanka.
Sri Lanka were never in the run as they kept losing wickets at regular interval.
After Salman Mirza removed in-form Lahiru Udara (5) early, it was Imran Randhawa who put great pressure by picking up the wickets of Sineth Jayawardena (22), Kusal Mendis (9) and Sahan Arachchige (0) in quick succession to break the back of the visitors.
Saim Aub then had Dasun Shanaka (9) before Shadab got rid of Kamindu Mendis (23) to leave Sri Lanka gasping at 74-6.
Chamindu Wickramasinghe resisted with 24-ball 29 before falling to Salman Mirza.
Maheesh Theekshana remained top-scorer with 32 not out which featured four fours.
Imran was ably backed by his new ball partner Salman Mirza with 2-28.
Earlier Maaz Sadqat and skipper Sahibzada Farhan did a glorious job to enable Pakistan post a big total on a batting track.
Maaz and Farhan shared 88 runs off 48 balls for the second wicket stand to take the hosts to a decent total in the end.
Farhan was dropped on 12 when he skied one early in the innings. However, he capitalised on the opportunity and went on to hit his second successive fifty of the series. He brought in his fifty off 31 balls and hammered five sixes and four fours in his commanding 44-ball 73.
Earlier, he, along with Fakhar Zaman provided a rapid start to the hosts, sharing 55 off 35 balls for the opening stand.
Fakhar fell for 17-ball 22 with four fours to off-spinner Maheesh Theekshana.
Maaz, who brought in his second successive fifty off 30 balls, then went after the ball and played some superb strokes.
He also hit Theekshana for three glorious sixes in one over which yielded 22 runs.
He along with Hasan Nawaz scored a rapid 72 runs for the third wicket partnership to take Pakistan to a huge total.
Maaz hammered seven sixes and six fours in his gallant 51-ball 96.
He lost his wicket off the final ball of the innings when he went for a big hit in a bid to complete his century but was held in the deep.
Hasan Nawaz remained not out on nine-ball 19 with one six and one four.
Pakistan scored 46 in the power-play, were 90-1 in ten overs, reached 145-2 in 15 and made 70 runs in the final five overs.
Theekshana remained the most expensive bowler as he finished with 1-55 in his quota of four overs.
Eshan Malinga (1-41) and Dasun Shanaka (1-30) were the other successful bowlers.
Earlier, Sri Lanka won the toss and elected to bowl first. Pakistan made one change, bringing in Salman Mirza in place of Razaullah who had made his T20I debut in the previous game at the same venue.
Sri Lanka made two changes.
The third and final game is scheduled for Tuesday at the same venue.

items.author: Debarghya Sil
items.content:
For years, Swiggy and Zomato have ruled the Indian foodtech sector with an iron fist, building vast restaurant networks and loyal customer bases that have made it difficult for new players to compete. But the duopoly is now facing fresh competition from three directions: Rapido’s Ownly, food delivery startup Swish’s new marketplace, Swish Go, and ecommerce giant Flipkart.
Ownly is already handling around 50,000 orders a day in Bengaluru and entered Hyderabad just two weeks ago. Swish, which started with quick food delivery, is expanding into restaurant aggregation with its new marketplace, Swish Go. Ecommerce giant Flipkart, too, is testing its food delivery service, Eat In, in Bengaluru.
All three are entering a market where consumers are already comfortable ordering food online. At the same time, restaurants are looking for alternatives to the high commissions charged by Swiggy and Zomato. But onboarding restaurants is only half the battle. What the emerging players need is to convince customers to order from their platforms regularly.
Hence, it is only natural for us to ask if these new players can challenge the dominance Swiggy and Zomato have built over the years and what gives the duopoly enough steam to keep the burgeoning rivals at bay.
Restaurants Are Hungry For An Alternative
Restaurant owners have long complained about the commissions and other charges they pay to Swiggy and Zomato. While online orders have become a major source of sales, delivery platforms can eat into margins, especially as restaurants become more dependent on them.
In July, National Restaurant Association of India (NRAI) president and Wow! Momo cofounder Sagar Daryani told Inc42 that food delivery had grown from 10% of a restaurant’s business before Covid-19 to around 50% for some restaurants.
This is where the new entrants see an opportunity. Rapido’s Ownly is trying to capitalise on the discontent by offering zero commission to restaurant partners. It has also integrated Ownly into the Rapido app, giving it access to an existing base of mobility users. The company can also draw on its delivery network for food orders, potentially reducing the cost of building a separate operation from scratch.
Ownly is already processing over 50,000 orders a day in Bengaluru. After entering Hyderabad last month, it has onboarded 10,000 restaurants in the city, with plans to expand that network to 30,000. The expansion gives Ownly a route to compete beyond Bengaluru.
Swish Go is taking a different approach. According to people familiar with the platform, its commission rates vary by order value, with one rate for orders below ₹100 and another for orders above that amount. Restaurant partners find this arrangement favourable, Inc42 has learnt. However, these attractive terms may not last forever.
An observer in the restaurant business believes Ownly could introduce commissions as it grows, with Swish Go potentially following the same path. The current offers are a way to attract restaurants that are unhappy with Swiggy and Zomato.
However, the person also questioned whether Swish ever intended to focus only on 10-minute food delivery. Established players such as Swiggy, Zepto and Rebel Foods have faced challenges with the format, making it difficult to sustain at scale.
Swish Go’s pricing also puts it in competition with Swiggy’s Toing. By waiving packaging and platform fees, Swish Go appears to be betting on a lower-cost ordering experience to attract customers.
The Real Battle Is Over The Users
Getting restaurants to join a new platform is one challenge, and convincing them to order from it regularly is another. Food delivery is already an established market, and new players must now give customers a reason to try their platforms and keep coming back.
An analyst cautioned that making money from these new services could prove difficult because their business models have not been tested at scale. This is pushing platforms towards restaurant aggregation, which allows them to offer a wider choice of food without running every kitchen themselves.
Swiggy and Zomato have also experimented with new food delivery formats, but those bets have not lasted. Swiggy shut down Snacc, its standalone app for 10-15 minute food delivery, in February 2026. Eternal, Zomato’s parent company, discontinued Zomato Quick, its 15-minute delivery service, and Zomato Everyday, which offered home-style meals, in May 2025. Earlier this year, Rebel Foods also shut down Quickies.
These show that even established platforms with large customer bases have struggled to make certain food delivery formats, primarily quick food delivery, work at scale. A new proposition may attract customers, but sustaining the business without compromising service or profitability will be crucial.
Meanwhile, a sectoral expert said that Swiggy and Zomato’s biggest moat is their large user base. But that advantage does not make their position immune to defeat.
Rapido already has a consumer base and delivery fleet it can draw on, while Swish is adding restaurants on top of its existing cloud kitchens and a loyal user base. Flipkart is also preparing to enter food delivery. With a user base of 500 Mn and the financial backing to fund expansion, Flipkart could also take a share of Swiggy and Zomato’s food delivery market. The company is likely to roll out the service before the end of 2026.
The likes of Swish and Flipkart are making moves at a time when Swiggy and Zomato remain much larger businesses. Eternal reported adjusted food delivery revenue of ₹3,537 Cr in Q1 FY27, up 33% year-on-year (YoY) from ₹2,657 Cr in Q1 FY26. This was up from around ₹3,135 Cr in Q4 FY26. Swiggy’s food delivery revenue reached ₹2,208 Cr in Q1 FY27, growing 23% from ₹1,799 Cr a year earlier and ₹2,075 Cr in the previous quarter.
Their restaurant networks are equally extensive. Zomato averaged around 3.28 lakh monthly active restaurant partners in Q1 FY27, while Swiggy reported over 2.7 lakh restaurant partners across more than 720 cities.
These numbers show the scale of the duopoly that Ownly and Swish Go must compete against. Beyond attracting restaurants with better commercial terms, the new entrants will need to build a large, active customer base and generate enough repeat orders to sustain their businesses.
They do not need to match Swiggy and Zomato across India immediately, but they must prove they can grow in select markets without relying indefinitely on low commissions and other attractive offers.
Quick Commerce: The Duopoly’s Strongest Moat
According to Anshika Jain, principal analyst at Counterpoint Research, Swiggy and Zomato’s biggest advantages are their established customer habits, wide restaurant selection and delivery networks built over years.
Ownly’s expansion into Bengaluru and Hyderabad, along with Swish Go’s Bengaluru pilot, puts these advantages to the test in local markets. Since customers and restaurants can use multiple platforms, the incumbents will need to keep their prices competitive and service reliable. Restaurants will also expect a steady flow of orders as new players offer better commercial terms.
However, Jain sees a higher entry barrier in quick commerce, which requires local inventory, supplier relationships, replenishment systems and substantial capital. These investments become defensible only when individual locations attract repeat demand and generate profits.
Quick commerce may therefore offer Swiggy and Zomato a stronger defence than food delivery alone.
For Swiggy and Zomato, food delivery remains an important source of business as they continue to invest in quick commerce. In due time, both businesses will turn self-sustaining at which point the new rivals may not have room to maneuver.
Their scale means there is a lot more that rivals have to do to compete in terms of bringing in users, but it does not prevent these new platforms from targeting restaurants with different commercial terms and undercut the two largest players.
For Flipkart, Rapido Ownly and Swish Go, the real test, for now, is whether early traction can turn into repeat orders. Only then can they loosen the duopoly’s hold.
Edited By Shishir Parasher

items.content:
•He took death to the swamp so we 
  could live — Igbokoda residents 
•Black box, voice recorder, victims missing 
  seven days after tragedy
By Dayo Johnson, Akure
It was drizzling in Igbokoda on Monday morning, October 5, 2026.
 It was the kind of quiet rain that makes fishermen stay indoors and mothers keep their children close.Then the sky screamed.
Residents did not first see the aircraft, with tail number NGR 931, carrying 32 people, comprising 25 passengers and seven crew members, on a routine flight from Benin to Lagos. They heard it. A tortured, rattling roar, like metal begging for mercy.
“It sounded like the engine was coughing blood,” one fisherman told me at the edge of the swamp. “We looked up and saw it wobbling. It was coming down on our heads.”
Where to die
Residents said the aircraft was already in trouble long before it crashed. They were unanimous in their belief that, had the pilot not struggled to control it, Igbokoda could have been counting hundreds of dead.
“Honestly, the pilot should be commended,” said Jomiloju, a resident. “Many lives would have been lost. It would have been a national tragedy if he had allowed the aircraft to go down in the middle of the community. He struggled with it and brought it down inside a deep swamp, 200 metres away from the town.”
Another resident corroborated the account, saying: “If the captain had attempted to bring it down inside the town, it would have caused a bigger disaster. He eventually went into the river and crashed over there.”
In Igbokoda, the pilot is no longer just a casualty. He is regarded as a hero.
“He is a big hero because he averted a tragedy,” another resident said. “The aircraft was heading towards the community, but he manoeuvred it into the swamp. He should be celebrated in death for saving us from catastrophe. Although we are not happy, 32 persons died. They are family members who paid the ultimate price.”
Engine 
The residents’ account was echoed by Governor Lucky Aiyedatiwa when he visited the crash site. According to the governor, eyewitnesses told him that the aircraft came down with a loud sound suggesting engine failure and appeared to be heading towards the town.
“But the pilot managed to manoeuvre the aircraft away from the community before it landed about 200 metres away and went straight into the swamp,” Aiyedatiwa said. “Only the pilot, if he had survived, could have explained what happened in those final moments.”
What followed was a scene the governor described as “a very gory sight”.
When he arrived at the swamp, body parts, military jackets, clothes and fragments of the aircraft were floating on water blackened by aviation fuel. The main fuselage was nowhere to be found.
“The aircraft has sunk deep. The nature and depth of the swamp could have caused it to become deeply submerged in the mud,” he said.
To reach the wreckage, the state deployed two amphibious excavators, known as swamp buggies, machines designed to float and dig at the same time. Despite the deployment, the main wreckage had yet to be recovered seven days after the crash.
Fragments
Divers from the Navy and local communities had been searching the swamp, bringing out only fragments of the aircraft.
“I saw the divers struggling to locate the main fuselage,” said the Commissioner for Environment, Dr Tob Loko. “One of them said he was able to spot it, but the small boats were insufficient to pull it out. That is why we had to deploy heavier equipment.”
The Commissioner for Works, Ayorinde Olawoye, expressed optimism that progress would soon be made.
“You can see the swamp buggy is set to float on water and go to where it happened. Within five hours, reasonable progress will be made,” he said.
However, the Commissioner for Health, Dr Banji Ajaka, painted a grimmer picture.
“It is not something a vehicle or speedboat can just go to. It has gone down with weight and force,” he said.
At the site, the Ondo State Commissioner of Police, Felix Ohagwu, who accessed the scene in a canoe, said there were no survivors.
“From what we have seen, there are no survivors. What we see is just body parts and clothes littered everywhere, floating in the water,” he said. “It is a very difficult terrain, the creeks, mangroves. Accessing the site was not easy.”
Journalists were initially denied access to the site. A television crew was reportedly arrested by Navy personnel for entering without clearance but was later released.
Voices 
For residents, the horror remained fresh.
“I was just trying to have my bath when I heard a loud noise. It was very frightening,” Jomiloju recounted. “We rushed towards the direction the sound came from. We had to sail to the location in canoes. All we saw was wreckage. The larger part of the plane was deep inside the swamp.”
Another resident, Lucky, added: “We have tried our best to rescue them, but the aircraft was deeply buried inside the swamp. Even the women and men took their canoes.”
Where is the black box?
Seven days after the crash, critical answers remained trapped in the swamp with the wreckage.
The Nigerian Air Force confirmed that the flight data recorder, commonly referred to as the black box, and the cockpit voice recorder had yet to be recovered.
“We hope to be able to find critical components of the aircraft that will speak to the investigators because the aircraft wreckage actually speaks to the investigators,”
Air Vice Marshal Ebimobo Ebiowe, NAF Superintendent of Standards and Evaluation, said at the site.
Investigation
The Chief of the Air Staff, Air Marshal Sunday Kelvin Aneke, who visited Igbokoda and inspected the site, ordered a high-level investigation involving military and civilian aviation safety experts, the Nigerian Safety Investigation Bureau and retired senior officers.
“I have flown on this aeroplane. My family has flown on this aeroplane. I know each of the crew personally. They are highly trained, professional and intelligent officers. The best we can do is to honour the sacrifice they have made,” Aneke said, appealing to Nigerians to avoid speculation.
Governor Aiyedatiwa described the incident as a national tragedy, commiserating with President Bola Tinubu, the Nigerian Air Force and the families of the personnel who died while in active service.
Scan sonar
As of Saturday, the Navy had deployed side-scan sonar equipment to map the swamp and locate the submerged fuselage. Aviation fuel was also reported to be leaking into the water, raising concerns about pollution.
In Igbokoda, two tragedies are being mourned: the 32 lives lost in the swamp and the potentially greater tragedy that residents believe was averted by a pilot who, in his final moments, steered the aircraft away from the town.
Whenever it drizzles on a Monday morning, they will remember the day the sky screamed and a man, in their eyes, chose where to die.

items.author: Christopher Louis
items.content:
Xiaomi 18 Pro Max mulai menunjukkan tanda-tanda kehadirannya di pasar internasional. Smartphone flagship tersebut terdeteksi dalam basis data Geekbench AI dengan nomor model 2611FPNFAG. Kemunculan ini mengindikasikan bahwa Xiaomi tengah menguji perangkat versi globalnya, meskipun jadwal peluncuran resminya belum diumumkan.
Sebelumnya, Xiaomi telah mengonfirmasi bahwa Xiaomi 18 Pro dan Xiaomi 18 Pro Max akan dipasarkan secara global, berbeda dari generasi sebelumnya. Jika rumor pembatalan Xiaomi 18 Ultra benar, model Pro Max berpotensi menjadi salah satu perangkat flagship tertinggi Xiaomi untuk memasuki 2027.
Global Xiaomi 18 Pro Max (2611FPNFAG) spotted on Geekbench AI
– Snapdragon 8 Elite Extreme Gen 6
– 12GB RAM
– Android 17#Xiaomi #xiaomi18proMax pic.twitter.com/MsQfYrJDMU— Anvin (@ZionsAnvin) October 9, 2026
Dalam pengujian Geekbench AI, perangkat tersebut menggunakan chipset Snapdragon 8 Elite Extreme Gen 6 yang juga dipakai versi China. Prototipe yang diuji dipadukan dengan RAM 12GB. Namun, hasil pengujian ini belum mengungkap seluruh konfigurasi perangkat yang akan tersedia ketika dipasarkan secara internasional.
Baca Juga: HyperOS 4 Dikabarkan Perkuat Integrasi dengan iPhone, Mac, dan iPad
Snapdragon Terbaru dan Konfigurasi Global
Di China, Xiaomi 18 Pro Max juga tersedia dengan RAM 16GB. Belum diketahui apakah varian tersebut akan hadir di pasar global atau Xiaomi hanya menawarkan konfigurasi RAM 12GB. Pilihan penyimpanan untuk versi China mencakup kapasitas 256GB, 512GB, dan 1TB, tetapi konfigurasi globalnya masih belum dikonfirmasi.
Perbedaan lain yang patut diperhatikan adalah kapasitas baterai. Xiaomi 18 Pro Max versi China membawa baterai 8.500 mAh, sedangkan Xiaomi 18 Pro menggunakan baterai 7.000 mAh. Kapasitas untuk model global, terutama varian yang dipasarkan di Eropa, masih menjadi tanda tanya. Belum ada kepastian apakah Xiaomi akan mempertahankan kapasitas yang sama atau menyesuaikannya untuk pasar tertentu.
Layar Ganda dan Kamera 200MP
Sebagai gambaran, Xiaomi 18 Pro Max versi China memiliki layar utama LTPO AMOLED 6,9 inci dengan resolusi 1208 x 2624 piksel, refresh rate 120Hz, dan kecerahan puncak 4.000 nit. Di bagian belakang, terdapat layar tambahan LTPO AMOLED 2,9 inci dengan refresh rate 120Hz dan tingkat kecerahan puncak yang sama.
Sektor kamera mengandalkan sensor utama 200MP dengan OIS, kamera periskop telefoto 200MP dengan OIS dan zoom optik 3,2x, serta kamera ultrawide 50MP. Kamera depannya memiliki resolusi 50MP. Versi globalnya diperkirakan menjalankan Android 17 dengan HyperOS 4, tetapi spesifikasi akhir, harga, dan tanggal peluncurannya masih menunggu konfirmasi Xiaomi.
Artikel berjudul Xiaomi 18 Pro Max Versi Global Muncul di Geekbench AI, Bawa RAM 12GB yang ditulis oleh Christopher Louis pertama kali tampil di Gizmologi.id

items.content:
A 45-year-old man shot and killed seven relatives and a family friend at a home in Pennsylvania before apparently taking his own life, authorities said Saturday.
The victims in the city of Erie included two young children and a woman who was eight months pregnant.
Police responded Friday evening to reports of shots fired and discovered two women dead in the street, Erie Police Chief Rick Lorah told reporters.
Video evidence showed the pair arriving at the residence appearing distressed, then attempting to contact neighbors and enter the house, Lorah said.
The gunman exited the house, shot them, and returned inside, he said.
The man barricaded himself inside the home as police surrounded the building and ordered him to exit. He was later found inside with an apparent self-inflicted gunshot wound, Lorah said.
The shooter and seven of his victims were related, Lorah said. The eighth victim was a family friend.
Dead inside the home were a five-year-old boy and a one-year-old girl. The others were men and women ranging in age from 19 to 51. One of the women was eight months pregnant.
Local news outlet Erie News Now said responding officers were being offered counseling over the horrifying incident.
“Many people across our community are hurting today: the neighbors who witnessed what happened, the families and friends of those who were killed, the officers and first responders who answered these calls, and others struggling to make sense of something so terrible,” Erie Mayor Daria Devlin told reporters Saturday.
“We cannot undo what happened last night, and we cannot take away the grief that these families are carrying, but we can make sure that they don’t have to carry it alone,” she said.
Mass shootings occur frequently in the United States, where guns vastly outnumber people and efforts to increase firearm restrictions face steep political and legal hurdles.

items.author: Henry Oduah
items.content:
By Peter Duru, Makurdi
At least nine persons have reportedly been killed in fresh attacks by suspected armed herdsmen on Tse-Nyaku, Tse-Biliji and adjoining communities in Mbatian Council Ward of Ngenev, Ukum Local Government Area of Benue State.
Several others were reportedly injured, while an unspecified number of residents were said to be missing following the attacks, which began at about 11pm on Friday.
A local source, who spoke on condition of anonymity, said the assailants invaded the communities in large numbers, shooting sporadically and forcing residents to flee their homes.
According to the source, nine bodies had so far been recovered from the affected communities.
“The attackers came in large numbers and started shooting in the communities. Luckily, many people managed to escape, except for the nine who have been confirmed dead for now because their corpses have been recovered.
“However, it is very likely that the number could increase because many people have not been seen, and no one knows whether they were killed or escaped to other communities.
“Our people discovered that one of armed herdsmen is in possession of the phones of one of the victims and he has been using it to make and receive calls.
“The attacked communities have also already been deserted. It is a very sad day for our people. The Sankera axis of Benue has become a shadow of itself due to the level of insecurity,” he said.
Reacting to the incident, the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) candidate for Ukum I (Ngenev) State Constituency in the Benue State House of Assembly, Livinus Tyodoo, described the invasion as “one attack too many.”
In a statement he personally signed, Tyodoo said he received disturbing reports of the deadly attacks on the communities on Friday night and in the early hours of Saturday.
He said the attacks, allegedly carried out by suspected herdsmen militia, had reportedly claimed more than nine lives, adding that several bodies had been recovered while other residents remained missing and some survivors sustained varying degrees of injuries.
“This is one attack too many. I unequivocally condemn the senseless killing, displacement and continued persecution of innocent citizens in their ancestral homes.
“The people of Ukum I (Ngenev) deserve to live in peace, cultivate their farmlands and pursue their legitimate means of livelihood without the constant fear of violence.
“Human civilisation has evolved beyond the Hobbesian state of nature, where life was characterised by insecurity and the constant fear of violent death. In the 21st century, the sanctity of human life must remain paramount, and no community should be abandoned to the mercy of armed assailants,” he said.
Tyodoo stressed that the incident should not be politicised, urging the authorities to take urgent and decisive action to prevent further bloodshed.
“This is not the time for politics or the exchange of blame. It is a time for urgent, coordinated and decisive action,” he said.
He called on the Benue State Government, Ukum Local Government Council and relevant security agencies to strengthen security operations in the affected communities and other vulnerable areas of the local government.
According to him, beyond issuing statements and ordering investigations, the government must ensure effective intelligence gathering, proactive security deployments, the arrest and prosecution of those responsible, and concrete measures to prevent further attacks.
“Our people must be able to return to their ancestral homes, reclaim their farmlands and carry on with their daily activities without fear. The protection of lives and property is a fundamental responsibility of government, and the people of Ukum deserve nothing less,” he added.
The PDP candidate also expressed condolences to the families of those reportedly killed, while praying for the safe return of missing persons and the speedy recovery of the injured.
“I pray for the peaceful repose of the souls of the departed, comfort for the bereaved families, the safe return of anyone still missing, and a speedy recovery for those who sustained injuries.
“May God comfort our grieving communities, protect our people and restore lasting peace to Ngenev, Ukum and Benue State at large. The time for urgent action is now. Our people deserve security, justice and lasting peace,” he said.
When contacted, the Police Public Relations Officer, DSP Peter Aondongu, said he was yet to receive a report on the incident.

By James Ogunnaike, Abeokuta
The Ogun State chapter of the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) has called on its members and supporters to remain calm following the omission of its governorship candidate, Hon. Oladipupo Adebutu, from a list published by the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC), expressing confidence that the issue would be resolved ahead of the 2027 governorship election.
The opposition party alleged that the development was the result of pressure from the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC), which it accused of being apprehensive about the PDP’s chances in the forthcoming election.
The party, however, maintained that Adebutu remained a bona fide member of the PDP, insisting that he had fulfilled the party’s membership registration requirements within the stipulated period.
In a statement issued by its Publicity Secretary, Arc. Kayode Adebayo, the PDP said, participated in the party’s digital membership registration exercise, during which his membership card was printed and verified before being submitted to INEC within the prescribed timeframe.
“We state emphatically that our candidate, Hon. Oladipupo Adebutu, has never left the Peoples Democratic Party at any time. He duly registered as a member of the party within the designated period of the digital registration exercise, and his membership card was printed, verified and submitted to INEC at the stipulated time,” the statement said.
The party attributed the omission to what it described as political interference, alleging that the APC was seeking to undermine its chances ahead of the 2027 governorship election.
“The omission of our candidate’s name from INEC’s list is a consequence of the undue pressure allegedly mounted on the commission by the ruling party out of fear of losing the election to our party,” Adebayo stated.
The PDP, however, expressed optimism that Adebutu’s name would be included in the relevant list of candidates, reaffirming its commitment to participating in the 2027 governorship election.
It urged the people of Ogun State not to be distracted by the development, calling on its members and supporters to remain focused on their political objectives and continue mobilising for the forthcoming election.
“While we urge the good people of Ogun State not to be perturbed or distracted from our collective resolve to vote out the APC, we remain resolute, unfazed and unwaveringly confident that our candidate is marching towards a decisive victory in the 2027 governorship election,” the statement added.
The opposition party further maintained that the development would not diminish what it described as the determination of the people of Ogun State to demand better governance and positive change.
“No amount of desperate manipulation, political witch-hunts or calculated distractions can alter the mandate of the people of Ogun State, who are overwhelmingly eager for true leadership and positive change,” the PDP said.
Reiterating its appeal for calm, the party urged its members, supporters and other stakeholders to remain steadfast and undeterred as it intensifies its political activities ahead of the election.
“Once again, we call on all our teeming supporters, party faithful and the general public to remain steadfast, vigilant and unintimidated as the unstoppable movement to rescue Ogun State and bring relief to our people continues to gain momentum,” the statement said.

items.author: Ayobami
items.content:
Yan Diomande earned Real Madrid a tight 1-0 victory over Villarreal on Saturday to keep them six points behind La Liga leaders Barcelona, even though winger Vinicius Junior was sent off for hair-pulling.
Brazil international Vinicius, on as a substitute, scored but his goal was disallowed and then he was dismissed after a VAR review showed he pulled the hair of Villarreal’s Nathan Saliba.
Jose Mourinho’s Madrid battled through the final stages with 10 men but held on to win and go provisionally third.
Champions Barca lead La Liga after a 3-0 win over Getafe, while Atletico Madrid are five points behind in second after they edged Alaves 2-1.
Striker Kylian Mbappe was fit to start the match for Madrid at their Santiago Bernabeu stadium after suffering a knee problem playing for France during the international break.
There were a smattering of whistles for the superstar forward, with some fans believing he has been unprofessional in recent weeks, but also applause from other supporters.
Mbappe, a candidate for the Ballon d’Or trophy later this month, was Madrid’s most threatening player in the first half, although he had little competition.
Mourinho started with out-of-form winger Vinicius on the bench, following his trips to Australia and India with Brazil during the international break.
Madrid improved defensively, giving Villarreal few chances of note, but struggled to build much in attack themselves in a drab opening half.
Mbappe struck the post from Alvaro Carreras’s lay-off as Madrid pushed Villarreal back early on.
Villarreal soon gained a foothold and restricted Madrid’s opportunities, until Mbappe forced a good save from Peter Gulacsi.
There was some more mild whistling for Madrid’s display from their fans at half-time, but soon they were able to celebrate summer arrival Diomande’s first goal for the club.
The Ivorian winger, Madrid’s record 140-million-euro ($157 million) signing, produced a sharp low finish into the far corner after good work from Federico Valverde to play him in.
Vinicius thought he had doubled Madrid’s lead after Jude Bellingham charged in down the left and cut the ball back for him.
However the winger’s joy turned to anger after referee Isidro Diaz de Mera was called to watch Vinicius’s hair pull on Saliba in the build-up by VAR and sent off the Brazilian, voiding his goal.
Madrid’s Belgian goalkeeper Thibaut Courtois, who had made a couple of smart saves earlier in the half, produced an acrobatic stop to thwart Carlos Romero.
Mbappe was denied again by Hungarian goalkeeper Gulasci as the forward left the Bernabeu frustrated in his hunt for goals, although his team were able to clinch three important points to stay on Barca’s trail.

items.author: Henry Oduah
items.content:
Nollywood actress Regina Daniels has disclosed that she has endured months of severe pain and difficulty walking, revealing that her condition has left her dependent on a wheelchair.
The actress shared the update in a video posted on her Instagram page on Saturday to celebrate her 25th birthday, using the opportunity to explain her absence from social media.
Daniels, a mother of two, said what initially appeared to be a minor health problem gradually worsened, leaving her unable to move freely and sometimes preventing her from walking.
“I know many of you may be surprised seeing me in a wheelchair. Well, welcome to another chapter of my life. Let me walk you through what my life has been since many of you have asked questions about my absence,” she said.
Recounting how her condition deteriorated, Daniels said she began experiencing more serious symptoms after hosting a children’s day carnival.
“For several months now, I have lost my freedom to move around as I please. It started as something minor, very minor, but eventually led to this.
“But things took a major turn after the last public gathering I hosted, my children’s day carnival. One test after another, I jokingly started calling myself a lab rat. The pain became excruciating. Sometimes I can walk, and sometimes I can’t move. I cried,” she added.
The actress expressed gratitude for the progress she said she had made in her recovery, noting that recent developments had encouraged her to speak publicly about her health.
“Well, me sitting here today, in front of this camera, sharing this with y’all, it’s because there’s been some really significant developments in my recovery. And I say, thank you, Lord,” she said.
Daniels also described the emotional difficulties associated with her condition, particularly having to rely on others for assistance with routine activities.
Despite the challenges, she said her faith in God had helped her through the experience and expressed hope for healing and peace.
The actress further disclosed that she had moved closer to her loved ones, especially her children, whom she described as being particularly dear to her.
She said she initially rented the property she moved into but later developed an interest in owning it.
Daniels married businessman and politician Ned Nwoko in 2019, and the couple have two children. Their relationship has since been marked by a public and contentious separation.

First Lady Sen Oluremi Tinubu says President Bola Tinubu will move Nigeria from economic reforms to prosperity if re-elected for a second term in 2027.
Tinubu said this on Saturday in Lafia at the North-Central Mega Rally organised by the All Progressives Congress (APC) to mobilise support for the re-election of President Bola Tinubu and Vice-President Kashim Shettima.
The First Lady urged party members to take the campaign to communities across the region and mobilise voters for the party’s candidates.
She highlighted some achievements of the Tinubu administration across various sectors, saying continuity was necessary to sustain the gains.
“President Tinubu is a man who believes in the unity, security and prosperity of our nation.
“The Independence Day message of Mr President was titled ‘From Reforms to Prosperity’.
“Therefore, Mr President is saying that they are going to reform the sector, but now is the time for prosperity, and we can see our economy is stabilising.
“Foreign exchange is going down, and investors are coming back to Nigeria, our farmers too. You can see all our governors here; they are doing infrastructural development like no other time before.
“I have been in the Senate for 12 years. This is the best time I will see the government fixing roads and building a lot of infrastructure,” she said.
Tinubu also cited the administration’s food support programme, saying it was designed to provide nutritious food for children, pregnant women and breastfeeding mothers.
“As you see now, we have just finished the food bank programme, where we are helping every child and mothers who are pregnant and also breastfeeding.
“This is to ensure that they can have more nutritious food, and also the children that are malnourished can get treatment and also get food to grow healthy,” she said.
She added that students were also benefiting from the administration’s education funding initiatives.
The First Lady urged party members to communicate the administration’s policies and programmes to Nigerians in their respective states.
She described Tinubu as a leader willing to take difficult decisions, expressing confidence that his policies would strengthen the economy and improve security.
She said the administration would continue to pursue a stronger economy, safer communities and a greater Nigeria if returned to office.
The First Lady also said the APC women’s wing had united its campaign efforts to promote a common message and goal ahead of the 2027 general elections.
She said the party’s campaign would focus on its programmes and policies without resorting to hate speech or actions capable of undermining national unity.
“Therefore, vote for continuity, vote for capacity, vote for prosperity, and vote for the re-election of Mr President and all the candidates of APC from top to bottom,” she said.
The rally was hosted by Gov. Abdullahi Sule of Nasarawa, with governors and other political leaders from the North-Central region in attendance. (NAN)

items.content:
A United States federal court has sentenced a Nigerian national, Edikan Adiakpan, to 30 months’ imprisonment for his involvement in a business email fraud scheme targeting American companies.
The U.S. Department of Justice disclosed this in a statement issued by the U.S. Attorney’s Office for the Southern District of Texas.
The department said Adiakpan, 35, a Houston resident, pleaded guilty on May 12 to illegally transmitting proceeds from an email fraud scheme.
U.S. District Judge Andrew Hanen sentenced him to 30 months in federal prison, followed by three years of supervised release.
According to the department, Adiakpan operates a company known as Akama Lifestyle, which he advertised as a luxury car service.
However, prosecutors said he used the company between 2020 and 2022 to transfer money received from fraudsters in exchange for a percentage of the proceeds.
The funds originated from a business email compromise scheme that targeted more than 10 victims.
The department explained that the fraudsters sent emails impersonating legitimate suppliers and creditors to deceive businesses into transferring payments to fraudulent bank accounts.
One victim, a small utility trailer company in Mississippi, lost substantial funds after receiving fraudulent payment instructions.
According to prosecutors, the company transferred $927,080 to the fraudsters, believing it was paying a legitimate supplier.
The fraudsters subsequently transferred portions of the proceeds to Adiakpan.
The department said Adiakpan deposited and redeemed several cashier’s cheques payable to himself and his luxury car company.
It said the transactions involved $359,000 belonging to the Mississippi company.
A victim impact statement describing the financial consequences of the fraud was presented during Adiakpan’s sentencing hearing.
The department disclosed that Adiakpan had temporary legal status in the United States when he was arrested.
It also identified another Nigerian, Ayobami Omoniyi, 27, as having participated in the scheme, and was subsequently sentenced on March 24 to 32 months in federal prison for his role.
The investigation was conducted by the FBI’s Houston Field Office and Bryan Resident Agency, alongside the Internal Revenue Service Criminal Investigation Division, while Assistant U.S. Attorney Belinda Beek prosecuted the case. (NAN)
