items.author: Onsa Mustafa
items.content:
Copyright protected content copied from PhoneWorld website.
Xiaomi shares climbed sharply on Friday after its new SkyNomad EV lineup received strong demand during its first month on the market. The company reported 70,000 orders for the newly launched models, boosting investor confidence in its growing automotive business.
Xiaomi shares rose by 7.6% to HK$25.46 during Friday’s trading session, making the company one of the top performers on Hong Kong’s Hang Seng Index. The benchmark index also gained around 1.3% as market sentiment improved.
According to Xiaomi’s social media announcement, the new SkyNomad N90 and SkyNomad N70 models secured a combined 70,000 orders in their first month of availability. The response indicates strong initial interest in the company’s latest vehicles as it works to expand its position in China’s competitive automotive market.
Xiaomi Shares Surge as SkyNomad EV Lineup Receives 70,000 Orders
Along with the strong order figures, Xiaomi reported delivering more than 10,000 SkyNomad vehicles in September. These deliveries helped push the company’s total vehicle deliveries above 40,000 units for the month.
September marked Xiaomi’s strongest monthly vehicle delivery performance so far in 2026. The results highlight the growing contribution of its automotive business as the company expands beyond its established smartphone and consumer electronics operations.
The latest figures also strengthened investor optimism about Xiaomi’s ability to compete in China’s electric vehicle market, where established automakers and technology companies are competing to attract customers with new models and advanced features.
How the SkyNomad Lineup Differs From Earlier Models
The SkyNomad series introduces a different approach from Xiaomi’s earlier electric vehicle offerings. Unlike its fully electric SU7 and YU7 models, the new lineup includes an internal combustion engine to provide additional driving range.
This setup allows the vehicles to combine electric driving with a fuel-powered engine, potentially appealing to customers who want the benefits of electric mobility without relying entirely on charging infrastructure for longer journeys.
The N90 and N70 are part of Xiaomi’s broader effort to diversify its vehicle lineup and reach a wider range of buyers. Their early order numbers suggest that the new models have attracted considerable attention shortly after launch.
Strong Demand Supports Xiaomi’s Automotive Expansion
Xiaomi’s latest sales performance comes as competition in China’s electric vehicle sector continues to intensify. Automakers are investing in new technologies, expanding their product ranges and introducing different powertrain options to meet changing customer preferences.
The company’s ability to attract substantial orders for the SkyNomad lineup, alongside continued deliveries of its existing vehicles, could help strengthen its position in this market.
However, orders do not necessarily translate into completed sales, and the company’s performance in the coming months will depend on its ability to convert customer demand into deliveries.
For now, the 70,000 first-month orders and September’s record delivery figures have provided a positive signal for Xiaomi’s automotive business. Investors will likely watch future delivery numbers closely to assess whether the company can maintain this momentum in China’s highly competitive vehicle market.

items.author: Shrishti Bisht
items.content:
Omnichannel menswear brand KISAH has raised ₹35.9 Cr (about $3.7 Mn) in a Series A funding round led by Fireside Ventures at a post-money valuation of around ₹211 Cr (about $22 Mn).
The startup plans to use the capital primarily to expand its retail network, while also investing in supply chain, warehousing, technology and backend infrastructure.
“We are learning retail right now. We’ve had very good positive early signs for us. The idea is that we are using this money to create our playbooks, and then the retail expansion is something which should be funded by franchisees,” cofounder Yash Sarawagi told Inc42.
Prior to this, the D2C startup had raised around ₹10 Cr from angel investors, including Sagar Daryani, founder of Wow! Momo, and Apoor Salarpuria of the Salarpuria Group.
Founded in 2018 by Sarawagi, KISAH is a Kolkata-based menswear and kidswear brand. Sarawagi’s sister Yashwi Ladsaria later joined the business as its cofounder, followed by Saurav Kothari as its third cofounder. KISAH began as a marketplace-led brand before expanding its own D2C platform as well as presence in physical stores.
The brand sells through marketplaces including Myntra, Amazon, AJIO and Nyka.
It sells contemporary ethnic and occasion wear, targeting wedding guests and consumers beyond the traditional groom market. Its range includes kurtas and sherwanis alongside more contemporary pieces such as bomber jackets, flared trousers and sneakers.
KISAH sits at the premium end of online ethnicwear but remains more affordable than traditional offline brands. Its products sell for an average of about ₹4,000 on Myntra, compared with roughly ₹1,000 for the platform’s wider ethnicwear category, according to Sarawagi.
KISAH’s Offline Push
KISAH began its offline expansion with a store in Kolkata’s Gariahat in 2025. The store generated around ₹45-50 Lakh in its first partial year of operations before reaching annual sales of about ₹70 Lakh, as per the cofounders.
The performance encouraged KISAH to accelerate its retail expansion. It opened its first flagship store in Bengaluru’s Indiranagar in September 2025, followed by a store at Hyderabad’s Sarath City in November last year.
As of now, KISAH operates a total of 12 stores across Bengaluru, Kolkata, Hyderabad, Mumbai and Visakhapatnam, among other markets. It plans to expand further in Bengaluru and test markets such as Jaipur and Visakhapatnam.
The brand plans to reach around 100 stores and ₹500 Cr in revenue before expanding into broader categories. Over the next 12-18 months, it also plans to integrate its online and offline operations as it builds an omnichannel shopping experience.
On the financial front, the startup claims to have clocked a revenue of ₹65 Cr in FY26 while maintaining profitability, with an EBITDA margin of around 5-6%.
It expects its revenue to cross ₹100 Cr in FY27, implying growth of about 70%, with retail expected to be the main growth driver. The offline business is projected to grow four-fivefold during the year and contribute 25-30% to its overall business in FY27.
As of now, D2C contributes around 20% of KISAH’s business, while marketplaces account for most of its online sales. International markets contribute around 8-10% of revenue, with the US its primary overseas market.

items.author: Usama Anjum
items.content:
Copyright protected content copied from PhoneWorld website.
Pakistan’s National Information Technology Board (NITB) and the Tourism Department have reached an agreement to digitize tourism-related public services, bringing information and departmental systems together on a unified digital platform.
The initiative aims to make tourism services more accessible to citizens across Pakistan by allowing them to access departmental services online, regardless of their location.
The agreement is part of the government’s Digital Economy Enhancement Project (DEEP), which focuses on improving public service delivery through digital systems.
Tourism Services to Be Integrated Into a Unified Portal
Under the agreement, tourism-related services, information and administrative processes will be connected to a central digital portal.
The proposed system will allow citizens to access Tourism Department services online from different parts of the country, reducing their reliance on physical visits to government offices.
The digitization effort will bring together existing departmental information, service procedures and related systems within a common digital framework.
The objective is to make public services easier to access while improving the efficiency of departmental operations.
Once implemented, the platform is expected to provide a more convenient way for citizens to interact with the Tourism Department through digital channels.
NITB to Provide Technical Support
NITB will provide technical assistance to the Tourism Department for the digitization of its services.
Both organizations will collaborate on the development, testing and implementation of the proposed digital solutions.
Their responsibilities will include coordinating the technical requirements needed to connect departmental systems with the unified platform.
The agreement establishes a framework for cooperation between the two organizations, with the development and implementation of digital services forming a central part of the partnership.
However, the information available does not specify a launch date for the proposed tourism portal or identify which individual services will become available first.
Part of Pakistan’s Digital Economy Enhancement Project
The tourism digitization initiative falls under the Digital Economy Enhancement Project (DEEP), a government programme supported by the World Bank.
According to the Ministry of Information Technology and Telecommunication, DEEP aims to strengthen Pakistan’s digital public infrastructure and improve the delivery of government services to citizens and businesses.
NITB is responsible for developing a unified digital services platform under the project, connecting public-sector institutions and making selected government services accessible through integrated digital channels.
The tourism agreement represents another planned integration of departmental services into this wider digital framework.
For citizens, the intended benefit is simpler access to tourism-related government services without having to depend entirely on conventional administrative procedures.
The effectiveness of the initiative will depend on the development, testing and rollout of the planned digital services.

items.author: Tom Jackson
items.content:
Pakistani startup KangarooCare AI is developing intelligent, AI-enabled medical devices that are utilising the latest technologies to improve healthcare outcomes, with a particular focus on neonatal care.
Founded by Islam Un Nisa in 2018, KangarooCare has built out a product portfolio that includes neonatal incubators, infant warmers, phototherapy solutions, and AI-enabled monitoring technologies.
“We are also developing intelligent features such as AI-assisted phototherapy, baby-cry detection and real-time monitoring, with the aim of supporting clinicians and improving the quality and efficiency of neonatal care,” Nisa told Disrupt Africa.
“Our vision is to make advanced healthcare technology accessible to hospitals that may not have the resources to purchase expensive imported systems.”
Iterating its own products
What is unique about KangarooCare is that it is not simply importing and reselling equipment – but rather iterating and developing its own products, assembling them locally, testing them, and providing after-sales support.
“Our long-term objective is to build a healthcare technology platform that combines medical devices, AI, data and clinical intelligence to address real-world healthcare challenges in emerging markets,” said Nisa.
The startup was founded in a bid to address the lack of affordable, reliable and technologically-advanced medical equipment designed around the realities of emerging healthcare markets.
“Hospitals in countries such as Pakistan often face a difficult choice – purchase expensive imported equipment with high upfront and lifecycle costs, or compromise on functionality by purchasing lower-cost alternatives,” said Nisa.
She said she believes there is a significant middle ground, with KangarooCare aiming to provide advanced functionality at an accessible price, while also providing local technical support and easier maintenance.
“We don’t want to compete purely on price. Our competitive advantage is the combination of affordability, intelligent technology,local engineering and serviceability, and understanding of emerging-market healthcare needs,” said Nisa.
“We believe that understanding the actual operating environment of hospitals is just as important as developing the technology itself.”
Strong demand
The uptake has been “very encouraging”. The company has sold approximately 1,600 equipment units, which Nisa said demonstrated it had moved beyond the prototype stage and achieved genuine commercial adoption.
“This traction has been extremely valuable because healthcare technology cannot be validated only in a laboratory. The real test is whether hospitals are willing to purchase, deploy and continue using the technology. Our customers and users have also provided valuable feedback, allowing us to continuously improve our products,” Nisa said.
“The next phase for us is therefore not simply about selling more units. It is about scaling the business sustainably, increasing production capacity, expanding our product portfolio and entering new markets.”
With that in mind, the previously bootstrapped KangarooCare is on the lookout for funding, and recently participated in the Standard Chartered Foundation’s Women in Tech Accelerator, locally implemented by INNOVentures Global, with support from Village Capital.
Participation came with a US$5,000 grant, but Nisa said a major additional benefit was the opportunity to become part of a broader entrepreneurial ecosystem.
“For a technology company, particularly one operating in healthcare hardware, it is easy to become too focused on the engineering side of the business. The programme helped us think beyond the product itself and focus more on market positioning, customers, scalability, partnerships and business growth,” she said.
“It also helped us gain greater confidence in presenting KangarooCare not simply as a medical-equipment company, but as a technology-driven healthcare company with international potential.”
An international plan
International potential indeed, but where specifically?
“We see significant opportunities in other emerging healthcare markets where hospitals face similar challenges around affordability, access to technology, maintenance and technical support,” Nisa said.
“Our expansion strategy is focused on markets across South Asia, the Middle East, Africa, and other emerging healthcare economies. We believe products developed around the realities of emerging markets can have a significant international opportunity because many healthcare systems face similar constraints.”
Clearly, the startup’s core business model is B2B, selling medical equipment directly to hospitals, healthcare institutions and other healthcare organisations.
“We are also investing in higher-value products and AI-enabled solutions, which we believe can create additional recurring and technology-driven revenue streams in the future,” said Nisa.
“Our ambition goes beyond manufacturing and selling medical equipment. Our mission is to democratise access to advanced healthcare technology. We believe that a hospital in an emerging market should not have to choose between affordability and innovation.”

Xiaomi could bring major battery and display upgrades to its upcoming Redmi Turbo 6 Max. According to a new leak, the smartphone may feature a battery exceeding 10,000mAh and a large display measuring around 7 inches.
The information comes from tipster Digital Chat Station, who shared details about an upcoming mid-range smartphone powered by MediaTek’s Dimensity 9500s chipset. Although the tipster did not mention the device’s name directly, the specifications suggest that it could be the Redmi Turbo 6 Max.
The device is expected to succeed the Redmi Turbo 5 Max, which Xiaomi launched earlier this year with a 9,000mAh battery and a 6.83-inch display.
Redmi Turbo 6 Max May Feature a 10,000mAh Battery and 7-Inch Display
The most notable upgrade could be the battery capacity. The Redmi Turbo 6 Max may pack a battery larger than 10,000mAh, offering more capacity than its predecessor.
If Xiaomi delivers this upgrade, the phone could appeal to users who prioritise long battery life and want to spend less time charging their devices. However, the actual battery capacity, charging speed, and battery life remain unconfirmed.
The Redmi Turbo 5 Max already features a 9,000mAh battery, so an increase beyond 10,000mAh would represent a significant step forward for the series.
A Large 7-Inch Display With 2K Resolution
The leaked information also points to a display measuring approximately 7 inches. An earlier rumour from July suggested that the Redmi Turbo 6 Max could feature a 7-inch screen with 2K resolution.
If these details prove accurate, the smartphone could offer a larger viewing area for watching videos, playing games, and browsing content. The higher resolution could also deliver sharper visuals, although Xiaomi has yet to confirm the display specifications.
The Redmi Turbo 5 Max comes with a 6.83-inch screen, meaning the new model could feature a noticeable increase in display size.
Minimalist Design Expected
The Redmi Turbo 6 Max could also retain a clean and simple design. A render leaked in July showed a smartphone with a horizontal, pill-shaped camera bar on the rear panel.
The latest leak also points towards a minimalist appearance, although the final design and available colour options remain unknown.
MediaTek Dimensity 9500s Chipset
The leaked smartphone is expected to use the MediaTek Dimensity 9500s chipset. This processor also powers the Redmi Turbo 5 Max, which suggests that Xiaomi could retain some of the existing hardware while focusing on improvements to the battery and display.
However, the latest information does not confirm whether the Redmi Turbo 6 Max will use the same chipset configuration as its predecessor or receive any other hardware changes.
Redmi Turbo 6 Max Launch Details Remain Unknown
Xiaomi has not officially announced the Redmi Turbo 6 Max or confirmed its specifications. The reported battery capacity, display size, resolution, and chipset should therefore be treated as unconfirmed information.
If the leaks are accurate, the Redmi Turbo 6 Max could stand out in the mid-range smartphone segment with its exceptionally large battery and near 7-inch display. More details about its launch date, pricing, charging capabilities, and other specifications will emerge in the coming weeks.

items.content:
Copyright protected content copied from PhoneWorld website.
Oppo has set a date for the Oppo Find X10 global launch. The Find X10 and Find X10 Pro Max will be unveiled on October 21 at an event in Mallorca, Spain.
The phones first appeared in China last month. Oppo has now confirmed they will reach international markets, though only two models from the series are expected to make the trip.
Two phones, not the whole series
Oppo launched the Find X10 series in China in September. The company’s global announcement names just the Find X10 and the Find X10 Pro Max.
That narrows the international line-up. Buyers outside China should expect fewer choices than Chinese customers had at launch.
Pricing is the open question
Oppo will announce global pricing and availability at the Mallorca event. Until then, there are no official figures.
A recent leak points to higher prices in the European Union than last year’s Find models carried. The leak is unconfirmed, and Oppo has not commented on it.
Oppo’s UK online store began taking pre-orders for the phones in September. That means some buyers committed to a purchase before the company had announced global pricing.
What the two phones offer
The specifications below are as reported. Battery capacity is the China figure.
Find X10
Find X10 Pro Max
Display
6.59-inch
6.78-inch
Chipset
Dimensity 9600M
Dimensity 9600 Pro
Rear cameras
Dual 200MP plus 50MP ultrawide
Triple 200MP
Battery (China)
8,000 mAh
8,000 mAh
Both phones use MediaTek’s Dimensity chips. The Pro Max gets the higher-tier 9600 Pro, while the standard model gets the 9600M.
The camera setups stand out. The Find X10 has two 200MP sensors alongside a 50MP ultrawide unit. The Pro Max goes further with three 200MP rear cameras.
The 8,000 mAh battery is large for a flagship phone. Many premium handsets ship with batteries well below that. Oppo has not said whether the global models will keep the same capacity, and battery sizes sometimes change between regions.
What to watch on October 21
Three details will settle most of the open questions. The first is the actual price in Europe and the UK, which will confirm or contradict the leak. The second is whether the global models keep the 8,000 mAh battery. The third is the list of countries where the phones go on sale.
The more telling signal may be the product range. A global launch with two models, held in Europe, tells buyers where Oppo is placing its bets. If prices do rise as the leak suggests, the company is wagering that its camera and battery specifications can justify a higher cost at the top of the market.

items.author: Rizwana Omer
items.content:
Copyright protected content copied from PhoneWorld website.
Before you call your mobile operator about a crackling line or a data connection that keeps dropping, the Pakistan Telecommunication Authority (PTA) wants you to check three things on your own side. In a new PTA 4G/LTE advisory, the regulator says the fix for many call and internet problems may sit in the phone’s settings or in the SIM card.
The advisory responds to a common complaint. Many users report unclear voice calls and mobile data that cuts out, sometimes in the middle of a call.
What the PTA is asking users to do
The first step is to open the phone’s network settings and make sure the 4G/LTE option is switched on. The PTA says good internet and clear calls depend on that configuration.
If the problem continues, the second step is to check the handset itself. The phone must actually support 4G services. Some older or basic models do not.
The third step is the SIM. Users should contact their mobile operator and ask whether the SIM currently supports 4G. A SIM that was issued some years ago may not be ready for 4G.
The PTA says that a compatible handset, a 4G-ready SIM and correct network settings together improve overall network performance.
Why the settings matter
LTE stands for Long-Term Evolution, the technical name for the standard behind 4G. When a phone is set to an older network mode, or when either the handset or SIM cannot use 4G, the connection falls back to older and slower technology. That can mean weaker data speeds and, depending on the network, poorer voice quality.
The PTA’s advisory does not go into that detail. It gives a simple checklist and leaves the technical explanation out. The explanation above is general background, not something the regulator spelt out.
A self-help step, with limits
The PTA says the check lets users resolve basic connectivity problems before turning to operator support. That could ease some pressure on helplines, and it gives users a quick first test that costs nothing.
There are limits, though. The advisory does not address problems that sit on the network side, such as weak coverage in a particular area or congestion at busy hours. A user with the right settings, a compatible phone and a 4G-ready SIM can still get a poor signal. For those cases, the advisory offers no further guidance.
The PTA does say it monitors operators’ quality of service and educates subscribers about available technologies. It also notes that reliance on mobile networks for internet applications and data services grows every day.
What it means for Pakistani users
For many subscribers, the advisory is a useful reminder. People who bought a phone years ago or kept an old SIM through several handset upgrades may never have checked whether 4G is switched on or supported. The check takes a minute.
The advisory also raises a question about how responsibility is shared. Users are being asked to confirm their own equipment first, which is reasonable, since a settings error is easy to fix. It would help if operators made it just as easy, for example, by telling customers with older SIMs that an upgrade is available. The advisory does not say whether operators are expected to do this.
The wider point is about expectations. Mobile networks are now used for banking, work calls, video and messaging. A regulator reminding users to check a setting is a small step. How well networks perform in the places people live and work is the larger test, and a settings check cannot settle it.
The post Poor Call Quality? PTA Tells Mobile Users to Check 4G Settings, Handset and SIM First appeared first on PhoneWorld.

items.title: Directions under Section 35 A read with Section 56 of the Banking Regulation Act, 1949 – Sri Mahatma Basaveshwar Co-operative Bank Ltd., Afzalpur
items.summary: It is hereby notified for information of the public that in exercise of powers vested in it under sub section (1) of Section 35 A read with Section 56 of the Banking Regulation Act, 1949, the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) vide Directive Ref. No. BLR.DOS.SSMS.No.S1220/09-01-243/2026-2027 dated October 07, 2026, has issued certain Directions to Sri Mahatma Basaveshwar Co-operative Bank Ltd., Afzalpur, (“the bank”), whereby, as from the close of business on October 08, 2026, the bank shall not, without prior approval of RBI in writing, grant or renew any loans and advances, make any investment, incur any liability including borrowal of funds and acceptance of fresh deposits, disburse or agree to disburse any payment whether in discharge of its liabilities and obligations or otherwise, enter into any compromise or arrangement and sell, transfer or otherwise dispose of any of its properties or assets except as notified in the RBI Direction dated October 07, 2026, a copy of which h
items.content:
It is hereby notified for information of the public that in exercise of powers vested in it under sub section (1) of Section 35 A read with Section 56 of the Banking Regulation Act, 1949, the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) vide Directive Ref. No. BLR.DOS.SSMS.No.S1220/09-01-243/2026-2027 dated October 07, 2026, has issued certain Directions to Sri Mahatma Basaveshwar Co-operative Bank Ltd., Afzalpur, (“the bank”), whereby, as from the close of business on October 08, 2026, the bank shall not, without prior approval of RBI in writing, grant or renew any loans and advances, make any investment, incur any liability including borrowal of funds and acceptance of fresh deposits, disburse or agree to disburse any payment whether in discharge of its liabilities and obligations or otherwise, enter into any compromise or arrangement and sell, transfer or otherwise dispose of any of its properties or assets except as notified in the RBI Direction dated October 07, 2026, a copy of which has been directed to be displayed on the bank's website / premises for perusal by interested members of the public. Considering the bank's present liquidity position, the bank has been directed not to allow withdrawal of any amount from savings bank or current accounts or any other account of a depositor but is allowed to set off loans against deposits subject to the conditions stated in the above RBI Directions. The bank may incur expenditure in respect of certain essential items such as salaries of employees, rent, electricity bills, etc., as specified in the said Directions.
2. RBI has in the last few years engaged with the Board and Senior Management of the bank for improvement in its functioning. However, lack of concrete efforts taken by the bank to address the supervisory concerns and to protect the interest of depositors of the bank, necessitated issuance of these Directions.
3. The eligible depositors would be entitled to receive deposit insurance claim amount of their deposits upto a monetary ceiling of ₹5,00,000/- (Rupees five lakh only) in the same capacity and in the same right, from the Deposit Insurance and Credit Guarantee Corporation (DICGC), as applicable under the provisions of the DICGC Act, 1961, based on submission of willingness by the depositors concerned and after due verification. The depositors may contact the bank officials for further information. Details may also be accessed on the DICGC website: www.dicgc.org.in.
4. The issue of the above Directions by the RBI should not per se be construed as cancellation of the banking license by RBI. The bank will continue to undertake banking business subject to restrictions specified in the said Directions till its financial position improves. The RBI continues to monitor the position of the bank and will take necessary actions including modifications of these Directions, as warranted, depending upon circumstances and in the interest of the depositors.
5. These Directions shall remain in force for a period of six months from the close of business on October 08, 2026 and are subject to review.
(Brij Raj)           
Chief General Manager
Press Release: 2026-2027/1286

items.title: HyperOS 4 Dikabarkan Perkuat Integrasi dengan iPhone, Mac, dan iPad
items.summary:
Xiaomi dikabarkan menyiapkan integrasi yang lebih luas antara HyperOS 4 dan ekosistem Apple. Pembaruan ini memungkinkan pengguna smartphone Xiaomi bertukar data dengan iPhone, sekaligus mengakses sejumlah fitur lintas perangkat yang sebelumnya lebih identik dengan ekosistem Apple sendiri.
Melalui integrasi tersebut, pengguna dapat berbagi foto, file, kontak, dan halaman web antara smartphone Xiaomi dan iPhone. HyperOS 4 juga disebut mendukung akses ke album foto berbasis cloud dari kedua perangkat, sehingga pengguna dapat melihat koleksi foto tanpa harus berpindah secara manual di antara masing-masing ponsel.
Selain berbagi data, Xiaomi dikabarkan menghadirkan sinkronisasi dua arah untuk notifikasi dan pesan. Pengguna juga dapat mengendalikan smartphone Xiaomi melalui layar Mac atau iPad menggunakan aplikasi Mi Connect Desktop. Jika seluruh fitur ini berjalan sesuai klaim, integrasi tersebut berpotensi memudahkan pengguna yang sehari-hari memakai perangkat dari kedua ekosistem.

items.content:
Xiaomi dikabarkan menyiapkan integrasi yang lebih luas antara HyperOS 4 dan ekosistem Apple. Pembaruan ini memungkinkan pengguna smartphone Xiaomi bertukar data dengan iPhone, sekaligus mengakses sejumlah fitur lintas perangkat yang sebelumnya lebih identik dengan ekosistem Apple sendiri.
Melalui integrasi tersebut, pengguna dapat berbagi foto, file, kontak, dan halaman web antara smartphone Xiaomi dan iPhone. HyperOS 4 juga disebut mendukung akses ke album foto berbasis cloud dari kedua perangkat, sehingga pengguna dapat melihat koleksi foto tanpa harus berpindah secara manual di antara masing-masing ponsel.
Selain berbagi data, Xiaomi dikabarkan menghadirkan sinkronisasi dua arah untuk notifikasi dan pesan. Pengguna juga dapat mengendalikan smartphone Xiaomi melalui layar Mac atau iPad menggunakan aplikasi Mi Connect Desktop. Jika seluruh fitur ini berjalan sesuai klaim, integrasi tersebut berpotensi memudahkan pengguna yang sehari-hari memakai perangkat dari kedua ekosistem.
Baca Juga: Xiaomi 18 Ultra Dikabarkan Batal, Harga Jadi Salah Satu Pertimbangannya
Berbagi Data dan Sinkronisasi Antar Perangkat
Kemampuan berbagi foto, dokumen, kontak, dan tautan menjadi salah satu bagian utama integrasi HyperOS 4. Dukungan album foto cloud juga memungkinkan akses koleksi gambar melalui iPhone maupun smartphone Xiaomi. Sementara itu, sinkronisasi notifikasi secara real-time dan balasan pesan instan dirancang agar aktivitas pengguna tetap terhubung di kedua perangkat.
Meski demikian, fitur lintas ekosistem ini tidak sepenuhnya otomatis tanpa persyaratan. Pengguna disebut perlu memasang aplikasi konektivitas Xiaomi dan menggunakan akun Xiaomi yang sama agar fitur terkait dapat berjalan. Artinya, pengalaman penggunaan tetap bergantung pada konfigurasi perangkat serta dukungan perangkat lunak yang tersedia.
HyperOS 4 Mulai Diperluas pada Oktober
HyperOS 4 disebut pertama kali hadir pada Xiaomi 18 Pro Max. Xiaomi juga diperkirakan mulai memperluas distribusinya pada 15 Oktober, meskipun jadwal tersebut belum menjamin seluruh perangkat akan menerima pembaruan pada waktu yang sama. Ketersediaan fitur tertentu juga berpotensi bergantung pada model perangkat dan versi aplikasi yang digunakan.
Integrasi ini memperlihatkan upaya Xiaomi untuk membuat perangkatnya lebih mudah digunakan bersama produk dari ekosistem lain. Namun, kemampuan berbagi data dan mengontrol ponsel melalui Mac atau iPad belum tentu menghadirkan pengalaman yang sepenuhnya setara dengan integrasi dalam satu ekosistem. Detail mengenai kompatibilitas perangkat, batasan fitur, dan cakupan distribusi masih diperlukan untuk menilai seberapa luas fungsi tersebut dapat digunakan.

items.author: Yus Lianson
items.content:
Apple akan menggelar acara bertajuk “Welcome Home” pada Selasa, (13/10/2026) pukul 09.00 waktu setempat atau sekitar 20.00 WIB. Kabar ini diperkuat lewat cuitan Greg Joswiak, Senior Vice President of Worldwide Marketing Apple, di akun X miliknya.
Seperti biasa, Apple tidak akan mengelar acara besar-besaran layaknya peluncuran perangkat di bulan September. Alih-alih, perusahaan mengundang sejumlah media untuk mencoba langsung perangkat barunya, dan mengirim rilis untuk masing-masing produk.
Baca Juga: OpenAI Ubah Cara ChatGPT Menjawab, Tak Lagi Sekadar Teks
Video teaser yang Greg unggah di X menampilkan logo ikonik Apple berwarna pelangi dengan tulisan “Welcome Home” memunculkan berbagai dugaan, di mana peluncuran kali ini berkaitan dengan perangkat rumah pintar (smart home).
Meski begitu, perusahaan berbasis di Cupertino tersebut belum mengungkap produk yang akan diperkenalkan. Namun berdasarkan beberapa rumor, setidaknya ada tiga perangkat yang bakal diungkap, yakni smart home hub, HomePod mini generasi baru, dan Apple TV 4K.
Apple Home Hub, Apa Itu?
Home hub. (Doc: MacRumors)
Sebelumnya, berbagai rumor tentang smart home hub ini sudah lama beredar di internet. Akan tetapi, perusahaan urung merilis perangkat ini ke pasaran dan siap diluncurkan bersamaan dengan Siri berbasis AI.
Tampil sebagai pusat kendali berbagai perangkat smart home dalam ekosistem Apple, perangkat ini dirumorkan punya layar 6 inci dengan dua pilihan desain, entah dipasang di dinding, dan memiliki dudukan dilengkapi speaker.
Sistem operasinya diperkirakan berbasis tvOS dengan nama homeOS, dengan tampilan aplikasi dan widget untuk menampilkan kalender keluarga, jam, serta kontrol perangkat rumah pintar yang terhubung.
Kabarnya, pengguna bisa mendapatkan informasi atau memberi perintah lewat suara ke Siri AI.
Home hub juga dirumorkan memiliki kamera untuk panggilan video dan memutar konten. Salah satu contoh penggunaannya adalah ditaruh di dapur untuk mengikuti panduan resep.
Lewat sensor kehadiran dan kamera dengan pengenalan wajah, perangkat ini disebut bisa mengenali anggota keluarga di dekatnya dan menampilkan antarmuka sesuai pengguna yang terdeteksi.
Harganya diperkirakan mulai sekitar USD 350. Angka ini belum dikonfirmasi raksasa teknologi tersebut.
HomePod mini dan Apple TV 4K?
HomePod mini.
HomePod mini generasi baru disebut mendapat prosesor lebih cepat dan pilihan warna tambahan. Pembuat iPhone ini juga dirumorkan memasang chip jaringan N1 yang mendukung Wi-Fi 7, Bluetooth 6, dan Thread. Peningkatan utama yang diperkirakan adalah Siri berbasis AI.
Apple TV 4K terbaru dirumorkan memakai chip A19 atau A19 Pro dengan RAM 8GB hingga 12GB, serta chip N1 yang sama. Lonjakan spesifikasi ini diduga terkait rencana Apple menghadirkan Siri AI yang lebih lengkap di perangkat hiburan rumah.
Acara Berbeda untuk Lini MacBook Baru?
Laporan terpisah menyebut perusahaan berpotensi menggelar peluncuran berikutnya pada 27 Oktober, dengan produk dirumorkan mencakup MacBook berlayar OLED touchscreen dan iPad mini dengan panel OLED. Pembaruan iMac serta MacBook Pro 14 inci juga disebut tengah dipersiapkan.
Akan tetapi, informasi mengenai acara 27 Oktober maupun perangkat tersebut masih berupa rumor, bukan jadwal peluncuran yang telah dikonfirmasi perusahaan.
Bagi pengguna di Indonesia, acara Welcome home akan menjadi kesempatan melihat arah pengembangan ekosistem rumah pintar Apple, terutama bagaimana perusahaan mengintegrasikan Siri berbasis AI dengan perangkat rumah tangga.
Belum ada informasi mengenai ketersediaan maupun harga produk-produk dirumorkan untuk pasar Indonesia. Kepastiannya baru dapat diketahui setelah Apple memberikan pengumuman resmi pada 13 Oktober mendatang.
CEO Baru Apple John Ternus Dikabarkan Siapkan Perombakan Besar
John Ternus, CEO Apple dengan iPhone Duo (Sumber: BBC)
Di sisi lain, John Ternus baru sekitar satu bulan menjabat sebagai CEO setelah resmi menggantikan Tim Cook pada 1 September 2026. Kini, John Ternus dikabarkan mulai menyiapkan perubahan terhadap cara Apple mengembangkan dan meluncurkan produk, dengan fokus pada proses yang lebih cepat serta struktur perusahaan yang lebih ramping.
Menurut laporan Bloomberg yang ditulis Mark Gurman, Ternus disebut ingin Apple tidak terlalu terpaku pada pola peluncuran produk selama ini, terutama jendela rilis pada musim semi dan musim gugur. Mantan kepala hardware engineering itu juga dikabarkan mendorong tim produk untuk lebih eksperimental dan mengembangkan lebih banyak perangkat dalam waktu yang lebih singkat.
Perubahan tersebut disebut mulai terasa di internal perusahaan. Sejumlah karyawan menggambarkan situasi sebagai cukup sibuk, sementara perusahaan juga dilaporkan telah melakukan pemangkasan posisi di divisi hardware engineering dalam beberapa pekan terakhir. Meski begitu, laporan tersebut belum menjelaskan secara pasti bagaimana perubahan ini akan memengaruhi strategi produk Apple dalam jangka panjang.

Treasuries held their gains from the US session, while a Bloomberg gauge of the dollar traded steady.“For now, the focus remains on whether the selling in AI and semiconductors develops into a broader risk reduction, or whether investors use the pullback to rebuild exposure ahead of earnings,” wrote Chris Weston, head of research at Pepperstone.The OpenAI revenue questions added to concerns over AI spending as elevated borrowing costs make the vast sums flowing into data centers and computing infrastructure harder to justify. Investors are increasingly looking for evidence that revenue can keep pace with the investment required to develop and run AI models.While OpenAI’s roughly $50 billion revenue is an uptick from the prior year, it’s still less than recently reported estimates.OpenAI, Anthropic and other AI firms have often touted their annualized revenue — a projection of annual sales based on a shorter period — as a key growth metric. However, not all companies measure it the same way. Anthropic’s annualized revenue hit $65 billion by the end of July, Bloomberg News previously reported. In stocks, the weakness remained concentrated in technology rather than spreading across the broader market. More than two-thirds of S&P 500 members advanced, while small-cap shares were little changed as investors rotated toward defensive sectors.Meanwhile, Treasuries advanced on Thursday after solid demand at a 30-year debt auction pulled long-dated yields back from more than two-decade highs. The rally extended after Trump said he would hold off on attacking Iran again until after the US midterm elections on Nov. 3.The gains provided some respite from a months-long selloff in longer-term debt, fueled by concerns that the Iran war will keep energy prices and inflation elevated, alongside mounting worries over government finances.The outlook for rates remained under pressure, however, as Federal Reserve officials signaled more tightening ahead. Governor Christopher Waller said further increases will probably be needed to bring inflation under control, while St. Louis Fed President Alberto Musalem said rates should rise over the next six to nine months without endorsing a move this month.“To bring inflation back to target in a timely manner, more monetary policy firming will be required,” Musalem said Thursday at a Bloomberg event in New York.

By Chidinma Chukwu, Abuja
ABUJA — The Federal Government has activated more than 1,400 primary healthcare centres, PHCs, across the country to provide primary eye care services as part of efforts to expand access to quality eye care and reduce avoidable blindness.
The Minister of State for Health and Social Welfare, Dr Iziaq Adekunle Salako, disclosed this on Thursday in Abuja at an event to commemorate the 2026 World Sight Day.
The event, themed, “The Value of Vision: Investing in People, Productivity and Nigeria’s Future,” highlighted the need for sustained investment in eye health and stronger integration of eye care into the primary healthcare system.
Represented by the Director of E-Health Division, Mrs Doris Afam-Aneke, Salako said the integration of eye care into the primary healthcare system was central to the government’s strategy of making eye health services accessible, affordable and sustainable, particularly for Nigerians in underserved communities.
He said the government had also trained more than 3,000 healthcare workers across 16 states, equipping them with skills to provide essential eye care services at the community level.
According to him, the trained workers were helping to improve early detection of eye conditions, raise community awareness and facilitate prompt referral of patients requiring specialised treatment.
Salako said, “A major pillar of our eye health strategy has been the integration and expansion of primary eye care services across the country.
“The evidence is clear. Sustainable progress in eye health can only be achieved when services are available at the point closest to the people. This is why government has prioritised the strengthening of primary healthcare systems as the foundation for delivering essential eye care interventions.”
He added that the integration of primary eye care into the PHC system had expanded the capacity of frontline health facilities to prevent, detect and manage common eye conditions, while ensuring timely referral of patients requiring specialised care.
Salako also disclosed that more than 1.5 million pairs of prescription spectacles had been distributed to Nigerians across 16 states through the Effective Spectacle Coverage Initiative, known as Jigi-Bola 2.0.
He said preparations were at an advanced stage to extend the initiative to 10 additional states, adding that the expansion would further improve access to affordable vision correction for Nigerians with uncorrected refractive errors.
The minister further disclosed that more than 1.5 million school-age children had been screened for visual problems through the school eye health programme, with those requiring treatment linked to appropriate care.
He said four additional vision centres were being established in Enugu, Edo, Sokoto and Nasarawa states to strengthen secondary eye care services, improve referral pathways and expand access to specialised treatment.
Salako reaffirmed the Federal Government’s commitment to eliminating avoidable blindness, announcing plans to conduct 25,000 free cataract surgeries across the country by the end of 2027.
He said improved vision would enhance learning, productivity and the quality of life of Nigerians.
The minister also said Nigeria would co-host the first Global Summit on Eye Health scheduled for November 2 in Antigua and Barbuda, describing it as an opportunity for the country to contribute to global efforts to integrate eye health into universal health coverage.
He said the National Eye Care Commitment was anchored on integrating primary eye care into PHCs, expanding the provision of ready-made spectacles through Jigi-Bola 2.0, improving effective cataract surgical coverage, strengthening the eye health workforce and removing barriers to eye care.
Over 80% of visual impairment avoidable
The National Coordinator, National Eye, Ear and Sensory Functions Health Programme, Dr Oteri Okolo Eme, said more than 80 per cent of visual impairment in Nigeria was avoidable, making the integration of primary eye care into the primary healthcare system a strategic priority.
Eme said the government had established a network of national master trainers across the six geopolitical zones and trained about 4,000 primary healthcare workers, while more than 2,200 others had received specific training in primary eye care.
She added that state-level trainers and facilitators had also been trained to support the expansion of primary eye care services.
The coordinator said the government was developing protocols for newborn eye screening to facilitate early detection and treatment of conditions that could lead to visual impairment.
“We are protecting our children and future generations. We are in the process of developing protocols for newborn screening because we believe that if we detect causes of visual impairment early, we will be able to address them and ensure better outcomes,” she said.
“We are also tackling national priority eye conditions by developing standardised guidelines.
“Nigeria will co-host the upcoming first-ever Global Summit on Eye Health in Antigua and Barbuda on November 2. This provides an opportunity to examine the current state of eye health and make the case for accelerated action.”
Eme called on governments, development partners, the private sector, health workers, teachers, the media and Nigerians to support efforts to improve eye health.
She urged governments to provide dedicated budgetary allocations for eye health and encouraged Nigerians to undergo regular eye examinations and take steps to protect their sight.
Also speaking, the Executive Secretary of the National Commission for Persons with Disabilities, Chief Ayuba Gufwan, said investment in eye health was an investment in people.
He added that supporting persons with visual impairment and ensuring accessible eye care services could significantly enhance participation in education, employment and community life.
The Chief Medical Director, National Eye Centre, Kaduna, Dr Amina Hassan Wali, called for stronger partnerships, greater public awareness, early presentation for eye problems, regular eye examinations and sustained investment in eye health.
“Let us work together to ensure that no one is left behind and that everyone can enjoy the gift of sight. Let us all love our eyes and make eye health a priority,” she said.
The high point of the event was the unveiling of the National Eye Health Commitments in alignment with the upcoming Global Summit on Eye Health.
The post World Sight Day: FG activates 1,400 PHCs for eye care appeared first on Vanguard News.

By James Ogunnaike, Abeokuta
Pensioners in Ogun State have appealed to Governor Dapo Abiodun to release outstanding gratuities owed retirees from January 2021 to June 2025 and approve consequential pension increases for long-serving retirees.
The Chairman of the Nigeria Union of Pensioners (NUP), Ogun State Council, Comrade Waheed Oloyede, made the appeal at the 2026 Pensioners’ Day celebration held in Abeokuta, the state capital.
Oloyede, while commending the Abiodun administration for what he described as its unprecedented compassion towards pensioners, urged the governor to take further steps to address the financial challenges confronting retirees in the state.
He said pensioners appreciated the achievements of the administration but appealed for additional interventions to give hope to members still awaiting their retirement benefits.
He said, “As Oliver Twist, we want to ask for more. We humbly request that you benevolently approve that the remaining gratuity from January 2021 to June 2025 be released to would-be beneficiaries, to give our long-expectant members a ray of hope.”
The NUP chairman also called for the implementation of consequential adjustments in pensions arising from the 2019 Federal Government circular and subsequent increases in the national minimum wage.
According to him, many retirees who left service 10, 25 and even 30 years ago still receive as little as N30,000 monthly pension despite the sharp rise in the cost of living.
Oloyede said the situation had made life increasingly difficult for elderly citizens, particularly as the prices of drugs, food and other essential commodities continued to rise.
“The cost of drugs, food and other necessities has skyrocketed beyond the reach of the ordinary citizen, resulting in serious health challenges and, eventually, untimely deaths,” he said.
He urged the state government to approve the pension adjustments, saying the move would provide relief to retirees, promote parity and improve the welfare of senior citizens in the state.
Oloyede added that implementing the adjustment would also leave a lasting legacy for the governor, saying it would “imprint the governor’s name in gold in the history of the state.”
Pensioners commend Abiodun
The pensioners’ leader, however, commended Abiodun for what he described as significant improvements in the welfare of retirees, particularly the prompt and regular payment of monthly pensions.
According to him, unlike in many states where pensioners still face delays, Ogun retirees now receive their monthly pensions as and when due.
“You have restored our dignity and given us peace of mind. You have wiped away tears from the faces of our aged members,” Oloyede said.
He also commended the administration for clearing the backlog of gratuities owed by previous administrations up to December 2020 for state retirees and December 2021 for local government retirees, describing the payments as running into multiple billions of naira.
“For many years, many of our members died without receiving their gratuity. Your administration has changed that ugly narrative,” he added.
Oloyede further appreciated the state government for introducing a free health insurance scheme for state and local government pensioners.
He, however, raised concerns over complaints about the implementation of the scheme at some health facilities, urging the agency supervising the programme to investigate the complaints and address identified challenges.
NLC seeks resolution of grievances
In his goodwill message, the Ogun State Chairman of the Nigeria Labour Congress (NLC), Comrade Hameed Ademola-Benco, commended the governor for his interventions in the welfare of pensioners.
He urged the state government to consider all outstanding grievances raised by retirees, stressing that pensioners should not be made to struggle before accessing benefits due to them.
“We appreciate the governor for all he has done. We appeal to him to kindly look into every grievance that has been tabled because retirees should not have to struggle for their benefits,” Ademola-Benco said.
Abiodun responds
Responding, Governor Abiodun, who was represented by the Head of Service, Mr Olaranwaju Saka, said the demands made by the pensioners were legitimate.
He assured the retirees that the administration was already looking into their requests and would continue to honour its obligations to pensioners.
According to him, the government would deploy available resources towards addressing outstanding retirement benefits and ensuring the welfare of retirees.

…..As Vanguard summit holds today
By Sola Ogundipe
Nigeria’s response to the mental health challenges facing its young people comes under fresh scrutiny today as policymakers, psychiatrists, health professionals, security and correctional authorities, regulators, media and other stakeholders converge in Lagos for the 4th Vanguard Mental Health Summit holding at the Civic Centre, Victoria Island, Lagos.
The summit, organised by Vanguard Media Limited, comes against growing concerns over depression, suicide, substance abuse, anxiety, trauma, social isolation and the mounting psychological pressures confronting young Nigerians online and offline.
With the theme, “Advancing Youth Mental Health in Nigeria through Access, Action and Advocacy,” and sub-theme, “Mental Health in a Digital Age: Navigating Social Media, Technology and Wellbeing,” the gathering is expected to move the conversation beyond awareness and confront the more difficult issues of access to care, early intervention, treatment, rehabilitation and accountability.
At the centre of the discussion is the question of what happens when a young Nigerian needs mental healthcare but cannot find, afford or access it. Beyond the expert presentations, the summit is expected to confront the gap between Nigeria’s mental health policies and the experience of young people who actually need care.
Chief Host of the summit is Lagos State Commissioner for Health, Prof. Akin Abayomi, while the Coordinating Minister of Health and Social Welfare, Prof. Muhammad Ali Pate, and Chairman of the National Drug Law Enforcement Agency (NDLEA) Brig. Gen. Buba Marwa (rtd.) are Special G inuests of Honour.
The forum will be chaired by Corps Marshal Shehu Mohammed of the Federal Road Safety Corps (FRSC). The Director-General of the National Agency for Food and Drug Administration and Control (NAFDAC) Prof. Mojisola Adeyeye, and the Controller of Corrections, Lagos State Command, Nigerian Correctional Service, Mr Daramola George are special guests.
Other stakeholders that will feature are President of the Association of Psychiatrists of Nigeria, Dr. Veronica Oluyemisi Nyamali; Professor Taiwo Lateef Sheikh, Professor of Psychiatry and Psychopharmacology at Ahmadu Bello University, Zaria; Prof. Mashudat Bello-Mojeed, Professor of Psychiatry and Public Health, as well as senior officials of the Lagos State Ministry of Health, mental health practitioners, academics, development partners, civil society organisations, youth representatives and educators.
Nyamali will deliver the keynote address, while Sheikh will speak on “Mental Health as Our Social Capital.” The President of the Nigerian Medical Association will speak on “Making Youth Mental Health Everyone’s Business: From Policy to Practice,” bringing the perspective of the nation’s umbrella body for medical practitioners to discussions on how mental health policies can translate into practical support and services for young Nigerians.
A major panel session, “Who Takes Responsibility for Young People’s Mental Health?”, will examine the roles of government, families, schools, healthcare providers, communities, civil society and technology platforms in preventing young people from reaching crisis points.
The summit will also examine substance abuse and its intersection with the justice system and other attendant effects. Technology’s growing role in mental healthcare will also come under scrutiny, including the use of Transcranial Magnetic Stimulation in treating common mental health conditions among young people who do not respond adequately to conventional treatment.
As the stakeholders gather, health commentators note that the question is no longer whether Nigeria has a youth mental health problem, rather, the question is whether its institutions are ready to take responsibility for tackling it. Their participation underscores how deeply mental health now cuts across substance abuse, public safety, the justice system, correctional services and drug regulation.
The post Mental health: Nigeria’s action gap comes under scrutiny appeared first on Vanguard News.

items.content:
By Ugochukwu Alaribe
UMUAHIA — The Medical and Dental Council of Nigeria (MDCN) has warned newly inducted medical doctors against professional misconduct in the discharge of their duties.
The Registrar of the council, Prof. Fatima Kyari, gave the warning in Aba while inducting 16 medical doctors who graduated from Rhema University.
Kyari, who was represented by Tijani Ali Mandaka, said medicine was one of the most regulated professions and that practitioners were subject to oversight by the council, the public and relevant government agencies.
She said allegations of professional misconduct against doctors were subject to investigation in accordance with the council’s procedures.
“Medicine and Surgery is one of the most regulated professions. The profession is under close watch by council and the public in the area of education, registration and practice. So, any allegation of misconduct against a doctor will be thoroughly investigated,” she said.
Kyari explained that the council had two disciplinary organs — the Medical and Dental Practitioners Investigation Panel and the Medical and Dental Practitioners Disciplinary Tribunal.
She said the Investigation Panel was responsible for preliminary investigations into allegations of professional misconduct, while cases established against practitioners could be referred to the Disciplinary Tribunal for further action in accordance with the law.
She added that sanctions available under the council’s disciplinary process could include admonition, suspension and removal from the council’s register, depending on the circumstances of each case and the applicable regulations.
The registrar urged the newly inducted doctors to take their housemanship programmes seriously as part of the requirements for registration and certification by the council.
She also advised them to uphold professional standards throughout their careers.
Describing the induction as a historic milestone, the Vice-Chancellor of Rhema University, Prof. Ogbonnaya Onwudike, reminded the new doctors that their medical degrees represented a responsibility to serve humanity.
Onwudike urged them to maintain good character, which he described as an important professional asset.
“As you take the physician’s oath, remember that a medical degree is not merely a certificate; it is a call to serve humanity. You are called to a life of great responsibility as human beings will trust their lives to your knowledge, judgment and compassion,” he said.
The Vice-Chancellor commended the MDCN for its role in maintaining standards in medical education and expressed appreciation for its support during the training and induction process.
He said the university remained committed to providing medical education in line with applicable national and international standards.
The Provost of the university’s College of Medicine, Prof. Maduka James Awa, urged the new doctors to be worthy ambassadors of the institution and apply their knowledge responsibly in their professional careers.
He also commended the Chancellor and Founder of the university, Bro Emma Okorie, for his vision for the institution.
Okorie, in his remarks, said the 16 newly inducted doctors had undergone the required training and urged them to contribute positively to the medical profession.
The event featured the presentation of awards to outstanding graduates, including the best graduating student, Dr Ugwokaegbe Anointing.

By Adeola Badru
IBADAN — The Senator Sharafadeen Alli Campaign Organisation (SSACO) has alleged attacks on All Progressives Congress (APC) candidates, supporters and political activities in Ibadan, Oyo State.
The organisation alleged that Alhaja Tawakalitu Alli, wife of the APC governorship candidate, Sharafadeen Alli, was attacked during a medical outreach she organised at Ibikunle House, Ayeye, Ibadan.
It also alleged that the campaign teams of the APC candidate for Oyo South Senatorial District, Aderemi Oseni, and the party’s candidate for Ibadan North-West/Ibadan South-West Federal Constituency, Folake Olunloyo-Oshinowo, were attacked during separate campaign events at Agbaje Market, Orita-Merin, and Idi-Arere, Ibadan.
In a statement issued by its Director of Media and Publicity, Bisi Oladele, SSACO described the alleged incidents as attempts to disrupt political activities ahead of the 2027 elections.
The organisation called on Governor Seyi Makinde and the Allied Peoples Movement (APM) governorship candidate, Bimbo Adekanmbi, to ensure that political actors are allowed to campaign freely.
“The SSACO is at the least miffed by the unwarranted and barbaric attacks by Allied People’s Movement (APM) hoodlums on Alhaja Tawakalitu Alli during a medical outreach she organised at Ibikunle House, Ayeye, Ibadan, on Wednesday,” the statement said.
It further alleged that Oseni and Olunloyo-Oshinowo were attacked during separate campaign events in the city.
SSACO said the alleged incidents would not force the APC to suspend its campaign activities, stressing that its candidates and supporters were entitled to associate, assemble and campaign within the law.
“The SSACO calls on Governor Seyi Makinde and the party’s governorship candidate, Hon. Bimbo Adekanmbi, to rein in on their supporters,” it said.
The organisation also called on security agencies to investigate the alleged attacks, identify those responsible and prosecute them where appropriate.
“The SSACO calls on security agencies to fish out these perpetrators of violence and bring them to book in order to serve justice to the victims and also serve as a deterrence to violence in our dear state,” it said.
SSACO further urged the state government to protect residents irrespective of their political affiliations, saying the alleged attacks posed a threat to peaceful political participation.
“As the chief security officer of the state, Governor Makinde carries the responsibility to protect all residents irrespective of their political leanings,” the organisation said.

items.content:
By Henry Ojelu
The Lagos State AIDS Control Agency, LSACA, has urged employers and workers in the food sector to end stigma and discrimination against people living with HIV, stressing that the virus cannot be transmitted through the preparation, handling or serving of food.
The agency made the call at a sensitisation meeting for food handlers and representatives of food-sector associations on HIV-related workplace practices and applicable legal provisions, held Thursday at the STO Resource Centre Hall, CBD, Ikeja.
The meeting was aimed at dispelling misconceptions about HIV transmission and promoting safe, inclusive and non-discriminatory practices in the food sector.
Speaking at the event, the Chief Executive Officer of LSACA, Dr. Folakemi Animashaun, represented by the Director, Projects, Mr. Michael Essien, said there was no scientific basis for excluding people living with HIV from food-related employment.
Animashaun said HIV was not transmitted through handling, preparing or serving food, sharing utensils or through ordinary workplace and social contact.
According to her, “a person’s HIV status does not make them a food-safety risk,” urging food-sector stakeholders to base workplace decisions on scientific evidence rather than fear and misinformation.
She cautioned against using legitimate food-safety and medical fitness requirements as a basis for discriminatory HIV screening or exclusion from employment.
The LSACA boss also stressed the need to protect the confidentiality of workers’ HIV-related information, saying such information must be handled with appropriate consent, respect and dignity.
She noted that stigma and discrimination could discourage people from testing, accessing treatment and using health services for fear of losing their jobs or having their status disclosed without consent.
Animashaun urged food establishments and associations to review their workplace policies to ensure compliance with the principles of confidentiality, informed consent and non-discrimination.
Also speaking, the facilitator, Mr. Tiamiyu Hussein of the Lagos State Safety Commission, stressed the importance of maintaining safe and healthy workplaces without discriminating against workers.
Hussein explained the distinction between legitimate medical fitness assessments for food handlers and HIV screening, urging employers to ensure that occupational health and safety procedures were appropriately implemented.
He further encouraged employers and workers to protect the confidentiality of health information and ensure that no person was subjected to unfair treatment on account of HIV status.
The sensitisation also covered HIV transmission, prevention and treatment, with participants reminded that there is no risk of acquiring HIV from food prepared, handled or served by a person living with the virus.
Participants were encouraged to challenge misconceptions, promote fair employment practices and support appropriate referral and grievance mechanisms across the food sector.

items.content:
To review pensions of former governors
By Henry Obetta
THE Lagos State Governorship Candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress, NDC, Mr Funso Doherty, has unveiled a 34-point manifesto he said would take the state to the next level, if elected. He also unveiled Mrs. Tolani Animashaun as his running mate in the February 6, 2027 governorship poll.
Presenting his manifesto titled: Ònà Tuntun (New Road), yesterday, in Lagos, Doherty said the manifesto contained 34 specific commitments across health, education, housing, transport, environment, jobs and small business and honest governance.
Specifically, Doherty, among others, promised to deliver in four years 150,000 homes, provide free healthcare for pregnant women and children under-16, free education through secondary school and technical colleges. He also promised to provide free textbooks, and nutritious meals for students in public schools.
He added: “Then for those children who are in public schools, Lagos State Public Schools, who need to be transported to their school, public transport for children in school uniforms going to their school will be provided.
“The whole objective is that there should be no child in Lagos State that will not benefit from a quality education because his or her parents cannot afford it or because of the circumstances of his or her birth. Because if we don’t, it is our future that we are mortgaging.”
On transportation, Doherty pledged to modernise the state’s transport system, particularly the Red and Blue Line rail networks, by improving connectivity between them. He also promised to establish decentralised road maintenance frameworks across the local governments to ensure more efficient and timely maintenance of roads.
The NDC governorship candidate pledged to run a transparent administration, promising to lead by example and ensure strict enforcement of the Code of Conduct for Public Officers.
He pledged to review all major public-private partnerships, PPPs in Lagos, saying the review would determine whether corrective actions were necessary. He also promised to review public servants’ salaries and allowances to ensure public officers receive reasonable remuneration, arguing that poor pay could undermine efficiency and integrity in the civil service.
The candidate also promised to subject the benefits and packages of former governors to an independent review and make the outcome public.
He further pledged to enforce compliance with government rules and prosecute criminal activity regardless of the position of those involved. “And this applies from the top all the way to the bottom,” he said, adding that his administration would regularly publish its progress and openly acknowledge areas where it fell short.
Doherty also criticised the current Lagos state government, arguing that it had failed to adequately meet the needs of residents despite the state’s substantial financial resources. He said the government should translate its revenue into improved public services and a better quality of life for Lagosians
In her remarks, the NDC deputy governorship candidate, Mrs Tolani Animashaun, pledged to work with Doherty, to build a Lagos where the government prioritises the needs of residents.
Citing her experience in education, finance and community mobilisation, she said the ticket would promote better opportunities for young people, improve education and ensure accountability in the management of public funds.
“Government that works for the people. That is what this team believes in and that is why I am here,” she said, urging residents to support the campaign and “lend us your hand” to achieve our vision for the state.

Amaechi also criticised Nigeria’s energy sector, arguing that the country had failed to harness its abundant natural resources to drive industrial production and economic growth.
He noted that Nigeria had substantial crude oil and natural gas reserves, particularly in the South-South region, but had failed to translate its resource wealth into sustainable prosperity for its citizens.
The former minister called for policies that would stimulate domestic production rather than increase the financial burden on consumers and businesses.
He said Atiku Abubakar, the ADC presidential candidate, would introduce production subsidies to strengthen local industries, boost domestic production and ease economic pressure on Nigerians if elected president in 2027.

items.author: Henry Oduah
items.content:
President Donald Trump on Thursday ruled out attacking Iran before the US midterm elections on November 3, saying Washington was holding “productive discussions” with Tehran.
Trump’s post on his Truth Social platform followed a surge in oil prices on Thursday driven by media reports suggesting potential new US strikes prior to those elections.
“I want to make it clear to everybody that, while Iran is in very bad condition, both Economically and Militarily, and while the Blockade will remain in full force and effect…we will not be attacking Iran at any time prior to the Midterm Elections,” he wrote.
“We are having productive discussions with the Islamic Republic of Iran,” he added, without providing additional details.
The Atlantic magazine reported on Wednesday that the White House had asked the Pentagon to develop options to strike Iranian targets that could be used before the midterms. The New York Times published a similar report on Thursday, saying the plans were being developed despite Trump’s “ambivalence”.
The rise in crude oil prices has also been fueled by persistent tensions in the Strait of Hormuz — a strategic chokepoint for the global oil trade — as well as hostilities between Yemen’s Iran-backed Houthis and Saudi Arabia.
In a recent sign of those tensions, an oil tanker sailing off the north coast of Qatar reported being struck “by multiple projectiles,” causing an unspecified number of casualties, the UKMTO maritime agency said Wednesday.
Polls suggest that US voters are strongly dissatisfied over rising fuel prices, linked to the conflict launched by the United States and Israel against Iran in February.
The US leader has repeatedly insisted in recent weeks that the United States has effectively won the Iran war, despite ongoing unrest and a recent security threat that forced the withdrawal of American bombers from a base in England.
But Trump’s claims that prices will fall as soon as the Iran war is over have so far fallen on deaf ears with voters.
The midterm elections will shape the final two years of Trump’s presidential term as his Republican Party risks losing its current grip on Congress.
Although Trump is not on the ballot, he is heavily involved in the campaign, holding numerous rallies in an attempt to limit the damage or even turn the political tide.
Trump has warned he faces a possible third impeachment if Democrats retake the House of Representatives, and the White House is preparing for a slew of investigations into corruption and abuse of power.
The US president also on Thursday sought to calm a furor over his comments at a rally earlier this week that Iran could “take out” the cities of Los Angeles and San Diego.
Trump, 80, blamed the “fake and artificial news” for misinterpreting the remarks, which Democrats pounced on.
“In actuality, what I was talking about was that a temporary increase in the price of Gasoline is a small price to pay for Iran not having a Nuclear Weapon and, if you want to see a big price, can you imagine what it would be like if they bombed San Diego and/or Los Angeles?” Trump said on Truth Social.

items.author: Henry Oduah
items.content:
By Ikechukwu Nnochiri
Former Governor of Kaduna State, Nasir El-Rufai, has failed to persuade the Federal High Court in Abuja to stop the Independent Corrupt Practices and Other Related Offences Commission (ICPC) and other anti-graft agencies in the country from freezing his bank accounts.
In a ruling by Justice Joyce Abdulmalik, the court dismissed a suit filed by the former governor, who has been in detention, seeking an order restraining federal government agencies from moving against his assets.
The court held that the suit not only lacked merit but was speculative, as no reasonable cause of action was disclosed against the agencies the applicant listed as defendants.
Therefore, the Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC), the Department of State Services (DSS) and the Attorney General of the Federation (AGF) were struck out from the case.
In the suit he filed on February 24, El-Rufai prayed the court for an interim injunction directing the respondents to maintain the status quo ante regarding his assets.
According to him, the order was necessary to prevent him from being placed in a state of helplessness. He insisted that the severance pay he received upon completing his tenure as governor of Kaduna State between 2015 and 2023 could not reasonably be suspected to be proceeds of any unlawful activity.
He urged the court to declare that properties purchased from his severance pay were lawfully acquired.
The banks the applicant prayed the court to protect from the respondents included Zenith Bank Plc, Naira Account Number: 1007158671; Zenith Bank Plc, Domiciliary Account Number: 507 1511327; Guaranty Trust Bank (GTB) Plc, Account Number: 0023824978; Access Bank, Dollar Account Number: 1396386493; and Access Bank, Naira Account Number: 1396382103.
El-Rufai also sought a declaration that any attempt by the respondents to apply for, obtain or execute any interim or final forfeiture or freezing order, without first establishing a reasonable suspicion supported by credible evidence as required by relevant law, would amount to a breach of his rights.
He relied on Section 17(1) of the Advance Fee Fraud and Other Related Offences Act, 2006, and the Supreme Court decision in Melrose General Services Ltd v. EFCC (2024) SC/1519/2019, to pray the court to declare that, as a citizen of Nigeria, he is entitled to the presumption of innocence and the protection of his fundamental rights.
He argued that any action by the respondents seeking to circumvent his constitutionally guaranteed rights through ex parte applications that conceal material facts would amount to a breach of Section 36(5) of the Constitution and a violation of the principles of fair hearing.

Six-time French champions Bordeaux, who were sanctioned in the summer for financial irregularities, will play the current season in the sixth tier of French football, the Nouvelle-Aquitaine league confirmed on Thursday.
Bordeaux were sanctioned for failing to provide the roughly 10 million euros ($11.6 million) needed for the 2025-2026 financial year as well as 2026-2027 and meet debt payments.
Once one of France’s leading football clubs and the team where the country’s new head coach Zinedine Zidane made his name, Bordeaux was sold last month for a symbolic one euro to US-based investment group Park Bench who agreed to take on the remaining debt.
Two days after appearing before the oversight commission of the Nouvelle-Aquitaine league, which approved their recovery budget and issued “a positive opinion on their possible participation in Regional 1,” the club was unanimously approved to play in the top tier.
“Rebuilding can now begin,” said Dominique Delport, the new president chosen by Park Bench, speaking to AFP.
The new owners are due in commercial court on October 20 to ratify the new continuation plan, which now runs over 12 years, with the debt halved from 26 to 13 million euros.
The team is largely amateur although they are permitted five players on professional contracts, one of which will go to former Ligue 1 striker Baptiste Guillaume.
The club has produced many big names of French football including academy products Bixente Lizarazu and Christophe Dugarry who both played alongside Zidane in the 1998 World Cup-winning team.
A decade earlier Alain Giresse and Jean Tigana were part of a celebrated France midfield that won the European championships in 1984.
However, they were relegated to Ligue 2 in 2022 and then placed in judicial restructuring in 2024, which caused them to relinquish their professional status and their highly-rated academy.
