items.author: Nwafor
items.content:
The Nigerian Guild of Editors (NGE) has denied allegations of partisanship over the 22nd All Nigeria Editors Conference (ANEC) in Enugu and urged Nation Newspaper to apologise over its editorial on the conference.
The Guild was reacting to an editorial published by the newspaper on October 8, 2026, titled “Journalists Failed Journalism,” which questioned the NGE’s conduct over the participation of Peter Obi, presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), and Prof. Pat Utomi, a chieftain of the party, at the conference.
In a statement signed by the NGE President, Eze Anaba, and General Secretary, Onuoha Ukeh, the Guild said the editorial made serious allegations against its leadership, including the suggestion that the NGE acted in a partisan manner by allowing Obi and Utomi to address editors at the conference.
The Guild said the conclusion was not supported by the facts, stressing that ANEC 2026 was a professional gathering of editors and other stakeholders devoted to interrogating critical issues concerning democracy, elections, the media, artificial intelligence, disinformation and the future of Nigeria.
According to the NGE, the conference programme specifically provided for an “Executive Session” on the second day, designed to feature governors, political party chairmen, heads of government agencies and parastatals and other stakeholders.
It said the purpose of the session was to provide a platform for engagement between the media and key actors in Nigeria’s political and public space.
The Guild said it officially invited political parties, including the All Progressives Congress (APC), African Democratic Congress (ADC) and NDC, to participate in the relevant engagement.
It listed the APC chairman, Prof. Nentawe Yelwatda; ADC chairman, Senator David Mark; and NDC chairman, Senator Cleopas Moses Zuwoghe, among those invited.
The NGE said the invitations were followed by reminders, adding that Anaba personally spoke with Yelwatda and ADC Vice-Presidential candidate, Chibuike Amaechi, in connection with participation at the conference.
It added that Ukeh personally followed up with Paul Ibe, media aide to the ADC presidential candidate, Atiku Abubakar, to encourage the participation of the party and its leaders.
“These are verifiable facts. They fundamentally undermine the central premise of The Nation’s editorial,” the Guild said.
The NGE questioned whether the absence of some invited political figures should have prevented a candidate who was available and willing to attend from participating.
“If the Guild duly invited the political parties, sent reminders and personally followed up with their leaders and representatives, and some of those invited chose not to attend, should it prevent a candidate who was available and willing to attend from participating?” it asked.
The Guild acknowledged the right of Nation Newspaper and other media organisations to scrutinise its activities and express editorial opinions about the conduct of the conference.
It said such scrutiny was an important part of the accountability expected of professional institutions, including the media.
However, the NGE said the editorial ignored the broader range of political and governmental voices that featured at the conference.
The Guild noted that Tunde Rahman, media adviser to President Bola Tinubu, spoke on the administration, while the Minister of Information and National Orientation, Mohammed Idris, was represented at the conference by the Managing Director of the News Agency of Nigeria (NAN).
It also pointed out that Vice President Kashim Shettima addressed editors virtually from the United States.
“These engagements demonstrate the very opposite of the partisan picture painted by the editorial,” the Guild said.
The NGE also rejected the description of Obi’s appearance as an “ambush”, arguing that he attended a professional conference at which hundreds of editors and stakeholders were present.
“There is a fundamental distinction between providing a platform for engagement and supporting a political position,” it said.
The Guild described as “particularly unfortunate” the newspaper’s reference to its conduct as an “impunity of silence.”
It argued that the conference was a public professional gathering attended by hundreds of editors, journalists and stakeholders.
The NGE said the fact that Nation Newspaper or another newspaper chose not to report an occurrence did not make it secret or establish professional misconduct.
The Guild reaffirmed its commitment to providing platforms for robust and independent engagement with political actors, public officials, civil society organisations, electoral institutions and other stakeholders, without fear or favour.
“That is not partisanship. That is journalism,” the Guild said.
The NGE called on Nation Newspaper’s Editorial Board to acknowledge what it described as omissions in its editorial, correct the “misleading impressions” and offer an apology to the Guild and its leadership.

items.author: Mumini AbdulKareem, Ilorin
items.content:
Nigerians have questioned President Bola Tinubu’s motives following the Federal Government’s announcement of a 30-day petrol discount at Nigerian National Petroleum Company Limited (NNPCL) filling stations.
Some described the move as an attempt to win public support ahead of the 2027 general election.
The reactions followed Thursday’s announcement by the Minister of Finance and Coordinating Minister of the Economy, Taiwo Oyedele, that the government would offer discounted petrol for an initial 30 days, prioritising public transport operators.
The measure comes more than three years after Tinubu announced the removal of petrol subsidy.
It has triggered fresh questions about why the government is introducing temporary relief now, following prolonged complaints over rising fuel prices, transportation costs and the cost of living.
Some Nigerians who reacted to the announcement on social media questioned whether the intervention was designed primarily to ease economic hardship or improve the electoral prospects of the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC).
Political commentator, Ugo Egbujo, said that the latest move was part of an attempt by the president to improve his chances in the 2027 election.
“Tinubu will do anything to win this election. He can temporarily return fuel subsidies and unfriend Chagoury and seize Wike’s Rolls-Royce. After winning, he will return his old habits,” Egbujo wrote.
Other Nigerians also questioned the timing and duration of the intervention.
Haroun El-Yahya Hassan asked why the government had waited so long before introducing the measure.
“Where were they 40 months ago? He must go forever, God’s willing,” he wrote.
Similarly, Almajir Abdullahi invoked a Hausa expression to suggest that the intervention had come too late.
“In Hausa we say, ‘Masa ta bayan biki,’ which literally means, no benefit to make a guest’s food after the ceremony,” he said.
The comments reflects a broader concern among critics that the administration, having defended the removal of petrol subsidy as a necessary economic reform, was now introducing a temporary concession as the next general election approaches.
Under the new arrangement, Oyedele said the government would offer a discount on petrol sold at NNPCL stations for 30 days, with priority given to public transport operators.
“We are offering a discount on petrol dispensed by NNPC Limited for the next 30 days in the first instance, with priority for public transporters nationwide. So, it’s not a subsidy; the government is just saying we sell to you at cost,” he said.
The minister also disclosed that the government was negotiating a ceiling of N1,350 per litre on petrol’s ex-gantry or landing cost, subject to monthly reviews, to moderate the impact of fluctuations in global crude oil prices and exchange rates on pump prices.
However, the announcement has not convinced some Nigerians that the intervention will provide lasting relief.
Abdulrahman Abba Saleh said he preferred a government that demonstrated commitment to a permanent solution rather than a temporary intervention.
“We prefer the person who has demonstrated readiness for a permanent solution (subsidy reversal) than one-month solution,” he wrote.
Ovie Ezimeruwe also questioned the sustainability of the arrangement.
He asked: “What will they do for that one month? Why can’t they do it after then? After one month, what next?”
For his part, Isiya Al’majir Keta questioned the change in the government’s position on fuel prices.
According to him, “They said petrol can never reduce the price, what has changed the story?”
Daily Trust reports that the latest development comes against the backdrop of Tinubu’s May 29, 2023, inauguration, when he declared that “fuel subsidy is gone”.
The decision led to sharp increases in petrol prices and transportation fares.
The administration has consistently defended the policy as necessary to reduce the financial burden of subsidising petrol and redirect public resources towards development.
However, the immediate consequences have remained a major source of public dissatisfaction, with higher transport and production costs feeding into the prices of food and other essential goods.
The fresh intervention has reopened the debate over whether the government is responding to the economic realities confronting Nigerians or seeking to address mounting public discontent ahead of the 2027 polls.
Usman Auwal Hassan suggested that the announcement would not have been made without the approaching election.
“If not because of the election, they shouldn’t say that,” he wrote.
Michael Otues argued that even a substantial reduction in petrol prices would not necessarily change his political preference.
“If you guys like, make the price of fuel N100, it is not going to change our mind to vote for APC. Nigerians are wise now,” he said.
Abdullazeez Abdullahi also called for the government to focus on winning public acceptance rather than resorting to electoral manipulation.
“All options considered… No way to rigging; let’s do what is acceptable by the masses. It’s too late,” he wrote.

items.author: Henry Oduah
items.content:
By Adeola Badru
The abduction of 20 prospective National Youth Service Corps (NYSC) members travelling to their orientation camps has triggered fresh calls for the Federal Government to overhaul the transportation and security arrangements for young graduates deployed across the country for national service.
The call came as the 20 prospective corps members, who were abducted in Imo State, returned safely to Ibadan on Thursday after seven days in captivity and were taken to the Department of State Services (DSS) headquarters in the Aleshinloye area of the city for debriefing.
The mother of one of the rescued corps members, Faith Felicia Abiala, said the incident had exposed the dangers faced by young graduates travelling long distances by road to fulfil their national service obligations.
Abiala, who described her daughter’s safe return as a moment of overwhelming relief, urged the government to provide stronger security arrangements for corps members travelling to their states of deployment or consider transporting them by air.
“My advice to the government is that when Corps members are posted to their service states, they should ensure proper security arrangements, or allow them to travel by air to avoid these kinds of dangerous road journeys,” she said.
The mother recalled the emotional trauma that followed the abduction of her daughter, saying she was so devastated when she received the news that she could not eat.
“I cannot recount all the tears and sorrow, but I give thanks to God that I am seeing her alive today. On the day she was taken, I was so devastated I couldn’t even eat, but today my heart is filled with joy,” Abiala said.
She also commended the DSS and the security teams from Oyo and Imo states for their efforts in securing the victims’ return.
“I thank God, and I thank the DSS officials—they really tried! The team from Oyo State and the team from Imo State, they really tried and stood by us until our children came out safe and sound,” she said.
Another relative of one of the victims, Alhaja Alimot Akande described their release as a major relief after days of uncertainty.
“It is good news! Good news! Good news!” she said.
She said the confirmation of the victims’ release finally enabled their families to sleep peacefully after days of anguish.
“Ah! Immediately I heard they were released yesterday, I slept soundly!” Akande said.
The abductors had reportedly demanded N50 million for each of the 20 victims, amounting to N1 billion, before the demand was allegedly reduced to N5 million per victim, bringing the total to N100 million.
The parents had earlier visited the private residence of the Olubadan of Ibadanland, Oba Rashidi Ladoja, in Ibadan, seeking his intervention in securing the release of their children.
The Oyo State Commissioner of Police, Olugbenga Abimbola, and the Aseyin of Iseyinland, Oba Sefiu Adeyeri, were also involved in efforts to secure the victims’ release.
The Olubadan subsequently announced the freedom of the prospective corps members after receiving confirmation from Imo State Governor, Hope Uzodinma.
“The kidnapped graduates have been released. The Imo State Governor, Hope Uzodinma, confirmed this in a telephone conversation at about 5.00pm,” Ladoja stated in a statement issued by his media aide, Adeola Oloko.
The 20 victims were among 30 prospective corps members travelling in two buses from Oyo State towards orientation camps in Abia State when gunmen attacked them along the Owerri-Onitsha Road in Umunoha, Mbaitoli Local Government Area of Imo State.
Ten of the prospective corps members escaped into the bush during the attack and subsequently made their way to safety, while the remaining 20 were abducted.
The victims spent seven days in captivity before regaining their freedom and being brought back to Ibadan, where they were received at the DSS facility.
The incident had generated widespread anxiety among their parents and relatives, with the families seeking intervention from government officials, security agencies and traditional rulers.

By Johnbosco Agbakwuru
PRESIDENT Bola Tinubu has expressed deep sorrow over the passing of Professor Idowu Akanbi Sobowale, an eminent Mass Communications scholar and former Commissioner for Education in Lagos State, who died at 85.
President Tinubu described the death of the renowned academic and journalist as a great loss to Nigeria, particularly the academic community, the media profession, and generations of students whose lives and careers he shaped through his scholarship and mentorship.
The President also condoled with the Association of Communication Scholars and Professionals of Nigeria on the passing of its Board of Trustees Chairman.
He acknowledged Professor Sobowale’s immense contributions to mass communication education and his enduring impact on journalism and media studies in Nigeria.
“Professor Sobowale was committed to intellectual excellence, professional ethics, and the training of young Nigerians. His life’s work helped strengthen the foundations of media education and professional journalism in the country.
“As a journalism educator, he emphasised empirical evidence over opinion. It was therefore no surprise that he led the first nationwide opinion poll to predict the outcome of the 1979 elections.
“He served my administration in Lagos State as special adviser and later education commissioner, performing creditably well in both roles.
“I commiserate with the family, colleagues, former students, and the entire academic and media communities.
“I urge them to find comfort in his remarkable legacy of service, scholarship and mentorship.
“May his soul rest in perfect peace,” Tinubu remarked.

items.author: Team Inc42
items.content:
With an eye on entering the homegrown electric two-wheeler (E2W) market, Vietnamese EV maker VinFast has signed letters of intent (LoIs) with more than 50 dealers across India.
The EV maker said that the agreements will pave the way for establishing 50+ electric motorcycle showrooms across 34 cities in 15 states and union territories (UTs). These showrooms will be set up across Delhi NCR, Rajasthan, Uttar Pradesh, Maharashtra, Karnataka, Tamil Nadu, West Bengal, among others.
In a statement, the EV giant said that the agreements will expand its distribution network and strengthen its position in the Indian E2W market. The LoIs were signed at VinFast’s manufacturing facility in Vietnam’s Hai Phong.
Citing its rationale for signing the agreements, VinFast said that the aforementioned cities have large two-wheeler markets, which offers a significant headroom for electrification. The company said that it plans to leverage these dealer locations to bring electric mobility solutions “closer to local consumers”.
As part of its local push, the company also plans to build charging infrastructure and strengthen after-sales services in the new cities.
“Partnering with more than 50 dealer partners across 15 states and territories and 34 cities marks the beginning of our journey to bring VinFast e-motorcycles across India. Alongside, we are also building charging infrastructure and strengthening after-sales services to ensure that customers across these locations receive the support they need throughout their ownership journey,” said Anurag Saxena, the India CEO of VinFast’s escooter division.
With this, VinFast is entering the burgeoning Indian E2W space, which is being driven by government incentives, new launches by domestic manufacturers, rising fuel prices, EV mandates, a growing charging infrastructure and rapid adoption by gig platforms.
The E2W segment is currently dominated by legacy players such as TVS Motor, Bajaj Auto and Hero MotoCorp. But the space has also spawned the rise of listed homegrown new-age mobility players such as Ather and Ola Electric.
However, unlike incumbents that focus on escooters, VinFast claims to be eyeing the Indian electric motorcycle market. Even here, the company will lock horns with homegrown players such as Oben Electric, MATTER and Ultraviolette.
This comes nearly a year after VinFast first said that it would enter the Indian E2W market in 2026. At the time, the company had said that it would invest $2 Bn in India to scale its annual production capacity from 50,000 units to 1.5 Lakh.
However, much has happened since then. Earlier this year, reports surfaced that the company was halting the production of select cars in India to reassess costs. Last month, it was also reported that the Vietnamese EV maker was in initial discussions with local suppliers to develop two new models for the Indian market.
That said, EVs continue to increase their share of India’s two-wheeler market. E2W registrations surged 12.2% month-on-month (MoM) to 2.07 Lakh units in September from 1.84 Lakh units in August.

items.author: Henry Oduah
items.content:
By Peter Duru, Makurdi
The Benue State Education Quality Assurance and Examinations Board, BEQAEB, has sealed Orenda and Opal Schools in Makurdi over alleged victimisation of learners and violation of the state government’s policy on textbook reuse and purchase.
The Executive Secretary of BEQAEB, Dr. Terna Francis, who led officials of the Board’s Directorate of Enforcement and Compliance to the schools, said the action followed several complaints by parents alleging that their children were being victimised for failing to purchase exercise and test books directly from the schools.
A court order authorising the sealing of the schools was served on the proprietor before officials of the Board locked the premises.
Francis said the enforcement action became necessary after repeated attempts by the Board to engage the schools and resolve the complaints failed.
According to him, “We went out with the enforcement team of the Benue State Education Quality Assurance and Examinations Board to seal Orenda and Opal schools here in Makurdi. This closure is as a result of the many complaints we received from parents regarding the victimisation of their learners in these schools.”
He said, “The schools have insisted that learners and their parents must buy exercise books and test books from their school, otherwise they will not be attended to, even after paying school fees. It is quite unfortunate because the Benue State Government, through the Ministry of Education and Knowledge Management, as well as the Benue State Education Quality Assurance and Examinations Board, have continually reminded school owners, proprietors and administrators that there is a textbook reuse policy in Benue State.”
Francis explained that the Board initially contacted the proprietor by telephone and directed her to stop the alleged practice, but the complaints persisted. “We approached this particular school, first through a phone conversation, and we spoke with the proprietor and asked her to desist from that victimisation. They went on and continued in the same manner,” he said.
He added that the Board subsequently wrote officially to the school and invited the proprietor, school management and PTA chairman for a meeting aimed at resolving the matter. “They came without the proprietor, and we asked why the proprietor did not attend our meeting. We rescheduled and asked the school administrator and the principal to pick a convenient date, which they did. On that day, they failed to come, and there was no reason given,” he said.
According to the Executive Secretary, complaints from parents subsequently indicated that the alleged victimisation had extended beyond the purchase of books. “We continued to hear from the parents of these learners that the victimisation done to the learners went to the extent that when they submit their homework, the teachers were directed not to mark, and they were not being marked,” he alleged.
He further said, “Their books were not allowed into the classroom, even after paying school fees. And so, the children started feeling withdrawn and demoralised, and of course, this is against the child protection laws of Benue State and the Federation.”
Francis stressed that the state’s textbook policy was designed to give parents flexibility and prevent them from being subjected to unnecessary financial pressure. He said, “If a particular school has textbooks for sale, it should not be made mandatory for parents to buy from the school. Parents are allowed the freedom to bring the textbooks of their older children and transmit them to the younger ones for use.”
He added that schools were also required to give parents the freedom to source prescribed textbooks elsewhere. “If the list of textbooks is available in a school, parents should be given a copy, and they should decide whether to buy it outside of the school in bookstores or to pick from the school. It is a matter of option and not a matter of necessity that parents must buy books from the school,” he stated.
Francis said the Board, in conjunction with the office of the Attorney-General of the State, approached a court of competent jurisdiction after the alleged violations persisted. “The continual victimisation of these parents and the children led us to approach the Court of Competent Jurisdiction, where, together with the Attorney-General of the State, we instituted and presented the facts before the court on this matter, and the court graciously granted us an order to seal the schools,” he said.
Asked how long the schools would remain sealed, the BEQAEB boss said, “The school will remain sealed indefinitely until we come to terms with the owner of the school and the administrators, and they are ready and willing, and until they demonstrate clearly before us through the conditions that we are going to put before them, and we are convinced that they are willing to operate the schools in a responsible manner, with respect for every learner and the parents that have enrolled their children in those schools,” he said.
On compliance by other private schools in the state, Francis said the Board had not received similar petitions against other schools but warned proprietors and administrators against violating government policies. “Our learners are in school at the moment. We have staff of the Board that are out on monitoring exercise, and they are interacting with parents.”
He urged parents facing similar challenges in other schools to report such cases to the Board with supporting evidence. “We call on parents who have such challenges in other schools to launch their complaints. They should bring before us petitions with evidence of victimisation, and we’ll take it from there,” Francis said.
The Executive Secretary described the action against Orenda and Opal Schools as “a deterrent to other proprietors, and we want to warn that if there is a breach in any school at all by any administrator or proprietor, we are going to clamp down on the school aggressively,” he warned.
The post Benue seals two schools over alleged victimisation of pupils, textbook policy violation appeared first on Vanguard News.

By Johnbosco Agbakwuru
The Presidency on Thursday explained that the measure taken by the Nigerian National Petroleum Company Limited (NNPCL) to forgo its petrol retail profit margin and sell to Nigerians at cost to cushion the impact of global crude oil price shocks and volatility on vulnerable households has the approval of President Bola Tinubu.
The Presidency, however, explained that the measure should not be interpreted to mean that the government is out to reverse a necessary reform designed to set the country on the path towards sustained prosperity.
It stated that it is to ensure its gains reach more Nigerians, faster and in more tangible ways.
A statement by the Special Adviser to President Tinubu on Information and Strategy, Mr. Bayo Onanuga, noted that the subsidy removal came at a price.
“To be clear, none of these measures restores a blanket subsidy. Doing so would create longer-term harm for a short-term cure. Each measure is designed to reach the people who need help, without putting the wider economy at risk.”
According to the statement, the Presidency acknowledged the challenges the people face over the high cost of fuel.
“Removing the fuel subsidy came at a price. But the alternative has been tried. Nigeria has already lived through that cycle: scarcity, smuggling, a collapsing currency and a fiscal crisis. We cannot afford to live through it again, least of all in response to a temporary disruption, and at the very moment the results of reform are gathering pace.”
“Government is not out to reverse a necessary reform designed to set our country on the path towards sustained prosperity. It is to ensure its gains reach more Nigerians, faster and in more tangible ways. That is our work, and we are committed to doing it.
“The Federal Government is also working on a comprehensive package of fiscal measures to bring inflation down to single digits sustainably in the near term.”
It stressed that the NNPC’s decision to forgo its petrol retail profit margin and sell to Nigerians at cost was aimed to cushion the impact of global crude oil price shocks and volatility on vulnerable households.
“NNPC Retail, which already sells petrol at the lowest price in the market, will offer this new deal within the next 30 days. This means if NNPC’s landing cost is N1300, it will sell fuel to Nigerians, especially commercial vehicles, at the same price,” it stated.
It further stated that the company’s discount gesture, backed by President Tinubu, was among the raft of measures the Finance Minister and Coordinating Minister of the Economy, Taiwo Oyedele, had earlier announced.
Oyedele had said he hoped other marketers would take a cue from the NNPC, as the sharp rise in crude and petrol prices is not expected to last long.
The presidency said that Oyedele was emphatic that NNPC agreeing to sell at a discount must not be misinterpreted as the restoration of petrol subsidy, which ended on May 29, 2023.
“In addition, Oyedele announced forward sales of crude to domestic refineries. As production rises and previously committed crude is freed up, this is expected to shield pump prices from global market volatility.
“Oyedele also said the Federal Government is negotiating a ceiling of N1,350 a litre on the ex-gantry or landing cost of petrol, to keep pump prices stable. Where costs rise above the ceiling, refiners and importers will carry the shortfall and recover it later, when crude prices or the exchange rate allow, without breaching the ceiling.
“This is neither a subsidy nor a price control: it is designed to smooth prices over time rather than suppressing them. The reasoning is simple. 1,400 naira a litre today and 1,400 tomorrow is better than 1,500 today and 1,300 tomorrow, because volatility itself adds to uncertainty and cost.
“And when fares rise sharply, they rarely fall as fast. The ceiling will be reviewed monthly, reset as costs require, and the figures published for transparency,” the presidency quoted Oyedele as having said.
Continuing, it said, “Oyedele also said that, under the 2025 tax reform laws, the Federal government, in collaboration with the states and security agencies, is reining in the collection of road taxes and levies that inflate fares and logistics costs.
“The Federal government is also increasing funding for cash transfers to the most vulnerable households and subsidised credit for small businesses and consumers.”
Other measures announced, it said, included a faster CNG rollout.
“The federal government is scaling up CNG deployment with the states. The government expects transporters to pass the savings on to passengers in lower fares. CNG is 60-70 per cent cheaper than petrol,” it said.
On excess profit tax, the statement said: “This will be considered for operators who take undue advantage of consumers, anywhere along the energy value chain.
“The government said it will use proceeds from taxes on price gouging exclusively to cushion the impact of fuel prices through transport support or vouchers for urban minimum-wage earners, who are most vulnerable. The Federal Government will also work with the National Assembly to consider enhanced tax relief for low-income earners under the 2027 Finance Bill.
Less red tape
“The Federal Government is cutting regulatory costs that feed into the cost of doing business and, indirectly, into higher prices of goods and services.
National Strategic Fuel Reserve
“To protect households and businesses from future energy shocks, the Federal Government is investing in a National Strategic Fuel Reserve. The government will release refined products into the market under clear, published rules whenever a global disruption or hoarding threatens supply and price stability.
“This is not a subsidy, and it does not fix prices; rather, it secures supply and reduces price volatility. It will prevent artificial scarcity, deter market manipulation, and anchor long-term energy security, so a deregulated market delivers stable growth rather than sudden price shocks.
Better traffic and logistics management
“Traffic management agencies will improve traffic flow, especially in major urban centres, to reduce fuel consumption. Also, NIPOST’s newly launched address codes will help make logistics more efficient and cheaper.”

items.author: Henry Oduah
items.content:
By Emma Ujah, Abuja Bureau Chief
The Nigeria Deposit Insurance Corporation, NDIC, has paid N1.48 billion to 10,312 insured depositors of 47 recently closed microfinance banks, MFBs, as part of efforts to strengthen confidence in the banking system.
Managing Director of the Corporation, Mr. Thompson Sunday, disclosed this in Abuja on Thursday while speaking at the NDIC’s 2026 Customer Service Week celebration, with the theme, “Go the Extra Mile.”
Sunday said the payments, which were made as of July 31, 2026, covered depositors of recently closed microfinance banks, including Abia SME Microfinance Bank, Frontline Microfinance Bank and Goldman Microfinance Bank.
He said the Corporation leveraged the Bank Verification Number, BVN, system to identify depositors and obtain alternative bank accounts, a development that simplified and accelerated the payment of claims.
The NDIC boss charged the Corporation’s staff to go beyond routine responsibilities in delivering professional and efficient services to depositors and other stakeholders.
He said: “Let us remember that service excellence is not a one-week activity. Customer Service Week may provide the occasion for us to celebrate and reflect, but the commitment to excellent service must continue in our daily work, in every Department, Zone, Unit and Office, at every level, and in every interaction.
“This year’s theme, ‘The Extra Mile’, adequately captures the spirit of excellence and commitment that we seek to demonstrate in all we do. It reminds us that excellent service is not simply about meeting expectations; it is about going beyond what is required to create a positive experience and meaningful value for those we serve.”
According to him, the NDIC’s responsibility goes beyond the payment of insured deposits, stressing that the Corporation remains a critical component of Nigeria’s financial safety net through deposit insurance, banking supervision in collaboration with the Central Bank of Nigeria, failure resolution and orderly liquidation of failed banks.
He said the stability and dependability of the financial system were essential to the wider economy, as individuals and businesses depended on financial institutions to safeguard funds, facilitate transactions, provide access to credit and create confidence for investment and growth.
Sunday, however, noted that the discharge of the Corporation’s mandate was not only about policies, processes and procedures, but also about how depositors and other stakeholders were treated.
“Fulfilling this responsibility is not only about the policies we develop, the processes we establish or the mandates we discharge. It is also about how we serve the people and institutions we interact with daily,” he said.
“It is about the experience we create in every encounter and our willingness to do a little more to ensure that our stakeholders receive the quality of service they deserve.”
He explained that going the extra mile did not necessarily mean doing something extraordinary, but could be demonstrated through everyday actions such as responding promptly to complaints, resolving issues professionally, showing empathy and collaborating across departments to ensure that assignments were completed properly and on time.
The NDIC managing director said the Corporation had itself gone the extra mile through its NDIC ASCENDS restructuring programme**, which he said was designed to strengthen its structures, improve processes, enhance collaboration and leverage technology and data to make the Corporation more efficient and responsive in delivering its mandates.
He added that the NDIC had also recently completed a comprehensive review of its Strategic Plan, resulting in a refreshed mission, strategic themes, objectives and initiatives, as well as a new set of core values captured in the acronym EPIIC — Excellence, Professionalism, Integrity, Innovation and Collaboration.
According to him, the initiatives were designed to continually improve the Corporation’s capacity to serve depositors and other stakeholders.
Sunday stressed that customer service was not the responsibility of a particular department or group of employees, insisting that every staff member was a service provider.
“Whether we interact directly with depositors, stakeholders and the public, or provide support to colleagues within the Corporation who do so, our actions contribute to the experience people have with the Corporation,” he said.
He commended NDIC staff for their dedication and commitment, saying their professionalism and continuous pursuit of improvement remained critical to the success of the Corporation.
The NDIC boss urged employees to use the Customer Service Week to renew their commitment to professionalism, responsiveness, empathy, integrity, accountability and excellence.
He said the celebration should also provide an opportunity for staff to learn, share experiences, explore innovative approaches and challenge themselves to raise the standard of service across the Corporation.
Sunday assured that the NDIC would continue to place depositors at the centre of its operations, noting that confidence in the financial system remained fundamental to economic stability and growth.

items.author: Arooj Fatima
items.content:
Inspector General of Sindh Police Javed Alam Odho has directed all Grade 17 and above police officers to submit their asset and income details through the Federal Board of Revenue (FBR) portal under the federal government’s new digital declaration system.
Letters have been sent to additional inspectors general, deputy inspectors general, senior superintendents of police, and superintendents of police, directing them to file declarations for the 2025-26 financial year by October 30.
The new system replaces the previous manual process and requires officers to submit details of their income, bank accounts, properties, investments, and movable and immovable assets digitally.
The declarations will also cover assets owned by spouses, along with vehicles, shares, prize bonds, domestic and foreign bank accounts, and other valuable holdings.
Officers must disclose their own income as well as the income of family members. They will also be required to provide details of their children’s education, educational institutions, and related expenses.
Other information to be declared includes electricity and gas bills, spending on private foreign travel, bank loans, and other liabilities. Officers must also explain any changes in the value of their assets compared with the previous financial year.
Authorities have further sought details of social media accounts and any foreign citizenship or permanent residency held by officers.
The FBR will scrutinize the submitted information, and officers may face disciplinary action for concealing or misrepresenting details. Failure to submit declarations by the deadline may also lead to disciplinary proceedings.
Officials will be allowed to make corrections until November 30, 2026, subject to approval from the relevant cadre administrator.
Selected non-sensitive information from the declarations will also be published on the FBR website for public access.

items.title: Pakistan Army Completes New Road Linking 2 Cities in Gilgit-Baltistan
items.summary:
The Pakistan Army has completed a 66-kilometer road track connecting Shagma in Astore with Manthokha in Skardu, improving travel between the two districts.
Built through difficult mountainous terrain in a short period, the new route has reduced the journey between Astore and Skardu to just a few hours.
The Shagma-Manthokha road has also restored direct access to district headquarters for eight villages in the Phoota Khas Valley of Gultari, making travel easier for local residents.
The improved link is expected to support local trade, agriculture, and livestock transportation, while providing better access to markets and essential services.
Residents have welcomed the project, saying it will make travel easier and support economic activity in the area.
The road is part of broader efforts to improve connectivity and promote social and economic development in Gilgit-Baltistan’s mountainous communities.

items.content:
By Haruna Aliyu, Birnin Kebbi
Troops of Sector 2, Joint Task Force, North West Operation FANSAN YAMMA, have repelled an attack by suspected members of the Lakurawa terrorist group on the Forward Operating Base in Maiyama Local Government Area of Kebbi State.
The attack occurred in the early hours of Wednesday, October 7, 2026, when the terrorists, reportedly numbering in large numbers and operating on more than 100 motorcycles, stormed the military base with assorted weapons.
The terrorists were said to be armed with General Purpose Machine Guns and Rocket-Propelled Grenades.
The troops, however, responded swiftly and effectively, forcing the attackers to withdraw from the area.
In a statement issued on Thursday, the Media Information Officer of the Joint Task Force, North West Operation FANSAN YAMMA, Lt. Col. Aliyu Danja, said the terrorists abandoned weapons, equipment and other logistics while fleeing the area.
Danja said, “The troops responded swiftly and effectively, repelling the attack and preventing the terrorists from achieving their objective.”
He added that troops subsequently conducted exploitation and pursuit operations around the area, leading to the recovery of 17 motorcycles, a PKT machine gun, an AK-47 rifle, assorted ammunition and a communication device.
According to him, the recoveries represented a significant setback to the operational capability of the terrorist group in the area.
“The recovery of the weapons, ammunition, communication equipment and motorcycles represents a significant setback to the terrorists’ operational capability in the area,” he said.
The military spokesman said the general area remained firmly under the control of the troops, adding that aggressive patrols, clearance and dominance operations were ongoing to track and neutralise fleeing members of the group.
He said Operation FANSAN YAMMA remained committed to protecting communities and denying terrorists freedom of operation within the Joint Operations Area.

items.author: Arooj Fatima
items.content:
The Lahore High Court (LHC) has summoned senior government officials over their failure to submit responses in a petition seeking a ban on the sale of camera-equipped smart glasses in Pakistan.
Chief Justice Aaliya Neelum, while hearing a petition filed by Nadira Bibi, expressed displeasure over the lack of replies despite notices being issued to the concerned authorities.
The court ordered the Interior Secretary, Federal Board of Revenue (FBR) chairman, Commerce Secretary, and Member of Customs to appear in person at the next hearing on October 15.
Deputy Director of the National Cyber Crime Investigation Agency (NCCIA) Hassan Naqvi and other officials appeared before the court during Thursday’s hearing alongside Deputy Attorney General Rafiqat Ali Dogar.
The deputy attorney general submitted a report on behalf of the NCCIA, while Pakistan Telecommunication Authority (PTA) legal adviser Muhammad Afzal Khan sought additional time to submit the authority’s response. The court granted the request.
During the hearing, the chief justice questioned why the remaining respondents had not submitted their replies despite receiving notices.
“Notices were also sent to the remaining parties. Why have their replies not been received?” she asked.
The court adjourned the case until October 15.
In her petition, Nadira Bibi raised concerns over the sale of camera-equipped glasses in markets and supermarkets, arguing that the devices could be used to secretly record people without their knowledge.
She claimed that the glasses could pose security and privacy risks and alleged that no approval had been obtained from any government institution for their sale.
The petitioner asked the court to seek explanations from the relevant authorities and impose an immediate ban on the sale of such devices.

items.summary:
Punjab Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz Sharif has provided two Pink Buses to Kohsar University Murree to improve transportation facilities for female students.
The buses are expected to make daily travel easier and safer for students who commute to the university through Murree’s rugged and mountainous routes, where transportation has remained a longstanding challenge.
Kohsar University Vice-Chancellor Professor Dr. Rafia Mumtaz thanked the Punjab chief minister for providing the buses, describing the initiative as a significant development for female students.
The new service is expected to ease commuting difficulties and provide students with a more regular and secure way to travel to the university.
For female students in Murree, the Pink Buses are being seen not only as a transport facility but also as a source of support in making their educational journey easier.

items.title: Trump misnames Muslim Senate candidate ‘Mohammed’
items.author: Henry Oduah
items.content:
A Muslim candidate for US Senate accused Donald Trump of “struggling” on Thursday after the president misnamed him “Mohammed” on social media amid increasingly bitter exchanges between the two men.
Trump attacked the left-wing Democratic candidate Abdul El-Sayed on his Truth Social platform, baselessly accusing him of being a “Terrorist Sympathizer.”
El-Sayed, an Arab American running for a Michigan Senate seat that could decide which party wins the US upper chamber in knife-edge midterm elections next month, said “I think Donald might be struggling a little bit.”
“He thinks my name’s Mohammed … My name’s Abdul, and you know it. And the only reason he won’t say it is I keep ripping you,” El-Sayed said at a campaign event in Grand Rapids, Michigan.
“So try again and get it right because we’re going to teach you how to say it properly,” he added to laughter at a restaurant photo-op, where he was joined by Michigan Governor Gretchen Whitmer and Delaware Senator Lisa Blunt Rochester.
Like many Muslim men, El-Sayed’s middle name is Mohamed, but he does not use it publicly.
Trump and his supporters have fixated on El-Sayed, accusing him and his family of ties to the Muslim Brotherhood and the Al-Qaeda jihadist group.
Trump said El-Sayed, locked in a knife-edge race with Republican Mike Rogers, was the “best friend” of “America Hating Hasan Piker,” the left-wing influencer who campaigned for El-Sayed during the Democratic primary.
The Michigan Senate seat is considered essential to Democratic hopes of regaining the Senate.
The party aims to retain the Michigan seat in Democratic hands while wresting four other seats in the 100-member chamber from Republicans.
The midwestern state backed Trump in the 2024 presidential election, even as Democrat Elissa Slotkin narrowly defeated Rogers for Michigan’s other Senate seat.
El-Sayed was backed by progressive leaders including Bernie Sanders, Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez and Elizabeth Warren, as well as the United Auto Workers union.
His platform includes health care for all, higher taxes on billionaires, ending unconditional US military aid to Israel and reducing the role of corporate money in elections.
AFP

items.title: 2027: Only mad people will vote for Tinubu – Amaechi
items.summary:
African Democratic Congress (ADC) Vice Presidential Candidate, Rotimi Amaechi, has said only mad people will cast their ballot for President Bola Tinubu in 2027.

items.content:
African Democratic Congress (ADC) Vice Presidential Candidate, Rotimi Amaechi, has said only mad people will cast their ballot for President Bola Tinubu in 2027.
Speaking at town hall meeting in Edo State, on Thursday, Amaechi charged Edo residents to reject Tinubu and support the opposition party in the forthcoming election.
“They are going about saying ‘Vote Tinubu! Vote Tinubu!’ Only thieves can vote for Tinubu. In fact, I read a comment on social media where someone said, ‘It’s in 2027 that we will know how many mad men we have in Nigeria.”
“Because it’s only a mad people that can vote for Tinubu. If Edo people vote for President Tinubu, that means Edo people are mad. If you’re not mad, Tinubu should not win here,” he said.
The former Minister of Transportation also accused the Tinubu administration of pursuing projects based on alleged financial interests rather than what he described as the broader economic needs of Nigerians.
Amaechi particularly questioned the planned development of another seaport in Ogun State, asking whether the state generates sufficient cargo to justify additional port infrastructure.
“So, Tinubu just hates you. No, I’m not joking. If Tinubu does not hate you, why is he building another seaport? In Ogun, what are the goods we are producing? What goods are we producing to have as many as that number of seaports? It is not because he likes Ogun people. It is the money he will make out of the construction.”
He warned opposition supporters against staying away from the country or electoral process and expecting a change in government.
“If you want Tinubu to go, please go home. Go home. Go home,” he said.
On subsidy, he said, “When we bring back subsidy, it’s not that one that will produce rich men. That subsidy where rich men will go to Ghana and come back to say, ‘We have bough fuel for you’. We are bringing back a subsidy called Production subsidy. If you don’t have a refinery in Nigeria, you will not get subsidy. We don’t have to pay for it. Government will not pay for the subsidy. All the government needs to do is to make a policy.
“The price at which I sell crude on the international market and price with which I sell crude in the Nigerian market will be different. I will do domestic pricing. If I sell crude at N15,000 on the international market, in Nigeria, I will sell to Dangote at N10,000. And here we have four modular refineries. The difference will be N5,000. I will then sit with Dangote and the modular refiners and tell them to give me a subsidy of N5,000. Once that happens, the price of fuel will come down. When the price of fuel comes down, the price of everything will go down.”

items.author: Mohammed I. Yaba
items.content:
The Arewa Consultative Forum (ACF) has called on the Federal Government to stop what it described as excessive focus on the 2027 elections and prioritise the worsening insecurity across the country.
The forum said the continued attacks, killings, abductions and destruction of livelihoods by armed groups posed an existential threat to Nigeria, accusing political office holders of paying greater attention to electioneering than the security and welfare of citizens.
In a statement issued by its National Publicity Secretary, Prof. T. A. Muhammad-Baba, the ACF said the government’s apparent inaction had allowed armed non-state actors to operate freely and wreak havoc on communities.
“Without equivocation ACF insists that now is the time to stop the politics and end the killings,” the forum said.
The group expressed concern over the continued abduction of citizens, saying scores of children were still being held by terrorists in Borno, Kwara and other states, while many other victims remained in captivity under what it described as horrendous conditions.
It also cited recent attacks in Zamfara State, where it said five separate incidents were recorded in one day, resulting in deaths, abductions and looting of property.
According to the ACF, attacks and killings have also continued in Plateau and Taraba states, while similar incidents have been reported in Benue, Niger, Katsina and Kogi states.
The forum expressed particular concern over increasing cases of abductions, killings and ransom demands in Chikun Local Government Area and other communities in and around Kaduna metropolis.
It also raised alarm over the reported abduction of prospective National Youth Service Corps members travelling to report at their orientation camp in Imo State, saying they were still being held as of the time of issuing the statement.
The ACF said the incidents were only a fraction of the security challenges confronting communities across the country.
It questioned how much more violence, bloodshed and abductions citizens must endure before those responsible for their protection take decisive action.
The forum also criticised what it described as the growing preoccupation of elected officials and other politically exposed persons with the 2027 elections.
According to the ACF, governance and protection of citizens must take precedence over political campaigns and re-election concerns.
It also faulted President Bola Ahmed Tinubu’s Independence Anniversary address, saying the speech made only a fleeting reference to insecurity despite the scale of the crisis confronting the country.
The forum urged the government to urgently redirect its attention towards tackling insecurity, warning that every new incident of violence should be treated as one too many.
“As time is fast running out, electioneering campaigns must give way to action over insecurity,” the ACF said.
The forum reiterated its call for urgent action to protect communities and restore security, stressing that political considerations should not be allowed to overshadow the government’s primary responsibility of protecting lives and property.

items.author: Business Desk
items.content:
The Economic Coordination Committee (ECC) on Thursday approved a Rs. 4 billion Technical Supplementary Grant (TSG) for Pakistan Revenue Automation Limited (PRAL) to support the restructuring and implementation of the Federal Board of Revenue’s (FBR) Transformation Plan.
The funding was approved on a summary submitted by the Revenue Division during the ECC meeting despite recent issues reported in the tax collector’s IRIS portal. The 2026 return filing season is officially ending on October 15, 2026.
PRAL provides technology and automation support to FBR, including systems used for tax administration. The grant is aimed at FBR’s efforts to upgrade its digital infrastructure and transform its revenue collection system.
FBR has faced persistent issues with its IRIS tax system, including disruptions and difficulties reported by taxpayers and tax professionals.
ECC also approved an amendment to SRO 693(I)/2006 concerning Additional Customs Duty on locally manufactured tyres, with the measure aimed at supporting domestic manufacturing.
Separately, the committee approved a financing framework developed by the State Bank of Pakistan to bring eligible Agency Financial Institutions under existing risk coverage schemes for small enterprises and small farmers.

items.title: India's IT firms face US' PERM wrath
items.summary: The United States on Thursday barred eight major technology companies, including Microsoft, Infosys, Wipro and Tata, from participating in a federal labour certification programme used to secure employment-based green cards for foreign workers, as the Trump administration stepped up scrutiny of immigration practices it says disadvantage American employees.The sweeping action, announced by Vice President JD Vance, Labour Secretary Keith Sonderling and Attorney General Todd Blanche under the US Anti-Fraud Task Force, targets some of the world's largest IT outsourcing companies and comes alongside a separate investigation into the use of exchange visitor visas by leading American universities.Also Read: US bars Microsoft from sponsoring green cards for H-1B workers over alleged abuseThe restrictions cover Cognizant, Infosys, Tata, Wipro, HCL, Capgemini, Microsoft and Adobe."I am hereby suspending from the Permanent Labour Certification Programme some of the largest IT outsourcing firms in
items.content: The United States on Thursday barred eight major technology companies, including Microsoft, Infosys, Wipro and Tata, from participating in a federal labour certification programme used to secure employment-based green cards for foreign workers, as the Trump administration stepped up scrutiny of immigration practices it says disadvantage American employees.The sweeping action, announced by Vice President JD Vance, Labour Secretary Keith Sonderling and Attorney General Todd Blanche under the US Anti-Fraud Task Force, targets some of the world's largest IT outsourcing companies and comes alongside a separate investigation into the use of exchange visitor visas by leading American universities.Also Read: US bars Microsoft from sponsoring green cards for H-1B workers over alleged abuseThe restrictions cover Cognizant, Infosys, Tata, Wipro, HCL, Capgemini, Microsoft and Adobe."I am hereby suspending from the Permanent Labour Certification Programme some of the largest IT outsourcing firms in the world, Cognizant, Infosys, Tata, Wipro, HCL, and Capgemini," Sonderling said.Microsoft and Adobe have also been suspended from the programme because of multiple ongoing federal investigations, according to the Labour Secretary.Under the decision, the US Department of Labour will neither accept fresh permanent labour certification applications nor process pending applications involving the eight companies.Microsoft faces criticism over layoffs, visa applicationsVance singled out Microsoft, accusing the technology giant of misusing the immigration system while reducing its American workforce."There has been no company in the United States, unfortunately, that has abused this system more than Microsoft," Vance said."Microsoft laid off 6,000 American workers in 2025 after certifying that it could not find qualified American employees - yet the company was approved for more than 6,000 H-1Bs and filed 3,682 PERM applications, including nearly 1,000 applications for the same positions as the laid off American workers," the vice president said.The administration also pointed to the scale of foreign worker recruitment by the companies covered under the suspension.Also Read: US announces investigation into 9 universities, including Ivy League schools, over J-1 visas"Since 2009, just these companies alone have requested almost three million foreign workers. They've received over 230,000 H-1B visa approvals and over 100,000 permanent labour certifications," Sonderling said.He argued that the figures represented hundreds of thousands of employment opportunities lost by American workers.The announcement carries particular significance for Indian technology professionals, who account for more than 70 per cent of approved H-1B petitions annually.During the announcement, Vance described foreign workers recruited through the H-1B programme as "foreign indentured servants" and characterised companies using the system as "visa mills".Harvard, Yale among universities facing J-1 visa scrutinyThe administration's immigration crackdown has also extended to American higher education institutions.Vance announced an investigation into the use of the J-1 visa programme for research scholars at nine major universities, including Harvard, Yale, Stanford and the California Institute of Technology (Caltech).The J-1 programme permits foreign nationals to enter the United States as exchange visitors for research, teaching, education and specialised professional activities.However, the Vice President alleged that universities were relying excessively on the programme to hire foreign researchers at the expense of American graduate students and academics."Something weird is going on at these universities. They're using these visas way too much. They're using them to undercut the wages of American grad students and American researchers," Vance said.He argued that immigration programmes intended to attract international talent should not be used to suppress domestic wages."This is a fundamental insult to the American worker and to the American way of life. We cannot allow visa programs that were designed to ensure that American corporations had access to the best and the brightest, to use them to undercut the wages of American workers," Vance said.US announces visa fraud strike teamThe administration also announced the establishment of a dedicated visa fraud strike team, bringing together investigators from across federal agencies to examine suspected violations.Department of Labour Inspector General Anthony D'Esposito warned universities that their reputation or financial resources would not shield them from enforcement action."I don't care how prestigious the university thinks it is. Break the law and screw the American people, and I will personally cuff you in the university square," Inspector General Anthony D'Esposito, Department of Labour, said."I don't care how large your endowment is, how powerful your alumni are, or how many politicians you have on speed dial. As Vice President Vance said, nobody is above the law. That's why we're establishing a visa fraud strike team, bringing together investigative expertise from across government," D'Esposito said.The measures mark a broader push by Washington to tighten oversight of employment-linked immigration programmes, with the administration focusing on companies and universities it alleges have used foreign worker visas to undercut wages and employment opportunities for Americans.With PTI inputs

items.author: Our Correspondent
items.content:
Federal Minister for Maritime Affairs Muhammad Junaid Anwar Chaudhry on Thursday said that direct shipping connectivity between Karachi and major European ports had been restored, providing relief to exporters facing longer transit times and increased freight costs due to disruptions in international shipping routes.
In a statement, the minister said Mediterranean Shipping Company (MSC) had reinstated its Premium Ipak service in response to the demand from exporters for a dedicated and direct European service.
Under the restored service, MSC will make a weekly call at Karachi Gateway Terminal Limited (KGTL), connecting Karachi with key European destinations through Colombo, Felixstowe, Rotterdam, Hamburg, Bremerhaven, Antwerp, Le Havre and London Gateway.
"The restoration of a dedicated European service is an important development for our export-oriented industries, particularly the textile sector, which has been facing increased transit times and logistics costs because of disruptions to international shipping routes," the minister said.
He said textile exporters had recently apprised him of the difficulties caused by changes in shipping routes, particularly those linked to the situation in the Red Sea. "Exporters told me recently that longer vessel journeys were increasing transportation costs and delivery times for shipments to European and US markets. These additional costs and delays have affected the competitiveness of exporters," he said.
The minister stressed that the government was taking up concerns of the export sector with shipping lines and other relevant stakeholders to improve maritime connectivity and facilitate international trade.
"Reliable and predictable shipping connectivity is essential for Pakistan's exporters. Our focus is to ensure that the maritime sector supports trade, reduces logistical bottlenecks and strengthens Pakistan's access to international markets," he remarked.
He welcomed MSC's decision to reinstate the Premium Ipak service, saying the weekly Karachi call would provide exporters with a more direct connection to important European markets. "The restored service will improve connectivity with major European ports and provide exporters with greater options for planning and moving their shipments," he said.
The minister, however, noted that the reinstatement of the service should not be viewed as a resolution of the wider challenges affecting international shipping routes. "Disruptions to established shipping routes continue to have implications for global trade. We will continue working with the shipping industry and exporters to address connectivity and logistics issues and to strengthen Pakistan's position in international trade," he said.
The federal minister lauded efforts of Karachi Port Trust (KPT) Chairman Rear Admiral (Retd) Shahid Ahmed and the management of KGTL for restoring the shipping link between Karachi and European markets.
KPT chairman said measures were underway to further improve the efficiency of the maritime logistics system. He said the restored shipping connection would improve access from Karachi to key European markets and facilitate the country's exporters.

items.author: Our Correspondent
items.content:
Federal Minister for Planning, Development and Special Initiatives Ahsan Iqbal chaired a meeting of the National Price Monitoring Committee (NPMC) on Thursday to review the monthly and weekly inflation situation, wholesale-retail price gaps, prices of essential commodities and implementation of previous decisions.
The minister expressed concern over rising prices of essential commodities, particularly wheat flour, and directed provincial and district administrations to strengthen the monitoring of supplies, market arrivals, hoarding, profiteering and unjustified price increases.
The meeting was informed that the Consumer Price Index (CPI)-based inflation stood at 10.3% year-on-year in September 2026, compared to 11.1% in August, while average inflation during July-September FY2026-27 stood at 10.2%. The Wholesale Price Index (WPI) increased 13.3% year-on-year, while the weekly Sensitive Price Indicator (SPI) for the week ended October 1 recorded an 11.53% year-on-year spike. Major annual increases were recorded in onions, LPG, electricity, diesel, petrol and wheat flour, while chicken, garlic, gram pulse and LPG recorded notable weekly increases.
Ahsan Iqbal directed the concerned authorities to compare current transport fares with fares prevailing after the previous fuel price hike to determine whether the increase in fuel prices had resulted in any disproportionate rise in fares. He also told the Ministry of National Food Security and Research to examine why DAP prices remained high in Pakistan despite a decline in international markets, stressing that the benefit of lower international prices should be reflected in the domestic market.
He emphasised that the inspection and quality assessment report regarding ghee, edible oil and milk products be submitted within one week. If the industry had proposed a third-party validation, he said, its cost should be borne by the industry and not the government.
The minister asked provincial governments to closely monitor wholesale and retail prices and take enforcement action where unjustified gaps existed, particularly in major markets including Lahore and Karachi. He also called for close monitoring of supply chains and distribution costs to prevent disproportionate pass-through of fuel price increases to essential food costs.
Ahsan Iqbal directed authorities to strengthen measures against hoarding, profiteering and overcharging and ensure uninterrupted supplies of essential commodities, particularly wheat flour, onions and other perishables. He told Ogra to take effective measures to reduce the gap between notified and prevailing market prices of LPG cylinders.
The minister stressed that price monitoring should focus not only on statistics but also on identifying the causes of price increases, addressing market distortions and ensuring timely enforcement to protect consumers.

items.author: Our Correspondent
items.content:
Pakistan's benchmark KSE-100 index fell over 1,130 points on Thursday despite the country's staff-level agreement with the International Monetary Fund (IMF), as renewed regional tensions added to selling pressure.
The index initially gained around 900 points and climbed to the intra-day high near 169,500 before reversing course, closing at 167,441.91, down 0.68%. Heavyweights including UBL, Fauji Fertiliser and Systems Limited led the decline, while market turnover also dropped sharply to 365.9 million shares from 586.9 million in the previous session. At the close of trading, the KSE-100 index of the Pakistan Stock Exchange (PSX) fell 1,138.50 points, or 0.68%, and settled at 167,441.91.
Arif Habib Limited (AHL) reported that the KSE-100 opened with early strength, climbing to the intra-day high near 169,500 before selling pressure and resistance pushed it lower. The benchmark closed at 167,441.9, down 1,138.5 points, or 0.68%, with market breadth negative as 76 index constituents fell against only 23 gainers. PSO, LOTCHEM and Abbott contributed the largest positive points, while UBL, Fauji Fertiliser and Systems Limited were the main drags. Regular-market turnover fell to 366 million shares.
The report linked the session's tone to two external developments. Pakistan and the IMF reached a staff-level agreement that could unlock roughly another $1.2 billion under the Extended Fund Facility and Resilience and Sustainability Facility once the executive board approves it, offering potential relief against inflation and the fiscal effects of the Middle East conflict.
Separately, Houthi strikes on two Saudi airports that killed three people and injured dozens reinforced regional risk, while a government comment that Pakistan may hit its 30% electric-vehicle sales target for 2030 earlier than planned as petrol prices encourage switching received only a brief mention. Technically, Arif Habib observed that the index had turned down from its first resistance zone; a further slide through 165,500 would open the path towards 160,000. The accompanying Bloomberg chart and PSX tables showed the day range of roughly 2,000 points and confirmed the close near the session low, consistent with independent reports of profit-taking after the prior day's modest gain.
Topline's market review noted that the KSE-100 index witnessed a volatile session, initially gaining around 906 points following positive sentiment surrounding Pakistan's staff-level agreement with the IMF. However, the early gains failed to sustain as investors resorted to profit-taking at higher levels, resulting in a 1,138-point (-0.68%) decline to close at 167,442. The index traded in a wide range of 167,450-169,487 during the session.
Index-heavy stocks remained under pressure, with UBL, FFC, SYS, EFERT, and POL emerging as the major detractors, collectively shaving 394 points off the KSE-100 index. Despite the decline in the benchmark, market activity remained modest, Topline said. Overall trading volumes were recorded at 365.9 million shares compared with the previous session's tally of 586.9 million. The value of shares traded during the day was Rs17.7 billion.
Shares of 496 companies were traded. Of these, 130 stocks closed higher, 324 fell, and 42 remained unchanged.
K-Electric was the volume leader with trading in 29.7 million shares, losing Rs0.08 to close at Rs5.96. It was followed by Cnergyico Pk with 21.3 million shares, losing Rs0.34 to close at Rs12.39, and Waves Home Appliances with 16.9 million shares, losing Rs0.08 to close at Rs7.77. Foreign investors sold shares worth Rs245 million, the National Clearing Company reported.

items.author: Anne Florentyna
items.content:
NABVENTURES, the venture capital arm of the National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development (NABARD), has announced the first close of its second fund at ₹450 Cr.
The firm, which invests in early to growth stage agritech startups, is targeting a corpus of ₹1,500 Cr for the fund. This also includes a greenshoe option.
India’s apex agriculture focused financial institution NABARD is the anchor investor in the fund
The investment arm intends to double down on early and growth stage startups using tech to address challenges across the agricultural value chain and rural markets. The fund will invest across sectors including agritech, food and agribusiness, rural fintech, climate smart solutions, supply chain and logistics, among other businesses focused on rural transformation.
The fund will also focus on businesses working on sustainability, climate resilience, financial inclusion and livelihood creation, NABARD chairman Dr Shaji Krishnan V said
NABVENTURES was incorporated on April 23, 2018, as a wholly owned subsidiary of NABARD, to invest in businesses working across agriculture and rural development. Besides Fund II, it backs startups via NABVENTURES Fund I and AgriSURE.
NABVENTURES’ portfolio includes startups like Unnati, Eggoz, Beyond Snack, Jai Kisan, among 23 startups. The investor backed companies such as aquaculture-focused agritech startup Aquapulse, which raised ₹25 Cr in an ongoing Series A round led by NABVENTURES and KisaanSay through its AgriSURE Fund earlier this year.
NABVENTURES’ claimed that its earlier funds have collectively backed 23 enterprises, providing it with an existing portfolio and track record in India’s agri and rural startup ecosystem
The firm’s focus on agritech comes at a time when the sector has lost some allure that it had for investors. Agritech startups raised $202 Mn across 36 deals in 2025, down nearly 25% from $269 Mn in 2024 and sharply below the $728 Mn and $840 Mn raised in 2021 and 2022, respectively.
The funding pullback has continued as investors have become wary of capital-heavy models, high customer acquisition costs and weak monetisation, particularly among marketplace and logistics-led agritech businesses.
The shift also comes against a broader tepid funding environment in the Indian startup ecosystem. In Q3, overall startup funding rose 5% to $2.2 Bn, but deal count fell 13% and the active investor pool shrank 24%, signalling a sharper focus on high-conviction bets.
Agritech, however, has seen some sizable bets in recent times. Balwaan Krishi raised $10.4 Mn in a Series B round in September, while Ninjacart raised $6 Mn in July.

items.author: Web Desk
items.content:
The federal government on Thursday increased the price of petrol and high-speed diesel (HSD) by Rs2.31 and 78 paisas, respectively, for October 9.
According to a notification issued by the Petroleum Division, the price of petrol was fixed at Rs398.96 per litre, while HSD would cost Rs395.72 per litre for Friday.
The latest revision comes a day after the government increased the price of petrol by Rs1.82 per litre, while decreasing the price of HSD by 91 paisas per litre for October 8.
Read: Govt increases petrol by Rs1.82, cuts diesel by 91 paisas for Oct 8
On July 17, the government announced a new pricing mechanism under which petroleum product prices would be reviewed and notified daily, replacing the weekly pricing mechanism, as renewed tensions between the United States and Iran continued to drive volatility in global oil markets and raise concerns over fuel supplies.
On September 13, PM Shehbaz announced a special relief scheme offering Rs100 per litre off petrol for motorcycles, three-wheeler rickshaws and cars with engines up to 800cc, in an attempt to shield lower-income consumers from the impact of rising petroleum prices.
Under the proposal, an estimated 11.8 million beneficiaries would be covered. Around 10 million two-wheeler users and 800,000 three-wheeler users would be entitled to relief on 20 litres of fuel per month, translating into a maximum monthly benefit of Rs2,000 per beneficiary.
Another one million users of cars up to 800cc would receive relief on 30 litres per month, providing them with a maximum benefit of Rs3,000 each.
On Sept 17, the government reintroduced austerity and fuel conservation measures amid rising fuel prices, tightening business operating hours and restricting public events.
Under the measures, notified with immediate effect, shops, markets, shopping malls, bazaars, departmental stores, grocery stores, general stores and kiryana shops would close by 9pm throughout the week, according to a notification issued by the Cabinet Division.
Marriage halls, marquees and other commercial venues hosting festive events would close by 10pm, while restaurants, cafes, eateries, food outlets and standalone fruit and vegetable shops would be allowed to operate until 11pm. Takeaway and home delivery services would remain exempt from the timing restrictions.
Global geopolitical developments continue to pose significant risks. International oil prices are influenced by decisions taken by OPEC+, conflicts in the Middle East, sanctions on oil-producing nations, and disruptions in critical shipping routes such as the Strait of Hormuz and the Red Sea. Any interruption in these supply chains can immediately increase crude oil prices and freight costs. Since Pakistan imports the majority of its petroleum requirements, these developments quickly translate into higher domestic fuel prices.
Oil prices jumped more than 5% on Thursday, then pared gains after President Donald Trump said the US will ‌not launch an attack on Iran before midterm congressional elections in November.
Brent crude futures were up $3.48, or 3.5%, at $103.73 a barrel by 12:41 pm ET (1641 GMT). US West Texas Intermediate (WTI) crude gained $2.69, or 3.1%, to $91. At their session highs, both contracts were up more than $5 a barrel, with Brent at its highest ​since September 29 on worries about potential imminent US strikes on Iran and a supply loss in the US Gulf ​of Mexico from Hurricane Isaias.
"Further details surrounding the G7's proposed 100 million-barrel SPR release have disappointed the market, as the barrels appear to be drawn from the previously announced ‌400 million-barrel ⁠release that has yet to be fully marketed," Staunovo added.

items.author: Anne Florentyna
items.content:
D2C lifestyle startup DailyObjects has raised ₹332 Cr ($34.3 Mn) in a Series C funding round co-led by Xponentia Capital Partners, Anicut Capital and Axiom Asia Private Capital. The round, which included both primary and secondary transactions, valued the startup at ₹1,050 Cr ($108.4 Mn).
As part of the secondary deal, DailyObjects’ early investor Roots Ventures partially exited with a 18X return on its initial investment.
Roots Ventures first invested $2 Mn in DailyObjects in February 2022. Following which, the investor doubled down on the startup during its $10 Mn Series B funding round in 2024.
The fresh funds will allow DailyObjects, which is known for its lifestyle and tech accessories like phone cases, watchbands, bags, wallets and wireless chargers, to scale its offline network, deepen its product and R&D capabilities, strengthen brand building and evaluate opportunities in international markets.
The startup is planning to expand its physical retail network to 150 exclusive brand outlets (EBOs) across India over the next five years.
“We are looking at this as capital to build a ₹1,000 Cr business over the coming years and, ultimately, a global design-led consumer brand from India. As we scale, capital efficiency and profitable growth will remain at the core of how we build,” DailyObjects cofounder and CEO Pankaj Garg said.
Founded in 2012 by Garg and Adlakha, DailyObjects started off as an online store which offered users with a range of smartphone and tablet accessories. Through its journey, the startup expanded to other lifestyle product lines like bags, wallets, among other lifestyle related products.
The startup opened its first offline retail experience store DailyObjects ‘Playground’ in Gurugram back in 2023. Further, the startup expanded its offline footprint by setting up nine retail stores across Tier I cities like Delhi NCR and Bengaluru.
Prior to this round, DailyObjects claimed to have raised about ₹100 Cr in equity over the last decade. Its cap table includes investors like Lenskart founder Peyush Bansal, Unilazer Ventures and RedBus founder Phani Sama.
On the financial front, Garg projected its FY26 net revenue to double to ₹220 Cr to ₹230 Cr from ₹111 Cr reported in FY25. He also expects its top line to further jump to ₹400 Cr by FY27.
