items.author: Reuters
items.content:
Indian opposition groups demonstrated for a third day on Thursday, protesting police ‌action against Congress party leaders and demanding the resignation of the chief election commissioner over a controversial revision of voter lists.
Opposition parties, their student units, and the "Cockroach" youth movement have been holding almost daily demonstrations seeking Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar's ​resignation. They have accused Prime Minister Narendra Modi's ruling Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) of using ​a revision of voter lists to fix them in its favour, in collusion ⁠with its appointees, including Kumar.
Kumar has not commented, but the Election Commission and the BJP have ​denied the allegations.
The protests present a new political challenge to Modi midway into his third term, ​just months after similar demonstrations led by the self-named Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) forced the resignation of his education minister over exam paper leaks.
Read: Modi's education minister quits as jubilant Indian youth protesters claim victory, end protest
Visuals from news agency ANI showed dozens of Congress supporters staging a protest march on Thursday in ​the southern state of Telangana, while the opposition Rashtriya Janata Dal organised a similar demonstration in ​the eastern state of Bihar.
Hundreds of supporters of the CJP youth movement also protested in tech hub Bengaluru, many ‌of ⁠them holding posters that said, "Every name counts, Every vote matters" and "Stop the Murder of Democracy".
"I think voting right is the most basic point of democracy ... People who actually want to vote, who actually care about the future of India, they are just being (denied) voting rights," Khushi Shrivastava, a 22-year-old architecture ​student who attended the ​Bengaluru protest, told Reuters.
Read more: India's 'cockroach' movement says will launch protest if poll panel chief doesn't quit in 48 hours
On ⁠Wednesday, Congress accused police of using "brute force" to briefly detain party leader Rahul Gandhi, his sister Priyanka Vadra, and other lawmakers as they tried to ​reach the Jantar Mantar protest site in New Delhi.
Delhi Police said the ​allegations were being ⁠used to "defame" the force.
"We are on the ground and, as officers, we also ensure that every kind of legal duty is followed and no illegal, unnecessary actions take place," senior police officer Shrishti Pandey ⁠told ANI.

items.author: Yus Lianson
items.content:
OpenAI baru saja meluncurkan Intelligent UI di ChatGPT, sebuah fitur yang memungkinkan jawaban chatbot dalam bentuk grafik, diagram, tombol, form, hingga tools interaktif seperti kalkulator.
Adapun fitur ini mulai digulirkan secara global bersamaan dengan peluncuran GPT-6 pada 7 Oktober 2026, dan sudah bisa dinikmati oleh pengguna ChatGPT Plus, Pro, Business, dan Enterprise, lalu disusul ke pengguna Free dan Go mulai hari ini.
Menurut perusahaan AI tersebut, tujuan diperkenalkannya Intelligent UI ini agar bentuk jawaban prompt pengguna bisa menyesuaikan pertanyaan, sehingga hasilnya bisa langsung dipakai, bukan hanya dibaca, sebagaimana dikutip dari laman web OpenAI, Kamis (8/10/2026).
Baca Juga: Google Playground Ubah Prompt Jadi Game, Tanpa Perlu Coding
OpenAI Perkenalkan Intelligent UI di ChatGPT, Apa Itu?
Intelligent UI adalah kemampuan GPT-6 menyusun jawaban dari tiga komponen, seperti teks, visual, dan elemen interaktif. Nanti, model AI akan memutuskan sendiri bagaimana ketiganya digabungkan, tergantung dari pertanyaan pengguna.
Jawaban pun bisa dibuat dalam bentuk perbandingan, sedangkan penjelasan konsep bisa ditampilkan dalam bentuk diagram interaktif. Pertanyaan sederhana juga tetap dijawab dengan teks biasa.
OpenAI menyebut, fitur ini sebagai langkah awal menuju software menyesuaikan diri dengan kebutuhan pengguna ChatGPT. Perusahaan juga menjelaskan, kemampuan Intelligent UI diigunakan dalam beberapa skenario.
Intelligent UI di GPT-6
Pertama adalah menjelajah ide, di mana visual interaktif dapat membantu pengguna melihat cara kerja sesuatu dan fokus pada bagian tertentu. Salah satu contoh demonstrasi adalah menampilkan informasi masing-masing komponen sepeda lebih detail.
Selanjutnya membuat tools atau app, pengguna bisa meminta kalkulator, pembagi tagihan makan bersama, atau game yang bisa dimainkan saat dalam percakapan. Intelligent UI ini juga sudah memahami konsep, dan terakhir adalah bisa menyesuaikan jawaban.
Menurut laporan Tech Startups, fitur baru ChatGPT ini juga bisa membuat rencana makan malam, menyusun pakaian, dan pembagian tagihan restoran berdasarkan struk.
Bagaimana Intelligent UI Bekerja?
Antarmuka tampil progresif, yaitu muncul saat model masih menghasilkan jawaban. OpenAI memakai library komponen native dan compiler yang menampilkan interface selama proses itu berlangsung.
Intelligent UI di GPT-6
GPT-6 juga bisa mulai menjawab sambil terus berpikir. OpenAI melaporkan GPT-6 Instant mulai menjawab pertanyaan yang membutuhkan web search rata-rata 44 persen lebih cepat dibanding GPT-5.6 Instant. Angka ini mengukur waktu mulai menjawab, bukan total waktu hingga jawaban selesai.
OpenAI mengakui kemampuan design judgment model, yaitu pilihan tata letak dan elemen interaktif, masih perlu dikembangkan.
Apa Bedanya dengan Generative UI Google?
Google lebih dulu memperkenalkan generative UI, juga disebut generative interfaces, bersama Gemini 3 pada 18 November 2025. Sebelum Intelligent UI, ChatGPT sudah punya grafik interaktif dan modul interaktif untuk lebih dari 70 topik matematika dan sains . Intelligent UI memperluas pendekatan itu ke berbagai jenis pertanyaan.
Apa Arti Perubahan Ini?
Bagi pengguna, perubahan utamanya ada pada bentuk jawaban. Pertanyaan soal keuangan bisa berujung pada kalkulator, penjelasan konsep pada diagram interaktif, dan kebutuhan sederhana tetap berupa teks.
Satu hal perlu dicermati. Tampilan yang rapi tidak menjamin isinya benar. Search Engine Journal mencatat pengumuman GPT-6 belum menjelaskan bagaimana sumber informasi ditampilkan ketika jawaban berbentuk grafik, perbandingan, atau alat. OpenAI sendiri masih menyebut kemampuan desain model sebagai area yang terus dikembangkan.

items.author: Shrishti Bisht
items.content:
AI startup Inner Sky Labs, the maker of children’s companion robots under the Miko brand, has launched a suite of foundation models designed to help machines perceive their surroundings, plan and execute physical actions, and check those actions against safety rules.
Alongside the launch, the startup is closing a ₹300 Cr (about $30.9 Mn) funding round involving existing backers YourNest Venture Capital and Keshav R Murugesh, as well as new global investors, cofounder and CEO Sneh Vaswani told Inc42.
Once completed, the round would take the business’s total funding to $100 Mn.
The startup plans to use the fresh capital for real-world data collection, computing infrastructure, and model training as it expands sales to enterprises, governments, and other machine makers.
The expansion builds on technology developed for Miko, which has been the business’ public-facing consumer brand since its early years. Founded in 2015 by IIT Bombay alumni Vaswani, Prashant Iyengar, and Chintan Raikar, the startup focused on children’s companion robots while developing the underlying AI models.
Vaswani said the broader physical AI initiative had been developed in stealth over the past decade. Inner Sky Labs is the newly unveiled umbrella brand for that business, operating under the same legal entity that owns Miko.
“We built these AI models ourselves, with a strong focus on safety and sovereignty. Now, we are scaling these models beyond Miko, taking them into enterprises, government applications that require sovereign AI, and other areas,” Vaswani told Inc42.
Taking Miko’s AI To Other Machines
The CEO said that the expansion had been planned since inception. During investor pitches in 2017, the team was already discussing developing AI models, with Miko as their first application before expanding into enterprise, software, and government use cases.
Limited demand for standalone AI models at the time led the team to focus on Miko. Its robots, designed to talk, play, and learn with children, provided an environment for deploying and testing the technology, particularly conversational safety.
With Inner Sky Labs, the startup is opening those capabilities to businesses building robots, industrial machines, and other systems. Customers can adopt individual models or the full platform, which is available to qualified partners by invitation.
Vaswani argued that developing foundation models is becoming too expensive for individual machine makers, particularly at modest production volumes. A common provider would allow multiple manufacturers to adopt the technology without each building their own models.
The startup describes its platform as hardware agnostic, supporting industrial arms, humanoids, mobile and companion robots, quadrupeds, cars, and CCTV systems.
AI For Sensing, Movement, And Safety
The platform combines three functions needed to operate these systems — perception, action, and safety.
Its perception models comprise Drishti for vision, Shruti for audio, and Sparsh for touch. Action models Kriya, Prana, and Karma use those inputs to help machines plan movements and anticipate their consequences.
Kavach, the independent safety layer, checks proposed actions before execution and can block those that breach predefined rules. The startup says the system has more than 20 guardrails, including checks on the presence of people, movement speeds, and permitted operating areas.
In a factory, for example, the models could help a robotic arm identify, grip, and move a component, while blocking movement if a person enters its operating area.
Vaswani said the models draw on almost a decade of physical-world data collection from factories, Miko’s manufacturing ecosystem, and other environments. He said they were developed in-house: “This is not fine-tuned on an open source model. It is our own model.”
The startup’s roadmap shows Kriya, Karma, and Prana scaling from 4 Bn, 4 Bn, and 9 Bn parameters to 12 Bn, 16 Bn, and 37 Bn, respectively.
According to Inner Sky Labs, the first generation is already being used in industrial applications, combining vision, information about a robot’s position and movement, and force and torque readings.
The next generation will focus on coordinating multiple robotic arms, handling more complex scenes, and processing richer touch signals from fingertips, fingers, and palms.
Sovereign AI And Enterprise Deployments
Beyond the models themselves, Inner Sky Labs is pitching control over deployment and operating rules as a selling point for enterprises and governments.
The startup positions its offering as sovereign AI, saying customers can run the models within their own infrastructure and define the rules governing their behaviour. Deployment options include cloud APIs, on-premise installations, and on-device processing, including offline and air-gapped environments isolated from external networks.
This allows sensitive operational data to be processed locally, with Vaswani citing drones and surveillance systems as potential applications.
“If you have CCTV cameras in a city, those cameras need to monitor exactly what has happened. You would not rely on a vision model coming from another country for any purpose. So, you would use a vision model from us,” he said.
Commercial deployments began two to three quarters before the public launch, Vaswani said. The startup has completed four to five large deployments across enterprises and governments, including outside India.
However, he did not disclose customer names or specific government applications. The startup claims to serve enterprise markets in the US and Europe and is exploring opportunities in Africa.
The launch comes amid growing activity in India’s physical AI ecosystem. While Addverb is developing humanoid robots for industrial applications, Mowito is building AI models that enable standard industrial robotic arms to learn tasks from human operators.
Edited by Vinaykumar Rai

items.author: Anadolu Agency
items.content:
A top adviser to the US ambassador to Israel had systematically suppressed, delayed and rewritten internal diplomatic cables to shield the government of Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu from scrutiny by Washington, The New York Times reported on Thursday.
David Milstein, an influential gatekeeper at the US Embassy in Jerusalem since April 2025 and principal aide to US Ambassador Mike Huckabee, repeatedly stymied assessments intended for senior policymakers, according to an investigation based on interviews with more than a dozen US officials and reviews of internal State Department records.
In late March, Israel approved record-breaking occupation expansions across the occupied West Bank. Embassy personnel drafted an alert warning that the move risked violating US President Donald Trump's explicit red line against annexation. Milstein quashed the memorandum, framing the land acquisitions as a domestic matter before sending a revised text claiming the move addressed unspecified humanitarian needs of occupiers.
Read More: Israel strikes Gaza on October 7 anniversary, at least two dead: officials
Milstein similarly altered reporting on surging violence in the occupied West Bank. When Israeli military commanders warned that attacks by occupiers could trigger a widespread Palestinian uprising, he blocked the dispatches suggesting that Israel failed to take action. Instead, an embassy cable authored under his name praised Netanyahu's initiatives and claimed authorities were actively combatting the unrest.
The aide also suppressed a detailed embassy inquiry into the killings of nine Palestinian Americans by Israeli forces and occupiers, effectively thwarting accountability requests from members of the US Congress. Despite findings showing investigations stalled without criminal charges, the mission forwarded an alternative letter claiming active cooperation with Israeli authorities.
Milstein also edited dispatches regarding aid distribution by the US-backed Gaza Humanitarian Foundation to describe the operations as successful, removing diplomatic warnings that the process was "chaotic, deadly," and risked "mass casualty events".
Staff members noted that the interventions caused reporting from the embassy's Palestinian affairs section to drop from several weekly cables to a few per month and prompted some officials to bypass official embassy channels to obtain unfiltered ground intelligence.
"The elements of the story The New York Times is trying to assemble are so lacking in fact that it ranks up with other Times farcical endeavours," said Huckabee. The US State Department said its personnel remain focused on advancing the administration's foreign policy priorities.

items.author: Reuters
items.content:
Amazon on Thursday unveiled a slate of higher-end tablets that for ​the first time feature its Alexa+ voice assistant and run on Google's Android operating system, a bet that consumers will pay ‌more for premium devices after years of focusing on the budget end of the market.
Seattle-based Amazon had been working on the tablets under the code name Kittyhawk, as Reuters reported exclusively last year, to transition away from its more limited homegrown Fire OS operating system software, after years of gripes from consumers and app developers. Fire OS is a “forked” version ​of Android, with modifications to make it work like a unique operating system.
Known as Alexa Tablets, the line features several different versions with ​starting prices from $230 to $500; all are made with aluminum cases, a switch from Fire tablets’ plastic.
The new tablets ⁠will cost as much as $550, a big bump from Amazon’s more recent top-of-the-line Fire HD 10 tablet which cost upwards of $180, though the company often ​discounted them.
The top Alexa tablet, with 128 gigabytes of memory, for $550 compares with an Apple iPad for $450 and Samsung's Galaxy tablet for $550.
 Read More: US suspends Microsoft, major IT firms from key green card programme
The product revamp marks a ​new strategy under devices chief Panos Panay to move upscale and away from the inexpensive gadgets Amazon sold at or near cost to hook customers into using Prime Video, Kindle, music apps and the main e-commerce website. That focus on affordability came with compromises, like lower screen quality and battery life, compared with rivals Apple and Samsung and others.
Alexa+, an ​advanced AI-powered version of the Alexa voice assistant, will feature prominently on the devices to help perform actions or answer questions using generative AI. Accessing Alexa+ ​on the tablets will require a Prime membership or Alexa+ subscription, Amazon said.
Amazon is pushing the pricier devices as worldwide tablet sales are falling, down 12% in the second ‌quarter from ⁠the year before to 33.6 million units, according to IDC data. The US market, which has been especially hurt by a shortage of memory chips, saw sales plunge 32% in the second quarter year over year, IDC data showed.
The Seattle company held just 1.9% of the global tablet market in this year’s second quarter, down from 8% a year earlier, according to IDC. Apple is the leader with 34%, followed by Samsung at 17.5%.
The tablet prices do not include ​a one-time fee customers have to pay ​to turn off advertising displayed ⁠on the lockscreen, though the highest-priced Alexa Tablet will not have the ads. It will require a one-time $20 fee to eliminate the ads, up from $15 for Fire OS tablets, a spokesperson said. Such ads help users “discover new content that’s relevant ​to their interests” and the revenue helps underwrite other innovations, the spokesperson said.
Upgrade from Fire OS
With Android, Alexa ​Tablet customers won’t be ⁠limited to the apps offered in the Fire OS app store, disdained by developers who had to make a third version of apps offered in the Google Play and Apple stores. And the built-in Alexa+ voice AI assistant helps to differentiate the tablets from others.
Amazon has spent billions overhauling Alexa to power it with generative ⁠AI and ​make it more capable for connected homes, shopping and accessing third-party services like Uber and Grubhub. ​The service, free with a Prime membership, is unprofitable.
Prior Fire OS tablets will still work, said the spokesperson, but she did not say whether Amazon will continue to maintain the operating system or ​app store. Earlier this year Amazon cut off support for older Kindle models, citing software maintenance costs as a reason.

Beauty and Beast, together in one phone
The POVA Curve 2 5G is not built around a single strength. It is an all-rounder, a complete package that arrives as a Beauty and a Beast together, and neither side comes at the cost of the other.
The Beauty is in plain sight: curved glass flowing into a remarkably slim body, finished in colours chosen to turn heads. It is the kind of phone that makes the person next to you ask what you are holding. How slim, and which colours? TECNO is keeping that to itself for now.
The Beast is underneath: a phone that does not need to be handled gently. Life in Pakistan is hard on phones: dust, rain, heat, crowded commutes and the drop nobody plans for. The new POVA Curve 2 5G is built with all-round environmental protection and drop protection, so its owner can stop worrying and simply use it.
Exactly how much it can take is another detail TECNO is saving for later.
The rest is still a secret
Beauty and Beast are the only two clues TECNO is giving away today. What sits inside, what it will cost and the day it arrives all remain under wraps, with more to be revealed soon. POVA became a fan favourite in Pakistan by outdoing what people expected of it, and this comeback is built to do it again. For now, one thing is certain: the wait Pakistan’s POVA fans have endured for two years is almost over.

items.title: Turkiye's FM Fidan maintains Makkah pact is 'defensive' in nature, will not send troops
items.summary:
Turkish Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan said on Thursday that Turkiye would not send troops to confront Yemen’s Houthis, while stressing that the Makkah defence pact with Saudi Arabia and Pakistan was "defensive", not offensive in nature and did not authorise attacks on other countries.
On August 7, Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye formalised their longstanding strategic relationship through the newly signed Makkah pact, a trilateral security framework that its proponents describe as a defensive arrangement aimed at strengthening collective deterrence, enhancing military cooperation and promoting regional stability.
Speaking at a joint ​press conference with his Hungarian counterpart Anita Orban in Ankara, Fidan said that the Makkah agreement provided for mutual defence if one of its signatories came under attack, further clarifying that the pact did not authorise Turkiye to deploy troops to another country's territory to carry out an attack.
LIVE: Turkish Foreign Minist
items.author: Reuters
items.content:
Turkish Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan said on Thursday that Turkiye would not send troops to confront Yemen’s Houthis, while stressing that the Makkah defence pact with Saudi Arabia and Pakistan was "defensive", not offensive in nature and did not authorise attacks on other countries.
On August 7, Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye formalised their longstanding strategic relationship through the newly signed Makkah pact, a trilateral security framework that its proponents describe as a defensive arrangement aimed at strengthening collective deterrence, enhancing military cooperation and promoting regional stability.
Speaking at a joint ​press conference with his Hungarian counterpart Anita Orban in Ankara, Fidan said that the Makkah agreement provided for mutual defence if one of its signatories came under attack, further clarifying that the pact did not authorise Turkiye to deploy troops to another country's territory to carry out an attack.
LIVE: Turkish Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan holds a joint press conference with Hungarian Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Anita Orban in Ankara https://t.co/yKVJhCOQYF
— TRT World (@trtworld) October 8, 2026
"But this is a defensive agreement. When a country party ​to the pact comes under attack, you stand by it in its defence. This is not an offensive ‌agreement. ⁠Turkiye will not send troops to another country to carry out attacks on its territory," he said.
"Yemen's legitimate government forces are already continuing the battle on the ground, and Saudi Arabia ​is supporting them. But at the same time, we are doing everything we can to help resolve the issue through peace and dialogue," Fidan added.
The Turkish FM underlined that military officials were assessing possible contributions, particularly in air defence, electronic warfare and technical support, further noting that they would determine Saudi Arabia's operational defence needs and what contributions Turkiye and Pakistan could make.
On Wednesday, two officials told Reuters that Turkiye was sending mainly defensive ​and technical support to ​Saudi Arabia to help ⁠its fight with Houthis.
Turkiye officials have said any support provided at this stage would largely be in a bilateral capacity, as ​Turkiye's parliament had not officially ratified the joint defence pact.
Fidan further stated that Turkiye had completed preparations to submit the Makkah defence agreement to parliament for approval. "The necessary work for the agreement to be submitted to parliament has been completed."
Turkish FM Hakan Fidan says Türkiye is assessing defence support for Saudi Arabia, particularly air defence, as the Mecca Joint Defence Agreement with Saudi Arabia and Pakistan moves toward parliamentary approval and institutional implementation pic.twitter.com/rFZ3y2DFCJ
— TRT World Now (@TRTWorldNow) October 8, 2026
He said he made a final presentation on the matter to Turkiye President Recep Tayyip Erdogan on Wednesday and that Turkiye had decided to send the agreement to parliament as soon as possible.
Fidan said Turkiye's participation in the October 5 meeting of the Strategic Political and Defence Committee of the Makkah Agreement for Joint Defence in Riyadh was primarily prompted by attacks targeting Saudi Arabia.
He said the extraordinary meeting also addressed several institutional issues, including the structure of the military headquarters, the status of the secretariat and the appointment of a new secretary.
Although the agreement was signed relatively recently, Fidan said institutionalisation and practical steps had advanced rapidly.
“The parties are showing through their determination that they are serious about this and want to see concrete results,” he said.
Fidan said the meeting also discussed possible Turkish contributions to Saudi Arabia's defence against attacks by Yemen's Houthi group.
Turkish FM Fidan:
- Türkiye is working on possible technical support for Saudi Arabia against attacks from Yemen
- Türkiye is not sending troops to carry out attacks on another country's land
- Mecca agreement is a defence pact, not an offensive alliance pic.twitter.com/3s6TAHJcu8
— TRT World (@trtworld) October 8, 2026
Turkiye, which has NATO's second-largest army and a robust ⁠defence industry, ​has condemned the Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia, voiced willingness ​to help meet Riyadh's technical military needs, and agreed to join a Saudi-led coalition to ensure navigational safety ​in the Red Sea.
Fidan’s remarks came after Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye activated the practical implementation of their collective defence commitments on Monday.
Read: Makkah defence alliance agrees to 'rapid force deployment' in Saudi Arabia: FO
According to a joint statement issued on Monday night, the activation entailed immediate deployment of "the agreed military forces and capabilities to the kingdom in response to security threats".
The decision was taken at an emergency meeting of the Strategic-Political and Defence Committee of the alliance, held in Riyadh to discuss the security developments and threats facing Saudi Arabia.
Saudi Arabia is currently engaged in an active conflict with Houthis, who have been targeting the various strategic and economic assets in the kingdom.
On Wednesday, Inter-Services Public Relations Director General Lieutenant General Ahmed Sharif Chaudhry said that Pakistani troops were present in Saudi Arabia in "multiple capabilities" amid the kingdom's conflict with Yemen's Houthis and developments related to it.
Read More: Makkah pact: DG ISPR says Pakistani troops present in Saudi Arabia in 'multiple capabilities'
In an interview with CNN, the military spokesperson was questioned about whether Pakistani military personnel were present in the kingdom as part of the Makkah Defence Alliance, to which he said: "I do confirm that the forces of Pakistan are already there ... the Pakistani troops have been there for decades in multiple capabilities."
The DG ISPR reiterated that forces were present in "multiple domains" in the kingdom.
Significance of the Makkah pact
The Makkah pact was the latest step in longstanding military and strategic cooperation between Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye. Signed in Makkah, the pact established a framework for collective deterrence and stipulated that an armed attack on any one of the three countries would be considered an attack on all three, while providing for wider cooperation across defence.
The agreement followed nearly a year of negotiations and came amid heightened instability across the Middle East. Turkiye and Pakistan had sought closer regional security cooperation, while Saudi Arabia had faced growing security concerns as conflicts spread across the region, threatening its territory, energy infrastructure and ambitious economic development plans.
For Pakistan and Saudi Arabia, the trilateral pact is built on their Strategic Mutual Defence Agreement signed in September 2025. That agreement stated that “any aggression against either country shall be considered an aggression against both” and committed the two sides to strengthening defence cooperation and joint deterrence.

items.author: Amiya Johar
items.content:
Indian authorities pushed back against Elon Musk’s claims that unnamed oligarchs were blocking Starlink from launching in the country, stating all three prospective operators remain broadly at the same stage of the regulatory process.
In a post on X, Musk accused “certain oligarchs” of trying to maintain a “monopolistic chokehold on the Indian people”, adding “you can guess who they are…” without naming the parties involved. “This is a crime against the people of India!” he wrote.
In a statement, India’s Ministry of Communications rejected the allegation, explaining its satellite communications framework is “fair and non-discriminatory”. It said assessments are currently underway for all licensed operators in India, with each required to meet security conditions before it can seek spectrum.
“At present, all the three entities are at broadly the same regulatory stage,” the ministry said, calling claims of discriminatory treatment “baseless and misconceived”.
The country’s telecoms sector is dominated by Mukesh Ambani’s Reliance Jio and Sunil Mittal’s Bharti Airtel. Both operators, alongside Musk’s Starlink, have secured initial approvals for satellite services but are awaiting spectrum assignment and final clearances.
Starlink’s approval process has stretched over four years, with security requirements and spectrum access among the key issues under scrutiny. Musk has previously clashed with Ambani over India’s satellite spectrum allocation, although both Reliance Jio and Bharti Airtel later struck agreements with the tech mogul to distribute Starlink services in the country.
The US satellite venture’s regulatory wait has also been marred by security concerns. Local media reports stated authorities recovered illegal Starlink equipment in two separate operations in late 2024, including a drug seizure in the Andaman and Nicobar Islands and an army search in the northeastern state of Manipur.
This week, Musk also disputed any suggestion the equipment was connected to an active Starlink service in India, posting on X that its satellite beams were “turned off over India” and “never on in the first place”.

items.author: REUTERS
items.content:
Max Verstappen said Thursday he was determined to settle his "unfinished business" at the Singapore Grand Prix, where he has never won.
The Red Bull driver took his first victory of 2026 at the Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia last weekend, the 72nd time that he has stood on the top step of the podium in a career that has brought him four world titles.
But none of those wins have come in Singapore where a bumpy track, slow corners and high humidity seem to favour other cars.
The Dutchman would love to break his long losing streak at the Marina Bay Circuit.
"I think in the last few years we have always been bad at low speed and over kerbing and bumps," Verstappen told reporters.
"This car is probably more competitive at low speed, but we still struggle on bumps and kerbs. We know that and so, of course, I have unfinished business here."
He finished second last year behind the Mercedes of George Russell and believes he can go one better and complete back-to-back victories in steamy southeast Asia.
"Every year I come back here and I'm trying to win it. I hope we can be a little more competitive this year compared to the last few years."
With a sprint race in Singapore this year, it means there is only one Friday practice session for the drivers and teams to get up to speed.
"It's always hectic, a sprint weekend, to make the right choices," said Verstappen.
"The most important thing is just to find a good balance with the car straight away. That will help a lot for the rest of the weekend."

items.title: US suspends Microsoft, major IT firms from key green card programme
items.summary:
The US government is suspending Microsoft, Adobe and several large IT firms from a programme that allows skilled foreign workers to gain permanent residency, senior US officials announced on Thursday, citing alleged fraud and an effort to push companies to hire more Americans.
"Our message to Microsoft is: You're a great American company, but you've got to hire great American workers," US Vice President JD Vance said.
Secretary of Labor Keith Sonderling added that some of the largest IT firms in the world would also be suspended from the programme, including Cognizant, Infosys, Tata, Wipro, HCL and Capgemini.
"We will not accept any new or process any pending permanent labor certification applications involving these companies," Sonderling said.

items.content:
The US government is suspending Microsoft, Adobe and several large IT firms from a programme that allows skilled foreign workers to gain permanent residency, senior US officials announced on Thursday, citing alleged fraud and an effort to push companies to hire more Americans.
"Our message to Microsoft is: You're a great American company, but you've got to hire great American workers," US Vice President JD Vance said.
Secretary of Labor Keith Sonderling added that some of the largest IT firms in the world would also be suspended from the programme, including Cognizant, Infosys, Tata, Wipro, HCL and Capgemini.
"We will not accept any new or process any pending permanent labor certification applications involving these companies," Sonderling said.
.@VP: "There has been no company in the United States, unfortunately, that has abused this system more than Microsoft."
Microsoft laid off 6,000 American workers in 2025 after certifying that it could not find qualified American employees — yet the company was approved for more… https://t.co/xh4ZYUDobZ pic.twitter.com/HGOY63Xwkf
— Rapid Response 47 (@RapidResponse47) October 8, 2026
Microsoft did not immediately respond to a request for comment.
Under the PERM process, employers seek certification from the Department of Labor that there is no qualified, willing or available US worker for a specific job. It is a step required before filing petitions for most employment-based green cards.
Vance also said nine universities, including Harvard, Yale and Stanford, would be investigated for allegedly bringing in international students to undercut American wages.
Labor Inspector General Anthony D'Esposito said subpoenas had already been served.
"We will investigate whether foreign influence, improper financial relationships, or visa abuse are compromising federally funded research," D'Esposito said.
"If an American university is breaking the law to save $1 while exposing American research to a foreign adversary, that is not academic excellence. It's institutional betrayal."

items.content:
Copyright protected content copied from PhoneWorld website.
Zong, is taking 5G beyond the smartphone and into the Pakistani home with the launch of Z HomeFi – Pakistan’s first 5G Fixed Wireless Access (FWA) home broadband service, ushering a new era of future-ready, technology-led connectivity.
Z HomeFi marks another milestone in Zong’s journey to transform connectivity into technology-led services, translating next-generation 5G innovation into a simple, accessible and customer-centric home broadband experience. By removing the need for fibre installation, fixed-line infrastructure and complex installations, Z HomeFi gives households greater flexibility and convenience while delivering high-speed, reliable connectivity designed around the evolving needs of today’s digitally connected consumers.
Z HomeFi is available across Pakistan’s top 10 cities, bringing next-generation home broadband within reach of more customers. The service is available exclusively through Zong’s Customer Service Centres, with plans to extend availability to franchises in the future.
Z HomeFi brings flexible home broadband options to households through 12 prepaid bundles, offering speeds ranging from 10 Mbps to 50 Mbps and monthly data allowances of 100 GB to 500 GB. Priced between PKR 4,500 and PKR 11,000 per month, inclusive of taxes, the bundles cater to varying household budgets and connectivity needs, from everyday browsing to streaming, remote working and online learning. The service’s 5G indoor Customer Premises Equipment (CPE), priced at PKR 22,000, supports a simple plug-and-connect setup.
The launch reinforces Zong’s role as a technology enabler of Digital Pakistan, harnessing its network, digital platforms and intelligent capabilities into developing solutions that create meaningful customer value today while enabling what comes next.
Commenting on the launch, Zong Head of Marketing Sajid Munir said:
“The true value of technology is measured by how it improves people’s everyday lives. With Z HomeFi, we are bringing 5G technology directly into Pakistani homes, giving customers a reliable and convenient broadband experience without the complexity of fibre installation or fixed-line infrastructure. Whether it is learning, working, streaming, creating or staying connected, Z HomeFi gives households greater flexibility and seamless access to the digital experiences that matter most.”
Through Z HomeFi, Zong is bringing its brand promise of ‘Aisa Hai Future’ to life, taking advanced 5G technology into homes and contributing to a more connected, inclusive and future-ready Pakistan.
Pakistan’s first 5G FWA home broadband is here, and Zong is leading the way.

items.author: Our Correspondent
items.content:
The judicial commission investigating the Mir Raza Ali case has concluded its proceedings after recording the statements of key witnesses, including a CPLC official and the investigating officer, according to a written order issued on Wednesday.
The order, issued by commission chairman Justice Omar Sial, said that Mir Hussain Ali Khan, Maryam Hussain, and Barrister Jibran Nasir were present during the proceedings, along with Additional Secretary Javed Ahmed Abro, CPLC witnesses Kashif Iftikhar and Taha Pracha, and Investigating Officer DSP Siraj Lashari.
The statements of Kashif Iftikhar and DSP Siraj Lashari were recorded.
Read: Missing CCTV puts Raza probe under fresh scrutiny
A K-Electric representative, Rabia, also appeared on behalf of Managing Director Syed Muhammad Talha and submitted a sealed envelope, which was taken on record.
Justice Sial thanked and commended Talha for his “prompt and effective” response to the commission’s request.
The commission’s email and WhatsApp accounts have now been deactivated, while the Rs100,000 reward announced earlier has also been withdrawn, the order said.
In his concluding remarks, Justice Sial thanked Sindh Chief Justice Zafar Ahmed Rajput for entrusting him with the responsibility of heading the commission.
He also acknowledged the support extended by Chief Minister Murad Ali Shah and Home Minister Zia Ul Hassan Lanjar, describing their cooperation as unwavering and complete.
Justice Sial thanked Faryal Talpur, who he said had proposed the commission to bring the facts to light and address public concerns and speculation surrounding the case.
Also Read: Judicial commission visits Mir Raza murder site, summons key witness
He praised Maryam, Alishba and Mir Hussain for displaying “exceptional patience, courage, dignity and civility” throughout the proceedings.
The chairman also thanked Additional Home Secretary Javed Abro, Section Officer Ejaz Ali Bhatti, and Deputy Home Secretary Naveed Arain for promptly responding to the commission’s directions and requests.
“They have worked very hard,” the order stated.
Justice Sial commended Nasir, counsel for the Mir Hussain family, for assisting the commission with dedication and maintaining a dignified attitude.
He also thanked Sindh Advocate General Javad Dero for appearing before the commission with dignity and civility after making a mistake on one occasion.
The commission chairman acknowledged lawyers Maruf Hussain and Khalid Mumtaz, who represented some of the witnesses, for complying with the commission’s requests and helping maintain its dignity and decorum.
He also praised members of the press and media for attending every hearing and reporting the proceedings professionally, accurately and seriously.
Justice Sial specifically mentioned journalists Babar Saleem and Sault Jafri, saying their investigative work had greatly assisted him, although they were unaware that their reporting was helping the commission.
Read More: Mir Raza judicial commission’s term extended until October 15
The chairman thanked all witnesses who appeared before the commission and maintained restraint and dignity while answering its questions.
He also acknowledged people who provided information that assisted him in his work, as well as those who had consistently criticised the commission.
Justice Sial concluded by praising the commission’s staff for working with dedication and commitment, often until late at night.
He requested the Sindh government to consider granting the staff a bonus equivalent to two basic salaries, noting that their pay was relatively low.
With the recording of statements completed and its communication channels deactivated, the commission has formally brought its proceedings to an end.

They were alive, eligible to vote and still living at the addresses listed on their electoral records. Yet, in Karnataka’s ongoing revision of electoral rolls, eight voters were allegedly marked dead and targeted for deletion — six of them Muslim women.
The cases have surfaced in Vijayapura, where expelled BJP MLA Basanagouda Patil Yatnal submitted a list seeking the deletion of 1,054 voters on August 31, barely a week after the draft electoral rolls were published on August 24.
According to activists and the affected voters, the deletion requests were supported by death certificates that matched the voters’ names but carried different details, including the names of parents or spouses and addresses.

They were alive, eligible to vote and still living at the addresses listed on their electoral records. Yet, in Karnataka’s ongoing revision of electoral rolls, eight voters were allegedly marked dead and targeted for deletion — six of them Muslim women.
The cases have surfaced in Vijayapura, where expelled BJP MLA Basanagouda Patil Yatnal submitted a list seeking the deletion of 1,054 voters on August 31, barely a week after the draft electoral rolls were published on August 24.
According to activists and the affected voters, the deletion requests were supported by death certificates that matched the voters’ names but carried different details, including the names of parents or spouses and addresses.
Also Read: India detains several in Gen Z voter protests
The victims include Malanbi Jamadar, 57; Mahabubi Peerazade Jahagirdar, 35; and Raziya Mehrunnisa Sheikh, 35, a resident of Ward-22, Langar Bazaar.
Government teacher Allama Bagwan, along with Abdul Razak Bagwan and Mumtaj Mulla, were also among those reportedly listed for deletion.
Activist Irfan Sheikh said the eight voters whose cases had been identified were alive and that the remaining 1,046 names on the list were also being verified.
The controversy has raised fresh questions over the use of bulk applications to remove voters from electoral rolls, particularly in constituencies with sizeable Muslim populations.
Bulk deletion requests
The allegations emerged during the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls, a nationwide exercise being overseen by Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar.
Activists claim more than 4,000 bulk Form-7 applications — the form used to request deletion of names from electoral rolls — have been submitted across Karnataka, with a significant number targeting Muslim voters.
In Babaleshwar alone, 1,373 Form-7 applications were reportedly submitted on September 22. Of these, 1,363 applications were allegedly filed by just 10 people.
The developments triggered protests outside the Vijayapura Deputy Commissioner’s office, while affected women and activists later held a press conference organised by Jagrutha Karnataka in Bengaluru.
The women demanded criminal cases against Yatnal, accusing him of attempting to facilitate the wrongful removal of legitimate voters from the electoral rolls.
Inquiry ordered
District Electoral Officer K Anand ordered an inquiry after preliminary scrutiny found that some of the death certificates submitted with the deletion requests appeared to belong to people with the same names as the voters or raised questions about their authenticity.
The findings have intensified concerns over whether electoral safeguards were followed before deletion requests were submitted or processed.
Under electoral procedures, objections seeking deletion of a voter’s name are subject to verification. The use of allegedly mismatched death certificates has therefore become a central issue in the Vijayapura controversy.
Yatnal has defended the electoral revision process and Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. He has also publicly alleged that "Muslims are the bogus voters”, a claim that has drawn criticism from activists who say the ongoing exercise risks disproportionately disenfranchising Muslim citizens.
The Vijayapura cases have become a flashpoint in the wider debate over the SIR, with activists warning that wrongful deletions could deprive eligible citizens of their constitutional right to vote.
For the affected women, however, the issue is more immediate: they remain alive, but their names were placed on a list that sought to treat them as though they were not.

Update| October 8, 2026, 16:54 IST
Shares of Paytm ended today’s trading session 5.4% lower at ₹1,640 apiece on the BSE.
Meanwhile, shares of Pine Labs fell 4.3% to ₹169.75, while Mobikwik declined 4.5% by the end of the session.
Original| October 8, 2026, 14:05 IST
Shares of fintech companies Paytm, Pine Labs and MobiKwik came under pressure today following reports that the proposed merchant discount rate (MDR) on select UPI transactions could be deferred.
Paytm’s stock fell as much as 10% to an intraday low of ₹1,560.60 apiece on the BSE. As of 13:30 PM IST, the stock was trading 5.21% lower at ₹1,643 apiece, giving the company a market capitalisation of ₹1,05,416.1 Cr ($10.8 Bn).
Pine Labs was trading 4.3% lower at ₹169.90 apiece, with a market capitalisation of ₹19,619.18 Cr ($2 Bn).
MobiKwik, meanwhile, was trading 5.7% lower at ₹241.25 apiece, with a market capitalisation of ₹1,899.7 Cr ($196.3 Mn).
The sell-off comes amid reports that the rollout of MDR on select UPI transactions may be deferred from October 15, to January 1, 2027.
As per a report by Business Standard, a proposal to defer the MDR rollout is under consideration, with a final decision expected in the coming days. The delay, if approved, would keep eligible merchant UPI payments free of MDR through the festive season.
The UPI and Services Steering Committee, headed by NPCI, met on Wednesday to discuss the proposed rollout among various other aspects of the framework.
The committee is also considering increasing the exemption threshold to businesses with an annual turnover of up to ₹40 Lakh. Under the earlier proposal, merchants receiving up to ₹1 Lakh a month through UPI QR codes directly into their bank accounts would be exempt from the fee.
Meanwhile, the RBI governor Sanjay Malhotra said on Wednesday that a “small fee” in the form of MDR is unlikely to have a major impact on UPI transaction volumes.
“As of now, we do not see any drop in volumes. And I don’t personally think that a small fee will have a major impact on the volumes,” Malhotra told reporters at the central bank headquarters.
Meanwhile, UPI transactions continued to grow, with the platform processing 24.07 Bn transactions worth ₹29.37 Tn in September, up 22.6% YoY in volume and 18% YoY in value.

items.author: Onsa Mustafa
items.content:
Copyright protected content copied from PhoneWorld website.
Samsung Electronics expects a major jump in quarterly profit as demand for artificial intelligence (AI) technology continues to boost the global semiconductor industry.
The South Korean technology giant estimates that its operating profit for the three months ending in September will reach 107.4 trillion won ($80 billion). This would represent a roughly nine-fold increase from the same period last year and mark Samsung’s fourth consecutive quarter of record earnings.
The company will release its complete third-quarter financial results at the end of October. However, Samsung has issued an early earnings forecast to give investors an indication of its expected performance.
Samsung Eyes $80 Billion Profit as AI Demand Drives Chip Sales
The strong results are largely linked to rising demand for memory chips used in AI data centres. AI companies require large quantities of high-performance memory and other advanced semiconductors to train and operate increasingly powerful AI systems.
Samsung is one of the world’s largest memory chip manufacturers. It is competing with SK Hynix of South Korea and Micron of the United States. Their chips are used in AI infrastructure developed by major technology companies, including Nvidia and other data-centre operators.
The rapid expansion of AI services has created strong demand for semiconductors and helped improve prices and sales across the industry.
Samsung Gets Support From Smartphone Business
Samsung’s semiconductor division is not the only part of the company expected to benefit. Its smartphone business could also receive a boost from the company’s latest foldable devices, which were launched in August.
Samsung remains one of the world’s largest smartphone manufacturers, with products including the Galaxy S26 series and Galaxy Fold lineup. Strong demand for its latest premium devices could provide additional support to its overall earnings.
However, the company’s expected profit surge is primarily being attributed to the semiconductor business and the ongoing AI-driven chip boom.
Global Investment in AI Chips Continues
The growing demand for AI computing has triggered a major increase in investment across the semiconductor and data-centre industries.
Major US technology companies, including Google, Amazon and Meta, will invest more than $650 billion in AI projects this year. Much of this spending is helping drive demand for computing infrastructure, processors and memory chips.
South Korea is also seeking to strengthen its position in the global semiconductor industry. In June, the country announced plans involving at least $880 billion in projects led by Samsung and SK Hynix to expand chip manufacturing capabilities over the coming years.
Companies in Japan, China and Taiwan are also investing heavily in new semiconductor facilities as they look to benefit from the long-term growth of AI.
See Also: Samsung Begins Mass Production of Exynos 2700 Ahead of Galaxy S27 Launch
Chip Shortage Pushes Up Prices
The rapid increase in demand for semiconductors has also created supply pressures in parts of the market. Manufacturers have responded by increasing chip prices as demand continues to outpace available supply for certain products.
Higher semiconductor costs can eventually affect consumer products, including smartphones and computers, potentially making some devices more expensive.
Samsung’s expected record earnings highlight how strongly the AI boom is affecting the wider technology industry. As companies continue to expand AI data centres and invest in advanced computing, demand for memory chips is expected to remain an important source of growth for major semiconductor manufacturers.

items.author: Anjali Jain
items.content:
Prime Minister Narendra Modi has urged global tech companies, financial institutions and telecom operators to collaborate and form a comprehensive framework to curb cyber fraud and deep fakes.
“At a time when telecom and digital technology have become so important, it is equally important to make the security framework associated with it ironclad. It is our priority to secure mobile phones and networks… trust is very important for ordinary citizens communicating or making payments through the phone,” PM Modi said.
Speaking at the India Mobile Congress 2026, the PM highlighted India’s successful endeavour to protect citizens from cyber attacks and frauds, noting that global cooperation is required to nip the issue in the bud, especially as most such operations are borderless.
He urged the GSM Association (GSMA), which is a global advocacy group for the telecom industry, and global telecom operators, to create a global mechanism that can potentially prevent cyber fraud before it reaches the masses.
He also offered India’s deep expertise in the area to global regulators, noting that authorities in the country have gained vast knowledge on fighting cyber crime.
He further noted that the discussions held during the IMC’s tenth edition this year will create a map for how the next decade of telecom will look like, in India and globally.
India’s Cyber Fraud Battle
The country has grappled with rising cyber fraud over the past few years, with Indians losing ₹3,588.2 Cr in more than 5.83 Lakh digital payment fraud cases between FY22 and FY26.
The government has consequently taken several steps to curb such frauds, including a dedicated portal to report suspected crime. The Sanchar Saathi portal has received 12.8 Lakh inputs on suspected fraud communications since launch in 2023. The Centre announced this week that suspected cyber-fraud losses of more than ₹5,000 Cr were prevented through the Financial Fraud Risk Indicator (FRI).
Nevertheless, nearly 7.1% of the attempted digital consumer transactions in India were suspected fraud in 2025, almost double the equivalent rate globally (3.8%).
To curb this, union home minister Amit Shah directed officials to improve the National Cybercrime Helpline using AI to ease the process of reporting cybercrimes. He also called for addressing the issues related to bank accounts being frozen as part of cyber fraud investigations.
The RBI has also come up with a compensation mechanism to aid fraud victims, under which the Centre and bank operators shoulder parts of the unrecovered losses. Customers, losing up to ₹50,000 in cybercrime cases, would be eligible for compensation of up to 85% of the net loss amount or ₹25,000, whichever is lesser.
The post PM Modi Calls For Global Framework To Tackle Cyber Fraud appeared first on Inc42 Media.

items.content:
Copyright protected content copied from PhoneWorld website.
The National Cyber Crime Investigation Agency (NCCIA) Peshawar has recovered Rs300,000 in an online financial fraud case and returned the money to the affected citizen.
The action came after the agency received a complaint from a citizen who reported losing money through an online fraud. Following the complaint, the NCCIA Peshawar team launched an investigation to trace the fraudulent transaction and determine how the funds were obtained.
NCCIA Recovers Rs300,000 in Online Fraud Case in Peshawar and Returns Money to Citizen
According to the NCCIA, its Peshawar team carried out a detailed investigation along with technical کارروائی to track the money involved in the fraud. The agency used digital investigation methods to follow the trail of the funds and identify the transaction linked to the complaint.
As a result of the investigation, the authorities managed to recover Rs300,000 that had been obtained through fraudulent means. The authority later returned the recovered amount to the complainant.
The recovery provides an example of how digital forensics and technical investigations can help authorities trace financial transactions linked to online scams and assist victims in recovering their money.
Cybercrime Protection Among NCCIA Priorities
The NCCIA said that protecting citizens from cybercrime and taking effective action against online financial fraud are among its key priorities.
The agency continues to conduct investigations into cybercrime cases using digital forensic techniques and other technical tools. These investigations can help authorities trace digital transactions, identify suspects, and collect evidence related to online crimes.
The agency’s efforts also aim to improve public confidence in reporting cybercrime and encourage victims to approach the authorities rather than ignoring fraudulent activity.
See Also: Peshawar Court Penalizes Easypaisa Over Unauthorized Rs40,000 Transfers From Customer Account
Citizens Advised to Report Online Fraud Quickly
The NCCIA has advised citizens to remain careful when conducting financial transactions through online platforms. People should avoid sharing sensitive information such as passwords, account details, PINs, and verification codes with unknown individuals.
NCCIA also asked citizens to report online financial fraud as soon as possible. Early reporting can provide investigators with an opportunity to trace transactions and take action against those involved.
The NCCIA provides an online complaint facility for citizens who want to report cybercrime. People who become victims of online scams or financial fraud can use the available reporting channels to submit their complaints and provide relevant details to investigators.
The agency has reiterated that timely reporting and cooperation from victims can assist in the investigation of cybercrime cases and efforts to recover funds lost through fraudulent activities.

items.author: Fact Check By iVerify
items.content:
Multiple Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) supporters shared Instagram stories on Oct 8, 2026, allegedly showing social media posts from Pakistani actresses Mahira Khan and Sajal Aly expressing their support for the Cockroach Janta Party’s (CJP) Oct 10 protest. However, the visuals are fake.
Thousands of protesters gathered in New Delhi and Mumbai in October 2026, demanding the resignation of India’s Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over allegations that revisions to electoral rolls had removed millions of voters. The protests began on Oct 2, with demonstrators accusing the Election Commission of India (ECI) of disenfranchising voters to benefit Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s ruling BJP. Both the ECI and BJP denied the allegations.
Amid the demonstrations, the Gen Z-led CJP, headed by Abhijeet Dipke, announced plans to hold a major rally in New Delhi at Jantar Mantar on Oct 10, demanding free and fair elections.
How it started
On Oct 8, a BJP supporter shared a post on X featuring images allegedly showing Mahira expressing support for the Oct 10 protest at Jantar Mantar through her Instagram stories.
The post was captioned: “Pakistani actress Mahira Khan supports the October 10 protest.”
It also included her alleged Instagram story, followed by the following caption: “Still, people in India are thinking this is a genuine protest. No bro, it’s a regime-change protest against Modi, the BJP and Hindutva. If they succeed, Pakistanis will return to India, and we might see a situation like 2007 again.”
The post gained 523,000 views.
The alleged story reads: “Just heard Abhijeet Dipke and Dhruv Rathee are going to protest against the BJP government on October 10. Full support to this protest. I can’t come because the BJP has banned Pakistani actors from entering India. Hopefully, after this protest, relations between India and Pakistan will improve again.
Another BJP supporter shared the same story with the following caption: “CJP has started receiving support from Pakistan.”
The post gained 40,000 views on X.
The claim was further shared by several other BJP supporters on X, further amplifying the virality, as can be seen here, here, here, here, here, here, here, here, here, here, and here; collectively accumulating 38,000 views.
Similarly, another visual circulating on social media purported to show an Instagram story shared by Sajal Aly, expressing support for protesters in India and suggesting that a change in the country’s government was imminent.
The text in the alleged story read: “Heard someone is getting kicked out of power in the neighbouring country. Well done, youth. Finally, the era of hatred will end. Hopefully, the new people in power will make our relations better, and we can work together again like brothers.”
The Insta story snapshot was shared by a BJP supporter with the following caption: “It’s one vs all now. This is Sajal Aly, who works in Pakistani TV. She thinks the Modi regime is going to be changed. Even she knows that if Modi gets removed, the new people in power will again make Pakistan their best friend. They will allow Pakistanis to come here and work. And then these snakes will silently plan attacks on our civilians. Pakistan, CJP, leftists and America want to defeat just one man. It’ll be proper cinema if Modi Ji wins in 2029 despite all this foreign funding and paid agenda.”
The post garnered 305,000 views on X.
Another BJP supporter shared the same claim on X with the following caption: “Pakistani actress wants regime change in India. Dumb Indians, open your eyes”
The post attracted 80,000 views.
The claim was further shared by several other BJP supporters, further amplifying its virality, as can be seen here, here, here, here and here.
Methodology
A fact-check was initiated to determine the veracity of the claim due to its high virality and keen public interest in the CJP protests in India, along with whether the Pakistani actresses had actually supported them or not.
A keyword search was conducted to verify whether any credible Indian or Pakistani media outlets had reported on the alleged Instagram stories, but nothing was found to corroborate them.
Furthermore, no social media posts were found from Pakistani users, fans and media industry personnel commenting on or reacting to any such alleged posts, casting further doubt about their authenticity.
Inspecting Mahira’s official Instagram account showed no such story. Instagram stories automatically disappear after 24 hours, whereas the viral claim had surfaced on Oct 8.
On closer examination of the viral post, the fingers of Abhijeet Dipke appear distorted, a common discrepancy in AI-generated images.
The image was analysed using OpenAI’s tool to detect the SynthID watermark, which identified a SynthID signal, indicating that the image was likely generated or edited using OpenAI tools.
SynthID works by embedding an invisible digital watermark directly into AI-generated media content. Unlike normal metadata, the watermark forms part of the content itself and is designed to remain detectable even after the media is doctored, such as cropping, applying filters or lossy compression.
The photo was subsequently analysed using other AI-detection tools. Sightengine flagged the visual as 99 per cent doctored, while AI or Not flagged it as 76pc AI-generated.
 
Meanwhile, Decopy flagged the image as 91pc AI-generated and Fake Image Detector labelled it as 78pc doctored.
 
 
Similarly, for the claim regarding Sajal, her official Instagram account also carried no such story.
Meanwhile, analysing Sajal’s post using Truthscan flagged the image as 95pc doctored content.
 
Undetectable AI labelled it as 95pc edited, and Fake Image Detector flagged it as 76pc computer-generated or modified image.
Fact-check status: false
The claim that screenshots of alleged Instagram posts from Mahira Khan and Sajal Ali show them supporting the CJP’s Oct 10 protest against the BJP party is false.
The viral visuals are AI-generated and the actresses have made no such posts.
-----------------
This fact check was originally published by iVerify Pakistan — a project of CEJ-IBA and UNDP.

According to the Islamabad Police’s official website, 1815 is the dedicated online women’s helpline. Women can contact the helpline to report problems, seek guidance, or request police assistance.

Online Women Police Station
Along with the helpline, Islamabad Police has also established an online women police station to make it easier for women to communicate with law enforcement and register their complaints.
The online facility provides women with an alternative way to approach the police, particularly in situations where visiting a police station in person may be difficult or uncomfortable. It also aims to make the complaint process more accessible for female citizens.
Complaints Referred for Action
When a complaint is received through the helpline or online service, Islamabad Police forwards it to the relevant police officials and the concerned police station for necessary action.
The concerned officers can then review the complaint and take further steps according to the nature of the issue. This system will ensure that complaints received through the dedicated women’s support channel reach the appropriate authorities.
Police Urges Women to Seek Help
Islamabad Police has encouraged women to contact 1815 without hesitation if they face harassment, violence, threats, or any other serious problem requiring police assistance.
The dedicated helpline and online police station provide women with another way to report concerns and seek support. By offering access to these services around the clock, Islamabad Police aims to make it easier for women to approach law enforcement and receive timely assistance when needed.

items.summary:
Google baru saja memperkenalkan Playground, platform gaming eksperimental berbasis browser di mana pengguna bisa membuat game mereka sendiri hanya dengan mengetikkan prompt teks tanpa harus memiliki pengalaman coding.
Google Playground sendiri dirilis pada 7 Oktober 2026, dan layanan ini memungkinkan game yang baru dibuat tersebut bisa langsung dimainkan, dimodifikasi, dan dibagikan kepada pengguna lainnya.
Saat ini, Google Playground hanya tersedia untuk pengguna berusia 18 tahun ke atas di Amerika Serikat dan harus berlangganan paket Google One, sebagaimana dikutip dari laman web perusahaan, Kamis (8/10/2026).

Bikin Game di Google Playground
Raksasa mesin pencari ini menjelaskan, Playground dirancang dengan antarmuka (User Interface, UI) layaknya ngobrol dengan chatbot. Hanya dengan menjelaskan ide game lewat teks, pengguna bisa langsung menguji game buatan langsung di browser.
Tak hanya berhenti pad
items.author: Yus Lianson
items.content:
Google baru saja memperkenalkan Playground, platform gaming eksperimental berbasis browser di mana pengguna bisa membuat game mereka sendiri hanya dengan mengetikkan prompt teks tanpa harus memiliki pengalaman coding.
Google Playground sendiri dirilis pada 7 Oktober 2026, dan layanan ini memungkinkan game yang baru dibuat tersebut bisa langsung dimainkan, dimodifikasi, dan dibagikan kepada pengguna lainnya.
Saat ini, Google Playground hanya tersedia untuk pengguna berusia 18 tahun ke atas di Amerika Serikat dan harus berlangganan paket Google One, sebagaimana dikutip dari laman web perusahaan, Kamis (8/10/2026).
Baca Juga: Google Pensiunkan Gemini Gems 17 November, Pengguna Dipindahkan ke Skills
Bikin Game di Google Playground
Raksasa mesin pencari ini menjelaskan, Playground dirancang dengan antarmuka (User Interface, UI) layaknya ngobrol dengan chatbot. Hanya dengan menjelaskan ide game lewat teks, pengguna bisa langsung menguji game buatan langsung di browser.
Tak hanya berhenti pada prompt pertama. Pengguna dapat meminta AI mengubah fisika di dalam game, aturan, karakter, hingga lingkungan tanpa harus masuk ke coding secara manual.
Perusahaan juga menyediakan kanvas konsong, prompt awal, serta panduan untuk membantu pengguna membentuk konsep awal game. Proses ini membuat Playground mirip proses iterasi lewat percakapan ketimbang tool menghasilkan kode sekali lalu selesai.
Google Playground
Dalam video teaser yang Google rilis, pengguna dapa membuat game dari ide sederhana, mencoba hasil, kemudian meminta perubahan berdasarkan apa yang ingin diperbaiki. Google menyebut, pengguna tetap memegang kendali atas kreatif sejak konsep awal sampai hasil akhir.
Game Bisa Langsung Dimainkan dan Dibagikan
Setelah game selesai dibuat, pengguna dapat menyimpannya secara privat, membagikan tautan kepada orang lain, atau menerbitkannya ke Playground Explore gallery.
Karena Playground berbasis browser, game dapat dimainkan melalui ponsel maupun laptop. Pada genre tertentu, Google juga menyediakan dukungan multiplayer dan leaderboard untuk membuat game lebih kompetitif.
Google Playground
Playground juga memiliki elemen komunitas melalui profil Play Games. Pengguna dapat memilih handle, menyukai game, mengikuti kreator, serta melihat game yang menonjol berdasarkan rating dan aktivitas bermain. 
Google mengatakan game yang dipublikasikan melewati pemeriksaan keamanan dan tetap menyediakan mekanisme pelaporan dari pengguna.
Ditopang Model AI Google
Menurut laporan The Verge, Playground menggunakan model AI Google seperti Gemini, Nano Banana, dan Lyria yang dipadukan dengan sistem internal untuk menangani proses pembuatan game. Informasi tersebut disampaikan juru bicara Google kepada The Verge.
Google sendiri tidak memosisikan Playground sebagai pengganti pengembang software atau kreator game profesional Platform ini disebut sebagai eksperimen awal untuk membuat proses kreasi game lebih mudah diakses.
Karena masih berstatus eksperimen, Google juga akan terus mengembangkan Playground berdasarkan penggunaan dan masukan komunitas.
Kehadiran Playground menunjukkan arah baru dalam pembuatan game: bukan lagi sekadar menggunakan AI untuk membantu pekerjaan teknis, tetapi menjadikan bahasa sehari-hari sebagai bagian dari proses membuat dan mengubah game yang dapat langsung dimainkan.

items.title: New FEMA Rules Explained: What Freelancers, Creators, And SaaS Startups Need To Know
items.summary:
RBI governor Sanjay Malhotra yesterday eased concerns over the new foreign exchange reporting framework, clarifying that individuals undertaking transactions of a personal nature would not have to report them. He also cited earnings from overseas tutoring and small software assignments among the transactions that would not require reporting.
The clarification follows concerns among freelancers, creators, and small service exporters about additional paperwork under the Foreign Exchange Management (Export and Import of Goods and Services) Regulations, 2026. The rules, which took effect on October 1, bring goods and services trade under a unified framework.
Malhotra said banks and authorised dealers would handle reporting to the RBI, while exporters could use self-declaration for bills of up to ₹10 Lakh — a threshold that applies per bill, not to annual earnings. For established SaaS startups already reporting software exports, industry participants expect mainly procedural changes.
What
items.author: Shrishti Bisht
items.content:
RBI governor Sanjay Malhotra yesterday eased concerns over the new foreign exchange reporting framework, clarifying that individuals undertaking transactions of a personal nature would not have to report them. He also cited earnings from overseas tutoring and small software assignments among the transactions that would not require reporting.
The clarification follows concerns among freelancers, creators, and small service exporters about additional paperwork under the Foreign Exchange Management (Export and Import of Goods and Services) Regulations, 2026. The rules, which took effect on October 1, bring goods and services trade under a unified framework.
Malhotra said banks and authorised dealers would handle reporting to the RBI, while exporters could use self-declaration for bills of up to ₹10 Lakh — a threshold that applies per bill, not to annual earnings. For established SaaS startups already reporting software exports, industry participants expect mainly procedural changes.
What Has The RBI Clarified?
Malhotra said individuals’ transactions of a personal nature do not require reporting, irrespective of the amount. Examples include subscriptions to apps, television channels, journals, and newspapers.
His clarification also covered individuals receiving payments for overseas tutoring and small software assignments, extending the reassurance beyond personal spending.
Deputy governor Rohit Jain said the framework aims to simplify trade processes and give authorised dealers greater flexibility. Acknowledging confusion over reporting obligations, he said the RBI would issue FAQs to clarify the requirements.
These FAQs are expected to explain how the clarification applies across different freelance and creator business arrangements.
What Changes For SaaS Startups And Banks?
Software exporters previously used SOFTEX, while goods exports followed a separate declaration process. Other service exports did not necessarily require equivalent declarations, although obligations to realise and repatriate overseas earnings still applied.
The regulations prescribe an Export Declaration Form (EDF) for services, including software, and permit a single declaration covering a month’s service exports.
According to CA Abhinarayan Mishra, a cross-border tax and FEMA expert, the broader use of “services” expands the reporting architecture. However, established SaaS companies already have reporting systems, so their changes could largely involve forms and procedures.
Naganand Doraswamy, founder and managing partner at Ideaspring Capital, similarly expects limited changes for startups already filing SOFTEX forms.
“From a founder’s perspective, there’s not a whole lot of change… what was being filed in SOFTEX, they’ll go by and file it in EDF and the banks have to match,” Doraswamy said.
He expects some transitional disruption but said processes should become smoother once the system settles. Banks would undertake more work matching invoices with remittances.
Manav Garg, cofounder and managing partner at Together Fund, said consolidating export reporting through authorised banks could simplify compliance for software and AI startups.
Mishra also expects banks to play a larger role in reconciliation and compliance, making their implementation of the revised processes important for startups.
What Does The ₹10 Lakh Route Allow?
The ₹10 Lakh threshold applies per export bill, not to total annual export earnings. Annual earnings exceeding ₹10 Lakh would therefore not, by themselves, rule out the simplified route for eligible individual bills.
Banks may close export-monitoring entries for bills up to ₹10 Lakh based on an exporter’s declaration that payment has been realised in full or otherwise. Exporters can also submit these declarations quarterly to their authorised dealer for bulk closure of eligible entries in the export-monitoring system.
This simplifies smaller transactions but does not remove every obligation to supply information to banks or constitute a blanket FEMA exemption.
What Reconciliation Issues Could Arise?
Mishra flagged reconciliation challenges where platform charges or deductions leave service providers receiving less than they invoiced, including through platforms such as PayPal.
Similar questions arise for YouTube creators and influencers earning from overseas platforms. Larger creators may have agencies or accountants handling documentation, while smaller creators often maintain their own records.
For service providers covered by the framework, these differences make it important to reconcile invoices, platform deductions, and actual receipts.
What About The Nine-Month Deadline?
Service export proceeds generally must be realised and repatriated within nine months of the invoice date. A 12-month period applies where exports are invoiced or settled in rupees, and authorised dealers may grant extensions on satisfactory grounds.
It is pertinent to mention that nine months is not a fresh reduction introduced on October 1. The RBI restored this deadline in June after a temporary extension to 15 months. Through an amendment in September, the central bank aligned the incoming regulations with it.
Mishra said larger companies may find it easier to structure contracts around deadlines, while smaller providers could struggle with delayed or disputed payments.
A $1,000 invoice settled for $900, for example, leaves $100 requiring reconciliation. The regulations allow authorised dealers to approve reduced realisation on satisfactory grounds for bills up to ₹10 Lakh. This may be based on self-declaration.
For cases where proceeds remain unrealised beyond one year after the applicable due date or extension, further exports require full advance payment or an irrevocable letter of credit. A disputed payment therefore does not automatically trigger an export ban when nine months expire.
Why Is RBI Expanding Services Reporting?
Malhotra said the framework would improve services trade data, bringing reporting closer to merchandise trade. Customers already provide information such as purpose codes, while the revised framework seeks additional details.
Mishra said more comprehensive reporting could give policymakers a clearer picture of emerging service exports, including the creator economy, and more timely information on overseas service earnings.
The post New FEMA Rules Explained: What Freelancers, Creators, And SaaS Startups Need To Know appeared first on Inc42 Media.
