items.author: Nwafor
items.content:
By Ikechukwu Nnochiri
The Supreme Court, on June 26, delivered a landmark judgment that appears to have placed in the dock decisions of the Legal Practitioners Disciplinary Committee (LPDC) on allegations of misconduct by lawyers.
In a five-to-two decision, a seven-member panel of the court declared section 12(7) of the Legal Practitioners Act (as amended) (LPA) unconstitutional, with the result that the court will no longer hear appeals from the LPDC.
The LPDC is the statutory body that disciplines legal practitioners in Nigeria.
It hears petitions and exercises quasi-judicial powers that allow it to impose sanctions as serious as striking a lawyer’s name off the Roll or suspending a lawyer from practice for a fixed period.
The Body of Benchers appoints the members of the LPDC on the nomination of the Nigerian Bar Association (NBA), and the Attorney-General of the Federation is its statutory chairman.
Before the June 26 judgment, appeals against rulings and directives of the LPDC were lodged directly with the Supreme Court.
This time, the appellant was a Warri-based lawyer whom the NBA had brought before the LPDC for allegedly obtaining money by false pretence as the purchase price for land that did not belong to him.
At the conclusion of the hearing, the LPDC found the lawyer culpable and directed the Chief Registrar of the Supreme Court to strike his name off the Roll of Legal Practitioners.
It also ordered the disbarred lawyer to refund the sum of N1.6 million to the nominal complainant, Mr. Tosan Olukpe, through the NBA within 30 days.
The ruling led to appeal number SC/481/2018, Ben Mene-Ejegi v. NBA & LPDC, which the Supreme Court has relied upon to divest itself of jurisdiction to entertain direct appeals from the LPDC.
When the case was called up, the apex court had suo motu raised a question for the parties to address on whether an appeal lies directly from a direction of the LPDC to the Supreme Court, in view of its decision in Osuji v LPDC (2025) 17 NWLR (Pt 2014) 317.
In their separate submissions, the parties agreed that appeals against LPDC directives lie to the Supreme Court.
Specifically, the NBA relied on sections 11 and 12(7) of the LPA to contend that, following the decision in LPDC v Fawehinmi (1985) 2 NWLR (Pt 7), the amendments leading to Decree No. 21 of 1994 restored the right of direct appeal.
It argued that the apex court had, in a plethora of decided cases, consistently exercised its jurisdiction in appeals from the LPDC.
The parties further drew the court’s attention to its decision in Okike v LPDC (2005) 3-4 SC 49, which they said affirmed that section 233(1) of the 1999 Constitution did not expressly or impliedly oust its jurisdiction to hear such appeals.
In the majority judgment, however, five Justices on the panel, after dismissing the parties’ submissions, held that section 12(7) of the LPA, to the extent that it purports to confer a direct right of appeal from the LPDC to the Supreme Court, is null and void by virtue of section 1(3) of the 1999 Constitution (as amended).
Referring to section 233 of the Constitution, which confers on the Supreme Court jurisdiction to hear appeals from the Court of Appeal, the panel noted that section 240 empowers the Court of Appeal to entertain appeals from a range of courts and tribunals.
Invoking the Latin maxim expressio unius est exclusio alterius, the majority stressed that although the National Assembly may expand the appellate jurisdiction of the Court of Appeal by statute, such as the LPA, it has no corresponding power to confer additional appellate jurisdiction on the Supreme Court.
The Court held that no Act of the National Assembly can enlarge the appellate jurisdiction of the apex court beyond the limits expressly prescribed by the Constitution.
The Supreme Court held that an appeal can reach it only from the Court of Appeal.
Therefore, the lawyer’s appeal against the LPDC was dismissed by the Supreme Court for want of jurisdiction.
Meanwhile, the judgment appears to have exposed a gap that could undermine the LPDC’s decisions, particularly since aggrieved lawyers have no legally viable channel of appeal.
Already, on September 28, the Federal High Court in Abuja halted the enforcement of a ruling by the LPDC that imposed a three-year suspension on a Senior Advocate of Nigeria (SAN), Chief Joe Kyari Gadzama.
The senior lawyer was accused of poaching a colleague’s brief, which led to a complaint of professional misconduct against him.
Despite his claim of innocence, the LPDC, after considering affidavit evidence from both parties, issued a Direction on July 29 imposing sanctions on Gadzama, including a three-year ban from practising law.
Dissatisfied with the decision, Gadzama, SAN, whose initial plan was to take the matter before the Supreme Court, on August 19 relied on the decision in Ben Mene-Ejegi v. NBA & LPDC to take a novel route of approaching the high court for leave to apply for judicial review and to seek an order of certiorari quashing the sanction against him.
After securing the court’s permission, he urged it to determine whether the LPDC’s Direction is liable to judicial review and liable to be quashed by an order of certiorari in the circumstances of the case.
The Applicant based his decision to bring the case before the high court on the absence of an appellate mechanism through which he could challenge the LPDC’s Direction, the Appeal Committee of the Body of Benchers having ceased to have appellate jurisdiction and the basis for a direct appeal to the Supreme Court having been held unavailable.
Gadzama told the court that, in his bid to eliminate any iota of doubt regarding the status of appeals against the LPDC’s Direction, he had written a letter to the Body of Benchers, requesting the constitution or operationalization of its Appeal Committee to enable him to challenge his suspension.
He said that by a letter dated August 13, the legal body informed him that under the present statutory framework, there is no statutory provision establishing an Appeal Committee, saying it would be unable to set up one with appellate jurisdiction, in view of the Supreme Court decision in Ben Mene-Ejegi’s case.
He prayed for the intervention of the court, lamenting that the sanction against him would become operative and enforceable notwithstanding the absence of an effective appellate remedy.
Expectedly, both the Body of Benchers and the LPDC, listed as respondents in the matter, urged the court to dismiss Gadzama’s application, which they said constituted a gross abuse of the judicial process.
It was the respondents’ contention that the high court was bereft of the jurisdiction to exercise supervisory power over the LPDC, its proceedings or Direction.
They contended that matters bordering on professional misconduct by or against legal practitioners are not listed under section 251 of the Constitution, which governs the jurisdiction of the Federal High Court.
Insisting that the discipline of legal practitioners is not connected to the jurisdiction of the court, the respondents argued that, contrary to the depositions of the Applicant, judicial review is not the appropriate procedure to challenge the LPA on any alleged contravention of section 36(2) of the Constitution, in the light of the recent Supreme Court verdict that struck down section 12(7) of the Act.
More so, they argued that Gadzama had no reason to apply for judicial review of the proceedings of the LPDC that led to the sanction against him, since he admitted that he fully participated in the proceedings.
They further argued that an application for judicial review is only available where an administrative or quasi-judicial body exceeds its jurisdiction, breaches the rules of natural justice, or fails to follow mandatory rules.
Delivering his judgment in the matter, Justice Obiora Egwuatu found merit in Gadzama’s case and issued an order halting the enforcement of the decision of the LPDC.
Justice Egwuatu held that it would be unjust to allow the implementation of the decision of the Committee, which is not the final arbiter, in the absence of an opportunity for an appeal to a higher judicial body.
“The law has always been that where there is a right, there is a remedy. This doctrine is expressed in the Latin maxim ubi jus, ibi remedium.
“This maxim is one of the oldest principles of law and the fulcrum of justice that states that where there is a right, there is a remedy. See BabaYusuf v. Stanbic IBTC Bank Plc (2025) LPELR-80393(CA).
“The Applicant’s right of appeal cannot be expropriated from him or denied him in circumstances not created by him and which could have been avoided by the 1st and 2nd Respondents had they taken a cue from the decision of the Supreme Court in Ben Mene-Ejegi’s case, delivered on the 26th of June, 2026, before the 2nd Respondent sat and issued her direction on the 29th of July, 2026.
“Taking the Applicant’s right of appeal from him and proceeding to implement the 2nd Respondent’s direction even before the Applicant exercises his constitutional right of appeal will be akin to beating a child and asking him not to cry. That will not be justice.
“It is on the basis of the above that I find some merit in this application, ” Justice Egwuatu held.
Among others, he barred the publication of the LPDC’s Direction as a final disciplinary determination against the Applicant until such a time that he is provided an avenue to exercise his constitutional right of appeal guaranteed by the Constitution and within the time allowed for such an appeal.
As it stands, the judgments of the Supreme Court and the High Court pose a major challenge to a key disciplinary mechanism in the judiciary, raising concerns about the entrenchment of necessary safeguards for the constitutionally guaranteed rights of access to justice, fair hearing, and appeal for lawyers accused of professional misconduct.
The post Bar Misconduct: Supreme Court judgment puts LPDC in the dock appeared first on Vanguard News.

items.author: Christopher Louis
items.content:
ASUS memperkenalkan ProArt P16, ProArt P14, dan mini PC ProArt GR1X yang menggunakan platform NVIDIA RTX Spark. Ketiga perangkat tersebut ditujukan untuk kreator, pengembang AI, hingga pengguna yang ingin menjalankan berbagai model kecerdasan buatan secara lokal tanpa sepenuhnya bergantung pada layanan cloud.
RTX Spark menggabungkan GPU NVIDIA Blackwell RTX, CPU NVIDIA Grace, Tensor Cores generasi kelima dengan dukungan FP4, serta teknologi NVLink-C2C dalam satu platform. ASUS menyebut konfigurasi tersebut dapat menawarkan hingga 1 petaflop performa AI dan unified memory hingga 128GB, meski kemampuan aktual tentu bergantung pada model, konfigurasi, serta jenis workload yang dijalankan.
Pendekatan local AI menjadi salah satu fokus utama perangkat ini. Dengan menjalankan model langsung di PC, pengguna dapat mengurangi ketergantungan terhadap biaya layanan cloud dan menjaga file maupun prompt tetap berada di perangkat. Namun, layanan cloud tetap memiliki keunggulan untuk model berukuran sangat besar dan kebutuhan komputasi yang sifatnya sementara atau membutuhkan kapasitas tambahan.
Baca Juga: Review ASUS ROG NUC (2025): Mini PC Gaming dengan Performa Kelas Atas
ProArt P16 dan P14 Bawa RTX Spark ke Laptop
ProArt P16 hadir dengan ketebalan 12,9 mm dan bobot 1,77 kg, sedangkan ProArt P14 memiliki ketebalan 13,9 mm dengan bobot 1,48 kg. Keduanya menggunakan layar Lumina Pro OLED dengan akurasi warna Delta E<1, tingkat kecerahan hingga 1.600 nits, refresh rate hingga 120Hz, serta lapisan anti-refleksi. P16 tersedia hingga resolusi 4K dengan NVIDIA G-SYNC, sementara P14 mencapai resolusi 3K.
Untuk mendukung penggunaan mobile, P16 membawa baterai hingga 99,9Wh dan P14 hingga 90Wh. ASUS juga membekali keduanya dengan sejumlah solusi AI lokal seperti MuseTree untuk pembuatan gambar menggunakan model FLUX dan Wan, serta StoryCube untuk pengelolaan aset. ASUS turut mengintegrasikan Hermes dari Nous Research dan ComfyUI untuk workflow AI berbasis agen.
ProArt GR1X Hadir sebagai Mini PC AI Lokal
Selain ASUS ProArt P16 atau ProArt P14, ASUS menghadirkan ProArt GR1X dalam format mini PC berukuran 150 x 150 x 51 mm. Perangkat ini dirancang untuk kebutuhan AI yang berjalan terus-menerus, termasuk model serving, generative AI, dan otomatisasi workflow. Sistem pendinginnya menggunakan konfigurasi dual-fan.
GR1X juga menawarkan dua slot M.2, koneksi 10GbE, Wi-Fi 7, Bluetooth 5.4, serta dukungan hingga empat monitor 4K. Untuk perangkat RTX Spark versi ProArt P14 dan P16, pre-order di Kanada dimulai 7 Oktober 2026 dengan pengiriman diperkirakan mulai 16 Oktober. P14 tersedia dalam konfigurasi 24GB dan 128GB, sementara P16 hadir dengan pilihan 32GB dan 128GB. Varian 48GB P14 dan 64GB P16 akan menyusul kemudian tahun ini.

items.author: Nwafor
items.content:
By Musa Ubandawaki, Sokoto
The Sokoto State Pilgrims Welfare Agency, PWA, has called for the decentralisation of passport offices from Abuja and Lagos to states across the country, saying the current arrangement is creating administrative bottlenecks in the processing of travel documents for intending pilgrims ahead of the 2027 Hajj.
Chairman of the agency, Alhaji Aliyu Musa, made the call in an interview in Sokoto, identifying passport processing as one of the major logistical challenges confronting Pilgrims Welfare Agencies during Hajj preparations.
Musa said restricting passport services largely to Abuja and Lagos had placed pressure on state pilgrims’ welfare agencies, particularly those coordinating large numbers of intending pilgrims within tight timelines for documentation and visa processing.
According to him, decentralising passport services to the states would reduce delays, ease pressure on pilgrims and enable welfare agencies to complete documentation more efficiently before the commencement of the annual pilgrimage.
“The centralisation of passport offices in Abuja and Lagos is creating administrative bottlenecks for Pilgrims Welfare Agencies across the states.
“There is an urgent need to decentralise passport services so that intending pilgrims can obtain and process their travel documents closer to their places of residence,” he said.
The PWA chairman stressed that Hajj preparations operated within strict timelines, making timely access to passports and other travel documents critical to the success of the exercise.
He noted that requiring intending pilgrims and state agencies to depend on only two major centres for passport-related services could result in unnecessary movement, additional expenses, congestion and delays, particularly during peak periods of Hajj preparations.
Musa therefore appealed to the Federal Government and relevant authorities responsible for passport administration to consider establishing functional passport offices in all states or strengthening existing state-level facilities.
He said such decentralisation would benefit intending pilgrims and strengthen coordination between state Pilgrims Welfare Agencies and federal authorities responsible for documentation and visa processing.
PWA clarifies 2027 registration
Meanwhile, Musa clarified that the Sokoto State PWA had not commenced fresh registration for the 2027 Hajj following the allocation of additional slots to the state by the National Hajj Commission of Nigeria, NAHCON.
He explained that the additional slots were specifically allocated to intending pilgrims who had already paid their Hajj fares but could not be registered because the state’s initial quota had been exhausted.
“The additional allocation is not for new applicants. It is meant for intending pilgrims who had already paid but could not secure seats because the available slots were limited at the time of registration,” Musa said.
He urged members of the public to disregard rumours and unverified reports that the agency had commenced another round of registration.
Musa advised intending pilgrims to rely exclusively on official information from the Sokoto PWA and NAHCON.
He also commended the support of Sokoto State Governor, Ahmed Aliyu, for the annual Hajj operation, saying the governor had continued to provide backing to facilitate the welfare and smooth coordination of pilgrims from the state.
Musa assured intending pilgrims that the agency would continue to pursue a transparent and orderly Hajj process while working with NAHCON and other relevant authorities to address administrative challenges and ensure that pilgrims were adequately prepared for the 2027 pilgrimage.

items.author: Nwafor
items.content:
By Musa Ubandawaki, Sokoto
The European Union, EU, has urged the Sokoto State House of Assembly to strengthen its oversight of public spending, improve legislative capacity and ensure that approved budgets translate into measurable improvements in the lives of citizens, particularly vulnerable groups.
The call was made during a policy dialogue involving the EU, development partners and lawmakers on budget implementation, legislative effectiveness, social protection and institutional accountability.
The EU, through its representatives, stressed that effective legislative oversight was essential to ensuring that public funds were released and utilised for the purposes for which they were appropriated.
Head of UNICEF Field Office in Sokoto, Michael Juma, said continuous capacity development was necessary for the Assembly to effectively discharge its constitutional responsibilities.
Juma said lawmakers needed stronger expertise in legislation, policy formulation, budget scrutiny, standard operating procedures and monitoring of government programmes to ensure that public spending achieved the desired results.
He also commended the Assembly for embracing programme-based budgeting, describing it as a system capable of linking government expenditure to specific targets, expected results and measurable development outcomes.
Juma urged lawmakers to pay particular attention to the timely release and effective utilisation of funds allocated to social programmes, warning that delays could undermine interventions targeted at children, women, persons with disabilities and other vulnerable groups.
He also commended the state for allocating more than 16 per cent of its budget to education and other social sectors, stressing that sustained investment in human development remained important to addressing poverty and vulnerability.
EU seeks stronger social protection
EU Programme Manager for Social Protection in Nigeria, Chioma Osuji, acknowledged the Sokoto State Government’s commitment to social protection, particularly the establishment of a dedicated committee in the Assembly and the inclusion of social protection in the state budget.
Osuji said institutionalising social protection through legislative and budgetary processes would provide a stronger foundation for sustainable interventions.
She urged the state to strengthen its Social Registry to ensure that assistance reached the poorest and most vulnerable residents.
She added that the EU was supporting Sokoto in areas including health, education and durable solutions, expressing confidence that the state would gradually assume greater ownership of the programmes.
Assembly seeks support for Tsangaya reform, digitalisation
Responding, the Majority Leader of the Assembly and Chairman of the House Committee on Social Protection, Hon. Muhammad Bello Idris, said the legislature valued its partnership with the EU, UNICEF and other development partners.
Idris said lawmakers had benefited from several capacity-building initiatives supported by the development partners.
He disclosed that the Assembly was considering the integration of English Language and Mathematics into the Almajiri and Tsangaya education system, describing the proposal as timely for equipping children with basic literacy and numeracy skills.
He said budgetary provision had already been made for the initiative, adding that the Assembly would examine the proposal to ensure the necessary appropriation and legislative backing for its implementation.
The Majority Leader also appealed to the EU and other development partners to support the Assembly’s transition from largely manual parliamentary operations to a fully digital legislative system.
According to him, digitalisation would improve efficiency, transparency, documentation and access to legislative records.
Representing the Speaker, Rt. Hon. Tukur Bala Bodinga, the Deputy Speaker, Hon. Kabiru Ibrahim Kware, assured the EU and other partners that the Assembly would continue to strengthen its constitutional oversight role.
Kware said the legislature would also collaborate with development partners on initiatives aimed at improving democratic governance, accountability and service delivery.
The Clerk of the House, Almustapha Sidi Attahiru, similarly called for additional support to strengthen the capacity of lawmakers and legislative staff in social protection, legislative research, policy development and parliamentary administration.
The EU delegation reaffirmed its readiness to deepen collaboration with the Assembly in budget oversight, digitalisation, social protection and institutional development.

items.title: FPIs sell Rs 21,745 crore in second half of Sep, in oil & gas, auto & financials
items.summary: Mumbai: Foreign portfolio investors (FPIs) stepped up selling in Indian equities in the second half of September, with financial, oil & gas, auto, telecom and metal stocks bearing the brunt of the outflows. FPIs sold ₹21,745 crore during September 16-30, after selling ₹14,116 crore in the first half of the month.Financial stocks saw the highest FPI selling at around ₹6,943 crore, compared with ₹6,204 crore in the first half. Oil & gas and auto stocks followed, with selling of ₹4,469 crore and ₹3,542 crore, respectively, against ₹2,385 crore and ₹2,670 crore in the first half.134777211"The selling reflects a combination of portfolio rebalancing, profit-taking and a greater focus on valuations relative to earnings growth," said Vishad Turakhia, CEO of Equirus Securities. YouTube memperkenalkan sejumlah pendekatan baru untuk membantu brand menghubungkan aktivitas pemasaran dengan kreator hingga tahap pembelian di Indonesia. Strategi tersebut diperkenalkan dalam YouTube Festival Indonesia 2026 dan berfokus pada tiga aspek, yaitu budaya, koneksi, serta perdagangan.
Berdasarkan data Kantar yang dikutip YouTube, sebanyak 95% penonton di Indonesia menyebut YouTube sebagai platform video yang paling mereka percaya, mengungguli TikTok, Facebook, dan Instagram. YouTube juga menyebut platformnya menjangkau hampir 90% populasi online Indonesia melalui berbagai perangkat, termasuk televisi.
Kepercayaan terhadap kreator kemudian menjadi bagian dari strategi komersial YouTube. Perusahaan mengklaim 90% penonton merasa YouTube membantu mereka lebih yakin ketika mengambil keputusan belanja. Dari sisi bisnis, YouTube menyebut ROI di Indonesia 1,44 kali lebih tinggi dibandingkan Paid Social dan 1,51 kali dibandingkan Linear TV. Angka tersebut merupakan klaim berdasarkan data yang disampaikan perusahaan, sehingga konteks metode pengukurannya tetap penting untuk diperhatikan.
Baca Juga: YouTube Perketat Aturan Monetisasi 2027: Syarat Jam Tayang dan Views Shorts Naik 2 Kali Lipat
Kreator Jadi Penghubung Brand dan Audiens
Salah satu fitur yang diperkenalkan adalah Shorts Series, yang memungkinkan kreator menyusun video Shorts secara berurutan seperti sebuah serial. Format ini juga ditawarkan sebagai ruang bagi brand untuk mengembangkan kampanye bersama kreator dalam bentuk cerita episodik.
Mereka juga memperluas Creator Partnerships melalui fitur Open Call. Indonesia menjadi salah satu pasar pertama yang menguji fitur tersebut, yang memungkinkan brand memberikan brief melalui YouTube Studio dan menerima ide storytelling dari kreator. Konten terpilih kemudian dapat diperluas melalui Creator Partnerships Boost dengan dukungan Google AI untuk distribusi iklan berbayar.
Pendekatan tersebut memanfaatkan karakter konten YouTube yang tidak selalu berhenti menghasilkan penayangan setelah pertama kali dipublikasikan. YouTube menyebut sekitar 40% views sebuah video justru diperoleh setelah satu bulan sejak konten tayang. Bagi brand, kondisi ini berpotensi membuat integrasi produk dengan kreator memiliki umur kampanye yang lebih panjang dibandingkan konten yang sangat bergantung pada momentum singkat.
YouTube Hubungkan Konten hingga Proses Pembelian
Di sisi commerce, YouTube memperkenalkan Commerce Media Network yang memungkinkan audiens mengakses halaman checkout marketplace setelah melihat iklan melalui perangkat seperti smartphone maupun Connected TV. Konsep ini dirancang untuk memperpendek perjalanan dari menemukan produk hingga melakukan transaksi.
YouTube juga menyebut program Shopping Affiliate telah bekerja sama dengan Shopee, Blibli, Lazada, dan Zalora di Indonesia. Lebih dari 11 juta video disebut telah memiliki tag produk dari kreator. Meski demikian, semakin dekatnya hubungan antara konten, iklan, dan transaksi juga membuat transparansi mengenai konteks promosi serta hubungan kreator dengan brand menjadi semakin penting bagi audiens.
Melalui strategi tersebut, YouTube berusaha menempatkan kreator bukan hanya sebagai sumber traffic atau awareness, tetapi sebagai bagian dari perjalanan konsumen sampai tahap pembelian. Namun, efektivitas pendekatan full-funnel tetap akan bergantung pada jenis produk, kualitas konten, audiens yang ditargetkan, serta bagaimana masing-masing brand mengukur hasil kampanyenya.

items.content:
By Alumona Ukwueze
NSUKKA — Former Minister of Power, Prof. Bart Nnaji, has called for increased funding of education at all levels, saying adequate investment in the sector is critical to building a globally competitive economy in the 21st century.
Nnaji made the call on Wednesday in Nsukka while delivering the University of Nigeria, UNN, 66th Founders’ Day Lecture, titled, “Grappling with 21st Century Development Challenges through Higher Education in Nigeria.”
He said Nigeria could not achieve sustainable economic development without substantial investment in education to strengthen institutions, promote research and drive technological innovation.
The former minister urged governments at all levels to increase funding for education and promote strategic partnerships between universities and industries.
According to him, such partnerships would strengthen collaboration between the academic and business sectors while bridging the gap between classroom knowledge and the skills required in the workplace.
“I urge government at all levels to increase investments in education because records have shown that leading nations in economy and technology invest adequately in education.
“With adequate investments in education, universities will not only produce graduates but also become centres of innovation, research and technological advancement capable of providing solutions to the country’s economic and developmental challenges,” he said.
Nnaji, who is also Chairman of Geometric Power Group, stressed the need to prioritise Science, Technology, Engineering and Mathematics, STEM, education, noting that the future of the global economy increasingly depended on technological competence, innovation and the ability to develop home-grown solutions.
He urged Nigerians to believe in themselves and have confidence in the younger generation, saying Nigerian youths possessed the talent and intellectual capacity to compete favourably with their counterparts globally if given the necessary opportunities and support.
Nnaji also stressed the importance of competence and capacity in leadership, saying those entrusted with public responsibilities must possess the knowledge, ability and character required to deliver positive results.
“Nigeria needs leaders who will think strategically, take difficult decisions and deploy available resources effectively for the benefit of the people,” he said.
He, however, said Nigeria’s development challenges could not be addressed by government alone, urging universities, industries, professional bodies and other stakeholders to collaborate in developing the human capital required for national transformation.
Nnaji commended UNN for sustaining the Founders’ Day Lecture, noting that its founder, Dr Nnamdi Azikiwe, envisioned the institution as a world-class university with global standards and a mandate to provide comprehensive education for Nigerians.
He expressed appreciation to the university for finding him worthy to deliver the 66th Founders’ Day Lecture.
The Chairman of the occasion and 13th Vice-Chancellor of UNN, Emeritus Prof. Bartholomew Okolo, said the university’s founding was anchored on a vision to establish an institution capable of attaining the highest standards of academic excellence.
Okolo said the founding fathers of the university conceived a bold vision and mission that remained relevant to Nigeria’s development aspirations.
The former vice-chancellor commended the current administration of the university, led by Prof. Simon Ortuanya, for its infrastructure transformation and efforts to improve the physical and academic environment.
In his remarks, the Vice-Chancellor of UNN, Prof. Simon Ortuanya, said the Founders’ Day Lecture was instituted to commemorate the establishment of the university and honour the vision of its founder, Dr Nnamdi Azikiwe.
Ortuanya said the annual lecture provided a platform for intellectual discourse on national and global issues, while promoting the ideals of the university’s founding fathers, encouraging scholarship and critical thinking, and reflecting on the role of the university in Nigeria’s socio-economic development.
He said the best way to honour the founding fathers was not merely to celebrate their achievements but to sustain and advance the vision upon which the university was established.
“Let us honour the founding fathers by finishing what they began,” Ortuanya said.

items.author: Nwafor
items.content:
By Obas Esiedesa, Abuja
ABUJA — The Abuja Electricity Distribution Plc, AEDC, has expanded its digital service channels with the launch of its MyPower Mobile and Web Apps to enable customers access and manage electricity services remotely.
The platforms bring key customer services into a single digital ecosystem, allowing customers to purchase electricity tokens, pay bills, report power outages and other service issues, as well as lodge and track complaints without visiting AEDC offices.
Customers can also use the platforms to monitor their energy consumption, access bills and payment receipts, manage multiple accounts and meters, and update their personal information digitally.
A statement by the company on Wednesday said the launch, which formed part of its Customer Service Week activities, was part of AEDC’s broader digital transformation programme aimed at improving customer experience.
Speaking at the launch, the Managing Director/Chief Executive Officer of AEDC, Engr. Chijioke Okwuokenye, said the initiative was designed to give customers greater control and convenience in their interactions with the company.
He said: “Our customers are at the heart of everything we do. As their needs and expectations evolve, we must evolve with them.
“The MyPower Mobile and Web Apps are significant steps in that direction, using technology to give our customers greater control over how they interact with AEDC and access the services they need.”
Okwuokenye said AEDC remained committed to improving its customer service and building an organisation that was more responsive, accessible and aligned with customers’ expectations.
The Chief Operating Officer of AEDC, Engr. Blessing Ogbe, said the digital platforms reflected the company’s commitment to continuously improving the customer journey.
“For us, this launch is another step in how we are redefining the way we serve our customers. We are building a culture where customer feedback informs how we design our processes, improve our channels and deliver our services,” she said.
Ogbe said the company would continue to listen, learn and innovate to ensure that its services kept pace with customers’ expectations.
As part of the digital rollout, AEDC also introduced a staff verification feature that enables customers to confirm the identity of company personnel before granting them access to their premises.
The company said customers who preferred mobile access could use the MyPower Mobile App, while those using computers or mobile browsers could access the Web App and enjoy similar services.

By Sola Ogundipe
Nigeria’s youth mental health crisis will come under sharp scrutiny as leading psychiatrists, public health experts and advocates press for stronger action on substance use, suicide, social isolation and the growing mental health pressures linked to social media and technology.
The 4th Vanguard Mental Health Summit on Friday October 9, at the Civic Centre, Victoria Island, in Lagos is expected to focus attention on the widening gaps in mental healthcare for young Nigerians, particularly the need for earlier intervention, accessible services and stronger support systems.
The event is themed “Advancing Youth Mental Health in Nigeria,” with “Mental Health in a Digital Age: Navigating Social Media, Technology and Wellbeing” as its sub-theme.
Lead presenter, Dr. Veronica Oluyemisi Nyamali, President of the Association of Psychiatrists in Nigeria and Chief Consultant Psychiatrist at the Federal Neuro-Psychiatric Hospital, Yaba, will speak on mental healthcare, addiction and suicide prevention.
Also speaking is Prof. Taiwo Lateef Sheikh, Professor of Psychiatry and Psychopharmacology at Ahmadu Bello University, Zaria, and former
President of the Association of Psychiatrists in Nigeria. His work includes
suicide prevention, mental health advocacy and policy.
Prof. Mashudat Bello-Mojeed, Professor of Psychiatry and Public Health and Chief Consultant Child Psychiatrist at the Federal Neuro-Psychiatric Hospital, Yaba, will address child and adolescent mental health, while Prof. Afekhide Ernest Omoti, 33rd President of the Nigerian Medical Association, will bring a broader healthcare perspective.
The addiction discussion will feature Dr. Daniel Ikpechukwu, a US-based substance abuse and behavioural health counsellor, and Dr. Ayantunde Kayode Ayankola, Senior Consultant Psychiatrist in Drug and Addiction Treatment and Rehabilitation at Neuropsychiatric Hospital, Aro.
The panel will include Dr. Tolu Ajomale, Director, Special Projects and Mental Health, Lagos State Ministry of Health; psychiatrists Dr. Olufunmilayo Akinola and Dr. Olufemi Oluwatayo; a legal practitioner, Ayo Adebusoye, Secretary-General, Nigeria Network of NGOs; and Deborah Omage, a mental health policy advocate and lived-experience leader. Ayankola will serve as lead panelist.
The discussions will examine the intersection of youth mental health with substance misuse, digital pressures, social isolation, family challenges and limited access to professional care.

items.content:
By Dickson Omobola
The Presidency, Wednesday, acknowledged that more Nigerians have been pushed into poverty under the administration of President Bola Tinubu, but said the situation is a consequence of the reforms being implemented by government.
The Presidency also faulted a report by The Economist on Nigerians’ dissatisfaction with Tinubu’s performance, describing it as watery and lacking substance.
On October 1, The Economist said President Tinubu might win the forthcoming 2027 polls despite public discontent.
The report, titled: ‘Nigerians dislike their president, but may re-elect him anyway’, identified a worsening security crisis, the biting
effects of the economic reforms and popular political challengers as factors that could work against the president’s re-election bid.
Reacting to the report on Politics Today, a Channels TV programme, Special Adviser to President Tinubu on Policy Communication, Daniel Bwala, questioned the research methodology of the report.
Bwala said: “Let me say that The Economist’s theory, as published, is watery. It doesn’t have the substance. If you want to write an opinion piece, and especially when you want to rely on data, you want to make a claim on the data, the first thing you should do is to conduct a survey. There would be some people who don’t like him (Tinubu), but there are others who like him.
“In other words, in democracy you have to allow the two voices to speak. When you make a claim that Nigerians don’t like him (Tinubu) without also saying that there are a lot of people, for example, one million families whose children have benefited from Nigerian Education Loan Fund, NELFUND, do you think they hate him? If you look at the agricultural sector in Nigeria, the kind of incentive and benefit they got, do you think they hate him? What about the incentive for the manufacturers in production?”
Asked whether more people had been thrown into poverty by the current administration, he said: “Do you know why? It is simply because we took a reform. There is no part of the world where reform comes with convenience. The population is 230 million, already at some stage of poverty. But we can’t make any progress until reform is carried out. None of the presidents that came before this president had the courage to do it because of fear.
“But the president said we can’t make any progress. So, he took that reform. Please let it be clear, even to the opposition. The reason why you have this number of poor people, and some of these doomsday analyses that people are giving, is because we undertook a reform. There is no part of the world where you start a reform like that, and there will not be discomfort. More people went down to poverty. I acknowledge it, I’m not doubting. But, there is a but to it. Since the reform started till today, we have made marked progress, which is what we have spent the last three years doing.”

He had considered running against Infantino following the resignation of Sepp Blatter in the wake of a corruption scandal in 2015.
And he tried to challenge his fellow Swiss in 2022, but failed to garner sufficient support to make it onto the ballot.
“The situation has evolved a lot since then,” Vega told AFP, adding FIFA’s member associations were “much more open to change” than when he previously sought to stand.

items.author: efosataiwo@vanguardngr.com
items.content:
Former Tottenham defender Ramon Vega has become the first person to announce he intends to run against incumbent Gianni Infantino in the FIFA presidential election next year.
The 55-year-old former Switzerland centre-back has been working in finance since he retired in 2004.
It is not the first time, though, that Vega has announced his intention to run for the top job at world football’s governing body.
He had considered running against Infantino following the resignation of Sepp Blatter in the wake of a corruption scandal in 2015.
And he tried to challenge his fellow Swiss in 2022, but failed to garner sufficient support to make it onto the ballot.
“The situation has evolved a lot since then,” Vega told AFP, adding FIFA’s member associations were “much more open to change” than when he previously sought to stand.
“I am standing because my life has prepared me to serve the game,” Vega added in an 11-page dossier announcing his candidacy.
“I believe I have a duty and a social responsibility to protect and defend football — its integrity, its people and its future.”
Pressure has been building on Infantino, who has lost the support of numerous FIFA member associations, since his aborted plan to create a commercial subsidiary to run FIFA’s biggest events, such as the World Cup and Club World Cup.
Last week, the Swiss Football Association became the latest to withdraw its support for Infantino, citing concerns over his record on transparency, accountability and institutional responsibility.
“Faith and trust across the football family have been deeply damaged,” said Vega in his dossier.
“We must rebuild both, restore FIFA’s credibility and reunite the global football family.”
It is not clear whether Vega would be able to stand.
He must first gain the backing of at least five of FIFA’s 211 member federations, but also be proposed by one of those.
And the rules stipulate a candidate must have been involved in football for two of the previous five years, and pass an eligibility review.
Potential candidates have until November 18 to meet those criteria.

items.content:
By Adeola Badru
The Oyo State Government has welcomed the release of the 20 prospective members of the National Youth Service Corps (NYSC) who were abducted while travelling to their orientation camps in Imo State, but urged the Federal Government to intensify efforts to tackle the persistent wave of kidnapping and banditry across the country.
The Commissioner for Information and Orientation, Mr. Dotun Oyelade, made the call while reacting to the release of the prospective corps members by their abductors on Wednesday, saying the development had brought relief to the state government, the affected families and the people of Oyo State.
Oyelade said, “Oyo State Government is relieved at the release of our children from the bondage of abduction once again.”
He congratulated the Imo and Oyo State Governments, as well as the Federal Government, over the release, while stressing that the development should also serve as a reminder of the need for stronger and more coordinated action against the growing insecurity in the country.
“We congratulate the Imo and Oyo State Governments and the Federal Government too,” he said.
The commissioner, however, said the Federal Government, which he described as having the greatest constitutional powers and capacity to address the security challenge, needed to do more to prevent such incidents from recurring.
According to him, “The Federal Government, which has the preponderance of power and capacity to effectively nip this embarrassing development in the bud, must be more proactive and live up to its promise to keep citizens safer across the land.”
Oyelade expressed concern that despite repeated assurances from the Presidency on efforts to improve national security, kidnapping and banditry continued to affect communities and citizens in different parts of the country.
“It is worrisome that large pockets of kidnappings and banditry still dominate the Nigerian landscape, the constant robust assurances from the Presidency notwithstanding,” he said.
He further raised concern over the number of Nigerians who, according to him, remained in captivity in forests across the country, saying the continued abduction of citizens underscored the need for more effective security measures.
“At the last count, not less than 200 Nigerians are still languishing in forests, abducted in circumstances in which government appears to have no clue,” the commissioner said.
The 20 prospective corps members were abducted while travelling to Imo State for the NYSC orientation exercise, causing anxiety among their families and loved ones and prompting efforts to secure their release.
Their release was confirmed on Wednesday by the Olubadan of Ibadanland, Oba Rashidi Ladoja, who received the information from Imo State Governor, Mr. Hope Uzodinma, during a telephone conversation at about 5pm.
The development was conveyed to the Olubadan by Governor Uzodinma personally, according to a statement by the monarch’s media aide, Adeola Oloko.
The Olubadan, who had closely monitored developments surrounding the abduction, expressed relief following confirmation that the prospective corps members had regained their freedom.

items.content:
By Gabriel Ewepu
The Federal Government, Wednesday, through the Federal Ministry of Federal Ministry of Budget and Economic Planning, said the the 32nd edition of the Nigerian Economic Summit tagged NES#32 will be used to examine what is working in the economy.
This was stated by the Minister of State for National Budget and Economic Planning, Dr. Doris Uzoka-Anite in a speech delivered at the World Press Conference on the 32nd Nigerian Economic Summit organised by the Nigerian Economic Summit Group, NESG, in Abuja, from the 26th-27th October, 2026 with theme ‘Growth that Works: Delivering Jobs, Productivity and Shared Prosperity’.
Uzoka-Anite while acknowledging the impact of the previous editions of the Summit said the recommendations by the NESG have been implemented while others are on the way.
She also urged the media to project the Summit as it has been doing in past editions, which had really informed the government, stakeholders and Nigerians.
She said the media is not just for publicity but are the arrowheads of the Summit, and added that all aspects of the Summit need to be critically reported for further actions.
She said: “The Nigerian Economic Summit provides a unique opportunity to examine what is working within our economy, identify the gaps that remain and develop practical and implementable recommendations for accelerating economic transformation.
“The summit brings together the country’s leading policymakers, business leaders, economists, academics, development partners, labor representatives, civil society organizations and other stakeholders to deliberate on the challenges confronting our economy and, more importantly, the opportunities before us.
“The ultimate objective is to move Nigeria from potential to prosperity by ensuring that economic policies and reforms translate into tangible improvements in the lives and livelihoods of Nigerians.”
Meanwhile, she said the Summit will also be organised around five key priorities: Work Nigeria – creating more and better jobs for our people; Produce Nigeria – increasing productivity, promoting industrialisation, and strengthening value addition; Invest
Nigeria – attracting investment while developing our human capital through education, healthcare, and social development; Scale Nigeria – unlocking the potential of our states and sub-national governments to drive inclusive and sustainable growth; and Secure Nigeria – strengthening national security and building the resilience needed to withstand economic and other shocks.
Earlier, the Chairman, Central Working Organizing Committee,
NES#32, Dr Aisha Umar, in a remark, said for over three decades, the Nigerian Economic Summit has brought together stakeholders under roof to confront Nigeria’s defining economic questions.
According to Umar, “NES#32 asks one profound question: how do we ensure growth translates into productive enterprises, decent jobs and rising incomes — not just stronger GDP numbers?”
However, she acknowledged that, “Nigeria’s reforms over the past three years — subsidy removal, exchange-rate unification, fiscal restructuring and bank recapitalisation — have begun to restore macroeconomic discipline, improve external buffers and revive investor confidence. These are real achievements. But stabilisation is necessary; it is not sufficient.
“The question before Nigeria has therefore shifted from restoring stability to converting it into transformation. The next phase must strengthen the transmission from reform to investment, investment to productivity, productivity to jobs, and jobs to shared prosperity. That is the growth that works.”
She also added that, “This is urgent: Nigeria still faces high production costs, infrastructure deficits, low productivity and insecurity, with over 90 per cent of employment informal. The task is not to grow faster, but to grow differently — raising productivity and creating jobs at scale.
“A fragmenting global economy brings both risk and opportunity. Nigeria’s large market, resources, youthful population and position within AfCFTA give it real advantages — but only if we can produce efficiently and attract productive capital.”
Meanwhile, according to the Chief Executive Officer, CEO, NESG, Dr Tayo Aduloju, 10 governors would participate during the Summit including local governments and the judiciary.
He also spoke on the impact of the NES on policies after 33 years of active and fruitful engagements with policy makers in both public and private sectors of the economy, which had led to reforms in the telecom industry, pensions, tax, and among others.

A post shared by Leo Messi (@leomessi)
The Al-Nassr forward wrote: “Leo, so many years defending your country and a story that will live on forever. You have all my respect for everything you’ve achieved with Argentina. A hug.”
The message highlights the respect that has developed between the two superstars despite their long-running rivalry, which defined an era of world football during their respective spells at Real Madrid and Barcelona.
Messi had announced his decision to retire from international football in late August, following Argentina’s defeat to Spain in the 2026 World Cup final.
The decision came after a physically and emotionally demanding tournament, which was also overshadowed by the illness and subsequent death of his father, Jorge Messi.
Messi leaves international football as Argentina’s record appearance holder, having made 208 appearances and scored 126 goals for the national team.
He also guided Argentina to the 2022 World Cup title and helped the country secure Copa América triumphs during his international career.
Ronaldo and Messi have continued to acknowledge each other’s achievements in recent years despite their historic rivalry.
Ronaldo also expressed his support for Messi following the death of the Argentine’s father earlier this year.
Both players are now in the later stages of their careers, with Messi continuing with Inter Miami in Major League Soccer and Ronaldo representing Saudi Pro League side Al-Nassr.

Special Adviser to President Bola Tinubu on Policy Communication, Daniel Bwala, has expressed confidence that the All Progressives Congress (APC) presidential candidate will secure a much wider margin over his opponents in the 2027 presidential election.
Bwala made the assertion while speaking on Channels Television’s Politics Today, in response to a question on what gave him confidence that Tinubu could win the 2027 election, despite arguments that the President’s 2023 victory was relatively narrow.
He said the odds had also been against Tinubu ahead of the 2023 election, arguing that developments at the time did not favour the President.
“The confidence I have is this: all of the statistics and results you read out which happened before President Bola Tinubu won the election at that time, there was nobody who did not know that the odds were not in his favour,” Bwala said.
“The governing party at that time, it was clear that they were not working for him. In the real sense of the word, there were policies that were reeled out just before the election that were quite damning to him.
“There were governors allegedly who were not excited about that because of some thinking here and there.”
According to Bwala, the odds were also against Tinubu during the presidential primary of the All Progressives Congress, APC.
“The odds were against him, even at the primary level. He could have been rigged out,” he said.
Bwala also pointed to the support Tinubu eventually secured from governors, particularly in the North-East.
“Do you know how many governors we recovered? A lot of the governors of the North-East,” he said.
He then made a categorical prediction about the margin he expects Tinubu to secure in 2027.
“Let me tell you and let me say it categorically, and I will be happy to come back, the gap that President Bola Tinubu will give each and every one of these candidates will be so much that you won’t believe it,” Bwala said.
He further cited the number of governors now supporting Tinubu, arguing that their positions give them significant influence over the political structures in their respective states.
“President Bola Tinubu has got how many governors on his side? How many governors have joined him? The governors are Chief Executive Officers of their respective states; they coordinate the structures of the state and won their election to be governors,” Bwala added.

items.content:
The Sultan of Sokoto, Alhaji Muhammad Sa’ad Abubakar III, has urged traditional institutions across the country to document their history themselves rather than allow outsiders to distort their heritage.
The Sultan made the call on Wednesday in Zaria at the presentation of a book title “Emirs of Zazzau” a Biographical study from 1800-2925, as part of activities marking the sixth anniversary of the enthronement of the Emir of Zazzau, Amb. Ahmed Nuhu Bamalli.
He commended the Emir for documenting the history of the emirate, describing the initiative as an important step towards preserving the identity and heritage of the people.
According to him, traditional institutions must take ownership of their history because they are better positioned to tell their stories accurately.
“You cannot allow someone to write your own history. You have to write your own history as it is because you know more than any other person,” he said.
The Sultan recalled that he had earlier challenged the Emir to emulate him by documenting the history of the Sokoto Caliphate, noting that he had published his own book, Sultans of Sokoto, many years ago.
He said the Zazzau history book was particularly significant because historians from the emirate’s four dynasties were involved in its production.
He also challenged other emirates across the country to undertake similar projects to ensure that their histories were properly documented for present and future generations.
“We need to know who we are, where we come from and where we are going. We should not allow social media to write whatever they want and try to change the course of history,” the Sultan said.
He warned against relying on accounts written by people unfamiliar with the history and traditions of Nigerian communities, saying such narratives could distort the past.
The Sultan also called on Nigerians to continue praying for the country’s leaders, including President Bola Ahmed Tinubu, state governors, emirs and other traditional and political leaders.
He urged citizens to support their leaders and pray for them to succeed, stressing that the success of leaders would ultimately benefit the people they govern.
In his remarks, Kaduna state Governor, Mallam Uba Sani, applauded the Emir of Zazzau for the initiative, describing the book as an important contribution to preserving the history of the Emirate.
He urged the Emir to remain patient, continue listening to the people and make use of constructive advice for the development of the emirate.
The governor also expressed appreciation to the Sultan for his continued support to Zazzau Emirate and his presence at the anniversary and book presentation.
In his speech, the Emir of Zazzau said the publication was necessary due to some historical distortions and inaccuracies regarding the history of Zazzau.
The Emir said every community that fail to document and preserve its history risk losing its identity, heritage and connection with future generations.
The event was attended by former Vice-President Namadi Sambo, government officials, traditional rulers, scholars, historians, members of the Zazzau Emirate Council, among other dignitaries.

The partner of Flight Lieutenant I.S. Bako, one of the 25 people killed in Tuesday’s Nigerian Air Force aircraft crash in Igbokoda, Ondo State, has mourned the deceased officer in an emotional social media post.
Joanna Yakubu, in a TikTok post on Tuesday, recalled her last conversation with Bako, a co-pilot aboard the ill-fated aircraft.
Yakubu said Bako had told her he was travelling to Abuja but gave no indication that he would not return.
“It actually Abuja you told me you are going to and you didn’t mention you will not come back. You left me,” she wrote.
The NAF aircraft, with registration number NAF 931, was on a routine mission from Benin to Lagos when it crashed into the swamps of Igbokoda, in Ilaje Local Government Area of Ondo State.
According to the Nigerian Air Force, 25 people were on board, comprising five crew members and 20 passengers. No survivor was found.
The Director of Public Relations and Information, NAF, Air Commodore Ehimen Ejodame, said search-and-rescue operations were immediately activated following the crash.
Ejodame said NAF 931 was conducting a routine mission from Benin to Lagos when the accident occurred, adding that rescue efforts were conducted in coordination with relevant authorities.
“No survivors have been found,” he said.
The Chief of the Air Staff, Air Marshal Sunday Kelvin Aneke, condoled with the families, colleagues and loved ones of the victims.
Aneke described the crash as “a deeply painful moment for the Nigerian Air Force and the nation” and assured the bereaved families of the full support of the Service.
Those killed
The deceased crew members were identified as Squadron Leader MI Aburime, flight captain; Squadron Leader AP Man-Ugwueje, co-pilot; Flight Lieutenant IS Bako, co-pilot; Warrant Officer Abubakar A, aircraft technician; and Corporal Uguru HC, aircraft technician.
The passengers were identified as Flight Lieutenant TL Lazarus, Flight Lieutenant M Akinloye, Flying Officer IM Adeshina, Master Warrant Officer Onwuka F, Master Warrant Officer Matini BA, Warrant Officer Nuhu FS, Flight Sergeant James RB, Flight Sergeant Mohammed AI, Sergeant Ani AE, Sergeant Izibenikien SI, Sergeant Alafuka C, Sergeant Mbadugha AN, Lance Corporal Ugwuba FC, Lance Corporal Eledan GE, Mrs Ezeh Nneka, Godstmine Tarabina, Joy Micheal, Sunday Micheal, Ukeme David and Gideon Omotola.
The NAF said Aneke had ordered a comprehensive investigation to determine the circumstances surrounding the crash.

items.content:
Canada will not allow medically assisted suicide for people whose only condition is mental illness, the justice minister said Wednesday, seeking to close debate on one of the country’s most controversial healthcare issues.
Canada legalized assisted dying for those at the end of life in 2016.
The right was extended to those suffering from serious and incurable illnesses in 2021, even if death was not “reasonably foreseeable.”
Initially, Canada was to allow assisted death regardless of condition by 2024, but that date was pushed back three years, with the government saying it wanted to make sure that the already overwhelmed mental health system was ready.
Without government action, people exclusively suffering from a mental illness would have had access to assisted suicide in March, when the exclusion was set to expire.
But Justice Minister Sean Fraser told reporters on Wednesday that Canada’s Liberal government plans to pass legislation that will prohibit assisted suicide for people whose only underlying medical condition is mental illness.
“Canada has made a decision not to move forward with the expansion (of assisted suicide),” Fraser said.
“While there is not a perfect consensus on this issue, we believe this is the correct approach.”
Fraser’s announcement follows recommendations from an advisory panel which in June urged the government not to expand assisted suicide rights.
That panel raised concern about the lack of mental health support in communities across the country, and the risk that suffering patients would choose death because they could not access care.
The committee also highlighted debate among mental health experts as to whether mental illness could ever be deemed incurable.
A majority of Canadians support the right to assisted suicide, but in recent months some medical professionals have called for a review of the policy, including how patients receive approval to end their lives.

items.content:
The United States Department of Homeland Security (DHS) has proposed a $70,000 fee for international students seeking to work in the country, in the latest move by the Trump administration to tighten rules around foreign students and immigration.
Under the proposed rule, schools would be required to pay the fee for every international student participating in the Optional Practical Training (OPT) programme, which allows eligible foreign students to work in jobs related to their fields of study while in school or after graduation.
International students are generally eligible to work for one year after completing their studies through OPT, while graduates in certain science, technology, engineering and mathematics (STEM) fields can receive an additional two years.
The proposed fee would be $70,000 for each student’s initial OPT application and $30,000 for each renewal, per report from AP News.
The policy could affect Nigerian students and other international students who rely on OPT to gain work experience in the United States after completing their studies.
American universities rely heavily on international students, including those from Nigeria and other countries, for tuition revenue.
Technology companies and other businesses also recruit international graduates for technical and specialised positions.
Fanta Aw, CEO of NAFSA, an association representing international education, said OPT allows international students to gain practical experience while helping employers fill labour shortages, particularly in STEM fields.
“Driving away the talents, perspectives, and aspirations of international students will only hurt American innovation, economic growth, workforce development, and global leadership,” Aw said in a written statement.
However, DHS said the proposed fee is intended to address what it considers fraud and abuse within the programme.
The department described OPT as a “pipeline for cheap foreign labor.”
The public will have 60 days to submit comments on the proposal before DHS can decide whether to finalise and implement the rule.
The proposal could also face legal challenges from higher education organisations and business groups, potentially delaying its implementation.
Trump administration tightens rules for international students
The proposed OPT fee is part of a broader effort by the Trump administration to tighten immigration rules and increase scrutiny of
international students in the United States.
Last year, the administration terminated the legal status of thousands of international students, with some subsequently detained or deported.
The administration also finalised a rule this summer that sought to limit international students’ stay in the US to four years unless they received approval from the federal government to remain longer.
Higher education leaders criticised the measure, arguing that it would create additional burdens for universities and noting that some degree programmes are designed to last longer than four years.
A federal court blocked the rule from taking effect in September.
Doug Rand, a former senior adviser at U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services during the Biden administration, predicted that the proposed OPT fee would face legal challenges.
He compared it with a $100,000 fee imposed on H-1B work visas, which are widely used by technology companies and universities to recruit skilled workers.
Rand argued that high fees were not the solution.
“When we educate international students at our universities, and they want to work and apply their talents here after graduating, of course we should embrace them — not use an exorbitant fee as a pretext to send them packing,” Rand said in an email.

Officers’ moments before crash

“He was the one who took everything from him. We did not know that he had collected the crown and other valuables. It was later that the police showed us everything,” he said.
The police said investigations were ongoing to arrest other members of the gang and recover the remaining stolen vehicles and alleged weapons.

items.content:
If you’ve ever lived with someone who insists the picture frame is “just a little” crooked, or that the paint colour is “almost” right but not quite, then you already know Mr. and Mrs. Thoda Sa. Brighto Paints’ newest Digital Video Commercial doesn’t invent a new kind of comedy, it borrows one straight from real Pakistani households, and that’s exactly why it works.
Titled “Mr. & Mrs. Thoda Sa,” the campaign stars Ali Safina and Hiba Bukhari as a married couple whose defining trait is a shared inability to ever be fully satisfied. It’s a small, specific, deeply relatable premise, and Brighto uses it to say something much bigger about its own brand.
Comedy Built on Character, Not Punchlines
Most advertising comedy relies on a joke, a twist, a one-liner. “Mr. & Mrs. Thoda Sa” takes a different route: it builds its humour entirely around character behaviour. Mr. Thoda Sa’s habit of finding fault with anything, a cushion that’s not straight enough, a shade that’s not quite bright enough, isn’t a joke told once. It’s a personality trait, repeated and escalated, until the audience is laughing not at a punchline but at recognition.
Ali Safina plays this perfectionism with restraint, letting small expressions and reactions do the work rather than exaggerated slapstick. Hiba Bukhari, as Mrs. Thoda Sa, matches him beat for beat, turning what could have been a one-note gag into a genuine back-and-forth dynamic between two people who’ve clearly been married a while.
This is what separates the DVC from typical celebrity-fronted advertising. The comedy isn’t performed at the audience, it’s performed as if the camera simply walked into someone’s living room.
The Paint Shop Twist
The comic tension pays off the moment the couple walks into a Brighto Paints outlet. Predictably, Mr. Thoda Sa can’t help himself, even standing in front of the Brighto shade card and paint bucket, he wonders whether something “thoda sa” better might still be out there.
It’s Mrs. Thoda Sa who shuts the search down, with the line that anchors the entire campaign: “Behtar nahi, perfect hai.” Not better. Perfect. She backs it up immediately, reminding him that Brighto is Pakistan’s first multinational paint company, sold in over 30 countries, and that her own mother has used it for the last 50 years. It’s enough. Mr. Thoda Sa, a man who has spent the entire film unable to accept anything as good enough, simply says: “Yehi chahiye.” This is what we need.
Why the Joke Lands as a Brand Message
The clever part of this creative idea is how naturally the comedy folds into product messaging. Nobody in the DVC recites specifications or lists product benefits. Instead, Brighto’s biggest credentials, its multinational status, its international footprint, its decades of consumer trust, arrive inside a punchline, delivered by a wife shutting down her husband’s endless second-guessing.
That’s a deliberate creative choice. Pakistani audiences are increasingly resistant to advertising that feels like a sales pitch dressed up as a story. “Mr. & Mrs. Thoda Sa” avoids that trap almost entirely by keeping the focus on the couple’s dynamic right up until the final seconds, at which point the brand message arrives less like an ad and more like the punchline the whole film has been building toward.
A Familiar, Exportable Kind of Humour
There’s also something notable about the choice of “thoda sa” as the comedic hook. It’s a phrase every Pakistani household uses, in one context or another, almost daily. By building an entire campaign around it, Brighto Paints has picked humour that requires no explanation and travels easily across age groups and regions, a fitting choice for a brand that itself operates across Pakistan and the UAE (Ras Al Khaimah), with distribution in more than 30 countries.
The Takeaway
“Mr. & Mrs. Thoda Sa” succeeds because it resists the urge to oversell. It lets two skilled actors, a recognisable domestic dynamic and one well-worn cultural phrase carry almost the entire weight of the brand message. By the time Mrs. Thoda Sa delivers her closing line, the audience isn’t just laughing, they’ve absorbed, almost without noticing, exactly why Brighto Paints positions itself as more than just another paint on the shelf: an international brand, trusted for 50 years, that doesn’t need to be “thoda sa” better than the competition, because, as the campaign puts it, it’s already perfect.
For a paint brand competing in a crowded, price-sensitive Pakistani market, that’s a difficult trick to pull off, and “Mr. & Mrs. Thoda Sa” makes it look effortless.

items.content:
The 20 corps members abducted on their way to the National Youths Service Corps (NYSC) orientation camp in Abia and Akwa Ibom States have regained freedom.
The victims, who were travelling from Ibadan, Oyo State, were attacked near Umunoha in Mbaitoli Local Government Area of Imo State, on October 1.
The kidnappers had initially demanded a ransom of N1 billion but later reduced their demand to N100 million.
However, on Wednesday, they were rescued from Amakohia-Ubi forest in Owerri West Local Government Area of the state.
According to security sources, their rescue followed a coordinated operation involving security agencies.
They are currently at the Department of State Services (DSS) Hospital in Owerri, where they are receiving medical attention and undergoing medical checks.
Governor Hope Uzodimma of Imo State has commended security agencies for securing the release of the 20 corps members.
In a statement he personally signed, Governor Uzodimma also expressed satisfaction with the collaborative efforts of both the Oyo and Imo State Governments towards the release of the captives.
He said that since the issue involved the security of lives, the government was cautious about releasing too much information to the public, hence the discreet manner in which it was handled.
The governor said he was particularly grateful to the security agencies for the discreet and collaborative manner in which they tackled the challenge.
