items.author: Sponsored Post
items.content:
African technologists and entrepreneurs are applying blockchain in innovative ways, creating a new financial infrastructure for the continent with wide-ranging benefits, including for the humanitarian sector.
Through its Blockchain Ventures investment programme – supported by Ethereum Foundation and GSR Foundation – UNICEF Office of Innovation provides funding and technical assistance to emerging market startups building innovative blockchain-based solutions.
The transparency and efficiency that make blockchain a powerful fintech tool also offer a solution to one of humanitarian response’s most persistent challenges, says Sandy Om’Iniabohs, Impact and Research Lead at Convexity in Nigeria: opacity, fraud and unverifiable impact.
What problem was Convexity Humanitarian Aid Transfer Solution (CHATS) originally built to solve?
The idea for CHATS came directly from our work on the ground. Our team used to conduct fraud investigations and projects for local and international NGOs, and we saw how funds were diverted when it came to distributing aid to recipients.
One example is from a programme focused on providing families living in displaced populations with access to healthcare. Before we began, we went around camps for displaced people conducting needs assessments. You’d ask community members why the camp clinic was closed, even though there was a clinic there. They would explain that a foundation, an organisation or the government had donated pharmaceutical products, but the people in charge were basically free to disburse them – and sometimes those products were just sold off for personal interest instead of being provided to the community.
We realised this was something we could help solve. CHATS is a digital cash and voucher distribution platform that makes it possible for all recipients to have a wallet account attached to an identifiable and verified individual. Beneficiaries without access to smartphones or the internet have multiple channels of claiming their aid using text short codes and QR codes, SMS vouchers, and tap-and-go cards. With CHATS and with blockchain, you can see clearly who is collecting what, where and when. It provides real oversight across the whole process.
How does CHATS help tackle aid diversion?
In plain language, diversion is stolen or misused aid. What CHATS does is make it much harder for people acting in their own self-interest to divert aid that is meant for displaced and impoverished people.
Every person has an assigned card or voucher connected to them. If someone who is supposed to receive one strip of malaria pills is suddenly collecting 10, you immediately see that something is wrong. The records are there. It raises flags and makes it far more difficult to hide what is going on.
CHATS also works for cash transfers. What advantages does it have over traditional systems?
We’ve done multiple cash transfers on CHATS. There are several advantages. CHATS is capable of coordinating the whole disbursement flow end-to-end.
In displacement settings, many people no longer have access to formal documentation like national ID cards. CHATS addresses that inside the system, so identity verification and documentation become part of the same workflow. The disbursements themselves and the monitoring are handled on CHATS too. Then you have reporting: you can do your impact reporting and have programme oversight from one place. So instead of stitching together lots of separate tools, programme stakeholders and managers can coordinate everything on a single platform.
Many humanitarian managers associate blockchain with cryptocurrencies, financial speculation and misuse. How do you explain it to them?
I like to explain blockchain as a notebook. Imagine a notebook with an infinite number of pages where everything that’s written stays there. It cannot be erased, it cannot be hidden, it cannot be changed. If I carry out a transaction, it is written there. If someone else carries out a transaction, it is written there. You can see the full history, and it is permanent.
On top of that, you can verify whatever is being conducted across the board. That verification and that transaction history save time. By saving time, they make things faster and cheaper. These are benefits we can apply directly to the problems we see in the field. By being cheaper and faster, we get to children and families more quickly while building in accountability.
Often when people hear “blockchain” they say it sounds very technical. You have to explain the benefits in non-technical terms. Don’t focus on how complicated it may be; focus on how beneficial it is to organisations and recipients. Convexity builds and maintains the technical side. For a user, they just need to know that it is fast, cheap, transparent, verifiable, and that the records cannot be changed.
CHATS has multiple access channels – quick codes, vouchers, QR codes. Why is that so important at the last mile?
Something we’ve learned is that adaptation looks very different across contexts. On the malaria programme, for example, we tried to stick to what already exists on the ground. We don’t want to introduce too much friction.
If you give people something they’re not used to, or say they have to rely on smartphones, you introduce friction and the programme can fail. So we meet recipients where they are. We make things as simple as possible and adapt the solution to their current context.
We’ve also learned it is important to configure where and how value is used. If you simply give a debit or credit card to a family and say, “You can use this in a primary healthcare centre,” there is a good chance they might use it outside that centre – go to an ATM and withdraw cash, for example. Then it’s not meeting the needs it was intended for.
With our NFC cards, if you give one to a family and it is configured for healthcare, the place they can spend it is that primary healthcare centre. So the original idea behind the aid – what it was intended for – is actually realised.
You also talk about “geofencing” aid disbursement. What does that mean in practice?
Geofencing creates a virtual boundary around a specific location, where certain things cannot occur outside that boundary. The idea came from observing a common challenge in humanitarian distribution. If the goal of a programme is to revive a region that has been affected by disaster, you often see funds being spent outside that region. The intention is to revive the local economy, but the money leaks out.
With geofencing, funds are used only within a specific location. If this room is geofenced, recipients can only use those funds within this room. It keeps money circulating inside the affected community, supports local businesses, and still meets the objectives for which the funds were provided.
UNICEF was one of your early institutional backers. Beyond funding, what difference has that made?
Beyond capital, the mentorship has been very important. We had business mentors and tech mentors who were amazing – going through our business models, how we reach out to partners and how we explain CHATS. The support and guidance we’ve had, and the relationships we’ve built with UNICEF, have really helped us grow.
Entrepreneurship can be very lonely. Founders are still figuring things out. So having access to mentors who help you build your skills, and to a community of like-minded founders, goes a long way. You also learn from others’ pain points so that when you encounter them, you have existing information on how to respond.
There is also credibility. When you go to a humanitarian agency, they often ask, “Who has used this?” Being able to say that UNICEF was an early funder of CHATS, and has been instrumental in building it, helps open conversations in a conservative sector.
Who are you looking to partner with now?
CHATS is a plug-and-play infrastructure layer, so we are looking to partner with organisations doing large volumes of disbursements, implementing large scale aid programmes.
Our current partners include Mercy Corps Ventures, Collaborative Futures and a consortium of partners, the Nigerian Red Cross, as well as private donors. We’re looking to build on these relationships as we expand.
What is the future for CHATS?
We’re expanding into other African countries – Sudan, Kenya and others – and we believe that CHATS will mean faster distributions that are more transparent and less fragmented. We are bridging the gaps that have prevented funds from reaching recipients over the last mile while making it harder for funds to be diverted.

items.title: Review Game The Blood of Dawnwalker: RPG Vampire dengan Konsep Waktu Unik
items.summary:
The Blood of Dawnwalker menjadi debut Rebel Wolves sebagai studio baru yang diisi sejumlah mantan developer CD Projekt Red, termasuk beberapa orang yang sebelumnya ikut mengembangkan The Witcher 3. Tidak heran jika game ini sejak awal membawa ekspektasi cukup tinggi, terutama karena pendekatannya juga mengandalkan cerita, pilihan pemain, serta dunia RPG yang kompleks.
Namun, Rebel Wolves tidak hanya mencoba membuat RPG open-world dengan formula yang sudah familiar. The Blood of Dawnwalker membawa satu batasan yang cukup berbeda, yaitu pemain hanya memiliki waktu 30 hari untuk menyelesaikan konflik utama sekaligus menyelamatkan keluarga Coen dari kekuasaan vampir.
Konsep tersebut memang terdengar sederhana, tetapi justru menjadi dasar dari sebagian besar pengalaman bermain. Pemain perlu menentukan prioritas, memilih karakter yang ingin dibantu, mengembangkan kemampuan Coen, dan menerima kenyataan bahwa tidak semua hal dapat diselesaikan dalam satu perjalanan.
Setelah menjelajahi Vale Sa
items.author: Christopher Louis
items.content:
The Blood of Dawnwalker menjadi debut Rebel Wolves sebagai studio baru yang diisi sejumlah mantan developer CD Projekt Red, termasuk beberapa orang yang sebelumnya ikut mengembangkan The Witcher 3. Tidak heran jika game ini sejak awal membawa ekspektasi cukup tinggi, terutama karena pendekatannya juga mengandalkan cerita, pilihan pemain, serta dunia RPG yang kompleks.
Namun, Rebel Wolves tidak hanya mencoba membuat RPG open-world dengan formula yang sudah familiar. The Blood of Dawnwalker membawa satu batasan yang cukup berbeda, yaitu pemain hanya memiliki waktu 30 hari untuk menyelesaikan konflik utama sekaligus menyelamatkan keluarga Coen dari kekuasaan vampir.
Konsep tersebut memang terdengar sederhana, tetapi justru menjadi dasar dari sebagian besar pengalaman bermain. Pemain perlu menentukan prioritas, memilih karakter yang ingin dibantu, mengembangkan kemampuan Coen, dan menerima kenyataan bahwa tidak semua hal dapat diselesaikan dalam satu perjalanan.
Setelah menjelajahi Vale Sangora sebagai Coen, berikut pengalaman dan penilaian saya terhadap The Blood of Dawnwalker.
Baca Juga: Review Days Gone Remastered: Alur Cerita Maksimal & Gameplay Agresif
Alur Cerita yang Menjadi Kekuatan Utama
Coen diceritakan sebagai penggali perak pada awal cerita (Louis/Gizmologi)
The Blood of Dawnwalker membawa pemain ke Vale Sangora pada abad ke-14. Coen, seorang pemuda asal Laslea, harus menghadapi tragedi setelah keluarganya ditawan oleh kelompok vampir yang menguasai wilayah tersebut. Dalam perjalanannya, Coen juga mengalami perubahan dan menjadi seorang Dawnwalker, makhluk yang berada di antara manusia dan vampir.
Perubahan tersebut kemudian menjadi salah satu bagian penting dari perjalanan Coen. Pada siang hari, ia masih menjalani aktivitas sebagai manusia dan menggunakan kemampuan tertentu yang berkaitan dengan witchcraft. Sementara ketika malam tiba, kekuatan vampirnya mulai muncul dan memberikan cara berbeda untuk menghadapi lingkungan maupun musuh.
Menurut saya, cerita menjadi salah satu alasan utama yang membuat The Blood of Dawnwalker menarik untuk terus dimainkan. Rebel Wolves berhasil membuat konflik antara manusia dan vampir terasa lebih kompleks daripada sekadar pertarungan dua kelompok. Pengaruh vampir juga terasa dalam kehidupan masyarakat, kepercayaan, hingga hubungan sosial penduduk Vale Sangora.
Hal tersebut semakin terlihat melalui berbagai side quest. Sejumlah misi sampingan tidak hanya berfungsi sebagai cara mendapatkan pengalaman atau equipment, tetapi juga membawa cerita dan konsekuensinya masing-masing. Bahkan, beberapa reviewer menempatkan side quest sebagai salah satu bagian yang paling menarik dari game ini.
Meski begitu, pengaruh The Witcher 3 masih cukup mudah dikenali. Mulai dari penyampaian cerita, struktur quest, hingga cara karakter dan konflik ditempatkan di dalam dunia game. Hal tersebut bukan masalah besar, tetapi membuat The Blood of Dawnwalker terkadang terasa sebagai pengembangan dari formula yang sudah ada, bukan sesuatu yang sepenuhnya baru.
Mekanisme Gameplay Tergolong Unik
Mekanisme gameplay yang terpaku dengan waktu jadi keunikan sendiri (Louis/Gizmologi)
Salah satu mekanisme paling menarik dalam The Blood of Dawnwalker adalah sistem 30 hari dan 30 malam. Waktu tidak berjalan secara real-time ketika pemain sekadar menjelajahi dunia. Sebaliknya, waktu akan berkurang ketika pemain menyelesaikan quest atau aktivitas tertentu. Artinya, eksplorasi tetap bebas dilakukan, tetapi keputusan besar akan berdampak pada sisa waktu yang tersedia.
Menurut saya, sistem ini menjadi salah satu eksperimen paling menarik yang ditawarkan game. RPG open-world biasanya memberikan waktu yang seolah tidak terbatas untuk menyelesaikan berbagai aktivitas. Di sini situasinya berbeda karena pemain memang harus menentukan apa yang lebih penting. Ketika memilih membantu satu karakter, ada kemungkinan pemain tidak sempat menyelesaikan quest karakter lainnya.
Di sisi lain, sistem tersebut juga dapat memunculkan rasa FOMO. Saya beberapa kali merasa perlu mempertimbangkan apakah sebuah aktivitas memang layak dilakukan karena waktu yang terpakai mungkin lebih berguna untuk quest lain. Mekanisme ini berhasil membuat pilihan terasa lebih berarti, tetapi sekaligus bisa mengurangi keinginan untuk menjelajah secara santai. Beberapa reviewer juga memberikan pandangan serupa mengenai sistem tersebut.
Untuk combat, Rebel Wolves menggabungkan serangan, block, parry, serta arah serangan. Ketika berubah menjadi vampir, Coen mendapatkan kemampuan tambahan seperti pergerakan supernatural, serangan menggunakan cakar, dan sejumlah kemampuan lain yang membuat pertarungan malam terasa berbeda dibandingkan siang hari.
Fondasi combat tersebut sebenarnya cukup menyenangkan, terutama ketika pemain mulai menguasai timing parry dan memanfaatkan kemampuan vampir. Sayangnya, variasi musuh belum sepenuhnya mampu mengimbangi potensi sistem tersebut. Sejumlah pertarungan bisa terasa repetitif karena pola serangan musuh relatif serupa. Boss fight biasanya menjadi pengecualian karena menawarkan tantangan serta variasi yang lebih menarik.
Grafis dan Performa Stabil
Perubahan tone yang drastis ketika siang dan malam hari
Secara visual, The Blood of Dawnwalker memiliki identitas yang cukup kuat. Vale Sangora dibangun dengan nuansa Eropa Timur yang gelap, lengkap dengan desa tua, hutan, bangunan abad pertengahan, dan atmosfer gothic yang sesuai dengan tema vampir. Menurut saya, daya tarik visual game ini lebih banyak berasal dari art direction dan atmosfer dibandingkan sekadar teknologi grafis yang digunakan.
Di PS5 standar, sejumlah pengujian menemukan frame drop yang lebih terasa dibandingkan PS5 Pro, terutama ketika pemain berada di area yang ramai. Beberapa masalah lain juga masih dapat ditemukan, seperti texture streaming, facial animation yang kurang natural, NPC yang tidak muncul dalam situasi tertentu, hingga model karakter yang mengalami glitch.
Sementara itu, kondisi di PC terlihat lebih menuntut. Pengujian teknis menunjukkan adanya camera stutter dan traversal stutter, sedangkan penggunaan GPU juga tergolong tinggi. Game memang menyediakan DLSS, FSR, dan XeSS untuk membantu performa, tetapi kebutuhan hardware yang cukup berat belum selalu terasa sebanding dengan kualitas visual yang diberikan.
Karena itu, saya melihat The Blood of Dawnwalker sebagai game yang cukup kuat dari sisi art direction, tetapi masih memiliki pekerjaan rumah pada aspek teknis. Versi PS5 tetap mampu memberikan pengalaman yang cukup nyaman, meski sejumlah bug dan masalah visual masih terasa sebagai bagian yang perlu diperbaiki Rebel Wolves.
World Building Vale Sangora yang Punya Identitas
Dunia dikemas dengan maksimal (Louis/Gizmologi)
Salah satu aspek yang paling saya sukai dari The Blood of Dawnwalker adalah bagaimana Rebel Wolves membangun Vale Sangora. Dunia ini tidak sekadar terasa seperti lokasi medieval yang kemudian diberi elemen vampir sebagai tambahan. Keberadaan vampir benar-benar memengaruhi kehidupan masyarakat di dalamnya.
Pengaruh tersebut bahkan masuk ke ranah keagamaan dan kehidupan sosial. Salah satu contoh yang menarik adalah bagaimana simbol serta praktik keagamaan dapat dimanfaatkan atau dipelintir oleh kekuasaan vampir. Hal seperti ini membuat ancaman mereka terasa lebih nyata karena pengaruhnya tidak hanya terlihat dari jumlah musuh yang harus dihadapi pemain.
World building juga diperkuat melalui karakter dan berbagai quest kecil yang ditemui sepanjang perjalanan. Bahkan aktivitas yang terlihat sederhana terkadang memiliki konteks cerita tersendiri sehingga Vale Sangora terasa lebih hidup. Menurut saya, hal ini menjadi alasan mengapa dunia The Blood of Dawnwalker tidak harus berukuran sebesar RPG open-world modern untuk tetap menarik dijelajahi.
Namun, kualitas setiap bagian dunia belum selalu konsisten. Beberapa aktivitas open-world masih menggunakan formula yang cukup familiar sehingga eksplorasi di titik tertentu dapat terasa seperti RPG pada umumnya. Rebel Wolves berhasil menciptakan dunia dengan identitas kuat, tetapi belum semua sudutnya memiliki daya tarik yang sama.
Pengalaman RPG? Tidak Sebebas itu
Pada akhirnya, berbagai mekanisme The Blood of Dawnwalker kembali pada satu pertanyaan: seberapa jauh game ini mampu menghadirkan pengalaman sebagai sebuah RPG?
Menurut saya, jawabannya cukup positif. Pemain dapat menentukan quest yang ingin dikerjakan, mengembangkan kemampuan Coen, memilih pendekatan dalam pertarungan, membangun hubungan dengan karakter tertentu, hingga mengambil keputusan yang memengaruhi perjalanan cerita. Sistem waktu juga membuat pemain memang tidak diarahkan untuk melihat seluruh konten dalam satu playthrough.
Konsep tersebut membuat replayability menjadi salah satu daya tarik. Keputusan berbeda dapat menghasilkan pengalaman yang berbeda pula. Dengan adanya beberapa kemungkinan ending, pilihan yang dibuat sepanjang permainan juga memberikan alasan untuk kembali memainkan game pada playthrough berikutnya.
Meski demikian, saya merasa fantasi menjadi vampir masih memiliki ruang untuk dikembangkan lebih jauh. Kemampuan vampir Coen memang memberikan variasi pada combat dan traversal, tetapi identitasnya sebagai makhluk di antara manusia dan vampir belum selalu terasa sedalam potensinya. Ada beberapa momen ketika saya merasa sedang memainkan action RPG biasa dengan karakter yang kebetulan memiliki kemampuan vampir.
Di sisi lain, batasan waktu justru menjadi mekanisme yang membuat pengalaman RPG-nya terasa berbeda. The Blood of Dawnwalker tidak memberikan kebebasan absolut kepada pemain. Sebaliknya, game ini meminta pemain menerima konsekuensi bahwa setiap keputusan juga berarti ada sesuatu yang mungkin harus dilewatkan.
Kesimpulan Game The Blood of Dawnwalker
The Blood of Dawnwalker bukan game yang sempurna. Combat masih dapat terasa repetitif, beberapa mekanisme belum dimanfaatkan secara maksimal, aktivitas open-world tidak selalu memberikan pengalaman yang konsisten, sementara masalah teknis menjadi salah satu kekurangan yang cukup terasa, terutama di PC.
Namun, keberanian Rebel Wolves dalam mencoba pendekatan berbeda justru menjadi salah satu daya tarik terbesar game ini. Di tengah RPG open-world yang semakin besar dan dipenuhi aktivitas, The Blood of Dawnwalker mengambil arah yang lebih terfokus. Dunia yang lebih terbatas dimanfaatkan untuk memberikan ruang lebih besar kepada cerita, karakter, serta konsekuensi dari keputusan pemain.
Sistem 30 hari menjadi contoh paling jelas dari pendekatan tersebut. Bagi sebagian pemain, batas waktu ini mungkin terasa mengganggu karena menciptakan tekanan dan FOMO. Namun bagi pemain yang menikmati RPG dengan konsekuensi pilihan, termasuk saya, mekanisme tersebut justru membuat setiap keputusan terasa lebih penting.
Pada akhirnya, The Blood of Dawnwalker terasa seperti fondasi yang menjanjikan untuk franchise baru Rebel Wolves. Game ini memang belum berhasil menyempurnakan seluruh ide yang dibawanya, tetapi berhasil menunjukkan bahwa sebuah RPG tidak harus selalu semakin besar untuk menjadi menarik.
Dengan cerita yang kuat, world building yang memiliki identitas, sistem waktu yang berani, serta pendekatan RPG yang mendorong pemain menerima konsekuensi dari pilihannya, The Blood of Dawnwalker menjadi salah satu RPG yang menarik untuk dimainkan, khususnya bagi penggemar game seperti The Witcher dan cerita bertema vampir.
Jika Rebel Wolves mampu membawa fondasi tersebut ke game berikutnya dengan combat, sistem vampir, dan performa yang lebih matang, franchise ini memiliki potensi untuk berkembang menjadi salah satu seri RPG baru yang patut diperhitungkan.

POCO F8 Pro
Rekomendasi HP pertama datang dari POCO F8 Pro menjadi pilihan menarik bagi pengguna yang mengutamakan performa. Smartphone ini dibanderol Rp8.999.000 melalui kanal resmi POCO Indonesia dan sudah menggunakan Snapdragon 8 Elite. Chipset tersebut memberikan performa kelas flagship sehingga masih memiliki headroom yang cukup besar untuk menjalankan aplikasi maupun game berat beberapa tahun ke depan.

Galaxy A57 5G menggunakan Exynos 1680, layar Super AMOLED 120Hz, baterai 5.000 mAh, serta sertifikasi IP68. Dukungan software Samsung yang panjang juga menjadi pertimbangan penting untuk penggunaan empat hingga lima tahun. Dengan begitu, A57 5G menjadi salah satu pilihan aman bagi pengguna yang tidak ingin terlalu sering mengganti smartphone.
OPPO Reno16 F 5G (Mulai dari Rp7.999.000)
OPPO Reno16 F 5G bisa menjadi rekomendasi HP bagi pengguna yang mengutamakan baterai dan penggunaan sehari-hari. Smartphone ini dibanderol mulai Rp7.999.000 untuk varian 8GB+128GB dan Rp8.699.000 untuk 8GB+256GB melalui kanal resmi OPPO Indonesia.
Reno16 F membawa layar AMOLED 120Hz serta kamera utama 50MP dengan OIS. Salah satu keunggulan terbesarnya adalah baterai 7.000 mAh yang dipadukan dengan pengisian cepat 80W. Kapasitas baterai besar dapat menjadi keuntungan untuk pemakaian jangka panjang karena pengguna tidak perlu terlalu sering mengisi daya ketika perangkat digunakan secara intensif.
Xiaomi 17T (Mulai dari Rp8.999.000)
Nah, rekomendasi HP kelima datang dari Xiaomi 17T menjadi pilihan terakhir dengan harga resmi Rp8.999.000 untuk varian 12GB+256GB. Smartphone ini menarik bagi pengguna yang mencari pengalaman mendekati flagship tanpa harus mengeluarkan dana hingga Rp10 juta.
Xiaomi 17T menawarkan layar dengan refresh rate tinggi, performa yang mumpuni, serta sistem kamera yang menjadi salah satu fokus utamanya. Dengan RAM 12GB dan penyimpanan 256GB, perangkat ini juga memiliki kapasitas yang cukup untuk penggunaan jangka panjang. Dukungan pembaruan software yang panjang turut menjadi faktor penting sehingga Xiaomi 17T masih relevan untuk digunakan beberapa tahun setelah pembelian.
Perlu diketahui bahwa harga-harga tersebut masih belum termasuk dengan potongan atau promo yang diadakan oleh beberapa marketplace resmi di Indonesia. Maka dari itu, harga masih besar kemungkinan lebih rendah dari yang direkomendasikan dalam artikel ini.

items.title: 12 African companies from AT50 take part in Egyptian Exchange event
items.summary:
Twelve companies represented in the AT50 Index (Africa Tech 50) took part in the AT50 Cairo Market Open at the Egyptian Exchange (EGX) on September 22, bringing together founders, regulators, institutional investors, banks and capital markets leaders from Egypt and across Africa.
The Cairo event marked AT50’s third major exchange engagement following its global launch at the London Stock Exchange in January 2026, and its first African exchange activation at the Johannesburg Stock Exchange in July.
The 12 AT50 companies represented in Cairo included nine Egyptian companies – MNT-Halan, Nawy, Paymob, Bosta, MaxAB, Vezeeta, MoneyFellows, Breadfast and Yodawy – alongside Chari from Morocco, and Flutterwave and Paga from Nigeria.

items.author: Tom Jackson
items.content:
Twelve companies represented in the AT50 Index (Africa Tech 50) took part in the AT50 Cairo Market Open at the Egyptian Exchange (EGX) on September 22, bringing together founders, regulators, institutional investors, banks and capital markets leaders from Egypt and across Africa.
The Cairo event marked AT50’s third major exchange engagement following its global launch at the London Stock Exchange in January 2026, and its first African exchange activation at the Johannesburg Stock Exchange in July.
The 12 AT50 companies represented in Cairo included nine Egyptian companies – MNT-Halan, Nawy, Paymob, Bosta, MaxAB, Vezeeta, MoneyFellows, Breadfast and Yodawy – alongside Chari from Morocco, and Flutterwave and Paga from Nigeria.
“Fintech stands as one of the most critical drivers poised to fundamentally reshape the capital markets landscape in the coming period. As companies scale and mature, their engagement with capital markets must not be deferred until the decision to go public is finalised; rather, this connection should be forged much earlier. Exchanges play a pivotal role in cultivating that familiarity and bridging ties between innovators, investors, and the broader financial ecosystem. Hosting the AT50 Index Market Open in Cairo presents an exceptional opportunity to deepen this vision and anchor institutional partnerships both in Egypt and across the continent,” said Omar Radwan, chairman of the Egyptian Exchange.

items.title: Honor X5d s Bawa Layar Kedua ke Smartphone Kelas Entry-Level
items.summary:
Honor tampaknya ikut mengadopsi tren layar sekunder di bagian belakang smartphone. Jika sebelumnya konsep tersebut lebih banyak digunakan pada perangkat flagship seperti Xiaomi 17 Pro dan 17 Pro Max, Honor justru membawanya ke kelas yang jauh lebih terjangkau melalui Honor X5d s.
Kehadiran layar belakang menjadi fitur paling mencolok dari perangkat ini. Layarnya berukuran 2,01 inci dengan resolusi 240 x 296 piksel dan ditempatkan di bagian belakang bodi. Honor memanfaatkannya untuk sejumlah fungsi sederhana, termasuk melihat notifikasi panggilan, mengontrol media, hingga membantu pengguna mengambil selfie menggunakan kamera utama.
Namun, spesifikasi keseluruhan Honor X5d s menunjukkan bahwa perangkat ini memang ditujukan untuk segmen entry-level. Smartphone tersebut menggunakan layar utama LCD 6,78 inci dengan resolusi 720 x 1576 piksel dan refresh rate 90Hz. Performanya ditopang Unisoc T610, RAM 4GB, penyimpanan 64GB, serta Android 16 Go Edition.

Baca Juga: Honor Siap Rilis Tiangong AXB35, Mini PC dengan NVIDIA RTX Spark dan 128GB Memory!
Honor X5d s hadirkan Layar Belakang Sebagai Fitur Utama
Penggunaan layar sekunder pada smartphone entry-level cukup menarik karena pendekatan Honor berbeda dari Xiaomi. Pada perangkat flagship Xiaomi, layar belakang menjadi salah satu fitur pembeda yang dipadukan dengan spesifikasi kelas atas. Honor justru mencoba menjadikan teknologi serupa sebagai fitur tambahan pada perangkat dengan spesifikasi yang lebih sederhana.
Fungsi utamanya juga cukup praktis. Layar 2,01 inci tersebut dapat digunakan sebagai viewfinder ketika pengguna ingin mengambil selfie menggunakan kamera utama 50MP. Selain itu, pengguna bisa melihat informasi panggilan dan mengakses kontrol pemutaran media tanpa harus membuka layar utama.
Meski demikian, ukuran dan resolusi layar belakang membuat pengguna tidak bisa mengharapkan pengalaman seperti menggunakan layar smartphone kedua secara penuh. Fitur tersebut lebih tepat dipandang sebagai shortcut tambahan dibandingkan layar sekunder dengan fungsi yang kompleks.
Spesifikasi Sederhana dengan Baterai 6.000 mAh
Honor X5d s membawa baterai 6.000 mAh, tetapi pengisian dayanya masih terbatas pada 15W. Smartphone ini juga memiliki kamera utama 50MP f/1.8 dan kamera selfie 5MP f/2.0. Pemindai sidik jari ditempatkan di tombol daya pada bagian samping.
Perangkat ini memiliki dimensi 168,3 x 78,5 x 8,72 mm dengan bobot 214 gram dan mengantongi sertifikasi IP52 untuk perlindungan terhadap debu serta percikan air. Saat ini Honor X5d s tercatat hadir di Afrika Selatan, lengkap dengan charger 15W dan casing TPU di dalam kotak.
Kehadiran layar belakang pada perangkat seperti ini menunjukkan bahwa konsep tersebut mulai dieksplorasi di luar segmen flagship. Namun, masih perlu dilihat apakah fitur tersebut benar-benar memberikan nilai tambah bagi pengguna entry-level atau sekadar menjadi gimmick yang menarik perhatian.

items.author: Tom Jackson
items.content:
Nigerian startup BlueBic has built an offline-resilient school information system (SIS) and enterprise resource planning (ERP) platform for African primary, secondary and multi-campus K-12 schools, and has grown to more than 190 partner schools without raising venture capital.
Founded in 2015 by Favourite Onwuemene, BlueBic focuses on three pain points. The first is academic assessment. BlueBic automates the calculation of cumulative first, second and third-term promotional grades in line with Nigerian Educational Research and Development Council (NERDC) and WAEC standards.
The company says work that traditionally took teachers two weeks, particularly in large schools with many class arms, can now produce Ministry-compliant broadsheets and report cards in under 10 minutes.
The second is fee management. BlueBic is integrated with Paystack and offers digital invoicing, automated payment reconciliation and instant digital receipts, which helps schools cut tuition leakage and administrative fraud. The third is connectivity. Built as a progressive web app (PWA), BlueBic lets teachers and bursars record attendance, test scores and student records offline during power cuts or network outages, and the data syncs automatically once the connection returns.
“Teachers were spending more than 50 per cent of their working hours on repetitive paper administration instead of teaching,” said Onwuemene. “Manual paper registers were lost or damaged, school proprietors suffered tuition leakage due to manipulated paper receipts, and end-of-term grading was a two-week administrative nightmare.”
Onwuemene said that when BlueBic launched, the market was split between fragile desktop software installed on single school computers and web portals that were either foreign tools unsuited to Nigerian grading rubrics or cumbersome local systems. Many of those portals also relied on scratch cards, charging parents NGN500 (US$0.4) to NGN1,500 (US$1.2) each term just to view their children’s results.
The startup, which was selected for the second cohort of Cape Town-based ed-tech incubator Injini in 2018, was built to handle large, multi-campus schools with 1,000 or more students, and it charges a transparent flat fee.
“If software requires a 50-page manual or a three-day workshop, it gets abandoned,” Onwuemene said. “We stripped away visual clutter and engineered a grade-entry interface that feels as fast and familiar as an Excel sheet.”
After graduating from Injini, where it received US$50,000 in incubation funding, BlueBic chose to stay bootstrapped and customer-funded. It now manages more than 45,000 active students and has reconciled hundreds of millions of naira in tuition fees through Paystack.
Growth has come mostly through word of mouth.
“Once a school transitions their student records, grading rubrics and fee ledgers to BlueBic, it becomes the indispensable operational OS of the institution,” said Onwuemene.
The startup makes money from a flat B2B SaaS subscription, while an enterprise tier offers dedicated infrastructure, data migration and service-level agreement (SLA) support for large networks. BlueBic says it is profitable and cash-flow positive, and currently operates across Lagos, Abuja, Delta, Edo, Ogun and Rivers states. It plans to expand into Ghana, Sierra Leone and The Gambia, which use the same WAEC continuous assessment structures.

items.author: Prasetyo Herfianto
items.content:
Masih dengan isu keterbatasan komponen seperti memori, sejumlah brand terpaksa menerapkan kenaikan harga pada produk-produk yang sedang dijual di pasaran. Salah satu yang paling terdampak tidak lain adalah smartphone, dan Samsung mulai menerapkannya di Indonesia, termasuk ke sejumlah seri yang sudah dirilis sebelumnya. Kini, harga Samsung Galaxy A57 mencapai lebih dari Rp8 juta, untuk opsi penyimpanan 128GB alias paling terjangkaunya.
Samsung sendiri pertama kali memperkenalkan Galaxy A57 5G bersamaan dengan Galaxy A37 5G, pada akhir Maret 2026 kemarin. Tidak lama kemudian, Samsung Indonesia membawa keduanya secara resmi ke pasar Tanah Air di awal April, dengan harga Samsung Galaxy A57 mulai Rp7 jutaan. Sementara harga awal generasi sebelumnya, mulai Rp6,1 jutaan.
Namun saat tim Gizmologi cek pada masa periode penjualan perdananya, harga Samsung Galaxy A57 masih bisa ditemukan lebih terjangkau di sejumlah e-commerce, dengan tambahan diskon khusus, menjadi Rp6 jutaan. Tentunya harga tersebut terasa pas, untuk sebuah smartphone kelas menengah dengan desain yang disempurnakan, setup kamera yang terbilang andal di kelasnya, ditambah dukungan pembaruan perangkat lunak jangka panjang khas smartphone Samsung.
Baca juga: Galaxy Buds On Debut di Korea, Jadi TWS Open Ear Perdana Samsung
Naik Signifikan, Harga Samsung Galaxy A57 Masih Lebih Murah di E-Commerce
Ya, per awal Oktober 2026, Samsung telah memajang harga Samsung Galaxy A57 5G signifikan lebih mahal lewat situs resminya. Untuk varian terendah dengan memori 8+128GB, kini dibanderol mulai Rp8,499 juta, alias alami kenaikan hampir Rp1,5 juta. Sementara untuk opsi 8+256GB, selisih Rp1 juta lebih mahal, alias dibanderol Rp9,499 juta.
Bagaimana dengan varian tertingginya? Harga Samsung Galaxy A57 dalam opsi 12+256GB, kini mencapai Rp10,999 juta, alias sudah mencapai lebih dari Rp10 juta. Bisa dibilang, sudah selisih tipis dengan opsi flagship terbarunya, Galaxy S26 FE yang dibanderol mulai Rp11,999 juta. Meski memang, harga tersebut merupakan opsi terendah dengan memori 8+128GB.
Namun bila Gizmo friends beruntung, sejumlah toko daring di-ecommerce masih memajang harga Samsung Galaxy A57 yang jauh lebih terjangkau dibandingkan harga baru pada situs resminya. Pada sejumlah toko, varian dengan memori 8+256GB dibanderol Rp6,5 jutaan, sudah termasuk dengan potongan tambahan dari diskon platform.
Tentu tidak menutup kemungkinan ketika stok semakin terbatas, penjual akan menaikkan harga perangkat, mendekati harga Samsung Galaxy A57 terbaru. Jadi kalau Gizmo friends memang sudah berencana untuk meminang smartphone Samsung kelas menengah satu ini, ada baiknya untuk disegerakan, sebelum harga naik di semua platform.
Keunggulan Samsung Galaxy A57 5G
Saat pertama kali diluncurkan secara resmi di Indonesia, Annisa Maulina, MX Product Marketing Senior Manager Samsung Electronics Indonesia mengatakan bila smartphone ini hadir untuk konsumen yang inginkan sebuah paket lengkap, dengan desain semakin premium dan performa chipset lebih kencang. Dengan begitu, lebih banyak fitur AI (atau yang Samsung sebut dengan “Awesome Intelligence”) bisa disematkan ke dalam perangkat, termasuk diproses secara lokal alias on-device.
Tampil lebih stylish, ketebalannya kini hanya 6,9mm, dan juga lebih ringan di 179 gram. Sisi depannya tetap didominasi layar 6,7 inci Super AMOLED+ 120Hz dengan Vision Booster. Sementara cip Exynos 1680 octa-core yang dibawanya, memberikan peningkatan performa NPU hingga 42%. Memberikan kemampuan baru seperti transkrip hasil rekaman suara secara lokal.
Kamera Galaxy A57 5G tetap diperkuat sensor utama 50MP, ultra-wide 12MP, dan makro 5MP. Namun begitu, Samsung mengklaim kualitas foto dan video lebih baik berkat ISP baru dan algoritma pemrosesan gambar yang sudah ditingkatkan. Kapasitas baterainya tetap 5000 mAh meski hadir dalam bodi lebih tipis, dan Samsung hadirkan dukungan pengisian daya cepat 45W.

items.author: Meha Agarwal
items.content:
Atta, oil, ghee, salt. These are staples that no one really considers twice before buying. Yet a growing crop of brands is asking Indian households to reconsider what they are buying, and many are going back to the roots to do that.
The pitch for these staples brands rests on familiar products made differently, such as freshly milled flour, cold-pressed oil or ghee made using traditional methods. For the buyer, the question is straightforward. Does that difference justify a higher grocery bill or is shopping in the regular aisle still the way to go?
Pretty much everything earns a place in the modern kitchen because of taste, health quotient or a trusted source. A household may experiment with one brand for a month, but making that a habit is hard. And this is particularly true for staples, because most people do not tinker with the basics and the foundation of their kitchen.
This is the biggest challenge for brands such as Anveshan, Barosi, Gramiyaa, Two Brothers India Farms, Khetika, Akshayakalpa Organic, Sid’s Farm, KisaanSay and others that are looking to change the equation.
There’s a big gap between customers trying something and sampling a new brand and becoming loyal to one brand. Bridging this gap is central to the next phase of growth.
Many of them have found buyers on quick commerce and other modern trade channels. Their bigger ambitions now depend on getting more households to keep choosing them.
The money backing those ambitions is substantial.
Funding rounds reported in 2026 across Zoff, KisaanSay, Anveshan, Anmasa, Sid’s Farm, Doodhvale Farms and Indic Wisdom together amounted to roughly ₹335 Cr in disclosed venture and debt funding, including Anmasa’s January bridge round.
Rosier Foods and Khetika also raised capital without disclosing amounts.
Much of that capital is going into manufacturing, procurement, testing and distribution. Scaling this category requires brands to build the capacity to deliver the same quality across more kitchens.
The revenue targets are getting bigger too. At its June fundraise, Anveshan claimed an annual revenue run rate of ₹280–₹300 Cr and aimed to cross ₹1,000 Cr over the following 24–30 months.
Khetika, which reported ₹247 Cr in FY25 revenue, outlined a ₹2,000 Cr ambition over the next two to three years in March. Those targets suggest confidence that sourcing and quality can support much larger businesses.
Established players and legacy giants are expanding their presence too. Tata Sampann crossed ₹1,500 Cr in FY26 revenue, growing 46% across its portfolio, while LT Foods’ Daawat launched an organic rice range in January. Brands are also finding ways to fit more naturally into household shopping. Organic Tattva introduced larger packs in July, including three-litre cooking oils and one-litre A2 cow ghee, positioned around convenience and better value.
Those ambitions raise a harder question. How many households can afford the premium every month?
Nikhil Sethi, partner and head of consumer goods at KPMG in India, cautioned, “Premiumisation is working, but the opportunity is often overstated. The number of households that can consistently spend meaningfully more on groceries remains relatively small, although this segment is growing quickly and has significant spending power.”
The growth test, then, is not simply whether brands can win more buyers. It is whether those buyers reorder at a price that works for both the household and the business. That requires a clear reason to pay more, consistent quality as volumes rise, and enough margin after acquiring and serving each customer.
Making The Premium Worth Repeating
Pranav Pai, founding partner and chief investment officer, 3one4 Capital, argues that a brand earns the right to charge more when the buyer can verify its promise in everyday use.
“Provenance, a known and traceable source. Freshness, a real cold chain and shorter time to plate. Processing integrity, cold-pressing, clean labels, no adulteration. And functionality, an outcome the household can feel,” he added.
These attributes are shaping different propositions within the same kitchen basket. Anmasa, for instance, offers made-to-order flour from more than 30 grains, allowing customers to customise blends. Its pitch starts with something households already buy, then gives them more control over what goes into it.
In July, after its fundraise, the company claimed a roughly 50% repeat purchase rate within 90 days, with repeat customers contributing 70% of D2C revenue. Those are company-reported figures, but they offer a useful measure of whether customers are buying into the proposition beyond the first order.
For Gramiyaa, the proposition centres on the cooking oil itself and the evidence behind it. The brand controls sourcing and pressing, tests batches in its own laboratory and provides QR codes through which customers can access batch-specific test reports. That gives a shopper something to check alongside the promise on the bottle.
The difference matters because some qualities are easier to experience than others. But as Pai cautioned, “Organic on its own tends to stall, because the difference is invisible in use while the price gap is large.”
Satyajit Hange, cofounder, Two Brothers India Farms, sees the same shift towards benefits consumers can understand, from traditional grain varieties to clearer sourcing and processing. But interest alone is not enough. “The real test is whether the consumer comes back and makes it part of their routine,” he said. For a staple, the benefit has to matter at the next meal and the next grocery purchase.
The Cost Of Reaching More Kitchens
Delivering that benefit at scale brings a second test. Can brands keep the premium affordable without compromising the product or their margins?
Arvind Mediratta, founder and CEO, Elixiir Foods, which operates omnichannel grocery distribution chain FreshTerra, identifies the price gap and the cost of selling online as the main bottlenecks.
“Pure-play online models are often trapped because high customer acquisition costs, repetitive ad spends, and courier logistics on bulky, heavy items force them to inflate retail prices simply to break even,” he said.
In his assessment, reaching more middle- and upper-middle-class households requires a smaller mark-up, supported by opportunities to discover products in stores and fulfil orders locally.
Competition adds another pressure. KPMG’s Sethi expects established FMCG companies to bring premium attributes to more accessible price points.
“Large FMCG companies will increasingly create ‘mass-premium’ products that bring premium cues to a much larger audience, while specialist brands continue serving the top end of the market,” he said.
Challenger brands need an advantage that goes beyond a label another company can reproduce.
Pranav Pai points to direct customer relationships, trust built through repeat purchases and the physical supply chain. These can reduce dependence on paid acquisition and take time for competitors to build. “In fresh and perishable staples, sourcing, cold chain and consistent quality at scale are genuinely hard to replicate, and that difficulty is itself the moat.”
But lower-priced alternatives from larger companies can introduce more consumers to the category, which is a win for D2C brands. If a larger player launches a similar-looking product at a lower price, it can actually help expand consumer awareness of the category. But new brands still need to show why buyers should choose their version over a cheaper alternative.
The evidence behind those promises matters too. Sethi said premium buyers research, compare and evaluate claims more carefully than mainstream consumers. That scrutiny now extends to regulators.
Inc42 reported in September that at least 20 new-age food brands had received FSSAI notices since May 2026 over labelling and advertising claims. The report also described scrutiny of claims on legacy brands such as Dabur’s honey, ghee and cooking oils. These notices concern disputed claims, rather than final findings of wrongdoing, but underline the need to substantiate the language used to justify a premium.
For brands, making prices more accessible cannot come at the expense of the sourcing, testing and production that justify the premium. Distribution can put a product within reach. Consistent quality and workable margins determine whether it stays there.
Categories that offer an external push for consumers to switch are best suited as targets for new brands. FreshTerra’s Mediratta sees room in fresh protein with clearer sourcing, speciality flours and dairy staples.
But a larger premium staples market will still be built category by category. Hange cautions against putting a single percentage on how much of India’s basket will trade up. Income, geography and the product itself will shape that choice, and it cannot be forced pan-India. Brands can expect adoption to trickle down from metros, as usual.
Even without assuming every household will replace its entire grocery basket, there’s a lot of room to grow as the number of new brands highlight, plus the investor confidence remains high in this category.
SPOTLIGHT | HOW ROOTED IS SOLVING HOME GARDENING BRAMBLE
Rooted positions itself as a one-stop solution for plant needs, equipment and related services. Besides plants and planters, its portfolio includes DIY gardening kits, plant bundles, gift plants and gift cards, and pots in fibre, ceramic and jute, including self-watering ones.
Plants can be browsed by placement (low light, well lit, balcony), by buyer experience level (beginner to expert), and by features such as air-purifying or auspicious plants. The company claims to sell through its own site, quick commerce platforms and marketplaces.
It also runs a services layer on top of retail — corporate gifting, landscaping and the “Rooted Living” subscription. The company says it has begun plant decor subscriptions for homes and offices, and it pitches personalised plant hampers as a way to normalise green gifting.
THE DEEP DIVE
ECOMMERCE BUZZ
Nykaa’s Q2 Vision: The beauty ecommerce giant has projected strong business momentum in its Q2 FY27 update. It is expecting the GMV to grow in the high twenties, while net sales value (NSV) growth is expected to be in the early thirties. The company expects its consolidated net revenue to grow in the late twenties in Q2 FY27, with both its beauty and fashion businesses contributing to the growth.
SBI Bets On Swiggy: SBI Mutual Fund acquired an additional 1.18 Cr equity shares of Swiggy via an open market transaction last week. Back then, the shares were worth around ₹300 Cr. Following the purchase, its total shareholding in Swiggy rose to 14.16 Cr equity shares or around 5.1% of Swiggy’s total equity.
ITC Snaps Up Yoga Bar: FMCG major ITC completed 100% acquisition of healthy snacking brand Yoga Bar after purchasing an additional 52.5% stake for around ₹645 Cr last week. ITC bought 13,445 equity shares of the parent entity Sproutlife Foods through a secondary purchase.
Balwaan Krishi Bags ₹100 Cr: The agritech startup raised ₹100 Cr in its Series B funding round to scale manufacturing of agricultural equipment like power sprayers,rice mills, oils and more. Its products are priced between ₹10,000 and ₹1 Lakh, targeting small and marginal farmers for whom larger machinery may be too expensive or unsuitable.
THE OPERATOR QUESTION
When Should A Premium Staples Brand Add Its Next Category?
After winning buyers for ghee or oil, adding more staples can seem natural. Durlabh Rawat, Cofounder, Barosi, says broader portfolios can reach ₹1000 Cr revenue faster, but bring greater challenges. Three considerations matter:
Long-term positioning: A focused brand can build recall around one category. A broader brand can serve more of the kitchen basket. New launches should reinforce the identity the business wants to build.
Distribution opportunity: Quick commerce creates space for newer brands to establish themselves within categories. Entering now can help build a relevant position, provided availability and product performance sustain it.
Depth versus complexity: Staying focused allows more investment in science, research and product development. Expansion adds suppliers, production processes and quality checks. The supply chain must grow alongside the portfolio, while protecting the consistency customers expect.

Update | October 6, 2026, 18:15 IST
Shares of Mamaearth parent Honasa Consumer closed at ₹478.1 on the BSE, up 8.2% from the previous close of ₹441.8. It touch an intra-day high of ₹492.9 around 11:00 IST before settling at the closing price.
Its market capitalisation on the BSE stood at ₹15,587.2 Cr (about $1.6 Bn).
Original | October 6, 2026, 10:05 IST
Shares of Mamaearth parent Honasa Consumer jumped as much as 8.2% to ₹478.20 on the BSE in early trade, after the beauty and personal care (BPC) company issued a strong business update for Q2 FY27.
At 10:03 IST, the stock was trading 6.9% higher at ₹472.35. The company’s market capitalisation stood at ₹15,368 Cr (about $1.6 Bn)
In an exchange filing, Honasa said it expects net sales value (NSV) growth in the low thirties on a YoY basis for the quarter ended September 2026, supported by growth across its focus categories and brands.
The company also expects a low double-digit operating margin, with strong YoY improvement, as it works towards expanding its EBITDA margin.
Its flagship brand Mamaearth is expected to register NSV growth in the high teens during the quarter, supported by higher brand penetration and offline expansion. Meanwhile, newer brands are expected to post NSV growth in the mid-forties.
This younger brand portfolio comprises The Derma Co, Aqualogica, BBlunt, Dr Sheth’s, Staze, Lumineve, and Reginald Men.
Offline channels continued to lead Honasa’s growth, with both general trade and modern trade expected to post strong growth. The company attributed this to deeper direct distribution in general trade and better execution at retail outlets. Online channels are also expected to sustain their growth momentum.
The growth estimates are on a like-for-like basis, with the Q2 FY26 base adjusted for a change in the Flipkart group’s settlement mechanism that affects revenue recognition for marketplace sellers.
In the preceding quarter, Honasa’s consolidated net profit more than doubled to ₹90.5 Cr from ₹41.3 Cr in the year-ago period. Operating revenue rose 27% YoY to ₹755.9 Cr, while EBITDA more than doubled to ₹110 Cr from ₹46 Cr.
In Q1 FY27, Honasa’s focus categories grew more than 35% YoY, while its younger brands grew over 40%. Both general trade and modern trade grew more than 40%, and its distribution network crossed 3 Lakh FMCG retail outlets.
The latest update follows Honasa’s overhaul of its offline distribution under Project Neev, which began in late 2024 and stabilised during 2025. The exercise removed the super-stockist layer and strengthened direct servicing of retailers through distributors.
Alongside the distribution reset, Honasa narrowed Mamaearth’s focus to five core categories — face wash, shampoo, sunscreen, moisturiser, and baby care — after its expansion into too many categories diluted focus and execution.
The company has been pursuing diversification through younger brands, spanning skincare, haircare, colour cosmetics, and men’s grooming.
Honasa also proposed acquiring a 58% stake in nutraceuticals startup Fluence Pharma for ₹135 Cr, but called off the transaction in August after certain closing conditions were not fulfilled. Despite this, it said it remained committed to entering nutraceuticals through organic and inorganic opportunities.

items.content:
Government of India (GoI) has announced the sale (re-issue) of two dated securities for a notified amount of ₹36,000 crore as per the following details:
Sr No Security Date of Repayment Notified Amount
(₹ Crore) GoI specific Notification Auction Date Settlement Date
1 7.06% GS 2041 Jul 27, 2041 23,000 F.No.4(1)-B(W&M)/2026 dated October 05, 2026 October 09, 2026
(Friday) October 12, 2026
(Monday)
2 7.43% GS 2076 Jan 19, 2076 13,000
  Total   36,000      
2. GoI will have the option to retain additional subscription up to ₹2,000 crore against each security mentioned above.
3. The securities will be sold through Reserve Bank of India Mumbai Office, Fort, Mumbai – 400001. The sale will be subject to the terms and conditions spelt out in the ‘Specific Notification’ mentioned above and the General Notification F.No.4(2)–B(W&M)/2018, dated March 26, 2025.
4. The auction will be conducted using multiple price method. Both competitive and non-competitive bids for the auction should be submitted in electronic format on the Reserve Bank of India Core Banking Solution (e-Kuber system) on October 09, 2026 (Friday). The non-competitive bids should be submitted between 10:30 a.m. and 11:00 a.m. and the competitive bids should be submitted between 10:30 a.m. and 11:30 a.m. The result will be announced on the same day and payment by successful bidders will have to be made on October 12, 2026 (Monday).
5. Bids for underwriting of the Additional Competitive Underwriting (ACU) portion can be submitted by ‘Primary Dealers’ from 09:00 a.m. up to 09:30 a.m. on October 09, 2026 (Friday) on the Reserve Bank of India Core Banking Solution (e-Kuber system).
6. The securities will be eligible for “When Issued” trading for a period commencing from October 06, 2026 – October 09, 2026.
7. Operational guidelines for Government of India dated securities auction and other details are given in the Annex.
Ajit Prasad          
Deputy General Manager
(Communications)    
Press Release: 2026-2027/1252
ANNEX
Type of Auction
1. For multiple price-based auction, successful bids will get accepted at the respective quoted yield/price for the security. For uniform price-based auction, bids will get accepted at the cut off yield/price accepted in the auction.
2. The auction will be yield based for new security and price based for securities which are re-issued.
3. In case of a Floating Rate Bonds (FRB), the auction will be spread-based for new security and price based for securities which are reissued. At the time of placing bids for new FRB, the spread should be quoted in percentage terms.
Minimum Bid Size
4. The securities will be issued for a minimum amount of ₹10,000/- (nominal) and in multiples of ₹10,000/- thereafter.
Non-Competitive Segment
5. In all the auctions, Government security up to 5% of the notified amount for sale of individual security will be allotted to the eligible individuals and institutions under the Scheme for Non-competitive Bidding Facility in the Auctions of Government Securities. Individual investors can also place bids as per the non-competitive scheme through the Retail Direct portal (https://rbiretaildirect.org.in).
6. Each bank or Primary Dealer (PD) on the basis of firm orders received from their constituents will submit a single consolidated non-competitive bid for individual security on behalf of its constituents in electronic format on the Reserve Bank of India Core Banking Solution (e-Kuber system).
7. Allotment under the non-competitive segment will be at the weighted average rate of yield/price of the successful bids that will emerge in the auction on the basis of the competitive bidding.
Submission of Bids
8. Both competitive and non-competitive bids for the auction should be submitted in electronic format on the Reserve Bank of India Core Banking Solution (e-Kuber system).
9. Bids in physical form will not be accepted except in extraordinary circumstances.
Business Continuity Plan (BCP)-IT failure
10. Only in the event of system failure, physical bids will be accepted. Such physical bids should be submitted to the Public Debt Office, Mumbai through (email; Phone no: 022-22603456, 022-22603457, 022-22603190) in the prescribed form which can be obtained from RBI website (https://www.rbi.org.in/Scripts/BS_ViewForms.aspx) before the auction timing ends.
11. In case of technical difficulties, Core Banking Operations Team should be contacted (email; Phone no: 022-69870466, 022-69870415).
12. For other auction related difficulties, IDMD auction team can be contacted (email; Phone no: 022-22702431, 022-22705125).
Multiple Bids
13. An investor can submit more than one competitive bid in electronic format on the Reserve Bank of India Core Banking Solution (e-Kuber system).
14. The aggregate amount of bids submitted by an investor in an auction should not exceed the notified amount of auction.
Decision Making Process
15. On the basis of bids received, the Reserve Bank will determine the minimum price/maximum yield up to which tenders for purchase of Government Security will be accepted at the auctions.
16. Bids quoted at rates lower than the minimum price/higher than the maximum yield determined by the Reserve Bank of India will be rejected.
17. Reserve Bank of India will have the full discretion to accept or reject any or all bids either wholly or partially without assigning any reason.
Issue of Securities
18. Issue of securities to the successful bidders will be by credit to Subsidiary General Ledger Account (SGL) or to Constituents’ Subsidiary General Ledger Account (CSGL), maintained with Reserve Bank of India.
Periodicity of Interest Payment
19. Interest on the Government Security will generally be paid half-yearly other than in case of securities with non-standard maturities. The exact periodicity of coupon payment is invariably mentioned in the specific notification for the issue of security.
Underwriting of the Government Securities
20. The underwriting of the Government Securities under auctions by the ‘Primary Dealers’ will be as per the “Revised Scheme of Underwriting Commitment and Liquidity Support” announced by the Reserve Bank vide circular RBI/2007-08/186 dated November 14, 2007 as amended from time to time.
Eligibility for Repurchase Transactions (Repo)
21. The securities will be eligible for Repurchase Transactions (Repo) as per the conditions mentioned in Master Direction – Reserve Bank of India (Repurchase Transactions (Repo)) Directions, 2025 as amended from time to time.
Eligibility for ‘When Issued’ Trading
22. The securities will be eligible for “When Issued” trading in accordance with the guidelines on ‘When Issued transactions in Central Government Securities’ issued by the Reserve Bank of India vide circular No. RBI/2018-19/25 dated July 24, 2018 as amended from time to time.
Investment by Non-Residents
23. Investments by Non-Residents are subject to the guidelines on ‘Fully Accessible Route’ for Investment by Non-residents in Government Securities and other related guidelines as issued by the Reserve Bank from time to time.

items.title: Makkah Pact Activated: Pakistan, Turkiye to Send Forces to Saudi Arabia Amid Houthi Attacks

items.author: Business Desk
items.content:
Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye agreed on Monday to rapidly deploy military forces and capabilities inside the kingdom under their Makkah Joint Defence Agreement, Pakistan’s Foreign Office said, in response to mounting security threats from the conflict in Yemen.
The decision followed an emergency meeting in Riyadh of the Strategic Political and Defence Committee (SPDC) of the Makkah Defence Alliance, held against a backdrop of Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia.
The committee “decided to move immediately to the practical implementation of the collective defence commitments” and to ensure the “rapid deployment in the kingdom” of agreed forces and capabilities, the Foreign Office said in a statement.
The move would take place “in accordance with the approved arrangements and the national legislation of the parties,” it added, without naming any specific threat.
The three members condemned “in the strongest terms” what they called the attempted targeting of Makkah and Madina, as well as continuing attacks on Saudi cities and civilian and economic facilities, reaffirming their rejection of any attack on the kingdom’s security and territorial integrity.
Deputy Prime Minister/Foreign Minister, Senator Mohammad Ishaq Dar @MIshaqDar50 , Federal Minister for Defence, Khawaja Muhammad Asif, and the Chief of Army Staff & Chief of Defence Forces, Field Marshal Syed Asim Munir attended the Emergency Meeting of the Strategic Political… pic.twitter.com/sglpXw8dNf
— Ministry of Foreign Affairs – Pakistan (@ForeignOfficePk) October 5, 2026
Pakistan and Turkiye separately commended the “vigilance and readiness” of Saudi forces in countering the attacks, the statement said.
Pakistan’s Defence Minister Khawaja Asif, speaking to new channel after the meeting, said Saudi Arabia had made gains in Yemen and “recovered some areas” in fighting with the Houthis. He said Pakistani and Turkish forces had a “presence in theatre” but that only Saudi troops were engaged in combat, with both allies playing a “supportive role.”
Asif said the meeting formalized the alliance’s operational structure. The SPDC appointed Pakistan’s Lieutenant General (Retd) Nauman Mahmood as the alliance’s first secretary general for a three-year term, the Foreign Office said.
Pakistan’s delegation included Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar, Chief of Army Staff Field Marshal Asim Munir and Defence Minister Asif.
The Makkah defence pact, signed on Aug 7, commits its members to treat an attack on one as an attack on all. The SPDC meeting came as Yemen’s Saudi-led coalition government launched a major campaign to recapture Houthi-held territory, with both sides trading strikes over the weekend, including a Houthi attack on an Aramco facility south of Riyadh.

items.author: Christopher Louis
items.content:
Xiaomi 18 Ultra dikabarkan tidak akan melanjutkan debutnya setelah Xiaomi mengumumkan Xiaomi 18 Pro dan Xiaomi 18 Pro Max untuk pasar global. Kabar tersebut kembali muncul dari leaker Digital Chat Station, yang sebelumnya juga mengungkap sejumlah informasi mengenai perangkat flagship Xiaomi. Namun, informasi ini masih perlu disikapi dengan hati-hati karena unggahan asli yang menjadi sumber kabar tersebut kini sudah tidak dapat diakses.
Salah satu alasan yang disebut menjadi pertimbangan Xiaomi adalah harga. Xiaomi 18 Ultra disebut-sebut akan dibanderol sekitar CNY 10.000 untuk konfigurasi 12GB RAM dan 256GB penyimpanan. Angka tersebut setara sekitar US$1.500 atau Rp23 jutaan jika dikonversi secara kasar, sekaligus menjadi kenaikan cukup besar dibandingkan Xiaomi 17 Ultra.
Xiaomi 18 Ultra has been cancelled, and its specs just leaked
As per Digital Chat Station, Xiaomi planned a crazy camera phone but killed it because the price would have been too high.
– Three 200MP cameras
– 1/1.12 inch LOFIC main camera, a new sensor tech that keeps bright… pic.twitter.com/bbXoWKZu2E— Abhishek Yadav (@yabhishekhd) October 5, 2026
Jika benar dibatalkan, keputusan tersebut cukup menarik karena Xiaomi 18 Ultra justru disebut membawa spesifikasi kamera yang sangat agresif. Perangkat ini dikabarkan dipersiapkan dengan tiga kamera 200MP, termasuk sensor utama berukuran besar dan kamera periskop dengan kemampuan continuous zoom. Namun, semakin tinggi spesifikasi kamera, semakin besar pula kemungkinan biaya produksi dan harga jual ikut meningkat.
Baca Juga: POCO F9 Pro dan F9 Ultra Resmi di Indonesia, Harga Mulai Rp 12,5 Juta
Xiaomi 18 Ultra Diklaim Punya Kamera Kelas Atas
Menurut informasi yang beredar, Xiaomi 18 Ultra dirancang dengan kamera utama 200MP berukuran 1/1,12 inci menggunakan teknologi LOFIC. Kamera periskopnya juga disebut menggunakan sensor 200MP 1/1,28 inci dengan lensa continuous zoom, sementara kamera ultrawide membawa sensor 200MP berukuran 1/1,56 inci.
Selain kamera, perangkat tersebut dikabarkan akan menggunakan chipset flagship, layar datar dengan bezel sekitar 1 mm, serta speaker stereo yang ditempatkan secara simetris. Dengan konfigurasi tersebut, sebagian besar biaya perangkat kemungkinan memang akan terserap pada sistem kameranya.
Harga Tinggi Bisa Jadi Penghambat
Harga CNY 10.000 akan membuat Xiaomi 18 Ultra berada jauh di atas Xiaomi 17 Ultra. Sebagai perbandingan, Xiaomi 17 Ultra sebelumnya dibanderol CNY 7.000 untuk varian 12GB/512GB, sedangkan Leica Edition dengan 16GB/512GB berada di CNY 8.000.
Meski begitu, belum bisa dipastikan apakah harga tersebut benar-benar menjadi alasan pembatalan. Harga flagship kamera dari kompetitor seperti vivo X500 Ultra dan Oppo Find X10 Ultra juga belum diketahui. Jika perangkat-perangkat tersebut nantinya berada di kisaran harga serupa, CNY 10.000 mungkin saja menjadi standar baru untuk kategori Ultra yang mengutamakan kemampuan fotografi.
Untuk saat ini, kabar pembatalan Xiaomi 18 Ultra masih sebatas rumor dan belum mendapat konfirmasi resmi dari Xiaomi.

items.author: Team Inc42
items.content:
AceVector’s Dull D-Street Debut
AceVector stepped onto Dalal Street with a weak show. Shares of the Snapdeal parent listed at a discount yesterday, before slumping even lower to finally close its first trading on a sombre note. But the subdued listing did not come as a surprise.
A Rough Debut: AceVector’s shares listed at ₹28.30 on the BSE, a discount of 11.6% to its issue price of ₹32 per share. On the NSE, the stock debuted at ₹28.32, an 11.5% discount to the IPO price. The downward trend continued as the shares finally closed the day more than 18% lower than the issue price. So, what went wrong with its IPO?
The Looming Shadow: AceVector’s IPO fumbled on persistent losses, negative operating cash flows and intense competition. Brokerages had previously also flagged thin take-rates as well as high marketing and logistics costs as key risks. With a modest 4.93X subscription, 6% GMP and limited institutional interest, investors remained wary of AceVector’s path to profitability despite Unicommerce’s SaaS growth and Snapdeal’s value-commerce niche.
The Meesho Gap: Despite strong brand recall and a focus on value shoppers, Snapdeal’s scale lags far behind Meesho’s. In FY26, Meesho reported NMV of ₹41,560 Cr, about 38X compared to Snapdeal’s ₹1,093.1 Cr. The Vidit Aatrey-led startup also handled 264.29 Mn annual transacting users in FY26 compared to Snapdeal’s 12.16 Mn users. Experts had also flagged that Snapdeal’s affordability and AI niches were no longer a differentiator in a crowded market.
The Unicommerce Advantage: While Snapdeal struggled with scale, AceVector’s listed SaaS arm continues to be a key growth engine. In FY26, its revenue jumped 51.6% YoY to ₹204.3 Cr, far outpacing Snapdeal’s 17.5% growth. Analysts had seen this higher-margin business as a potential valuation anchor, although it remains too small to offset Snapdeal’s challenges.
While it would be interesting to see if the company picks up pace in its post-IPO era, here is all about AceVector’s weak listing on the D-Street…
From The Editor’s Desk
Founders Pledge Stakes
Ola Electric founder and CMD Bhavish Aggarwal has pledged a 4.32% stake in the EV maker to fund his participation in the company’s upcoming ₹1,000 Cr rights issue. The arrangement involves pledging 20 Cr shares in favour of CTL Trusteeship Ltd.
Separately, ideaForge’s promoter and CEO Ankit Mehta has pledged 2.8 Lakh shares, or 0.56% of the company’s total share capital, for “personal financial requirements.” The pledged shares were worth around ₹20 Cr.
The developments come as Ola Electric’s board recently cleared a broader ₹1,500 Cr fundraising plan. There appears no clarity on whether or how it will raise the remaining ₹500 Cr. Meanwhile, ideaForge recently raised ₹500 Cr through a QIP in July.
Leverage Edu Eyes ₹500 Cr
The study abroad platform is exploring a ₹500 Cr pre-IPO fundraise. The startup has already held talks with a couple of global PE firms and expects to close the round soon.
Leverage Edu now plans to file its DRHP by the end of next year. The edtech startup is currently out in the market to finalise investment bankers for the IPO. This comes as the company is targeting ₹600 Cr in revenue in FY27.
Inc42 had earlier reported that Leverage Edu is planning a ₹2,000 Cr to ₹3,000 Cr IPO, comprising a fresh issue of shares and an OFS. The startup is targeting a valuation of over $900 Mn for the IPO. It also turned EBITDA profitable in FY26.
Top Investors In Q3 2026
The Indian startup funding market remained selective in Q3 2026. Total funding saw a meagre uptick, VCs backed fewer startups, the pool of active investors shrank and venture debt continued to be the most prominent source of capital.
Venture debt firm Stride Ventures emerged as the most active investor in Q3 with 38 deals, followed by Alteria Capital with 31. The duo have maintained this lead throughout 2026.
Among equity investors, 3one4 Capital topped the list with 19 investments in Q3, followed by the likes of Rainmatter with 16, IvyCap Ventures with 15 and Antler with 14.
PhysicsWallah’s Lending Retreat
The listed edtech major’s subsidiary FinZ Finance has agreed to sell its ₹95.79 Cr loan portfolio to Auxilo Finserve. The deal, which is expected to result in partial closure of PW’s lending operations, will conclude in the next two months.
PhysicsWallah said the sale is part of its broader push to optimise capital allocation and focus on its core business. Lending would now be facilitated via third-party NBFCs to reduce balance sheet exposure and credit risks.
In May, PW approved a ₹120 Cr infusion into FinZ Finance. However, the decision put pressure on the company’s shares and raised concerns about its capital allocation priorities. The listed edtech then said that it would retreat from the lending space.
Marico Ups Stake In Plix
The FMCG giant has acquired an additional 24.09% stake in the plant-based nutrition brand for ₹1,012.03 Cr in an all-cash deal. With this, Marico’s total holding in the startup has now increased to 84.09%.
Marico will now acquire the remaining 14.09% stake in Plix by July 2027. The consideration for this tranche will include a base amount of up to ₹592 Cr, along with additional payments linked to milestones.
Separately, Walmart-owned Flipkart has picked up a minority stake in B2B travel tech startup TravClan for an undisclosed amount to bolster its international travel offerings, expand holiday packages and enhance on-ground support across.

Inc42 Startup Spotlight
Can Physioplus’ AI Stack Track India’s Recovery Journey?
Physiotherapy often breaks down between appointments. While patients struggle to follow exercises, therapists lack real-time visibility into progress. To solve this, Physioplus is building a digital layer that keeps assessment and recovery tracking connected beyond the clinic.
A Digital Coach: Founded in 2022, Physioplus’ AI-powered platform helps patients discover physiotherapists, book consultations, request home visits and receive support for chronic pain and post-surgery rehabilitation. The platform is designed to make access more convenient while helping clinicians understand a patient’s history before treatment begins.
The Rehabilitation Stack: For practitioners, Physioplus combines digital practice management, patient records, clinical assessments, documentation and tech-enabled monitoring. Its monitoring layer also supports home-based rehabilitation by capturing exercise adherence, pain changes and functional progress over time.
Growing Steadily: Physioplus claims to have so far onboarded over 1,000 patients. It is now focusing on scaling product development, expanding its physiotherapist network and fueling growth across India. With the homegrown digital health and rehabilitation market projected to become a $14.8 Bn opportunity by 2033, can Physioplus make physiotherapy more measurable and consistent beyond the clinic?
