Represented by the Commissioner for Youth and Sports Development, Segun Henry Omoyofunmi, the governor said the security and welfare of corps members remained priorities of his administration.
“Let me assure you that the security and welfare of corps members remain important priorities of this administration.
“The state government will continue to work closely with the NYSC and relevant security agencies to ensure that corps members serving in Ondo State enjoy a safe, peaceful and conducive environment throughout their service year,” he said.
The governor urged the corps members to take full advantage of the Skills Acquisition and Entrepreneurship Development (SAED) programme, saying the skills acquired could help them become self-reliant after their service year.
“The skills you acquire through this programme can become valuable tools for self-reliance, entrepreneurship and sustainable livelihoods beyond the service year.
“The Ondo State Government remains committed to creating an enabling environment for young people to develop their talents, establish businesses and contribute meaningfully to the economic growth of our state,” he said.
Aiyedatiwa also advised the corps members to serve with integrity and discipline while respecting the people and institutions in their host communities.
He urged them to embrace diversity, build relationships across cultural and geographical boundaries, and remain committed to national unity and peaceful coexistence.
“I therefore charge you to uphold the rules and regulations of the NYSC scheme and to conduct yourselves in a manner worthy of responsible Nigerian youths.
“Be ambassadors of unity, agents of positive change and champions of peace wherever you find yourselves,” he added.
In her address, the NYSC State Coordinator, Kuburat Omowumi Bakare, also urged the corps members to take the SAED programme seriously.
She said the initiative offered practical and entrepreneurial skills that could enhance their economic independence and contribute to job creation.
“This initiative offers you practical and entrepreneurial skills that can enhance your economic independence and contribute to job creation.
“I urge you to take full advantage of the training opportunities available and to develop competencies that will remain relevant beyond your service year,” she said.
Bakare advised the corps members to be good ambassadors of the NYSC, their families and their institutions, urging them to serve with humility, integrity and dedication.
She also appreciated Governor Aiyedatiwa for his continued support for the NYSC scheme and the welfare of corps members in the state.
The Chairman of the NYSC Governing Board, represented by the Permanent Secretary, Lanre Abiodun, urged the corps members to approach their service year with an open mind, a positive spirit and a determination to make meaningful contributions.
He also appealed for continued cooperation among government institutions, host communities, employers, traditional institutions, security agencies and other partners to enable corps members contribute effectively wherever they are deployed.

items.content:
By Joseph Erunke
Former Minister of Information and Culture, Alhaji Lai Mohammed, has urged African governments to reposition the Meetings, Incentives, Conferences and Exhibitions (MICE) industry as a major economic tool, saying the continent currently accounts for only about four per cent of a global market estimated at $1.3 trillion.
Mohammed said African countries could no longer afford to treat MICE mainly as a tourism activity, arguing that business events should be deliberately used to attract investment, expand trade, build partnerships and create jobs.
The former minister made the call while speaking as a panellist at the ninth Africa MICE Summit in Mombasa, Kenya, themed, “Building Africa’s MICE Economies.”
He said conferences and exhibitions should serve as platforms for bringing investors, buyers, policymakers, experts and businesses directly into African economies.
“ MICE should not be seen simply as people coming to Africa, staying in hotels, eating in restaurants and flying home.
“MICE is an economic instrument. It can bring investors, buyers, policymakers, experts and businesses into our economies. In other words, MICE can become Africa’s deal-making engine,” he said.
Mohammed urged African countries to develop MICE strategies around their respective economic and cultural strengths rather than competing indiscriminately for the same events.
He cited Nigeria’s entertainment industry, Kenya’s athletics and tourism sectors, South Africa’s conference industry and Rwanda’s emergence as a regional business gateway as examples of comparative advantages that could be converted into stronger MICE economies.
The former minister also advocated collective African bids for major international events, with hosting responsibilities shared among countries.
He cited the joint hosting of the 2026 FIFA World Cup by Canada, Mexico and the United States as an example of how countries could collaborate to stage major international events.
Turn events into economic ecosystems
Mohammed identified Lagos as a potential case study in transforming events into wider economic opportunities, recalling a study commissioned during his tenure as minister which indicated that about 20,000 events were held in the city every month.
He also cited the growth of “Detty December” as evidence of how major events could stimulate activity across sectors including aviation, hospitality, transportation, entertainment, media, fashion, technology and retail.
“The opportunity is to turn events into ecosystems,” he said.
However, Mohammed, who chairs the Board of Trustees and Governing Council of the Eko Tourism Foundation, said Africa’s MICE ambitions would remain constrained without significant improvements in infrastructure and ease of movement across the continent.
He listed convention centres, hotels, airports, transportation networks, digital infrastructure and reliable utilities among the facilities needed to attract major international events.
He also called for improved intra-African air connectivity, wider adoption of e-visas and visa-on-arrival arrangements where appropriate, as well as expedited visa processing for accredited conference delegates.
Beyond physical infrastructure, Mohammed said African countries must strengthen their broader investment environments, warning that political uncertainty, policy reversals, weak institutions and corruption could undermine investor confidence.
“Africa does not only have to sell its opportunities. It has to sell credibility,” he said.
Shift from delegate numbers to investment
Mohammed said African governments should also change how they measure the success of business events.
Rather than focusing mainly on delegate numbers and hotel occupancy, he urged governments to track investments attracted, business meetings held, trade generated and jobs created through MICE activities.
He further advocated the establishment of empowered National Convention Bureaux in African countries to bid for major international events, coordinate government and private-sector efforts, facilitate business visitors, generate MICE intelligence and measure the economic impact of events.
According to him, smaller African countries could also become significant MICE destinations by positioning themselves as platforms connecting businesses and markets rather than merely as destinations for consumption.
He cited Rwanda’s positioning as a regional business gateway as an example of how a smaller country could leverage strategic positioning to attract business events.
Mohammed said the ultimate test of any MICE event should go beyond attendance figures.
“Did an investment come? Did a trade relationship begin? Did a business partnership emerge? Did jobs get created?
“That is when MICE stops being merely an event, and becomes an engine of economic transformation,” he said.
Delegates from 19 countries participated in the two-day summit, which was formally opened by the County Executive Council Member for Tourism, Culture and Trade, County of Mombasa, Mohamed Osman Ali.

items.content:
US President Donald Trump has called on Congress to introduce mandatory prison sentences for people convicted of defrauding Medicare, Medicaid and Social Security, while proposing personal financial liability for state and local politicians who knowingly fail to stop fraud.
Trump made the call in a video posted on Truth Social on Saturday, saying the proposed legislation would eliminate probation as an option for people convicted of stealing from federal benefit programmes.
“Today, I’m calling on Congress to pass legislation to address fraud in Medicare, Medicaid, and Social Security programs,” Trump said.
“First, Congress must impose mandatory minimum sentences on fraudsters who steal from critical benefit programs designed to take care of the sick, feed the hungry, care for our children, and protect our senior citizens, retirees.”
He said people convicted of stealing from the programmes should face lengthy prison terms, with tougher penalties based on the amount stolen.
“Under our proposal, probation is no longer an option for the fraudsters. If you steal from the American people, you will go to prison, and for a long period of time,” he said.
“And the more you steal, the longer you’ll stay in that prison. Not only that, but if you’re a convicted fraudster who gets caught stealing from the American people a second time, your sentence will be doubled.”
Trump also proposed doubling the sentence of convicted fraudsters who are caught committing the offence for a second time.
“If you’re a convicted fraudster who gets caught stealing from the American people a second time, your sentence will be doubled,” he said.
The president further proposed making state and local politicians personally liable for losses caused by fraud if they knew about it, had the power to stop it but failed to act.
“Under our proposal, if a state or local politician knows about fraud and has the ability to stop it, but does nothing about it, they can be personally liable for the full loss of the American taxpayers’ money that they should have stopped and they should have saved,” Trump said.
Trump did not provide specific sentencing ranges or explain in the video what legal standard would determine whether an elected official knew about fraud or had the ability to prevent it.
The proposal comes amid stepped-up federal efforts by the Trump administration to combat fraud involving government benefit programmes.
“This legislative proposal will make fraudsters think long and hard before they keep stealing from the American people and will make crooked and corrupt politicians think also long and hard before they ignore fraud that they can stop and that they should stop,” Trump said.
He ended the video with a warning: “So from now on, fraudsters, we’re watching you.”

items.content:
…as FG okays quarterly policy dialogue
By Ikechukwu Nnochiri
ABUJA — Civil Society Organisations (CSOs) on Friday identified vote-buying as a major problem that the Federal Government must find ways to tackle ahead of the 2027 general elections.
In separate presentations at the 2026 National CSOs Summit held in Abuja, representatives of various organisations working to promote credible, transparent and inclusive elections in the country decried the repeated failure to prosecute individuals previously arrested for vote-buying.
They said the country’s electoral process would continue to be undermined unless stringent measures were adopted to ensure the prosecution and conviction of offenders, thereby serving as a deterrent to others.
In his remarks, the Executive Director of the Value Rebirth and Empowerment Initiative (VREI), Pastor Edewor Egedegbe, argued that a credible and peaceful election requires informed citizens.
He maintained that reports of inadequate funding for the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) “raise serious concerns about preparations for the election, which is just months away.”
He added that late funding not only disrupts the planning process but also increases the risk of avoidable failures.
Insisting that the electoral body had not done much in terms of voter enlightenment, Egedegbe said INEC must also open its books by publishing what it has received so far.
“It should start procurement of needed items and embark on the training of essential manpower.
“Democracy succeeds where citizens participate in the process without fear or intimidation,” he added.
For his part, the Executive Director of the Peering Advocacy and Advancement Center in Africa (PAACA), Chief Ezenwa Nwagwu, highlighted the importance of encouraging citizens to register and obtain the Permanent Voters Card (PVC), which he said carries more value than a bank Automated Teller Machine (ATM) card.
“This is what we should be emphasising. The cost of electricity is embedded in the PVC, so also is the cost of education and everything about life in the country.
“It is not about asking people to take money from candidates and vote their conscience. When you sell your PVC, it diminishes your citizenship.
“The fact that you think the law does not work in the country does not mean that you cannot be used as an example to show how the law works,” Nwagwu stated.
He blamed the recurring cases of vote-buying during elections on what he described as “the pauperisation of citizens.”
“Until we realise the powers we have as citizens, we will continue to shortchange ourselves.
“We should always ask ourselves this question: if votes don’t count, why then do politicians place value on your votes?
“As we move towards the 2027 general elections, we as citizens have to re-examine ourselves and take over the power of polling units from the politicians. The citizens must drive the process,” he insisted.
Meanwhile, the federal government said it had approved the establishment of a quarterly civil society policy dialogue forum to institutionalise citizens’ participation in policy formulation, implementation and evaluation.
The Secretary to the Government of the Federation, Senator George Akume, who represented President Bola Tinubu at the summit, said the forum would provide a structured platform for evidence-based advocacy and ensure that community-level concerns were reflected in government decisions.
He also pledged the FG’s commitment to expand civic space for social accountability, including greater collaboration with accredited CSOs on public finance transparency, budget tracking and monitoring of humanitarian and grassroots interventions.
“This administration firmly believes that no nation can achieve inclusive, equitable and sustainable development without a vibrant, credible and responsible civil society operating within an open and enabling civic space,” he added.
The National Convener of the CSOs Summit, Ambassador Kunle Yusuff, who is the Director-General of the Civil Society Organisations on Community Advancement and Humanitarian Empowerment Initiative (CSCHEI), said the aim was to galvanise the various organisations to brainstorm on the way forward as the nation braces for another round of elections.
Yusuff said the summit was proposing a sustainable partnership compact through which the government, civil society and the private sector could work jointly on national priorities rather than operating from positions of suspicion.
According to him, the proposed framework will provide a mechanism for monitoring government policies, budgets and electoral promises, while ensuring that information generated from communities reaches relevant authorities.

items.author: Henry Oduah
items.content:
Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu on Saturday invited to Israel as a guest of honour the Indian captain of a Tel Aviv-bound flydubai flight who offered a dramatic account of how he saved the plane after being attacked.
Netanyahu said he wanted Captain Smit Machchhar and Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi, one of Israel’s key international partners, to light a flame at a national ceremony for Israel’s Independence Day next May, saying the role was usually reserved for Israeli citizens.
“You are a true hero of the brave peoples of India and Israel and you are a hero of the entire world,” Netanyahu said in a video his office released of his telephone conversation with the hospitalised captain.
UAE investigators have said that the co-pilot planned the “terrorist act” by attacking Machchhar with an axe.
Asked how the attack unfolded, Machchhar said the co-pilot had asked to take time to pray, as devout Muslims do five times a day.
“A lot of locals, they do pray, which is not out of the ordinary. While he was praying, out of respect, I was just looking at the front and not at the back,” Machchhar said.
“Suddenly after I think I would say about four to five minutes, there was a big blow to the back of my head. My first thought was that there was catastrophic damage to the aircraft and something is not right.
“But then after that the blows kept coming one after the other. That’s when I realised that it’s not the aircraft, it’s the other guy who was in the cockpit with me.”
While saying his memory was not entirely clear due to his injury, Machchhar said he managed to pull open the cockpit door “but I think he shut it back closed.”
“I had that one last fight left in me,” Machchhar explained, saying he knew he faced certain death if not.
“That’s when I pushed against everything. I gave everything that I had and just went for the door and opened the door and thankfully people were waiting.”
AFP

It added that the DIG also reviewed the operational strategies, deployment of personnel as well as operational assets, and provided further directives to strengthen the coordinated response.
The statement further explained that the assessment was conducted alongside the Imo State Commissioner of Police, Audu Bosso; the Commissioner of Police, Federal Operations, Akpan Anifiok; the Commissioner of Police in charge of the Police Mobile Force; as well as other Service Commanders and members of the Management Team of the Imo State Police Command.
It pointed out that the search-and-rescue operation had been further intensified, with additional deployments of tactical teams and operational assets across identified areas, backed by intelligence-led tracking of the suspects.
The statement added that “the Police are working in close coordination with sister security agencies to ensure the safe rescue of the abducted persons and the apprehension of the perpetrators.
“The DIG Operations, DIG Shehu Umar Nadada, assured members of the public that the Nigeria Police Force is committed to securing the safe rescue of the 20 abducted persons and will sustain the operation until the mission is successfully concluded.
“He urged members of the public and the media to remain calm and vigilant and encouraged anyone with credible information that could assist the operation to promptly contact the Police or the nearest security formation.”
The statement assured that “all information received will be treated with strict confidentiality and further updates will be issued as the operation progresses.”

items.author: Reuters
items.content:
The co-pilot of flydubai flight FZ1073, which was bound for Israel, attempted to carry out a "terrorist attack" with an axe during the flight, the United Arab Emirates prosecutor general said on Saturday.
The co-pilot was identified as Hammam al-Hammami, an Omani national, a source with direct knowledge of the matter told Reuters.
A second source briefed on the investigation confirmed the co-pilot's name. UAE authorities did not immediately respond to a request for confirmation of his identity.
Disaster was averted on Wednesday after passengers and crew subdued the co-pilot, who had attacked the captain in what Israeli officials said was an apparent attempt to crash the plane carrying more than 170 passengers and crew.
While Emirati authorities and the airline have not publicly identified the co-pilot, Israeli officials have previously said he is an Omani national. Oman has not commented on the incident.
"Investigations into the incident involving flydubai flight FZ1073 found that the co-pilot had attempted to carry out a terrorist attack," Prosecutor General Hamad Saif Al Shamsi said in a statement carried by the UAE's state news agency.
The co-pilot attacked the pilot inside the cockpit with a crash axe and attempted to take control of the aircraft, the prosecutor general said. A crash axe is typically kept in the cockpit for use during emergencies such as crashes.
The investigation into flight FZ1073, including the suspect's motives, is ongoing, and the findings will be released once the "necessary procedures" have been completed, the prosecutor general said. The UAE is leading the investigation.
The airline is owned by Dubai's government.
The prosecutor general's comments were the first by Emirati investigators to describe the incident as an attempted terrorist attack.
Following the release of the prosecutor general's statement, Anwar Gargash, a senior adviser to the UAE president, said on X that the Gulf country had zero tolerance for terrorism and would show no leniency toward extremist rhetoric.
Flydubai said the circumstances surrounding the incident were still under investigation and that it was not in a position to comment further, a spokesperson said on Saturday.
Reuters could not immediately verify professional and social media pages reportedly belonging to the co-pilot, which suggested he had worked for other airlines.
Royal Air Maroc told Reuters, in response to a question about his potential employment there in the past, that he had undergone a three-month training with the airline in 2025 but his application to work there afterwards was rejected. RAM did not elaborate.

items.author: Khalid Mehmood
items.content:
Marathon talks between the government and opposition on Saturday failed to find a middle ground in an effort to break the deadlock over the PTI's long march, as both sides pressed competing demands and remained at an impasse.
The talks, chaired by National Assembly Speaker Ayaz Sadiq, followed an initial round on Friday in which the two sides exchanged their positions but failed to reach an agreement.
PTI leader Asad Qaiser confirmed that the talks ended without reaching an agreement.
The two sides remained divided over who should take the first step to ease tensions surrounding the opposition party's planned march.
The government wanted the PTI to take the initiative by cancelling the march, while the opposition wanted the government to first facilitate a meeting with its jailed founder, according to sources familiar with the talks.
Members of the two negotiating teams were also seen stepping outside the National Assembly speaker's chamber to consult with one another during the discussions.
The sources said the two sides had reached agreement on all points by 9pm, but the talks ran into a fresh hurdle after Opposition Leader in the National Assembly Mahmood Khan Achakzai raised a different position.
Achakzai said the authority to call off the march rested with PTI founder Imran Khan and Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa Chief Minister Sohail Afridi, according to the sources.
The sources said Achakzai's position led to a deadlock, while tensions increased after Afridi posted about the march on social media platform X.
The sources said President Asif Ali Zardari and Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif wanted the issues to be resolved through negotiations
This development followed the second round of talks between the government, the PPP and the opposition, chaired by National Assembly Speaker Ayaz Sadiq. The talks were convened as the October 4 deadline for the PTI-backed long march approached.
According to sources, the government agreed to several demands during the negotiations, including facilitating a meeting between opposition leaders and Imran Khan.
Sources also said an understanding was reached regarding the release of some leaders and workers detained under Section 3 of the Maintenance of Public Order (MPO), including Imran's three sisters.
The government also reportedly agreed to consider implementing the Supreme Court's August order concerning Imran's treatment at a private hospital and offered to establish a committee to examine complaints regarding the shrinking political space for the opposition.
The government's reported concessions were linked to the opposition's willingness to call off the October 4 march, which remained the principal point of contention in the negotiations. Earlier, the government had sought cancellation of the protest, while the PTI side had linked any decision to the outcome of talks and access to Imran Khan.
The talks, however, encountered a fresh hurdle when Achakzai contacted PTI Chairman Barrister Gohar Ali Khan and former NA speaker Asad Qaiser and made it clear that no final announcement should be made before meeting Imran Khan.
According to sources, Achakzai maintained that any decision by the PTI or the opposition alliance to call off the street movement would require Imran's approval.
TTAP spokesperson Akhundzada Hussain Ahmed Yousufzai said Achakzai had instructed the opposition delegation to seek a meeting with Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa (K-P) Chief Minister Sohail Afridi as its first priority, followed by meetings with Achakzai and Allama Nasir Abbas.
The preference for meeting Afridi first was linked to the fact that the K-P chief minister had announced the long march, which was earlier scheduled for September 27 but later postponed until today (October 4).
According to the spokesperson, Afridi could brief the former prime minister o0n the progress made during the two days of negotiations and obtain his response.
Achakzai's position effectively meant that the reported understanding between the government and opposition could not immediately be converted into a final announcement about the march.
Reports said Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi, who played a key role in the negotiations, left Parliament House with the draft understanding and went to the Prime Minister's House to consult the senior leadership before returning to Parliament House, after which talks resumed.
The second round followed an inconclusive first round held on Friday.
The initial meeting ended with both sides exchanging their respective positions but without a breakthrough. They agreed to resume negotiations on Saturday. The National Assembly described Friday's meeting as being held in a "cordial" and constructive atmosphere.
The opposition's demand for access to Imran Khan had emerged as a central issue from the outset. During the first round, opposition representatives maintained that major political decisions could not be taken without consulting the PTI founder.
The government delegation included Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi, Minister for States and Frontier Regions Amir Muqam, Minister for Parliamentary Affairs Tariq Fazal Chaudhry, Minister of State for Interior Talal Chaudhry and Prime Minister's Adviser Rana Sanaullah, along with PPP representatives Senator Sherry Rehman, Naveed Qamar and Ijaz Hussain Jakhrani.
The opposition delegation included Mahmood Khan Achakzai, Barrister Gohar Khan, Raja Nasir Abbas, Asad Qaiser, Salman Akram Raja, Amir Dogar and Haleem Adil Sheikh. Achakzai had earlier declined to attend the talks at the Speaker's chamber, seeking a neutral venue.
The negotiations are taking place against the backdrop of heightened tensions between the federal and K-P governments and the PTI's plan to bring supporters towards Islamabad.
A number of federal ministers have threatened to consider imposing Governor's Rule in K-P, where the PTI is in power, if the opposition continued with its plans to march on the capital.
On Friday, the military's top brass also underscored the importance of internal stability and resolved that any attempt to cause agitation or create a May 9-like situation, "on any pretext whatsoever, will be dealt with decisive force and rule of law, without hesitation and discrimination.
On May 9, 2023, the PTI supporters and workers staged violent protests after arrest of former prime minister Imran Khan from the premises of the Islamabad High Court and attacked dozens of military installations, followed by a grand crackdown against the former ruling party.

items.title: FO summons Indian envoy over civilian killings
items.summary:
The Ministry of Foreign Affairs (MoFA) on Saturday summoned the Indian Chargé d'Affaires and lodged a strong protest over the killing of two Pakistani civilians by personnel of the Indian Border Security Force (BSF) in the Bedian Sector along the International Border on Friday.
"The BSF personnel resorted to unprovoked lethal force against unarmed civilians. Such use of force was wholly unjustified and grossly disproportionate, resulting in the tragic loss of two precious lives. Pakistan categorically rejects any attempt to mischaracterise the deceased as 'infiltrators," said a statement issued by MoFA.
The statement came a day after two Pakistani civilians were killed, and another was injured after Indian BSF personnel opened fire near the Pakistan-India international border in Kasur. The incident reportedly occurred when three residents from Ladhar village moved a few steps beyond a border pillar, upon which BSF personnel opened fire on the men without warning.

items.author: Hamisu Kabir Matazu
items.content:
The North-East Governors’ Forum (NEGF) has called on the Federal Government to revive stalled oil exploration activities in Borno State, even as it commended President Bola Ahmed Tinubu for the ongoing revival of the Kolmani oil drilling project in Gombe State.
The appeal was part of a communiqué issued at the conclusion of the 13th regular meeting of the NEGF, held at the Borno Government House in Maiduguri, on Saturday.
The two-day summit, which ran from October 2 to October 3, 2026, brought together governors and top officials from the six North-Eastern states—Adamawa, Bauchi, Borno, Gombe, Taraba, and Yobe—to deliberate on regional security, economic integration, and infrastructure.
Reading the communiqué, the Forum’s Vice Chairman and Governor of Adamawa State, Rt. Hon. Umaru Fintiri, urged the Federal Government to revisit petroleum exploration activities that had earlier commenced but subsequently stalled in the Magumeri and Gubio Local Government Areas of Borno State.
The governors expressed deep appreciation to President Tinubu for renewed federal attention on key regional infrastructure projects.
These include the Port Harcourt–Jos–Bauchi–Gombe–Maiduguri rail corridor, frontier oil exploration at Kolmani, and the Akwanga–Jos–Bauchi–Gombe–Biu–Maiduguri highway.
Reflecting on its six-year journey since its inaugural meeting in Gombe in March 2020, the Forum touted regional unity as its most significant achievement, enabling a collective voice that has driven tangible developmental results.
On energy, the governors praised member states for shifting toward a regional energy agenda, highlighting the Dadinkowa hydropower plant, which now feeds the national grid, and encouraged states to leverage the new electricity law and abundant solar resources to expand mini-grid solutions.
Also, the Forum reiterated its call on the Federal Government to expedite the completion of the long-neglected Mambila Hydropower Plant, following the recent clearance of legal encumbrances through an arbitration ruling.
To ease transportation costs and stimulate economic activities, the Forum announced a partnership with Green Ville Energy to establish more Compressed Natural Gas (CNG) and Liquefied Natural Gas (LNG) stations across the region.
The forum also acknowledged the Federal Government and the North East Development Commission (NEDC) for providing 10,000 electric tricycles, 10 electric buses, and 300 electric taxis set to launch in October, alongside plans to float a North-East regional air shuttle service to facilitate faster movement of people and goods.
While acknowledging appreciable successes in the ongoing fight against insurgency—and praising the sacrifices of the Armed Forces—the Forum noted that the subregion still faces daunting humanitarian and infrastructural hurdles.
The governors reaffirmed their commitment to intelligence sharing, inter-state security cooperation, and addressing the root socio-economic drivers of youth exploitation by extremist elements.
Recognizing that the North-East holds one of the youngest populations in the country, the Forum pledged to prioritize quality education, vocational and entrepreneurial training, and technology-driven employment for youth.
The governors also called on the NEDC to ramp up investments in education, expedite long-awaited scholarship awards for indigent students, reduce the number of out-of-school children, and support Tsangaya education.
To combat environmental degradation, the region agreed to partner with the Institute of Forest Research to train local forest experts and counter deforestation.
The Forum announced that its next meeting will be held on December 18–19, 2026, in Gombe State.

He also enjoined them to use wisdom to promote peace and unity in the country.
Kabara, who is also the leader of the Qadiriyya Islamic Movement, said this in an address to mark the 76th Maukibi celebration, on Saturday in Kano.
He stressed the need for clerics and politicians to understand the influence of their words on society, urging them to use respectful and constructive language capable of strengthening peaceful coexistence.

The Qadiriyya leader said responsible communication was important in promoting peace and unity, particularly given their influences on the people.
Also, Nasiru Haruna-Kabara, a member of the 76th Maukibi Organising Committee, said that an estimated five million followers participated in the event.
He described the 2026 edition as one of the best in the history of the annual gathering, attributing the large turnout to participation by followers across the globe.
The chairman said that the event attracted participants from Lagos, Ogun, Kogi and other parts of the country, as well as the United Kingdom, United States, Niger Republic, Côte d’Ivoire, among others.
“The 76th edition also marked a new chapter in the history of the Maukibi, as the celebration was held at a new venue provided by the Kano State Government,” he said.
He commended the Kano government over the construction of the new facility for the Qadiriyya community, adding that the gesture provided a more suitable space for the growing number of participants.
Sheikh Kabara left the Qadiriyya House at Kabara area of Kano metropolis at about 9:15 a.m.
He led the procession through Makwarari; Yan-Mota, Koki and Kofar Mazugal before proceeding to the celebration venue along Katsina Road.
The event was attended by Sen. Abdul’Aziz Yari, Sen. Aminu Waziri Tambuwal, and Ibrahim Kabiru-Masari, who represented President Bola Tinubu, as well as Gov. Abba Yusuf, representatives of traditional rulers and other dignitaries.
The Maukibi provides an opportunity for Qadiriyya followers to strengthen religious ties, promote unity and remind participants of the importance of peace and harmonious relations among members of the society. (NAN)

The businessman also highlighted Africa’s position in the global artificial intelligence race, saying the continent accounts for less than one per cent of the world’s AI computing capacity and about three per cent of its AI talent.
“The constraint is not talent. It is electricity. We leapfrogged landlines with mobile. We will not leapfrog electricity,” Elumelu said.
He said African countries must urgently address their electricity challenges to avoid missing opportunities presented by the digital economy.
According to him, the continent’s AI race is also a race to secure adequate electricity generation and computing capacity.
“My closing advice: To the youth in the room: start before you are qualified. I did,” he said.
He also called on investors and partners to support the growth of young African businesses, citing the Tony Elumelu Foundation’s seed-capital programme.
“Tony Elumelu Foundation seed capital has proved that young African entrepreneurs are investible. Now co-invest with us to take them to scale,” he said.

items.title: Apple Tightens macOS Privacy After AI Agent Message Access Concerns
items.summary:
Apple is changing macOS Full Disk Access after warning that some developers are using the permission in ways that can expose users’ files, emails, messages, and browsing history without users fully understanding what they are granting.
The company said it will introduce additional controls so apps can only receive this level of access through more explicit user action. Apple said the issue is becoming more important as AI agents become more capable and autonomous.
Meta Muse Incident Raised Questions
Apple’s announcement comes shortly after tech columnist Jason Aten said Meta’s Muse AI agent sent him an unsolicited notification based on a private Apple Messages conversation.
Aten said he had not knowingly permitted Muse to read his messages.
Meta CTO David Singleton disputed the idea that Muse could access Messages without the user enabling the required settings. He said the Messages integration is opt-in and requires both Full Disk Access and the Muse Messages connector to be enabled.
items.author: Afaq Wajdan Malik
items.content:
Apple is changing macOS Full Disk Access after warning that some developers are using the permission in ways that can expose users’ files, emails, messages, and browsing history without users fully understanding what they are granting.
The company said it will introduce additional controls so apps can only receive this level of access through more explicit user action. Apple said the issue is becoming more important as AI agents become more capable and autonomous.
Meta Muse Incident Raised Questions
Apple’s announcement comes shortly after tech columnist Jason Aten said Meta’s Muse AI agent sent him an unsolicited notification based on a private Apple Messages conversation.
Aten said he had not knowingly permitted Muse to read his messages.
Meta CTO David Singleton disputed the idea that Muse could access Messages without the user enabling the required settings. He said the Messages integration is opt-in and requires both Full Disk Access and the Muse Messages connector to be enabled.
Apple Says Full Disk Access Can Expose Messages
Apple did not mention Meta or Muse by name.
However, Apple said Full Disk Access can allow apps to see sensitive information, including messages, mail, files, and browsing history.
Security researcher Patrick Wardle also argued that apps with Full Disk Access can technically read most non-root files on a Mac, including chats, browser cookies, and browsing data.
Muse Has Faced Other Security Concerns
Apple’s announcement also follows the disclosure of a Muse vulnerability that could allow locally running apps or commands to take control of the AI assistant and use its existing privileges.
Meta later released a fix for the issue.
The incidents highlight the privacy and security risks created when AI agents receive broad access to personal data and system-level permissions.
Apple has not yet detailed exactly how the new Full Disk Access controls will work or when they will be introduced.

A series of recent incidents involving AI agents has raised concerns across the industry about whether existing safeguards are strong enough as models become more capable.
The Hugging Face incident remains the most serious case OpenAI has publicly identified as part of its ongoing review.

items.author: Afaq Wajdan Malik
items.content:
Google has launched a refrigerator-sized satellite carrying four Tensor Processing Units (TPUs) as part of Project Suncatcher, its research effort to test AI computing in space.
The satellite will run a version of Google’s Gemma AI model for about 15 minutes at a time because of heat limits. Google will test how its chips handle launch stress, radiation, and extreme temperatures in orbit.
Google Wants AI Data Centers in Space
The company eventually wants to build clusters of satellites that work together as orbital data centers powered by solar energy.
Each future satellite could carry dozens of TPUs and communicate with other satellites and Earth using lasers. Google plans to launch two more satellites next year to test those connections.
The current prototype was developed with satellite company Planet and launched aboard a SpaceX rocket. The mission is expected to operate for about a year.
Major Challenges Remain
Cooling is one of the biggest problems because traditional air- and water-based cooling does not work in space. Google is testing pipes and radiators to remove heat from the chips.
Repairs would also be much harder than in normal data centers, while launches remain expensive.
Google also says space-based data centers are unlikely to become cheaper than terrestrial facilities within the next five years.
Other companies are exploring similar ideas. Starcloud previously launched an Nvidia H100 chip into space, while SpaceX has said it could begin deploying orbital AI compute satellites as early as 2028.
Google describes Project Suncatcher as a long-term “moonshot” rather than something expected to replace Earth-based data centers soon.

items.author: Arsalan Khattak
items.content:
Sindh Chief Minister Syed Murad Ali Shah has directed the School Education Department to make newly upgraded schools fully operational by April 2, 2027, while ordering a province-wide enrollment drive to bring out-of-school children back to classrooms.
He issued the directives during a review meeting on the Sindh Secondary Education Improvement Project (SSEIP) at the Chief Minister’s House in Karachi. The SSEIP and SELECT programs cover 1,133 schools across Sindh, including 838 under SSEIP and 295 under SELECT.
Officials expect to complete 552 schools by December 2026 and 801 by March 2027, while the overall program has a completion target of December 2027. Murad Shah directed officials to ensure that schools scheduled for completion by March 2027 have furniture, teachers and other essential facilities in place by April 2.
The chief minister also ordered the Education Department to expand an enrollment campaign launched as a pilot in five upgraded secondary schools in Thatta. The nine-day campaign enrolled 702 students in Classes VI to X, including 409 girls, while 102 out-of-school or dropout children returned to education.
Community teams visited 116 feeder schools, 17 neighborhoods and 23 villages and conducted door-to-door outreach. Murad Shah directed officials to expand the campaign across Sindh, particularly targeting girls and children who have dropped out. He also ordered officials to finalize a transparent framework for managing upgraded schools.

items.author: Afaq Wajdan Malik
items.content:
Around 2.3 million new cancer cases worldwide in 2024 were linked to infections, equal to about 12% of all cancer cases, according to a study published in The Lancet Oncology.
Most of these cases were linked to Helicobacter pylori, human papillomavirus (HPV), hepatitis B and C viruses, and Epstein-Barr virus (EBV).
Researchers said many infection-related cancers could be prevented through vaccination, testing and treatment.
Five Infections Cause Most Cases
The study estimated that H. pylori caused about 760,000 cancer cases, or 4% of all cases worldwide.
HPV was linked to about 750,000 cases, also around 4%, followed by hepatitis B with 360,000 cases, EBV with 260,000 cases, and hepatitis C with 160,000 cases.
David Greenberg of Hackensack Meridian Jersey Shore University Medical Center said the findings show that a large part of the global cancer burden could be prevented by better controlling infections.
How These Infections Can Cause Cancer
HPV is a common sexually transmitted infection and can cause cervical, anal, genital, mouth and throat cancers. A vaccine can prevent HPV and works best when given before a person becomes sexually active.
Chronic hepatitis B and hepatitis C can damage the liver and lead to cirrhosis and liver cancer. Hepatitis B can be prevented with a vaccine and treated with antiviral medicines, although treatment usually does not cure the infection.
There is no vaccine for hepatitis C, but more than 90% of patients can be cured with direct-acting antiviral medicines taken for two or three months.
H. pylori is the most common bacterial cause of cancer. It can cause stomach ulcers and may lead to stomach cancer, a rare type of lymphoma and possibly colorectal cancer.
The bacterium spreads through saliva and contaminated food or water and is more common in lower-income countries. Most infections happen during childhood. Doctors can treat it with antibiotics and medicines that reduce stomach acid.
EBV is a common herpesvirus that causes mononucleosis. It stays in the body and can contribute to nasopharyngeal cancer, some lymphomas and stomach cancer.
More than 90% of adults show signs of previous EBV infection. There is currently no vaccine or approved antiviral treatment for it.
Other Cancer-Causing Infections
The study also included HIV, which is classified as a cancer-causing virus.
People with advanced HIV can develop AIDS-related cancers such as Kaposi sarcoma and non-Hodgkin lymphoma. Even people whose HIV is well controlled with treatment still have a higher risk of several cancers.
Kaposi-sarcoma-associated herpesvirus, also known as HHV-8, usually causes no illness in healthy people but can cause tumors in people with weakened immune systems.
Other infections included in the study were human T-cell lymphotropic virus, Merkel cell polyomavirus, Schistosoma haematobium, and the liver flukes Opisthorchis viverrini and Clonorchis sinensis.
These infections can cause cancers including bladder, liver and bile duct cancer.
Lower-Income Countries Carry Most of the Burden
More than three-quarters of infection-related cancer cases occurred in low- and middle-income countries.
East Asia had the largest number, with around 990,000 cases, or 42% of the global total.
Rates were also higher than the global average in sub-Saharan Africa, Central and Eastern Europe, and Southeast Asia.
Prevention Could Reduce Cancer Cases
The researchers said better infection control could prevent many cancer cases.
They highlighted HPV and hepatitis B vaccination, testing and treatment for HIV, H. pylori, hepatitis B and hepatitis C, safer injection practices, access to condoms and HIV PrEP, and screening for precancerous cervical and anal changes linked to HPV.
The researchers also said more investment is needed to develop new prevention tools, especially for EBV.

items.content:
The Yadgar-e-Fatah Monument, commemorating Pakistan’s victory over India in the Marka-e-Haq Operation 2025 and paying tribute to the martyrs who sacrificed their lives for the country, was opened to the general public on Saturday.
A special ceremony jointly organised by the Ministry of Information and Broadcasting and the Capital Development Authority (CDA) was held at the monument’s premises, drawing people from different walks of life to celebrate what was described as a moment of national pride.
Speaking on the occasion, Information and Broadcasting Secretary Ashfaq Ahmad Khalil said the Yadgar-e-Fatah monument served as a landmark of the nation’s victory, anchored in courage and unwavering determination.
Read: Armed forces vow 'stronger response' to any hostile design as Pakistan marks first anniversary of Marka-e-Haq
He termed the opening of the monument a moment of pride for the nation and future generations.
The ceremony was attended by prominent figures, including President Chess Federation Zeeshan Naqvi, emerging national cricketer Razaullah and well-known sports personality ‘Chacha Cricket’.
Razaullah paid tribute to the bravery of Pakistan’s armed forces and their sacrifices. He said the armed forces had defeated the enemy decisively in the past and would continue to do so in the future. He added that he felt immensely proud to be a Pakistani.
Chacha Cricket waves the national flag during the opening ceremony of the Yadgar-e-Fatah (Monument of Victory) in Islamabad on Saturday. Photo: APP
Chacha Cricket congratulated the nation on the “remarkable victory” in Marka-e-Haq and said the nation was ready to sacrifice its lives for the motherland. He said Pakistan had earned a prominent place in the world through its achievements.
A documentary was also screened at the ceremony, showcasing the eight-month construction journey of the monument and the concept behind its architecture and design.
The monument features five archways, symbolising the five pillars of Islam as well as the five pillars of the country — the government, military, media, people and the ideology underpinning the nation.
Its design also represents the three wings of Pakistan’s armed forces — the Army, Air Force and Navy — along with cyber defence and space warfare branches.
A projection-mapping show was presented on the monument, using lights and visuals to narrate its significance and highlight key moments associated with the country’s victory in the Marka-e-Haq Operation.
Also Read: PM Shehbaz warns India over water, says ‘every drop’ is Pakistan’s red line
A musical performance also drew appreciation from the audience, with two finalists of Pakistan Idol appearing on stage.
School and college students in uniform were seen taking pictures and making videos in front of the illuminated monument.
The Yadgar-e-Fatah monument will remain open to the public daily from 5pm to 10pm, except Mondays. Free entry tickets can be obtained through the website Yadgarefatah.net.
The monument was inaugurated by President Asif Ali Zardari and Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif earlier this year on the eve of Pakistan’s 80th Independence Day.
Pahalgam attack and Marka-e-Haq
On April 22, 2025, escalation between Pakistan and India began when an attack in Pahalgam killed 26 people. India immediately blamed Pakistan for the incident. However, Pakistan categorically rejected the Indian blame.
In response, India undertook a series of hostile actions the next day, on April 23, 2025, including suspending the 65-year-old Indus Waters Treaty (IWT), cancelling visas for Pakistani citizens, closing the Wagah-Attari border crossing, ordering the shutdown of the Pakistan High Commission in New Delhi, and reducing diplomatic staff at each other's embassies.
Tensions further escalated in the early hours of May 7, 2025, when missile strikes hit six cities in Punjab and Azad Jammu and Kashmir (AJK), destroying a mosque and killing dozens of civilians, including women, children, and the elderly.
Read More: French intelligence official confirms downing of Rafale by Pakistan
In a swift military response, Pakistan’s armed forces shot down Indian warplanes, including three Rafale jets. The confrontation intensified again in the early hours of May 10, 2025, when India targeted several Pakistani airbases with missile strikes. In retaliation, Pakistan launched Operation Bunyanum Marsoos, damaging Indian military installations, including missile storage sites, airbases, and other strategic targets.
On May 10, 2025, US President Donald Trump announced that a ceasefire had been reached following intense overnight diplomatic efforts. Minutes later, the agreement was confirmed separately by Pakistan’s Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar and the Indian foreign secretary.

The company created by the $110 billion merger of Paramount and Warner Bros. Discovery will officially be called Skydance, Paramount Skydance CEO David Ellison has confirmed.
The deal is expected to close this month after clearing a major regulatory hurdle in September. It will combine the two long-running Hollywood studios while bringing HBO Max and Paramount+ under the same corporate owner.

items.author: Afaq Wajdan Malik
items.content:
The company created by the $110 billion merger of Paramount and Warner Bros. Discovery will officially be called Skydance, Paramount Skydance CEO David Ellison has confirmed.
The deal is expected to close this month after clearing a major regulatory hurdle in September. It will combine the two long-running Hollywood studios while bringing HBO Max and Paramount+ under the same corporate owner.
The combined company will also control major entertainment properties including Harry Potter, DC, Game of Thrones and Mission: Impossible, alongside television assets such as CBS and CNN.
What once was the peak, is now just the beginning.
Paramount and Warner Bros. shaped over a century of culture. By combining them, we aren't rewriting history — we're equipping these iconic studios with a more powerful engine. Together, we are Skydance: a creative-first home for… pic.twitter.com/uInLRY3IrE
— David Ellison (@davidellison) October 2, 2026
Why the Company Is Being Called Skydance
Ellison announced the name through a newly created X account, saying the goal was to give the combined business its own identity without replacing the Paramount and Warner Bros. brands.
He said both studios have distinct identities and long histories, and that the new corporate name is intended to keep those brands in the spotlight rather than overshadow them.
The Skydance name comes from the production company Ellison founded in 2006.
CNN and CBS News Will Be Under the Same Owner
The merger will also place CNN and CBS News under the same parent company, raising questions about how the two news organizations will operate after the deal closes.
Paramount has agreed to establish an independent News Editorial Independence Board intended to oversee both organizations and support editorial independence.
Skydance Commits to More Theatrical Releases
The company has also reportedly committed to releasing at least 30 theatrical films per year.
Skydance Corporation is expected to become the legal name of the combined company once the transaction closes, bringing Paramount, Warner Bros. and their major film, television and streaming businesses under one corporate structure.

items.content:
The Capital Development Authority (CDA) has accelerated development work in Islamabad’s Sector E-12 after recovering more than 1,000 kanals of land that had remained occupied for decades.
CDA Chairman and Chief Commissioner Sohail Ashraf said the authority aims to complete development of the sector within six months, potentially ending a delay that has kept the project stalled for 37 years.
The CDA launched E-12 in 1989, but development remained incomplete largely because local landowners occupied acquired land and several compensation cases remained unresolved. The authority recently conducted an operation to recover the occupied land and has so far retrieved more than 1,000 kanals worth billions of rupees.
The civic agency also recently handed over around 15 allotment letters to local landlords and promised to resolve genuine outstanding compensation cases. Development has already progressed significantly in three sub-sectors, while the CDA has now shifted its focus to stalled Sub-Sector 4.
The authority said the recovered land has removed a major obstacle to development and allowed infrastructure work to move forward. The CDA plans to develop roads, municipal infrastructure and other civic facilities for future residents. Ashraf credited the CDA team and Interior Minister Syed Mohsin Raza Naqvi for supporting the land-recovery effort.
Development also remains pending in C-13, C-15, C-16, D-13, E-13 and F-13 because the CDA has yet to resolve compensation cases.

items.author: Afaq Wajdan Malik
items.content:
Meta is expanding its Muse AI agent beyond the upcoming Muse Charm with a new open-source initiative called Muse Gadgets, which will let developers build their own Muse-powered hardware.
The company is also launching its own example device, called the Muse Home Link, which connects the AI agent to smart home products.
Developers Can Build Their Own Muse Devices
Nat Friedman, head of product at Meta’s Superintelligence Labs, said the company is releasing open-source firmware and a Linux SDK that developers can use to bring Muse to different types of hardware.
Meta has suggested several possible form factors, including a dedicated E Ink display, an HDMI dongle for TVs, and a small touchscreen accessory similar in size and shape to the Muse Charm.
The platform appears designed to support other hardware as well, giving developers and hobbyists flexibility in how they use the AI agent.
Meta has also created a dedicated Discord community for developers working with Muse Gadgets.
Muse Home Link Connects Muse to Smart Home Devices
The Muse Home Link is a small USB-C-powered device that allows Muse to connect to a home network and communicate with compatible smart home devices.
According to Friedman, the device can connect to products such as TVs, speakers, and other devices that expose HTTPS interfaces.
Meta plans to give away 5,000 Muse Home Link units to Muse subscribers.
Muse Hardware Push Expands
It remains unclear whether Meta plans to turn Muse Gadgets into a broader hardware platform, but creations from developers and hobbyists could help shape the company’s future hardware work.
CEO Mark Zuckerberg unveiled the Muse Charm last week at Meta Connect, describing it as another way for users to interact with the Muse agent without having to wear Meta’s smart glasses.
The Muse Gadgets project now gives developers another route to bring the same AI agent to dedicated devices of their own.

items.author: Anne Florentyna
items.content:
Kuku Technologies Limited, parent company of audio OTT platform Kuku FM and microdrama app Kuku TV, swung into the black in the fiscal year FY26, reporting a net profit of ₹182.7 Cr against a net loss of ₹152.6 Cr incurred in FY25.
The company’s profitability came on the back of a notable uptick in its top line performance. The IPO-bound startup, which filed its confidential DRHP with the SEBI earlier this year, saw its operating revenue for the fiscal year zoom more than sixfold to ₹1,484.2 Cr in FY26 from ₹241.6 Cr in the previous fiscal. Including other income of ₹26.2 Cr, total income for the fiscal stood at ₹1,510.4 Cr.
Subscriptions remained the overwhelming source of Kuku Technologies’ revenue during FY26.
The company generated ₹1,475.4 Cr from subscriptions, accounting for more than 99% of its operating revenue. This was followed by ₹6.9 Cr from pay-per-piece (PPV) content purchases, while advertising brought in the remainder ₹1.9 Cr.
India continued to account for the vast majority of its business, contributing ₹1,463.6 Cr, or roughly 99% of operating revenue. International markets contributed ₹20.5 Cr during the year.
The profitability was also charged by a deferred tax credit of ₹98.2 Cr and a tax expense of ₹4 Cr. Excluding that, the profit for the year stood at ₹88.6 Cr.
At the operating level, Kuku Technologies swung to an EBITDA profit of ₹82.9 Cr in FY26 from an EBITDA loss of ₹159.8 Cr in FY25.
Kuku Turns Profitable Ahead Of IPO
The company, which operates audio OTT platform Kuku FM, microdrama app Kuku TV, among others, has swung to the black ahead of going public. Earlier in September, the markets regulator Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) approved the proposed listing of Kuku Technologies.
Kuku filed its confidential DRHP with the SEBI in June. As per sources, the IPO’s size could be in the range of ₹2,500-3,500 Cr ($261-366 Mn) and could potentially value it at ₹15,000 Cr (about $1.8 Bn).
The IPO will consist of a fresh issue of shares as well as an offer-for-sale component. Kuku plans to deploy the capital to upgrade its tech, AI infrastructure, content production and fuel geographic expansion.
As of now, the startup’s content library spans more than 20,000 titles across seven languages and multiple genres including drama, finance, and well-being. It claims to have more than 1 Cr listeners and creators on its platform and 400 Mn app downloads across its portfolio.
Kuku has raised over $156 Mn to date from the likes of Fundamentum Partnership, Krafton, Vertex Ventures, IFC, 3one4 Capital, among others. Its most recent $85 Mn Series C funding round, in October 2025, was led by Granite Asia.
Magnifying Kuku FM’s Spending
Total expenses for the fiscal year surged 3.5X to ₹1,421.8 Cr in the year under review from ₹411 Cr in FY25. Here is a breakdown of where the startup spent a major share of its expenses:
Marketing And Advertisement Expenses: Constituting 77.7% of the overall expenses, Kuku FM spent ₹1,105.1 Cr on marketing and advertising in FY26. This is a near 4X jump compared with around ₹284.8 Cr spent on marketing in FY25.
Operational Costs: Spending under this head rose 11X to ₹96.3 Cr in the year under review from ₹8.7 Cr in the previous fiscal.
Employee Benefit Expenses: Employee-related expenses grew at a much slower pace, increasing about 24% to ₹74.1 Cr in FY26 from ₹59.9 Cr in FY25.

items.author: Akshit Pushkarna
items.content:
New-age tech stocks remained under pressure this week, with 47 stocks declining as benchmark indices recorded their eighth consecutive weekly fall.
Moneyview’s market debut this week took the number of new-age tech companies under Inc42’s coverage to 66. Despite the addition, their combined market capitalisation fell to $153.61 Bn from the $166.6 Bn commanded by 65 companies last week.
Shares of Moneyview made their debut on Thursday (October 1) at ₹55.6 on the BSE, nearly 64% above the issue price of ₹34. The stock closed at ₹54.03, down 2.8% from the listing price but 58.9% above its issue price.
Of the 65 stocks under Inc42’s coverage at the end of last week, 47 fell between 0.08% and 20.1% this week. Eighteen stocks gained between 0.17% and 22.55%.
Turtlemint led the losers, falling 20.1% to ₹69.75, while PB Fintech declined 15.66% to ₹983 following IRDAI’s proposed changes to insurance commissions.
ESDS was the second-biggest loser, falling 18.54% to ₹1,431.70 after announcing its Q1 FY27 results on September 24. However, it remained more than 91% above its listing price.
Swiggy, Fractal, Menhood, and IndiaMART touched fresh lows during the week. Eternal, Lenskart, Ather Energy, Paytm, and Nykaa also declined this week.
SME-listed Zappfresh led the gainers, rising 22.55% to ₹60.49 after hitting an all-time low of ₹47.10 on September 25. RentoMojo, Meesho, BlackBuck, and Go Digit also gained, while Aequs, Kissht, Nazara, SEDEMAC, and Zelio touched fresh highs.
The stock markets were closed yesterday on account of Gandhi Jayanti.
Beyond stock movements, the week saw GST notices, stake sales, and expansion plans across listed new-age tech companies. Here’s a closer look at the key developments.
GST Notices Put Companies In Focus
Kissht’s NBFC arm, Si Creva, received a GST show cause notice involving ₹44.06 Cr over alleged input tax credit discrepancies and tax shortfalls for FY23. This comprises ₹22.03 Cr in tax, ₹19.83 Cr in interest, and ₹2.2 Cr in penalties. The company said it would contest the notice.
WeWork India received a ₹11.01 Cr show cause notice over alleged excess input tax credit utilisation arising from differences between its annual returns and audited books. Urban Company faced a ₹3.05 Cr demand over alleged incorrect input tax credit claims and tax shortfalls for FY23.
ideaForge received a ₹109.17 Cr GST demand and penalty for allegedly paying 5% instead of 18% on drone sales between January 2022 and March 2024. It plans to appeal, citing a 2025 government clarification that drones attract 5% GST, and expects no immediate material financial or operational impact.
Stake Sales And Purchases
TPG, through NewQuest Asia Fund IV (Singapore), sold 40 Lakh Shadowfax shares at ₹284.03 apiece for ₹113.6 Cr, following its ₹202 Cr exit from FirstCry on September 25.
SBI Mutual Fund bought 1.18 Cr Swiggy shares for an estimated ₹300.6 Cr, raising its holding from 4.7% to 5.12%.
MobiKwik cofounder and CFO Upasana Taku bought 1.07 Lakh shares for ₹2.1 Cr in two September transactions, increasing her stake from 10.11% to 10.24%.
RateGain Names New CFO
RateGain appointed former Optum India executive Chetan Garg as CFO, effective Monday (September 28). Garg, who also held senior finance roles at Whirlpool, will oversee global finance operations, capital allocation, and risk management.
SEDEMAC Reports Record Unit Sales
SEDEMAC’s quarterly sales of control-intensive electronic control units (ECUs) rose 37.5% to a record 14.53 Lakh units in Q2 FY27 from 10.56 Lakh units in Q2 FY26.
Trailing 12-month sales rose 44.2% YoY to a record 45.97 Lakh units. Cumulative sales of its sensorless ISG+EFI ECUs crossed 1 Mn units in September, 23 months after launch.
AceVector Heads For Listing
Snapdeal parent AceVector will list on Monday (October 5), after its ₹420 Cr IPO was subscribed 4.93X.
Several OFS participants booked losses. SoftBank’s sale fetched substantially less than the acquisition cost of its shares sold, while returns varied across Nexus Venture Partners’ investment vehicles.
BlackBuck, LEAP India Back Subsidiaries
BlackBuck invested ₹22 Cr in wholly owned subsidiary TZF Logistics Solutions, subscribing to 34.08 Lakh shares at ₹64.55 apiece. The rights issue will support expansion, working capital, and compliance with RBI requirements for its prepaid payment instrument licence.
Separately, LEAP India incorporated packaging manufacturer Vimprotech after its board approved two wholly owned subsidiaries on Tuesday (September 29).
Vimprotech will receive an initial ₹4.03 Cr investment. The second proposed subsidiary, Total International Packaging Solutions, will provide returnable packaging pooling services to automotive and manufacturing businesses, with an initial ₹1.65 Cr investment.
Now, let’s take a look at the broader market trends this week.
Benchmarks Extend Losing Streak
The aforementioned developments unfolded against a weak market backdrop, with rising US bond yields, foreign investor selling, and crude oil concerns weighing on sentiment.
The Sensex fell 2.69% to 71,909.70, while the Nifty 50 declined 3.11% to 22,421.95. Midcap and smallcap indices also declined around 3.5% each.
Despite the fall in indices, domestic fundamentals remained resilient, with industrial production growth accelerating to 8% YoY in August.
Domestic triggers ahead include the RBI’s policy decision, September services and composite PMI readings, and Q2 FY27 earnings, starting with TCS and DMart.
Religare Broking’s SVP of research Ajit Mishra expects caution to persist, with bond yields, crude prices, geopolitical developments, and RBI policy providing direction.
Against this backdrop, here’s a closer look at Aequs’ rally and Turtlemint’s continued decline.
Aequs Rallies On Fundraise Plan
Aequs gained 11.66% to ₹274.90, taking its gains over the listing price to 96.36% and market capitalisation to $1.92 Bn.
Its board approved a ₹650 Cr preferential warrant issue to promoter-group entity Mellwood Trustee Services on September 25. Priced at ₹231.55 apiece, the warrants require ₹325 Cr upfront payment and the balance upon conversion.
Proceeds will support aerospace and consumer capacity expansion, including the Hosur facility, subsidiaries, and joint ventures. The infusion is also expected to support ₹800 Cr in additional term borrowing.
Aequs expects 25-30% aerospace revenue growth in FY27. Motilal Oswal said its aerospace order book of over $1 Bn supports potential revenue CAGR of 25-30% over five years.
The stock hit a fresh intraday high of ₹286.05 on Wednesday (September 30).
Turtlemint Falls On Commission Concerns
Turtlemint’s 20.1% weekly decline reduced its market capitalisation to about $210 Mn.
The stock hit the lower circuit in multiple sessions following IRDAI’s September 23 proposals for commission ceilings across insurance products and distribution channels, including renewals and portability. Comments are due by October 25.
Lower commissions would pressure revenue from Turtlemint’s point-of-sale persons (PoSPs) network. Separately, Jefferies estimated that a 10% reduction in new-business commission rates could translate into a 10-12% earnings decline for both Turtlemint and PB Fintech.
Motilal Oswal had initiated coverage on Turtlemint on September 17 with a ‘Buy’ rating and ₹180 target, citing its more than 5.5 Lakh certified PoSPs, presence across 19,186 pin codes, and potential profitability improvements. However, it had flagged commission regulation as a key risk.

items.author: Daily Trust
items.content:
Governor Uba Sani is embarking on massive infrastructural development and rural transformation for the benefit of Kaduna State citizens of all generations and not for the next election.
The Governor has also spread projects across all senatorial districts, with each of the 23 local governments, including rural and urban areas benefiting, since he assumed office over three years ago.
The Uba Sani Aides Assembly (USAA), a forum of Technical Assistants, Special Assistants and Senior Special Assistants to the Governor, made this observation after touring a few legacy projects.
Speaking to newsmen after the inspection tour, the Chairman of the Forum, Hon Ibrahim Mohammed noted that the Governor ‘’ has initiated 160 new road projects in addition to inherited ones, bringing the total road network under construction to 1,355 kilometres across the 23 LGAs. Both urban and rural communities are benefiting.’’
Hon Mohammed pointed out that ‘’infrastructural development has not been concentrated in the capital while rural areas wait. The quality of work, the use of reputable contractors and insistence on timelines show a government that is serious about value for money.’’
The Chairman who noted that no administration in Kaduna’s history has made such huge investments in urban and rural infrastructure, commended the Governor for the quality, scale and even spread of these projects.
He listed three flagship projects that the Governor Uba Sani administration has implemented, including the Kaduna Modern Inter-State Bus Terminal at Millennium City in Chikun local government; the Kabala Costain to Aliyu Makama Road and Bridge linking the northern and southern parts of Kaduna city and the ongoing reconstruction of the Ahmadu Bello Stadium.
According to the Chairman, ‘’the Kaduna Modern Inter-State Bus Terminal sits on 18 hectares at Millennium City. It is the largest of its kind in sub-Saharan Africa, with capacity for 5,000 vehicles.
‘’Designed as a modern transport hub with state-of-the-art facilities, it is powered entirely by an independent solar grid, making it efficient, environmentally responsible, and a model for public infrastructure,’’ he added.
Hon Mohammed argued that the ‘’ terminal will ease traffic congestion in Kaduna city by diverting inter-state and heavy vehicle movement to Millennium city, reducing travel time, improving safety, and enhancing the passenger experience.’’
The Chairman of Uba Sani Aides Assembly (USAA further noted that the terminal ‘’ will also create jobs, open opportunities for small businesses and attract investment to Chikun and adjoining communities.’’
He noted that the terminal is not a stand-alone project but part of a wider transport vision that includes the Bus Rapid Transit (BRT) system, the planned Light Rail and the modernisation of motor parks across the state.
The USAA leader disclosed that the Kabala to Aliyu Makama Road and Bridge is a strategic corridor which was initially stalled since 2022 due to unpaid contractor certificates, unresolved compensation claims and utility relocation costs.
According to him, the present administration Inherited the project at about 30 percent completion, adding that ‘’Governor Uba Sani settled the outstanding obligations and remobilized contractors to site.’’
The aides noted that the historic Ahmadu Bello Stadium is being reconstructed and ‘’expanded from 16,000 to 33,000 seats, making it the second largest in Nigeria after the Moshood Abiola National Stadium. It will feature a hybrid football pitch and Olympic-standard facilities.’’
‘’The stadium will remain a national asset, open to national teams, federal sporting programmes and major events. Beyond sports, it is an economic investment that will attract tournaments and visitors, boost hotels, restaurants and transport services, create jobs for youths and restore Kaduna’s place as a centre of football and athletics,’’ Hon Mohammed noted.
He promised that the Assembly soon commence a statewide awareness campaign to sensitise citizens in all 23 local governments on the projects and their benefits, just he called on the electorate to renew their trust in the Governor and the All Progressives Congress (APC) to consolidate the gains achieved by the present administration.
“We will take this message to markets, villages, towns and communities, and we will ask our people to stand with a government that is delivering. Continuity is the surest way to consolidate these gains and build on them,” the Chairman added.

items.title: Bodies of Pakistanis killed in Somalia being repatriated, arrive in Addis Ababa: PMO
items.summary:
The bodies of three Pakistanis killed in an operation to recover a hijacked oil tanker off the Somali coast have reached Addis Ababa, with arrangements under way for their repatriation, the PMO said on Saturday
The Palau-flagged MT Honour 25, carrying 18,500 barrels of oil and a 17-member crew, including 10 Pakistanis, was seized on April 21, around 30 nautical miles off Puntland while sailing from Oman to Somalia. Puntland’s Maritime Police Force said it rescued the tanker in an operation off Dharin-baar, but the pirates opened fire on the hostages, killing five, including three Pakistanis and injuring four others.
According to the PMO statement, the bodies of Syed Kafeel Omar, Ahmad Ansari and Rafiullah had arrived in Ethiopia’s capital Addis Ababa, where Ethiopian Airlines staff were reviewing arrangements for their transfer to Pakistan.

items.author: Web Desk
items.content:
The bodies of three Pakistanis killed in an operation to recover a hijacked oil tanker off the Somali coast have reached Addis Ababa, with arrangements under way for their repatriation, the PMO said on Saturday
The Palau-flagged MT Honour 25, carrying 18,500 barrels of oil and a 17-member crew, including 10 Pakistanis, was seized on April 21, around 30 nautical miles off Puntland while sailing from Oman to Somalia. Puntland’s Maritime Police Force said it rescued the tanker in an operation off Dharin-baar, but the pirates opened fire on the hostages, killing five, including three Pakistanis and injuring four others.
According to the PMO statement, the bodies of Syed Kafeel Omar, Ahmad Ansari and Rafiullah had arrived in Ethiopia’s capital Addis Ababa, where Ethiopian Airlines staff were reviewing arrangements for their transfer to Pakistan.
Read: Three Pakistani sailors killed in Somali ship rescue operation
وزیراعظم محمد شہباز شریف کی ہدایت پر صومالیہ میں جاں بحق پاکستانیوں شہریوں کی میتوں کی پاکستان منتقلی کے انتظامات جاری ہیں. اس سلسلے میں جاں بحق پاکستانی شہریوں کی میتیں ایک گھنٹہ قبل ایتھوپیا کے دارالحکومت ادیس ابابا پہنچ گئی ہیں۔
ایتھوپین ایئرلائنز کا عملہ میتوں کی پاکستان…
— Prime Minister's Office (@PakPMO) October 3, 2026
The PMO said final approval would be granted for the bodies to be dispatched to Karachi once the necessary preparations had been completed.
In accordance with the prime minister’s directives, relevant officials were in constant contact to expedite the repatriation process, the statement said.
The prime minister had assured every possible assistance in bringing back the bodies of the three Pakistani citizens, according to the PMO.
It said PM Shehbaz had spoken by telephone on Friday with Izaan Kafeel, the son of deceased Syed Kafeel Omar, and expressed his condolences over the death of his father and assured him that the government would take all necessary measures to swiftly repatriate his body along with those of the other deceased Pakistanis.
Also Read: Four Pakistani crew members from hijacked MT Honour 25 to arrive in Karachi tomorrow: Dar
A day earlier, the prime minister announced financial assistance of Rs12.5 million for the families of each of the three Pakistanis killed during a Somali operation to rescue the crew from pirates.
He also announced free education and healthcare for the deceased’s children, while each bereaved family would be provided with a house.
The oil tanker Honour 25, sailing under the Somali flag from Oman to Somalia, was hijacked by pirates on April 21. There were 17 crew members aboard, 10 of them Pakistani nationals. The families of the Pakistani hostages spent months seeking the safe release of their loved ones, staging peaceful protests and repeatedly approaching government authorities.
During their captivity, the pirates initially demanded a ransom of $3 million, which was later reduced to $1.9 million and subsequently to $1 million. All the Pakistani crew members who were killed or injured were from different areas of Karachi.
The pirates came under pressure during a rescue operation and, while retreating from the vessel, opened indiscriminate fire on the abducted crew before fleeing the ship. Five sailors were killed, including three Pakistanis — Second Officer Kashif Umar, Third Engineer Mahmood Ansari and Boiler Rafiullah. The other two deceased crew members were an Indian sailor, Tanveer, and the chief engineer from Myanmar.
Four sailors were injured — Usman, Yasir, Ameen and Vicky from Indonesia — while Hussain Yousuf, Imran Ali and Yaseen remained safe. The two surviving Pakistani crew members later contacted the Ansar Burney Welfare Trust in Karachi using the ship captain’s mobile phone and provided details of the incident.
Puntland police said the Honour 25 had 18,500 barrels of oil on board when it was hijacked. The police had been pursuing three hijacked vessels off the Somali coast and had also rescued another oil tanker, Sibu 1, on Friday. However, 28 of the 41 pirates arrested during that operation later escaped while being transferred to jail, with several Puntland security officials accusing local police of complicity.
