items.author: ZAFAR BHUTTA
items.content:
The Cabinet Committee on Energy (CCOE) has directed the Power Division to take provinces on board in the operationalisation and implementation of the national Integrated Energy Plan (IEP).
During discussions in a recent meeting of the CCOE, it was noted that the IEP would be a 10-year plan with a 33-year perspective for the time horizon of 2027-2060. The forum was informed that the proposed governance framework would ensure coordination among federal and provincial stakeholders through the IEP steering committee, IEP Secretariat and sub-working groups, with policy oversight from the CCOE and the Council of Common Interests (CCI).
It was highlighted that responses from provinces were awaited despite a number of reminders and considerable lapse of time. It was also mentioned that representatives of all provincial governments and other stakeholders were present during the steering committee meeting.
The Ministry of Energy (Power Division) explained that the CCOE had approved the proposed Integrated Energy Planning Ecosystem, Secretariat Structure and High-Level Roadmap 2025 on December 24, 2025, with directives that the High-Level Design Report be developed and approved after comprehensive consultations with all relevant stakeholders. Accordingly, the Power Division completed the exercise and developed the IEP High-level Design after engaging in extensive nationwide consultations.
In the process, more than 50 stakeholders including international development partners, leading academic institutions, key ministries, provincial governments, regulatory authorities including Nepra and Ogra, and major energy-sector entities such as Wapda, Private Power and Infrastructure Board, Inter-State Gas Systems, PSO and K-Electric were consulted.
The CCOE appreciated the Ministry of Energy (Power Division) as well as all other stakeholders for having accomplished the task of preparing a national Integrated Energy Plan and expressed confidence that focused efforts of the minister of power and his team would lead to the transformation of Pakistan's power sector.
The Power Division apprised the CCOE that the High-Level Design was developed through extensive consultation, led by the IEP Secretariat, under the Ministry of Energy, and nationwide technical consultations were held with more than 50 federal and provincial stakeholders.
The division added that subsequently the draft High-Level Design, after incorporating the feedback received during consultations, was presented to the IEP steering committee for review and strategic guidance. The steering committee's feedback and recommendations were incorporated into the finalised High-Level Design Report.
The Ministry of Energy (Power Division) emphasised that the IEP High-Level Design "establishes the strategic, analytical and governance framework for developing a comprehensive national Integrated Energy Plan". Key elements of the plan are explicated as follows:
Analytical framework: It is structured around four interdependent pillars: energy (adequate, reliable and resilient supply); economics (competitive and financially sustainable); equity (inclusive and accessible energy transition); and environment (sustainable, low-carbon and climate-resilient future).
The plan covers both demand and supply sides of Pakistan's energy system, integrating infrastructure planning across the energy value chain. IEP is spread over the period 2027-2060, comprising a 10-year action plan.
Governance framework: It ensures coordination among federal and provincial stakeholders through the IEP steering committee, IEP Secretariat and sub-working groups, with policy oversight from the CCOE and the CCI.
The IEP steering committee, chaired by ministers of power and petroleum, is responsible for the development of IEP strategic oversight and reviews progress before submission to the CCOE and the CCI.
The IEP Secretariat, led by the Ministry of Energy (Power and Petroleum Divisions) and the Ministry of Planning, Development and Special Incentives, serves as the central coordinating body responsible for stakeholder engagement, analytical work and development of the IEP and Energy Information System (EIS), supported by sub-working groups comprising federal and provincial stakeholders providing technical input on different IEP activities.
The Power Division sought authorisation for the IEP Secretariat to proceed with the development of the EIS and directives to all relevant ministries/departments and organisations to support and integrate data systems to develop the EIS.

items.content:
Short-term inflation stayed in double digits for the week ended October 1, with the Sensitive Price Indicator (SPI) up 11.53% from a year earlier, as the energy shock from the US-Israel war with Iran continued to pass into household costs.
The Pakistan Bureau of Statistics (PBS) said the SPI rose 0.21% week-on-week to 370.46 points, from 369.69 a week earlier. The yearly pace eased from 11.92% in the previous reading, but remained well above single digits.
The conflict, which has disrupted shipping through the Strait of Hormuz since early 2026, is still visible in the annual fuel bill. Diesel is 44.50% dearer than a year ago at Rs402.53 a litre and petrol is up 44.05% at Rs389.51.
Liquefied petroleum gas, widely used for cooking, rose 1.17% in the week to Rs5,103 for an 11.67kg cylinder, and was 66.59% higher than last October. Electricity charges for Q1 were up 58.59% on the year.
There was some relief at the pump. Diesel fell 3.43% and petrol 0.65% over the week, in line with a partial recovery in crude flows, even as supply of refined products remained tight.
Food showed a split picture. Chicken jumped 7.25% in the week to Rs365.31 a kilogramme and was 13.60% higher than a year ago. Garlic rose 1.85%, gram pulse 1.30% and eggs 0.72%.
Onions, up only 0.39% in the week, were 114.20% costlier than a year earlier at Rs189.42 a kilogramme. Wheat flour was up 32.65%, with a 20kg bag at Rs2,697. Mutton was 15.07% higher, beef 12.90% and fresh milk 8.10%.
Offsets came from perishables and sweeteners. Tomatoes were 45.52% cheaper than last year, potatoes 39.54% and sugar 21.95%. Eggs, despite the weekly rise, remained 17.47% below last October.
Of the 51 items tracked in 50 markets across 17 cities, prices of 20 rose, 10 fell and 21 were unchanged. The burden was uneven. The lowest spending group saw a 0.19% weekly rise and a 9% annual increase. The highest quintile recorded an 11.99% year-on-year hike, against 11.53% for the combined index.
It is pertinent to mention that the monthly Consumer Price Index (CPI) rose 10.3% year-on-year in September 2026, which was lower than the increase of 11.1% year-on-year in August.

items.author: Our Correspondent
items.content:
The Central Development Working Party (CDWP) has approved seven foreign-funded development projects for Sindh covering water supply and sanitation, education, irrigation, property revenue enhancement, environmental sustainability and urban infrastructure.
The projects, approved on October 2, carry combined foreign financing of $895 million, besides a major irrigation project estimated at Rs50.99 billion. The largest initiative is the Sindh Transformational Accelerated Rural Water Supply, Sanitation and Hygiene (STAR WASH) Services Phase-I Project, with a total financing of $450 million. The project comprises a $300 million World Bank financing and a $150 million Asian Development Bank (ADB) component and seeks to improve water supply, sanitation and hygiene services in rural areas of Sindh.
The CDWP also approved $15 million in Project Readiness Financing (PRF) for preparing urban and water-sector projects in Sindh. The initiative falls under the Local Government, Housing & Town Planning Department and is aimed at developing projects for future financing and implementation.
Another major project is the Sindh Property Revenue Enhancement Programme (Sindh PREP), supported by a $150 million World Bank financing. The programme, also under the Local Government, Housing & Town Planning Department, is designed to strengthen property revenue systems in the province.
In the education sector, the CDWP approved the $150 million Sindh Early Learning Enhancement Project through Classroom Transformation (SELECT-II), financed by the World Bank. The project will focus on improving early learning outcomes through classroom transformation under the School Education & Literacy Department.
The Sindh Secondary Education Improvement Project – Second Additional Financing was also approved. The project includes a $100 million ADB loan and a $10 million grant to support improvements in secondary education across the province.
Meanwhile, the Pakistan Finance for Lowering Emissions in the Water Sector (PAK-FLOW) project received approval for $20 million in World Bank financing. The initiative aims to reduce emissions in the water sector while supporting environmental sustainability.
The seventh project involves the Water Requirement for K-IV Project, specifically improvement of the Kalari Baghar Feeder and Keenjhar Lake. It includes cement-concrete lining of the Kalari Baghar Feeder Upper Phase-I at an estimated cost of Rs50,989 million and falls under the Sindh Irrigation Department.

items.author: editorial
items.content:
Despite hopes for a thaw amid the widening Middle East conflict, the Houthis' surge is acting as a spanner in the works. Reports that the pro-Iran Yemeni militia launched drone attacks on an electricity facility in the holy city of Medina have taken the Muslim world by surprise, pushing the regional security paradigm to the edge. Likewise, unconfirmed reports indicate that American authorities are investigating potential Iranian links to a thwarted midair insider attack on a Flydubai airliner en route to Tel Aviv. This, too, has upped the ante, with US warning of a severe backlash against Iran. Finally, an unannounced, lethal conflict between Yemeni state security forces and the Houthis is hampering navigation across the strategic Bab-el-Mandeb waterway, escalating Saudi Arabia's security risks to unprecedented heights.
This escalation on the part of the Houthis is uncalled for. The non-state actor is unnecessarily expanding the orbit of war, inviting retribution with dire consequences for the entire region. Loud explosions were also heard in the Yemeni capital, Sanaa, which is controlled by Houthi forces. This indicates that the Iranians, too, are engaged in a power struggle, using proxies as leverage for realpolitik. Furthermore, the prospective withdrawal of US troops from Iraq and Syria, paired with Washington's positioning as an ally of Saudi Arabia, represents a new twist in regional dynamics. Moreover, the US deployment of additional Patriot missile batteries to Saudi Arabia and Qatar and the Pentagon signing a massive contract for the production of SM-6 missiles are clear signs of broadening warfare.
The million-dollar question is: where are statecraft and diplomacy? Why do they take a backseat every second day? Why are the Pentagon and the IRGC so obsessed with warmongering while their respective diplomatic echelons strive for a thaw in all sincerity? It is a fact that non-state actors are a reality in the Middle East power dynamics, but the Houthis are going over the brink as spoilers. Tehran has a responsibility to prevail over the Houthis and ensure that Saudi Arabia's territorial integrity is not breached.

items.author: editorial
items.content:
The internet has become an ordinary part of childhood, but the protections surrounding young users remain anything but ordinary. A new Kaspersky analysis offers a revealing picture of where Pakistani children are spending their time online. During the first eight months of 2026, YouTube accounted for 31.2% of their mobile app activity, followed by Instagram at 18.8% and WhatsApp at 17.4%. Multiplayer games and platforms such as Roblox and Discord also featured prominently in their digital lives.
Such spaces offer entertainment and companionship. The concern is that the same features that make them attractive to young users also make them accessible to people seeking to deceive or exploit them. Multiplayer games allow strangers to communicate directly with children. Phishing links can arrive disguised as offers of free game currency or rewards, while friendships formed online can gradually become vehicles for grooming or blackmail. The scale of the problem in Pakistan is already difficult to dismiss. Research released by UNICEF, ECPAT International and Interpol last month found that nearly one in 16 internet-using Pakistanis between the ages of 12 and 17 had experienced some form of technology-facilitated sexual exploitation or abuse within a year. That translates into roughly 1.5 million children. The research also found that fear, stigma and possible repercussions within the family often discourage victims from seeking help. AI is making an already difficult problem more complicated. Across an 11-country study, at least 1.2 million children reported having their images manipulated into sexually explicit deepfakes during the preceding years.
Children will not retreat from the digital world, nor should they be expected to. The task is to make that world safer for them. As technology becomes better at creating convincing falsehoods and predators become more adept at exploiting trust, Pakistan's safeguards must evolve just as quickly. Connectivity without protection leaves children carrying risks they are too young to manage alone.

items.content:
Punjab's launch of 33 mobile police stations, including six dedicated "Pink" units for women, seems like a good attempt to make it easier for citizens to approach law enforcement authorities. The initiative offers 14 services, from FIR registration to driving licences, and will visit different neighbourhoods, along with universities and colleges, on fixed schedules. This will be of great benefit for anyone who has to get some work done at a police station, but especially for women, who have long hesitated to enter male-dominated police stations to report harassment or domestic violence and may find women's police stations too hard to reach. By saving time and travel costs for citizens in remote areas, the scheme could genuinely bridge the public-police divide.
But the biggest problem for the Punjab Police is not accessibility. It is the Punjab Police. The law enforcers are notorious for corruption within the ranks. Almost 85,000 complaints were lodged against the force in the first seven months of this year, with nearly 15,000 centred on corruption and bribery. Surveys consistently rank Punjab Police as Pakistan's most corrupt provincial department. Mobile stations may make it easier to file a report, but if the underlying culture of impunity - where cases are refused registration and investigations are botched for a price - remains untouched, the vans will merely become new venues for old abuses.
Critics will also question the cost. The 33 units require vehicles, technology and specialised staff, all funded by taxpayers. While the benefits could potentially be huge, that is still an assumption. The expenditure is already a fact. To ensure the taxpayer gets value for money, the exercise needs genuine accountability, with merit-based hiring and staffing and independent oversight.
The mobile police stations could be of great value, but that value can only be realised if provincial leaders in parliament and at the Central Police Office recognise that no fleet of vans can substitute for the difficult work of reforming the institution.

items.author: Farrukh Khan Pitafi
items.content:
Last week, when the story of the centralisation of electoral rolls in India and the arbitrary deletion of voters broke, the name of Dr Seema Khanna was propelled into the limelight. Today, as Director General of Information Technology at the Election Commission of India, she oversees ECINet, which journalist Ritika Chopra revealed centralises voter rolls and bypasses decentralised statutory officers.
Her name is not unknown to those who covered the union government's response to the Covid crisis. She oversaw the rapid development and deployment of Aarogya Setu. Deployed by executive decree without statutory safeguards, the tool harvested sensitive health records and mapped citizens' private social networks. Critics warned that vacuuming up medical history and social interactions without privacy laws normalised permanent state surveillance under the cover of a public health crisis.
Of course, you can argue that this speaks to her competence. But as I keep reminding you, competence only compounds the severity of an offence. She cannot plead ignorance to rationalise locking out on-ground Electoral Registration Officers, preventing them from executing statutory duties.
I know, I know, the harvesting of health records and social context is an even graver issue. Consider the warning of UK judge Sir Nicolas Browne-Wilkinson in the 1992 Marcel case: "If the information obtained by the police, the Inland Revenue, the social security offices, the health service and other agencies were to be gathered together in one file, the freedom of the individual would be gravely at risk. The dossier of private information is the badge of the totalitarian state."
The dossier of private information should worry any citizen in any given country. But weigh it against two compounding factors: In which country is this happening? And in which technological age is it happening?
Country first. Last week, when I showed you how Shudra identity is being systematically dissolved, it did not mean their names are already being purged from electoral rolls, nor that prejudice against them has vanished. Their overt targeting is simply deferred until after a Hindu Rashtra is consolidated. Like slow-boiling frogs, right now, they are led to believe that the rising temperature is meant exclusively for Muslims, minorities, Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes, an intoxicating illusion of "Hindu consolidation" that masks their own gradual erasure.
Yet, while the word "Shudra" has practically been scrubbed from polite public discourse, the ironclad mandate of endogamy has not. Open any newspaper matrimonial page and the obsession with wedding within one's varna stares back at you. When social prejudice cannot be sanctioned by law, it retreats into an unspoken shadow ledger of social rating. India is the textbook case. Consider how many instances of Pratiloma violence, inter-caste honour killings, are sanitised in police registers as random murders or suicides. Even though the constitutional state claims to view its citizens as equals, society does not. Use your imagination: what happens when such a dossier of private information is handed to a centralised state apparatus captured by an entrenched upper-caste elite?
Now consider the age. Only a decade ago, the Cambridge Analytica scandal revealed how mere social media breadcrumbs could be weaponised: first to build psychographic profiles of individual citizens, and then to push their psychological buttons to manipulate democratic outcomes. Technology has not stood still. It has accelerated exponentially since then.
Rukmini S's Whole Numbers and Half Truths reveals a terrifying reality: the ground-level data feeding this surveillance machine is inherently prejudiced. When police manipulate FIRs to classify inter-caste marriages as kidnappings, or municipal clerks miss rural deaths, they hardcode bias and incompetence into the system. Sucked into national registries, this flawed data is laundered into objective truth, weaponised by algorithms to deny welfare and profile citizens under an illusion of infallibility.
The rollout of the surveillance state started ostensibly with great innocence in 2009 when the Unique Identification Authority of India, led by Nandan Nilekani, introduced Aadhaar. Stated as a benevolent tool to plug welfare leakages, it instead created the master architectural key. Tethering biological markers (facial photograph, scans of both irises and ten fingerprints) to a twelve-digit number stripped citizens of anonymity, anchoring all future dossiers.
By 2013, the intellectual engine room moved to Bengaluru with the formation of the Indian Software Product Industry Round Table, or iSPIRT, co-founded by Sharad Sharma. This think tank engineered the India Stack. Where Silicon Valley pioneered surveillance capitalism for advertising, Bengaluru adapted these tools into surveillance statecraft, building the plumbing to monitor, categorise and manage a population.
Between 2014 and 2015, the vision accelerated through the Jan Dhan, Aadhaar and Mobile trinity. Sold for direct benefit transfers, JAM served as a digital enclosure, soldering biological identity, communication trails and banking ledgers. The sledgehammer of 2016 followed. Demonetisation corralled the cash economy onto digital rails, paving the way for the Unified Payments Interface. UPI eliminated the privacy of the informal bazaar, logging transactions to map financial behaviour in real time.
Between 2017 and 2019, the architecture leapt to algorithmic governance. Using Telangana's Samagra Vedika as a testing ground, algorithms fused isolated departmental databases into a single predictive profile without citizen consent. This laid the foundation for the National Social Registry, a 360-degree database tracking every life event, resulting in algorithms silently cancelling pensions.
The 2020 Covid crisis justified completing the biological ledger through Aarogya Setu, developed by the National Informatics Centre with Dr Seema Khanna overseeing operations. Evolving into the Ayushman Bharat Digital Mission, it converted a temporary epidemic response into permanent biological surveillance.
Now consider this. Nandan Nilekani and Sharad Sharma are Brahmin. Seema Khanna a Khatri. All movers and shakers of iSPIRT belong to the upper castes. The totalitarian state's panopticon is ready and actively being deployed. How it is used after safeguards of a secular state and constitution are removed does not require much imagination.
This raises a final question about Western media, international wire services, search engines and news aggregators. They never tire of spotlighting Chinese security measures, yet this story rarely reaches your screens. We will need another piece to explore exactly why. Stay tuned.

items.author: Imtiaz Gul
items.content:
Pakistan's "well-planned and calibrated" airstrikes against terrorist hideouts inside Afghanistan, described as a continuation of Operation Ghazab Lil Haq, reflect an escalating pattern of unilateral military action in response to TTP- and BLA-linked violence inside the country. Pakistani officials claim these strikes have eliminated dozens, if not hundreds, of militants operating from cross-border sanctuaries.
Officials describe this approach as "unavoidable", with the implied objective of compelling the Kabul regime to take demonstrable action against terrorist groups targeting Pakistan. The closure of border crossings for almost a year is also rooted in the same rationale. Official messaging increasingly suggests that relations with Afghanistan have reached a "point of no return" because of Kabul's alleged failure to rein in violent groups operating from its territory.
However justified Pakistan's counterterrorism responses may be, they carry a costly consequence: deepening hostility with the rulers in Kabul, an endless cycle of mutual accusations and little prospect of an end to daily violence. This exposes a structural flaw in the current policy: every military or militant action triggers reciprocal accusations, further erodes trust and narrows the space for cooperative solutions.
Historical evidence from Vietnam, Afghanistan (both for the US and the former Soviet Union), and Iraq (for the US and UK) suggests that military action can temporarily suppress violence and create space for other measures. Yet, durable outcomes depend heavily on political legitimacy, local ownership, economic opportunity and addressing underlying grievances.
Counterinsurgency doctrine emphasises "clear, hold and build", yet the "build" phase - governance, public services and a sustainable political settlement - has often proved the most difficult.
China's approach in its Muslim-majority Xinjiang region illustrates a different, highly integrated model combining strict security and law-enforcement measures, large-scale deradicalisation and vocational training programmes, as well as substantial economic investment, infrastructure development, poverty alleviation and improved public services. Chinese official data and statements report an absence of major violent terrorist incidents for several years, often dating this trend to around 2017. They also cite a substantial increase in the public's sense of security, from the high 80 per cent range a decade earlier to over 99 per cent in some surveys, alongside the elimination of extreme poverty, significant GDP growth and expanded access to education, healthcare and connectivity.
China, as the sovereign authority with a monopoly over the use of force, extensive control over the public narrative and considerable resources, implemented an integrated strategy involving coercion, ideological re-education and development. Unlike external interventions, this approach operated within a different political and institutional framework, without comparable democratic or legal constraints. It enabled the rapid suppression of violence and produced measurable economic and security gains according to official indicators, although concerns over human rights, coercive practices and restrictions on civil liberties remain central to international assessments of the policy.
Pakistan's own kinetic operations in Swat, Waziristan and Khyber, including Operation Zarb-e-Azb in 2014 and subsequent nationwide efforts such as Radd-ul-Fasaad, also achieved significant tactical successes. Militants were dislodged from key strongholds, large numbers were killed, violence declined sharply for a period in the mid-to-late 2010s, and state authority was re-established in areas previously lost to militant groups.
However, the "hold and build" approach has remained largely confined to the "hold" phase. Reconstruction has been slow, improvements in public service delivery limited, and governance gaps persistent, particularly in the former tribal districts. Socioeconomic grievances, weak institutions and limited economic opportunities continue to provide fertile ground for militant recruitment, the survival of ideological networks and the regeneration of sanctuaries. The Taliban's return to power in Afghanistan in August 2021 has further complicated this landscape.
It is, therefore, hardly surprising that violence in Pakistan has resurged and that Islamabad has been unable to persuade the Afghan Taliban to meet its demands for decisive action against the TTP.
The lesson from Pakistan's kinetic campaigns, both at home and across the border, is that force can create temporary security, disrupt militant networks and buy time. But without sustained efforts to establish legitimate governance, deliver responsive public services, expand economic opportunities and ensure political inclusion, the underlying problems persist, recur or mutate into new forms.
Force is often necessary, but it is rarely sufficient. Sustainable solutions require addressing the material and political conditions that allow militancy to take root, while recognising that identity, ideology and external support networks complicate any purely technical fix based on governance and development. Outcomes depend heavily on local context, institutional capacity, political legitimacy and the willingness to move beyond narrowly defined kinetic measures of success.
Pakistan now faces a double whammy: an indigenous militancy rooted in local grievances, including human rights and governance concerns, alongside cross-border and proxy-linked terrorism. This complex challenge requires minimising the factors that fuel non-state agendas while countering external drivers of violence. Counterterrorism demands a coordinated, indiscriminate and sustained whole-of-government approach that targets militant sanctuaries, strengthens local institutions and combines security operations with political engagement and development.
A policy centred predominantly on military pressure and border restrictions risks adding further layers of animosity and discontent on both sides of the divide. The real challenge for Islamabad and Kabul is to break this cycle through a combination of credible security guarantees, sustained dialogue, effective governance and a shared commitment to preventing their territories from being used for violence against each other.

Amazon also claims books open 30% faster than on the previous-generation Kindle. The power button has moved to the right side, while battery life is rated at up to six weeks.
The 16GB Ube and Graphite models start at $150, while the 32GB aluminum-backed versions cost $190.

items.title: Shopify Launches Canvas, an AI Tool That Builds Stores From Chat
items.summary:
Shopify has launched Canvas, a new AI-powered website builder that lets merchants create and edit online stores by chatting with the company’s Sidekick assistant.
Previously, Shopify’s no-code tools allowed merchants to customize themes by rearranging sections and blocks. More advanced changes often required editing code or hiring a developer.
Canvas is designed to reduce that need by letting users describe what they want in natural language.
Builds the Store in Real Time
As Sidekick makes changes, Canvas renders the actual store in real time.
Shopify says this is not a static preview. Canvas displays the real code behind the storefront, allowing merchants to test animations, interactions and layouts as they would appear on the live site.
Users can also switch between different screen sizes to see how the store will look across devices.
Sidekick takes screenshots of the interface while working so it can see the same version of the store that the merchant sees.
&&&&&
items.author: Afaq Wajdan Malik
items.content:
Shopify has launched Canvas, a new AI-powered website builder that lets merchants create and edit online stores by chatting with the company’s Sidekick assistant.
Previously, Shopify’s no-code tools allowed merchants to customize themes by rearranging sections and blocks. More advanced changes often required editing code or hiring a developer.
Canvas is designed to reduce that need by letting users describe what they want in natural language.
Builds the Store in Real Time
As Sidekick makes changes, Canvas renders the actual store in real time.
Shopify says this is not a static preview. Canvas displays the real code behind the storefront, allowing merchants to test animations, interactions and layouts as they would appear on the live site.
Users can also switch between different screen sizes to see how the store will look across devices.
Sidekick takes screenshots of the interface while working so it can see the same version of the store that the merchant sees.
&&&&&&&
Users Can Still Edit Manually
Merchants are not limited to chat commands.
Canvas still allows users to click individual elements and make changes directly, while also offering zoom and pan controls for navigating the full storefront.
Sidekick itself is not new. Shopify has already used the assistant for writing code, building apps, customizing themes and making other store changes.
Canvas brings those capabilities together into a dedicated site-building environment.
Shopify Changed Its Theme Architecture
To make Canvas possible, Shopify gave Sidekick direct access to theme files and simplified the underlying theme architecture.
The company says this makes a store’s structure, logic, and design easier for the AI to understand and modify.
Several Features Are Still Missing
Canvas is still in an early stage and currently works only on desktop.
At launch, it does not support third-party themes, app blocks and extensions, Markets, translations, rollouts or theme updates.
Shopify says it plans to add support for those areas over time.
Canvas joins a growing number of AI-powered site-building tools from companies including Wix, Squarespace, Webflow and Framer, as well as newer vibe-coding platforms such as Lovable and Replit.

items.title: Govt Ends 60% Permanent Vacant Jobs
items.summary:
The federal government has decided to abolish permanent government posts that have remained vacant for one year or longer.
According to a notification issued by the Controller General of Accounts (CGA), 60 percent of such vacant posts will be abolished.
However, posts that became vacant due to transfers, postings or promotions will not be abolished under the decision.
The posts being abolished will be removed from the quotas allocated for initial recruitment and direct recruitment.
All concerned accounts offices have been directed to prepare new vacancy rosters in line with the decision.
The authorities have also been instructed to process promotion cases according to the revised vacancy position.

items.title: OpenAI Adds Virtual Try-On and Favorites to ChatGPT Shopping
items.summary:
OpenAI has launched two new shopping features for ChatGPT globally, adding a virtual try-on tool and a Favorites feature to help users shop more easily.
The update expands ChatGPT’s role in online shopping as AI companies continue testing consumer-focused features in this category.
Virtual Try-On Comes to ChatGPT
The new virtual try-on feature allows users to upload a selfie or full-body photo to see how clothing or accessories might look on them.
The option will appear as a new “Try On” button in ChatGPT’s shopping results.
Users can also upload an image of an item, such as a screenshot from the web, and ask ChatGPT to show how it would look when worn.
OpenAI said the feature is powered by its recently launched ChatGPT Images 2.5 model, which the company says offers more natural lighting, richer textures, more reliable editing and lower image generation latency.
Favorites Lets Users Save Products
The second new feature, Favorites, allows users to save products they discover in ChatGPT
items.author: Afaq Wajdan Malik
items.content:
OpenAI has launched two new shopping features for ChatGPT globally, adding a virtual try-on tool and a Favorites feature to help users shop more easily.
The update expands ChatGPT’s role in online shopping as AI companies continue testing consumer-focused features in this category.
Virtual Try-On Comes to ChatGPT
The new virtual try-on feature allows users to upload a selfie or full-body photo to see how clothing or accessories might look on them.
The option will appear as a new “Try On” button in ChatGPT’s shopping results.
Users can also upload an image of an item, such as a screenshot from the web, and ask ChatGPT to show how it would look when worn.
OpenAI said the feature is powered by its recently launched ChatGPT Images 2.5 model, which the company says offers more natural lighting, richer textures, more reliable editing and lower image generation latency.
Favorites Lets Users Save Products
The second new feature, Favorites, allows users to save products they discover in ChatGPT to a Library for later viewing.
According to OpenAI, saved items will appear alongside users’ virtual try-on images inside the app.
Broader Push Into Shopping
OpenAI said ChatGPT can also assist shopping in other ways.
For example, users can describe a style they want and ask ChatGPT to find items to build that look. They can also upload photos of celebrity outfits and ask the chatbot to identify similar items available for purchase.
That pushes ChatGPT further into a space already occupied by platforms like Google and Pinterest, especially in fashion discovery and visual shopping.
Shopping Remains an Experimental Area
The update comes as OpenAI continues experimenting with how ChatGPT can support shopping.
The company had previously tested an instant checkout feature, but later moved away from that idea after it failed to perform well.
The broader AI shopping market is also seeing mixed reactions. While some companies are promoting proactive product recommendations, not all users have welcomed those efforts.
Whether ChatGPT becomes a preferred shopping tool for users remains uncertain, particularly as competitors like Google have already introduced virtual try-on features.

items.title: Issues Tinubu Left Out In 66th Independence Day Speech
items.summary:
Nigeria marked its 66th Independence Anniversary on Thursday, October 1, 2026.
President Bola Ahmed Tinubu, who returned to the country on Tuesday after a four-week vacation in Europe, delivered his address to Nigerians in commemoration of the important event.

FLASHBACK: In December, Tinubu vowed to terminate rollover of budgets
Nigerians await cheaper fares
Daily Trust takes a look at some major issues that were either not discussed or were brief
items.author: Rilwan Muhammad
items.content:
Nigeria marked its 66th Independence Anniversary on Thursday, October 1, 2026.
President Bola Ahmed Tinubu, who returned to the country on Tuesday after a four-week vacation in Europe, delivered his address to Nigerians in commemoration of the important event.
Like last year, Tinubu’s administration had skipped the traditional Independence Day ceremonial military parade and opted for a low-key celebration which included nationwide Presidential broadcast, public lecture and religious services.
In his Independence Day broadcast, the President listed what he described as economic gains and other achievements recorded under his administration, saying the government’s central economic objective had now shifted from correcting the country’s economic course to achieving “shared and widespread prosperity.”
FLASHBACK: In December, Tinubu vowed to terminate rollover of budgets
Nigerians await cheaper fares
Daily Trust takes a look at some major issues that were either not discussed or were briefly mentioned in the President’s broadcast.
Insecurity
Although the President acknowledged the efforts of security forces in tackling insecurity in the country, he did not specifically speak about the rising wave of killings, kidnappings and attacks on communities across the country.
“We are grateful for the men and women of our Armed Forces and security services who place themselves in harm’s way so that the rest of us may live in peace.” Tinubu had said.
This is as several media reports indicated that more than 800 people were kidnapped in the last three months and several others killed in different attacks across the country.
According to Civil society organisations (CSOs) and the National Human Rights Commission (NHRC), more than 34,000 Nigerians have been killed in incidents linked to mass atrocities within the last five years.
The groups disclosed this during a Conflict-Specific Dialogue (CSD) held in Abuja on Thursday, May 28, 2026, where they called on authorities to stem the tide of rising insecurity in the country.
On Monday, just three days to the 66th Independence Day, parents and community members of Mussa and Lassa in Askira/Uba Local Government Area of Borno State threatened to storm the Presidential Villa in Abuja within six days if their abducted children were not rescued from Boko Haram captivity.
In August, scores of worshipers were killed after gunmen attacked four mosques in Borgu Local Government Area of Niger State.
The State Governor, Mohammed Umaru Bago, reportedly put the number of the abducted persons at 33, a figure the affected communities contradicted, releasing the names of 547 worshipers kidnapped during the attacks on Mosques in Dekara District.
Communities in Sokoto, Zamfara, Katsina, Benue, Borno, Plateau have continued to lament the rising spate of killings and abductions in their respective areas.
Cheaper transportation fares
President Tinubu had on August 27, after a meeting with governors, said the government would take steps that would crash transportation cost across the nation to cushion the effect of harsh economic conditions in the country.
Acknowledging the rising cost of intra-state transportation, the President said he had directed additional rollout of another 500 CNG refuelling stations across the country in addition to the 500 stations ordered earlier this year, bringing the number to 1,000 stations.
A few weeks after the promise, Tinubu, while giving an update on the promise for cheaper transportation from October 1, 2026, claimed that the initiative had already started yielding results, with Nigerians, according to him, now enjoying cheaper fares.
But many Nigerians have countered the President’s claims, saying the transportation fares have not reduced.
Although the President said in the broadcast that his administration’s priority was to bring down the cost of living by lowering the cost of production and transportation, he did not specifically provide evidence to back his claim that Nigerians have started enjoying cheaper transportation fares.
Subsidy savings
Since the removal of fuel subsidy by Tinubu during his inauguration, many Nigerians have continued to bear the brunt of the action, although the President has repeatedly defended the policy and warned that returning to the subsidy regime could take the country backwards.
In August 2026, the Federal Government said the removal of the petrol subsidy and the liberalisation of the naira had generated N15.8 trillion in savings for the federation between June 2023 and December 2025.
The Minister of Finance and Coordinating Minister of the Economy, Taiwo Oyedele, said the money saved from the reforms has created additional fiscal space for governments to fund critical programmes, pay workers and pensioners, invest in infrastructure, support vulnerable Nigerians and expand access to credit.
The President, in his broadcast, maintained that the reforms embarked upon by his administration (including subsidy removal on fuel) were necessary steps to strengthen the country’s economy.
“Our reforms did not create the weaknesses in our economy. They confronted them. Now, as certain influential but regressive voices would have us abandon the treatment and return ourselves to the abuse of addictive subsidies, we must resist their siren song. We must remember why we began this journey and how far we have already come.”
He, however, did not discuss the breakdown of the savings, where they had gone or how they had been invested to bring about improvement in the quality of life of Nigerians.
Electricity, Energy
During the 2023 presidential campaign, Tinubu had reportedly declared, “If I don’t give you constant electricity in four years, don’t vote for me for a second term.”
In March 2026, the Nigerian Independent System Operator (NISO) said the continued decline in electricity generation on the national grid as a result of persistent gas supply constraints was affecting several thermal power plants in the country.
In a statement, NISO said as at 05:00 hours of Thursday, 5th March 2026, total generation on the national grid stood at 3,940.53 MW, which was below the expected capacity, due to existing gas supply limitations impacting a number of generating stations.
According to the Nigerian Electricity Regulatory Commission (NERC), Nigeria’s 28 electricity power plants have a combined capacity to produce 13,625 megawatts (MW) of electricity but due to some challenges, an average of 5,395.72MW is produced per hour.
This means that more than 8,000MW of generation capacity lay idle across the 28 electricity generation companies connected to the national grid.
This is amid growing concerns among Nigerians over the rising cost of electricity and its stability.
The President, in his October 1, 2026 address, said gas would be used to power new industries
“We will use our gas to power new industries. We will support businesses that work to bring factories back to life in our great industrial centres.” Tinubu had said.
He, however, did not give detailed strategies or measures that the administration would adopt to ensure reduction in electricity costs and improving supply to households and businesses.
Borrowing, debt burden
The President also spoke about how, under his administration, the foreign reserves have been rebuilt and foreign exchange market stabilised, with the country recording, according to him, its highest revenue from non-oil exports in 2025.
“Oil theft is down. Inflation has fallen substantially from its peak. Our foreign reserves have been rebuilt, our foreign exchange market has stabilised, and in 2025, this country recorded its highest revenue from non-oil exports in its history, exceeding $6 billion. This is real money being made by real Nigerian businesses.” he had said.
However, the President did not explain how that could be used to service the country’s existing debts.
Daily Trust had reported that the Federal Government was seeking $1.5bn in fresh financing from the World Bank to enhance social protection, improve early childhood development and scale up climate-resilient interventions, amid concerns over Nigeria’s total public debt hitting N166.79tn.
What Nigerians say about the broadcast
Presidential Candidate of the African Democratic Congress (ADC), Atiku Abubakar, on Thursday tackled Tinubu for declaring that Nigeria has entered an “age of prosperity”.
‎
‎The former Vice President, in his Independence Day address delivered in Abuja on Thursday, said millions of Nigerians are still struggling with food, transport, healthcare, insecurity and other challenges.
‎“Today, Bola Tinubu told us that the ‘emergency treatment is over’ and the ‘age of prosperity’ has begun,” Atiku said.
‎
‎“A President may announce a new chapter in a speech. He cannot announce food onto a family’s table or money into a worker’s pocket.
“Bola, where is this prosperity?”
‎Atiku said the President’s claim about drop in inflation did not reflect the realities on ground as prices of essential commodities continue to soar.
‎‎
‎“Bola says inflation has fallen. A slower rise in prices does not restore what families have lost,” he said.
A former Minister of Youth and Sports, Solomon Dalung, described Tinubu’s Independence Day broadcast as disappointing, saying it failed to give clear account of the achievements recorded by the administration since its assumption of office in 2023.
Dalung, who spoke on Thursday during his appearance on Channels Television, said the President should have given Nigerians accountability.
He added that Tinubu should have used the opportunity to discuss, in broader perspective, issues such as insecurity, agriculture, economy, unemployment, hunger, poverty and Nigeria’s foreign policy.
“Because I think a speech by the president at our 66th anniversary—and he said three and a half years in office—should have concentrated more on giving Nigerians accountability; show concrete successes recorded so far by the reforms in the last three and a half years.
“But all that the president has done was to tell Nigeria the same stories: ‘Oh, be patient and expect our reforms will yield.”
Commenting on the President’s cancer metaphor, Dalung said, “The question is, when shall the cancer victim recover? Because it does appear that the surgery has put him in a coma.”
He added, “So if we have recorded 4% economic growth, how has that been able to affect an average Nigerian? Because it has to be translated into putting something before the ordinary Nigerians.”
Further picking holes in the speech as not having addressed the issue of insecurity, Lalung cited Plateau as one of the states already running what he called full-blown war.
“Plateau State, for example, we are already running a full-blown war, because every day there is one attack or the other. Every day there are mass burials, so we are at war,” he said.
A social media commentator, Muhammad Al-amin Usman, also faulted the broadcast, saying it failed to dwell on key challenges affecting Nigerians, especially insecurity.

items.author: Abdulyassar Abdulhamid
items.content:
The Jigawa State Government has converted 1,200 former J-TEACH personnel to permanent and pensionable status and recruited additional 820 youths under the J-TEACH programme as part of efforts to address teacher shortages across the state.
The state government also distributed 450 bicycles donated by Guaranty Trust Bank (GTB) to pupils and students who travel long distances to schools in hard-to-reach communities.
Governor Umar Namadi disclosed this on Friday while presenting appointment letters to beneficiaries and handing over the bicycles at the Banquet Hall, Government House, Dutse.
Namadi said the appointments were designed to address inherited gaps in pupil-teacher and student-teacher ratios, particularly in underserved rural communities.
Outrage as Patient dies after police stopped ambulance for minster’s convoy
Ensuring city resilience
He said the 2,020 beneficiaries comprised 1,200 former J-TEACH personnel who had successfully completed the required training and selection process and 820 newly recruited personnel joining the programme.
According to him, the initiative was not only aimed at strengthening the teaching workforce but also at creating jobs and sustainable livelihoods for qualified young people in the state.
The governor said the intervention complemented recent government efforts in the education sector, including the distribution of school uniforms, bags and writing materials to thousands of learners across the state.
He stressed that education remained central to his administration’s vision for a “Greater Jigawa”, noting that quality education was essential for individuals and communities to prosper in an increasingly technology-driven world.
“Investments in classrooms, furniture, instructional materials, technology and school governance must be matched by enough qualified, motivated and properly supported teachers,” he said.
Namadi said his administration had deliberately expanded the teaching workforce since 2023 through the J-TEACH pathway.
He explained that 7,500 personnel had been brought into basic education through the programme, with 3,000 subsequently converted to permanent and pensionable appointments after training and competitive selection.
At the post-basic level, he said nearly 2,000 personnel had entered through the same programme, with 1,000 later securing permanent status.
Namadi added that the government had also deployed more than 2,100 graduate teachers and employed about 600 teaching and non-teaching staff for Mega Schools and other boarding senior secondary schools across the state.
He directed the Ministry of Higher Education, its agencies and school administrators to ensure that the latest appointments translated into measurable improvements in schools.
Namadi said postings and redeployments must be based on verified needs, relevant qualifications, merit, subject specialisation and performance, with particular attention to preventing renewed imbalances between urban and rural schools.
He urged the newly appointed teachers to demonstrate punctuality, discipline, competence and compassion, while embracing training and accepting deployment to areas where their services were most needed.
The governor also commended teachers for their resilience and dedication to educating children, saying the government would continue to support them through induction, mentoring, supervision and fair performance assessment.
On the 450 bicycles donated by GTB, Namadi said the gesture would reduce the burden of long-distance journeys to school and improve punctuality, attendance and retention among beneficiaries.
He commended the bank for supporting the government’s efforts to improve access to education through its corporate social responsibility initiative.
The governor called on traditional and religious leaders, parents and communities to support the newly appointed teachers and hold them accountable for results.
Some of the newly appointed workers expressed appreciation to the state government, pledging to abide by civil service rules and regulations and remain accountable in the discharge of their duties.

items.title: Open Source Flux 3 Image Offers Precise AI Image Editing
items.summary:
Black Forest Labs has launched FLUX 3 Image, a new AI image-generation model designed to give users more control over composition, editing, and reference images.
The model is based on the company’s FLUX 3 foundation model and supports image generation at resolutions of up to 4K.
More Control Over Object Placement
One of FLUX 3 Image’s main features is the ability to define where subjects should appear inside an image using bounding boxes.
Users can specify the location of individual people, buildings or other objects before generating the image. Black Forest Labs says the model can preserve these requested positions while still producing a coherent final image.
This gives users more direct control over composition instead of relying entirely on text prompts.

items.author: Afaq Wajdan Malik
items.content:
Black Forest Labs has launched FLUX 3 Image, a new AI image-generation model designed to give users more control over composition, editing, and reference images.
The model is based on the company’s FLUX 3 foundation model and supports image generation at resolutions of up to 4K.
More Control Over Object Placement
One of FLUX 3 Image’s main features is the ability to define where subjects should appear inside an image using bounding boxes.
Users can specify the location of individual people, buildings or other objects before generating the image. Black Forest Labs says the model can preserve these requested positions while still producing a coherent final image.
This gives users more direct control over composition instead of relying entirely on text prompts.
Introducing FLUX 3 Image.
Control every pixel.
Make precise multi-turn edits without changing any other pixel.
Lay out the image exactly how you want using bounding boxes.
Generate in up to 4K to preserve details.
Use up to 10 references to compose an image.
Commercial… pic.twitter.com/u7XqRzxkGr
— Black Forest Labs (@bfl_ai) October 1, 2026
Up to 10 Reference Images
FLUX 3 Image can accept as many as 10 reference images in a single generation.
The model can use these images to influence the final result, while users can also specify where objects taken from individual references should appear within the generated image.
Black Forest Labs has also demonstrated the model generating images containing Japanese text, including vertical writing.
Pixel-Level Image Editing
The model supports targeted image editing, allowing users to change only selected parts of an existing image.
According to Black Forest Labs, FLUX 3 Image can preserve the original image at the pixel level outside the edited region, reducing unwanted changes to areas the user did not ask to modify.
This could make the model more suitable for workflows where precise local edits are required instead of regenerating an entire image.
Make precise edits without changing any other pixel. pic.twitter.com/TudAziRnqR
— Black Forest Labs (@bfl_ai) October 1, 2026
4K Image Generation
FLUX 3 Image supports output at up to 4K resolution, allowing it to retain small details when images are viewed or cropped more closely.
The model is currently available as a paid service from Black Forest Labs.
The company also plans to release an open model version in the coming weeks.

items.title: Punjab Launches Birth Registration Drive in 100 Villages
items.summary:
The Punjab Local Government Department has launched a birth registration campaign across 100 villages in the province to make the registration process more accessible to residents.
The campaign covers villages in Rajanpur, Dera Ghazi Khan, Lodhran, Chiniot, Bhakkar, Multan and Muzaffargarh, along with selected villages in Chakwal, Khushab, Sargodha, Bahawalpur, Bahawalnagar, Jhang and Pakpattan.
Authorities have established special birth registration camps in the 100 selected villages as part of the campaign. The camps will provide on-site digital birth registration services, allowing residents to register births without traveling to distant government offices.
The initiative aims to bring the registration facility directly to rural communities and make the process more convenient for families in the selected villages.
The post Punjab Launches Birth Registration Drive in 100 Villages appeared first on ProPakistani.

items.content: Weaker-than-expected jobs growth in the US pushed traders to reduce bets on another interest rate hike by the Federal Reserve this year.The US economy added 29,000 jobs last month, the Labor Department reported, well below economists’ estimate of 90,000. Payroll growth for August was also revised lower, while the unemployment rate edged up to 4.2% from 4.1%.For live updates on US Markets, click hereThe employment data prompted traders to scale back expectations for another Fed rate increase. Interest-rate futures were pricing in less than a 20% chance of a hike at the Fed’s October meeting, down from more than 25% previously.Expectations for a December increase also eased, although markets still put the probability at nearly 90%.The labor-market data comes after the Fed raised its benchmark short-term interest rate by 25 basis points last month, as policymakers sought to bring inflation back toward their 2% target.Fed officials have indicated that another rate increase could still be warranted before year-end if inflationary pressures remain elevated, particularly amid the impact of the Iran war and other supply shocks. However, the latest employment figures add to the case for caution, especially if labor-market weakness persists.The data leaves the Fed balancing two competing risks: keeping rates high enough to contain inflation while avoiding excessive pressure on an already weakening labor market.(Disclaimer: This article is based on inputs from agencies. These do not represent the views of The Economic Times)

items.author: Nasir Butt
items.content:
The Judicial Commission probing the Mir Raza Ali case has sent questionnaires to senior police officers, including AIG Karachi Azad Khan, involved in the investigation, seeking answers to questions raised by the victim’s family.
The sealed questionnaires were delivered through the commission’s designated Nazir, Tajammal Lodhi, to AIG Azad Khan, DIG Amir Farooqi, head of the investigation team, and DIG Farukh Lanjhar.
The questions were submitted to the commission by Mir Raza’s mother, sister and father through their counsel, Advocate Jibran Nasir.
Read: Mir Raza judicial commission’s term extended until October 15
Separately, Sindh government focal person Javed Abro met commission chairman Justice Umar Sial in his chamber and informed him that the commission’s term had been extended until October 15.
The commission has also issued notices to CPLC official Kashif Iftikhar and DSP Siraj Lashari. Their statements will be recorded on October 5.
The commission is examining the circumstances surrounding Mir Raza’s death and has been recording statements and seeking responses from officials and other relevant witnesses.
The Sindh cabinet on Thursday extended the tenure of the Judicial Commission probing the death of Mir Raza Ali until October 15, giving the panel additional time to complete its proceedings and finalise its findings.
The cabinet was told that the commission, headed by Justice Umar Sial, had recorded statements from several witnesses but needed more time to complete its inquiry. It was also authorised to continue proceedings beyond October 15 if required.
The case so far
Mir Raza Ali, the 25-year-old owner of dessert brand Wafflix, went missing from Karachi’s PECHS area on July 28, 2026. His body was found the following day in bushes near a wedding hall in Gulistan-e-Johar. Police initially treated the death as a possible suicide, but a second post-mortem conducted after his exhumation found a firearm entry wound, multiple ante-mortem injuries and signs of internal bleeding, leading investigators to treat the case as murder.
The initial post-mortem had faced several objections, with the Karachi police surgeon identifying 14 deficiencies, including the absence of an X-ray, failure to collect hand swabs for gunshot-residue analysis and the lack of chemical examination of gunpowder marks around the bullet wound.
The investigation subsequently came under scrutiny from Raza’s family, who alleged serious lapses in the handling of evidence and CCTV footage and sought the formation of a joint investigation team. The Sindh High Court later rejected the family’s plea for a JIT but directed the relevant authorities to conduct the investigation impartially, fairly and expeditiously.
Read More: Mir Raza commission rejects family's plea to summon top cops
Police told a Senate committee in September that they had recorded statements from 78 people but had not found evidence linking anyone to Raza’s alleged murder. Investigators nevertheless continued to treat the case as murder, while reviewing medical, chemical, forensic and digital evidence.
The Sindh government had meanwhile established a judicial commission headed by Sindh High Court Justice Umar Sial to examine the circumstances surrounding Raza’s death, the conduct of the investigation and any possible negligence or concealment of evidence by police or other officials.
The judicial commission had so far examined police records, witness statements and the circumstances surrounding Mir Raza Ali’s death, with its proceedings raising discrepancies in witness accounts, the handling of evidence and the initial post-mortem. The commission also questioned senior police and health officials over the investigation, including the handling of CCTV footage, Raza’s phone and smartwatch, and the initial focus on a possible suicide.

items.author: Shrishti Bisht
items.content:
JSW Group’s B2B ecommerce marketplace JSW One Platforms narrowed its consolidated net loss by 50.9% to ₹106.5 Cr in FY26 from ₹217 Cr in the previous financial year, helped by revenue growth outpacing the rise in expenses.
Its operating revenue jumped 44.9% to ₹5,743.4 Cr from ₹3,962.8 Cr in FY25, according to its DRHP. The company runs a technology-led platform that combines procurement of manufacturing and construction materials with logistics, processing, and access to credit.
Including other income of ₹44.2 Cr, total income stood at ₹5,787.6 Cr in FY26, compared with ₹3,979.5 Cr a year earlier.
The financial disclosures come as JSW One prepares for a proposed ₹3,054 Cr IPO.
For the June quarter of FY27, JSW One reported a consolidated profit of ₹14.2 Cr on an operating revenue of ₹1,642.5 Cr. The DRHP did not disclose the comparable Q1 FY26 numbers.
What Drove JSW One’s Revenue Growth In FY26?
Sales of goods remained JSW One’s largest revenue source, rising 45.5% to ₹5,619.6 Cr in FY26 from ₹3,862.1 Cr in FY25. This business includes steel and related products, cement, and other construction materials.
The company attributed the growth primarily to the expansion of its private brands and service centre business. Steel volumes increased 51.2% to 27.1 Lakh tonnes, while cement volumes rose 23.9% to 2.6 Lakh tonnes.
Services revenue grew 11.4% to ₹109.6 Cr from ₹98.4 Cr. Within this, commission income from the MSME business increased to ₹100.3 Cr from ₹83 Cr, while homes business commissions rose to ₹9.3 Cr from ₹7.5 Cr.
Financial services revenue increased more than sixfold to ₹14.2 Cr from ₹2.3 Cr, although it contributed just 0.2% of consolidated operating revenue.
Where Did JSW One Spend?
JSW One’s total expenses increased 40.5% to ₹5,894.1 Cr in FY26 from ₹4,196.5 Cr in FY25.
Material Purchases: Purchases of stock-in-trade, its largest expense, rose 42.7% to ₹5,444.1 Cr from ₹3,815.4 Cr as the company procured more materials to support its distribution and private brands businesses.
Employee Costs: Employee benefit expenses declined 1.2% to ₹264.3 Cr from ₹267.6 Cr. The decline was driven by lower share-based payment expenses, which fell to ₹16 Cr from ₹59.5 Cr. However, salaries and wages increased to ₹217 Cr from ₹185.7 Cr.
Transportation Costs: Transportation expenses climbed 58% to ₹152.1 Cr from ₹96.2 Cr, reflecting the expansion of its delivery network and higher freight costs.
Technology Expenses: Platform and technology expenses increased 32.9% to ₹29.6 Cr from ₹22.3 Cr, driven by higher transaction volumes and associated cloud hosting, software licensing, and maintenance costs.
Inside JSW One’s B2B Ecommerce Business
Promoted by JSW Steel and JSW Cement, JSW One operates a B2B ecommerce marketplace for manufacturing and construction MSMEs. Its technology platform allows customers to discover and compare materials, place orders, arrange financing, and track fulfilment.
The business combines a commission-based marketplace with a distribution model. In marketplace transactions, JSW One earns a commission for connecting buyers and sellers. Through subsidiary JSW One Distribution, it also purchases materials, arranges processing and customisation, and sells them to customers, recognising the full sale value as revenue.
Its offerings overlap with those of startups such as OfBusiness, Infra.Market and Zetwerk subsidiary Terra91 across materials procurement, construction supplies and manufacturing services.
Incorporated as JSW Retail in 2018, the company was renamed JSW One Platforms in December 2020. It launched the JSW One MSME and JSW One Homes portals in 2021, subsequently expanding into private brands and lending. Its subsidiary JSW One Finance received its NBFC registration in 2024.
JSW One raised ₹205 Cr in a Series A round led by Mitsui & Co. in April 2023 at a valuation of ₹2,750 Cr.
It later closed a ₹575 Cr funding round in October last year, with participation from SBI, Principal Asset Management, One-Up, International Conveyors, Scarlett Ventures, and JSW Steel.
JSW One’s ₹3,054 Cr IPO Plan
JSW One’s proposed IPO comprises a fresh issue of ₹1,300 Cr and an OFS of ₹1,754 Cr.
JSW Steel plans to sell shares worth up to ₹811 Cr, JSW Cement up to ₹123 Cr, and Mitsui & Co. up to ₹820 Cr through the OFS.
From the fresh issue proceeds, the company plans to invest ₹500 Cr in JSW One Finance to strengthen its capital base, ₹350 Cr in technology and platform development, and ₹125 Cr in marketing and brand-building through JSW One Distribution. The remaining net proceeds will be used for general corporate purposes.
JSW One may also undertake a pre-IPO placement of up to ₹260 Cr, which would reduce the fresh issue size by the amount raised.
Edited by Vinaykumar Rai

items.author: Web Desk
items.content:
Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi said on Friday that the "country's system was about to be reset" and that this move would improve the state of affairs in Pakistan.
Naqvi’s latest remarks come amid an ongoing debate over the creation of new provinces and restructuring of the country’s administrative setup, after he said earlier this year that the governance system had collapsed and was no longer capable of addressing the country’s challenges
Addressing a ceremony of the Lahore Chamber of Commerce and Industry to congratulate its newly elected office-bearers, Naqvi stated that Pakistan should learn from the "experience and systems" of developed countries.
Also Read: Naqvi vows not to back down from demand for new provinces, says decision must reflect public will
"I will not delve into the details right now, but I have been trying, and while we have achieved many things, I can tell you that the system of this country is going to be reset. For this reset to take place, we need the business community's support. When the system is reset, I remain hopeful that many things will improve," he remarked.
He said the solution to the country’s economic problems was to increase exports by any means possible, adding that whether the target was $170 billion or $9 billion, “every dollar is important” to him.
“Wherever you need me, I am available to you 24 hours a day. As long as I am sitting in this seat, I am here for you,” he told members of the chamber.
He said that over the past three to four months, he had frequently travelled to Iran for mediation efforts aimed at resolving the conflict between Tehran and Washington, which had engulfed the region since Feb 28, when the United States and Israel attacked Iran.
Naqvi said those who had not visited Iran might assume that the country, having been at war and under sanctions for 30 to 40 years, would be devastated, but those who travelled with him were surprised by the level of self-reliance there.
“They have a construction industry, an automobile industry — name anything and they manufacture it in their own country,” he said.
He urged the members to consider shifting towards “Made in Pakistan”, saying that if the goods currently imported from abroad were produced domestically, it would be highly beneficial for the country.
“If Iranians can manufacture and do everything themselves, why can’t we?” the minister asked.
While acknowledging that the country would continue to rely on oil imports, he said Pakistan also imported other goods worth more than $40 billion annually and that this bill could be reduced to $20 billion.
“This is also very easy to do. If we set targets of $10 billion and $5 billion and start working towards them, God willing, we can make significant progress in three to four years,” he said.
He suggested that the chamber should, alongside increasing exports, also prepare a “Made in Pakistan” proposal for Islamabad so that work could be undertaken on both fronts.
Read: Governance system has collapsed: Naqvi
The current debate over new provinces began on July 30, when Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi called for additional administrative units or provinces as part of a broader overhaul of the country’s governance system. Naqvi argued that meaningful structural reforms were needed to improve governance, deliver justice and create opportunities for young people.
A day later, his proposal appeared to receive support from Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR) Director General Lt Gen Ahmed Sharif Chaudhry, who said an administrative reset, if required, should be undertaken to ensure good governance
The proposal quickly became politically sensitive in Sindh, where the PPP strongly opposed any move to divide the province. Sindh Chief Minister Murad Ali Shah rejected Naqvi’s assessment that the governance system had collapsed and called the proposal outdated, warning that no bloodshed would be allowed over the creation of new provinces.
The debate widened in August when Muttahida Qaumi Movement–Pakistan (MQM-P) backed the creation of new provinces and called for a national dialogue with political parties. The party argued that Pakistan’s growing population, poor governance and concentration of political power made greater administrative devolution necessary. The move put the party, which is part of the federal coalition but sits in opposition in Sindh, at odds with the PPP’s position on the province.
The PPP, meanwhile, maintained that administrative reform and the division of Sindh were separate questions. Sindh minister Nasir Hussain Shah said the provincial government was willing to discuss measures to improve governance and devolve power, but rejected linking those reforms to the creation of a new province.
The dispute reached the Sindh Assembly at the beginning of September. On September 3, the house unanimously passed a resolution rejecting any proposal to divide Sindh or alter its territorial limits. The resolution described Sindh as a “historic, civilisational and constitutional entity” and declared that “Sindh is one and shall remain one”.
Read More: PTI's Barrister Gohar warns against dividing provinces without broad public consensus
Naqvi, however, showed no sign of backing away. On September 5, he said he would continue to support new provinces regardless of whether he remained in office, arguing that the ultimate decision should belong to the people rather than politicians or governments. He said the public should first be told the “pros and cons” of creating new administrative units before being allowed to decide.
That position has since raised another question over how public opinion could be formally established. A constitutional debate emerged over whether a referendum could be used to gauge support for new provinces. Article 48(6) allows a matter of national importance to be put to a referendum following approval by a joint sitting of Parliament, although a referendum itself would not create a new province; any change to provincial boundaries would still have to follow the constitutional process.
Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf Chairman Barrister Gohar Ali Khan warned on September 7 that dividing Sindh or any other province without the consent of its people and representatives would weaken the federation. He called for a commission and extensive deliberations before the issue was taken to parliament.
Defence Minister Khawaja Asif, while accepting that Sindh had the right to take its own position, also said a final decision would have to emerge through consensus. Asif separately suggested that Islamabad could be used as a starting point for any future administrative restructuring, while Prime Minister’s Adviser Rana Sanaullah said the question of new provinces should be taken up at the relevant forums and resolved through consensus among political parties.

items.title: Govt increases petrol by Rs2.1, diesel by 30 paisas till Oct 5

The federal government on Friday increased the price of petrol and high-speed diesel (HSD) by Rs2.1 and 30 paisas per litre, respectively, till October 5.
According to a notification issued by the Petroleum Division, the price of petrol was fixed at Rs392.76 per litre, while HSD would cost Rs399.64 per litre from October 3 to October 5.

items.content:
The federal government on Friday increased the price of petrol and high-speed diesel (HSD) by Rs2.1 and 30 paisas per litre, respectively, till October 5.
According to a notification issued by the Petroleum Division, the price of petrol was fixed at Rs392.76 per litre, while HSD would cost Rs399.64 per litre from October 3 to October 5.
The latest revision comes a day after the government increased the price of petrol by Rs3.26 per litre, while decreasing the price of HSD by Rs1.01 per litre for October 2.
Read: Govt increases petrol by Rs3.26, cuts diesel by Rs1.01 for Oct 2
On July 17, the government announced a new pricing mechanism under which petroleum product prices would be reviewed and notified daily, replacing the weekly pricing mechanism, as renewed tensions between the United States and Iran continued to drive volatility in global oil markets and raise concerns over fuel supplies.
On September 13, PM Shehbaz announced a special relief scheme offering Rs100 per litre off petrol for motorcycles, three-wheeler rickshaws and cars with engines up to 800cc, in an attempt to shield lower-income consumers from the impact of rising petroleum prices.
Under the proposal, an estimated 11.8 million beneficiaries would be covered. Around 10 million two-wheeler users and 800,000 three-wheeler users would be entitled to relief on 20 litres of fuel per month, translating into a maximum monthly benefit of Rs2,000 per beneficiary.
Another one million users of cars up to 800cc would receive relief on 30 litres per month, providing them with a maximum benefit of Rs3,000 each.
On Sept 17, the government reintroduced austerity and fuel conservation measures amid rising fuel prices, tightening business operating hours and restricting public events.
Under the measures, notified with immediate effect, shops, markets, shopping malls, bazaars, departmental stores, grocery stores, general stores and kiryana shops would close by 9pm throughout the week, according to a notification issued by the Cabinet Division.
Marriage halls, marquees and other commercial venues hosting festive events would close by 10pm, while restaurants, cafes, eateries, food outlets and standalone fruit and vegetable shops would be allowed to operate until 11pm. Takeaway and home delivery services would remain exempt from the timing restrictions.
Global geopolitical developments continue to pose significant risks. International oil prices are influenced by decisions taken by OPEC+, conflicts in the Middle East, sanctions on oil-producing nations, and disruptions in critical shipping routes such as the Strait of Hormuz and the Red Sea. Any interruption in these supply chains can immediately increase crude oil prices and freight costs. Since Pakistan imports the majority of its petroleum requirements, these developments quickly translate into higher domestic fuel prices.
Oil prices fell $2 after European leaders agreed ​on Friday to a request by US President Donald Trump to release diesel from their reserves to lower ‌prices and reduce the need to import fuel from America.
Brent was down $1.80, or 1.76%, at $100.50 a barrel at 10:49 am CDT (1649 GMT). West Texas Intermediate dropped $2.02, or 2.18%, to $90.85 a barrel.
European Union countries agreed to a French ​proposal to release additional diesel stockpiles, a source familiar with details of the discussion told Reuters.
"Europe is feeling pretty vulnerable," said Phil Flynn, senior ​analyst with the Price Futures Group. "Europe would be one of the areas to suffer the most if we put an export ban on ​diesel."
